knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical threshold complexity of Unweighted MaxSAT.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an explicitly represented CNF multiset \(F\) and integer \(k\), deciding whether an assignment satisfies at least \(k\) clauses is NP-complete. Hardness already holds for \(k=|F|\), where the question is CNF satisfiability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deciding whether at least k clauses can be satisfied is NP-complete.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) and \(k\) are explicitly encoded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{(F,k):\operatorname{OPT}(F)\ge k\}\text{ is NP-complete}.
knowledge_statements.title: Unweighted MaxSAT Decision Complexity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective range and exact satisfiability boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an unweighted MaxSAT instance containing \(m\) clauses, \[0\le\operatorname{OPT}(F)\le m,\qquad \operatorname{OPT}(F)=m\iff\bigwedge_{C\in F}C\text{ is satisfiable}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The optimum is at most the number of clauses and reaches that value exactly when the CNF is satisfiable.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite multiset of \(m\) clauses.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\le\operatorname{OPT}(F)\le m,\quad\operatorname{OPT}(F)=m\iff F\text{ is satisfiable}.
knowledge_statements.title: SAT Threshold Characterization
Unweighted MaxSAT
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite propositional CNF with every clause contributing one unit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=\{C_1,\ldots,C_m\}\) be a finite multiset of clauses over Boolean variables \(X\). Unweighted MaxSAT asks for an assignment \(x\in\{0,1\}^{X}\) maximizing the number of satisfied clauses:
\[\operatorname{OPT}(F)=\max_{x\in\{0,1\}^{X}}\sum_{i=1}^{m}\mathbf{1}[x\models C_i].\]
Equivalently, it minimizes \(\sum_{i=1}^{m}\mathbf{1}[x\not\models C_i]\). Repeated clauses are counted with their multiplicities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unweighted MaxSAT finds a Boolean assignment satisfying as many clauses as possible, with every clause worth one unit.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite multiset of propositional clauses.
Assignments are total on the finite variable set \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{OPT}(F)=\max_x\sum_{i=1}^{m}\mathbf{1}[x\models C_i]\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically standard, precise, and appropriate for the Unweighted MaxSAT container, but no citation or inspectable locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Threshold complexity for binary-encoded nonnegative integer weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given explicitly represented clauses with nonnegative integer weights and threshold \(K\), deciding whether some assignment satisfies clauses of total weight at least \(K\) is NP-complete. Hardness persists when every weight is one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Attaining a specified satisfied weight is NP-complete, even with unit weights.
assumptions_latex: Weights and \(K\) are nonnegative integers encoded in binary.
The clause family is explicitly represented.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{(F,w,K):\exists x\ \sum_iw_i\mathbf1[x\models C_i]\ge K\}\text{ is NP-complete}.
knowledge_statements.title: Weighted MaxSAT Decision Complexity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Range, zero-weight invariance, and full-weight satisfiability boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W=\sum_iw_i\) with \(w_i\ge0\). Then \[0\le\operatorname{OPT}(F,w)\le W.\] Deleting zero-weight clauses preserves every objective value, and \(\operatorname{OPT}(F,w)=W\) exactly when all positive-weight clauses are jointly satisfiable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The optimum lies between zero and total weight; zero-weight clauses are irrelevant, and full weight is attainable exactly when all positive-weight clauses are jointly satisfiable.
assumptions_latex: \(w_i\ge0\) for every clause.
\(W=\sum_iw_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\le\operatorname{OPT}(F,w)\le W,\quad\operatorname{OPT}(F,w)=W\iff\bigwedge_{i:w_i>0}C_i\text{ is satisfiable}.
knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Objective Bounds
Weighted MaxSAT
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite MaxSAT with a nonnegative numerical weight on every clause.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=\{C_1,\ldots,C_m\}\) be clauses over Boolean variables \(X\), with weights \(w_i\ge 0\). Weighted MaxSAT asks for an assignment \(x\in\{0,1\}^{X}\) satisfying
\[\operatorname{OPT}(F,w)=\max_x\sum_{i=1}^{m}w_i\mathbf{1}[x\models C_i].\]
Equivalently, because \(\sum_i w_i\) is constant, it minimizes the total weight \(\sum_i w_i\mathbf{1}[x\not\models C_i]\) of falsified clauses. Unweighted MaxSAT is the special case \(w_i=1\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted MaxSAT maximizes the total weight of satisfied clauses, equivalently minimizing the weight of falsified clauses.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) and \(X\) are finite.
\(w_i\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}\) for every clause.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{OPT}(F,w)=\max_x\sum_i w_i\mathbf{1}[x\models C_i]\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The weighted objective and its equivalence to minimizing falsified weight are correct for finite instances with nonnegative weights, but the record has no supporting citation or locator.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decision complexity of unit-weight Partial MaxSAT.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given hard clauses \(H\), soft clauses \(S\), and \(0\le k\le |S|\), deciding whether some assignment satisfies every clause in \(H\) and falsifies at most \(k\) clauses in \(S\) is NP-complete. Hardness already holds when \(H=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Requiring all hard clauses and allowing at most k violated soft clauses is NP-complete.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) and \(S\) are finite explicitly represented clause multisets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists x\left(x\models H\land\sum_{C\in S}\mathbf1[x\not\models C]\le k\right)\text{ is NP-complete}.

notation.meaning: Maximum allowed number of falsified soft clauses.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial MaxSAT Threshold Complexity
Partial MaxSAT
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unweighted optimization of soft clauses subject to mandatory hard clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) and \(S\) be finite multisets of hard and soft clauses over Boolean variables \(X\). Partial MaxSAT seeks an assignment \(x\in\{0,1\}^{X}\) such that \(x\models C\) for every \(C\in H\), while maximizing
\[\sum_{C\in S}\mathbf{1}[x\models C].\]
An instance is feasible exactly when the conjunction of the hard clauses is satisfiable. If feasible, its optimum may equivalently be expressed by minimizing the number of falsified soft clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partial MaxSAT requires every hard clause and maximizes the number of satisfied soft clauses.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) and \(S\) are finite clause multisets.
Every feasible assignment must satisfy all clauses in \(H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max\{\sum_{C\in S}\mathbf{1}[x\models C]:x\models H\}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The hard/soft-clause definition fits Partial MaxSAT and is mathematically coherent, but no relevant source with a specific locator is provided.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decision complexity of Weighted Partial MaxSAT.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given hard clauses, explicitly represented soft clauses with nonnegative integer weights, and threshold \(K\), deciding whether an assignment satisfies every hard clause and soft clauses of total weight at least \(K\) is NP-complete. Hardness persists when the hard set is empty and when every soft weight is one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Attaining a weighted soft-clause threshold while satisfying every hard clause is NP-complete.
assumptions_latex: Soft weights and \(K\) are nonnegative integers encoded in binary.
Hard and soft clauses are explicitly represented.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists x\left(x\models H\land\sum_iw_i\mathbf1[x\models C_i]\ge K\right)\text{ is NP-complete}.
knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Partial MaxSAT Threshold Complexity
Weighted Partial MaxSAT
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted soft-clause optimization under inviolable hard clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be a finite multiset of hard clauses and let \(S=\{C_1,
\ldots,C_m\}\) be soft clauses with weights \(w_i\ge 0\), all over Boolean variables \(X\). Weighted Partial MaxSAT seeks
\[\max_{x\in\{0,1\}^{X}}\left\{\sum_{i=1}^{m}w_i\mathbf{1}[x\models C_i]:x\models C\text{ for every }C\in H\right\}.\]
Equivalently, among assignments satisfying \(H\), it minimizes the total weight of falsified soft clauses. The instance is infeasible when \(H\) is unsatisfiable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted Partial MaxSAT satisfies all hard clauses while maximizing the weight of satisfied soft clauses.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) and \(S\) are finite.
Each soft-clause weight satisfies \(w_i\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max\{\sum_iw_i\mathbf{1}[x\models C_i]:x\models H\}\).

notation.meaning: Soft clause and its nonnegative weight.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition correctly combines mandatory hard clauses with weighted soft clauses, but it lacks the required source and inspectable locator.

children.title: Lexicographic MaxSAT
children.top_down_role: MaxSAT objectives governed by a strict ordering among preference criteria.

assumptions_latex: The reported objective values are recomputed from the supplied assignment.
Every conditional scalar upper-bound certificate is independently sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^*\models H\land\bigwedge_{\ell=1}^{L}\left[\max\{f_\ell(x):x\models H,\ f_j(x)=v_j\ (j<\ell)\}\le v_\ell=f_\ell(x^*)\right]\Rightarrow x^*\in\operatorname{Argmax}_{\mathrm{lex}}f.

notation.meaning: attained value of level ell at the candidate assignment

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate interpretation for a lexicographically optimal MaxSAT assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A hard-feasible assignment \(x^*\), its values \(v_\ell=f_\ell(x^*)\), and checked certificates proving \(f_\ell(x)\le v_\ell\) under \(H\land\bigwedge_{j<\ell}(f_j=v_j)\) for every level certify that no feasible assignment is lexicographically preferred to \(x^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasibility plus a matching conditional upper-bound certificate at every priority level certifies lexicographic optimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Levelwise Lexicographic Optimality Certificate

assumptions_latex: Each level has finite total soft-clause weight.
Both conventions use the same level order and clause weights.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f(x)\succeq_{\mathrm{lex}}f(y)\iff g(x)\preceq_{\mathrm{lex}}g(y).

notation.meaning: violated weight at priority level ell
total soft-clause weight at priority level ell

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent maximization and minimization conventions for lexicographic MaxSAT.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W_\ell=\sum_{C_i\in S_\ell}w_i\) and \(g_\ell(x)=W_\ell-f_\ell(x)\). For any hard-feasible assignments \(x,y\), the satisfied-weight vector of \(x\) is lexicographically at least that of \(y\) exactly when the violation-cost vector of \(x\) is lexicographically at most that of \(y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lexicographically maximizing satisfied weight is equivalent to lexicographically minimizing violated weight at the same priority levels.
knowledge_statements.title: Satisfied-Weight and Violation-Cost Equivalence
Lexicographic MaxSAT
knowledge_statements.scope_note: MaxSAT with totally ordered objective components and strict priority.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be hard clauses and let \(S_1,\ldots,S_L\) be priority classes of weighted soft clauses, where level \(1\) has highest priority. For each assignment \(x\models H\), define \(f_\ell(x)=\sum_{C_i\in S_\ell}w_i\mathbf{1}[x\models C_i]\). Lexicographic MaxSAT selects an assignment whose vector
\[f(x)=(f_1(x),\ldots,f_L(x))\]
is lexicographically maximal: \(x^*\) is optimal when no feasible \(y\) has, at the first level \(k\) where \(f_k(y)\ne f_k(x^*)\), the strict inequality \(f_k(y)>f_k(x^*)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lexicographic MaxSAT optimizes the highest-priority clause class first, then each lower class without degrading earlier optima.
assumptions_latex: \(H,S_1,\ldots,S_L\) are finite.
Priority levels are totally ordered from \(1\) to \(L\).
Soft weights are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x^*)=\max_{\mathrm{lex}}\{f(x):x\models H\}\).

notation.meaning: Soft clauses at priority level ell.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The lexicographic formulation is internally consistent and fits the container, but MaxSAT terminology for hierarchical and lexicographic variants is not uniform; an authoritative source with a specific locator is required.

children.title: Multilevel MaxSAT
children.top_down_role: MaxSAT formulations partitioned into ordered priority levels.

assumptions_latex: Every conditional optimality certificate is sound.
The final assignment satisfies the hard clauses and attains every recorded level value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall\ell\quad v_\ell=\max\{f_\ell(x):x\models H,\ f_j(x)=v_j\text{ for }j<\ell\}.

notation.meaning: conditional optimum value at level ell

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composable certificate for sequentially fixed priority levels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each level \(\ell\), a checked certificate that no assignment satisfying \(H\) and \(f_j=v_j\) for all \(j<\ell\) has \(f_\ell>v_\ell\), together with a final assignment attaining all \(v_\ell\), certifies the complete multilevel optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One conditional optimality certificate per level, plus a final assignment attaining every recorded value, certifies the multilevel result.
knowledge_statements.title: Multilevel Conditional-Optimum Certificate

assumptions_latex: Each scalar level subproblem is solved exactly.
Every attained-value equality has an exact representation accepted by the scalar solver.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{scalar\ optimization\ calls}}=L.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle-call complexity of the sequential multilevel construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(L\) ordered levels, the sequential fixing construction performs exactly \(L\) scalar optimization calls. This is an oracle-call count, not a polynomial-time bound on those NP-hard scalar subproblems; the additional bookkeeping consists of the \(L-1\) previously attained-value constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sequential multilevel optimization makes one exact scalar optimization call per level; this does not make the scalar subproblems tractable.
knowledge_statements.title: Levelwise Oracle Complexity
Multilevel MaxSAT
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Priority classes represented by sequential constrained MaxSAT subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) and level objectives \(f_1,\ldots,f_L\) be as in hierarchical MaxSAT, with level \(1\) highest. Define \(v_1=\max\{f_1(x):x\models H\}\), and recursively for \(\ell=2,\ldots,L\),
\[v_\ell=\max\{f_\ell(x):x\models H,\ f_j(x)=v_j\text{ for }j<\ell\}.\]
The multilevel feasible optimum set is
\[\{x:x\models H,\ f_\ell(x)=v_\ell\text{ for every }\ell\}.\]
Thus strict multilevel optimization is represented by sequentially fixing every attained higher-level optimum before optimizing the next level.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multilevel MaxSAT solves priority levels sequentially, fixing each higher-level optimum before optimizing the next level.
assumptions_latex: The clause sets and priority levels are finite.
The hard clauses admit at least one satisfying assignment.
Each level objective is bounded on feasible assignments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Argmax}_{\mathrm{lex}}f=\{x:x\models H,\ f_\ell(x)=v_\ell\ \forall\ell\}\).

notation.meaning: Sequentially attained optimum at level ell.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The sequential fixing construction correctly represents lexicographic optimization, but no source establishes that this is the intended Multilevel MaxSAT convention. The selected representation kind also depends on that convention.

children.title: Priority-Level Interaction
children.top_down_role: Structural relationships between lexicographic ordering and multilevel objective organization.

assumptions_latex: The attainable set \(Y\) is finite.
The multipliers are fixed before comparing outcomes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \left[\forall y,z\in Y,\ y\succ_{\mathrm{lex}}z\iff F_M(y)>F_M(z)\right]\iff F_M\text{ represents the strict lexicographic order on }Y.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient criterion for representing the full lexicographic order on a fixed attainable set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y=\{f(x):x\models H\}\) and \(F_M(y)=\sum_{\ell=1}^{L}M_\ell y_\ell\). The scalar score represents the full strict lexicographic order on \(Y\) exactly when, for every distinct \(y,z\in Y\), \(y\succ_{\mathrm{lex}}z\) if and only if \(F_M(y)>F_M(z)\). This condition implies equality of the scalar-maximal and lexicographically maximal outcome sets. The seed's range-dominance inequalities are a uniform sufficient condition for it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a fixed attainable set, scalar multipliers represent lexicographic priority exactly when they preserve every strict lexicographic pairwise comparison.
knowledge_statements.title: Full-Order Pairwise Criterion

assumptions_latex: Both displayed outcome vectors are attainable.
Level 1 has priority over level 2.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M_1<M_2R\Rightarrow F_M(z)>F_M(y);\qquad M_1=M_2R\Rightarrow F_M(z)=F_M(y),
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp two-outcome failure when a higher-level multiplier does not dominate lower-level range.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For attainable vectors \(y=(1,0)\) and \(z=(0,R)\), lexicographic order prefers \(y\). With \(F_M(u)=M_1u_1+M_2u_2\), \(M_1<M_2R\) makes the scalar score prefer \(z\), while \(M_1=M_2R\) ties \(z\) with the lexicographically superior \(y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the top-level multiplier is below the full lower-level contribution, lower priority reverses the decision; equality admits an improper tie.
knowledge_statements.title: Lower-Level Overturning Counterexample
Priority-Level Interaction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dominance condition for encoding strict priorities by one scalar objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For integer-valued level objectives \(f_1,\ldots,f_L\), let \(R_\ell=\max f_\ell-\min f_\ell\) over feasible assignments. A scalar objective \(F(x)=\sum_{\ell=1}^{L}M_\ell f_\ell(x)\), with \(M_\ell>0\), preserves lexicographic priority whenever
\[M_k>\sum_{\ell=k+1}^{L}M_\ell R_\ell\qquad(k=1,\ldots,L-1).\]
Under this condition, a unit improvement at level \(k\) outweighs every possible aggregate change at lower levels. Hence every maximizer of \(F\) is lexicographically maximal; if the condition fails, lower levels may overturn a higher-level improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scalar encoding preserves strict priorities when every level's multiplier dominates the largest possible contribution of all lower levels.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_\ell\) is integer-valued and bounded on the feasible set.
Level \(1\) has highest priority.
Scalar multipliers satisfy \(M_\ell>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_k>\sum_{\ell>k}M_\ell R_\ell\Rightarrow\operatorname{Argmax}F\subseteq\operatorname{Argmax}_{\mathrm{lex}}f\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated dominance inequality is sufficient for bounded integer-valued objectives because any strict higher-level improvement is at least one unit. The condition fits the container, but its MaxSAT-specific use and the boundary statement require a relevant source.

children.title: Multiobjective MaxSAT
children.top_down_role: MaxSAT instances with multiple simultaneously relevant objective components.

assumptions_latex: At least two attainable vectors are ranked differently by admissible preference rules, or are incomparable under componentwise order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\mathcal X,f)\text{ without a declared preference relation or requested output set does not determine a unique optimum concept}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between a vector-valued instance and a fully specified optimization task.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The feasible set \(\mathcal X\) and vector map \(f:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R^p\) determine the attainable set \(Y=f(\mathcal X)\), but not which outcomes are requested. Lexicographic order, Pareto nondominance, and a chosen scalarization can select different assignments from the same \(Y\). Thus the comparison rule or requested solution set is part of the problem semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Objective vectors alone do not determine what is optimal; the comparison rule or requested solution set must also be declared.
knowledge_statements.title: Preference-Relation Underspecification

assumptions_latex: There are finitely many clauses and objective components.
All objective components are evaluated on the same hard-feasible assignments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f_j(x)=\sum_i w_{ij}\mathbf 1[x\models C_i]\qquad(j=1,\ldots,p).

notation.meaning: nonnegative objective-weight vector of clause i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unified representation allowing one clause to contribute to several objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assign each soft clause \(C_i\) a vector weight \(w_i\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}^{p}\) and define \(f(x)=\sum_iw_i\mathbf1[x\models C_i]\). Componentwise, this is equivalent to listing \(C_i\)'s contribution in each objective class whose corresponding weight is nonzero, without duplicating the Boolean constraint itself.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A soft clause can carry a vector weight and contribute to several objectives without duplicating its logical semantics.
knowledge_statements.title: Vector-Weighted Clause Representation
Multiobjective MaxSAT
knowledge_statements.scope_note: MaxSAT with several simultaneously evaluated clause-satisfaction objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be hard clauses and let \(f=(f_1,\ldots,f_p)\) be objective functions on assignments satisfying \(H\), where each \(f_j(x)\) is the total weight of clauses from objective class \(j\) satisfied by \(x\). Multiobjective MaxSAT is the finite vector optimization problem
\[\max_{x\models H} f(x)\]
under a specified preference relation on \(\mathbb{R}^{p}\), commonly componentwise Pareto order, lexicographic order, or an explicitly chosen scalarization. Without such a relation, the instance determines attainable objective vectors but generally not a single optimal assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiobjective MaxSAT evaluates feasible assignments by several clause-satisfaction objectives and requires an explicit vector preference rule.
assumptions_latex: The variables, hard clauses, and objective clause classes are finite.
Every objective weight is nonnegative.
At least one assignment satisfies \(H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max\{f(x):x\models H\}\) is interpreted through a declared preference relation.

notation.meaning: Value of objective j at assignment x.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The vector-optimization definition is coherent and locally appropriate, but the meaning of Multiobjective MaxSAT and its admissible preference regimes must be supported by a specific MaxSAT or multiobjective-optimization source.

children.title: Pareto MaxSAT
children.top_down_role: Nondominated solution concepts within multiobjective MaxSAT.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite exact enumeration of distinct Pareto objective vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(V=\varnothing\). Repeatedly seek \(x\in\mathcal X\) satisfying \(\bigwedge_{v\in V}\bigvee_{j=1}^p f_j(x)>v_j\). If none exists, stop. Otherwise repeatedly replace \(x\) by a feasible strict dominator until none exists, emit \(f(x)\), and add it to \(V\). For finite \(\mathcal X\), the procedure terminates and emits each nondominated objective vector exactly once.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly find an outcome outside the regions dominated by emitted vectors, improve it to nondominance, and exclude its dominated region.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X\) is finite.
All dominance and feasibility queries are exact.
Every objective component is maximized.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: V=\operatorname{Max}_{\succeq}(f(\mathcal X))\text{ at termination}.

notation.meaning: Set of emitted nondominated objective vectors.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Pareto-Vector Enumeration

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact Pareto-optimality test for a hard-feasible assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For hard-feasible \(x\), let \[D_x:=H\wedge\bigwedge_{j=1}^p(f_j\ge f_j(x))\wedge\bigvee_{j=1}^p(f_j>f_j(x)).\] Then \(x\) is Pareto-optimal if and only if \(D_x\) is unsatisfiable. A feasible witness for \(x\), checked objective values, and a checked refutation of \(D_x\) therefore certify Pareto optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible assignment is Pareto-optimal exactly when no feasible strict dominator exists.
assumptions_latex: \(x\models H\).
The objective comparisons are encoded exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x\text{ is Pareto-optimal}\iff D_x\text{ is unsatisfiable}.
knowledge_statements.title: Dominance-Query Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence and domination coverage for finite feasible outcome sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\mathcal X\) is finite, a Pareto-optimal assignment exists exactly when \(\mathcal X\neq\varnothing\). Every vector in \(f(\mathcal X)\) is weakly dominated by some nondominated vector in \(f(\mathcal X)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every nonempty finite instance has a Pareto optimum, and every feasible outcome lies below a nondominated outcome.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X\) is finite.
\(f:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R^p\) and every component is maximized.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal X\neq\varnothing\iff\operatorname{Max}_{\succeq}(f(\mathcal X))\neq\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Pareto Existence
Pareto MaxSAT
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiobjective MaxSAT under componentwise nondominance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a feasible assignment set \(\mathcal{X}=\{x:x\models H\}\) and maximization objective vector \(f:\mathcal{X}\to\mathbb{R}^{p}\), an assignment \(x^*\in\mathcal{X}\) is Pareto-optimal when no \(y\in\mathcal{X}\) satisfies
\[f_j(y)\ge f_j(x^*)\text{ for every }j,\qquad f_k(y)>f_k(x^*)\text{ for some }k.\]
Pareto MaxSAT asks for one or all such assignments, or equivalently their nondominated objective vectors. Distinct Pareto-optimal assignments may produce the same objective vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pareto MaxSAT seeks feasible assignments that cannot improve one objective without worsening at least one other objective.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal{X}\) is the finite set of assignments satisfying the hard clauses.
All objective components are maximized.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^*\) is Pareto-optimal exactly when no feasible assignment dominates it componentwise.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The componentwise nondominance definition is correct and fits Pareto MaxSAT, but no authoritative citation or specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Pareto Frontier Structure
children.top_down_role: Organization, representation, and size regimes of nondominated objective outcomes.

assumptions_latex: The attainable objective set is finite.
Candidate generation is complete for the residual region.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite exact enumeration of distinct nondominated objective vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Repeatedly obtain an attainable vector outside the downward closure of previously returned vectors, improve it to a nondominated vector \(y\), output \(y\), and add the blocking constraint \(\bigvee_j(f_j>y_j)\). Exact residual candidate generation and exact improvement return every distinct member of \(Y^{\mathrm{ND}}\); finiteness gives termination after all such vectors have been output and the residual query is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Improve residual candidates to nondominated vectors and block each output's downward closure; exact exhaustion enumerates the frontier without duplicate outcomes.
knowledge_statements.title: Dominance-Blocking Frontier Enumeration

assumptions_latex: All comparisons use componentwise maximization order.
Every reported vector has a checked feasible preimage.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A reported set \(P\) is the complete Pareto frontier when each \(p\in P\) has a feasible preimage, \(P\) is an antichain, and checked infeasibility evidence establishes that no feasible objective vector lies outside \(\downarrow P=\bigcup_{p\in P}\{y:y\le p\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Frontier completeness requires witnesses for every output, pairwise nondominance, and certified coverage of every attainable vector by a reported vector.

Distinct assignments yield distinct vectors, and for any two assignments some complementary component improves in each direction, so neither vector dominates the other. Consequently all \(2^n\) attainable vectors lie on the frontier.

For any Pareto-optimal assignment \(x^*\), choosing \(\epsilon_j=f_j(x^*)\) makes \(f(x^*)\) an optimal objective vector of the constrained problem; ties can only be assignments with that same vector.

Objective Scalarization Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted-sum scalarization and its limitation for discrete Pareto fronts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathcal{X}\to\mathbb{R}^{p}\) be maximized over the finite feasible set \(\mathcal{X}\). For \(\lambda\in\mathbb{R}^{p}_{>0}\), every maximizer of
\[F_\lambda(x)=\sum_{j=1}^{p}\lambda_j f_j(x)\]
is Pareto-optimal. With merely nonnegative coefficients, a maximizer is guaranteed only to be weakly Pareto-optimal unless ties are refined. Because the attainable set may be nonconvex, some Pareto-optimal vectors may fail to maximize any positive weighted sum; lexicographic or constraint-based scalarizations can recover nonsupported frontier points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive weighted sums return Pareto optima, but discrete nonconvex fronts may contain Pareto points no weighted sum can recover.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal{X}\) is finite and nonempty.
All components of \(f\) are maximized.
For the strong guarantee, \(\lambda_j>0\) for every \(j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^*\in\operatorname{Argmax}F_\lambda\) and \(\lambda>0\Rightarrow x^*\) is Pareto-optimal.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The positive-weight guarantee and unsupported-frontier limitation are standard, but the claim about merely nonnegative coefficients needs the additional condition that at least one coefficient is positive; if all coefficients are zero, an arbitrarily dominated point is a maximizer and need not even be weakly Pareto-optimal. A source is also required before choosing a complete corrected formulation.

The assignment, the set \(V(x)\), one falsified member clause for every \(g\in V(x)\), and verification that every clause in each \(G_g\) with \(g\notin V(x)\) is satisfied certify the exact cost \(\sum_{g\in V(x)}w_g\).

assumptions_latex: x\models H

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Introduce \(z_g\in\{0,1\}\) for every group and, for every membership \(C\in G_g\), include \((C\lor z_g)\). Retain all hard clauses and minimize \(\sum_g w_gz_g\). A clause belonging to several groups contributes one relaxed membership clause for each group. For every hard-feasible assignment \(x\), the minimum extension has objective \(\sum_gw_g\mathbf1[\exists C\in G_g:x\not\models C]\). For \(w_g>0\), every minimum extension sets \(z_g\) to the corresponding indicator; for \(w_g=0\), a minimum extension with that canonical value exists.

Group MaxSAT
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clauses incur cost collectively through designated soft groups.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be hard clauses and let \(G_1,\ldots,G_q\) be finite groups of soft clauses, with group weights \(w_g\ge0\). A group \(G_g\) is violated by assignment \(x\) when at least one clause in it is falsified. Group MaxSAT minimizes
\[\sum_{g=1}^{q}w_g\mathbf{1}[\exists C\in G_g:\ x\not\models C]\]
subject to \(x\models H\). Thus all violations inside one group incur its cost only once. In unweighted Group MaxSAT, \(w_g=1\) for every group.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Group MaxSAT minimizes the weight of soft clause groups containing at least one falsified clause while satisfying every hard clause.
assumptions_latex: The variables, hard clauses, and soft groups are finite.
Every group weight satisfies \(w_g\ge0\).
Feasible assignments satisfy all clauses in \(H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{x\models H}\sum_gw_g\mathbf{1}[\exists C\in G_g:x\not\models C]\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed once-per-violated-group objective is coherent, but Group MaxSAT conventions can differ regarding overlaps, hard clauses, and whether the formulation is stated through violated groups or removable groups. An authoritative source with a precise locator is required.

children.title: Labelled MaxSAT
children.top_down_role: MaxSAT regimes organized through labels attached across clauses.

assumptions_latex: The label set is finite.
Every hitting-set subproblem is solved exactly.
Every failed residual SAT check returns an unsatisfiable subformula of that residual formula.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F_D\text{ satisfiable at an iteration}\Rightarrow D\in\operatorname*{argmin}\{w(D'):F_{D'}\text{ satisfiable}\},
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact implicit hitting-set algorithm specialized to label cores.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain discovered label cores \(\mathcal U\). Repeatedly compute a minimum-weight set \(D\) hitting every member of \(\mathcal U\) and test \(F_D\). If it is satisfiable, return \(D\). Otherwise extract an unsatisfiable subformula \(Q\subseteq F_D\), add \(U(Q)\) to \(\mathcal U\), and continue. The new core is disjoint from \(D\), so it was not previously hit; finiteness of \(L\) gives finite termination whenever a feasible deletion exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternate exact minimum-weight hitting sets with residual SAT checks; each failure adds a new unhit label core, and the first feasible candidate is optimal.
knowledge_statements.title: Core-Guided Label Hitting-Set Search

assumptions_latex: Weights and \(K\) are nonnegative integers encoded in binary.
The formula and label annotations are explicitly represented.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \textsc{Labelled-MaxSAT-Decision}\text{ is NP-complete}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical complexity of bounded-cost label deletion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Deciding whether some \(D\subseteq L\) satisfies \(F_D\) and \(\sum_{\ell\in D}w(\ell)\le K\) is in NP and is NP-complete. Hardness already holds when every labelled soft clause has its own singleton label, since weighted partial MaxSAT is then a special case.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded-cost Labelled MaxSAT is NP-complete, already for singleton, clause-specific labels.
knowledge_statements.title: Labelled MaxSAT Decision Complexity

assumptions_latex: \(F\) and \(L\) are finite.
The unlabelled clauses are satisfiable; otherwise the empty label core makes every deletion infeasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F_D\text{ is satisfiable}\iff \forall U\in\mathcal U_{\min},\ D\cap U\ne\varnothing.

notation.meaning: inclusion-minimal label unions of unsatisfiable clause subformulas

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact hitting-set characterization using label unions of unsatisfiable subformulas.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every unsatisfiable clause subformula \(Q\subseteq F\), form its label union \(U(Q)=\bigcup_{C\in Q}\lambda(C)\), and let \(\mathcal U_{\min}\) contain the inclusion-minimal such unions. A deletion \(D\) makes \(F_D\) satisfiable exactly when it intersects every member of \(\mathcal U_{\min}\). Hence minimum-cost label deletion is the minimum-weight hitting-set problem over these minimal label cores.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasible label deletions are exactly the hitting sets of the minimal label unions arising from unsatisfiable clause subformulas.
knowledge_statements.title: Label-Core Hitting-Set Characterization

assumptions_latex: \(D\subseteq D'\subseteq L\).
The inclusion-minimality conclusion assumes \(w(\ell)>0\) for every label.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F_D\text{ satisfiable}\Rightarrow F_{D'}\text{ satisfiable};\qquad w>0\Rightarrow D^*\text{ is inclusion-minimal among feasible deletions}.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(D\subseteq D'\), then \(F_{D'}\subseteq F_D\), so feasibility is upward closed. If all label weights are strictly positive, every minimum-cost feasible deletion is inclusion-minimal. With zero-weight labels, an optimal deletion can contain a redundant label and have a proper feasible subset of equal cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasible deletions are upward closed; positive weights force optimal deletions to be inclusion-minimal, while zero weights permit redundant optima.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual Monotonicity and Minimality

assumptions_latex: \(F\) and \(L\) are finite.
Each label uses one shared Boolean selector.
Selector costs are the declared nonnegative label weights.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact shared-selector representation of label deletion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Introduce one Boolean selector \(s_\ell\) for each label \(\ell\). Replace every clause \(C\) by \(C\lor\bigvee_{\ell\in\lambda(C)}s_\ell\) and minimize \(\sum_\ell w(\ell)s_\ell\). For \(D=\{\ell:s_\ell=1\}\), the augmented clauses admit an assignment to the original variables exactly when \(F_D\) is satisfiable, and their selector cost is \(w(D)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One shared selector per label yields an exact optimization formulation: selecting a label disables every clause carrying it.
knowledge_statements.title: Shared Label-Selector Encoding
Labelled MaxSAT
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum-cost label deletion semantics for labelled CNF formulas.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A labelled MaxSAT instance is a triple \((F,L,w)\), where \(F\) is a finite CNF formula, \(L\) is a finite label set, each clause \(C\in F\) has an annotation \(\lambda(C)\subseteq L\), and \(w:L\to\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}\). For \(D\subseteq L\), deleting \(D\) disables every clause whose annotation intersects \(D\); the residual formula is \(F_D=\{C\in F:\lambda(C)\cap D=\varnothing\}\). The optimization problem is \[\min\left\{\sum_{\ell\in D}w(\ell):D\subseteq L,\ F_D\text{ is satisfiable}\right\}.\] Clauses with \(\lambda(C)=\varnothing\) are hard and cannot be disabled by deleting labels. If at least one feasible deletion exists, an optimal deletion exists because \(L\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Delete a minimum-cost set of labels so that removing every clause carrying a deleted label leaves a satisfiable CNF formula; unlabelled clauses remain hard. An optimum exists whenever some deletion is feasible.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) and \(L\) are finite.
\(w(\ell)\geq 0\) for every \(\ell\in L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\{D\subseteq L:F_D\text{ is satisfiable}\}\neq\varnothing\), then \(D^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}\{\sum_{\ell\in D}w(\ell):D\subseteq L,\ F_D\text{ is satisfiable}\}\) exists.

Group–Label Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact correspondence under group-deletion and label-deletion semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a finite CNF formula with hard clauses \(H\subseteq F\), a finite index set \(J\), soft groups \(G_j\subseteq F\setminus H\) for \(j\in J\), and group costs \(w_j\geq 0\); a nonhard clause may belong to several groups. Introduce one distinct label \(\ell_j\) per group, set \(w(\ell_j)=w_j\), annotate each clause \(C\in F\setminus H\) by \(\lambda(C)=\{\ell_j:C\in G_j\}\), and set \(\lambda(C)=\varnothing\) for \(C\in H\). For every \(S\subseteq J\), let \(D_S=\{\ell_j:j\in S\}\). Then \[F_{D_S}=H\cup\{C\in F\setminus H:C\notin G_j\text{ for every }j\in S\},\qquad \sum_{\ell\in D_S}w(\ell)=\sum_{j\in S}w_j.\] Thus \(S\mapsto D_S\) is a bijection that preserves residual formulas, satisfiability, and deletion costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Give each soft group a distinct label and attach every applicable label to each nonhard clause. Deleting groups then exactly matches deleting their labels, including for overlapping groups, while hard clauses remain unlabelled.

\(G_j\subseteq F\setminus H\) for every \(j\in J\).

Therefore this shared-clause behavior requires overlapping groups or an auxiliary construction that preserves the same deletion semantics.

Linear Pseudo-Boolean Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimization with a linear objective and linear inequalities over binary variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A linear pseudo-Boolean optimization instance consists of rational data \(c\in\mathbb{Q}^n\), \(A\in\mathbb{Q}^{m\times n}\), and \(b\in\mathbb{Q}^m\). In minimization form it is \[\min\{c^\top x:Ax\leq b,\ x\in\{0,1\}^n\}.\] If the feasible set is nonempty, an optimizer is a feasible vector \(x^*\) satisfying \(c^\top x^*\leq c^\top x\) for every feasible \(x\), and such an optimizer exists because the binary domain is finite. Maximization is obtained by replacing \(c\) with \(-c\), and linear equalities may be expressed by two opposite inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimize a linear rational objective subject to linear rational constraints and binary decision variables; an optimizer exists whenever the feasible set is nonempty.
assumptions_latex: \(m,n\in\mathbb{N}\).
All numerical input data are rational.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:Ax\leq b\}\neq\varnothing\), then \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\{0,1\}^n,\ Ax\leq b}c^\top x\neq\varnothing\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact minimization by monotone threshold queries.

Binary search therefore finds \(\min_{x\in X}\sum_{i\in S}x_i\) using at most \(\lceil\log_2(|S|+1)\rceil\) exact threshold queries once feasibility is known.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Because cardinality-bound feasibility is monotone, binary search finds the exact minimum with logarithmically many threshold queries.
assumptions_latex: \(X\neq\varnothing\).

Hardness already holds for \(S=\varnothing\) and \(k=0\), when the question is whether \(X\) is nonempty.

For every hard-feasible assignment, the number of falsified soft clauses equals \(\sum_{i\in S}x_i\). Thus the cardinality problem and the resulting Partial MaxSAT instance have identical optimal assignments.

assumptions_latex: The Boolean feasible set \(X\) is represented by hard clauses \(H\).
The cardinality objective is minimized.

Boolean Cardinality Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimization of the number of true variables under Boolean constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) be the set of assignments satisfying a specified Boolean constraint system, and let \(S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\). Boolean cardinality minimization is \[\min_{x\in X}\sum_{i\in S}x_i.\] Its objective counts the variables indexed by \(S\) that are true. Cardinality maximization replaces the minimum by a maximum. The unweighted cardinality objective is the special case of a linear pseudo-Boolean objective in which every selected variable has coefficient one and every unselected variable has coefficient zero. If \(X\neq\varnothing\), an optimum exists because \(X\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Among assignments satisfying Boolean constraints, minimize or maximize how many variables in a specified index set are true. This is a unit-coefficient special case of linear pseudo-Boolean optimization.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\).
\(S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\).

children.title: Degree-Reduction Bridges
children.top_down_role: Structural transformations from higher-degree objectives to lower-degree representations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formulation-size bound for quadratizing one positive binary monomial by product substitution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x_1\cdots x_d\) with \(d\ge3\), set \(y_2=x_1x_2\), then \(y_t=y_{t-1}x_t\) for \(3\le t\le d-1\), and replace the original monomial by \(y_{d-1}x_d\). Exact pair-product linking reduces the term to degree two using \(d-2\) auxiliary binaries and \(3(d-2)\) linking inequalities, hence size \(O(d)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A degree-d positive binary monomial can be reduced to quadratic form with d−2 auxiliary binaries and 3(d−2) product-linking inequalities.
assumptions_latex: Each chain variable is constrained as the product introduced at that step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d-2\text{ auxiliaries and }3(d-2)\text{ linking inequalities suffice for }d\ge3.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Size Chain Quadratization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp binary counterexamples obtained by omitting a product-linking inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For binary \(x_i,x_j,y\), each inequality in \(y\le x_i\), \(y\le x_j\), and \(y\ge x_i+x_j-1\) is necessary to enforce \(y=x_ix_j\). Omitting them respectively admits the incorrect product assignments \((x_i,x_j,y)=(0,1,1)\), \((1,0,1)\), and \((1,1,0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Omitting any one of the three product-linking inequalities admits an explicit binary point with an incorrect auxiliary product.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{y\le x_i,\ y\le x_j,\ y\ge x_i+x_j-1\}\text{ is irredundant over binary points}.
knowledge_statements.title: Omission Failures for Product Linking
Degree-Reduction Bridges
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact quadratization of products using auxiliary binary variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For binary variables \(x_i,x_j\), introduce \(y\in\{0,1\}\) and impose \[y\leq x_i,\qquad y\leq x_j,\qquad y\geq x_i+x_j-1.\] These inequalities hold exactly when \(y=x_ix_j\). Therefore any multilinear monomial of degree greater than two can be reduced recursively: replace a selected factor pair by \(y\), impose the three linking inequalities, and repeat until every objective term has degree at most two. For every original assignment there is a unique consistent auxiliary assignment, so the extended quadratic formulation preserves all original objective values and the optimum after projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace binary products by auxiliary variables constrained with three linear inequalities; recursive replacement converts higher-degree objectives into an exact quadratic extended formulation.
assumptions_latex: Each introduced auxiliary variable is constrained by its defining product inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y=x_ix_j\), and recursive substitutions preserve the projected feasible objective values.

notation.meaning: auxiliary variable representing a binary product

assumptions_latex: \(X\subsetneq\{0,1\}^n\) may impose identities among variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Full-cube multilinear degree need not equal the minimum degree modulo identities valid on \(X\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Uniqueness of multilinear representation requires agreement on all of \(\{0,1\}^n\). On \(X=\{x\in\{0,1\}^2:x_1=x_2\}\), the degree-two polynomial \(x_1x_2\) and the degree-one polynomial \(x_1\) agree at every feasible point. Thus the minimum degree modulo identities valid on \(X\) can be smaller than the full-cube degree.

knowledge_statements.title: Loss of Degree Uniqueness on a Restricted Feasible Set
Nonlinear Representation Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict degree boundary without auxiliary variables or domain extension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every function \(f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) has a unique multilinear polynomial representation. For \(1\leq d\leq n\), the function \(m_d(x)=\prod_{i=1}^d x_i\) has multilinear degree exactly \(d\). Consequently, no polynomial of degree less than \(d\) agrees with \(m_d\) at every point of \(\{0,1\}^n\). Thus the pseudo-Boolean degree hierarchy is strict when representations use only the original variables; lowering degree requires auxiliary variables, additional constraints, or failure to preserve the function on the entire Boolean cube.

A valued language \(\Delta\) consists of cost functions \(\phi:\{0,1\}^r\to\mathbb Q\cup\{+\infty\}\), and a valued instance minimizes a sum of such local costs. Replacing each cost function by the relation of tuples having finite cost preserves feasibility but can discard all comparisons among feasible assignments.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boolean optimization restricted to relations from a fixed constraint language.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A Boolean constraint language is a set \(\Gamma\) of finitary relations over \(\{0,1\}\). A \(\Gamma\)-constraint has the form \(R(x_{i_1},\ldots,x_{i_r})\) with \(R\in\Gamma\) of arity \(r\). A \(\Gamma\)-instance is a finite conjunction of such constraints, and its feasible set is \[X_\Gamma=\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:(x_{i_1},\ldots,x_{i_r})\in R\text{ for every stated constraint}\}.\] Constraint-language-restricted Boolean optimization minimizes or maximizes a specified objective over \(X_\Gamma\), permitting only relations belonging to \(\Gamma\).

Under normalization as a set of distinct literals, this padding is unavailable, and adding complementary literals makes a clause tautological. Therefore exact-\(k\) and at-most-\(k\) syntax are not interchangeable without an explicit convention.

Clause-Arity Restrictions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Syntactic restriction on the number of literals per CNF clause.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\bigwedge_{t=1}^m C_t\) be a finite CNF formula, where \(m\in\mathbb{N}_0\) and each \(C_t\) is a disjunction of literals. For an integer \(k\geq 1\), \(F\) satisfies the at-most-\(k\) clause-arity restriction precisely when \[|C_t|\leq k\qquad\text{for every }t\in\{1,\ldots,m\},\] where \(|C_t|\) counts literal occurrences under the stated clause normalization. It satisfies the exact-\(k\) restriction when \(|C_t|=k\) for every clause. These universal conditions hold vacuously when \(m=0\). The arity bound restricts individual clauses, not the total number of variables or clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite CNF formula has at-most-k clause arity when every clause contains at most k literals, and exact-k arity when every clause contains exactly k literals. The condition is vacuous for a formula with no clauses.

Conversely, for each fixed \(k\), the set of all relations on \(D\) having arity at most \(k\) is finite. knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes language-level arity from the maximum scope length realized by an instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I=(V,C)\) be a finite Boolean constraint instance over \(\Gamma\), where every \(c\in C\) has a relation \(R_c\in\Gamma\) and an ordered scope \(S_c\in V^{\operatorname{ar}(R_c)}\). Define \[\operatorname{ar}(I):=\begin{cases}\max_{c\in C}|S_c|,&C\neq\varnothing,\\0,&C=\varnothing.\end{cases}\] Then \[\operatorname{ar}(I)\leq \operatorname{ar}(\Gamma):=\sup_{R\in\Gamma}\operatorname{ar}(R).\] A bound on \(\operatorname{ar}(\Gamma)\) therefore bounds every instance over \(\Gamma\). Conversely, \(\operatorname{ar}(I)\leq k\) only asserts that this instance uses relations of arity at most \(k\); it does not exclude higher-arity relations from \(\Gamma\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Language arity bounds every instance over the language. An instance with low arity may nevertheless be over a language that also contains higher-arity relations; an instance with no constraints is assigned arity zero.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a reformulation replacing each constraint of \(I\) by a gadget in \(I'\). Bounded arity transfers only if every gadget constraint has uniformly bounded scope. Bounded variable occurrence transfers only if each occurrence of an original variable creates uniformly many gadget occurrences and every auxiliary variable has uniformly bounded occurrence. Without these conditions, transfer can fail: a family of Boolean relations of unbounded arity can be represented, after existentially introducing auxiliary variables, by bounded-arity constraints, while duplicating a variable and enforcing equality can exchange one high-occurrence variable for many bounded-occurrence copies. Thus semantic equivalence under projection alone preserves neither restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equivalent gadget formulations need not preserve arity or occurrence bounds; preservation requires uniform bounds on gadget scopes, replication, and auxiliary-variable use.
knowledge_statements.title: Restriction Transfer Boundaries

assumptions_latex: Incidence graphs are constructed from the displayed constraint list, including logically redundant constraints.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary separating representation structure from feasible-set semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The unconstrained feasible set \(\{0,1\}^n\) has an edgeless incidence graph when represented by no constraints. A logically equivalent representation can adjoin, for every pair \(i<j\), a tautological constraint whose declared scope is \(\{x_i,x_j\}\). Its incidence graph is the subdivision of the complete graph on the variables and contains cycles for \(n\geq3\). Thus acyclicity, width, degree, and related incidence predicates are properties of the chosen representation unless the allowed transformations are fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding redundant tautological constraints can change incidence structure without changing any feasible assignment, so incidence restrictions are representation-sensitive.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Convert the supplied decomposition to a nice decomposition and process it bottom-up. A bag state records truth values for variable vertices in the bag and, for each clause vertex in the bag, whether a processed incident literal has satisfied that clause. Introduce, forget, and join transitions retain the least accumulated soft-clause penalty and reject a forgotten unsatisfied hard clause. There are \(2^{O(t)}\) states per bag, yielding exact optimization and solution reconstruction in \(2^{O(t)}\operatorname{poly}(|I|)\) time. Arithmetic is polynomial in the encoded weight lengths.

children.title: Acyclicity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Instance classes governed by acyclic hypergraph or incidence structure.

assumptions_latex: \(B_I\) is the finite simple incidence graph of a Boolean constraint instance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_I\) is a forest if and only if repeated deletion of a vertex of current degree at most one deletes every vertex.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recognition and certification of graph-theoretic incidence acyclicity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a queue with all vertices of \(B_I\) having degree at most one and repeatedly delete a queued vertex, updating its neighbor's degree. The graph is incidence-acyclic exactly when every vertex is deleted. A complete deletion order is a certificate in which every vertex has at most one later neighbor. If vertices remain, the residual graph has minimum degree at least two; following predecessor-free edges until a vertex repeats extracts a cycle. With adjacency lists, recognition and certificate extraction use \(O(|V(B_I)|+|E(B_I)|)\) time and space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly deleting vertices of degree at most one recognizes incidence forests in linear time. A complete deletion order certifies acyclicity, while a cycle extracted from a nonempty residual 2-core certifies failure.
knowledge_statements.title: Leaf-Stripping Recognition and Certificates

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relates primal and incidence treewidth when constraint rank is bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r=\max_{c\in C}|S_c|\), counting distinct variables. Then \[\operatorname{tw}(B_I)\leq \operatorname{tw}(P_I)+1\] and \[\operatorname{tw}(P_I)\leq r\bigl(\operatorname{tw}(B_I)+1\bigr)-1.\] Consequently, bounded primal treewidth implies bounded incidence treewidth without an arity assumption, whereas bounded incidence treewidth implies bounded primal treewidth only together with bounded \(r\). In particular, a single constraint incident with arbitrarily many variables has an incidence graph that is a star of treewidth one, while its primal graph is a clique of unbounded treewidth.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Replace every soft clause \(c\) by \(w_c\) identical unit-weight copies. An assignment violating \(c\) violates exactly \(w_c\) copies, so its total unweighted violation count equals its original weighted cost. The expansion contains \(\sum_c w_c\) copies. It is polynomial-size when weights are unary encoded or polynomially bounded in the input length, but can be exponential in their binary encoding length; therefore cost equivalence does not imply a polynomial-size binary reduction by duplication.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose a positive common multiple \(D\) of the denominators of all \(w_c\). Then \(W_c=Dw_c\in\mathbb Z\) and \[DF(x)=\sum_{c\in C}W_c\phi_c(x).\] Since \(D>0\), the rational- and integer-weight instances have identical minimizers and maximizers, and their optimum values differ by the factor \(D\). Taking the product of the input denominators gives a valid \(D\) whose binary length, and the binary lengths of the resulting \(W_c\), are polynomially bounded by the total input bit length.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Query feasibility of the hard constraints together with \(f(x)=r_i\) in increasing order. The first feasible query returns a globally minimizing assignment; if all \(K\) queries are infeasible, the original instance is infeasible. A promise only that \(|f(X)|\leq K\), without an explicitly enumerable superset of candidate values, does not itself provide this enumeration algorithm.

assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\), \(f:X\to\mathbb Z\), and \(g(x)=af(x)+b\).
\(a,b\in\mathbb Z\) and \(a\neq0\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Behavior of prescribed and cardinality objective ranges under affine recoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(g(x)=af(x)+b\) with \(a\neq0\), \[g(X)=\{ar+b:r\in f(X)\},\] and the map \(r\mapsto ar+b\) is injective, so \(|g(X)|=|f(X)|\). Thus range cardinality is invariant under every nonzero affine recoding, while a prescribed set \(R\) transforms to \(aR+b\). If \(a=0\), the range collapses to \(\{b\}\) whenever \(X\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero affine recoding maps the attainable range bijectively and preserves its cardinality; zero scaling collapses every nonempty range to one value.

A cardinality restriction instead requires \(|f(X)|\leq K\) for a specified integer \(K\geq 0\). An interval restriction is the prescribed-value case \(R=\{L,L+1,\ldots,U\}\), where \(L,U\in\mathbb Z\) and \(L\leq U\). These restrictions concern attainable objective values rather than coefficient magnitudes in a representation of \(f\).

children.title: Numeric-Restriction Interaction
children.top_down_role: Combined effects of coefficient, weight, and objective-range limitations.

assumptions_latex: \(f(x)=\sum_{S\in\mathcal S}a_S\prod_{i\in S}x_i\) has integer coefficients.
\(|\mathcal S|\leq s\) and \(|a_S|\leq B\) for every represented term.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f(\{0,1\}^n)\subseteq[-sB,sB]\cap\mathbb Z\quad\text{and}\quad |f(\{0,1\}^n)|\leq 2sB+1.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative interaction of support size, coefficient or weight magnitude, and attainable objective range.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every Boolean monomial is zero or one, so every assignment satisfies \[|f(x)|\leq\sum_{S\in\mathcal S}|a_S|\leq sB.\] Hence \(f(\{0,1\}^n)\subseteq[-sB,sB]\cap\mathbb Z\) and \(|f(\{0,1\}^n)|\leq2sB+1\). Likewise, if \(F(x)=\sum_{c=1}^m w_cz_c(x)\), where \(z_c(x)\in\{0,1\}\) and integral \(0\leq w_c\leq B\), then \(F(x)\in\{0,\ldots,mB\}\) and \(|F(X)|\leq mB+1\) for every feasible set \(X\). Thus a magnitude bound gives a uniform range bound only when represented support size is also controlled.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With at most s integer terms of magnitude B, a Boolean objective lies in [-sB,sB]; nonnegative weighted penalties with m weights at most B lie in [0,mB].
knowledge_statements.title: Magnitude-to-Range Bounds Under Bounded Support
Numeric-Restriction Interaction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical independence of coefficient-magnitude and attainable-range bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The two restrictions do not imply one another uniformly. For \(X_n=\{0,1\}^n\), the objective \(f_n(x)=\sum_{j=1}^n x_j\) has coefficients bounded by \(1\), while \(|f_n(X_n)|=n+1\). Conversely, for \(Y=\{0\}\subseteq\{0,1\}\) and any \(M>0\), the representation \(g_M(x)=Mx\) has coefficient magnitude \(M\), while \(g_M(Y)=\{0\}\). Thus bounded coefficients need not give a uniform objective-range bound, and bounded feasible range need not bound coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Small coefficients can produce arbitrarily many attainable values, while an arbitrarily large coefficient can be invisible on a restricted feasible set.
assumptions_latex: \(n\geq1\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Neither a uniform coefficient bound nor a uniform bound on \(|f(X)|\) implies the other without additional assumptions.

knowledge_statements.title: Hard Feasibility Layer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible assignments induced by mandatory clauses in partial MaxSAT.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\) be Boolean variables and let \(H\) be a finite family of hard clauses over \(V\). The hard feasibility layer is the set \(F_H=\{x\in\{0,1\}^{V}:x\models C\text{ for every }C\in H\}\). A hard–soft instance is feasible exactly when \(F_H\neq\varnothing\). Optimization over soft clauses is restricted to \(F_H\); no finite improvement in the soft objective permits violation of a clause in \(H\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hard clauses define the mandatory feasible set. Soft preferences are optimized only among assignments satisfying every hard clause.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary indicators and aggregate cost for violated soft clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=\{C_1,\ldots,C_m\}\) be soft clauses and let \(x\) satisfy all hard clauses. Define \(v_i(x)=1\) when \(x\not\models C_i\) and \(v_i(x)=0\) otherwise. Given weights \(w_i\geq0\), the soft-clause violation cost is \(L(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m w_i v_i(x)\). In unweighted partial MaxSAT, \(w_i=1\) for every \(i\), so \(L(x)\) equals the number of violated soft clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each soft clause contributes its weight exactly when violated; the total violation cost is minimized over hard-feasible assignments.

\(w_i\geq0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\)

knowledge_statements.title: Preference Semantics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between maximizing satisfied preference weight and minimizing violation penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=\{C_1,\ldots,C_m\}\) be soft clauses with weights \(w_i\geq0\). For each hard-feasible assignment \(x\in F_H\), define \(s_i(x)=\mathbf 1\{x\models C_i\}\), \(v_i(x)=1-s_i(x)\), and \(W=\sum_{i=1}^m w_i\). Then \(\sum_{i=1}^m w_i s_i(x)=W-\sum_{i=1}^m w_i v_i(x)\). Consequently, maximizing satisfied preference weight over \(F_H\) and minimizing violated preference weight over \(F_H\) have exactly the same optimal assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite weighted family of soft clauses, satisfied weight plus violated weight is constant. Therefore maximizing satisfied weight and minimizing violated weight select the same hard-feasible assignments.
assumptions_latex: \(S=\{C_1,\ldots,C_m\}\) is a finite family of soft clauses
\(x\in F_H\)
\(w_i\geq0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\)

knowledge_statements.title: Preference-Conflict Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact boundary between simultaneous preference satisfaction and unavoidable violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) and \(S=\{C_1,ldots,C_m\}\) be finite families of hard and soft clauses, respectively, and assume the hard-feasible set \(F_H\) is nonempty. The soft preferences are jointly compatible with hard feasibility precisely when \(\bigwedge_{C\in H\cup S}C\) is satisfiable. If every soft weight satisfies \(w_i>0\), this is equivalent to \(\min_{x\in F_H}\sum_{i=1}^m w_i v_i(x)=0\). If the conjunction is unsatisfiable, every hard-feasible assignment violates at least one soft clause.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Assuming the hard clauses are feasible, preferences are conflict-free exactly when one assignment satisfies every hard and soft clause. With strictly positive weights, this is also exactly when the minimum violation cost is zero.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) and \(S=\{C_1,\ldots,C_m\}\) are finite clause families
\(F_H\neq\varnothing\)
\(w_i>0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\)

Pseudo-Boolean-to-Weighted-MaxSAT Reductions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact, cost-preserving reduction; polynomial size requires polynomial-size encodings of the pseudo-Boolean constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) be defined by integer-coefficient pseudo-Boolean constraints, and let \(f:F\to\mathbb Z\). An exact reduction to weighted partial MaxSAT consists of hard clauses \(H\), weighted soft clauses \(S\), auxiliary variables \(y\), and \(K\in\mathbb Z\) such that \(x\in F\) exactly when some \(y\) satisfies \(H\), and
\[f(x)=K+\min_{y:(x,y)\models H}\sum_{(C,w)\in S}w\,\mathbf 1[(x,y)\not\models C].\]
Consequently, projecting any optimal MaxSAT assignment onto \(x\) yields an optimizer of \(f\) over \(F\). The reduction is polynomial only when the selected constraint and monomial encodings have polynomial size.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact encoding preserves feasibility and objective value up to a constant; optimal MaxSAT assignments then project to optimal pseudo-Boolean assignments.

All hard-constraint and auxiliary-variable encodings are satisfiability preserving.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an attained integer-valued minimization problem, \(t\in\mathbb Z\) is the optimum if and only if \(D(t)\) is feasible and \(D(t-1)\) is infeasible. Thus a witness for \(D(t)\) and a valid certificate of infeasibility for \(D(t-1)\) certify optimality. Without a known positive spacing between attainable values, the predecessor test is invalid; for example, optimum \(1/2\) makes \(D(1)\) feasible and \(D(0)\) infeasible although \(1\) is not optimal.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sublevel feasibility representation and bounded-integer value recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonempty \(F\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\), an attained objective \(f:F\to\mathbb R\), and threshold \(\tau\), define \(D(\tau)\) to ask whether some \(x\in F\) satisfies \(f(x)\le\tau\). If \(v^*=\min_{x\in F}f(x)\), then \(D(\tau)\) is feasible exactly when \(v^*\le\tau\), and feasibility is monotone in \(\tau\). If \(f(F)\subseteq\mathbb Z\) and \(L\le v^*\le U\) are known integers, binary search recovers \(v^*\) in at most \(\lceil\log_2(U-L+1)\rceil\) threshold queries.

Objective-Threshold Decision Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decision formulation of a finite Boolean minimization problem at a prescribed threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a nonempty set \(F\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\), objective \(f:F\to\mathbb R\), and threshold \(\tau\in\mathbb R\), define
\[D(\tau):\quad \text{find }x\in F\text{ such that }f(x)\le \tau.\]
Writing \(v^*=\min_{x\in F}f(x)\), the decision instance \(D(\tau)\) is feasible if and only if \(v^*\le\tau\). If \(f(F)\subseteq\mathbb Z\) and known bounds \(L\le v^*\le U\) are available, repeated threshold queries recover \(v^*\) by integer binary search using at most \(\lceil\log_2(U-L+1)\rceil\) queries.

The minimum of \(f\) over \(F\) exists.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extended binary-linear representation of multilinear pseudo-Boolean expressions by monomial variables.

Let \(p(x)=c_0+\sum_{S\in\mathcal S}c_S\prod_{i\in S}x_i\) on \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\). Introduce \(y_S\in[0,1]\) for every \(S\in\mathcal S\) and impose

\[y\le x_i\ (i=1,\ldots,k),\qquad y\ge\sum_{i=1}^k x_i-k+1.\]
The disjunction \(y=\bigvee_{i=1}^k x_i\) is represented exactly by
\[y\ge x_i\ (i=1,\ldots,k),\qquad y\le\sum_{i=1}^k x_i.\]
Thus the binary solutions of each linear system are precisely the truth-table assignments of the corresponding logical connective.

knowledge_statements.title: Indicator Linearizations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Big-M linearization of a one-sided linear indicator implication.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \(z\in\{0,1\}\), and consider \(z=1\Rightarrow a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\). If
\[M\ge\sup_{x\in X}(a^{\mathsf T}x-b)<+\infty,\]
then, for \(x\in X\), the indicator implication is represented exactly at binary points by
\[a^{\mathsf T}x\le b+M(1-z).\]
When \(z=1\), the indicated inequality is enforced; when \(z=0\), the bound defining \(M\) makes it redundant. The smallest valid nonnegative \(M\) gives the strongest relaxation within this single-inequality big-M family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite valid big-M converts a linear indicator implication into one inequality, with the smallest valid value giving the strongest such relaxation.

\(\sup_{x\in X}(a^{\mathsf T}x-b)\) is finite.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q_1\) and \(Q_2\) be continuous extended relaxations associated with the same binary feasible set \(F\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\), and let \(P_i=\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_i)\). Formulation \(Q_1\) is at least as strong as \(Q_2\) in the projected sense when \(P_1\subseteq P_2\). Then, for every \(c\in\mathbb R^n\),
\[\inf_{x\in P_1}c^{\mathsf T}x\ge\inf_{x\in P_2}c^{\mathsf T}x.\]
A projected formulation is ideal when
\[P_i=\operatorname{conv}(F).\]
Thus an ideal projected relaxation is strongest under this inclusion ordering, although formulations with equal projections may differ in size or numerical behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smaller projected continuous relaxation is stronger and gives no weaker linear minimization bounds; an ideal projected formulation equals the convex hull of the binary feasible set.
knowledge_statements.title: Linearization Strength Regimes

\(P_1\nsubseteq P_2\) and \(P_2\nsubseteq P_1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists c,d\in\mathbb R^n\) witnessing strict minimization-bound superiority in opposite directions.

notation.meaning: Projected continuous relaxations in a common original-variable space.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-objective consequence of noncontainment between compact convex projected relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_1,P_2\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty compact convex relaxations. If neither contains the other, then there exist vectors \(c,d\in\mathbb R^n\) such that \[\min_{x\in P_1}c^{\mathsf T}x>\min_{x\in P_2}c^{\mathsf T}x,\qquad \min_{x\in P_2}d^{\mathsf T}x>\min_{x\in P_1}d^{\mathsf T}x.\] Hence neither relaxation gives uniformly no-weaker bounds for all linear minimization objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If two compact convex relaxations are incomparable by inclusion, each gives a strictly stronger bound for some linear objective.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective Witnesses for Incomparable Relaxations

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\in X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and \(z\in\{0,1\}\), consider the implication \(z=1\Rightarrow a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\). A nonnegative finite constant \(M\) makes
\[a^{\mathsf T}x\le b+M(1-z)\]
an exact representation on \(X\times\{0,1\}\) if and only if
\[M\ge\sup_{x\in X}(a^{\mathsf T}x-b).\]
If the supremum is infinite, no finite nonnegative \(M\) gives an exact formulation of this form. If \(M\) is valid but exceeds the smallest valid nonnegative value, binary feasibility is preserved, while the continuous relaxation with \(0\le z\le1\) is weakly enlarged and may be strictly weaker.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A single big-M indicator formulation requires a finite bound on the inactive-domain violation; an oversized valid bound preserves binary feasibility but may weaken the continuous relaxation.
knowledge_statements.title: Indicator Applicability Boundaries

children.title: Objective Reformulations

knowledge_statements.title: Objective Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Epigraph reformulation of a Boolean objective as a linear objective plus constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) be nonempty and \(f:F\to\mathbb R\). Introducing an epigraph variable \(t\in\mathbb R\) gives the exact reformulation
\[\min_{x\in F}f(x)=\min\{t:x\in F,\ f(x)\le t\}.\]
Whenever the original minimum is attained, the projected optimal solutions of the epigraph problem are exactly \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}f(x)\), and every optimal extended solution satisfies \(t=f(x)\). Further linearization is possible when the epigraph inequality has an exact linear or mixed-integer extended representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Epigraph reformulation moves a nonlinear objective into a constraint while minimizing a new scalar variable, preserving optimal values and optimizers.
assumptions_latex: \(\varnothing\ne F\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\).
The minimum of \(f\) over \(F\) is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}f(x)=\operatorname{proj}_x\operatorname*{argmin}\{t:x\in F,\ f(x)\le t\}\).

Constraint Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact slack-variable reformulation of scalar inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) and \(g:F\to\mathbb R\). The inequality \(g(x)\le0\) has the exact extended reformulation
\[g(x)+s=0,\qquad s\ge0.\]
Indeed, an assignment \(x\in F\) satisfies the inequality exactly when it admits the unique slack \(s=-g(x)\). Thus replacing each inequality \(g_j(x)\le0\) by an equality with its own nonnegative slack preserves the projection of the feasible set onto \(x\). If \(g_j\) is pseudo-Boolean, its monomials may subsequently be represented by binary-linear auxiliary variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative slack converts each inequality into an equality without changing the feasible assignments in the original variables.

\(g(x)\) is finite for every \(x\in F\).

\(C\subsetneq F\) is nonempty.
\(f:F\to\mathbb R\).

\(\delta:=\min_{x\in F\setminus C}v(x)>0\).

notation.meaning: Smallest positive violation on the finite domain

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint-to-objective transfer by a sufficiently large finite penalty on a finite Boolean domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be the assignments satisfying a hard constraint and let \(v(x)\ge0\) vanish exactly on \(C\). Put \(R=\max_{x\in F}f(x)-\min_{x\in F}f(x)\) and \(\delta=\min_{x\in F\setminus C}v(x)>0\). Every \(M>R/\delta\) makes \[\min_{x\in F}\bigl(f(x)+Mv(x)\bigr)\] exact: all minimizers lie in \(C\) and coincide with the minimizers of \(f\) over \(C\). If \(M\delta\le R\), exactness is not guaranteed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a finite Boolean domain, a hard constraint can be moved into the objective using a violation penalty larger than the objective range divided by the smallest positive violation.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Domain Exact Penalty Transfer

assumptions_latex: \(\varnothing\ne F\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\).
The minimum of \(f\) over \(F\) is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v^*=\min_{x\in F}f(x)=\min\{\tau\in\mathbb R:F_\tau\ne\varnothing\}\) and \(F_{v^*}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}f(x)\).
