knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sublevel-set representation connecting objective minimization and threshold constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a nonempty set \(F\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) and a function \(f:F\to\mathbb R\), define \(F_\tau=\{x\in F:f(x)\le\tau\}\). Then
\[\min_{x\in F}f(x)=\inf\{\tau\in\mathbb R:F_\tau\ne\varnothing\}.\]
If the minimum is attained with value \(v^*\), then \(F_\tau=\varnothing\) for \(\tau<v^*\), and
\[F_{v^*}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}f(x).\]
Thus objective minimization has an equivalent parameterized threshold representation, with the optimum equal to the least feasible threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The minimum objective value is the least threshold whose sublevel constraint is feasible, and the feasible points at that threshold are exactly the optimizers.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective–Constraint Transfer

children.title: Reformulation Equivalence Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits on preserving feasible outcomes or optimization meaning across reformulations.

assumptions_latex: \(F\ne\varnothing\).
For every \(x\in F\), the auxiliary fiber \(\{y:(x,y)\in Q\}\) is nonempty and its objective infimum is well-defined in the extended real sense.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two displayed conditions are necessary and sufficient for feasibility projection and pointwise objective-value preservation up to the constant \(K\); failure of either condition prevents that full cost-preserving equivalence.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundaries between full cost-preserving reformulations, relaxations, and threshold decision surrogates.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\min\{f(x):x\in F\}\) and an extended problem \(\min\{\widehat f(x,y):(x,y)\in Q\}\). The extended problem preserves feasibility under projection and preserves every pointwise objective value up to a constant \(K\) independent of \(x\) if and only if
\[\operatorname{proj}_x Q=F\]
and
\[\inf_{y:(x,y)\in Q}\widehat f(x,y)=f(x)+K\qquad(x\in F).\]
These conditions imply equality of optimal values up to \(K\) and preservation of projected optimizers. If the projection strictly contains \(F\), the construction is a relaxation rather than a feasibility-equivalent reformulation. If the pointwise auxiliary value differs from \(f(x)\) by a nonconstant amount, feasibility may be preserved while objective values, and potentially optimizers, change. A fixed constraint \(f(x)\le\tau\) is only a threshold decision formulation unless \(\tau\) is optimized or searched.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full cost-preserving equivalence requires exact feasibility projection and preservation of each original objective value up to one constant; weaker conditions may preserve only feasibility, one decision threshold, or the particular optimizer set.
knowledge_statements.title: Reformulation Equivalence Boundaries

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Attainment boundary for passing from fiber-infimum value equivalence to optimizer preservation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{a\}\), \(Q=\{(a,y):y>0\}\), \(f(a)=0\), and \(\widehat f(a,y)=y\). Then \(\operatorname{proj}_xQ=F\) and \[\inf_{y:(a,y)\in Q}\widehat f(a,y)=0=f(a),\] yet the extended infimum is not attained and the extended problem has no optimizer. Therefore exact projection and pointwise equality of fiber infima preserve optimal values, but projected-optimizer preservation additionally requires suitable attainment of the relevant fiber minima and of the extended optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact projection and matching fiber infima do not by themselves preserve optimizers when the extended infimum is unattained.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{a,b,c\}\), with \((f(a),f(b),f(c))=(0,1,2)\) and \((g(a),g(b),g(c))=(0,1,3)\). Both minimization problems have optimal value \(0\) and unique optimizer \(a\), but \(g-f\) takes values \(0,0,1\). Thus equality of optimal values and optimizer sets does not imply pointwise cost preservation up to an assignment-independent constant.

children.title: Formulation Strength
children.top_down_role: Relaxation quality of Boolean and integer-programming formulations.

knowledge_statements.title: Formulation Strength
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected-relaxation ordering for formulations of one discrete feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a discrete feasible set, and let \(Q_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+p_i}\) be continuous relaxations of two valid extended formulations satisfying \(F\subseteq P_i:=\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_i)\). Formulation \(1\) is stronger than formulation \(2\) in the projected sense when
\[P_1\subseteq P_2,\]
and strictly stronger when the inclusion is strict. For minimization of any linear objective \(c^{\mathsf T}x\), this ordering implies that the relaxation bound from formulation \(1\) is at least the bound from formulation \(2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One formulation is stronger when its projected continuous relaxation is contained in the other's, yielding no weaker linear minimization bounds.
assumptions_latex: Both formulations represent the same discrete set \(F\).
Strength is compared after continuous relaxation and projection onto the same original variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_1\subseteq P_2\Rightarrow\inf_{x\in P_1}c^{\mathsf T}x\ge\inf_{x\in P_2}c^{\mathsf T}x\) for every \(c\in\mathbb R^n\).

source_refs.locator: 5.1 Comparing the Strength of Different Formulations p. 70

source_witnesses.locator: 5.1 Comparing the Strength of Different Formulations p. 70

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent support-function characterization of projected-relaxation containment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonempty closed convex sets \(P_1,P_2\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \[P_1\subseteq P_2\iff \inf_{x\in P_1}c^{\mathsf T}x\ge\inf_{x\in P_2}c^{\mathsf T}x\quad\text{for every }c\in\mathbb R^n.\] Consequently, projected strength is equivalent to uniform dominance of all linear minimization bounds. If containment fails, a separating linear objective witnesses failure of dominance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projected containment is equivalent to obtaining a no-weaker bound for every linear minimization objective.
assumptions_latex: \(P_1\) and \(P_2\) are nonempty closed convex sets.
Both sets occupy the same original-variable space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P_1\subseteq P_2\iff \inf_{x\in P_1}c^{\mathsf T}x\ge\inf_{x\in P_2}c^{\mathsf T}x\quad\forall c\in\mathbb R^n.
knowledge_statements.title: All-Objectives Characterization of Strength

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strongest valid projected relaxation and the absence of a ranking for incomparable relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonempty finite discrete set \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), a valid projected relaxation \(P\supseteq F\) is ideal when \(P=\operatorname{conv}(F)\). Equivalently, it has the exact discrete optimum for every linear objective. This does not require every LP optimizer to be integral, because a fractional point may lie in an optimal face. If two valid projected relaxations are incomparable by inclusion, each has an objective direction in which the other gives a strictly stronger bound, so neither has objective-independent dominance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An ideal relaxation equals the integer hull; incomparable relaxations can exchange which gives the stronger bound as the objective changes.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is nonempty and finite.
\(P\) is a closed convex relaxation containing \(F\).
Incomparability compares projections in the same original-variable space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P=\operatorname{conv}(F)\iff \min_{x\in P}c^{\mathsf T}x=\min_{x\in F}c^{\mathsf T}x\quad\forall c\in\mathbb R^n.
knowledge_statements.title: Ideality and Incomparability

children.title: Formulation Size
children.top_down_role: Constraint, variable, and representation growth across formulations.

assumptions_latex: The formulation is encoded over rational data in binary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Formulation size is measured by \((V,I,L)\), permitting separate comparison of structural counts and encoding length.

notation.meaning: number of variables, including auxiliary variables
total binary encoding length of coefficients, bounds, and variable declarations

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses an explicit three-coordinate size convention for rational mixed-integer formulations; this should not be mistaken for a uniquely standardized scalar definition.

source_refs.locator: Section 1.3.1, Problems, Instances, Encoding Size, p. 17

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a rational mixed-integer formulation \(Ax+By\le b\), with \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(y\in\mathbb{R}^q\times\mathbb{Z}^r\), define its size coordinates to be \((V,I,L)\). Here \(V=n+q+r\) is the number of original and auxiliary variables, \(I\) is the number of listed inequalities, and \(L\) is the total binary encoding length of the rational coefficients, right-hand sides, bounds, and variable-domain declarations. Relative to this convention, a family has polynomial-size formulations when \(V\), \(I\), and \(L\) are bounded by polynomials in the binary encoding length of the represented instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated convention, formulation size records the variable count, constraint count, and total binary encoding length; polynomial size requires all three coordinates to be polynomially bounded in the instance encoding length.
knowledge_statements.title: Formulation Size

source_witnesses.locator: Section 1.3.1, Problems, Instances, Encoding Size, p. 17

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum inequality count over linear extensions, distinguished from complete encoded formulation size.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a polytope \(P\), its linear extension complexity \(\operatorname{xc}(P)\) is the minimum number of inequalities in a polyhedron \(Q\) admitting a linear projection \(\pi(Q)=P\), under a stated convention for equations. It measures minimum row count over extensions, not the binary length of a particular formulation; by itself it does not bound coefficient length, auxiliary-variable count, or constructive complexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extension complexity is the least inequality count of a linear extension and is not a complete bit-size measure.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a nonempty polytope.
Extensions are polyhedra with linear projections onto \(P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{xc}(P)=\min\{m:\exists Q=\{z:Az\le b\}\text{ with }m\text{ inequalities and }\pi(Q)=P\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear Extension Complexity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonnegative-rank characterization of minimum linear-extension size.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be a positive-dimensional polytope and let \(S\) be a facet-versus-vertex slack matrix, \(S_{ij}=b_i-a_i^{\mathsf T}v_j\). Under the convention that extension size counts inequalities, the Yannakakis factorization theorem gives \[\operatorname{xc}(P)=\operatorname{rank}_+(S),\] where \(\operatorname{rank}_+(S)\) is the least \(r\) for which \(S=TU\) with \(T\in\mathbb R_+^{m\times r}\) and \(U\in\mathbb R_+^{r\times N}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polytope's minimum extension inequality count equals the nonnegative rank of its slack matrix.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a positive-dimensional polytope.
\(S\) uses a facet description and all vertices.
Extension size counts inequalities under the same convention as \(\operatorname{xc}(P)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{xc}(P)=\operatorname{rank}_+(S).
knowledge_statements.title: Slack-Matrix Characterization of Extension Complexity

children.title: Projection Behavior
children.top_down_role: Relationships between extended formulations and their original-variable spaces.

assumptions_latex: \(x_1,x_2,z\in\{0,1\}\) in the integer formulation.
The continuous relaxation replaces these domains by \([0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_I)=\{(0,0),(1,1)\}\) but \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_L)=[0,1]^2\).

notation.meaning: Integer-feasible extended set defined by the displayed equality.
Continuous relaxation of the same extended equality.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit separation between exact integer projection and ideal projected relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[Q_I=\{(x_1,x_2,z)\in\{0,1\}^3:x_1+x_2=2z\}.\] Then \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_I)=\{(0,0),(1,1)\}\). After replacing all binary domains by \([0,1]\), the relaxation \(Q_L\) projects to the full square \([0,1]^2\), because \(z=(x_1+x_2)/2\) is feasible for every point of that square. Hence exact integer projection does not imply that the projected continuous relaxation equals the convex hull of the target set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A parity equality can project exactly to two diagonal binary points while its continuous relaxation projects to the whole unit square.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Integer-Exact Projection Need Not Be Ideal
knowledge_statements.title: Integer-Exact Projection Need Not Be Ideal

assumptions_latex: \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+d}\).
\(\pi_x\) is a linear coordinate projection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi_x(\operatorname{conv}S)=\operatorname{conv}(\pi_x(S))\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convexification identity for coordinate projections of extended feasible sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any set \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+d}\) and linear coordinate projection \(\pi_x\), \[\pi_x(\operatorname{conv}S)=\operatorname{conv}(\pi_x(S)).\] Consequently, if an integer-feasible extended set \(Q_I\) projects exactly to \(X\), then \(\pi_x(\operatorname{conv}Q_I)=\operatorname{conv}X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projecting after convexification gives the same set as convexifying after projection.
knowledge_statements.title: Projection Commutes with Convexification

assumptions_latex: The auxiliary-variable formulation has rational linear constraints.
The original variables are distinguished from the auxiliary variables.
The continuous relaxation contains every integer-feasible point of the formulation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The formulation is exact precisely when \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_I)=X\), and its projected continuous relaxation is \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_L)\).

notation.meaning: target feasible set in the original variables
mixed-integer feasible set of the extended formulation
continuous relaxation containing the mixed-integer feasible set

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exact extended formulations are characterized by projection onto the original variables
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes projection of the integer-feasible formulation from projection of a specified continuous relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) be the target set and let \(Q_I\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\times Y_I\) be the feasible set of a rational mixed-integer extended formulation. Let \(Q_L\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n+d}\) be a continuous relaxation satisfying \(Q_I\subseteq Q_L\), obtained by replacing the declared integrality domains with specified continuous supersets while retaining the linear constraints. The formulation represents \(X\) exactly when \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_I)=X\). Its projected continuous relaxation is \(P=\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_L)\), and exactness implies \(\operatorname{conv}(X)\subseteq P\). Exactness permits multiple feasible auxiliary lifts of the same \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An extended formulation is exact when its mixed-integer feasible set projects to the target set. Projecting a specified continuous relaxation determines the formulation's relaxation in the original variables.
knowledge_statements.title: Projection Behavior

children.title: Strength–Size Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Navigation across compactness and relaxation-quality regimes.

assumptions_latex: Formulation size counts an explicit rational system's variables and inequalities.
The extended formulation must project exactly to the even-parity polytope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_n^{\mathrm{even}}\) has exponentially many original-space facets and an exact extended formulation of size \(O(n)\).

notation.meaning: Convex hull of binary vectors having even Hamming weight.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boolean existence family showing exponential original-space size and linear exact extended-formulation size at equal projected strength.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[P_n^{\mathrm{even}}=\operatorname{conv}\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:\textstyle\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\equiv0\pmod 2\}.\] Its original-space facet description contains an odd-set inequality for every odd subset of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\), and therefore has exponentially many facets. A two-state layered parity automaton has \(O(n)\) arcs and nodes; its unit-flow polytope, linked to the chosen bit on each layer, is an exact extended formulation whose projection is \(P_n^{\mathrm{even}}\). Thus equal ideal projected strength can coexist with exponential original-space size and linear extended size.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The even-parity polytope has exponentially many original-space facets but a linear-size exact network extension, demonstrating a genuine Boolean strength-size separation.
knowledge_statements.title: Parity-Polytope Strength-Size Separation

assumptions_latex: Two formulations represent the same binary feasible set after projection.
Strength is compared through inclusion of projected continuous relaxations.
Size is evaluated using a fixed size measure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Size order alone does not generally determine projected-relaxation inclusion, so comparisons must report both coordinates.

notation.meaning: projection of the continuous relaxation of formulation F

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: formulation size and projected relaxation strength are separate comparison coordinates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States a comparison principle rather than a universal claim about every pair of formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For exact formulations \(F_1\) and \(F_2\) of the same set \(X\), write \(F_1\succeq F_2\) when \(P(F_1)\subseteq P(F_2)\); under this convention, the smaller projected relaxation is the stronger one. In general, the size inequality \(S(F_1)\le S(F_2)\) alone implies neither \(P(F_1)\subseteq P(F_2)\) nor \(P(F_2)\subseteq P(F_1)\). A strength-size comparison should therefore report the selected size measure and the inclusion relation, if any, between the projected relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Formulation size and projected relaxation strength are separate comparison coordinates: a smaller description is not, in general, enough to determine which relaxation is stronger.
knowledge_statements.title: Strength–Size Tradeoffs

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unit-propagation behavior on partial assignments to input variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the pairwise AMO CNF, assigning \(x_k=1\) derives \(x_j=0\) for every \(j\ne k\) by unit propagation. Any partial assignment containing two true inputs is therefore refuted by unit propagation, and every input literal forced by AMO under a consistent partial assignment is derived.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The pairwise encoding propagates every other variable false after one is true and immediately detects any two-true conflict.
assumptions_latex: The CNF contains every pairwise negative clause.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_k=1\vdash_{\mathrm{UP}}\bigwedge_{j\ne k}\neg x_j.
knowledge_statements.title: Propagation Completeness of Pairwise AMO

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactly-one augmentation of the pairwise AMO encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Conjoining the pairwise AMO clauses with \((x_1\lor\cdots\lor x_n)\) represents exactly \(\sum_i x_i=1\), uses no auxiliary variables, and has \(\binom n2+1\) clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One at-least-one clause added to pairwise AMO gives the auxiliary-free exactly-one encoding.
assumptions_latex: n\ge1
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \left(\bigvee_i x_i\right)\land\bigwedge_{i<j}(\neg x_i\lor\neg x_j)\iff\sum_i x_i=1.
knowledge_statements.title: Exactly-One Pairwise Variant

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp lower bound for exact CNFs over the original input variables only.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(n\ge2\), the nontrivial prime implicates of \(\sum_i x_i\le1\) are exactly \((\neg x_i\lor\neg x_j)\) for \(i<j\). Every exact CNF using only \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\) has at least \(\binom n2\) clauses, and the pairwise encoding attains this bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The binary pair exclusions are the prime implicates of AMO, and no auxiliary-free exact CNF uses fewer than one clause per forbidden pair.
assumptions_latex: n\ge2
The CNF uses no auxiliary variables and is exact on all Boolean input assignments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |F|\ge\binom n2,\qquad \left|\bigwedge_{i<j}(\neg x_i\lor\neg x_j)\right|=\binom n2.

notation.meaning: An auxiliary-free CNF representing AMO exactly.

knowledge_statements.title: Prime-Implicate and Auxiliary-Free Clause Minimality

assumptions_latex: The variables \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\) are Boolean.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The clauses are satisfied exactly by assignments with \(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\le 1\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the pairwise AMO encoding is the canonical auxiliary-free binary-clause representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical auxiliary-free CNF representation of an at-most-one constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For Boolean variables \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\), the pairwise encoding of \(\operatorname{AMO}(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\) is \[\bigwedge_{1\le i<j\le n}(\neg x_i\lor\neg x_j).\] Its satisfying assignments are exactly the vectors \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\) satisfying \(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\le 1\). The encoding uses no auxiliary variables and has \(\binom{n}{2}\) binary clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The pairwise encoding forbids every pair of Boolean variables from being simultaneously true. It uses one binary clause per pair, no auxiliary variables, and represents exactly the at-most-one relation.
knowledge_statements.title: Pairwise Encodings

children.title: Ladder Encodings
children.top_down_role: At-most-one or exactly-one encodings organized through ladder-like auxiliary structure.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unit-Propagation Strength of the Sequential Ladder
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Input-level propagation and conflict detection for the seed's one-way ladder clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the sequential ladder CNF, unit propagation from \(x_k=1\) derives \(x_j=0\) for every \(j\ne k\). Hence any partial assignment containing two true inputs is refuted by unit propagation. This does not imply that every auxiliary variable equals the exact prefix disjunction on every satisfying partial assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The ladder propagates all other inputs false after one becomes true and detects two-true conflicts, although its auxiliaries are not fully reified prefix states.
assumptions_latex: n\ge2
The ladder CNF is the one-way sequential encoding stated in the seed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_k=1\vdash_{\mathrm{UP}}\bigwedge_{j\ne k}\neg x_j.
knowledge_statements.title: Unit-Propagation Strength of the Sequential Ladder

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactly-one augmentation of the sequential ladder AMO encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Conjoining the sequential ladder AMO encoding with \((x_1\lor\cdots\lor x_n)\) yields an encoding whose projection is exactly \(\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:\sum_i x_i=1\}\). It uses \(n-1\) auxiliary variables and \(3n-3\) clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding one at-least-one clause to the ladder AMO encoding produces an exactly-one encoding.
assumptions_latex: n\ge2
The sequential ladder clauses are those stated in the seed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists s\;F_{\mathrm{ladder}}(x,s)\land\bigvee_i x_i\iff\sum_i x_i=1.
knowledge_statements.title: Exactly-One Ladder Variant

assumptions_latex: The variables \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\) are Boolean and \(n\ge 2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Existentially eliminating \(s_1,\ldots,s_{n-1}\) yields exactly \(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\le 1\).

notation.meaning: Boolean ladder variables that propagate whether a true input has occurred in a prefix

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the displayed clauses are a standard sequential AMO encoding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential ladder representation of at-most-one; the clauses do not force each auxiliary variable to equal the exact prefix disjunction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For Boolean inputs \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\) with \(n\ge 2\), introduce Boolean ladder variables \(s_1,\ldots,s_{n-1}\). The sequential ladder CNF contains \((
eg x_1\lor s_1)\), \((
eg x_n\lor
eg s_{n-1})\), and, for each \(2\le i\le n-1\), the clauses \((
eg x_i\lor s_i)\), \((
eg s_{i-1}\lor s_i)\), and \((
eg x_i\lor
eg s_{i-1})\). Its projection onto the input variables is \(\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\le 1\}\). It uses \(n-1\) auxiliary variables and \(3n-4\) clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The sequential ladder encoding uses Boolean prefix-propagation variables and local clauses. Projecting out those variables yields exactly the at-most-one relation, with n minus one auxiliaries and 3n minus 4 clauses.
knowledge_statements.title: Ladder Encodings

children.title: Regular Encodings
children.top_down_role: Constraint encodings based on regular state-transition structure.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear Size for a Fixed Counting Automaton
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic size under a fixed finite transition-to-CNF template.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If every automaton layer uses a fixed positive number of state indicators and each state and transition condition is compiled by a fixed finite CNF template, then the AMO or EO regular encoding has \(\Theta(n)\) auxiliary variables and \(\Theta(n)\) clauses. Constants depend on whether the rejecting state is represented explicitly and on the chosen template.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed finite-state regular encoding has linear size in the input length, with convention-dependent constants.
assumptions_latex: The automaton state set is fixed independently of n.
Each layer uses a fixed positive number of state indicators.
A fixed finite CNF template compiles every layer and transition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |\mathrm{vars}_{\mathrm{aux}}|=\Theta(n),\qquad |\mathrm{clauses}|=\Theta(n).
knowledge_statements.title: Linear Size for a Fixed Counting Automaton

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactly-one specialization of the prefix-counting regular encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the seed's counting automaton, replacing the accepting-state set \(\{0,1\}\) by \(\{1\}\), while retaining the initial state and transitions, yields an exact regular encoding whose input projection is \(\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:\sum_i x_i=1\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accepting only the state representing exactly one true input changes the regular encoding from at-most-one to exactly-one.
assumptions_latex: The state and transition compilation is exact.
The automaton and input order are those of the seed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: q_n=1\iff\sum_{i=1}^n x_i=1.

notation.meaning: Automaton state after the final input.

knowledge_statements.title: Exactly-One Accepting-State Variant

assumptions_latex: The variables \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\) are Boolean.
The deterministic automaton reads the variables in index order.
The chosen CNF compilation enforces exactly one state at each position and the stated transition relation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Accepting runs exist exactly for inputs satisfying \(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\le 1\).

notation.meaning: automaton state after reading the first i inputs
states denoting zero, one, or at least two true inputs

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-automaton representation of at-most-one; exact clause counts depend on the selected regular-constraint-to-CNF compilation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the deterministic automaton with state set \(\{0,1,\bot\}\), initial state \(0\), accepting states \(\{0,1\}\), and transitions \(\delta(0,0)=0\), \(\delta(0,1)=1\), \(\delta(1,0)=1\), and \(\delta(1,1)=\bot\), with \(\bot\) absorbing. A regular CNF encoding introduces indicators for the state \(q_i\) after each input position, enforces \(q_0=0\), enforces \(q_i=\delta(q_{i-1},x_i)\) for \(1\le i\le n\), and excludes \(q_n=\bot\). Under an exact CNF compilation of these state and transition conditions, projection onto \(x\) is precisely \(\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\le 1\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regular encoding compiles a deterministic three-state counting automaton. With exact state and transition clauses, its accepted input projections are exactly the Boolean sequences containing at most one true input.
knowledge_statements.title: Regular Encodings

children.title: Ladder–Regular Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural similarities and distinctions between ladder and regular representations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bijection for Fully Reified Prefix States
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Auxiliary-state correspondence under fully reified ladder and deterministic regular conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a ladder variant enforces \(s_i\leftrightarrow\bigvee_{j=1}^i x_j\) together with AMO, and a deterministic regular encoding has unique indicators \(u_{i,0},u_{i,1}\) for zero and exactly one true input after position \(i\). For every feasible input assignment, \(s_i=u_{i,1}=1-u_{i,0}\). This identification is a bijection between the auxiliary assignments of these fully reified encodings.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With fully reified ladder prefixes and unique regular states, each ladder bit is exactly the regular state indicating that one true input has appeared.
assumptions_latex: The input assignment satisfies at-most-one.
The ladder prefix variables are fully reified.
The regular encoding enforces one unique deterministic state at every position.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: s_i=u_{i,1}=1-u_{i,0}\qquad(1\le i<n).

notation.meaning: Regular indicators for zero or exactly one true prefix input.

knowledge_statements.title: Bijection for Fully Reified Prefix States

assumptions_latex: The ladder encoding is the one-way sequential encoding stated in the Ladder Encodings record.
The regular encoding exactly compiles the deterministic at-most-one automaton.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Both encodings project to the same at-most-one relation, but their auxiliary assignments need not correspond bijectively.

notation.meaning: ladder prefix-propagation variable after position i
regular-encoding indicator that exactly one true input has appeared by position i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The correspondence is projection-level for the displayed one-way ladder encoding; stronger clause-level equivalence requires a different, fully reified ladder convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(u_{i,1}\) denote the regular-encoding state indicator that exactly one true input has appeared among \(x_1,\ldots,x_i\). This indicator has the intended prefix meaning associated with a ladder variable. Both the exact regular encoding and the one-way sequential ladder encoding project onto \(\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\le 1\}\). However, identifying \(s_i\) with \(u_{i,1}\) does not in general give a bijection between auxiliary assignments, because the displayed ladder clauses may admit noncanonical values of \(s_i\). Clause-level coincidence requires a ladder variant that fully reifies the prefix state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The regular and sequential ladder encodings represent the same at-most-one relation after auxiliary variables are projected out. For the one-way ladder clauses stated here, their auxiliary assignments are not generally identical or uniquely corresponding.
knowledge_statements.title: Ladder–Regular Correspondence

children.title: Commander Encodings
children.top_down_role: Constraint encodings organized through commander variables and grouped literals.

assumptions_latex: The \(n\) inputs are partitioned into nonempty groups \(G_1,\ldots,G_m\).
Pairwise AMO clauses are used inside each group and over the \(m\) commanders.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{\mathrm{aux}}=m,\qquad N_{\mathrm{clause}}=n+\sum_{j=1}^m\binom{|G_j|}{2}+\binom m2\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct count of clauses in the one-level pairwise commander construction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact structural size of the one-level commander encoding with pairwise AMO subencodings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a one-level commander encoding with pairwise AMO clauses inside every group and over the commanders, there are \(m\) auxiliary variables. There are \(n\) input-to-commander implications, \(\sum_{j=1}^m\binom{|G_j|}{2}\) local exclusion clauses, and \(\binom m2\) commander exclusion clauses, for a total of \[n+\sum_{j=1}^m\binom{|G_j|}{2}+\binom m2.\] If the commander AMO is recursively commander-encoded, the final term is replaced by the size of that recursive encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A one-level pairwise commander encoding uses one auxiliary per group and has n implication clauses plus pairwise clauses within groups and among commanders.
knowledge_statements.title: One-Level Commander Size

assumptions_latex: Each local group AMO encoding is propagation complete on its input variables.
The AMO encoding over the commanders is propagation complete on the commander variables.
For every \(x\in G_j\), the clause \((\neg x\lor c_j)\) is present.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_i=1\Longrightarrow\operatorname{UP}(E\land x_i)\models\neg x_h\quad(h\ne i)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: compositional unit propagation through commander implications and propagation-complete AMO subencodings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Input-level propagation under propagation-complete commander components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(E\) be a commander encoding whose local group AMO encodings and commander AMO encoding are propagation complete. If \(x\in G_j\) is set true, \((
eg x\lor c_j)\) propagates \(c_j\). Local AMO propagation sets the other inputs of \(G_j\) false; commander AMO propagation sets every \(c_\ell\), \(\ell
e j\), false; and each clause \((
eg y\lor c_\ell)\) then sets every \(y\in G_\ell\) false. Hence one true input propagates all other inputs false. Exactness of the subencodings alone does not imply this propagation property.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When both local and top-level AMO components are propagation complete, one true input in a commander encoding unit-propagates every other input false.
knowledge_statements.title: Commander Input Propagation

assumptions_latex: The Boolean inputs are partitioned into nonempty groups \(G_1,\ldots,G_m\).
Each group has a Boolean commander \(c_j\).
Every invoked at-most-one subencoding is exact under projection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The resulting CNF projects exactly to \(\operatorname{AMO}(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: grouped AMO with one commander per group is the standard commander construction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-level commander representation; the at-most-one constraint on commanders may itself be encoded recursively.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition \(\{x_1,\ldots,x_n\}\) into nonempty groups \(G_1,\ldots,G_m\) and introduce Boolean commanders \(c_1,\ldots,c_m\). For every \(x\in G_j\), include \((\neg x\lor c_j)\). Include an exact at-most-one encoding over each group \(G_j\), and include an exact at-most-one encoding over \(c_1,ldots,c_m\). The projection of the resulting CNF onto \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\) is exactly \(\operatorname{AMO}(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Commander encoding partitions the inputs, enforces at most one input within each group, and uses group commander variables with an at-most-one constraint to prevent selections from different groups.
knowledge_statements.title: Commander Encodings

children.title: Product Encodings
children.top_down_role: Constraint encodings organized through multidimensional product structure.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Input Propagation of the Pairwise Product Encoding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Input-level unit propagation when both coordinate AMO constraints use pairwise clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the seed's product encoding with pairwise row and column AMO clauses, assigning \(x_k=1\) makes \(r_{\rho(k)}=c_{\kappa(k)}=1\) by unit propagation and then derives \(x_j=0\) for every \(j\ne k\). Any assignment setting two distinct inputs true is refuted by unit propagation because their injectively assigned cells differ in at least one coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With pairwise coordinate constraints, one true input propagates every other input false, and two true inputs cause a unit-propagation conflict.

Both coordinate AMO constraints contain all pairwise negative clauses.

children.title: Bimander Encodings

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Input-level propagation of the standard bimander AMO encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the standard bimander encoding \(E\), assigning an input \(x\in G_j\) true propagates every selector bit to \(\gamma(j)\). Local pairwise clauses propagate all other inputs in \(G_j\) false. For every other group \(G_\ell\), injectivity supplies a code bit differing from \(\gamma(j)\), and its selector clause propagates every input in \(G_\ell\) false. Thus one true input unit-propagates every other input false, and any two true inputs produce a unit-propagation conflict.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a standard bimander AMO encoding, setting one input true unit-propagates every other input false, and any two true inputs cause a propagated conflict.
knowledge_statements.title: Bimander Input Propagation

children.title: Grouping-Granularity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Encoding behavior across alternative group sizes and decomposition granularities.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp dependence of within-group pair counts on group balance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a_1,\ldots,a_m\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}\) and \(\sum_j a_j=n\). Writing \(n=mq+r\), \(0\le r<m\), the minimum of \(\sum_j\binom{a_j}{2}\) is \((m-r)\binom q2+r\binom{q+1}{2}\), attained exactly when all group sizes differ by at most one. Its maximum is \(\binom{n-m+1}{2}\), attained by \((n-m+1,1,\ldots,1)\) up to permutation. Thus the balanced \(\Theta(n^2/m)\) estimate need not hold for arbitrary partitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Balanced groups minimize within-group pairs, while a maximally unbalanced partition can retain quadratically many pairs.
assumptions_latex: m\ge1
n\ge m
a_j\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}
\sum_{j=1}^m a_j=n

knowledge_statements.title: Balanced and Unbalanced Group-Size Extremes

assumptions_latex: The \(n\) inputs are divided as evenly as possible among \(m\) nonempty groups.

The asymptotic estimate \(\Theta(n^2/m)\) is taken over \(1\le m\le n/2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(1\le m\le n/2\), its clause count is \(\Theta(n^2/m+n\log m)\).

notation.meaning: group size up to integer rounding

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the bound follows by counting within-group pairs and selector implications
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clause-count regimes for balanced bimander grouping; propagation behavior and literal counts are outside scope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(1\le m\le n/2\) and the balanced groups satisfy \(|G_j|\in\{\lfloor n/m\rfloor,\lceil n/m\rceil\}\). Then \[\sum_{j=1}^m\binom{|G_j|}{2}=\Theta(n^2/m).\] Binary group selection contributes exactly \(n\lceil\log_2 m\rceil\) implication clauses and \(\lceil\log_2 m\rceil\) auxiliary variables. Consequently, the total clause count is \(\Theta(n^2/m+n\log m)\). Constant \(m\) gives quadratic clause count, while \(m=\Theta(n/\log n)\), equivalently balanced group size \(g=\Theta(\log n)\), gives \(\Theta(n\log n)\) clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For balanced bimander groups with at most half as many groups as inputs, the clause count is of order n squared over m plus n log m. Constant group count is quadratic, while logarithmic group size yields order n log n clauses.
knowledge_statements.title: Grouping-Granularity Regimes

children.title: At-Most-One Constraint Semantics
children.top_down_role: Encoding requirements specific to at-most-one constraints.

assumptions_latex: The variables \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\) take values in \(\{0,1\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The at-most-one predicate holds if and only if \(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\le 1\).

notation.meaning: at-most-one relation on n Boolean variables

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: AMO is the elementary Boolean cardinality predicate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boolean cardinality semantics independent of any particular CNF or integer-programming encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For Boolean variables \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\), the predicate \(\operatorname{AMO}(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\) is true exactly when at most one coordinate equals \(1\). Equivalently, \[\operatorname{AMO}(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\iff\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\le 1.\] Its logical form is \(\bigwedge_{1\le i<j\le n}\neg(x_i\land x_j)\). The all-zero assignment is feasible. Adding the requirement \(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\ge 1\) instead yields the exactly-one condition \(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An at-most-one constraint permits either no true variable or exactly one true variable. Equivalently, the sum of its Boolean variables is at most one.
knowledge_statements.title: At-Most-One Constraint Semantics

children.title: Exactly-One Constraint Semantics
children.top_down_role: Encoding requirements specific to exactly-one constraints.

assumptions_latex: \(x_i\in\{0,1\}\) for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{ExactlyOne}(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\iff \sum_{i=1}^{n}x_i=1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boolean unit-cardinality semantics, independent of any particular CNF encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For Boolean variables \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\), the exactly-one constraint is satisfied precisely when one variable is true. Formally, \[\operatorname{ExactlyOne}(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\iff \sum_{i=1}^{n}x_i=1.\] Equivalently, it is the conjunction of the at-least-one clause \(x_1\lor\cdots\lor x_n\) and the at-most-one condition \(\sum_{i=1}^{n}x_i\le 1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exactly-one constraint holds precisely when one, and only one, of its Boolean variables is true.
knowledge_statements.title: Exactly-One Constraint Semantics

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete upper-bound convention for a sequential at-most-k encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For integer \(k\), an at-most-k constraint is unsatisfiable when \(k<0\), can be encoded by the sequential counter when \(0\le k<n\), and is tautological when \(k\ge n\). For \(k=0\), the direct clauses \(\bigwedge_{i=1}^n\neg x_i\) avoid introducing counter variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negative bounds are impossible, zero forces every input false, interior bounds use the counter, and bounds at least n are vacuous.
assumptions_latex: \(k\in\mathbb Z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: k<0\Rightarrow\bot,\quad k=0\Rightarrow\bigwedge_i\neg x_i,\quad k\ge n\Rightarrow\top.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Size and input-level propagation behavior of the standard forward at-most-k sequential counter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(1\le k<n\), the standard forward sequential counter with prefix-threshold variables \(s_{i,j}\) and its carry, monotonicity, and overflow-prevention clauses has \(O(nk)\) auxiliary variables and clauses and is constructible in \(O(nk)\) time. Unit propagation derives a conflict after any \(k+1\) inputs are set true and, after exactly \(k\) inputs are true, derives \(\neg x_h\) for every remaining unassigned input. These properties do not imply that a one-direction variant defines every \(s_{i,j}\) biconditionally as \([\sum_{h=1}^i x_h\ge j]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The standard at-most-k sequential counter has O(nk) size and is generalized-arc-consistent on input variables. One-direction counter clauses need not give every auxiliary bit its intended biconditional meaning.
assumptions_latex: The standard prefix-carry, monotonicity, and overflow clauses are all present.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |\operatorname{aux}(F_{\mathrm{seq}})|=O(nk),\quad |F_{\mathrm{seq}}|=O(nk).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Gate-Level Translation of a Fixed Parallel Counter
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic and size guarantee for translating a specified bounded-fanin population-count circuit to CNF.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a finite acyclic bounded-fanin counter circuit whose output predicate accepts exactly the required Hamming weights. Replacing every gate relation by a constant-size logically equivalent definitional CNF gives \[|F_C|=O(|C|),\qquad \exists z\,F_C(x,z)\iff C(x)\text{ accepts}.\] This projected equivalence does not by itself imply propagation completeness for the cardinality constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A specified bounded-fanin parallel counter has a linear-size gate-level CNF translation preserving accepted inputs under projection, but semantic correctness alone does not guarantee strong unit propagation.

The output and overflow convention of \(C\) is specified and accepts exactly the intended Hamming weights.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp output-width boundary for a nonmodular population count.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An unsigned binary output represents every population count in \(\{0,\ldots,n\}\) without overflow precisely when \(m\ge\lceil\log_2(n+1)\rceil\). With fewer bits, overflow must be separately excluded for a bound comparison to remain sound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact population count needs ceiling log2(n+1) bits; fewer bits cause wraparound or require a separate overflow constraint.
assumptions_latex: The population count is represented by an unsigned \(m\)-bit output.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary value-preserving component of binary population-count encodings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An exact full adder satisfies \(s=a\oplus b\oplus c_{\mathrm{in}}\), \(c_{\mathrm{out}}=(a\land b)\lor(a\land c_{\mathrm{in}})\lor(b\land c_{\mathrm{in}})\), and equivalently \(a+b+c_{\mathrm{in}}=s+2c_{\mathrm{out}}\).

assumptions_latex: \(a,b,c_{\mathrm{in}},s,c_{\mathrm{out}}\in\{0,1\}\).
The gate encoding is definitional and exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: a+b+c_{\mathrm{in}}=s+2c_{\mathrm{out}}

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists z,b\;F_{\mathrm{add}}(x,z,b;k)\iff \sum_{i=1}^{n}x_i\le k\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An adder encoding builds a Boolean arithmetic circuit whose binary output satisfies \[\sum_{r=0}^{\lceil\log_2(n+1)\rceil-1}2^r b_r=\sum_{i=1}^{n}x_i.\] Tseitin clauses represent its half-adders, full-adders, or equivalent gates, and a comparator enforces that the binary output is at most \(k\). Thus \[\exists z,b\;F_{\mathrm{add}}(x,z,b;k)\iff \sum_{i=1}^{n}x_i\le k.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An adder encoding computes the number of true inputs in binary and compares that binary count with the permitted bound.

children.title: Counter–Adder Hybrids
children.top_down_role: Encodings combining parallel counting components with arithmetic addition.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Interface Composition and Loss Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Architecture-independent correctness condition for composing local counters with an aggregate adder.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If each block formula \(C_t(X_t,y_t)\) represents \(\operatorname{val}(y_t)=\sum_{i\in X_t}x_i\) exactly and \(A(y_1,\ldots,y_m,z)\) represents \(\operatorname{val}(z)=\sum_{t=1}^m\operatorname{val}(y_t)\) exactly, then \[\exists y,z\;\bigwedge_{t=1}^m C_t(X_t,y_t)\land A(y_1,\ldots,y_m,z)\land[\operatorname{val}(z)\le k]\iff\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\le k.\] If two attainable local counts \(a<b\) share an interface word and an attainable remainder \(r\) satisfies \(a+r\le k<b+r\), no downstream formula observing only that word can encode the bound exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact counter interfaces and exact addition compose into an exact cardinality encoding. Collapsing locally distinguishable counts is unsound whenever a common remainder places them on opposite sides of the bound.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\) is partitioned into blocks \(X_1,\ldots,X_m\).
Every local counter and the aggregate adder is exact on its exposed interface.

If partial counts are combined by a balanced binary tree and each merge is treated as a constant-depth bounded-word counter component, the component depth is \(O(\log n)\). If merges are expanded into bit-level bounded-fanin adders, their internal depth must be added, so the resulting bound depends on the chosen adder architecture.

children.title: Totalizer Encodings
children.top_down_role: Cardinality encodings organized through tree-structured unary aggregation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static size of a balanced, untruncated totalizer using direct merge clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a balanced binary totalizer tree with all unary thresholds retained, the sum of internal output-sequence lengths is \(O(n\log n)\). Under the direct pairwise merge encoding, the total number of merge clauses is \(O(n^2)\), and the encoding is constructible within the same asymptotic bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A balanced full totalizer uses O(n log n) auxiliary threshold variables and O(n²) direct merge clauses.
assumptions_latex: The merge tree is balanced.
All thresholds are retained.
The standard direct pairwise bidirectional merge encoding is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |\operatorname{aux}(F_{\mathrm{tot}})|=O(n\log n),\qquad |F_{\mathrm{tot}}|=O(n^2).
knowledge_statements.title: Balanced Full-Totalizer Size

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unary Ordering and Input-Level Generalized Arc Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Threshold ordering and propagation of the standard bidirectional totalizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a standard bidirectional totalizer, each internal merge defines its parent unary thresholds from its two child sequences. Hence \[F_{\mathrm{tot}}\models u_{r,j+1}\rightarrow u_{r,j}\qquad(1\le j<n).\] With \(\neg u_{r,k+1}\), unit propagation conflicts whenever at least \(k+1\) inputs are true and forces every remaining unassigned input false after exactly \(k\) inputs are true. This input-level generalized arc consistency need not survive removal of the reverse merge clauses, even if the weakened formula remains an exact existential encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A standard bidirectional totalizer has an ordered unary root and is generalized-arc-consistent on inputs for an at-most-k bound. Weaker one-direction merges may preserve projection correctness without preserving that propagation strength.
assumptions_latex: Every merge contains the standard forward and reverse threshold clauses.
\(0\le k<n\) and \(\neg u_{r,k+1}\) is asserted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F_{\mathrm{tot}}\models u_{r,j+1}\rightarrow u_{r,j}\quad(1\le j<n).

notation.meaning: Root threshold indicating at least j true inputs
Bidirectional totalizer CNF with active root bound

knowledge_statements.title: Unary Ordering and Input-Level Generalized Arc Consistency

assumptions_latex: A rooted binary tree has the inputs as leaves.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists u\;F_{\mathrm{tot}}(x,u;k)\iff \sum_{i=1}^{n}x_i\le k\).

notation.meaning: Threshold output meaning that at least j leaves below node v are true
Totalizer CNF with root bound k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unary tree representation of an at-most-\(k\) cardinality constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At every tree node \(v\), unary outputs \(u_{v,j}\) represent the predicate that at least \(j\) leaves in the subtree of \(v\) are true. Merge clauses combine the two child sequences so that the root sequence represents all thresholds of \(\sum_i x_i\). Adding the root unit clause \(\neg u_{r,k+1}\) yields \[\exists u\;F_{\mathrm{tot}}(x,u;k)\iff \sum_{i=1}^{n}x_i\le k.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A totalizer merges unary subtree counts in a binary tree; forbidding the root's threshold k+1 enforces an at-most-k constraint.
knowledge_statements.title: Totalizer Encodings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the totalizer leaf, but the input list is malformed and \(k\) is not introduced or quantified. The root literal \(u_{r,k+1}\) normally requires \(0\le k<n\), unless an explicit overflow convention is supplied. A cited totalizer construction is needed to validate the merge semantics and projection equivalence.

children.title: Incremental Totalizer Encodings
children.top_down_role: Totalizer representations designed for changing cardinality bounds.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Persistent Reuse and Monotone Threshold Extension
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incremental use and conservative extension of a consistently truncated totalizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_K\) be a persistent totalizer containing all node thresholds and merge clauses required through root threshold \(K+1\). Already represented bounds are selected by root assumptions. To extend support to \(K'>K\), add the missing node thresholds and every newly enabled merge clause using the same tree and merge semantics: \[F_{K'}=F_K\land\Delta_{K,K'}.\] The extension preserves the projected meaning of every previously supported bound. This guarantee fails if old thresholds are redefined, old clauses are deleted, or a required merge clause for a new threshold is omitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An incremental totalizer reuses one persistent tree for bound assumptions and can be extended by adding missing thresholds and merge clauses. Conservative extension preserves all earlier bound queries.
assumptions_latex: \(F_K\) is a correct consistently truncated totalizer.
New variables and clauses use the same tree and do not redefine existing thresholds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F_{K'}=F_K\land\Delta_{K,K'}\quad\text{and every bound }k\le K\text{ retains its projected semantics}.

notation.meaning: Persistent totalizer supporting thresholds through K+1
New thresholds and merge clauses required for extension

knowledge_statements.title: Persistent Reuse and Monotone Threshold Extension

assumptions_latex: \(B\subseteq\{0,,n\}\) is the set of bounds queried during solving.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_{\mathrm{base}}(x,u)\land\neg u_{r,k+1}\iff F_{\le k}(x,u)\) for each \(k\in B\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Assumption-controlled reuse of a totalizer across changing upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Construct the totalizer clauses \(F_{\mathrm{base}}(x,u)\) once, retaining the root threshold variables. For a queried bound \(k<n\), enforce \(\sum_i x_i\le k\) by asserting \(\neg u_{r,k+1}\), optionally as a solver assumption. Consequently, for every \(k\in B\), \[F_{\mathrm{base}}(x,u)\land\neg u_{r,k+1}\iff F_{\le k}(x,u),\] and changing \(k\) does not require rebuilding the merge tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An incremental totalizer retains one counting structure and changes the active upper bound by asserting the corresponding root-threshold literal.
knowledge_statements.title: Incremental Totalizer Encodings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the incremental-totalizer leaf. Both variable and bound ranges contain malformed double commas, while \(B\subseteq\{0,,n\}\) is not a valid range and appears to admit \(k=n\), for which \(u_{r,k+1}\) may not exist. Moreover, \(F_{\le k}\) is not independently defined, making the displayed biconditional potentially tautological. A source must establish the intended incremental variant and bound domain.

children.title: Bound-Reuse Regimes
children.top_down_role: Reuse of totalizer structure across related bound queries.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Activation rules for a reusable base having exact retained root thresholds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(F_{\mathrm{base}}\) defines every retained root literal by \(u_{r,j}\leftrightarrow[\sum_i x_i\ge j]\). For integer \(k\), activation is unsatisfiable when \(k<0\), uses \(\neg u_{r,k+1}\) when \(0\le k<n\), and needs no bound literal when \(k\ge n\). Consequently, for \(0\le k<n\), \[\exists u\;F_{\mathrm{base}}(x,u)\land\neg u_{r,k+1}\iff\sum_i x_i\le k.\] Bound literals may be changed across solver calls when supplied as retractable assumptions; a permanently asserted tighter bound cannot be relaxed merely by adding another unit clause.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Interior bounds select one negated root threshold, negative bounds are impossible, and bounds at least n are vacuous. Retractable assumptions permit both tightening and relaxation; permanent units permit only further tightening.
assumptions_latex: Every root threshold used by a query is definitionally exact and retained in the permanent base.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists u\;F_{\mathrm{base}}(x,u)\land\neg u_{r,k+1}\iff\sum_i x_i\le k\quad(0\le k<n).

notation.meaning: Root threshold for at least j true inputs

knowledge_statements.title: Complete Bound-Reuse Regimes

assumptions_latex: \(F_{\mathrm{base}}(x,u)\) correctly represents all retained root thresholds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_i x_i\le k\iff \neg u_{r,k+1}\) under \(F_{\mathrm{base}}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity condition for changing an upper bound without reconstructing the totalizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A totalizer supports direct bound reuse over a set \(B\subseteq\{0,,n-1\}\) when its permanent clause set defines every root threshold \(u_{r,k+1}\) needed for \(k\in B\). Under that condition, activating bound \(k\) consists solely of asserting \(\neg u_{r,k+1}\), and \[F_{\mathrm{base}}\models\left(\neg u_{r,k+1}\iff \sum_{i=1}^{n}x_i\le k\right).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bound is reusable when the permanent totalizer contains its required root threshold; activating that bound then needs only one threshold literal.
knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Reuse Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind is suitable for a bound-reuse regime, but the set \(\{0,,n-1\}\) is malformed. More substantively, standard totalizer clause sets may guarantee only selected implication or propagation properties unless full threshold equivalence is encoded. The phrase 'correctly represents' is insufficient to validate the model-theoretic biconditional without a construction-specific source.

children.title: Incrementality Overhead
children.top_down_role: Representation costs associated with supporting incremental use.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural overhead for a balanced direct-merge totalizer retaining thresholds through a maximum reusable bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L=K+1\), and truncate every node sequence to \(\min\{L,|X_v|\}\) thresholds in a balanced totalizer tree. With the direct pairwise merge clauses, the retained auxiliary-variable count is \(O(n\log(L+1))\), and the clause count is \(O(nL)\). Thus the full case \(K=n-1\) has \(O(n\log n)\) auxiliary variables and \(O(n^2)\) clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A balanced totalizer truncated through threshold K+1 retains O(n log(K+2)) auxiliary thresholds and O(n(K+1)) direct merge clauses; the full encoding has O(n log n) variables and O(n²) clauses.
assumptions_latex: The totalizer tree is balanced.
Every node sequence is truncated consistently at \(L=K+1\).
The merge encoding materializes the standard direct threshold-pair clauses.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |\operatorname{aux}(F_K)|=O(n\log(K+2)),\qquad |F_K|=O(n(K+1)).
knowledge_statements.title: Balanced Truncated-Totalizer Storage Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Construction-and-activation accounting only; SAT solving time is excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(q\) bound queries over one input set and tree, let \(T(K)\) and \(S(K)\) be the construction time and retained size of a base supporting the maximum requested bound \(K\). Persistent reuse costs \[T(K)+O(q)\] for construction and assumption activation and retains \(S(K)\), whereas rebuilding costs \(\sum_{t=1}^qT(k_t)\). Reuse saves construction work only when avoided rebuilding exceeds the cost of materializing and retaining the shared base; one query or an unnecessarily large \(K\) may therefore incur strictly greater overhead.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reusable base is built once and changes represented bounds with one assumption per query. It amortizes repeated construction but may waste memory and work for one query or an overlarge supported maximum.
assumptions_latex: All queries use the same inputs and totalizer tree.
The accounting excludes SAT-search time and measures only encoding construction, retention, and activation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{incremental work}=T(K)+O(q),\qquad\text{retained size}=S(K).

notation.meaning: Construction time through maximum bound K

knowledge_statements.title: Amortized Reuse and Overprovisioning Boundary

assumptions_latex: \(n\) Boolean inputs are arranged in a balanced totalizer tree.
Only thresholds through \(K+1\), where \(0\le K<n\), are materialized at every merge.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The truncated construction uses \(O(nK)\) auxiliary variables and \(O(nK^2)\) merge clauses in the direct pairwise-merge formulation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Storage overhead for a directly merged totalizer truncated at a maximum reusable bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When every node sequence is truncated to length at most \(K+1\), the total number of retained unary threshold variables is \(O(nK)\). In the direct merge formulation, clauses are generated for relevant pairs of child thresholds, giving the conservative bound \(O(nK^2)\) clauses over the tree. Once this base is stored, switching among supported upper bounds adds only one active root literal per solver call.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A totalizer truncated at maximum bound K stores O(nK) thresholds and, with direct pairwise merges, O(nK²) clauses; each bound change activates one literal.
knowledge_statements.title: Incrementality Overhead

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity_bound kind fits the incrementality-overhead leaf, and the stated bounds are plausible conservative bounds for a direct pairwise merge construction. Their validity depends on exactly which threshold pairs and clauses are materialized at each node, so an authoritative source with a specific complexity analysis is required.

children.title: Sorting Networks
children.top_down_role: Cardinality encodings derived from comparator networks that fully order Boolean inputs.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constructive bounds for classical bitonic and odd-even merge sorting networks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Classical Batcher bitonic and odd-even merge constructions have \(O(n\log^2 n)\) comparators and \(O(\log^2 n)\) synchronous comparator depth, with padding when required by the recursive construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Batcher's classical sorting networks use order n log-squared n comparators and log-squared n layers.
assumptions_latex: Comparator count and synchronous layer depth are measured.
Unsupported input sizes are padded in the usual correctness-preserving way.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S(n)=O(n\log^2 n),\qquad D(n)=O(\log^2 n)
knowledge_statements.title: Batcher Sorting-Network Bounds

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical correctness criterion for oblivious comparator networks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A comparator network sorts every length-\(n\) sequence over a totally ordered domain if and only if it sorts every input in \(\{0,1\}^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A comparator network sorts arbitrary ordered values exactly when it sorts every zero-one input.
assumptions_latex: \(N\) is a fixed oblivious comparator network on \(n\) wires.
Each comparator outputs its inputs in a consistent sorted orientation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N\text{ sorts all ordered inputs}\iff N\text{ sorts all Boolean inputs}
knowledge_statements.title: Zero-One Principle

assumptions_latex: The comparator network sorts Boolean inputs in nonincreasing order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y_j=1\iff \sum_{i=1}^{n}x_i\ge j\) for every \(j\in\{1,,n\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boolean sorting-network representation of all cardinality thresholds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Replace every comparator by the Boolean mapping \((a,b)\mapsto(a\lor b,a\land b)\) and encode its gates by CNF. If the network sorts in nonincreasing order, its outputs satisfy \[y_j=1\iff \sum_{i=1}^{n}x_i\ge j\qquad(1\le j\le n).\] Hence an at-most-\(k\) constraint is represented by the output clause \(\neg y_{k+1}\), while an at-least-\(k\) constraint is represented by \(y_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Boolean sorting network produces unary threshold outputs: output j is true exactly when at least j inputs are true.
knowledge_statements.title: Sorting Networks

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the sorting-network leaf, and the threshold-output identity is standard. However, several lists and index ranges contain malformed double commas, and the final at-most/at-least claims introduce \(k\) without a domain; \(y_{k+1}\) and \(y_k\) also require separate boundary handling. No inspectable citation is supplied.

children.title: Cardinality Networks
children.top_down_role: Comparator-based encodings specialized to cardinality-relevant output information.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint-level propagation guarantee for standard cardinality-network CNF encodings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a propagation-complete definitional cardinality-network encoding of \(\sum_i x_i\le k\), unit propagation derives conflict after any \(k+1\) inputs are set true and forces every remaining input false after any \(k\) inputs are set true.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A propagation-complete cardinality network detects k+1 true inputs and forces all remaining inputs false once k inputs are true.
assumptions_latex: The cardinality network uses a comparator CNF known to preserve generalized arc consistency for the asserted at-most bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_{i\in T}x_i=k+1\implies\operatorname{UP}(F)=\bot
knowledge_statements.title: Propagation Completeness for At-Most Bounds

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recursive unary-count invariant underlying cardinality-network construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An exact cardinality merger of sorted Boolean sequences \(a_1\ge\cdots\ge a_p\) and \(b_1\ge\cdots\ge b_q\) produces \(c_1\ge\cdots\ge c_{p+q}\) satisfying \(c_j=1\iff\sum_{r=1}^{p}a_r+\sum_{s=1}^{q}b_s\ge j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cardinality merger combines two sorted unary counts into the sorted unary count of their union.
assumptions_latex: \(a_1\ge\cdots\ge a_p\) and \(b_1\ge\cdots\ge b_q\) are Boolean unary sequences.
The merger is exact and count-preserving.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: c_j=1\iff\sum_{r=1}^{p}a_r+\sum_{s=1}^{q}b_s\ge j
knowledge_statements.title: Cardinality-Merger Invariant

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists z,y\;F_{\mathrm{card}}(x,z,y;k)\iff \sum_{i=1}^{n}x_i\le k\).

notation.meaning: CNF encoding of the cardinality network

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparator network specialized to the output prefix needed by an at-most-\(k\) constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A cardinality network is a comparator network constructed so that the relevant outputs form a unary threshold prefix, with \(y_j=1\) exactly when at least \(j\) inputs are true. Outputs beyond the range required for the bound may be omitted. After encoding its comparators and asserting \(\neg y_{k+1}\), correctness is \[\exists z,y\;F_{\mathrm{card}}(x,z,y;k)\iff \sum_{i=1}^{n}x_i\le k.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cardinality network computes only the sorted threshold outputs needed for a cardinality bound; forbidding output k+1 enforces at most k true inputs.
knowledge_statements.title: Cardinality Networks

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the cardinality-network leaf, but the input and output lists are malformed and the specialized comparator-network construction is not identified. Padding, truncation, and omitted-output conventions can affect the exact correctness statement, so the existential equivalence requires a construction-specific authoritative source and locator.

children.title: Network Truncation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Network structures retaining only outputs relevant to a target bound.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient semantic condition for retaining a selected output rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A truncated formula \(G(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{z},y_r)\) is exact at rank \(r\) precisely when, for every \(a\in\{0,1\}^n\), \(\{y_r:\exists\mathbf{z}\,G(a,\mathbf{z},y_r)\}=\{\mathbf{1}[\sum_i a_i\ge r]\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Truncation is exact exactly when every retained output remains uniquely fixed to its original threshold value for every input.
assumptions_latex: Auxiliary variables of \(G\) are interpreted existentially.
\(y_r\) is intended to retain rank \(r\) of an exact comparator network.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall a:\ \{y_r:\exists\mathbf{z}\,G(a,\mathbf{z},y_r)\}=\left\{\mathbf{1}\!\left[\sum_i a_i\ge r\right]\right\}
knowledge_statements.title: Safe-Truncation Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-sided truncation retaining the ranks required for a cardinality interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If retained outputs satisfy \(y_j\leftrightarrow\sum_i x_i\ge j\), then for \(1\le L\le U<n\), \[L\le\sum_i x_i\le U\iff y_L\land\neg y_{U+1}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cardinality interval requires the lower threshold output and the first forbidden upper threshold output.
assumptions_latex: Ranks \(L\) and \(U+1\) are retained exactly.
\(1\le L\le U<n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L\le\sum_{i=1}^{n}x_i\le U\iff y_L\land\neg y_{U+1}
knowledge_statements.title: Interval-Rank Truncation

assumptions_latex: Inputs satisfy \(x_i\in\{0,1\}\) for \(i=1,\ldots,n\).
The retained comparator subnetwork correctly computes the first \(k+1\) outputs in nonincreasing order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\le k\iff y_{k+1}=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Truncation for an at-most-\(k\) constraint using only the output cone needed to determine rank \(k+1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\in\{0,1\}\), and let a comparator network order its relevant outputs nonincreasingly. To encode \(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\le k\), it suffices to retain a subnetwork that correctly computes the first \(k+1\) ranks, because its output \(y_{k+1}\) satisfies \(y_{k+1}=1\) exactly when at least \(k+1\) inputs are true. A definitional CNF encoding of the retained comparators together with the unit clause \(\lnot y_{k+1}\) is therefore equisatisfiable with the cardinality constraint after existentially quantifying auxiliary variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An at-most-k encoding may discard comparators irrelevant to rank k+1; forcing that ranked output false enforces the bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Network Truncation Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the truncation-regime leaf, but no cited source supports the output-cone truncation or its CNF encoding. The required range for k, normally 0≤k<n, is also unstated.

children.title: Comparator-Network Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Size, depth, and propagation considerations across network encodings.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison of classical full sorting networks with standard bound-specialized cardinality networks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under constant-size comparator encodings, a Batcher full sorting network has \(O(n\log^2 n)\) CNF size, while a standard at-most-\(k\) cardinality-network construction has \(O(n\log^2(k+1))\) size, including the usual padding conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Classical full sorting costs order n log-squared n, whereas a standard bound-specialized cardinality network costs order n log-squared of k+1.
assumptions_latex: Each comparator contributes \(\Theta(1)\) auxiliary variables and clauses.
The stated standard Batcher and cardinality-network constructions, including required padding, are used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |F_{\mathrm{sort}}|=O(n\log^2 n),\qquad |F_{\mathrm{card}}|=O(n\log^2(k+1))

notation.meaning: CNF of a full Batcher sorter
CNF of a bound-specialized cardinality network

knowledge_statements.title: Full Versus Bound-Specialized Network Size

assumptions_latex: Each comparator is represented by a fixed-size definitional CNF encoding.
The compared networks compute the same required output ranks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|F_N|=\Theta(|N|)\), while propagation strength is not determined by \(|N|\) alone.

notation.meaning: Definitional CNF encoding of the network

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates syntactic size and depth from semantic propagation behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a comparator network \(N\) encoded with a constant number of auxiliary variables and clauses per comparator, the resulting CNF \(F_N\) has \(\Theta(|N|)\) variables and clauses beyond the inputs. Network depth bounds parallel evaluation depth but does not by itself determine CNF size. Two networks computing the same ranks can therefore trade comparator count against depth. Moreover, equal functional correctness does not imply equal unit-propagation strength: propagation depends on the network topology, retained outputs, and chosen comparator clauses, not solely on \(|N|\) or depth.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Comparator count controls CNF size, depth controls parallel evaluation, and neither measure alone determines unit-propagation strength.
knowledge_statements.title: Comparator-Network Tradeoffs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits the tradeoff leaf. The linear-size claim is plausible under the stated fixed-size encoding assumption, but the topology-dependent unit-propagation comparison requires a construction-specific source.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit definitional CNF for the canonical ordered diagram of an unweighted at-most-k constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Use states \(s\in\{0,\ldots,k+1\}\), where \(k+1\) is rejecting overflow, and variables \(q_{i,s}\) denoting the unique state after \(x_1,\ldots,x_i\). Set \(q_{0,0}\) true and define \(q_{i,s}\) by the deterministic transition \(s=\min\{k+1,s'+x_i\}\), using constant-size Tseitin definitions for every transition. With \(\neg q_{n,k+1}\), the resulting CNF satisfies \[\exists q,z\;F_D(x,q,z)\iff\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\le k.\] It has width at most \(k+2\) and \(O(n(k+1))\) states, transitions, variables, and clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A one-hot layered diagram tracks the capped partial sum and rejects its overflow state. Its explicit definitional CNF is exact and has O(nk) size.
assumptions_latex: The constraint is the unweighted inequality \(\sum_i x_i\le k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists q,z\;F_D(x,q,z)\iff\sum_i x_i\le k,\qquad |F_D|=O(n(k+1)).

notation.meaning: State s is active after processing i inputs
Auxiliaries introduced by constant-size transition definitions
Definitional CNF of the layered diagram

knowledge_statements.title: Exact One-Hot Partial-Sum Diagram Encoding

assumptions_latex: The constraint is \(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\le k\) with \(x_i\in\{0,1\}\).
The diagram follows the variable order \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists z\,F_D(x,z)\iff \sum_{i=1}^n x_i\le k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Layered partial-sum diagram for an unweighted at-most cardinality constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Construct a layered diagram \(D\) whose state after variables \(x_1,\ldots,x_i\) is the capped partial sum \(s_i=\min\{k+1,\sum_{j=1}^i x_j\}\). From state \(s\), the arc labeled \(b\in\{0,1\}\) enters \(\min\{k+1,s+b\}\). States \(0,\ldots,k\) in the final layer accept, while state \(k+1\) rejects. Any sound definitional CNF \(F_D(x,z)\) enforcing a consistent accepting path is an encoding precisely when \(\exists z\,F_D(x,z)\) holds if and only if \(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\le k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A layered partial-sum diagram accepts exactly assignments with at most k true inputs and can be translated definitionally to CNF.
knowledge_statements.title: Decision-Diagram Cardinality Encodings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The layered capped-sum diagram matches the cardinality-encoding topic, but “any sound definitional CNF” does not identify an inspectable translation whose projected equivalence can be checked.

Represent each a_ix_i as an L-bit word, successively add the words using L-bit ripple-carry adders, and compare the final word with K. The construction uses O(nL) bounded-fan-in gates. A constant-size definitional CNF template per gate therefore uses O(nL) auxiliary variables, clauses, and literals.

assumptions_latex: x_i\in\{0,1\} and a_i,K\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}.
