assumptions_latex: Coefficients \(a_i\) and bound \(K\) are nonnegative integers.
Inputs satisfy \(x_i\in\{0,1\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists z\,F(x,z)\iff \sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i\le K\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Circuit-to-CNF representation of a nonnegative pseudo-Boolean upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(m\) with \(2^{m+1}>\sum_{i=1}^n a_i\). Expand each product \(a_i x_i\) into its binary-weighted bit contributions, combine those contributions by half-adders and full-adders, and obtain bits \(s_0,\ldots,s_m\) satisfying \(S=\sum_{j=0}^m 2^j s_j\). Conjoin definitional CNF clauses for every gate with a binary comparator circuit imposing \(S\le K\). If \(z\) denotes all internal wires, the resulting formula \(F(x,z)\) must satisfy \(\exists z\,F(x,z)\) if and only if \(\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i\le K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary adders compute the weighted Boolean sum, and a binary comparator enforces that the resulting sum does not exceed K.
knowledge_statements.title: Binary-Adder Encodings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind and terminal placement are appropriate, but the gate encoding, addition architecture, and comparison circuit have no cited construction or locator.

children.title: BDD Encodings
children.top_down_role: Pseudo-Boolean encodings derived from binary decision diagrams.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Output-sensitive size relative to an already constructed explicit BDD; construction cost and width growth are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an explicit rooted ordered BDD D=(V,E), any exact local translation using O(1) auxiliary variables and clauses per node or arc has size O(|V|+|E|). Because each nonterminal binary node has two outgoing arcs, this is O(|V|).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constant-size local translation produces CNF linear in the explicit BDD size.
assumptions_latex: D=(V,E) is an explicit rooted ordered BDD with accepting and rejecting terminals.
The selected exact translation uses O(1) variables and clauses per node or arc.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear BDD Translation Size

assumptions_latex: The pseudo-Boolean predicate is evaluated in a fixed Boolean variable order.
The diagram is a rooted acyclic binary decision diagram with accepting and rejecting terminals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists z\,F_D(x,z)\iff D(x)=1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existential CNF encoding of an ordered binary decision diagram.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) represent a Boolean predicate over \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\). Each nonterminal node labeled \(x_i\) has a low successor selected by \(x_i=0\) and a high successor selected by \(x_i=1\). Introduce auxiliary variables \(z\) and definitional clauses expressing the truth value or selected successor of every reachable node, fix the root as active, and forbid the rejecting terminal. A correct BDD encoding \(F_D(x,z)\) satisfies \(\exists z\,F_D(x,z)\) exactly when the unique path selected by \(x\) reaches the accepting terminal, equivalently when \(D(x)=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A BDD encoding tracks the unique binary path selected by an assignment and permits extensions exactly for accepting paths.
knowledge_statements.title: BDD Encodings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record has the correct representational role, but it alternates between node-truth and path-selection translations without specifying clauses or citing a source that establishes the projected equivalence.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Output-sensitive size relative to an explicit MDD and a selected Boolean encoding of finite-domain values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Introduce path variables and O(1) local constraints per node or arc, and channel every selected arc e to a Boolean literal \lambda_e for its value. The diagram portion has size O(|V|+|E|). If the domain encoding and channeling constraints have size H, the complete encoding has size O(|V|+|E|+H).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An explicit MDD translates linearly in its nodes and arcs, plus finite-domain channeling cost.
assumptions_latex: M=(V,E) is an explicit layered MDD.
Each arc label has an available Boolean value literal.
The chosen exact path template uses O(1) clauses per node or arc.

notation.meaning: Boolean value literal for arc e

knowledge_statements.title: MDD Translation Size

The diagram is layered consistently with a fixed variable order.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-domain decision-diagram representation, including pseudo-Boolean state diagrams with multivalued arcs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a layered acyclic diagram for variables \(v_i\in D_i\), where every outgoing arc from a node in layer \(i\) is labeled by a value in \(D_i\). An assignment \(v\) is accepted when its labels select a root-to-accepting-terminal path. A correct CNF or finite-domain encoding \(F_M(v,z)\) satisfies \(\exists z\,F_M(v,z)\) if and only if \(M(v)=1\).

children.title: Diagram Reduction Regimes
children.top_down_role: Effects of state merging and diagram reduction on encoding structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact reduction of deterministic ordered BDDs and MDDs; approximate state merging is excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assign identifiers to the terminals and process nodes in reverse layer order. Delete a node whose value-labeled successors are all identical. Otherwise form its signature from its variable label and ordered tuple of successor identifiers, and merge nodes with equal signatures. Sorting or balanced dictionaries implement the reduction in O((|V|+|E|)\log |V|) time and O(|V|+|E|) space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reverse-layer successor signatures delete redundant tests and merge equivalent states exactly.
assumptions_latex: D=(V,E) is a finite deterministic ordered acyclic BDD or MDD.
Outgoing arcs are indexed by the values of the node's variable.
Nodes are processed from the terminals toward the root.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure returns an equivalent reduced ordered diagram in O((|V|+|E|)\log |V|) deterministic time.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonicity for a fixed variable order, domains, arc-label convention, and terminal convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed ordered finite variable domains and fixed terminal labels, every represented function has, up to rooted arc-labeled isomorphism, a unique deterministic ordered decision diagram with no node whose outgoing arcs all share one successor and no two nodes having the same variable label and successor tuple.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For fixed ordering and conventions, exact deletion and merging produce a unique reduced ordered BDD or MDD up to isomorphism.
assumptions_latex: The diagrams represent the same finite-domain function.
They use the same variable order, domains, arc labels, and terminals.
Both diagrams satisfy the exact deletion and merging reduction conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two reduced ordered diagrams are isomorphic.
knowledge_statements.title: Reduced Ordered Diagram Canonicity

assumptions_latex: The decision diagram is ordered and acyclic.
Reduction preserves terminal labels and outgoing-arc labels.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D'(x)=D(x)\) for every assignment \(x\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact semantic reductions for ordered BDDs or MDDs; approximate state merging is excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Two nodes in the same layer may be merged when they represent identical residual functions, equivalently when their equally labeled outgoing arcs lead to equivalent successors. A nonterminal node may be eliminated when all of its value-labeled arcs lead to the same successor. Repeated application of these exact reductions produces a diagram \(D'\) satisfying \(D'(x)=D(x)\) for every complete assignment \(x\). Consequently, replacing \(D\) by \(D'\) before a sound diagram-to-CNF translation preserves the projected set of satisfying assignments while potentially decreasing auxiliary variables and clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Merging equivalent residual states and deleting redundant tests preserves every accepted assignment while potentially shrinking the encoding.
knowledge_statements.title: Diagram Reduction Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind correctly captures exact diagram reduction, and the scope excludes approximate merging. A decision-diagram source is still required for the merge, redundant-test elimination, and projected-CNF preservation claims.

children.title: Diagram-Width Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Applicability limits associated with decision-diagram width growth.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete binary instance showing exponential sensitivity of exact width to variable order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For EQ_m(u,v), the order u_1,\ldots,u_m,v_1,\ldots,v_m induces 2^m distinct residual tests v=u after u_m and therefore width at least 2^m. Under u_1,v_1,\ldots,u_m,v_m, only a constant number of states is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bit-vector equality has exponential width under a grouped order and constant width under an interleaved order.
assumptions_latex: EQ_m(u,v)=1 iff u=v for u,v\in\{0,1\}^m.
Reduced ordered BDDs are used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The grouped order has width at least 2^m, while the interleaved order has constant width.
knowledge_statements.title: Equality Variable-Order Separation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic width characterization for reduced deterministic ordered BDDs and MDDs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a cut after variables 1,\ldots,k, two prefix assignments reach the same reduced-diagram state if and only if they induce the same residual function on the remaining variables. Hence the cut width equals the number of distinct nonterminal residual functions induced by those prefixes, with constant residuals represented by terminals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reduced-diagram width at a cut equals the number of distinct residual functions induced by prefixes.
assumptions_latex: A finite-domain function is represented by a reduced deterministic ordered decision diagram.
All prefixes respect the fixed variable order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: w_k=|\{f_\alpha:\alpha\text{ is a length-k prefix}\}|, with constant residuals identified with terminals.

notation.meaning: Residual function induced by prefix alpha

knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Function Width Characterization

assumptions_latex: A fixed variable order defines layers \(0,\ldots,n\).
Only exact decision diagrams are considered.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|V(D)|\le 2+(n+1)w(D)\), but \(w(D)\) may be exponential in \(n\).

notation.meaning: Maximum number of nonterminal nodes in a layer

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Width as the boundary between compact and potentially exponential exact diagram encodings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a layered ordered decision diagram \(D\) on \(n\) variables, define \(w(D)\) as the maximum number of distinct residual states in any layer. Then the number of nonterminal nodes is at most \((n+1)w(D)\), so any local constant-size node translation yields encoding size \(O(nw(D))\). This guarantee is conditional: fixed-width diagrams give polynomial-size encodings, whereas predicates whose residual functions are pairwise distinct across an exponential-size layer force exponential width for that variable order. Thus exactness alone supplies no polynomial bound on diagram or CNF size.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded layer width yields polynomial encodings, but exponentially many distinct residual functions force exponential diagram width and size.
knowledge_statements.title: Diagram-Width Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the leaf, and the conditional O(nw(D)) bound is plausible. The exponential-width assertion lacks a cited lower-bound result or a specified predicate family and variable order.

children.title: Generalized Totalizers
children.top_down_role: Totalizer-style encodings adapted to weighted pseudo-Boolean sums.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural size of the declared forward transition scheme.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With one output variable per nonzero retained state, the number of such variables is at most \(\sum_v|S_v|\), and the forward merge clauses number at most \(\sum_{v\text{ internal}}|S_p||S_q|\). Since \(|S_v|\le K+2\) under overflow saturation, a binary tree with \(O(n)\) nodes has \(O(nK)\) output variables and \(O(nK^2)\) forward merge clauses. These are construction-size bounds, not SAT-runtime bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Saturated generalized-totalizer size is controlled by node state counts and child-state pairs, with coarse O(nK) variables and O(nK squared) merge clauses.
assumptions_latex: The declared forward threshold scheme is used.
The tree has \(O(n)\) nodes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: V=O(nK),\qquad C=O(nK^2)

notation.meaning: retained saturated states at node v

knowledge_statements.title: Reachable-State Construction Size

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe single-state overflow saturation for nonnegative sums.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\sigma(u)=\min\{u,K+1\}\) and nonnegative integers \(s,t\), \[\sigma(s+t)=\sigma(\sigma(s)+\sigma(t)).\] Thus exact values need be retained only through \(K\), with one state \(K+1\) for all overflow values; the root is in that state exactly when the weighted sum exceeds \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All sums above K may share one overflow state because saturation is compatible with recursive addition.
assumptions_latex: All partial sums are nonnegative integers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sigma(s+t)=\sigma(\sigma(s)+\sigma(t))

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Corrected threshold-literal construction for a nonnegative weighted upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
After deleting zero-weight terms, build a binary tree over \(a_ix_i\), with \(a_i>0\), and set \(\sigma(u)=\min\{u,K+1\}\). At node \(v\), let \(S_v\) be the reachable saturated subtotal values, include \(0\), and use \(o_{v,s}\) for the threshold assertion that the subtree subtotal is at least \(s\), treating \(o_{v,0}\) as true. At leaf \(i\), impose \(o_{i,a_i}\leftrightarrow x_i\). For children \(p,q\), add \[(
eg o_{p,s}\lor
eg o_{q,t}\lor o_{v,\sigma(s+t)})\] for all \(s\in S_p,t\in S_q\), omitting tautological zero outputs, and assert \(
eg o_{r,K+1}\) at the root. The resulting CNF \(F_T\) satisfies \(\exists z\,F_T(x,z)\leftrightarrow\sum_i a_ix_i\le K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A generalized totalizer propagates reachable subtotal thresholds through a binary tree and forbids the saturated overflow threshold at the root.
assumptions_latex: \(K\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\).
Positive weights are integers; zero-weight terms are removed.
Inputs are Boolean.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists z\,F_T(x,z)\leftrightarrow\sum_i a_ix_i\le K

notation.meaning: reachable saturated subtotal values at node v

knowledge_statements.title: Forward Generalized-Totalizer Encoding

assumptions_latex: Coefficients \(a_i\) and bound \(K\) are nonnegative integers.
Inputs satisfy \(x_i\in\{0,1\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists z\,F_T(x,z)\iff \sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i\le K\).

notation.meaning: Reachable sum set at node v
Literal indicating a reachable sum threshold

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tree-structured reachable-sum encoding of a nonnegative pseudo-Boolean upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Build a binary tree \(T\) whose leaves correspond to terms \(a_i x_i\). For each node \(v\), let \(S_v\) contain the sums reachable from leaves below \(v\), and introduce literals \(o_{v,s}\) representing attainment of the encoded sum or threshold \(s\). For children \(p,q\), add clauses propagating every compatible combination \(s"+"t\) to the parent value, with values above \(K\) represented by an overflow class. Link leaf literals to \(x_i\) and forbid overflow at the root. The resulting formula \(F_T(x,z)\) satisfies \(\exists z\,F_T(x,z)\) exactly when \(\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i\le K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A generalized totalizer combines reachable weighted sums in a tree and forbids the root overflow state to enforce the bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Generalized Totalizers

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation belongs in the generalized-totalizer leaf, but the record conflates exact-sum and threshold-literal semantics and contains the malformed expression s\"+\"t. A specific clause scheme and authoritative source are needed.

children.title: Reduced Generalized Totalizers
children.top_down_role: Generalized totalizer variants using restricted or merged representable sums.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural state-count effect of quotienting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Since \(R_v=\rho_v(S_v)\), \(|R_v|\le|S_v|\). Under a construction emitting one state variable per representative and at most one candidate transition per representative pair, \(|R_p||R_q|\le|S_p||S_q|\). This does not imply smaller total CNF after strengthening clauses, stronger propagation, or lower SAT runtime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quotienting cannot increase representative-state or representative-pair counts, but need not reduce final CNF size or solving time.
assumptions_latex: \(R_v\) is the image of \(S_v\).
The declared representative-pair transition scheme is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |R_v|\le|S_v|,\qquad |R_p||R_q|\le|S_p||S_q|
knowledge_statements.title: Reduction Size Monotonicity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compositional exactness criterion for deterministic reduced totalizer states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f_v:S_p\times S_q\to S_v\) be the exact transition and \(\rho_u:S_u\to R_u\) surjective reduction maps. A deterministic reduced transition \(g_v\) exists exactly when equal child representatives always induce equal parent representatives: \[\rho_p(s)=\rho_p(s'),\ \rho_q(t)=\rho_q(t')\Longrightarrow \rho_v(f_v(s,t))=\rho_v(f_v(s',t')).\] Equivalently, \(\rho_v(f_v(s,t))=g_v(\rho_p(s),\rho_q(t))\). If this holds at every internal node and root acceptance factors through \(\rho_r\), reduced bottom-up evaluation preserves the exact accept/reject result.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A deterministic reduced totalizer is exact when its state maps form transition congruences and root acceptance depends only on the root representative.
assumptions_latex: Every exact state is reachable.
Each reduction map is surjective.
Exact node transitions are deterministic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \rho_v(f_v(s,t))=g_v(\rho_p(s),\rho_q(t))
knowledge_statements.title: Transition-Congruent Reduction

assumptions_latex: Coefficients \(a_i\) and bound \(K\) are nonnegative integers.
Every discarded sum is mapped to an explicitly defined representative class.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists z\,F_R(x,z)\iff \sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i\le K\), provided the reduction preserves the root overflow distinction.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced generalized-totalizer scheme parameterized by explicit sum-state quotient maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At each totalizer node \(v\), replace its exact reachable-sum set \(S_v\) by a reduced set \(R_v\) and a map \(\rho_v:S_v\to R_v\). Parent transitions combine child representatives and apply the parent map. The reduction is an exact encoding of \(\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i\le K\) when all realizable child combinations are represented and the induced root map separates every sum at most \(K\) from every sum greater than \(K\). With overflow forbidden, the reduced CNF \(F_R\) then satisfies \(\exists z\,F_R(x,z)\) if and only if the pseudo-Boolean inequality holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reduced totalizer quotients reachable sums, remaining exact only when the root representation still separates feasible sums from overflow.
knowledge_statements.title: Reduced Generalized Totalizers

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the reduced-totalizer leaf, but root overflow separation alone is not presented with sufficient transition-consistency conditions to establish exactness of the local quotient maps.

children.top_down_role: Structural choices governing which partial sums remain represented.

assumptions_latex: R_\ell\text{ and }R_r\text{ are exactly the reachable threshold-saturated states of the two children}
u\oplus_K v=\min\{u+v,K+1\}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bottom-up computation of reachable states for the threshold-saturated regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a binary node \(v\), combine its child sets by \(R_v=\{u\oplus_K v':u\in R_\ell,\ v'\in R_r\}\) and remove duplicate capped states. This enumerates exactly the reachable threshold-saturated parent states. It performs \(O(|R_\ell||R_r|)\) capped additions and produces at most \(\min\{K+2,|R_\ell||R_r|\}\) states.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Combine every pair of reachable child states using capped addition and deduplicate; this exactly constructs the reachable capped parent states.
knowledge_statements.title: Bottom-Up Threshold-Saturated Reachability

assumptions_latex: a_i\in\mathbb Z_{\ge 0}
K\in\mathbb Z_{\ge 0}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_i a_i x_i\le K\iff q_K\!\left(\sum_i a_i x_i\right)\le K,\qquad |\operatorname{range}(q_K)|=K+2.

notation.meaning: threshold-saturation map on nonnegative integer sums

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-state reduction for one nonnegative pseudo-Boolean upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i\le K\), define \(q_K(s)=\min\{s,K+1\}\) and \(u\oplus_K v=\min\{u+v,K+1\}\). Then \(q_K(s+t)=q_K(s)\oplus_K q_K(t)\), and \(s\le K\) if and only if \(q_K(s)\le K\). Hence all sums exceeding \(K\) may share one overflow state without changing satisfaction of the upper-bound constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonnegative upper bound, retain sums through K and merge every larger sum into one overflow state; capped addition preserves the constraint exactly.
knowledge_statements.title: Threshold-Saturated Sum Regime

assumptions_latex: The target inequality is \(\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i\le K\) with nonnegative integer data.
Reduction maps are defined at every internal totalizer node.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s\sim_v t\) is admissible only when all feasible continuations give the same truth value for \(\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i\le K\).

notation.meaning: Reachable partial sums at node v
Contribution from variables outside node v

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic criterion for exact merging of partial-sum states in a generalized totalizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S_v\) be the reachable partial sums below node \(v\). A sum-set reduction may merge \(s,t\in S_v\) only if they are indistinguishable under every reachable outside contribution \(r\): 
\[s+r\le K\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad t+r\le K.\]
Equivalently, each equivalence class of \(\sim_v\) must lie wholly on one side of every residual threshold \(K-r\) induced by a feasible continuation. The exact regime retains all such distinguishable classes; coarser merging is valid only when additional clauses or refinement restore the lost distinction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two partial sums may share a reduced state exactly when every feasible outside contribution makes them simultaneously feasible or infeasible.
knowledge_statements.title: Sum-Set Reduction Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind is appropriate and the residual-threshold criterion is mathematically plausible, but no source defines the reachable continuations or proves that this semantic equivalence is the exact admissibility regime for the intended reduction construction.

children.title: Reduction-Fidelity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits on reduction while preserving the intended pseudo-Boolean constraint.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local obstruction to deterministic exact reduced transitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose reduced parent behavior may depend only on the two child representatives. If \[\rho_p(s)=\rho_p(s'),\quad \rho_q(t)=\rho_q(t'),\quad \rho_v(f_v(s,t))\ne\rho_v(f_v(s',t')),\] then no deterministic transition on the reduced child pair can be exact for both cases. The four child states and two distinct required parent classes are a finite failure certificate. Additional distinguishing state may repair the obstruction; clauses seeing only the original representatives cannot.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If one reduced child pair requires two different parent classes, no deterministic transition using only those representatives can be exact.
assumptions_latex: Reduced parent behavior depends only on the child representatives.
The exact node transition is deterministic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The displayed witness implies that no deterministic exact reduced transition exists.}
knowledge_statements.title: Transition-Congruence Failure

assumptions_latex: The encoding represents the upper bound \(\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i\le K\).
Reduced states are the only information passed from a subtree to its parent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_v(s)=\rho_v(t)\) with opposite feasible continuations implies that the reduced encoding cannot be exact.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp semantic failure condition for quotienting generalized-totalizer sum states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a reduction merges two reachable sums \(s\) and \(t\) at node \(v\), so \(\rho_v(s)=\rho_v(t)\). If there exists a reachable contribution \(r\) from variables outside the subtree such that \(s+r\le K\) but \(t+r>K\), then the merged state cannot determine whether the completed assignment satisfies the inequality. Any encoding whose parent clauses depend only on \(\rho_v(s)\) must consequently accept an infeasible completion or reject a feasible one. Exact reduction therefore fails precisely when a merged class crosses a residual feasibility threshold induced by some reachable continuation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Merging sums that some feasible continuation places on opposite sides of K necessarily destroys exactness unless extra distinguishing information is added.
knowledge_statements.title: Reduction-Fidelity Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind matches the terminal container. The indistinguishable-state argument is plausible under the stated information restriction, but the claimed precise boundary requires a formal source defining the reduced encoding model and reachable continuations.

children.title: Coefficient-Decomposition Encodings
children.top_down_role: Pseudo-Boolean encodings structured by decomposing numeric coefficients.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linking requirement when coefficient pieces use fresh variables instead of repeated occurrences of the original literal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a=\sum_k c_k and fresh variables y_k replace repeated occurrences of x, imposing y_k=x for every nonzero piece is sufficient to preserve ax=\sum_k c_ky_k. Without constraints ensuring this equality, projection can change: 2x\le1 permits only x=0, whereas y_1+y_2\le1 with no links to x admits x=1,y_1=y_2=0.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fresh piece variables require value-preserving links to the original Boolean variable; independent copies can destroy exactness.
assumptions_latex: a=\sum_{k=1}^m c_k with c_k\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Equality links y_k=x preserve the decomposed value; omitting value-preserving links can invalidate projection equivalence.

notation.meaning: Fresh variable associated with coefficient piece k

review_flags: revised_builder_overstatement: individual equalities are sufficient but not logically necessary under every possible alternative linking system
knowledge_statements.title: Unlinked-Copy Failure Boundary

assumptions_latex: \(a_i,b\in\mathbb Z_{\ge 0}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The decomposed inequality and the original pseudo-Boolean inequality have identical satisfying assignments in \(x\).

notation.meaning: number of pieces used for coefficient a_i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exact decomposition follows from finite distributivity over integer coefficients
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact additive decomposition of nonnegative integer coefficients before CNF encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each \(i\), choose \(m_i\ge 1\) and coefficients \(a_{ik}\in\mathbb Z_{\ge 0}\) satisfying \(a_i=\sum_{k=1}^{m_i}a_{ik}\). A coefficient-decomposition representation of \(\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i\le b\) is
\[
\sum_{i=1}^n\sum_{k=1}^{m_i}a_{ik}x_i\le b.
\]
Because the repeated occurrences refer to the same Boolean variable, every assignment satisfies \(\sum_{k=1}^{m_i}a_{ik}x_i=a_ix_i\). Thus decomposition may expose smaller weighted components to a downstream CNF encoder without changing the represented pseudo-Boolean constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Splitting every integer coefficient into nonnegative pieces preserves the pseudo-Boolean inequality exactly when all pieces multiply the same Boolean variable.
knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient-Decomposition Encodings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The additive identity and representation role are precise, but no inspectable source supports its placement as a pseudo-Boolean coefficient-decomposition encoding.

children.title: Mixed-Radix Encodings
children.top_down_role: Pseudo-Boolean encodings using positional systems with nonuniform radices.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact arithmetic recurrence underlying column-and-carry encodings; the Boolean encoding of each recurrence remains open.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Process columns from least to most significant with k_0=0 and impose C_j+k_j=s_j+q_jk_{j+1}, where 0\le s_j<q_j. Equivalently, s_j=(C_j+k_j)\bmod q_j and k_{j+1}=\lfloor(C_j+k_j)/q_j\rfloor. The normalized digits and final carry represent the original weighted sum exactly; comparison with the mixed-radix representation of b therefore enforces the original bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Least-to-most-significant carry equations normalize mixed-radix columns without changing the weighted sum.
assumptions_latex: C_j=\sum_i d_{ij}x_i is a nonnegative integral column load.
q_j\ge2 and k_0=0.
The final carry is retained or sufficient top capacity is provided.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C_j+k_j=s_j+q_jk_{j+1},\ 0\le s_j<q_j, preserves the exact total value across columns.
knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Radix Carry Normalization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical finite mixed-radix representation below the capacity of the selected positions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If r_0=1, r_{j+1}=q_jr_j, q_j\ge2, and 0\le N<r_{L+1}, then there is a unique vector d_0,\ldots,d_L with 0\le d_j<q_j and N=\sum_{j=0}^L d_jr_j. Without the digit bounds uniqueness can fail; if N\ge r_{L+1}, another top position or explicit overflow is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded digits represent every value below the selected mixed-radix capacity uniquely; overflow requires an additional representation.
assumptions_latex: r_0=1 and r_{j+1}=q_jr_j with q_j\in\mathbb Z_{\ge2}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There is a unique (d_0,\ldots,d_L) with 0\le d_j<q_j and N=\sum_{j=0}^L d_jr_j.
knowledge_statements.title: Unique Bounded Mixed-Radix Digits

assumptions_latex: \(x_i\in\{0,1\}\) and \(a_i,b\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\).
\(r_0=1\) and \(r_{j+1}=q_jr_j\) with integer \(q_j\ge2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Replacing each \(a_i\) by its mixed-radix expansion preserves \(\sum_i a_ix_i\le b\) exactly.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite mixed-radix expansion for nonnegative pseudo-Boolean coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose \(L\ge0\) so that every coefficient has an expansion
\[
a_i=\sum_{j=0}^{L}d_{ij}r_j,
\]
where \(0\le d_{ij}<q_j\) for \(j<L\) and \(d_{iL}\ge0\). The corresponding mixed-radix representation is
\[
\sum_{j=0}^{L}r_j\left(\sum_{i=1}^n d_{ij}x_i\right)\le b.
\]
The equality of the two weighted sums holds for every Boolean assignment. A CNF construction may therefore encode the digit columns and their carries while retaining existential equivalence to the original inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mixed-radix encoding expands each coefficient into positional digits and encodes digit columns and carries without altering the weighted inequality.
knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Radix Encodings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite mixed-radix identity is coherent, but the encoding interpretation involving digit columns, carries, and existential equivalence lacks an inspectable specialized source.

children.title: Radix-Selection Regimes
children.top_down_role: Representation choices among alternative mixed-radix bases.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact selection over a finite declared radix-search domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\subseteq\{2,3,\ldots\}\) be finite and \(L_{\max}<\infty\). Enumerate \(\mathcal R=\{(q_0,\ldots,q_{L-1}):1\le L\le L_{\max},\ q_j\in Q,\ \prod_jq_j>A\}\), evaluate the declared cost \(C\) on every member, and return \(\widehat r\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{r\in\mathcal R}C(r)\). At most \(\sum_{L=1}^{L_{\max}}|Q|^L\) candidates are tested. The guarantee does not extend to an unbounded domain or unevaluable cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enumeration returns a minimum-cost admissible radix sequence over a finite multiplier-and-depth domain.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\) and \(L_{\max}\) are finite and declared.
\(\mathcal R\ne\varnothing\).
\(C(r)\) is evaluable for every \(r\in\mathcal R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat r\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{r\in\mathcal R}C(r)
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Domain Radix Selection

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Depth and digit range for a fixed-base coefficient representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With place values \(1,q,\ldots,q^{L-1}\) and digits \(d_j\in\{0,\ldots,q-1\}\), every integer in \([0,A]\) is representable exactly when \(q^L>A\). The least depth is \(L=\lceil\log_q(A+1)\rceil\). Increasing \(q\) weakly decreases depth but enlarges the digit range and the carry range required by a column encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The minimum fixed-base depth is ceiling log base q of A+1; larger bases shorten the representation but enlarge local digit and carry ranges.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\).
\(q\in\mathbb Z\) and \(q\ge2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L=\lceil\log_q(A+1)\rceil
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Base Depth and Digit Tradeoff
Radix-Selection Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classification of radix sequences used in coefficient-column encodings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a coefficient bound \(A\in\mathbb Z_{\ge 0}\), a radix sequence is admissible when \(r_0=1\), \(r_{j+1}=q_jr_j\) with integers \(q_j\ge2\), and \(r_L>A\). It is fixed-base when \(q_j=q\) for every \(j\), binary when \(q=2\), and genuinely mixed when at least two multipliers differ. Given a declared encoding-cost functional \(C\), a data-dependent regime selects an admissible sequence from
\[
\operatorname*{argmin}_{(q_j)} C((q_j);a_1,\ldots,a_n,b).
\]
The cost functional and the admissible search domain are part of the regime specification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An admissible radix regime has place values sufficient for the coefficient bound; fixed-base, binary, genuinely mixed, and cost-selected regimes are distinguished by their multiplier sequences and selection rule.
assumptions_latex: \(a_i\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) and \(a_i\le A\) for every coefficient.
\(q_j\in\mathbb Z\) and \(q_j\ge2\) for every radix multiplier.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Admissible fixed-base, binary, genuinely mixed, and data-dependent regimes are distinguished by the sequence \((q_j)\) and, where applicable, its declared selection functional.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: regimes are defined by admissible positional systems

children.title: Decomposition–Radix Interaction
children.top_down_role: Structural relationships between coefficient decomposition and radix selection.

knowledge_statements.title: Decomposition–Radix Interaction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic interaction between additive coefficient pieces and positional digit columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every Boolean assignment,
\[
\sum_i a_ix_i
=\sum_{i,k}c_{ik}x_i
=\sum_j r_j\left(\sum_{i,k}d_{ikj}x_i\right)
=\sum_j r_jD_j.
\]
Hence coefficient decomposition and radix expansion commute at the level of the represented integer value. They need not yield the same auxiliary CNF: changing the pieces can change the digit-column loads \(D_j\), carry ranges, and the variables or clauses introduced by a chosen column encoder, even though the projection onto the original variables remains unchanged when both encodings are exact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Decomposition and radix expansion preserve the same weighted value, but a different decomposition can change column loads, carry states, and CNF size.
assumptions_latex: \(x_i\in\{0,1\}\) and \(a_i=\sum_k c_{ik}\) with \(c_{ik}\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\).
Each piece has an expansion \(c_{ik}=\sum_j d_{ikj}r_j\) in one common mixed-radix system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Decomposition before radix expansion gives \(D_j=\sum_{i,k}d_{ikj}x_i\) and preserves the original weighted sum exactly, while potentially changing encoder-specific auxiliary structure.

notation.meaning: digit of piece c_ik in column j
Boolean load of radix column j

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the interaction identity follows by rearranging finite sums

children.title: Hybrid Encodings
children.top_down_role: Single encodings that combine multiple representation mechanisms.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural size accounting for explicit hybrid composition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(H=(\bigwedge_tE_t)\wedge L\), with disjoint private auxiliary sets and explicitly represented links, clause and literal-occurrence counts are the sums of their component and linking counts, and \(|\operatorname{aux}(H)|=\sum_t|y_t|+|y_L|\). Polynomial-size components yield a polynomial-size hybrid only if the number of emitted components and the complete linking representation are polynomially bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hybrid size is component size plus linking overhead; compact components alone do not ensure a compact hybrid.
assumptions_latex: Component clause occurrences and private auxiliary sets are disjoint.
The linking CNF is explicit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |\operatorname{aux}(H)|=\sum_t|y_t|+|y_L|
knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Construction Size

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient exactness condition for conjunctively composed component encodings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(P(x)=\bigwedge_{t\in T}P_t(x)\), each \(E_t(x,y_t)\) satisfies \(P_t(x)\leftrightarrow\exists y_t\,E_t(x,y_t)\), and the auxiliary sets \(y_t\) are pairwise disjoint, then \[P(x)\leftrightarrow\exists (y_t)_{t\in T}\;\bigwedge_{t\in T}E_t(x,y_t).\] Shared original variables retain one common assignment. Shared auxiliary state is not covered without an explicit compatibility argument.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conjoining exact component encodings with disjoint private auxiliaries exactly encodes the conjunction of their semantic components.
assumptions_latex: \(P=\bigwedge_tP_t\).
Every \(E_t\) is existentially exact for \(P_t\).
The auxiliary sets are pairwise disjoint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P(x)\leftrightarrow\exists (y_t)_{t\in T}\;\bigwedge_tE_t(x,y_t)
knowledge_statements.title: Independent-Component Composition

assumptions_latex: A pseudo-Boolean constraint \(P(x)\) is partitioned into components indexed by \(t\in T\).
Each component encoding \(E_t(x,y_t)\) is existentially exact for its assigned component.
The auxiliary sets \(y_t\) are pairwise disjoint unless explicit linking constraints are supplied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The hybrid formula \(H(x,y)=\bigwedge_{t\in T}E_t(x,y_t)\wedge L(x,y)\) is exact precisely when its existential projection equals \(P(x)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: existential projection is the standard correctness criterion for auxiliary-variable encodings

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact composition of heterogeneous CNF encoders through partitioning and linking.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A hybrid encoding combines possibly different component encoders as
\[
H(x,y)=\bigwedge_{t\in T}E_t(x,y_t)\wedge L(x,y),
\]
where \(y=\bigcup_{t\in T}y_t\). It is an exact encoding of \(P\) when, for every \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\),
\[
P(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \exists y\;H(x,y).
\]
The linking formula \(L\) must enforce every shared sum, carry, or boundary condition required by the component partition; componentwise exactness alone does not imply exactness of the conjunction when components interact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hybrid encoding combines heterogeneous component encoders and is correct exactly when the combined formula projects to the original feasible assignments.
knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Encodings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The existential-projection criterion is coherent and the representation kind fits, but the proposed hybrid composition and linking requirements lack an inspectable specialized source.

children.title: Encoding Portfolios
children.top_down_role: Collections of alternative encodings available for instance-dependent selection.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Best-member guarantee with selector overhead separated from member cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the nonempty finite applicable set \(\mathcal E(P)\), let \(S^*(P)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{E\in\mathcal E(P)}c(E,P)\). Then \(c(S^*(P),P)=\min_Ec(E,P)\). If selection costs \(h(P)\ge0\), total cost is \(h(P)+\min_Ec(E,P)\); it improves on a fixed member only when the member-cost saving covers \(h(P)\). A predicted selector has the oracle guarantee only when it returns a realized-cost minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An oracle selector attains the least applicable-member cost, but portfolio cost also includes selector overhead.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal E(P)\) is nonempty and finite.
Realized cost is available for every applicable member.
Selector overhead is nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: c(S^*(P),P)=\min_{E\in\mathcal E(P)}c(E,P)
knowledge_statements.title: Oracle Portfolio Bound

assumptions_latex: Each candidate encoder accepts constraints from a declared domain.
Correctness is interpreted by existential projection onto original variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every selected portfolio member must satisfy \(P(x)\leftrightarrow\exists y_k E_k(P;x,y_k)\); selection changes the encoding, not the represented feasible set.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: portfolio correctness requires every selectable representation to be exact

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Instance-level selection among exact pseudo-Boolean-to-CNF encoders.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An encoding portfolio is a finite family \(\mathcal E=\{E_1,\ldots,E_m\}\) together with a selector \(S\) satisfying \(S(P)\in\mathcal E\) for every supported pseudo-Boolean instance \(P\). Each member must be exact on its declared domain:
\[
P(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\exists y_k\;E_k(P;x,y_k).
\]
The portfolio output is \(S(P)(P;x,y)\). The selector may depend on coefficients, arity, bound, sparsity, or predicted solver cost, but it may not select an encoder outside its correctness domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An encoding portfolio is a finite set of exact encoders plus a selector that chooses one valid encoder for each supported instance.
knowledge_statements.title: Encoding Portfolios

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is internally consistent, but no source establishes this selector-based construction as an encoding portfolio in the exact pseudo-Boolean-to-CNF context.

children.title: Component-Selection Criteria
children.top_down_role: Instance features guiding the choice of encoding components.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound elimination under a nonnegative weighted component-selection score.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J(u)=\sum_k\lambda_kM_k(u)\), where \(\lambda_k\ge0\). If admissible candidates \(s,t\) satisfy \(M_k(s)\le M_k(t)\) for every \(k\), with strict inequality for some coordinate having \(\lambda_k>0\), then \(J(s)<J(t)\). Hence \(t\) cannot minimize \(J\). Crossing metric vectors are not ordered by this test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A candidate weakly worse in every metric and strictly worse in a positively weighted metric cannot minimize the weighted score.
assumptions_latex: Both candidates satisfy every hard applicability and compatibility condition.
All score weights are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: J(s)<J(t)

notation.meaning: metric coordinate k of candidate u

knowledge_statements.title: Pareto-Dominance Elimination

assumptions_latex: Each candidate component has a declared applicability domain and an exactness guarantee.
Every candidate has measurable or predicted resource and propagation attributes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A component is selectable only if it is applicable and compatible; among selectable components it minimizes the declared score \(J_t(P)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: constrained argmin formalizes multi-attribute component selection
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility and score conditions for selecting components of a composite encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D_t(P)\) assert that encoder \(t\) is correct and applicable to component \(P\), and let \(K_t(P)\) assert compatibility with adjacent components and linking constraints. For nonnegative weights \(\lambda_s,\lambda_a,\lambda_p\), define
\[
J_t(P)=\lambda_s S_t(P)+\lambda_a A_t(P)+\lambda_p W_t(P),
\]
where \(S_t\) is predicted CNF size, \(A_t\) auxiliary-state count, and \(W_t\) a declared propagation-cost or weakness measure. A valid selection belongs to
\[
\operatorname*{argmin}_{t:\,D_t(P)\wedge K_t(P)}J_t(P).
\]
If the feasible index set is empty, hybrid construction is undefined for that partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A component may be selected only when applicable and compatible; a declared weighted score then chooses among feasible encoders.
knowledge_statements.title: Component-Selection Criteria

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits, but the particular weighted score and its propagation-weakness component are modeling choices requiring a cited source or an explicitly sourced declared framework.

children.title: Hybridization Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where combined representations introduce excessive size or weak propagation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exactness Does Not Preserve Unit Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete separation of existential exactness from unit-propagation strength.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P(x)\equiv x\) and \(E(x,y)=(x\lor y)\wedge(x\lor\neg y)\). Then \(\exists y\,E(x,y)\leftrightarrow x\), but with no assignment neither clause is unit, so unit propagation does not derive \(x\); the direct CNF \((x)\) does. Semantic exactness therefore does not ensure propagation completeness or preserve monolithic propagation strength.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact two-clause extension represents x but does not unit-propagate x, unlike the direct unit clause.
assumptions_latex: Unit propagation is the compared inference mechanism.
Correctness means existential projection onto original variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists y\,E(x,y)\leftrightarrow x\quad\text{while unit propagation on }E\text{ does not derive }x
knowledge_statements.title: Exactness Does Not Preserve Unit Propagation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of compactness caused by explicit hybrid links or component multiplicity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Since \(L_N\) is a subformula of \(H_N=(\bigwedge_tE_{t,N})\wedge L_N\), a superpolynomial explicit-size lower bound for \(L_N\) is also one for \(H_N\). Likewise, emitting a superpolynomial number of nonempty components prevents polynomial total size. Polynomial-size components alone therefore do not ensure a polynomial-size hybrid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polynomial-size components do not produce a polynomial-size hybrid when links or the number of emitted components are superpolynomial.
assumptions_latex: Each component is explicitly represented.
The linking CNF is a subformula of the hybrid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |L_N|\notin N^{O(1)}\Longrightarrow |H_N|\notin N^{O(1)}
knowledge_statements.title: Linking-Overhead Boundary

assumptions_latex: Correctness of an auxiliary encoding means existential equivalence after projecting onto original variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Componentwise existential exactness does not guarantee exactness after identifying auxiliary variables across components.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explicit two-formula counterexample is directly checkable
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure caused by unvalidated sharing of auxiliary variables between exact components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the always-true constraint \(P(x)=\top\) on \(x\in\{0,1\}\). The formulas \(E_1(x,y)\equiv(y\leftrightarrow x)\) and \(E_2(x,z)\equiv(z\leftrightarrow\neg x)\) are each existentially exact for \(P\), since a suitable auxiliary value exists for every \(x\). If hybridization incorrectly identifies \(z=y\), the conjunction becomes
\[
(y\leftrightarrow x)\wedge(y\leftrightarrow\neg x),
\]
which is unsatisfiable for both values of \(x\). Thus auxiliary-state identification is sound only when the induced compatibility constraints preserve the existential projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two individually exact components can become unsatisfiable when their auxiliary variables are incorrectly shared, so componentwise correctness alone is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.title: Hybridization Failure Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The explicit counterexample is mathematically sound and the failure-boundary kind fits, but the record has no inspectable citation supporting its use as a named hybridization failure boundary.

children.title: Encoding Size
children.top_down_role: Clause and literal growth introduced by an encoding.

assumptions_latex: The CNF is represented explicitly as a finite list of clauses.
Integer parameters are written in binary unless another convention is declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The encoding size is the declared bit length \(\lvert E\rvert_{\mathrm{bit}}\), with clause and literal counts serving only as convention-dependent proxies.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit representational size of a pseudo-Boolean-to-CNF encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an explicitly represented CNF encoding \(E\), its encoding size is the number \(\lvert E\rvert_{\mathrm{bit}}\) of bits required by the declared serialization of variable identifiers, literal signs, clause boundaries, and any retained numerical data. Two common structural measures are
\[
C(E)=\text{number of clauses},\qquad L(E)=\sum_{K\in E}|K|.
\]
When identifiers use \(O(\log V(E))\) bits, where \(V(E)\) is the number of variables, \(L(E)\) alone is not literally the bit size; the reporting convention must therefore be stated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Encoding size is the bit length of an explicit CNF representation; clause and literal counts are structural proxies whose serialization convention must be stated.
knowledge_statements.title: Encoding Size

children.title: Auxiliary-State Growth
children.top_down_role: Growth in auxiliary variables or represented intermediate states.

assumptions_latex: The source interface declares its original variable set \(X(P)\).
A fixed encoding family and instance family \(\mathcal P_N\) are used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Auxiliary-variable growth is the asymptotic behavior of \(A_E^{\max}(N)\) under the declared interface and parameterization.

notation.meaning: declared original variables of the source instance

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Growth in Boolean variables introduced by a fixed encoding family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an encoding \(E(P)\) of a source instance with declared original-variable set \(X(P)\), let \(Y_E(P)=\operatorname{Var}(E(P))\setminus X(P)\) and \(A_E(P)=|Y_E(P)|\). For an instance family \(\mathcal P_N\), define \(A_E^{\max}(N)=\max_{P\in\mathcal P_N}A_E(P)\). A growth claim must declare \(N\), the original-variable interface, and how shared, redundant, or reusable auxiliary variables are counted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Auxiliary-variable growth is the worst-case number of encoding variables outside the declared source interface, measured over a fixed instance family and input parameter.
knowledge_statements.title: Auxiliary-Variable Growth

assumptions_latex: All auxiliary coordinates are Boolean.
A semantic-state interpretation, if used, is declared separately from the variable set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Auxiliary-coordinate growth and represented-state growth are different resources and must not be reported under one count without an explicit convention.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Prevents conflation of introduced variables with assignments or semantic states represented by them.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A set of \(a\) auxiliary Boolean variables has \(2^a\) possible assignments, although an encoding may admit fewer reachable semantic states or may map several assignments to one state. Consequently, auxiliary-variable count, reachable auxiliary-assignment count, and semantic-state count are not interchangeable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Counting auxiliary variables is different from counting their possible assignments or the semantic states those assignments represent.
knowledge_statements.title: Variables Versus Represented States

assumptions_latex: An encoding \(E(P;x,y)\) separates original variables \(x\) from introduced variables \(y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Auxiliary-state growth is the asymptotic behavior of \(A_E(P)=\lvert\operatorname{Var}(E)\setminus\operatorname{Var}(P)\rvert\) over a declared instance family.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: auxiliary variables are exactly variables absent from the original instance
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Growth rate of introduced Boolean state under a fixed encoding family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a pseudo-Boolean instance \(P\) and its CNF encoding \(E(P;x,y)\), define
\[
Y_E(P)=\operatorname{Var}(E(P))\setminus\operatorname{Var}(P),
\qquad A_E(P)=|Y_E(P)|.
\]
Given a family \(\mathcal P_N\) indexed by an explicitly declared input-size parameter \(N\), auxiliary-state growth is the asymptotic behavior of
\[
A_E^{\max}(N)=\max_{P\in\mathcal P_N}A_E(P).
\]
The parameterization must specify whether coefficient magnitudes contribute through their values or their binary bit lengths; otherwise growth claims are not comparable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Auxiliary-state growth counts variables introduced by an encoding and studies their worst-case asymptotic count under a declared input-size parameter.
knowledge_statements.title: Auxiliary-State Growth

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The variable-set definition and parameterization warning are coherent, but no inspectable source supports the asymptotic auxiliary-state-growth formulation in this encoding taxonomy.

children.title: Size–State Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Relationships between emitted constraints and auxiliary-state requirements.

assumptions_latex: Tautological clauses and unconstrained fresh variables are permitted syntactically.
Semantic exactness is judged after projection to the original variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Projection exactness alone implies no monotone or inverse relationship between encoding size and auxiliary-variable count.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp boundary against interpreting exactness as a universal resource tradeoff theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: From any exact encoding, arbitrarily many tautological clauses can be added without adding auxiliary variables, and arbitrarily many unused fresh variables can be declared without adding clauses that affect the projection. Both padded families preserve the represented source solutions. Thus exactness by itself forces neither resource to decrease when the other increases and does not imply Pareto efficiency.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Padding an exact encoding with tautologies or unused auxiliaries changes one resource without improving semantics, so exactness alone creates no universal inverse size–state law.
knowledge_statements.title: No Universal Inverse Tradeoff

assumptions_latex: All compared encodings represent the same source semantics on the same instances.
The size and auxiliary-variable conventions are identical across encodings.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pareto efficiency is relative to the declared comparison class, instance set, and dominance quantifier.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pareto comparison of encoding size and auxiliary-variable use.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_E(P)=(S_E(P),A_E(P))\). Encoding \(F\) dominates \(E\) on \(P\) if both coordinates of \(R_F(P)\) are no larger and at least one is smaller. Within a declared class \(\mathcal C\), \(E\) is Pareto-efficient on \(P\) if no \(F\in\mathcal C\) dominates it. For families, the comparison must state whether domination is pointwise for every instance, worst-case by input size, or eventual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A size–state tradeoff is a Pareto comparison under common semantics and counting conventions; efficiency is always relative to a declared competitor class and comparison rule.
knowledge_statements.title: Size–State Pareto Comparison

assumptions_latex: Two exact encodings are compared on the same instance family and under the same size conventions.
Smaller encoding size and fewer auxiliary variables are preferred.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An encoding is Pareto-efficient when no exact competitor is no worse in both \(S\) and \(A\) and strictly better in at least one.

notation.meaning: pair of size and auxiliary-state costs

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Pareto dominance gives a checkable two-resource tradeoff criterion
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pareto comparison of explicit CNF size and introduced auxiliary state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Associate with each exact encoding \(E\) of instance \(P\) the resource pair
\[
R_E(P)=(S_E(P),A_E(P)).
\]
Encoding \(F\) dominates \(E\) on \(P\) when \(S_F(P)\le S_E(P)\) and \(A_F(P)\le A_E(P)\), with at least one strict inequality. Encoding \(E\) is Pareto-efficient within a declared class \(\mathcal C\) when no \(F\in\mathcal C\) dominates it. A claimed size–state tradeoff must therefore identify the encoding class, instance family, and size convention; exactness alone does not impose a universal inverse relation between the two resources.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Size–state tradeoffs are Pareto comparisons: an encoding is efficient when no exact competitor uses no more of both resources and less of one.
knowledge_statements.title: Size–State Tradeoffs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Pareto criterion is mathematically precise and the property kind is defensible, but the size–state tradeoff framework lacks an inspectable source in the pseudo-Boolean encoding context.

children.title: Asymptotic Growth Regimes
children.top_down_role: Encoding-resource behavior as instance dimensions increase.

knowledge_statements.title: Asymptotic Growth Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic classification of CNF size and auxiliary-state resources.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix an instance family \(\mathcal P_N\), a scalar input-size parameter \(N\), and a resource \(R_E(N)\in\{S_E^{\max}(N),A_E^{\max}(N)\}\). The labels constant, logarithmic, linear, degree-\(k\) polynomial, and exponential mean, respectively,
\[
R_E(N)=O(1),\qquad R_E(N)=\Theta(\log N),\qquad R_E(N)=\Theta(N),\qquad R_E(N)=\Theta(N^k),\qquad R_E(N)=2^{\Theta(N)},
\]
where \(k>1\) is fixed. These labels are not exhaustive. If \(N\) is binary input length and a resource bound is polynomial in a numerical magnitude \(U(P)\) that may be exponential in \(N\), the bound is pseudopolynomial in the encoded input rather than polynomial in \(N\). Every regime claim must identify the resource and its counting convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Growth regimes give exact asymptotic orders for a declared resource and input parameter; a bound polynomial in numerical values can still be pseudopolynomial in binary input length.
assumptions_latex: An instance family \(\mathcal P_N\) and scalar input-size parameter \(N\) are fixed.
The worst-case resource functions are finite for every \(N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Constant, logarithmic, linear, fixed-degree polynomial, exponential, and pseudopolynomial descriptions are meaningful only relative to the declared resource, parameter, and numerical encoding convention.

notation.meaning: largest relevant numerical magnitude in the instance

assumptions_latex: \(R(N)>0\) eventually and the input parameter \(N\) is fixed across comparisons.
Logarithm bases are fixed constants greater than one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The polynomial, quasipolynomial, superpolynomial, and subexponential labels are well defined relative to \(N\), but overlap unless an exact-order or exclusivity condition is stated.

notation.meaning: declared nonnegative encoding resource as a function of input size

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Broad asymptotic classes supplementing the exact-order regimes in the immutable seed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A resource is polynomially bounded if \(R(N)=O(N^k)\) for some fixed \(k\), quasipolynomially bounded if \(R(N)=\exp((\log N)^{O(1)})\), superpolynomial if \(R(N)/N^k\to\infty\) for every fixed \(k\), and subexponential if \(\log R(N)=o(N)\). These are broad classes rather than mutually exclusive exact orders: polynomial bounds are quasipolynomial and subexponential, while a function can be both superpolynomial and subexponential.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polynomial, quasipolynomial, superpolynomial, and subexponential are broad, overlapping growth classes defined relative to a declared input parameter.
knowledge_statements.title: Broad Asymptotic Classes

children.title: Propagation Strength
children.top_down_role: Deductive power exposed by an encoding to the underlying solver.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation between projection equivalence and propagation equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E_1=(x)\) and \(E_2=(x\vee y)\land(x\vee\neg y)\). Although \(\exists y\,E_2\equiv E_1\), unit propagation under the empty input assignment derives \(x\) from \(E_1\) and no input literal from \(E_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A unit clause and an auxiliary two-clause encoding have the same input solutions but different propagation strength.
assumptions_latex: Auxiliary variable \(y\) is existentially projected.
Propagation is compared on input variable \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E_1\succ_{\mathrm{UP}}E_2\).
knowledge_statements.title: Semantic Equivalence Without Propagation Equivalence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Precise input-relative propagation comparison including contradiction outcomes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an encoding \(E\) and partial input assignment \(\alpha\), let \(O_E(\alpha)=\bot\) if unit propagation refutes \(E\land\alpha\), and otherwise let \(O_E(\alpha)\) be the set of propagated input literals. Define \(E_1\succeq_{\mathrm{UP}}E_2\) when, for every \(\alpha\), (i) \(O_{E_2}(\alpha)=\bot\) implies \(O_{E_1}(\alpha)=\bot\), and (ii) if \(O_{E_2}(\alpha)\ne\bot\), then either \(O_{E_1}(\alpha)=\bot\) or \(O_{E_2}(\alpha)\subseteq O_{E_1}(\alpha)\). This relation is reflexive and transitive; mutual domination defines propagation equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One encoding is at least as propagation-strong as another if it preserves every refutation and every propagated input literal under every partial input assignment.
assumptions_latex: The encodings are projection-correct for the same constraint on the same input variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\succeq_{\mathrm{UP}}\) is a preorder and mutual domination is an equivalence relation.

notation.meaning: Contradiction or the input literals derived by unit propagation.

knowledge_statements.title: Contradiction-Aware Unit-Propagation Preorder

assumptions_latex: \(E_1(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y}_1)\) and \(E_2(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y}_2)\) encode the same Boolean constraint on input variables \(\mathbf{x}\).
Unit propagation is applied after any partial assignment \(\alpha\) to \(\mathbf{x}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E_1\succeq_{\mathrm{UP}}E_2\) exactly when every input consequence propagated by \(E_2\) is also propagated by \(E_1\).

notation.meaning: Set of input literals derived by unit propagation

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard unit-propagation preorder for comparing Boolean encodings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compares encodings only through unit-propagated consequences on original input variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For encodings \(E_1\) and \(E_2\), define \(E_1\succeq_{\mathrm{UP}}E_2\) if, for every partial input assignment \(\alpha\), either unit propagation on \(E_1\land\alpha\) derives contradiction, or
\[
\operatorname{UP}_{\mathbf{x}}(E_2\land\alpha)\subseteq \operatorname{UP}_{\mathbf{x}}(E_1\land\alpha).
\]
Contradiction is treated as stronger than every consistent set of propagated literals. Encodings are propagation-equivalent when both preorder directions hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One encoding is at least as propagation-strong as another when unit propagation derives every input consequence the other derives under every partial input assignment.
knowledge_statements.title: Propagation Strength

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the Propagation Strength leaf and the definition content kind, but it has no inspectable citation. Its treatment of contradiction is also incomplete: the displayed inclusion does not explicitly require E1 to refute whenever E2 refutes, so the intended preorder cannot be validated as stated without an authoritative source and a precise convention for UP on inconsistent formulas.

children.title: Consistency Preservation
children.top_down_role: Retention of relevant consistency behavior under translation.

assumptions_latex: \(C(\mathbf{x})\) is a Boolean constraint and \(E(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y})\) is its encoding.
\(\alpha\) ranges over partial assignments to the input variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The encoding preserves consistency when unit propagation detects every partial input assignment having no extension satisfying \(C\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard unit-refutation consistency condition for constraint encodings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses consistency preservation in the unit-refutation sense under partial assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The encoding \(E(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y})\) preserves consistency for \(C(\mathbf{x})\) when it is projection-correct,
\[
C(\mathbf{x})\iff \exists\mathbf{y}\,E(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y}),
\]
and, for every partial assignment \(\alpha\) to \(\mathbf{x}\),
\[
C\land\alpha\text{ is unsatisfiable}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \operatorname{UP}(E\land\alpha)=\bot.
\]
Thus unit propagation recognizes every inconsistent input domain represented by \(\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A projection-correct encoding preserves consistency if unit propagation refutes every partial input assignment that cannot extend to a solution of the original constraint.
knowledge_statements.title: Consistency Preservation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition matches consistency preservation in the unit-refutation sense, introduces the relevant variables, and uses an appropriate condition content kind. No source reference or section-level locator is supplied, so the precise terminology and equivalence to the intended local consistency regime require authoritative support.

children.title: Propagation-Completeness Regimes
children.top_down_role: Encoding classes differentiated by the completeness of solver-visible propagation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict separation of input-relative propagation completeness from unit-refutation completeness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every input-relative PC encoding is URC. Conversely, \(E=(x\vee y)\land(x\vee\neg y)\) projection-encodes \(C(x)=x\). Under \(x=0\), unit propagation derives a contradiction, so every inconsistent input restriction is refuted. Under the empty assignment, however, \(C\models x\) while unit propagation on \(E\) does not derive \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Propagation completeness strictly strengthens unit-refutation completeness.
assumptions_latex: Auxiliary variables are existentially projected.
URC and PC are interpreted relative to partial assignments and consequences on input variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathrm{PC}\subsetneq\mathrm{URC}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Strict Input-Relative URC-PC Hierarchy

assumptions_latex: \(E(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y})\) projection-encodes a Boolean constraint \(C(\mathbf{x})\).
\(\alpha\) is any partial assignment to \(\mathbf{x}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Unit-refutation completeness detects inconsistency; propagation completeness additionally derives every forced input literal.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard distinction between unit-refutation and propagation completeness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates contradiction detection from complete propagation of forced input literals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The encoding is in the \(\mathrm{URC}\) regime if \(C\land\alpha\) unsatisfiable implies \(\operatorname{UP}(E\land\alpha)=\bot\). It is in the \(\mathrm{PC}\) regime if it is \(\mathrm{URC}\) and, for every unassigned input literal \(\ell\),
\[
C\land\alpha\models\ell\quad\Longrightarrow\quad E\land\alpha\vdash_{\mathrm{UP}}\ell.
\]
Hence \(\mathrm{PC}\) preserves all forced input literals, whereas \(\mathrm{URC}\) preserves only inconsistency detection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unit-refutation completeness detects every impossible partial assignment; propagation completeness also derives every input literal forced by the constraint under that assignment.
knowledge_statements.title: Propagation-Completeness Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition cleanly distinguishes unit-refutation completeness from propagation of forced input literals and fits the leaf and definition content kind. Because propagation completeness is variously defined over input variables or all encoding variables, the input-relative scope must be supported by a specific source; none is cited.

children.title: Strength–Size Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Relationships between propagation quality and representation growth.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalable witness that added clauses can strengthen propagation without changing projected semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(C_n=\bigwedge_{i=1}^n x_i\), let \(E_s^{(n)}=\bigwedge_i[(x_i\vee y_i)\land(x_i\vee\neg y_i)]\) and \(E_t^{(n)}=E_s^{(n)}\land\bigwedge_i(x_i)\). Both project to \(C_n\). The first has \(2n\) clauses and propagates no \(x_i\) from the empty assignment; the second has \(3n\) clauses and propagates every \(x_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear family of redundant unit clauses preserves semantics while turning a propagation-weak encoding into a propagation-complete one.
assumptions_latex: Size is measured by clause and literal-occurrence counts.
Auxiliary variables are existentially projected.
knowledge_statements.title: Scalable Size-Strength Separation

assumptions_latex: Encoding size is measured by the number of clauses plus literal occurrences.
Strength is compared by the unit-propagation preorder on a fixed input constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A smaller encoding need not retain the propagation consequences of a larger encoding; size and propagation strength are separate comparison coordinates.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: auxiliary clauses and variables can increase propagation while increasing encoding size
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the qualitative boundary only; no universal quantitative lower bound is asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For projection-correct encodings \(E_s\) and \(E_t\) of the same constraint, the inequality \(|E_s|<|E_t|\) does not imply \(E_s\succeq_{\mathrm{UP}}E_t\). Removing auxiliary definitions or redundant clauses may preserve
\[
\exists\mathbf{y}_s\,E_s\iff\exists\mathbf{y}_t\,E_t
\]
while eliminating unit-propagation derivations. Consequently, minimization of encoding size alone does not preserve \(\mathrm{URC}\) or \(\mathrm{PC}\); those properties must be checked independently.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Logical equivalence can survive clause removal while propagation weakens, so minimizing an encoding does not by itself preserve unit-refutation or propagation completeness.
knowledge_statements.title: Strength–Size Tradeoffs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The qualitative non-implication belongs in Strength–Size Tradeoffs, and failure_boundary is suitable. However, the claim that smaller projection-equivalent encodings need not preserve propagation strength or URC/PC is a nontrivial failure claim requiring a cited construction, counterexample, or theorem; none is provided.

children.title: Incremental Bound Encodings
children.top_down_role: Encodings supporting changes to optimization or feasibility bounds over time.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Activation-gated append-only incremental encoding model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A bound-specific clause \(D\) may be appended permanently as \((\neg a_k\vee D)\), while the current query assumes \(a_k\). Releasing \(a_k\) disables that batch without deleting it. For each bound, the persistent core together with its activation assumptions must project exactly to \(f(\mathbf{x})\le k\). Making \(a_k\) a permanent unit is sound only when every later query implies that bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Guarded clauses support reversible bound updates; permanent activation is valid only when every later query implies the activated bound.
assumptions_latex: Each bound-specific batch is guarded by a fresh activation literal.
Activation literals are controlled by call assumptions and otherwise do not constrain the input semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists\mathbf y,\mathbf a\,[F\land A_k]\iff f(\mathbf x)\le k\) for every represented bound \(k\).

notation.meaning: Activation literal for a bound-specific clause batch.

knowledge_statements.title: Activation-Gated Append-Only Bound Updates

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Output-literal interface for selecting upper bounds from one persistent encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a shared CNF \(F(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y},\mathbf{o})\) expose outputs satisfying, under projection, \(o_j\leftrightarrow[f(\mathbf{x})\ge j]\). Then the temporary assumption \(\neg o_{k+1}\) selects exactly the query \(f(\mathbf{x})\le k\). Replacing the assumption changes the represented bound without changing the persistent core.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reusable threshold output selects an upper bound by assuming that the next threshold is false.
assumptions_latex: The persistent core gives the stated projection-equivalent threshold outputs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists\mathbf y,\mathbf o\,[F\land\neg o_{k+1}]\iff f(\mathbf x)\le k\).

notation.meaning: Output literal indicating that the value reaches threshold \(j\).

knowledge_statements.title: Threshold-Output Incremental Bound Interface

assumptions_latex: \(f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb{Z}\) and admissible bounds belong to a finite ordered set \(K\).
Each bound is selected through assumptions over designated interface literals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: One persistent clause database represents all bounds, and changing assumptions selects the required inequality without rebuilding the shared encoding.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard assumption-controlled incremental SAT encoding of bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covers assumption-controlled incremental encodings of finite integer bound families.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An incremental bound encoding for \(f(\mathbf{x})\le k\), with \(k\in K\), is a shared formula \(F(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y},\mathbf{b})\) and assumption sets \(A_k\) such that, for every input assignment \(a\),
\[
f(a)\le k\iff \exists\mathbf{y},\mathbf{b}\;F(a,\mathbf{y},\mathbf{b})\land A_k.
\]
The clauses of \(F\) persist between solver calls; updating the bound changes only \(A_k\), or appends clauses that do not invalidate earlier clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An incremental encoding keeps one shared formula and selects each bound using temporary assumptions or append-only clauses, while preserving the inequality's solutions under projection.
knowledge_statements.title: Incremental Bound Encodings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits Incremental Bound Encodings, and the projection equation formalizes assumption-selected bounds.
