The record then also permits append-only clause updates, which are not represented by the fixed formula and assumption-set equation. A source is needed to determine the intended incremental model and its exact semantic contract.

children.title: Reusable Bound Encodings
children.top_down_role: Encoding structures shared across multiple related bound queries.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Construction-independent interface for selecting cardinality bounds from one persistent threshold formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(0\le U<n\), \(F\land\neg y_{U+1}\) represents \(\sum_i x_i\le U\). For \(1\le L\le n\), \(F\land y_L\) represents \(\sum_i x_i\ge L\). For \(1\le L\le U<n\), \(F\land y_L\land\neg y_{U+1}\) represents \(L\le\sum_i x_i\le U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Threshold outputs form a reusable interface: unit assumptions select upper, lower, or interval bounds without rebuilding the persistent formula.
assumptions_latex: Every input assignment has an extension satisfying \(F\).
\(F\models\left(y_j\leftrightarrow\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\ge j\right)\) for \(1\le j\le n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\land\neg y_{U+1},\quad F\land y_L,\quad F\land y_L\land\neg y_{U+1}
knowledge_statements.title: Reusable Threshold Interface

assumptions_latex: \(F\) encodes every bound in a prescribed set \(K\) through interface assumptions.
Auxiliary variables have no meaning outside existential projection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The same formula is reusable exactly when each bound has a projection-correct interface assignment over the shared database.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: projection-correct selector interface formalizes reusable bound encodings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines reuse semantically, independently of a particular cardinality or pseudo-Boolean construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A bound encoding \(F(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y},\mathbf{b})\) is reusable over \(K\) if every \(k\in K\) has a consistent interface assumption set \(A_k\) satisfying
\[
\{a\in\{0,1\}^n:f(a)\le k\}=\{a:\exists\mathbf{y},\mathbf{b}\;F(a,\mathbf{y},\mathbf{b})\land A_k\}.
\]
Reuse requires no deletion or weakening of clauses in \(F\); learned clauses valid for \(F\) remain valid, while bound-specific literals are supplied as assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bound encoding is reusable when every supported bound is selected by a projection-correct interface assignment over one persistent formula without deleting or weakening clauses.
knowledge_statements.title: Reusable Bound Encodings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The semantic definition fits Reusable Bound Encodings and its definition content kind. The projection-correct selector interface and claims about persistent learned clauses have no cited source or inspectable locator, so this candidate cannot pass source review.

children.title: Monotone Bound Sequences
children.top_down_role: Reuse behavior for progressively tightening or relaxing bounds.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-way transfer of feasibility information along nested upper-bound queries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(f(\mathbf{x})\le k\) is UNSAT, then every tighter query with \(k'\le k\) is UNSAT. A witness satisfying a tighter bound also satisfies every relaxed bound, but satisfiability of a relaxed bound does not imply satisfiability of a tighter one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: UNSAT transfers to tighter upper bounds, while a tighter-bound witness transfers to relaxations.
assumptions_latex: All queries use upper bounds on the same function.
Solver answers and returned witnesses are sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_k=\varnothing\land k'\le k\Rightarrow S_{k'}=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.title: Monotone Feasibility-Certificate Transfer

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combinatorial update bound for finite monotone bound sequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A strictly increasing or decreasing sequence drawn from a finite totally ordered set \(K\) contains at most \(|K|\) queries and at most \(|K|-1\) strict updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strict monotone sequence over a finite bound set makes at most one fewer updates than there are admissible bounds.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is finite and totally ordered.
Every update changes the bound strictly in one fixed direction.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Monotone Update Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Append-only semantics for a monotonically tightening upper-bound sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(k_0\ge k_1\ge\cdots\ge k_t\) and each \(B_{k_j}\) exactly encodes \(f(\mathbf{x})\le k_j\), then, provided their auxiliary extensions are compatible, \(\bigwedge_{j=0}^tB_{k_j}\) has the same projected input solutions as \(B_{k_t}\). Thus exact tightening clauses may remain permanently, whereas this permanence is generally invalid after increasing the bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Along a tightening sequence, retaining compatible earlier exact bounds is projection-equivalent to retaining the current tightest bound.
assumptions_latex: The sequence satisfies \(k_{t+1}\le k_t\).
The bound encodings use disjoint auxiliary variables or guarantee a common auxiliary extension whenever the tightest bound holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_{\mathbf x}(\bigwedge_{j=0}^tB_{k_j})=\{\mathbf x:f(\mathbf x)\le k_t\}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Append-Only Tightening Equivalence

assumptions_latex: \(k_0,k_1,\ldots,k_T\) are bounds for constraints \(f(\mathbf{x})\le k_t\).
All inequalities use the same integer-valued function \(f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Decreasing bounds yield nested feasible sets, while increasing bounds yield reverse nesting.

notation.meaning: Feasible input set at bound k

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: elementary nesting property of scalar upper-bound constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Records the nesting property that enables append-only tightening and assumption-based relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
S_k=\{\mathbf{x}\in\{0,1\}^n:f(\mathbf{x})\le k\}.
\]
If \(k_{t+1}\le k_t\), then \(S_{k_{t+1}}\subseteq S_{k_t}\); hence a tightening sequence produces nested feasible sets. If \(k_{t+1}\ge k_t\), then \(S_{k_t}\subseteq S_{k_{t+1}}\). A permanent clause encoding a tighter bound is therefore sound for later tighter bounds, but generally not for a later relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Upper-bound feasible sets are nested: decreasing bounds shrink them and increasing bounds enlarge them, determining when permanent tightening clauses can remain valid.
knowledge_statements.title: Monotone Bound Sequences

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The nesting statement is mathematically precise, agrees between plain text and LaTeX, and property is the correct content kind. Nevertheless, the record supplies no citation for its encoding-reuse consequence, and standard-field rationale alone does not satisfy the required citation check.

children.title: Nonmonotone Reuse Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits on reuse when successive bound changes do not follow one direction.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical boundary for retaining learned consequences across arbitrary changes of bound assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(F\land A\models C\), then \(F\models(A\rightarrow C)\). The clause \(C\) is sound under every later assumption set precisely when \(F\models C\); otherwise its sound persistent form is the guarded clause \(A\rightarrow C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A consequence learned under bound assumptions is unconditionally reusable only when the persistent core entails it; otherwise it must remain guarded by those assumptions.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is the persistent clause database.
\(A\) is the conjunction of query-local bound assumptions.
\(C\) is derived soundly from \(F\land A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\models C\quad\text{or, conditionally,}\quad F\models(A\rightarrow C).
knowledge_statements.title: Guarded-Lemma Reuse Criterion

assumptions_latex: A solver permanently adds clauses encoding \(f(\mathbf{x})\le k_t\).
A later bound \(k_{t+1}>k_t\) is intended to relax the constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Permanent clauses for the tighter bound cannot generally be reused for the relaxation; selector guarding or database reconstruction is required.

notation.meaning: Feasible input set for bound k

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: permanent strengthening excludes assignments restored by a later relaxed bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies relaxation after permanent tightening as the principal nonmonotone reuse failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(k_{t+1}>k_t\) and there exists an input \(a\) with
\[
k_t<f(a)\le k_{t+1}.
\]
Then \(a\notin S_{k_t}\) but \(a\in S_{k_{t+1}}\). Any unguarded permanent clauses whose projection enforces \(S_{k_t}\) still exclude \(a\), so retaining them cannot correctly represent the relaxed bound. Correct nonmonotone reuse must guard bound-specific clauses by selectors, use retractable assumptions, or rebuild the affected database.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After permanent tightening, a later relaxation may restore assignments already excluded by retained clauses; selectors, temporary assumptions, or rebuilding are then necessary.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonmonotone Reuse Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The witness condition correctly identifies the failure of retaining an unguarded tighter-bound encoding during relaxation, and failure_boundary fits the leaf. The necessity and listed remedies are unsupported by any inspectable source, so authoritative sourcing is required.

children.title: Proof-Producing Encodings
children.top_down_role: Encodings equipped to emit evidence supporting translation or solving claims.

assumptions_latex: A certificate language \(\mathcal L\), verifier \(V\), and certified relation \(\mathcal R\) are fixed independently of each translator run.
All source, target, projection, and objective data needed by \(\mathcal R\) are explicit verifier inputs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The translator is proof-producing for \(\mathcal R\) when every output includes evidence accepted under independently specified rules whose soundness establishes \(\mathcal R\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate-emitting translation relative to an independently specified checker judgment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A translation procedure is proof-producing for a declared relation \(\mathcal R\) if it returns \(T(I)=(F_I,\pi_I)\), where \(\pi_I\) belongs to a fixed certificate language and \(V(I,F_I,\pi_I)=1\). The verifier rules must be defined independently of the assertion being certified and be sound in the sense that acceptance implies \(\mathcal R(I,F_I)\). The relation may concern projection correctness, objective preservation, or a stated solver claim, but the chosen claim must be explicit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proof-producing translator emits an encoding and a certificate accepted by an independently defined sound verifier for a declared translation or solving relation.
knowledge_statements.title: Proof-Producing Translation

assumptions_latex: A target solver certificate establishes only its declared property of the target formula.
No checked source-to-target fidelity certificate is included.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A solver certificate for \(F_I\) does not alone certify that \(F_I\) faithfully encodes \(I\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates evidence about the target instance from evidence about the translation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A valid satisfiability witness, refutation, bound certificate, or optimality certificate for \(F_I\) establishes a claim about \(F_I\). Without a separately checked relation connecting \(F_I\) to \(I\), it does not establish projection correctness or objective fidelity of the translation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid target solver certificate does not by itself certify that the target formula faithfully represents the source instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Solver Evidence Is Not Translation Evidence
knowledge_statements.title: Solver Evidence Is Not Translation Evidence

assumptions_latex: \(T\) translates a source constraint instance \(I\) into a Boolean formula \(F_I\).
\(V\) is a deterministic checker for translation certificates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Accepted certificates establish projection correctness of the emitted encoding, making translation correctness independently checkable.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: proof-producing translation pairs an encoding with a checkable projection-correctness witness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Treats proof production as certification of translation correctness, not merely solver unsatisfiability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A proof-producing encoding procedure returns \(T(I)=(F_I,\pi_I)\), where \(F_I(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y})\) is the encoding and \(\pi_I\) is accepted by \(V\) only if it certifies
\[
I(\mathbf{x})\iff\exists\mathbf{y}\,F_I(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y}).
\]
For optimization bounds, the certified equivalence applies separately to each represented bound. The certificate format must expose every translation step needed by \(V\), and acceptance must depend only on \(I\), \(F_I\), and \(\pi_I\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proof-producing translator emits both an encoding and a certificate whose independent checker establishes that projection of the encoding equals the source constraint.
knowledge_statements.title: Proof-Producing Encodings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Certificate is an appropriate content kind for Proof-Producing Encodings, but the proposed certificate is defined only through the semantic property it is supposed to establish. No certificate calculus, checker contract, or authoritative source is identified, making the mathematical notion and its checkability unreliable as stated.

children.title: Proof-Friendly Encodings
children.top_down_role: Encodings structured for compatibility with proof logging and checking.

assumptions_latex: The encoding translation is semantically correct for the source instances.
No efficient proof transformation is assumed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Semantic correctness is necessary for the intended correspondence but is insufficient to establish proof friendliness.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between semantic preservation and efficient proof simulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Equisatisfiability or projection correctness of \(T(I)\) does not by itself provide an effective proof translation or a polynomial bound on target proofs. Therefore proof friendliness cannot be inferred solely from semantic correctness; it must be established for the selected proof systems and judgment class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A semantically faithful encoding need not preserve short proofs, so semantic correctness alone does not make an encoding proof-friendly.
knowledge_statements.title: Semantic Correctness Is Insufficient

assumptions_latex: \(P_s\) and \(P_t\) are fixed proof systems with fixed proof encodings.
The instance translation \(T\) specifies the target judgment corresponding to each source judgment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Proof friendliness is polynomial simulation through the encoding relative to the declared proof systems and judgment class.

notation.meaning: source proof and translated target proof

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polynomial proof simulation as a parameterized compatibility criterion for an encoding family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An encoding family \(T\) is proof-friendly from \(P_s\) to \(P_t\) for a declared class of judgments if an effective transformation maps every \(P_s\)-proof \(\pi\) of a source judgment about \(I\) to a \(P_t\)-proof \(\widehat\pi\) of the corresponding judgment about \(T(I)\), with \(|\widehat\pi|\le p(|I|+|\pi|)\) for one fixed polynomial \(p\). Refutation friendliness is the restricted variant in which the declared judgments are unsatisfiability claims and both proofs are refutations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An encoding is proof-friendly only relative to fixed source and target proof systems when source proofs can be effectively translated into corresponding target proofs with polynomial size overhead.
knowledge_statements.title: Proof-System-Relative Friendliness

assumptions_latex: \(P_s\) and \(P_t\) are fixed source and target proof systems.
\(T(I)=F_I\) is projection-correct.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Proof friendliness means source proofs can be translated into target proofs with controlled polynomial overhead.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: polynomial proof simulation is a standard formalization of proof-friendly translation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses polynomial proof simulation as the precise proof-friendliness criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The encoding family \(T\) is proof-friendly from \(P_s\) to \(P_t\) if there is a polynomial \(p\) and an effective transformation such that every \(P_s\)-derivation \(\pi\) for an instance \(I\) yields a \(P_t\)-derivation \(\widehat{\pi}\) for \(F_I=T(I)\) with
\[
|\widehat{\pi}|\le p(|I|+|\pi|).
\]
If this condition is required only for refutations, both \(I\) and \(F_I\) must be unsatisfiable and \(\widehat{\pi}\) must refute \(F_I\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An encoding is proof-friendly when source derivations can be transformed effectively into target derivations with polynomially bounded proof-size overhead.
knowledge_statements.title: Proof-Friendly Encodings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The polynomial-simulation property is a plausible exact role for Proof-Friendly Encodings, and property is suitable. The source and target proof systems, the conclusions preserved by the transformation, and the relevant simulation convention are left abstract without a citation, so the stated criterion cannot be validated.

children.title: Translation-Certificate Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Boundaries between encoding transformations and certificate-producing solver pipelines.

assumptions_latex: The formats of \(I\), \(F\), \(\rho\), and \(\pi\) are fixed and machine-readable.
The deterministic verifier terminates on every well-formed or malformed proposed input.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The interface is sound when acceptance implies the declared semantic relation and complete only relative to its admitted certificate language and translation family.

notation.meaning: declared target-to-source assignment or value map
declared semantic relation between source and target

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Machine-checkable contract between a translator and an independent certificate verifier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A translation-certificate interface accepts a tuple \((I,F,\rho,\pi)\) and returns a deterministic judgment \(V(I,F,\rho,\pi)\). For a declared semantic relation \(\mathcal R(I,F,\rho)\), soundness means \(V=1\Rightarrow\mathcal R\). Completeness for a declared translation family and certificate language means \(\mathcal R(I,F,\rho)\Rightarrow\exists\pi\,V(I,F,\rho,\pi)=1\) for tuples in that family. If optimization data are translated, \(\mathcal R\) must state objective-value or bound preservation separately from feasibility projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A translation-certificate interface fixes all data formats and a terminating verifier; acceptance must soundly imply the declared source-target relation, while completeness is relative to a certificate language and translation family.
knowledge_statements.title: Translation-Certificate Contract

assumptions_latex: Soundness is interpreted only as absence of false accepted judgments.
Completeness requires certificates for all correct translations in a declared family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Soundness alone provides no completeness guarantee.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp logical separation between interface soundness and completeness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The verifier that rejects every proposed certificate is sound because it accepts no incorrect translation, but it is incomplete whenever the declared family contains a correct translation. Hence soundness does not imply completeness, and completeness must be evaluated relative to the admitted certificate language.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A checker that rejects everything is sound but generally incomplete, so soundness and completeness are independent interface requirements.
knowledge_statements.title: Soundness Does Not Imply Completeness

assumptions_latex: The source instance, emitted formula, and variable projection map have fixed machine-readable formats.
The verifier is deterministic and terminates on every proposed certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The interface is sound when verifier acceptance implies projection correctness, and complete when every correct translation admits an accepted certificate.

notation.meaning: Map from target assignments to source assignments

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: soundness and completeness specify a checkable translation-certificate interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specifies the semantic contract between a translator and an independent certificate checker.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A translation-certificate interface accepts tuples \((I,F,\rho,\pi)\). It is sound if
\[
V(I,F,\rho,\pi)=1\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \forall a\;\bigl(I(a)\iff\exists b\,[F(b)\land\rho(b)=a]\bigr).
\]
It is complete for a translation family when every correctly translated tuple \((I,F,\rho)\) has some certificate \(\pi\) accepted by \(V\). Verification time and certificate length are measured separately from the time used to construct \(F\) and \(\pi\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A translation-certificate interface is sound if acceptance guarantees projection correctness, and complete if every correct translation has an accepted certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Translation-Certificate Interfaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The soundness/completeness interface fits Translation-Certificate Interfaces and the certificate content kind. No certificate language or source with a specific locator is supplied, and completeness for every semantically correct translation can depend strongly on the allowed certificate system; sourcing is therefore necessary.

children.title: Proof-Overhead Regimes
children.top_down_role: Representation and checking costs associated with proof support.

assumptions_latex: Source instances, formulas, and certificates use fixed finite encodings.
Generation and verification times use a declared deterministic computation model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Proof overhead is a resource vector; a polynomial or linear claim must identify its coordinates, baseline, and aggregation convention.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinatewise classification of representation, generation, and checking overhead caused by proof support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For output \((F_I,\pi_I)\), record \(H(I)=(H_f,H_s,H_g,H_v)=(|F_I|,|\pi_I|,\operatorname{time}_{\rm gen}(I),\operatorname{time}_V(I,F_I,\pi_I))\). Relative to a declared baseline \(B(I)\), a coordinate is output-linear when it is \(O(B(I))\), polynomial when it is \(B(I)^{O(1)}\), and superpolynomial when it is not bounded by any fixed polynomial in \(B(I)\). A family-level aggregate classification must state whether it uses a sum, maximum, or separate coordinatewise bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proof overhead is a vector containing encoding length, certificate length, generation time, and verification time; every asymptotic claim must identify its baseline and aggregation rule.
knowledge_statements.title: Proof-Overhead Resource Vector

assumptions_latex: Certificate length and verifier time are measured under fixed but potentially different resource conventions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Neither certificate length nor local inference cost alone determines total verification overhead.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Prevents one proof-overhead coordinate from being used as a proxy for all others.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A short certificate may invoke checks whose computation is expensive, while a long certificate may consist of individually cheap steps. Thus certificate length and verification time require separate bounds. Under a sequential explicit-input model that reads the whole certificate, \(H_v(I)=\Omega(H_s(I))\); this lower bound need not apply unchanged to random-access, streamed, or partially inspected interfaces unless their access costs are declared.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Short certificates can be expensive to check and long certificates can have cheap steps, so proof length and verification time are distinct overhead coordinates.
knowledge_statements.title: Independent Overhead Coordinates

assumptions_latex: \(|I|\), \(|F_I|\), and \(|\pi_I|\) use fixed symbol-count encodings.
Verifier time counts deterministic elementary computation steps.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Proof overhead is classified by certificate length and verification time relative to source and encoding size.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: certificate size and checking time are the standard proof-overhead resources
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classifies overhead without asserting that every encoding family achieves a polynomial regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a proof-producing translation \(T(I)=(F_I,\pi_I)\), define
\[
H_s(I)=|\pi_I|,
\qquad
H_v(I)=\operatorname{time}_V(I,F_I,\pi_I).
\]
The family has polynomial proof overhead when a polynomial \(p\) satisfies
\[
H_s(I)+H_v(I)\le p(|I|+|F_I|)
\]
for every \(I\). It has output-linear certificate overhead when \(H_s(I)=O(|I|+|F_I|)\). Superpolynomial certificate length or checking time places the family outside the polynomial-overhead regime under this measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proof overhead is measured by certificate length and verification time; polynomial overhead bounds their sum polynomially in the source instance and emitted encoding sizes.
knowledge_statements.title: Proof-Overhead Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record fits Proof-Overhead Regimes, and complexity_bound is appropriate for the stated asymptotic classifications. Its particular aggregate measure, including verifier time in the same polynomial bound as certificate length, is definitional rather than universally standard and has no supporting citation or locator.

children.title: Boolean Optimization Complexity Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Complexity classifications needed before interpreting exact, parameterized, or approximate solution guarantees.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming
top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Problems, algorithms, encoding size, P, NP, and co-NP
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Integer Programming
top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Complexity, problem reductions, optimization, and separation
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Integer Programming

assumptions_latex: Clause weights are positive integers encoded in binary.
Strong hardness is asserted with respect to the numerical clause-weight parameter.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Weighted general MaxSAT is strongly \(\mathsf{NP}\)-hard with respect to clause weights.}
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistence of exact weighted-MaxSAT hardness under the unit-weight restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Weighted general MaxSAT remains \(\mathsf{NP}\)-hard when every clause weight equals \(1\), since that restriction is unweighted general MaxSAT. Its exact optimization hardness is therefore strong with respect to clause-weight magnitudes: pseudo-polynomial dependence on the largest weight does not give a polynomial-time algorithm unless \(\mathsf P=\mathsf{NP}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted general MaxSAT is already NP-hard with unit weights, so large numerical weights are not the source of its exact hardness.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong NP-Hardness of Weighted General MaxSAT
knowledge_statements.title: Strong NP-Hardness of Weighted General MaxSAT

assumptions_latex: The input is a finite CNF formula \(F=C_1\land\cdots\land C_m\).
The threshold \(t\in\{0,\ldots,m\}\) is encoded in binary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The threshold problem is \(\mathsf{NP}\)-complete, and computing \(\operatorname{opt}(F)\) is \(\mathsf{NP}\)-hard.

notation.meaning: number of clauses of F satisfied by assignment x

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unweighted, unrestricted CNF MaxSAT under polynomial-time many-one reductions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a CNF formula \(F=C_1\land\cdots\land C_m\), define \(s_F(x)=|\{j:x\text{ satisfies }C_j\}|\) and \(\operatorname{opt}(F)=\max_{x\in\{0,1\}^n}s_F(x)\). The decision task asks whether \(\operatorname{opt}(F)\ge t\). It belongs to \(\mathsf{NP}\), because an assignment certifies the threshold, and it is \(\mathsf{NP}\)-hard by the special threshold \(t=m\), which asks whether \(F\) is satisfiable. Hence exact optimal-value computation is also \(\mathsf{NP}\)-hard.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: General MaxSAT threshold decision is NP-complete; exact optimal-value computation is NP-hard because SAT is the threshold case requiring every clause.
knowledge_statements.title: General MaxSAT Hardness Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The unrestricted MaxSAT hardness claims are mathematically standard and fit the hardness-regime container, but no inspectable citation is supplied.

children.title: Restricted-Language Classifications
children.top_down_role: Complexity regimes indexed by the permitted Boolean relation language.

assumptions_latex: \(\Gamma\) is a fixed finite set of Boolean relations.
Every constraint applies a relation from \(\Gamma\) to a tuple of variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The complexity classification assigns the resulting exact optimization or threshold problem to its polynomial-time or hardness regime as a function of \(\Gamma\).

notation.meaning: maximum number of satisfied constraints in instance I

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the fixed-language MaxSAT classification problem without asserting a particular clone-theoretic dichotomy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A restricted-language MaxSAT instance over \(\Gamma\) is a finite multiset \(I\) of constraints \(R(v_1,\ldots,v_r)\), where \(R\in\Gamma\) and the variables are Boolean. Its objective is \(\operatorname{opt}_{\Gamma}(I)=\max_{x}|\{c\in I:x\text{ satisfies }c\}|\). A restricted-language classification partitions fixed languages \(\Gamma\) according to the complexity of computing this value, producing an optimal assignment, or deciding whether \(\operatorname{opt}_{\Gamma}(I)\ge t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restricted-language classification fixes the allowed Boolean relations and classifies the resulting MaxSAT value, witness, or threshold task by complexity.
knowledge_statements.title: Restricted-Language Classifications

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is coherent and locally relevant, but its framing of restricted-language classification has no cited primary classification source.

children.title: Restricted-Arity Classifications
children.top_down_role: Complexity regimes indexed by clause-width bounds.

assumptions_latex: Instances are unweighted CNF formulas.
Clause width is bounded by a fixed integer \(k\ge 1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The threshold task is polynomial-time solvable for \(k=1\) and \(\mathsf{NP}\)-complete for every fixed \(k\ge 2\).

notation.meaning: maximum number of clauses of F simultaneously satisfied
fixed upper bound on clause width

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical unweighted bounded-width CNF MaxSAT classification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a CNF formula whose clauses have at most \(k\) literals, and ask whether \(\operatorname{opt}_k(F)\ge t\). For \(k=1\), each variable can be optimized independently by choosing the truth value satisfying the larger number of its positive or negative unit clauses, so the task is in \(\mathsf{P}\). For every fixed \(k\ge2\), the threshold task is \(\mathsf{NP}\)-complete; consequently, exact value and optimal-witness computation are \(\mathsf{NP}\)-hard.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unweighted Max-1-SAT is polynomial-time solvable, whereas the threshold version of Max-k-SAT is NP-complete for every fixed width at least two.
knowledge_statements.title: Restricted-Arity Classifications

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated Max-1-SAT versus fixed-width Max-k-SAT classification is standard and the content kind fits, but the NP-completeness claim lacks an inspectable citation.

children.title: Language–Arity Dichotomies
children.top_down_role: Classification boundaries produced by jointly varying language and arity.

assumptions_latex: \(\Gamma\) is a fixed finite Boolean constraint language of maximum arity \(k\).
Complexity is measured for the threshold problem under polynomial-time reductions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A dichotomy theorem must classify every pair \((\Gamma,k)\) into a tractable side or an \(\mathsf{NP}\)-complete side by an explicit structural criterion.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Schema for a joint language-and-arity dichotomy; the structural tractability criterion remains source-dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed \(\Gamma\) and \(k\), let \(\operatorname{MaxCSP}(\Gamma,k)\) maximize the number of satisfied constraints drawn from \(\Gamma\), with every constraint having arity at most \(k\). A language–arity dichotomy is a complete statement of the form: an explicit algebraic or relational predicate \(P(\Gamma,k)\) implies polynomial-time solvability, while failure of \(P(\Gamma,k)\) implies \(\mathsf{NP}\)-completeness of deciding whether the optimum is at least \(t\). The predicate and reduction model are essential parts of the theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A language–arity dichotomy needs an explicit structural predicate placing every fixed language and arity bound on either a tractable or NP-complete side.
knowledge_statements.title: Language–Arity Dichotomies

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This describes the form of a dichotomy but supplies neither the structural predicate nor an actual language–arity classification. A primary source is needed to determine the intended theorem.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed identification whose validity depends on the unresolved meaning of the arity restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the arity cap merely deletes relation symbols of arity greater than \(k\), define \(\Gamma_{\le k}=\{R\in\Gamma:\operatorname{arity}(R)\le k\}\); under that convention only, the admissible instances are those of \(\operatorname{MaxCSP}(\Gamma_{\le k})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An arity cap becomes sublanguage deletion only if arity restriction is explicitly defined as filtering relation symbols.
assumptions_latex: \Gamma\text{ is a finite Boolean relational language.}
k\in\mathbb N.
The cap filters relation symbols and does not instead bound clause width, scopes, occurrences, or implementations of relations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{MaxCSP}(\Gamma,k)=\operatorname{MaxCSP}(\Gamma_{\le k})\text{ only under the stated filtering convention}.

notation.meaning: relations in Γ whose declared arity is at most k

knowledge_statements.title: Proposed Arity-Truncated-Language Identification

intermediate_metadata.reason: The leaf lacks an identifiable dichotomy and even the arity semantics are materially ambiguous, so the proposed truncation claim is deferred. Pure fixed-language and width-only classifications, and transfer validity, remain excluded sibling scopes.

children.title: Classification Transfer Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits on transferring complexity classifications between restriction families.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equisatisfiability Does Not Preserve MaxSAT Value
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete failure of unchanged-value and unchanged-threshold transfer under mere equisatisfiability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=(x)\land(
eg x)\) and \(G=(x)\land(
eg x)\land(z\lor
eg z)\). Both are unsatisfiable and hence equisatisfiable, but \(\operatorname{opt}(F)=1\) and \(\operatorname{opt}(G)=2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equisatisfiable formulas can have different maximum satisfied-clause counts, so equisatisfiability alone preserves neither the MaxSAT value nor unchanged thresholds.
assumptions_latex: Each clause, including a tautological clause, contributes one unit to the unweighted MaxSAT objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{opt}(F)\ne\operatorname{opt}(G).

notation.meaning: maximum number of clauses of H simultaneously satisfied

knowledge_statements.title: Equisatisfiability Does Not Preserve MaxSAT Value

assumptions_latex: A reduction maps instances of one Boolean optimization family to another in polynomial time.
The reduction is intended to preserve a specified value, threshold, approximation, or witness relation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A classification transfers only when the reduction preserves the task feature on which the original classification is stated.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between valid complexity transfer and representation changes that destroy the classified task relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A complexity classification transfers through a polynomial-time instance map \(\rho\) only with the relevant preservation guarantee. For threshold decision, computable maps \(g_I\) must satisfy \(\operatorname{opt}_A(I)\ge t\iff\operatorname{opt}_B(\rho(I))\ge g_I(t)\). Exact-value transfer additionally requires a polynomial-time recoverable relation between \(\operatorname{opt}_A(I)\) and \(\operatorname{opt}_B(\rho(I))\); witness transfer requires polynomial-time decoding of target solutions. Equisatisfiability alone preserves only the all-constraints-satisfied threshold and does not justify transferring general MaxSAT value or approximation classifications.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A classification transfers only through reductions preserving its relevant thresholds, values, witnesses, or approximation gaps; mere equisatisfiability is insufficient for general MaxSAT.
knowledge_statements.title: Classification Transfer Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The preservation boundary is plausible and fits the failure-boundary container, but the asserted requirements for threshold, value, and witness transfer have no cited formal reduction framework.

children.title: Decision Complexity
children.top_down_role: Complexity of threshold or existence questions associated with MaxSAT optimization.

assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite CNF formula with \(m\) clauses.
\(t\in\{0,[1;1H[1;1H\ldots,m\}\) is a threshold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The decision language is \(\{(F,t):\operatorname{opt}(F)\ge t\}\), which is \(\mathsf{NP}\)-complete for unrestricted CNF.

notation.meaning: maximum number of clauses satisfiable by one assignment

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Threshold decision version of unweighted unrestricted MaxSAT.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The MaxSAT decision task maps \((F,t)\) to YES exactly when there exists \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\) satisfying at least \(t\) clauses, equivalently when \(\operatorname{opt}(F)\ge t\). A truth assignment is a polynomially checkable certificate, so the language lies in \(\mathsf{NP}\). Taking \(t=m\) yields CNF satisfiability, establishing \(\mathsf{NP}\)-hardness and hence \(\mathsf{NP}\)-completeness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: MaxSAT decision asks whether some assignment satisfies at least the threshold number of clauses; for unrestricted CNF it is NP-complete.
knowledge_statements.title: Decision Complexity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The NP-completeness argument is standard, but no citation is supplied and the threshold domain in assumptions_latex contains corrupted terminal-control text.

children.title: Optimal-Value Complexity
children.top_down_role: Complexity of determining the optimum objective value.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard function-complexity classification for the exact optimum count of unrestricted unweighted MaxSAT.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an unweighted CNF formula \(F\) with \(m\) clauses, \(V(F)=\operatorname{opt}(F)\) belongs to \(\mathsf{FP}^{\mathsf{NP}[O(\log m)]}\) by threshold binary search and is complete for \(\mathsf{FP}^{\mathsf{NP}[O(\log n)]}\) under standard polynomial-time metric reductions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The exact unweighted MaxSAT optimum is complete for polynomial-time function computation with logarithmically many NP-oracle queries.
assumptions_latex: F\text{ is an unrestricted unweighted CNF formula.}
n\text{ denotes the binary input length and }m\text{ its number of clauses.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: V\in\mathsf{FP}^{\mathsf{NP}[O(\log n)]}\text{ and is complete for this class under polynomial-time metric reductions}.

notation.meaning: exact maximum number of clauses of F simultaneously satisfied
polynomial-time functions using logarithmically many adaptive NP-oracle queries

knowledge_statements.title: Exact MaxSAT Value Function Complexity

assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite unweighted CNF formula with \(m\) clauses.
An oracle decides whether \(\operatorname{opt}(F)\ge t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The value \(\operatorname{opt}(F)\) is computable with \(O(\log(m+1))\) adaptive decision-oracle calls and polynomial additional work.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-value recovery from threshold decision for unweighted MaxSAT.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(L=0\) and \(U=m\). While \(L<U\), set \(q=\lceil(L+U+1)/2\rceil\) and query whether \(\operatorname{opt}(F)\ge q\). Set \(L=q\) after a YES answer and \(U=q-1\) after a NO answer. When the loop stops, output \(L\). Monotonicity of the threshold predicate gives \(L=\operatorname{opt}(F)\), and binary search uses \(O(\log(m+1))\) adaptive oracle queries.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary search over thresholds recovers the exact MaxSAT value using logarithmically many decision-oracle calls.
knowledge_statements.title: Optimal-Value Complexity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The binary-search oracle algorithm and query bound are correct and fit this container, but the function-complexity relation has no inspectable source.

children.title: Optimal-Witness Complexity
children.top_down_role: Complexity of producing an assignment attaining an optimum value.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates verification of an assignment's attained value from certification of global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an assignment \(x\), its attained count \(s_F(x)\) is computable in polynomial time. Writing \(v=s_F(x)\), the assignment is optimal exactly when \(D(F,v+1)=\mathrm{NO}\). Thus \(x\) alone certifies its attained value, but global optimality additionally requires a valid upper-bound or threshold-NO justification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An assignment efficiently certifies how many clauses it satisfies, but proving it globally optimal additionally requires evidence that no assignment satisfies more.
assumptions_latex: v=s_F(x).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x\text{ is optimal}\iff D(F,v+1)=\mathrm{NO}.

notation.meaning: number of clauses of F satisfied by assignment x
predicate that some assignment satisfies at least t clauses

knowledge_statements.title: Optimal-Witness Verification Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower bound for producing an optimal assignment of unrestricted unweighted MaxSAT.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If an oracle outputs an optimal assignment \(W(F)\) for every CNF formula \(F\) with \(m\) clauses, then satisfiability is decided by counting the clauses satisfied by \(W(F)\) and testing whether the count is \(m\). Hence optimal-witness production is \(\mathsf{NP}\)-hard under polynomial-time oracle reductions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Producing an optimal MaxSAT assignment is NP-hard because its attained clause count decides whether all clauses are simultaneously satisfiable.
assumptions_latex: F\text{ is an unrestricted unweighted CNF formula with }m\text{ clauses.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{SAT}\le_T^p W.

notation.meaning: an assignment attaining the maximum satisfied-clause count of F

knowledge_statements.title: NP-Hardness of Optimal-Witness Production

assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a CNF formula on \(n\) variables.
A threshold oracle is available for formulas obtained by fixing variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An optimal assignment can be recovered using \(O(\log(m+1)+n)\) adaptive threshold-oracle calls and polynomial additional work.

notation.meaning: partial assignment after fixing i variables

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Search-to-decision self-reduction for unrestricted unweighted CNF MaxSAT.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: First recover \(v=\operatorname{opt}(F)\) by threshold binary search. Starting with the empty partial assignment \(p_0\), process variables \(x_1,[1;1H[1;1H\ldots,x_n\). For each \(i\), query whether some completion of \(p_{i-1}\cup\{x_i=0\}\) satisfies at least \(v\) original clauses. If YES, choose that extension; otherwise choose \(p_i=p_{i-1}\cup\{x_i=1\}\). knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient Encoding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard explicit binary-versus-unary encoding convention for integer pseudo-Boolean data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an explicitly represented pseudo-Boolean inequality \(\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i\le b\), where \(x_i\in\{0,1\}\) and \(a_i,b\in\mathbb Z\), a sign bit together with a binary magnitude representation uses \(1+\lceil\log_2(|a|+1)\rceil\) bits for a signed integer \(a\), up to fixed delimiters. Unary magnitude encoding instead uses \(\Theta(|a|+1)\) symbols. Thus coefficient magnitudes contribute logarithmically to binary input length and linearly to unary input length.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary encoding measures an integer coefficient logarithmically in its magnitude, while unary encoding measures it linearly; this choice changes the formal input size.
assumptions_latex: All pseudo-Boolean coefficients and right-hand sides are integers.
The input explicitly lists every nonzero coefficient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Binary encoding contributes \(1+\lceil\log_2(|a|+1)\rceil\) bits per signed coefficient, whereas unary encoding contributes \(\Theta(|a|+1)\) symbols.

knowledge_statements.title: Weak Complexity Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak hardness associated with binary-encoded pseudo-Boolean numerical data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F\) be a family of pseudo-Boolean decision instances, let \(L(I)\) be the binary encoding length of \(I\in\mathcal F\), and let \(M(I)\) bound the absolute values of its integral coefficients and right-hand sides. knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complexity consequences of restricting pseudo-Boolean coefficients to unit weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A cardinality constraint has the form \(\sum_{i\in P}x_i+\sum_{j\in N}(1-x_j)\mathrel{\bowtie}k\), where \(x_i\in\{0,1\}\), \(\bowtie\in\{\leq,=,\geq\}\), and \(k\) is integral. Feasibility of a conjunction of such constraints belongs to NP. It is NP-complete without further structural restrictions: clauses are cardinality inequalities, since \(\ell_1\lor\cdots\lor\ell_r\) is equivalent to \(\sum_{t=1}^{r}\ell_t\geq1\). Thus unit coefficients remove numeric-magnitude complexity but do not by themselves remove combinatorial NP-hardness.

children.title: Restriction Collapse Regimes
children.top_down_role: Cases where cardinality and general pseudo-Boolean complexity distinctions disappear.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact same-variable normalization extending the seed’s common-sign case.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If every nonzero coefficient of \(\sum_i a_ix_i\geq b\) has the same absolute value \(c>0\), let \(N=\{i:a_i=-c\}\). Then \[\sum_i a_ix_i\geq b\iff \sum_{i:a_i=c}x_i+\sum_{i\in N}(1-x_i)\geq\left\lceil\frac{b+c|N|}{c}\right\rceil.\] Analogous threshold normalization applies to \(\leq\) and equality. Thus coefficients in \(\{-c,0,c\}\) give a cardinality constraint over literals without auxiliary variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equal absolute coefficient magnitude suffices for direct collapse: negative coefficients become complemented literals and the threshold shifts.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polynomial-size auxiliary cardinality formulation under a total-magnitude bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be the sum of the absolute coefficient magnitudes in an integral PB system. If auxiliary Boolean copies and cardinality linking constraints are allowed, coefficient copying produces an exact cardinality extended formulation of size \(O(M)\). Hence the translation is polynomial-size when \(M\) is polynomially bounded in the PB input length, including the usual unary-magnitude regime. Unrestricted binary coefficients do not guarantee such a polynomial-size copy expansion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With auxiliaries and polynomially bounded total coefficient magnitude, exact coefficient copying collapses PB systems to polynomial-size cardinality systems.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coefficient restrictions under which linear pseudo-Boolean inequalities become cardinality inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_n\in\{0,1\}\) be Boolean literals. If every nonzero coefficient of \(\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_i\ell_i\geq b\) equals a fixed integer \(c>0\), then the inequality is equivalent to \(\sum_{i:a_i=c}\ell_i\geq\lceil b/c\rceil\). If every nonzero coefficient equals \(-c\), it is equivalently \(\sum_{i:a_i=-c}\ell_i\leq\lfloor-b/c\rfloor\). Thus equal-magnitude, common-sign coefficients yield a unit-weight cardinality representation without auxiliary variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When all nonzero PB coefficients have one magnitude and one sign, division by that magnitude converts the inequality exactly into a cardinality inequality.
assumptions_latex: There is a fixed integer \(c>0\) such that either \(a_i\in\{0,c\}\) for every \(i\), or \(a_i\in\{0,-c\}\) for every \(i\).

children.title: Complexity-Preserving Formulation Bridges
children.top_down_role: Translations that retain relevant complexity characteristics across the two formalisms.

knowledge_statements.title: Complexity-Preserving Formulation Bridges
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct equivalence between linear PB and binary integer-program formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A linear PB system \(\sum_i a_{ji}x_i\geq b_j\) with \(x_i\in\{0,1\}\) is already a 0–1 integer program. Conversely, each 0–1 linear inequality is a PB constraint. Replacing \(\geq\) by \(\leq\) through multiplication by \(-1\), and replacing equalities by two opposite inequalities, produces equivalent instances. These transformations preserve feasible assignments and objectives and increase encoding length by at most a constant factor. Therefore feasibility, threshold decision, and approximation ratios transfer between the two explicit linear representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear PB systems and 0–1 integer programs translate directly into each other with constant-factor encoding overhead.
assumptions_latex: Both representations are explicit and linear.
Coefficients use the same binary encoding convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I_{\mathrm{PB}}\equiv I_{\mathrm{01IP}}\) with \(|I_{\mathrm{01IP}}|=O(|I_{\mathrm{PB}}|)\) and conversely.

notation.meaning: binary encoding length of an instance

children.title: Correspondence Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits caused by representation growth, coefficient encoding, or formulation restrictions.

knowledge_statements.title: Correspondence Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Where formulation equivalence ceases to preserve computational complexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A PB-to-0–1-IP formulation bridge is complexity preserving only when its output length and coefficient bit lengths are polynomial in the input length and solutions map back in polynomial time. Semantic equivalence alone is insufficient. If a translation enumerates exponentially many assignments, monomials, or constraints, so that an input of length \(L\) yields length \(2^{\Omega(L)}\), polynomial time in the translated formulation may be exponential in the original input. Likewise, replacing succinctly represented coefficients by unary expansion can destroy encoding-sensitive complexity correspondence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equivalent formulations need not preserve complexity when translation size, coefficient length, or solution recovery grows superpolynomially.
assumptions_latex: The original formulation has binary encoding length \(L\).
Complexity is measured against the original input length.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|T(I)|\not\leq\operatorname{poly}(|I|)\) prevents the translation \(T\) from establishing a polynomial-time complexity correspondence.

A one-way reduction does not establish the converse implications or complexity equivalence; those require a reverse reduction or an appropriate polynomially invertible correspondence.

children.top_down_role: Approximation guarantees obtained from randomized truth assignments.

assumptions_latex: Variables are assigned independently.
\(0\leq p_i\leq1\), and all clause weights satisfy \(w_C\geq0\).
Clauses are normalized so that no clause contains a complementary literal pair or repeated variable.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonuniform product-distribution variant of random-assignment MaxSAT approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Independently set variable \(x_i\) true with probability \(p_i\). For a normalized clause \(C\) with positive-variable set \(C^+\) and negative-variable set \(C^-\), its unsatisfaction probability is \(\prod_{i\in C^+}(1-p_i)\prod_{i\in C^-}p_i\). Consequently the expected satisfied weight is \(\sum_C w_C\left(1-\prod_{i\in C^+}(1-p_i)\prod_{i\in C^-}p_i\right)\). Any polynomial-time probability-selection rule establishing that this expectation is at least \(\alpha\operatorname{OPT}\) yields a randomized \(\alpha\)-approximation in expectation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent nonuniform truth probabilities give an exact product formula for expected satisfied weight and may improve on fair assignment for restricted instances.
knowledge_statements.title: Independent Biased Random Assignment
Random-Assignment Approximation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent unbiased assignment for weighted MaxSAT.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a weighted CNF formula with nonnegative clause weights \(w_C\), independently assign every variable true with probability \(1/2\), and output the resulting assignment. A nonempty clause \(C\) containing \(k_C\) distinct, noncomplementary literals is unsatisfied with probability \(2^{-k_C}\). Hence the expected satisfied weight is \(\sum_C w_C(1-2^{-k_C})\). In particular it is at least \(W/2\), where \(W=\sum_Cw_C\), and therefore at least \(\operatorname{OPT}/2\). The procedure is a randomized \(1/2\)-approximation in expectation for weighted MaxSAT without empty clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent fair variable assignments satisfy expected clause weight at least half of total weight, hence at least half of optimum.
assumptions_latex: Clause weights satisfy \(w_C\geq0\).
Clauses are nonempty and contain no repeated or complementary literal pair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[\operatorname{val}(X)]=\sum_Cw_C(1-2^{-k_C})\geq\tfrac12W\geq\tfrac12\operatorname{OPT}\).

notation.meaning: number of distinct literals in clause C

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: expectation follows from independent fair bits and linearity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The expected-value calculation and randomized one-half approximation are correct under the stated clause and weight assumptions, and algorithm is the correct kind, but no authoritative MaxSAT approximation locator is supplied.

assumptions_latex: \(\Phi(\sigma)\) and its two one-variable extensions are computable in polynomial time.

notation.meaning: Pessimistic estimator under partial assignment sigma.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional-expectation variant used when exact conditional objective expectations are inconvenient to compute.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\) be an undesirable event and let \(\Phi(\sigma)\) be a polynomial-time computable estimator for every partial assignment \(\sigma\), with \(\Pr(B\mid\sigma)\leq\Phi(\sigma)\) and \(\min_{b\in\{0,1\}}\Phi(\sigma,x_i=b)\leq\Phi(\sigma)\). Fix each next variable to a value minimizing \(\Phi\). If \(\Phi(\varnothing)<1\) and every complete assignment in \(B\) has estimator at least \(1\), the resulting complete assignment avoids \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Greedily keeping a valid pessimistic estimator nonincreasing derandomizes bad-event avoidance when its initial value is below one.
knowledge_statements.title: Derandomization by Pessimistic Estimators
Conditional-Expectation Derandomization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic realization of the random-assignment MaxSAT guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Order the variables as \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\). Starting with no assignments, at step \(i\) compute the conditional expected satisfied weight obtained by setting \(x_i=0\) and by setting \(x_i=1\), while all unassigned variables remain independent fair bits. Choose a value attaining the larger conditional expectation. After \(n\) steps output the complete assignment. Because the current conditional expectation is the average of the two candidate expectations, it never decreases; the final objective value is therefore at least the original random-assignment expectation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fix variables greedily to preserve conditional expected satisfied weight, producing deterministically an assignment matching the random guarantee.
assumptions_latex: Conditional expectations are computable in polynomial time.
The initial distribution assigns independent fair bits.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{val}(x^{\mathrm{out}})\geq\mathbb E[\operatorname{val}(X)]\geq\tfrac12\operatorname{OPT}\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: method of conditional expectations is standard

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional-expectation algorithm and guarantee are correctly stated, with polynomial-time computability explicitly assumed, but an authoritative derandomization source with a specific locator is absent.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit small sample space for fixed-width Boolean assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose distinct \(a_1,\ldots,a_n\in\mathbb F_q\) and choose uniformly a polynomial \(P(z)=c_0+\cdots+c_{k-1}z^{k-1}\). For every set of at most \(k\) distinct indices, the corresponding evaluations are jointly uniform. Applying a fixed nonzero \(\mathbb F_2\)-linear functional to each evaluation gives unbiased k-wise-independent bits. The coefficient seed space has size \(q^k\), so all assignments can be enumerated in polynomial time when \(k\) is fixed and \(q\) is polynomially bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluations of random degree-less-than-k finite-field polynomials give an explicit k-wise-independent Boolean assignment family of polynomial size for fixed k.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded-wise-independent distributions preserving bounded-width MaxSAT expectations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let every clause contain at most \(k\) distinct variables, and let \(X\in\{0,1\}^n\) be drawn from a distribution whose coordinates are unbiased and \(k\)-wise independent. For each clause \(C\), its variables are jointly uniform, so \(\Pr[C\text{ is unsatisfied}]=2^{-|C|}\), exactly as under full independence. Consequently \(\mathbb E[\operatorname{val}(X)]=\sum_Cw_C(1-2^{-|C|})\). If the distribution has a polynomial-size enumerable sample space, evaluating all its assignments yields deterministically an assignment at least as valuable as this expectation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unbiased k-wise independence preserves random-assignment expectations for clauses of width at most k; enumerable families permit deterministic selection.
assumptions_latex: Every clause has width at most \(k\).
The assignment distribution is unbiased and \(k\)-wise independent.
Clause weights are nonnegative.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic LP-relaxation rounding template for weighted Boolean maximization problems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a weighted Boolean maximization instance and a linear relaxation \(P\subseteq[0,1]^n\), compute an optimal fractional solution \(x^*\in P\). The map must produce a feasible Boolean solution for every \(\omega\in\Omega\). An \(\alpha\)-rounding family satisfies \(\mathbb E[\operatorname{val}(\widehat x)]\geq\alpha\operatorname{LP}(I)\geq\alpha\operatorname{OPT}(I)\) for every instance \(I\), where the expectation is over \(\omega\). A deterministic member replaces sampling by a choice attaining at least the same conditional expectation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Triangle Family with a Nonunit Max-2SAT SDP Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit integrality-gap family for the stated truth-reference weighted Max-2SAT SDP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(t\geq1\), take \(t\) disjoint triangles. For every edge \(\{i,j\}\), include the two unit-weight clauses \((x_i\vee x_j)\) and \((\neg x_i\vee\neg x_j)\). Each edge contributes one plus its cut indicator, so every triangle has Boolean optimum \(5\). Assign the three vectors of each triangle mutual inner product \(-1/2\), using any unit truth-reference vector \(v_0\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Satisfied-Weight and Violation-Cost Ratios Are Not Interchangeable
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between multiplicative approximation conventions for complementary MaxSAT objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let total soft weight be \(W>0\), satisfied weight \(V(a)\), and violation cost \(C(a)=W-V(a)\). Thresholds must therefore fix the objective orientation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condition for composing reductions with nonidentical intermediate gaps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the first reduction guarantee intermediate completeness at least \(c_1\) and soundness at most \(s_1\), while the second is valid on promises \(\operatorname{OPT}_B\geq c_2\) and \(\operatorname{OPT}_B\leq s_2\). Direct composition is justified when \(c_1\geq c_2\) and \(s_1\leq s_2\). Otherwise the first reduction can output instances outside the promise cases required by the second.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reductions with different intermediate thresholds compose when the first output gap is at least as strong as the second reduction requires.

assumptions_latex: The source and target are promise problems with separated completeness and soundness cases.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A transformation that maps every source completeness instance to a target completeness instance but does not map source soundness instances to target soundness instances is insufficient to transfer gap-decision hardness: a target gap algorithm has no prescribed behavior on an image outside its soundness promise. The analogous failure holds when only soundness is preserved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Preserving only the yes side or only the no side does not transfer promise-gap hardness; both implications are required.

assumptions_latex: Both reductions have polynomial running time and polynomial output length.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transitivity of compatible completeness-soundness gap transfer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(f\) is a polynomial-time \((c,s)\)-to-\((c',s')\) gap-preserving reduction from maximization problem \(A\) to \(B\), and \(g\) is a polynomial-time \((c',s')\)-to-\((c'',s'')\) gap-preserving reduction from \(B\) to \(C\). Then \(g\circ f\) is a polynomial-time \((c,s)\)-to-\((c'',s'')\) gap-preserving reduction from \(A\) to \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compatible gap-preserving reductions compose, so promise-gap hardness transfers transitively.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Approximation Excluded by a Promise Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conversion of normalized completeness-soundness hardness into an approximation-ratio upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a maximization problem have nonnegative normalized values, and suppose it is hard under a stated assumption to distinguish \(\operatorname{OPT}(I)\geq c\) from \(\operatorname{OPT}(I)\leq s\), where \(c>s\geq0\). If a polynomial-time algorithm always returned a feasible solution of value at least \(\rho\operatorname{OPT}(I)\) and \(\rho c>s\), its returned value could be compared with a threshold strictly between \(s\) and \(\rho c\) to distinguish the cases. Thus no such ratio \(\rho>s/c\) exists under the same assumption.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hard completeness-soundness gap rules out every guaranteed approximation ratio whose completeness-case value exceeds the soundness bound.
assumptions_latex: c>s\geq0.
\text{The algorithmic guarantee holds on every instance, not merely in expectation}.
\text{Returned values are feasible and hence at most }\operatorname{OPT}(I).
\text{The }(c,s)\text{ promise distinction is hard under an explicit assumption}.

knowledge_statements.title: Approximation Excluded by a Promise Gap

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transformation of completeness and soundness thresholds under a common positive-affine objective normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the target value be renormalized by \(v'(J,z)=\alpha v(J,z)+\gamma\), where \(\alpha>0\) and \(\gamma\) are independent of the instance \(J\) and feasible solution \(z\). Then \[\operatorname{OPT}'(J)=\alpha\operatorname{OPT}(J)+\gamma,\] so a completeness-soundness gap \((c,s)\) is equivalently represented by \((\alpha c+\gamma,\alpha s+\gamma)\). A nonpositive or instance-dependent scale need not preserve the same promise ordering or fixed thresholds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A common positive-affine objective renormalization transports both promise-gap thresholds and preserves their order.
assumptions_latex: \alpha>0.
\alpha\text{ and }\gamma\text{ are independent of instances and feasible solutions}.
v'(J,z)=\alpha v(J,z)+\gamma.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) and \(B\) be encoded maximization problems with a fixed common value orientation and normalized optima. A polynomial-time map \(f\) is an \((c,s)\)-to-\((c',s')\) gap-preserving reduction when \(c>s\), \(c'>s'\), its output encoding has length polynomial in the input length, and for every source instance \(I\), \[\operatorname{OPT}_A(I)\geq c\Rightarrow\operatorname{OPT}_B(f(I))\geq c',\qquad \operatorname{OPT}_A(I)\leq s\Rightarrow\operatorname{OPT}_B(f(I))\leq s'.\] Therefore an algorithm distinguishing the target promise cases would distinguish the source promise cases.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A gap-preserving reduction maps both source promise sides to separated target sides in polynomial time and polynomial output size.

f\text{ is polynomial-time computable}.
|f(I)|\leq\operatorname{poly}(|I|).
\text{Objective orientation and normalization are fixed}.

A polynomial-time map \(f\) is a \((c,s)\)-to-\((c',s')\) minimization gap-preserving reduction, where \(c<s\) and \(c'<s'\), if \[\operatorname{OPT}_A(I)\leq c\Rightarrow\operatorname{OPT}_B(f(I))\leq c',\qquad \operatorname{OPT}_A(I)\geq s\Rightarrow\operatorname{OPT}_B(f(I))\geq s',\] and \(|f(I)|\leq\operatorname{poly}(|I|)\). Hence hardness of distinguishing low source cost from high source cost transfers to the corresponding target promise.

assumptions_latex: c<s.
f\text{ is polynomial-time computable}.
|f(I)|\leq\operatorname{poly}(|I|).
\text{Objective orientation and normalization are fixed}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Gap}^{\min}_A(c,s)\leq_m^p\operatorname{Gap}^{\min}_B(c',s').

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) and \(B\) be maximization problems with normalized optimum in \([0,1]\). A polynomial-time map \(f\) is an \((c,s)\)-to-\((c',s')\) gap-preserving reduction if \(c>s\), \(c'>s'\), and every instance \(I\) satisfies \[\operatorname{OPT}_A(I)\geq c\Rightarrow\operatorname{OPT}_B(f(I))\geq c',\qquad \operatorname{OPT}_A(I)\leq s\Rightarrow\operatorname{OPT}_B(f(I))\leq s'.\] The encoding length of \(f(I)\) must be polynomial in that of \(I\). Consequently, hardness of distinguishing the two cases for \(A\) transfers to the corresponding distinction for \(B\).

\(f\) is computable with polynomial output size.
