knowledge_statements.title: Hardness-of-Approximation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formal separation of exact, scheme-level, constant-factor, and threshold hardness regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a maximization problem \(\Pi\), let \(R_{\mathrm{poly}}(\Pi)\subseteq[0,1]\) contain every ratio guaranteed by some polynomial-time algorithm. The problem admits a PTAS exactly when \(1-\varepsilon\in R_{\mathrm{poly}}(\Pi)\) for every \(\varepsilon>0\). It is APX-hard when a stated approximation-preserving reduction transfers every problem in APX to \(\Pi\); under \(\mathrm P\ne\mathrm{NP}\), this excludes a PTAS. Constant-threshold hardness at \(\rho\in(0,1)\) means that, under the stated assumption, no polynomial-time algorithm guarantees \(\rho+\varepsilon\) for any \(\varepsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximation regimes distinguish PTAS availability, APX-hardness, and hardness beyond a fixed constant ratio under stated reductions and assumptions.
assumptions_latex: \(\Pi\) is a finite-input maximization problem with polynomially evaluable solutions.
Each hardness assertion names its reduction and complexity assumption.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The position of \(R_{\mathrm{poly}}(\Pi)\) relative to \(1\) and a constant \(\rho\) determines the stated approximation regime.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits a regimes leaf, but the PTAS, APX-hardness, and constant-threshold conventions have no cited support. In particular, the reduction notion and assumptions needed for the claimed PTAS exclusion must be tied to an authoritative source.

children.title: Solution-Cost Parameters
children.top_down_role: Parameters based on target cost, unsatisfied weight, or objective value.

assumptions_latex: The objective \(w_I(x)\) is integer-valued and polynomially evaluable.
The maximization or minimization convention is fixed.
The threshold \(k\) is a nonnegative integer included in the parameterized input.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The parameterized instance is \((I,k)\), with solution-cost parameter \(k\).

notation.meaning: Objective value of assignment x for instance I.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameterization of a Boolean optimization decision problem by its requested solution value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) be a Boolean optimization instance with feasible assignments \(x\) and integer-valued objective \(w_I(x)\). For maximization, the solution-cost parameterization asks, given \((I,k)\), whether there exists a feasible assignment \(x\) such that \(w_I(x)\geq k\). For minimization, it asks whether there exists a feasible assignment \(x\) such that \(w_I(x)\leq k\). In either convention, the parameter is the requested objective threshold \(k\), rather than a structural measure of \(I\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The solution-cost parameter is the requested objective threshold in the decision version of the Boolean optimization problem.
knowledge_statements.title: Solution-Cost Parameters

children.title: Above-Guarantee Parameters
children.top_down_role: Parameters measuring improvement beyond a guaranteed baseline.

knowledge_statements.title: Above-Guarantee Parameters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameterization by improvement over a polynomially computable guaranteed baseline.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) be a maximization instance and let \(B(I)\) be a polynomially computable guaranteed value such that \(\operatorname{OPT}(I)\geq B(I)\). The above-guarantee decision problem asks, for an integer \(k\geq0\), whether \[\operatorname{OPT}(I)\geq B(I)+k.\] The parameter is the requested excess \(k\), not the total target value. For a minimization problem with an efficiently certified upper guarantee \(B(I)\), the analogous question is whether \(\operatorname{OPT}(I)\leq B(I)-k\). The baseline and its guarantee direction must be part of the problem specification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An above-guarantee parameter measures the requested improvement over a computable bound that every instance is guaranteed to meet.
assumptions_latex: \(B(I)\) is polynomially computable.
The guarantee \(\operatorname{OPT}(I)\geq B(I)\) holds for maximization.
\(k\) is a nonnegative integer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The maximization target is \(B(I)+k\), with parameter \(k\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits the leaf, and the maximization and minimization guarantee directions are internally consistent. No dedicated source is supplied for the above-guarantee parameterization or its baseline requirements.

children.title: Baseline-Sensitive Parameterizations
children.top_down_role: Regimes distinguished by the selected reference guarantee.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-way transfer between two parameters of the same decision problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\kappa_1,\kappa_2\) parameterize the same instances and suppose \(\kappa_1(I)\le g(\kappa_2(I))\) for a computable function \(g\). If the problem is decidable in time \(f(\kappa_1(I))|I|^{O(1)}\), define \(\bar f(r)=\max_{0\le j\le r}f(j)\). It is then decidable in time \(\bar f(g(\kappa_2(I)))|I|^{O(1)}\), so it is FPT under \(\kappa_2\). Reverse transfer requires a bound on \(\kappa_2\) in terms of \(\kappa_1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: FPT transfers in one direction when the old parameter is computably bounded by the new one; mutual bounds are needed only for transfer in both directions.
assumptions_latex: \(\kappa_1\) and \(\kappa_2\) parameterize the same encoded instances.
\(\kappa_1(I)\le g(\kappa_2(I))\) for a computable function \(g\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathrm{FPT}(\kappa_1)\Longrightarrow\mathrm{FPT}(\kappa_2)\text{ in the stated direction}.

notation.meaning: A nondecreasing computable envelope of the original parameter dependence.

knowledge_statements.title: Direction-Sensitive FPT Transfer

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polynomial Domination Required for Direct Kernel Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Kernel-transfer condition for two parameters on the same encoded decision problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a kernelization for parameter \(\kappa_1\) outputs an equivalent instance of complete length at most \(p(\kappa_1(I))\), where \(p\) is polynomial. If \(\kappa_1(I)\le q(\kappa_2(I))\) for a polynomial \(q\), the same kernelization has output length at most \(p(q(\kappa_2(I)))\) and is a polynomial kernel under \(\kappa_2\). A merely computable domination yields no polynomial size guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Direct polynomial-kernel transfer needs polynomial, not merely computable, domination of the old parameter by the new one.
assumptions_latex: Both parameters apply to the same encoded problem instances.
The original kernel has complete output length polynomial in \(\kappa_1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \kappa_1\le q(\kappa_2)\text{ with polynomial }q\Longrightarrow\text{the }\kappa_1\text{-kernel is polynomial in }\kappa_2.
knowledge_statements.title: Polynomial Domination Required for Direct Kernel Transfer
Baseline-Sensitive Parameterizations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence of parameter values and complexity claims on the selected guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a maximization instance \(I\) and two valid baselines \(B_1(I)\leq B_2(I)\leq\operatorname{OPT}(I)\), define excess parameters \(k_j(I)=\operatorname{OPT}(I)-B_j(I)\). Then \[0\leq k_2(I)\leq k_1(I),\qquad k_1(I)-k_2(I)=B_2(I)-B_1(I).\] Hence changing the baseline can change the parameter by an unbounded instance-dependent amount. Fixed-parameter tractability or kernel bounds stated for one baseline therefore transfer to another only when the two resulting parameters are bounded by computable functions of one another.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stronger baseline yields a smaller excess parameter, but complexity results transfer only when alternative parameters computably bound each other.
assumptions_latex: \(B_1\) and \(B_2\) are valid maximization lower guarantees.
\(B_1(I)\leq B_2(I)\) for every instance \(I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(k_2(I)\leq k_1(I)\), but parameterized-complexity transfer requires computable mutual bounds.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property role fits the leaf and the displayed baseline identities are correct. The final transfer claim is overstated: transferring an FPT or kernel bound in a specified direction generally needs an appropriate one-way computable bound, not necessarily mutual bounds. A source and a direction-sensitive correction are required.

children.title: Treewidth Parameters
children.top_down_role: Width parameters derived from structural graph representations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boolean feasibility and locally additive optimization on a supplied primal decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a width-\(k\) tree decomposition of the primal graph, dynamic programming over bag assignments decides feasibility and optimizes an additive objective whose constraint and objective-term scopes are processable locally. Each bag has at most \(2^{k+1}\) Boolean assignments, yielding time \(2^{O(k)}|I|^{O(1)}\). The bound requires an explicitly represented local constraint language with polynomial-time table transitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A supplied width-k primal decomposition supports single-exponential bag-assignment dynamic programming for locally represented Boolean feasibility and additive optimization.
assumptions_latex: The chosen graph is the primal graph.
A width-\(k\) decomposition is supplied.
Constraint and objective-term scopes are locally evaluable in polynomial time.

notation.meaning: Width of the supplied primal decomposition.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Treewidth Dynamic Programming

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact parameterized recognition and construction, without asserting a particular dependence on the parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: There is a computable function \(f\) such that, given a finite graph \(G\) and integer \(k\), one can decide whether \(\operatorname{tw}(G)\leq k\) in time \(f(k)|G|^{O(1)}\) and, in the affirmative case, produce a tree decomposition of width at most \(k\). Thus supplying the decomposition is unnecessary for FPT membership, although it affects the concrete algorithm and bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Treewidth at most k can be recognized and a width-k decomposition produced in fixed-parameter time.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a finite explicitly represented graph.
\(k\) is the requested width bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{tw}(G)\leq k\) is decidable, with decomposition construction, in \(f(k)|G|^{O(1)}\) time.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Parameter Treewidth Recognition

assumptions_latex: \(G_I\) is a finite undirected graph determined by the instance \(I\).
The graph representation used to construct \(G_I\) is explicitly specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The structural parameter is \(k=\operatorname{tw}(G_I)\) for the explicitly selected graph representation.

notation.meaning: Chosen graph representation of instance I.
Bag indexed by tree node t.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Treewidth of an explicitly selected graph representation associated with a Boolean optimization instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G_I\) be a specified finite undirected graph representation of a Boolean optimization instance \(I\), such as its primal graph or incidence graph. A tree decomposition of \(G_I\) consists of a tree \(T\) and bags \(X_t\subseteq V(G_I)\) for \(t\in V(T)\), such that every vertex of \(G_I\) occurs in a nonempty connected set of bags and every edge of \(G_I\) has both endpoints in some bag. Its width is \(\max_{t\in V(T)}|X_t|-1\), and \[\operatorname{tw}(G_I)=\min_{(T,(X_t)_{t\in V(T)})}\left(\max_{t\in V(T)}|X_t|-1\right).\] A treewidth parameterization must state which graph representation supplies \(G_I\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Treewidth is the minimum, over tree decompositions of a specified instance graph, of the largest bag size minus one.
knowledge_statements.title: Treewidth Parameters

children.title: Incidence-Structure Parameters
children.top_down_role: Parameters based on variable-constraint incidence structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: SAT and additive weighted-clause optimization on a supplied incidence decomposition; not unrestricted succinct global constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a width-\(k\) tree decomposition of a CNF incidence graph, dynamic programming can store assignments to bag variables and satisfaction flags for bag clauses. SAT and additive weighted-clause optimization are solvable in \(2^{O(k)}|I|^{O(1)}\) time. The extension to another Boolean constraint language requires a finite bag summary of size bounded solely by \(k\) and polynomial-time transitions; incidence width alone gives no such bound for arbitrary succinct constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Incidence-treewidth dynamic programming is single-exponential for CNF and analogous constraints with bounded bag summaries, but not automatically for arbitrary succinct constraints.
assumptions_latex: A width-\(k\) incidence decomposition is supplied.
Constraints are clauses, or admit finite bag summaries bounded as a function of \(k\).
Objective contributions can be combined locally and exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T(I)=2^{O(k)}|I|^{O(1)}\) for the stated constraint representations.

notation.meaning: Width of the supplied incidence decomposition.

knowledge_statements.title: Incidence-Decomposition Dynamic Programming

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison of standard primal and incidence treewidth, including the necessary bounded-arity boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the standard primal graph \(G_{\mathrm p}(I)\) and incidence graph \(G_{\mathrm{inc}}(I)\), \(\operatorname{tw}(G_{\mathrm{inc}}(I))\leq\operatorname{tw}(G_{\mathrm p}(I))+1\). If every constraint has arity at most \(r\), then \(\operatorname{tw}(G_{\mathrm p}(I))\leq r(\operatorname{tw}(G_{\mathrm{inc}}(I))+1)-1\). Without bounded arity, incidence treewidth one can coexist with unbounded primal treewidth, as for one constraint incident with arbitrarily many variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Incidence width is bounded by primal width; bounded arity gives a reverse bound, while one large constraint shows that the arity assumption is essential.
assumptions_latex: The standard primal and bipartite incidence graphs are used.
The reverse bound assumes maximum constraint arity \(r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{tw}(G_{\mathrm{inc}})\leq\operatorname{tw}(G_{\mathrm p})+1\), and under arity \(r\), \(\operatorname{tw}(G_{\mathrm p})\leq r(\operatorname{tw}(G_{\mathrm{inc}})+1)-1\).
knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Incidence Treewidth Comparison

assumptions_latex: The instance \(I\) has finite variable set \(V\) and finite constraint set \(C\).
The selected graph invariant \(p\) and the treatment of labels are explicitly specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The parameter has the form \(k=p(G_{\mathrm{inc}}(I))\) for an explicitly chosen graph invariant \(p\).

notation.meaning: Variable-constraint incidence graph of instance I.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameters derived from the bipartite variable-constraint incidence graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) be a Boolean optimization instance with variable set \(V\) and constraint or clause set \(C\). Its incidence graph is the bipartite graph \(G_{\mathrm{inc}}(I)=(V\sqcup C,E)\), where \((v,c)\in E\) exactly when variable \(v\in V\) occurs in constraint \(c\in C\). An incidence-structure parameterization assigns to \(I\) a specified graph invariant \(p(G_{\mathrm{inc}}(I))\), such as treewidth, pathwidth, feedback-vertex number, or vertex-cover number. Signed occurrences, multiplicities, and weights remain labels unless the chosen invariant explicitly incorporates them.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Incidence parameters are specified graph invariants of the bipartite graph connecting variables to the constraints or clauses in which they occur.
knowledge_statements.title: Incidence-Structure Parameters

children.title: Backdoor Parameters
children.top_down_role: Parameters measuring distance to tractable target classes.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Use of a supplied strong backdoor; detection of such a backdoor is a separate problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a strong \(\mathcal B\)-backdoor \(S\) of size \(k\), enumerate its \(2^k\) assignments and solve every residual in \(\mathcal B\). This decides feasibility in \(O(2^k(q(|I|)+|I|^{O(1)}))\) time when residual construction, membership, and solution in \(\mathcal B\) take polynomial preprocessing and time \(q(|I|)\). The same bound applies to optimization only when each branch objective is exactly recoverable from the residual solution in polynomial time. It does not include the cost of finding \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A supplied strong backdoor gives a 2^k residual-enumeration algorithm, provided the base class is tractable and branch objective values can be recovered exactly.
assumptions_latex: A strong \(\mathcal B\)-backdoor \(S\) is supplied.
Residual construction, membership testing, and solving in \(\mathcal B\) have the stated bounds.
For optimization, residual solutions determine the original branch objective exactly in polynomial time.
knowledge_statements.title: Strong-Backdoor Residual Enumeration

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard weak satisfiability backdoors and convention-dependent deletion distance to a fixed Boolean base class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A set \(S\) is a weak \(\mathcal B\)-backdoor of \(I\) if some assignment \(\tau:S\to\{0,1\}\) yields a satisfiable residual \(I[\tau]\in\mathcal B\); its minimum size is \(\operatorname{wb}_{\mathcal B}(I)\). Under a specified variable-deletion operation, \(S\) is a deletion \(\mathcal B\)-backdoor if \(I-S\in\mathcal B\), and \(\operatorname{db}_{\mathcal B}(I)=\min\{|S|:I-S\in\mathcal B\}\). Weak, strong, and deletion backdoors are distinct parameters and must not be interchanged without hypotheses on \(\mathcal B\) and the simplification operation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weak backdoors require one successful assignment into the base class; deletion backdoors require membership after a specified deletion operation. Both differ from strong backdoors.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal B\) is a fixed class of Boolean residual instances.
Residual assignment, satisfiability, and variable deletion are explicitly defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{wb}_{\mathcal B}\), \(\operatorname{sb}_{\mathcal B}\), and \(\operatorname{db}_{\mathcal B}\) are separately specified distance-to-tractability parameters.
knowledge_statements.title: Weak and Deletion Backdoor Parameters

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal B\) is a fixed tractable class of Boolean formulas or constraint instances.
\(\mathcal B\) is closed under the specified partial-assignment simplification operation.
Residual instances \(I[\tau]\) use explicitly stated Boolean simplification rules.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The structural parameter is \(\operatorname{sb}_{\mathcal B}(I)\), the minimum size of a strong \(\mathcal B\)-backdoor of \(I\).

notation.meaning: Residual instance after applying partial assignment tau.
Minimum strong-backdoor size relative to the base class.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong backdoors from a Boolean instance into a specified tractable base class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal B\) be a fixed tractable class of Boolean formulas or constraint instances that is closed under the specified partial-assignment operation. A set \(S\) of variables is a strong \(\mathcal B\)-backdoor of an instance \(I\) if, for every assignment \(\tau:S\to\{0,1\}\), the residual instance \(I[\tau]\) belongs to \(\mathcal B\). The strong backdoor number is \[\operatorname{sb}_{\mathcal B}(I)=\min\{|S|:S\text{ is a strong }\mathcal B\text{-backdoor of }I\}.\] The base class and whether the backdoor notion is strong, weak, or deletion-based must be specified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strong backdoor is a minimum-size variable set such that every assignment to it reduces the instance to a fixed tractable base class.
knowledge_statements.title: Backdoor Parameters

children.title: Combined Structural Parameter Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes using multiple structural measures without conflating their roles.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: FPT equivalence and transfer for a fixed finite tuple of nonnegative structural parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p_1,\ldots,p_r\) be a fixed finite tuple of nonnegative integer parameters and let \(s=\sum_{i=1}^r p_i\). A problem is FPT for the tuple exactly when it is FPT for \(s\). More generally, an FPT bound in parameters \(p_1,\ldots,p_r\) transfers to a parameter tuple \(q\) whenever every \(p_i\) is bounded by a computable function of \(q\). No such transfer follows from merely listing additional parameters or from an aggregate that fails to bound every parameter used by the algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed finite tuple, vector-FPT is equivalent to FPT by the sum. FPT also transfers along explicitly stated computable parameter bounds.
assumptions_latex: The number of component parameters is fixed.
All component parameters are computable nonnegative integers.
Any claimed transfer states computable bounds for every parameter used by the original algorithm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathrm{FPT}[p_1,\ldots,p_r]=\mathrm{FPT}[\sum_i p_i]\) for fixed \(r\), with domination-based transfer under the stated bounds.

notation.meaning: Sum of the fixed component parameters.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Dimensional Aggregation and Domination

assumptions_latex: Each \(p_j(I)\) is a computable nonnegative integer for \(j\in\{1,\ldots,r\}\).
The instance encoding, component measures, and choice between vector and aggregate parameterization are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For the vector regime, fixed-parameter tractability means a runtime of the form \(f(p_1(I),\ldots,p_r(I))|I|^{O(1)}\) for a computable function \(f\).

notation.meaning: Scalar sum aggregate of the component parameters.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameterized regimes formed from multiple explicitly selected Boolean-instance structure measures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p_1,ldots,p_r\) be explicitly defined nonnegative structural measures of a Boolean optimization instance \(I\). A combined structural parameterization may use the vector \(k(I)=(p_1(I),ldots,p_r(I))\) or a specified scalar aggregate such as \(\widehat{k}(I)=\sum_{j=1}^r p_j(I)\). For the vector parameter, an algorithm is fixed-parameter tractable if its running time is \(f(p_1(I),ldots,p_r(I))|I|^{O(1)}\) for some computable function \(f\). For an aggregate parameter, fixed-parameter tractability is defined with respect to that aggregate. The selected parameter representation must therefore be stated explicitly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A combined structural regime uses an explicitly specified vector or scalar aggregate of structural measures, with fixed-parameter runtime measured against that chosen parameter.
knowledge_statements.title: Combined Structural Parameter Regimes

children.title: Polynomial Kernelization Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes admitting polynomially bounded equivalent instances.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Kernel Size Uses Complete Encoding Length
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bit-size requirement for polynomial kernels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a reduced instance \((I',k')\), bounds only on variable, clause, or constraint counts are insufficient when coefficients, weights, thresholds, or indices can have unbounded encodings. Polynomial kernelization requires \(|\operatorname{enc}(I',k')|\le p(k)\) for the complete serialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polynomial kernel must bound all encoded data, not only structural counts.
assumptions_latex: All numeric and structural data belong to the serialized reduced instance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |\operatorname{enc}(I',k')|\le p(k).

notation.meaning: Complete binary serialization of the reduced instance and parameter.

knowledge_statements.title: Kernel Size Uses Complete Encoding Length

knowledge_statements.scope_note: General kernelization characterization and the stronger polynomial-size regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A decidable parameterized problem is fixed-parameter tractable if and only if it admits a kernelization whose complete output length is bounded by some computable function \(g(k)\). Requiring \(g\) to be polynomial is a stronger condition and defines the polynomial-kernel regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: FPT is equivalent to a computably bounded kernel, while a polynomial kernel is an additional preprocessing guarantee.
assumptions_latex: The parameterized problem is decidable.
Kernel size is measured by complete output encoding length.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q\in\mathrm{FPT}\Longleftrightarrow Q\text{ admits a kernel of size }g(k)\text{ for some computable }g.
knowledge_statements.title: Kernelization Characterization of Fixed-Parameter Tractability

assumptions_latex: \((I,k)\) is an instance of a parameterized Boolean optimization decision problem, with encoding length \(|I|\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((I,k)\mapsto(I',k')\) in polynomial time, with \(|I'|+k'\le p(k)\) and equivalent yes/no answers.

notation.meaning: A polynomial independent of the input length

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard definition of polynomial kernelization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decision-version kernelization for parameterized Boolean optimization problems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A polynomial kernelization is an algorithm that, given \((I,k)\), runs in time polynomial in \(|I|+k\) and returns an instance \((I',k')\) of the same parameterized problem such that \((I,k)\) is a yes-instance if and only if \((I',k')\) is a yes-instance, and \[|I'|+k'\le p(k)\] for some polynomial \(p\) independent of \(I\). A regime admits a polynomial kernel when one uniform algorithm and one such polynomial apply to every instance in that regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polynomial kernel efficiently replaces an instance by an equivalent instance of the same problem whose total encoding size is polynomial in the parameter.
knowledge_statements.title: Polynomial Kernelization Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and content kind fit the polynomial-kernelization leaf, but no inspectable source or locator supports the same-problem equivalence and polynomial size requirements.

children.title: Compression Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes permitting reduced representations outside the original problem language.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Compression Into a Decidable Language Implies FPT
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic complexity consequence of bounded compression output.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a polynomial compression map \((I,k)\) to \(y\) with \(|y|\le p(k)\) and \((I,k)\in Q\Longleftrightarrow y\in L\), where \(L\) is decidable. If \(T_L(m)\) bounds a fixed decider for \(L\) on strings of length at most \(m\), then \(Q\) is decidable in time \((|I|+k)^{O(1)}+T_L(p(k))\) and is fixed-parameter tractable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polynomial compression into a fixed decidable language yields an FPT algorithm by deciding its parameter-bounded output.
assumptions_latex: The compression runs in polynomial time.
The target language \(L\) is decidable.
The output length is bounded by a polynomial in k.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q\in\mathrm{FPT}.

notation.meaning: Worst-case running time of a fixed decider for L on strings of length at most m.

knowledge_statements.title: Compression Into a Decidable Language Implies FPT

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inclusion relation between same-problem kernelization and arbitrary-language compression.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a parameterized problem \(Q\) has a polynomial kernel \((I,k)\mapsto(I',k')\), serializing \((I',k')\) gives a polynomial compression into \(\widehat Q=\{\operatorname{enc}(J,\ell):(J,\ell)\in Q\}\). The converse does not follow from the definitions because a compression output need not encode an instance of \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every polynomial kernel is a polynomial compression, but a compression may target another language and therefore need not be a kernel.
assumptions_latex: The kernel bounds the complete encoding length of its output polynomially in k.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{polynomial kernel}\Longrightarrow\text{polynomial compression}.

notation.meaning: The unparameterized encoding language associated with Q.

knowledge_statements.title: Polynomial Kernels Are Polynomial Compressions

assumptions_latex: \((I,k)\) is an instance of a parameterized Boolean optimization decision problem over an alphabet \(\Sigma\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((I,k)\mapsto y\) in polynomial time, where \(|y|\le p(k)\) and \(y\in L\) exactly when \((I,k)\) is a yes-instance.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard definition of polynomial compression
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polynomial compression may target a different language and need not output a same-problem instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A polynomial compression into a language \(L\subseteq\Sigma^*\) is an algorithm that, on input \((I,k)\), runs in time polynomial in \(|I|+k\) and outputs a string \(y\in\Sigma^*\) satisfying \[|y|\le p(k)\quad\text{and}\quad y\in L\Longleftrightarrow (I,k)\text{ is a yes-instance},\] where \(p\) is a polynomial independent of \(I\). Unlike a kernelization, the output need not encode an instance of the original parameterized problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polynomial compression maps an instance to a parameter-bounded string in any fixed target language while preserving its yes/no answer.
knowledge_statements.title: Compression Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition correctly distinguishes compression from same-problem kernelization and fits the leaf, but it has no inspectable citation with a specific locator.

children.title: Kernel Lower-Bound Regimes
children.top_down_role: Complexity settings limiting polynomial preprocessing.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conditional Scope of Cross-Composition Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical boundary of the standard compression and kernel exclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An applicable OR-cross-composition theorem excludes polynomial compression only under the assumption \(\mathrm{NP}\nsubseteq\mathrm{coNP}/\mathrm{poly}\). It is not an unconditional output-size lower bound and does not prohibit polynomial-time preprocessing whose output size remains dependent on the original input length.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cross-composition conditionally excludes parameter-polynomial compression, not all useful preprocessing.
assumptions_latex: The OR-cross-composition hypotheses stated in the seed hold.
The standard non-collapse assumption is adopted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathrm{NP}\nsubseteq\mathrm{coNP}/\mathrm{poly}\Longrightarrow\text{no polynomial compression in the stated regime}.
knowledge_statements.title: Conditional Scope of Cross-Composition Lower Bounds

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer of preprocessing lower bounds through parameter-preserving reductions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\le_{ppt}R\) map \((I,k)\) in polynomial time to an equivalent \((J,k')\) with \(k'\le p(k)\) for a polynomial \(p\). A polynomial kernel for \(R\) then gives a polynomial compression for \(Q\). Consequently, a known exclusion of polynomial compression for \(Q\) transfers to \(R\). To transfer only a polynomial-kernel exclusion for \(Q\), an additional polynomial-time reduction from the unparameterized form of \(R\) back to that of \(Q\) is required to recover a same-problem kernel.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polynomial parameter transformation directly transfers compression lower bounds; transferring kernel-only lower bounds additionally requires same-problem recovery.
assumptions_latex: The transformation preserves membership.
The target parameter is polynomially bounded in the source parameter.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q\text{ has no polynomial compression}\Longrightarrow R\text{ has no polynomial kernel}.

notation.meaning: Polynomial parameter transformation from Q to R.

knowledge_statements.title: Polynomial-Parameter-Transformation Transfer Boundary

assumptions_latex: A parameterized problem \(Q\) admits an OR-cross-composition from an NP-hard language \(L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q\) has no polynomial compression, and hence no polynomial kernel, unless \(\mathrm{NP}\subseteq\mathrm{coNP}/\mathrm{poly}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard conditional lower-bound regime based on OR-cross-composition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an NP-hard language \(L\) OR-cross-composes into a parameterized problem \(Q\): polynomially many equivalent-class inputs \(x_1,\ldots,x_t\) are mapped in polynomial time to \((I,k)\) such that \((I,k)\in Q\) exactly when some \(x_i\in L\), while \(k\) is polynomially bounded in \(\max_i|x_i|+\log t\). Then \(Q\) admits no polynomial compression, and therefore no polynomial kernel, unless \[\mathrm{NP}\subseteq\mathrm{coNP}/\mathrm{poly}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An OR-cross-composition from an NP-hard language rules out polynomial compression and polynomial kernels unless a standard complexity-class collapse occurs.
knowledge_statements.title: Kernel Lower-Bound Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound role fits the lower-bound leaf, but an authoritative theorem locator is required to confirm that the stated cross-composition hypotheses exclude polynomial compression, not merely polynomial kernels.

children.title: Parameterized MaxSAT Complexity
children.top_down_role: Parameterized complexity classifications specific to MaxSAT formulations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact enumeration parameterized by the number of Boolean variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a weighted partial MaxSAT instance with \(n\) variables and complete input length \(N\), enumerate all \(2^n\) assignments, discard those violating a hard clause, and minimize the falsified soft-clause weight over the remainder. This solves optimization and threshold decision in \(O(2^n\operatorname{poly}(N))\) time and polynomial working space apart from the stored instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted partial MaxSAT is FPT by the number of variables through exhaustive assignment enumeration.
assumptions_latex: Clause evaluation and binary-encoded weight arithmetic take time polynomial in N.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T(N,n)=2^n\operatorname{poly}(N),\quad\text{so the problem is FPT parameterized by }n.
knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Count FPT Algorithm for MaxSAT

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Allowed Unsatisfied Cost Gives a Para-NP-Hard Parameterization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Zero-slice failure boundary for unrestricted MaxSAT parameterized by permitted falsified cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For unweighted MaxSAT parameterized by the permitted number \(k\) of falsified clauses, the slice \(k=0\) is CNF-SAT. Hence this parameterization is para-NP-hard and is not fixed-parameter tractable unless \(\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}\). The same conclusion holds for weighted partial MaxSAT classes whose zero-cost slice requires satisfaction of an unrestricted NP-hard family of hard and positive-weight soft clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Allowed unsatisfied cost alone does not make unrestricted MaxSAT FPT because its zero slice already contains SAT.
assumptions_latex: The formula class contains an unrestricted NP-hard satisfiability family.
The parameter is the permitted falsified clause count or positive falsified weight.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{MaxSAT parameterized only by }k\text{ is para-NP-hard}.

notation.meaning: Maximum permitted falsified clause count or weight.

knowledge_statements.title: Allowed Unsatisfied Cost Gives a Para-NP-Hard Parameterization

assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a weighted partial CNF formula with hard clauses and nonnegative integer weights on soft clauses.
\(k\in\mathbb N\) is a specified parameter computable from \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The parameterized decision problem asks whether \(\operatorname{OPT}(F)\le B\); it is fixed-parameter tractable when decidable in \(f(k)|F|^{O(1)}\) time.

notation.meaning: Minimum total weight of falsified soft clauses

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: parameterized decision formulation and FPT criterion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic parameterized formulation; complexity depends on the chosen structural or objective parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a weighted partial MaxSAT instance \(F\), define \(\operatorname{OPT}(F)\) as the minimum total weight of falsified soft clauses among assignments satisfying every hard clause, with value \(+\infty\) if the hard clauses are inconsistent. Given a bound \(B\), the parameterized decision problem is \[(F,B,k)\longmapsto [\operatorname{OPT}(F)\le B].\] For the selected parameter \(k\), the regime is fixed-parameter tractable when some computable function \(f\) yields running time \(f(k)|F|^{O(1)}\); otherwise its classification must be stated relative to that particular parameterization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parameterized MaxSAT asks whether the optimum meets a bound, with complexity measured as a function of a chosen objective or structural parameter.
knowledge_statements.title: Parameterized MaxSAT Complexity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is a generic parameterized formulation rather than a parameter-specific MaxSAT classification. A source is needed, and the running-time input size should explicitly include the encodings of the bound and parameter rather than using only |F|.

Enumerating every \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\), checking all constraints, and evaluating the objective solves feasibility, threshold decision, and optimization in time \(O(2^n\operatorname{poly}(N))\). Thus the problem is fixed-parameter tractable parameterized by \(n\).

assumptions_latex: Every constraint and objective value is evaluable in time polynomial in its explicit encoding length.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Descending linear search beginning from a satisfiable objective bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(L\leftarrow L_0\), retain a model of cost \(U\leftarrow U_0\), and repeat while \(L<U\). Upon termination output the retained model and \(U\). Since every satisfiable query strictly decreases the integer upper bound and the first unsatisfiable query proves \(C\ge U\), the output satisfies \(L=U=\operatorname{OPT}(F)\).

Therefore \(C(a)=b=\operatorname{OPT}(F)\).

The SAT model is checked.

Every preceding query proves \(\operatorname{OPT}(F)>b-1\), while the final model proves \(\operatorname{OPT}(F)\le C(a)\le b\). Hence \[C(a)=b=\operatorname{OPT}(F).\] If an initial feasible upper bound \(U_0\) is known, reaching \(b>U_0\) signals inconsistent input bounds.

If the transcript terminates with equal valid bounds \(L=U=v\) and retains a checked model \(a\) of cost \(v\), then \(a\) is optimal.

Every transcript response and bound update is independently checked.

If satisfiable with model \(a\), retain \(a\) and set \(U\leftarrow C(a)\), which is at most \(b\). If unsatisfiable, set \(L\leftarrow b+1\). When \(L=U\), output the retained model. The invariant \[L\le\operatorname{OPT}(F)\le U\] is preserved, and the interval length is at least halved by every query, giving at most \(\lceil\log_2(U_0-L_0+1)\rceil\) queries.

children.title: Hybrid Bound Search
children.top_down_role: Search policies combining multiple objective-bound refinement strategies.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case threshold-query bound under strict integer-gap reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L_0\le U_0\) be valid integer bounds. If every hybrid threshold query preserves \(L\le\operatorname{OPT}(F)\le U\) and strictly decreases \(U-L\), then at most \(U_0-L_0\) queries occur before \(L=U\). The bound is attained by policies reducing the gap by exactly one per query; midpoint phases can be faster.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any sound hybrid policy with strict integer-gap progress terminates within the initial bound gap.
assumptions_latex: \(L_0,U_0\in\mathbb Z\).
Every nonterminal query strictly decreases \(U-L\).
All updates preserve valid bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{queries}}\le U_0-L_0.
knowledge_statements.title: Policy-Independent Hybrid Query Bound

assumptions_latex: A satisfiability oracle decides \(F\land(C\le b)\).
At every iteration, \(L\le\operatorname{OPT}(F)\le U\), with a model witnessing \(U\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize valid integer bounds \(L,U\) and retain a model of cost \(U\). While \(L<U\), a policy chooses either a linear threshold or a midpoint threshold \(b\) with \(L\le b<U\), then queries \(F\land(C\le b)\). On SAT with model \(a\), retain \(a\) and set \(U\leftarrow C(a)\). On UNSAT, set \(L\leftarrow b+1\). Require every chosen threshold to make \(U-L\) strictly smaller. Stop at \(L=U\) and output the retained model, whose cost equals \(\operatorname{OPT}(F)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hybrid search switches among valid threshold policies while preserving bounds and requiring every SAT call to shrink the objective interval.
knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Bound Search

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invariant underlying most-significant-bit-first objective search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Immediately before processing bit position \(r\), suppose \[p2^{r+1}\le\operatorname{OPT}(F)<(p+1)2^{r+1}.\] Querying whether \(C<(2p+1)2^r\) selects the lower half on SAT and the upper half on UNSAT. Updating \(p\) to \(2p\) or \(2p+1\), respectively, yields \[p'2^r\le\operatorname{OPT}(F)<(p'+1)2^r.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each exact threshold response fixes the next binary digit and halves the power-of-two interval containing the optimum.

Threshold queries are exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: After processing bit \(r\), the updated prefix \(p'\) identifies the unique width-\(2^r\) interval containing the optimum.

Bitwise Bound Search

For \(r=q-1,q-2,\ldots,0\), query whether a feasible assignment satisfies \[C<(2p+1)2^r.\] If the query is satisfiable with model \(a\), set \(p\leftarrow2p\) and retain \(a\); otherwise set \(p\leftarrow2p+1\). children.title: Bound-Policy Switching Regimes
children.top_down_role: Conditions governing transitions between bound-search policies.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sound Updates Alone Do Not Ensure Termination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary for adaptive bound-policy switching without admissible-threshold or fairness requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(L<U\), a feasible incumbent has cost \(U\), and a policy may query \(b=U\). The query may return the same incumbent, so the sound update \(U\leftarrow C(a)=U\) leaves \((L,U)\) unchanged. Repeating this choice preserves \(L\le\operatorname{OPT}(F)\le U\) indefinitely but does not terminate. Thus bound soundness alone is insufficient for a general termination guarantee; an interior-threshold, well-founded-progress, or suitable fairness condition is additionally required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sound switching policy can loop forever if it repeatedly chooses a threshold that leaves both bounds unchanged.
assumptions_latex: The policy permits the nonprogressing threshold \(b=U\).
The incumbent satisfies \(C\le U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Bound validity is preserved while \(U-L\) remains unchanged, so termination does not follow from soundness alone.

notation.meaning: Current valid lower and feasible upper bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Sound Updates Alone Do Not Ensure Termination

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: correctness conditions for adaptive bound-policy switching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correctness conditions for switching among linear, binary, and bitwise bound policies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A bound-policy switching rule is sound when, for every history \(H\), it selects a threshold \(b\) satisfying \(L\le b<U\), interprets SAT by replacing \(U\) with a witnessed cost at most \(b\), and interprets UNSAT by replacing \(L\) with \(b+1\). It is terminating when every selection strictly decreases the nonnegative integer measure \(U-L\). Under these conditions, arbitrary finite switching among policies preserves \[L\le\operatorname{OPT}(F)\le U\] and terminates only at \(L=U=\operatorname{OPT}(F)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A switching policy is correct when every selected threshold preserves valid bounds and strictly shrinks their integer interval.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unweighted partial MaxSAT, using core-local relaxation and one-unit core constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize the working formula with \(H\cup S\) and counter \(j\leftarrow0\). On SAT, output the model and \(j\). On UNSAT, obtain a core \(K\). If \(K\subseteq H\), report hard-clause inconsistency. Otherwise set \(j\leftarrow j+1\); for each soft clause \(C\in K\) not already relaxed for this core, introduce a fresh variable \(r_C\) and replace its core occurrence by \(C\lor r_C\). Add the core-local constraint \[\sum_{C\in K\cap S}r_C=1,\] encode it propositionally, and repeat. Under the MSU1 core-relaxation invariant, the first satisfiable iteration has optimum cost \(j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: MSU1 repeatedly relaxes soft clauses in an unsatisfiable core, adds a one-unit core constraint, and stops when the working formula becomes satisfiable.
knowledge_statements.title: MSU1 Algorithm Family

children.title: Core-Local Relaxation

knowledge_statements.title: Core-Local Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unweighted partial MaxSAT relaxation of the soft clauses occurring in one detected unsatisfiable core.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=H\land\bigwedge_{C\in S}C\), where \(H\) contains hard clauses and \(S\) contains soft clauses. For an unsatisfiable core \(U\subseteq H\cup S\), put \(S_U=U\cap S\). Introduce a fresh relaxation variable \(r_C\) for every \(C\in S_U\), replace \(C\) by \(C\lor r_C\), and add the core-local constraint \[\sum_{C\in S_U}r_C=1.\] Clauses outside \(S_U\) remain unchanged, and no hard clause is relaxed. Every assignment satisfying the transformed formula designates exactly one soft clause from the core as the relaxation selected for that iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relax only soft clauses in the current unsatisfiable core, attach fresh indicators, and require exactly one indicator to be selected.

\(U\) is an unsatisfiable core containing at least one soft clause.
All \(r_C\) are fresh Boolean variables.

children.title: Core-Local Relaxation Boundaries

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accounting boundary when repeated core occurrences receive independent indicators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose one original soft clause \(C\) occurs in two processed cores and distinct transformed copies \(C\lor r_1\) and \(C\lor r_2\) are retained. Any assignment falsifying \(C\) forces \(r_1=r_2=1\), so \(r_1+r_2=2\) although only one original soft clause is violated. Thus summing occurrence-specific indicators need not equal original MaxSAT cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent indicators for overlapping core occurrences can count one violated clause more than once.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exactly-One Local Relaxation Is Not Projection-Equivalent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of interpreting an exactly-one core constraint as a standalone relaxation of original soft clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For soft clauses \(C_1=(x)\) and \(C_2=(x)\), the formula \((C_1\lor r_1)\land(C_2\lor r_2)\land(r_1+r_2=1)\) has no extension when \(x=0\), although \(x=0\) is a valid assignment of the original MaxSAT instance with cost two. knowledge_statements.title: Exactly-One Local Relaxation Is Not Projection-Equivalent
Core-Local Relaxation Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary for independently adding relaxation variables and local cardinality constraints to overlapping cores.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Core-local constraints are not, by themselves, a global encoding of the number of violated original soft clauses. Consider one original soft clause \(C\) occurring in two extracted cores. If separate iterations replace it by copies \(C\lor r_1\) and \(C\lor r_2\), then an assignment falsifying \(C\) forces both \(r_1=r_2=1\). Thus \(r_1+r_2=2\), although only one original soft clause is violated. Consequently, summing independently created local indicators can overcount violations unless the algorithm maintains clause-copy semantics, compatible cardinality constraints, or another invariant relating indicators to original clauses.

children.title: MSU3 Algorithm Family
children.top_down_role: Structural variants associated with the MSU3 lineage.

knowledge_statements.title: MSU3 Algorithm Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear lower-bound form of unweighted core-guided MaxSAT using one global cardinality bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given hard clauses \(H\) and soft clauses \(S\), initialize \(R=\varnothing\) and \(\lambda=0\). Repeatedly call a SAT solver on \[H\land\bigwedge_{C\in S}(C\lor r_C)\land\left(\sum_{r\in R}r\leq\lambda\right),\] where a variable \(r_C\) is created and added to \(R\) when \(C\) first occurs in an returned unsatisfiable core. If the call is satisfiable, return its assignment and cost \(\lambda\). If it is unsatisfiable and the core contains an unrelaxed soft clause, create the corresponding variables, set \(\lambda\leftarrow\lambda+1\), rebuild the global bound, and continue. A core consisting only of hard clauses certifies infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: MSU3 grows a global set of relaxation variables and increases one global violation bound after each relevant unsatisfiable core.
assumptions_latex: The instance is unweighted partial MaxSAT.
The SAT solver returns an unsatisfiable core when its query is unsatisfiable.
Each soft clause receives at most one relaxation variable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A satisfiable query at bound \(\lambda\) returns a solution permitting at most \(\lambda\) selected relaxations.

children.title: Global Bound Constraints
children.top_down_role: Objective-bound constraints spanning the accumulated relaxation variables.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Incomplete Indicator Coverage Is Not a Global Cost Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coverage boundary for interpreting an at-most constraint as a bound on total MaxSAT cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a counted soft clause has no indicator in \(R\), and no other bounded indicator is forced by its falsity, then \(B(R,\lambda)\) does not bound total soft-clause violations. In particular, \(B(\varnothing,0)\) holds for every assignment regardless of how many unrepresented soft clauses are false.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An at-most constraint is a global cost bound only for violations covered by its indicator set and accounting map.
assumptions_latex: At least one counted soft-clause violation is unrepresented in \(R\).
No alternative bounded variable charges that violation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: B(R,\lambda)\not\Rightarrow |\{i:C_i(x)=0\}|\leq\lambda.
knowledge_statements.title: Incomplete Indicator Coverage Is Not a Global Cost Bound

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nesting and Monotonicity of Global Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order properties of global at-most constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For Boolean sets \(R\subseteq R'\) and integers \(0\leq\lambda<\mu\), \[B(R,\lambda)\Rightarrow B(R,\mu),\qquad B(R',\lambda)\Rightarrow B(R,\lambda).\] Thus lowering the numerical bound or enlarging the bounded indicator set strengthens the constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Smaller limits and larger covered indicator sets produce stronger global bounds.
assumptions_latex: All indicators are Boolean.
Every displayed bound is well formed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: B(R,\lambda)\Rightarrow B(R,\mu)\text{ and }B(R',\lambda)\Rightarrow B(R,\lambda).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Global At-Most Bound and Projection Semantics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact unweighted threshold representation when every counted soft clause has one associated indicator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For soft clauses \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\), introduce Boolean indicators \(r_i\) and impose \[\bigwedge_{i=1}^m(C_i\lor r_i)\quad\land\quad B(R,\lambda):\sum_{i=1}^m r_i\leq\lambda.\] For every assignment \(x\) to the original variables, an extension \(r\) exists if and only if at most \(\lambda\) of the clauses \(C_i\) are false under \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The global indicator bound projects exactly to the constraint that at most lambda indexed soft clauses are false.
assumptions_latex: Each indexed soft clause has exactly one Boolean indicator in \(R\).
No additional constraint forces an indicator to one when its clause is true.
\(0\leq\lambda\leq m\) is integral.

Global Bound Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global cardinality encoding for the relaxation variables accumulated by an unweighted core-guided solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R=\{r_1,\ldots,r_m\}\) be Boolean relaxation variables attached to soft clauses and let \(0\leq\lambda\leq m\). The global-bound constraint is \[B(R,\lambda):\quad \sum_{i=1}^{m}r_i\leq\lambda.\] In conjunction with relaxed clauses \(C_i\lor r_i\), every satisfying assignment can falsify no more than \(\lambda\) clauses whose falsity forces their associated indicators to one. The bound is global because it contains every relaxation variable introduced so far, rather than only variables belonging to the most recently extracted core.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A single cardinality constraint limits the total selected relaxation indicators accumulated across all processed cores.
assumptions_latex: Every \(r_i\) is Boolean.
Each included indicator is associated with a relaxed soft clause.

children.title: Global-Bound Refinement Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes governing refinement of globally scoped bounds.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle-call bounds for linear and bisection refinement of a fixed nested threshold family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For bounds in \(\{0,\ldots,n\}\), consecutive linear refinement needs at most \(n+1\) threshold queries. Given valid bounds \(L<U\) with thresholds below \(L\) infeasible and threshold \(U\) feasible, bisection needs at most \(\lceil\log_2(U-L)\rceil\) additional threshold queries to identify the minimum feasible bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed threshold family supports linear scanning or logarithmic bisection; these counts do not cover formula-changing core updates.
assumptions_latex: Every query belongs to the same nested threshold family.
The bisection regime begins with a valid infeasible/feasible bracket.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q_{\mathrm{linear}}\le n+1,\qquad Q_{\mathrm{bisect}}\le\lceil\log_2(U-L)\rceil.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Universe Threshold-Probe Counts

Such an implication requires an explicit transformation invariant preserving the represented original assignments and their costs.

knowledge_statements.title: Growing-Universe Comparability Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimality of threshold refinement over one fixed relaxation-variable universe.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\) be fixed and let \(F_k=F\land(\sum_{r\in R}r\le k)\). Then \(F_k\Rightarrow F_{k+1}\). If \(F_0,\ldots,F_{k-1}\) are unsatisfiable and \(F_k\) is satisfiable, then \(k\) is the minimum feasible bound over \(R\).

Global-Bound Refinement Regimes

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed Boolean variables \(R\), the feasible sets of the global constraints are nested: \[\{r:B(R,0)\}\subseteq\{r:B(R,1)\}\subseteq\cdots\subseteq\{r:B(R,|R|)\}.\] Hence a linear lower-bound regime may initialize \(\lambda=0\) and replace \(\lambda\) by \(\lambda+1\) whenever the current query is unsatisfiable. If \(R\) grows after core extraction, the next query uses the enlarged set in the same global constraint. The first satisfiable query identifies the smallest tested bound only when every smaller bound has been proved unsatisfiable under the corresponding relaxation-variable invariant.

children.title: MSU4 Algorithm Family
children.top_down_role: Structural variants associated with the MSU4 lineage.

knowledge_statements.title: MSU4 Algorithm Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract two-sided core-guided MaxSAT scheme; exact MSU4 update conventions remain source-dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain integer bounds \(L\) and \(U\) on the optimum number of violated soft clauses, initially \(L=0\) and \(U=|S|\) or the cost of a known feasible assignment. Choose an integer probe \(k\) with \(L\leq k<U\) and query a relaxed SAT encoding containing \(\sum_{r\in R}r\leq k\). A satisfiable query yields a model of cost \(c\leq k\) and updates \(U\leftarrow\min(U,c)\). An unsatisfiable query, together with its core and a sound relaxation update, establishes a stronger lower bound and updates \(L\). Stop when \(L=U\), returning the incumbent model and value \(L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The MSU4 family combines core-derived lower bounds with model-derived upper bounds and terminates when the bounds meet.
assumptions_latex: The instance is unweighted partial MaxSAT.
Every unsatisfiable update produces a valid lower bound.
Every incumbent cost is a valid upper bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When \(L=U\), the common value is the optimum and the incumbent is optimal.

notation.meaning: current lower and upper bounds on optimum cost

A primary source is needed to fix probe and core-update rules.

children.title: Two-Sided Core-Guided Search
children.top_down_role: Core-guided search maintaining complementary objective bounds.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic protocol using exact bounded queries, UNSAT evidence, and feasible incumbents without imposing MSU4-specific transformations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain \(L\le f^*\le U\), where \(U\) is attained. Choose \(k\) with \(L\le k<U\) and issue an exact query equivalent to \(\exists x\,[x\models H\land f(x)\le k]\). If SAT returns \(x\), set \(U\leftarrow\min(U,f(x))\). If UNSAT, optionally accompanied by a core validating the result, set \(L\leftarrow k+1\). Repeat until \(L=U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Probe an exact objective threshold; a model lowers the incumbent, while an unsatisfiable threshold raises the lower bound.
assumptions_latex: The objective is integer-valued.
Each bounded query is equivalent to the stated original-instance threshold problem.
Every SAT model is checked against the original hard clauses and objective.
Every UNSAT result is sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L=U\Longrightarrow f^*=L=U.
review_flags: This is a generic exact search protocol, not a claim about a particular MSU4 implementation.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Two-Sided Core-Guided Threshold Search

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condition under which an UNSAT transformed query may raise the original objective lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Unsatisfiability of an auxiliary or relaxed formula \(G_k\) justifies \(f^*>k\) only if every original hard-feasible assignment \(x\) with \(f(x)\le k\) extends to a model of \(G_k\). Without this extension property, \(G_k\) may be unsatisfiable even though the original instance has cost at most \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A transformed query can raise the global lower bound only when it represents every original solution within the tested threshold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{UNSAT}(G_k)\Rightarrow f^*>k\text{ requires threshold-complete encoding}.
knowledge_statements.title: Transformed-Query Soundness Boundary
Two-Sided Core-Guided Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bound-convergence principle combining unsatisfiable cores and feasible MaxSAT assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f^*\) denote the minimum number of violated soft clauses. A two-sided core-guided search maintains \(L\leq f^*\leq U\). Unsatisfiable bounded SAT queries and their cores may increase \(L\), while satisfying assignments of cost \(c\) may decrease \(U\) to \(\min(U,c)\). Every update must preserve the invariant \(L\leq f^*\leq U\). If an iteration produces \(L=U\), then no assignment has cost below \(L\), and the incumbent attaining \(U\) has cost \(L\); therefore the incumbent is optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cores raise a lower bound, feasible models lower an upper bound, and equality of the two bounds certifies optimality.
assumptions_latex: The objective is the number of violated soft clauses.
Lower-bound updates are sound.
The upper bound is attained by a stored feasible assignment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L=U\) certifies that the stored assignment has optimal cost \(f^*=L=U\).
review_flags: General bound principle is standard, but its intended MSU4 specialization lacks a relevant source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bound-convergence principle is mathematically sound and its content kind fits, but no citation supports its intended specialization to the MSU4 family.

children.title: Two-Sided Bound Interaction
children.top_down_role: Interaction between the complementary bounds during search.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact certification when complementary bounds meet.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(L\le f^*\), a checked hard-feasible assignment \(x\) has cost \(f(x)=U\), and \(L=U\), then \(f(x)=f^*=L=U\). Numeric equality is not a certificate if the lower bound lacks global validity or the upper value is not attained by a checked assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A globally valid lower bound and an attaining feasible assignment certify optimality when their values agree.
assumptions_latex: \(L\) is globally valid.
\(x\) is checked hard-feasible and \(U=f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L=U\Longrightarrow f(x)=f^*.
knowledge_statements.title: Attained Zero-Gap Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp failure of termination when strict progress is omitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any \(f^*\in[0,1]\), the constant sequence \(L_t=0\), \(U_t=1\) is valid and monotone for all \(t\), yet its gap never closes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Monotone bounds alone do not ensure termination: both bounds may remain unchanged forever.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Monotonicity}\not\Rightarrow\text{finite convergence}.
knowledge_statements.title: Monotonicity Without Progress

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interaction of valid attained upper bounds and valid lower bounds during exact MaxSAT search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(L_t\le f^*\le U_t\), \(L_{t+1}\ge L_t\), and \(U_{t+1}\le U_t\), then \(0\le U_{t+1}-L_{t+1}\le U_t-L_t\). If the bounds are integral and every nonterminal iteration strictly changes at least one bound, termination occurs after at most \(U_0-L_0\) nonterminal iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Valid lower bounds rise, attained upper bounds fall, and strict integer progress closes the interval in at most its initial width.
assumptions_latex: All bounds are integral.
Every update preserves \(L_t\le f^*\le U_t\).
At least one bound changes strictly at every nonterminal iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T\le U_0-L_0.

notation.meaning: lower and upper objective bounds at iteration t

knowledge_statements.title: Monotone Integer Bound Interval
Two-Sided Bound Interaction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonicity and termination condition for interacting lower and upper MaxSAT bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose iteration \(t\) maintains valid integer bounds \(L_t\leq f^*\leq U_t\). A sound core-derived update and a feasible-model update satisfy \[L_t\leq L_{t+1}\leq f^*\leq U_{t+1}\leq U_t.\] Thus the interval width \(U_t-L_t\) never increases. If every nonterminal iteration strictly raises \(L_t\) or strictly lowers \(U_t\), the process terminates after at most \(U_0-L_0\) unit reductions of the integer interval. At termination with zero width, both bounds equal the optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sound lower bounds rise, attained upper bounds fall, and strict integer progress forces convergence when their interval closes.
assumptions_latex: All costs and bounds are integers.
Each update preserves \(L_t\leq f^*\leq U_t\).
Every nonterminal iteration strictly shrinks the bound interval.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U_t-L_t\) decreases to zero in at most \(U_0-L_0\) strict unit reductions.

children.title: Weighted MSU Families
children.top_down_role: MSU-style families for weighted soft clauses.

knowledge_statements.title: Weighted MSU Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Core-guided weighted partial MaxSAT using residual weights and minimum-weight core extraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let each soft clause \(C\) have positive integer residual weight \(w_C\), and initialize \(L=0\). Query the current residual formula. If it is unsatisfiable, extract a core with soft portion \(K\), set \(m=\min_{C\in K}w_C\), update \(L\leftarrow L+m\), and split each \(C\in K\) into a residual copy of weight \(w_C-m\) when positive and an extracted copy of weight \(m\) carrying a fresh relaxation indicator. Add the family-specific core constraint over the new indicators and repeat. If the residual query is satisfiable, return the resulting model with the accumulated weighted accounting prescribed by the maintained constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted MSU algorithms extract the minimum residual core weight, split core clauses, and add constrained relaxation indicators.
assumptions_latex: Soft-clause weights are positive integers.
Every unsatisfiable query returns a core containing a positive-weight soft clause.
Splitting and core constraints preserve weighted-cost accounting.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each core iteration increases the certified lower bound by \(m>0\) and preserves an equivalent residual accounting problem.

soft clauses in the extracted core
minimum residual weight in the core

children.title: Weight-Splitting Variants
children.top_down_role: Variants partitioning clause weights across relaxation events.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between an algebraic split and equivalence of the fully augmented solver state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After different relaxation variables or auxiliary constraints are attached to descendants, weight conservation remains necessary but is no longer sufficient for transformed-instance equivalence. Equivalence additionally requires that minimizing over auxiliary variables reproduces the original clause penalty for every assignment to original variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Once split copies receive different auxiliary constraints, their weights summing correctly does not by itself preserve the optimization problem.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Replacing a unit-weight clause \((C,1)\) by two identical copies of weights \(1/4\) and \(1/4\) changes the penalty of every assignment violating \(C\) from \(1\) to \(1/2\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact decomposition of one soft-clause penalty before auxiliary constraints distinguish descendants.

Descendant weights are nonnegative and sum exactly to \(w\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive clause-weight decomposition used when a weighted unsatisfiable core is processed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let a soft clause \(C\) have residual weight \(w>0\), and let \(m\) satisfy \(0<m\leq w\). Replace its weighted penalty by two copies of the same clause with weights \(w-m\) and \(m\), omitting the first copy when \(w=m\). For every truth assignment \(x\), \[w\,\mathbf{1}[x
ot\models C]=(w-m)\mathbf{1}[x
ot\models C]+m\mathbf{1}[x

\(m\) satisfies \(0<m\leq w\).

children.title: Residual-Weight Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes distinguished by the treatment of remaining clause weight.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite progress when an extraction subtracts positive integral weight from at least one active residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\sum_C\rho_C\) over the canonical active residual ledger. If each iteration chooses an integer \(m\ge1\) and subtracts it from every member of a nonempty set \(K\), then \(P' = P-|K|m<P\). Hence at most \(P_0\le\sum_C w_C\) such iterations occur.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With positive integral extraction and a canonical residual ledger, total residual weight strictly decreases and bounds the number of extractions.
assumptions_latex: Residual weights are positive integers when active.
The potential counts each original clause's active residual exactly once.
Extracted layers are not re-added to the residual potential.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{extract}}\le P_0\le\sum_Cw_C.

notation.meaning: nonempty set of residuals reduced in an extraction

knowledge_statements.title: Integral Residual-Extraction Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Why copy-level sums require a canonical ownership convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If multiple syntactic descendants representing the same residual weight are all included in \(P\), copy creation or duplication can increase \(P\) even while each selected copy is reduced. Therefore a decreasing-potential claim requires a canonical per-original-clause ledger or another explicitly conserved aggregate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Summing every syntactic copy can double count residual weight, so the progress potential must have canonical ownership.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Uncanonical copy sum need not be monotone}.
knowledge_statements.title: Duplicate-Residual Potential Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-clause accounting invariant for repeated extraction of positive weight layers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each original soft clause \(C\) of weight \(w_C\), maintain extracted layer weights \(a_{C,1},\ldots,a_{C,q}\ge0\) and active residual weight \(\rho_C\ge0\) such that \(w_C=\rho_C+\sum_{j=1}^q a_{C,j}\). Extracting \(m\le\rho_C\) replaces \(\rho_C\) by \(\rho_C-m\) and appends a layer of weight \(m\), preserving the identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every original clause weight is conserved as active residual weight plus its extracted layers.
assumptions_latex: All layer and residual weights are nonnegative.
Every extraction is charged once in the clause's ledger.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: w_C=\rho_C+\sum_j a_{C,j}\text{ remains invariant}.

notation.meaning: active residual weight of original clause C
j-th extracted weight layer of C

knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Layer Conservation Ledger
Residual-Weight Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Progress invariant for minimum-core-weight subtraction with positive integral residual weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an extracted core with positive residual weights \(\{w_C:C\in K\}\), define \(m=\min_{C\in K}w_C\) and update each residual by \(w'_C=w_C-m\). Then \(w'_C\geq0\) for every \(C\in K\), and at least one clause satisfies \(w'_C=0\). Zero-weight residual copies may be removed, while positive residual copies remain eligible for later cores. Moreover, if \(W=\sum_C w_C\), then every iteration decreases the total residual weight by at least \(m\geq1\); consequently no more than the initial value of \(W\) such positive integral extractions are possible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subtracting a core's minimum residual weight preserves nonnegativity, eliminates at least one residual layer, and gives finite progress for integer weights.
assumptions_latex: All active residual weights are positive integers.
The extracted core has a nonempty soft portion \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(w'_C\geq0\), some \(w'_C=0\), and the aggregate residual weight strictly decreases.

notation.meaning: soft portion of the current core
minimum active residual weight in K

children.title: PM2 Algorithm Family

knowledge_statements.title: PM2 Algorithm Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract PM2 scheme using covers of accumulated cores to generate regional cardinality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an unweighted partial MaxSAT instance, associate a Boolean relaxation variable \(r_C\) with each relaxable soft clause and maintain a family \(\mathcal{K}\) of discovered soft-core sets. After an unsatisfiable SAT query returns a core \(K\), add \(K\) to \(\mathcal{K}\), select a cover \(\mathcal{Q}\) whose regions contain every set in \(\mathcal{K}\), and impose family-specific cardinality bounds on \(\sum_{C\in Q}r_C\) for \(Q\in\mathcal{Q}\). Reissue the SAT query with the updated cover constraints. Terminate on satisfiability and return the model, or report infeasibility if a hard-only core is found. Soundness requires the regional bounds to encode a valid lower-bound accounting of all covered cores.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: PM2 accumulates soft cores, groups them into covers, and refines regional cardinality constraints until the relaxed formula becomes satisfiable.
assumptions_latex: The instance is unweighted partial MaxSAT.
Every unsatisfiable query supplies a core.
Cover constraints preserve valid accounting across overlapping cores.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A satisfiable terminal query yields a model consistent with all accumulated cover-based constraints.

notation.meaning: relaxation variable for soft clause C

review_flags: PM2 cover construction and bound formulas cannot be fixed reliably from the path alone.
Primary PM2 source required before promotion.

children.title: Cover-Based Constraint Families

knowledge_statements.title: Cover-Based Constraint Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract PM2-style representation; exact cover construction varies among implementations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\) be the relaxation literals of a partial MaxSAT instance, and let \(\mathcal K\subseteq 2^B\) be the relaxation-literal sets induced by discovered unsatisfiable cores. A cover is a subfamily \(\mathcal C\subseteq\mathcal K\). Writing \(U(\mathcal C)=\bigcup_{K\in\mathcal C}K\), a cover-based constraint has the form \[\sum_{b\in U(\mathcal C)} b\geq \lambda(\mathcal C),\] where \(\lambda(\mathcal C)\) is a valid lower bound on the number of relaxed soft clauses required jointly by the covered cores. Every assignment satisfying the original hard clauses and all soft-clause relaxations must satisfy each such constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A family of discovered cores yields lower-bound constraints on how many relaxation literals must be selected across the cores’ union.
assumptions_latex: \(B\) is finite and Boolean-valued.
Each member of \(\mathcal K\) arises from a valid unsatisfiable core.
Each \(\lambda(\mathcal C)\) is a valid joint relaxation lower bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{b\in U(\mathcal C)}b\geq\lambda(\mathcal C)\) is valid for every selected cover \(\mathcal C\).

PM2-specific definition of cover multiplicity requires source confirmation.

children.title: Cover-Selection Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Cover-Selection Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity condition shared by alternative PM2-style cover-selection policies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given discovered core sets \(\mathcal K\), a cover-selection regime chooses a sequence \((\mathcal C_t,\lambda_t)\), where \(\mathcal C_t\subseteq\mathcal K\). It is admissible if, at every iteration \(t\), every assignment \(x\) satisfying the hard clauses and the relaxed soft clauses obeys \[\sum_{b\in U(\mathcal C_t)}x_b\geq\lambda_t.\] Regimes may select one core, a disjoint collection, or an overlapping collection, but overlap must not cause the same core-derived lower-bound contribution to be counted twice without an independently valid joint argument.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cover-selection policy is admissible exactly when every generated lower-bound constraint remains valid, including when selected cores overlap.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal K\) contains only valid core-induced relaxation sets.
\(U(\mathcal C_t)=\bigcup_{K\in\mathcal C_t}K\).
