children.title: WPM1 Algorithm Family
children.top_down_role: Structural variants associated with the WPM1 lineage.

knowledge_statements.title: WPM1 Algorithm Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard weighted partial-MaxSAT core-splitting form of WPM1.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input hard clauses \(H\) and weighted soft clauses \((C_i,w_i)\) with positive integer weights. Initialize \(L=0\). Repeatedly call SAT on the current clauses. If satisfiable, return the model and cost \(L\). Otherwise obtain an unsatisfiable core \(U\), let \(\delta=\min\{w_i:C_i\in U\}\), and set \(L\leftarrow L+\delta\). For every soft clause in \(U\), retain residual weight \(w_i-\delta\) when positive and create a weight-\(\delta\) copy \((C_i\lor b_i,\delta)\). Add a hard constraint \(\sum_{C_i\in U}b_i=1\), then repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: WPM1 repeatedly extracts a core, splits its clauses by the minimum core weight, raises the lower bound, and enforces one relaxation.
assumptions_latex: All soft weights are positive integers.
The SAT solver returns a valid unsatisfiable core.
Relaxation literals introduced in an iteration are fresh.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Upon a satisfiable iteration, the returned model has optimum weighted soft-clause violation cost \(L\).
review_flags: No relevant WPM1 source locator was supplied.
Equality versus alternative core-cardinality encodings should be checked against the intended variant.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the correct content kind, but a primary WPM1 source is required to verify the splitting procedure, exact-one constraint, objective-offset convention, and optimality conclusion.

children.title: Weighted Core Relaxation
children.top_down_role: Core relaxation sensitive to soft-clause weights.

knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Core Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum-weight splitting of a weighted unsatisfiable core.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\) be an unsatisfiable core containing weighted soft clauses \((C_i,w_i)\), and put \(\delta=\min_{C_i\in U}w_i\). Replace each such term by a residual copy \((C_i,w_i-\delta)\) when \(w_i>\delta\) and a relaxed copy \((C_i\lor b_i,\delta)\), with fresh \(b_i\). Add the hard constraint \[\sum_{C_i\in U}b_i=1.\] The extracted layer contributes \(\delta\) to the objective lower bound, while the residual copies preserve all weight above \(\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Split every core clause at the minimum core weight, relax the extracted layer, and preserve any remaining weight as a residual clause.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) is an unsatisfiable core.
Every \(w_i\) is positive.
Each \(b_i\) is fresh.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The transformation extracts a mandatory cost layer \(\delta\) and preserves residual weights \(w_i-\delta\).
review_flags: No relevant weighted MaxSAT source locator was supplied.
Exact equivalence convention depends on whether accumulated lower-bound offsets are explicit.

children.title: Weighted Relaxation Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Applicability limits arising from weighted core treatment.

knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Relaxation Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary conditions required for sound WPM1 weight extraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a weighted core \(U\), an extracted amount \(\delta\) is admissible only if \[0<\delta\leq\min_{C_i\in U}w_i.\] Each affected weight must be decomposed exactly as \(w_i=(w_i-\delta)+\delta\), zero-weight residual copies must be deleted, and the new relaxation constraint must charge exactly one extracted core layer. Choosing \(\delta\) above the minimum creates a negative residual weight; omitting a positive residual changes the objective; independently charging overlapping extracted layers without their linking constraints can overcount the lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sound weighted relaxation requires a positive extraction no larger than every core weight, exact residual preservation, and correctly linked relaxation charges.
assumptions_latex: All original soft weights are positive.
\(U\) is a valid unsatisfiable core.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stated boundaries prevent negative residuals and preserve the weighted objective accounting.
review_flags: No relevant WPM1 source locator was supplied.
Overlap accounting differs across weighted core-guided variants.

knowledge_statements.title: WPM2 Algorithm Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract WPM2 family characterized by weighted lower-bound constraints and refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input hard clauses \(H\) and soft clauses represented by relaxation literals \(b_i\) with positive weights \(w_i\). Initialize a valid objective lower bound \(L=0\) and no core constraints. Repeatedly solve \(H\land\bigwedge_i(C_i\lor b_i)\) under the current weighted bound encoding. If satisfiable at bound \(L\), return the model. If unsatisfiable, extract a core, identify a positive admissible weight layer \(\delta\), refine the core’s relaxation-literal partition and its cardinality or pseudo-Boolean constraints, and increase \(L\) by the certified increment \(\delta\). Stop at the first satisfiable certified bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: WPM2 alternates SAT calls with core-driven refinement of weighted relaxation bounds, stopping when the current certified lower bound becomes feasible.
assumptions_latex: All weights are positive integers.
Every extracted core and bound increment is valid.
Each refinement preserves all assignments of cost below the next tested bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The first satisfiable certified bound equals the optimum weighted violation cost.
review_flags: No relevant WPM2 source locator was supplied.
The intended WPM2 partition and cover-update rules cannot be selected reliably without a primary source.

children.title: Weighted Bound Refinement

knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Bound Refinement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invariant for core-driven refinement of a weighted MaxSAT lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\sum_i w_i b_i(x)\) be the relaxation cost and let \(L\) be a certified lower bound on \(\min f\) over assignments satisfying the hard clauses. A refinement generated from an unsatisfiable bounded instance is sound when it produces \(L'>L\) such that every hard-feasible assignment satisfies \(f(x)\geq L'\). If the refinement is encoded by additional cardinality or pseudo-Boolean constraints, those constraints must exclude only assignments whose cost is below \(L'\). Consequently, satisfiability at the refined bound certifies optimality whenever all smaller bounds have been excluded soundly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weighted refinement raises the lower bound only when the extracted core certifies that every feasible assignment has at least the new cost.
assumptions_latex: \(L\) is a valid lower bound.
The bounded instance at the excluded level is unsatisfiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A sound refinement yields \(L'>L\) with \(f(x)\geq L'\) for every hard-feasible assignment \(x\).

This invariant does not identify the variant-specific refinement formula.

children.title: Weight-Stratified Refinement Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Weight-Stratified Refinement Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admissibility condition for processing weighted soft clauses by descending thresholds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the distinct positive soft weights be \(\tau_1>\tau_2>\cdots>\tau_m\). A weight-stratified regime activates at stage \(k\) every objective contribution whose current residual weight is at least \(\tau_k\), while preserving lower-weight residuals for later stages. It is admissible if each split is exact, each stage constraint is valid for the active weight layer, and progress from \(\tau_k\) to \(\tau_{k+1}\) retains all earlier constraints. Under these conditions, the sum of certified layer increments never exceeds the optimum weighted cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Descending weight strata are sound when every split preserves total weight and all constraints certified at earlier thresholds remain active.
assumptions_latex: Soft weights form a finite set of positive values.
Every stage uses valid core-derived constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accumulated stratified lower bound is no greater than the optimum weighted violation cost.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which minimizing relaxation literals reproduces soft-clause violation cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the hard relaxation \(C_i\lor b_i\), if \(b_i\) is clause-specific, has no additional constraints affecting its minimizing value, and has coefficient \(w_i>0\), then \[\min_{b_i\in\{0,1\}}\{w_i b_i:C_i\lor b_i\}=w_i\mathbf 1[\neg C_i].\] With \(w_i=0\), the optimal value remains correct but \(b_i\) need not equal the violation indicator. With \(w_i<0\), minimization favors \(b_i=1\) even when \(C_i\) is true. Sharing one literal between clauses can undercount simultaneous violations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive coefficients and unconstrained clause-specific literals give both correct cost and indicator semantics; zero weights lose indicator uniqueness, negative weights reverse the incentive, and sharing may undercount.
assumptions_latex: C_i\lor b_i\text{ is imposed as a hard clause}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min\{w_i b_i:C_i\lor b_i\}=w_i\mathbf 1[\neg C_i]\text{ under the stated clause-specific positive-weight conditions}.

knowledge_statements.title: Clause-Specific Literal and Weight Boundary
Soft-Clause Objective-Literal Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-literal representation used by OLL-style MaxSAT algorithms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For hard clauses \(H\) and soft clauses \(C_i\) with weights \(w_i>0\), introduce a fresh objective literal \(b_i\) and replace each soft clause by the hard clause \(C_i\lor b_i\). Then the weighted partial-MaxSAT problem is represented as \[\min\left\{\sum_i w_i b_i: H\land\bigwedge_i(C_i\lor b_i),\ b_i\in\{0,1\}\right\}.\] For any assignment to the original variables, minimizing over the fresh literals sets \(b_i=1\) exactly when \(C_i\) is false, so the objective equals the violated-soft-clause weight.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Make each soft clause hard by adding a fresh objective literal; minimizing those literals reproduces the total violated soft-clause weight.
assumptions_latex: Each \(b_i\) is fresh and appears only in its relaxation and objective-related constraints.
Every \(w_i\) is positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reformulated Boolean objective has the same optimum as the weighted partial-MaxSAT instance.

notation.meaning: objective literal for soft clause i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of a core reformulation that retains only the first excess indicator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(q=3\), let \(o_2\leftrightarrow(b_1+b_2+b_3\ge2)\). At \((b_1,b_2,b_3)=(1,1,1)\), the original core contribution is \(3\), whereas the truncated expression \(1+o_2\) equals \(2\). Thus retaining only \(o_2\) is cost-preserving only when the encoding or other constraints ensure \(\sum_j b_j\le2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With three true core literals, a constant plus only the at-least-two output undercounts the objective by one.
assumptions_latex: o_2\leftrightarrow(b_1+b_2+b_3\ge2).
knowledge_statements.title: Truncated-Output Undercounting

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact unit-weight objective identity for an unsatisfiable core of objective literals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B_U=\{b_1,\ldots,b_q\}\) and suppose the hard constraints entail \(s:=\sum_{j=1}^q b_j\ge 1\). If unary cardinality outputs \(o_k\) satisfy \(o_k=1\Longleftrightarrow s\ge k\) for \(k=2,\ldots,q\), then on every feasible assignment \[\sum_{j=1}^q b_j=1+\sum_{k=2}^q o_k.\] Hence one objective unit may be transferred to a constant lower-bound offset while all excess cost is represented by the outputs \(o_2,\ldots,o_q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid unit core contributes one unavoidable objective unit; every further selected core literal is represented by the corresponding unary counting output.
assumptions_latex: b_j\in\{0,1\}\quad(j=1,\ldots,q).
\models\sum_{j=1}^q b_j\ge 1.
o_k\leftrightarrow\left(\sum_{j=1}^q b_j\ge k\right)\quad(k=2,\ldots,q).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_{j=1}^q b_j=1+\sum_{k=2}^q o_k.

notation.meaning: number of true objective literals in the core

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Unary-Output Core Reformulation
Cardinality-Core Objective Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: OLL reformulation of a core of unit objective literals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B_U=\{b_1,\ldots,b_q\}\) be unit-weight objective literals occurring in an unsatisfiable core under assumptions \(\neg b_j\). Since they cannot all be zero, every feasible assignment satisfies \(\sum_{j=1}^q b_j\geq1\). Introduce an indicator \(r\) for the residual excess and replace the core’s unit objective contribution by a constant lower-bound increment of one together with a cardinality encoding satisfying \[r=1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\sum_{j=1}^q b_j\geq2.\] Thus \(\sum_j b_j=1+r+e\), where any higher excess \(e\) is represented by further output literals when needed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A unit-weight core contributes one unavoidable violation; cardinality outputs represent whether the core incurs further violations beyond that first unit.
assumptions_latex: The assumptions \(\{\neg b_j:1\leq j\leq q\}\) form an unsatisfiable core.
The cardinality encoding is logically correct.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: One objective unit is extracted as a lower bound, while cardinality outputs preserve every additional unit of core cost.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp undercounting failures in minimum-weight core reformulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the minimum-weight layer identity, deleting a positive residual term \((w_i-\delta)b_i\) undercounts every feasible assignment with \(b_i=1\). Deleting an output term \(\delta o_k\) undercounts every feasible assignment with \(\sum_{i\in U}b_i\ge k\). knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact weighted OLL objective identity for one valid core of objective literals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f=\sum_i w_i b_i\) with \(w_i>0\), let \(U\) satisfy \(s_U:=\sum_{i\in U}b_i\ge1\), and put \(\delta=\min_{i\in U}w_i\). If \(o_k\leftrightarrow(s_U\ge k)\) for \(k=2,\ldots,|U|\), then on every feasible assignment \[f=\delta+\delta\sum_{k=2}^{|U|}o_k+\sum_{i\in U}(w_i-\delta)b_i+\sum_{i\notin U}w_i b_i.\] Thus \(\delta\) is an extractable constant layer, while every positive residual coefficient and every excess-count output must remain in the transformed objective.

knowledge_statements.title: Minimum-Weight Layer Identity
Weighted Objective-Reformulation Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weight-layer extension of objective-literal core reformulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For weighted objective \(f=\sum_i w_i b_i\) and a core indexed by \(U\), choose \(\delta=\min_{i\in U}w_i\). Decompose \[f=\delta\sum_{i\in U}b_i+\sum_{i\in U}(w_i-\delta)b_i+\sum_{i\notin U}w_i b_i.\] Because the core entails \(\sum_{i\in U}b_i\geq1\), extract the constant \(\delta\), represent the excess \(\delta(\sum_{i\in U}b_i-1)\) by cardinality-output objective literals, and retain every positive residual term \((w_i-\delta)b_i\). The resulting objective has the same value up to the extracted constant.

All objective weights are positive.

knowledge_statements.title: Incremental-Encoding OLL Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incremental maintenance of cardinality encodings in OLL-style core processing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize the relaxed formula, objective literals, and lower bound \(L=0\). top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Core-Guided Binary Search Algorithms for Maximum Satisfiability

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact integer-cost threshold search in which extracted cores may strengthen later queries only through globally valid consequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given integral bounds \(L\leq\operatorname{OPT}\leq U\) and a hard-feasible incumbent of cost \(U\), repeat while \(L<U\): set \(m=\lfloor(L+U)/2\rfloor\) and decide whether a hard-feasible assignment of cost at most \(m\) exists. If a model of cost \(c\leq m\) is returned, set \(U\leftarrow c\); otherwise set \(L\leftarrow m+1\). If unsatisfiable, set \(L=m+1\); any extracted soft-assumption core \(K\) may additionally be recorded through the valid constraint \(\sum_{i\in K}y_i\geq1\). Return the incumbent when \(L=U\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Extract cores \(K_1,\ldots,K_q\) while requiring them to be pairwise disjoint, and add a relaxation variable \(y_i\) for every soft clause. knowledge_statements.scope_note: Family-level exact search interleaving midpoint and bound-adjacent integer thresholds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain integral bounds \(L\leq\operatorname{OPT}\leq U\) and an incumbent of cost \(U\). Retain core-derived constraints only where valid. A hybrid policy may alternate midpoint and bound-adjacent choices, but must ensure eventual strict reduction of \(U-L\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Family-level exact scheme allowing binary and bound-adjacent MaxSAT oracle queries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain an incumbent of cost \(U\), a valid lower bound \(L\), and accumulated core constraints. At each iteration choose either a binary threshold \(b=\lfloor(L+U)/2\rfloor\) or a bound-adjacent threshold such as \(b=L\) or \(b=U-1\). Query the relaxed MaxSAT encoding with objective at most \(b\). For a satisfiable result of cost \(c\), set \(U=\min\{U,c\}\). For an unsatisfiable result, set \(L=b+1\) and retain any extracted valid core constraint. The selection policy may change between iterations, but must ensure that whenever \(L<U\), some query strictly decreases \(U-L\). Terminate when \(L=U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method interleaves midpoint and bound-adjacent cost queries. Exactness follows from valid bound updates, retained core constraints, and strict progress until the bounds meet.

assumptions_latex: The current exact MaxSAT search state has integer bounds \(L<U\).

Either selected regime preserves valid bounds and makes finite progress.

notation.meaning: Estimated costs of binary and hybrid phases

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A formal policy template; particular solvers may estimate work and choose thresholds differently.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given state statistics \(s\), define the transition predicate \(P(s)\) by \[P(s)\iff \bigl(g\leq\tau\bigr)\lor\bigl(\widehat T_h(s)\leq\widehat T_b(s)\bigr),\] where \(g=U-L\), \(\tau\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), and \(\widehat T_b,\widehat T_h\) are fixed estimators chosen before applying the comparison. Continue midpoint binary queries while \(P(s)\) is false; once it is true, use bound-adjacent or mixed hybrid queries. The transition rule is admissible for exact search only if every post-transition update preserves \(L\leq\operatorname{OPT}\leq U\) and reduces the integral gap after finitely many oracle calls.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Switch from midpoint search when the remaining gap is small or estimated hybrid work is no greater, provided all later updates preserve bounds and eventual progress.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: SAT-oracle interface used by implicit hitting-set MaxSAT methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(S\subseteq I\), query \[H\land\bigwedge_{i\in I\setminus S}C_i.\] If the formula is satisfiable, return its model; clauses indexed by \(S\) are the only soft clauses permitted to be violated. If it is unsatisfiable, extract and return \(K\subseteq I\setminus S\) such that \(H\land\bigwedge_{i\in K}C_i\) is unsatisfiable. The core may be inclusion-minimized but need not be minimum. Because no assignment satisfying \(H\) can satisfy every clause in \(K\), every feasible removal set \(S'\) must obey \(S'\cap K\neq\varnothing\). Thus \(K\) is a valid constraint for the hitting-set master.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The oracle tests the clauses not removed by a master candidate. It returns either a feasible model or an unsatisfiable core that every feasible removal set must intersect.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exactness over the Complete Core Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact master characterization when every soft-clause core is represented.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal K_{\mathrm{all}}=\{K\subseteq I:H\land\bigwedge_{i\in K}C_i\text{ is unsatisfiable}\}\). If \(H\) is satisfiable, then \(H\land\bigwedge_{i\in I\setminus S}C_i\) is satisfiable exactly when \(S\cap K\ne\varnothing\) for every \(K\in\mathcal K_{\mathrm{all}}\). Thus the complete-core hitting-set optimum equals the weighted partial-MaxSAT optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hitting every soft-clause core is equivalent to being a feasible removal set, so the complete-core master is exact.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) is finite.
\(H\) is satisfiable.
\(w_i\ge0\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_{S:\forall K\in\mathcal K_{\mathrm{all}},\ S\cap K\ne\varnothing}\sum_{i\in S}w_i=\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{MaxSAT}}.

notation.meaning: Family of all soft-index cores relative to the hard clauses

knowledge_statements.title: Exactness over the Complete Core Family

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Component Decomposition of the Current-Core Master
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact decomposition when the current core hypergraph has disconnected incidence components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition \(I=I_1\dot\cup\cdots\dot\cup I_p\) so that every \(K\in\mathcal K\) is contained in exactly one \(I_j\), and let \(\mathcal K_j=\{K\in\mathcal K:K\subseteq I_j\}\). Then the current-core minimum-weight hitting-set master decomposes into independent component masters, \[v(\mathcal K)=\sum_{j=1}^p v(\mathcal K_j).\] The union of component-optimal hitting sets is globally optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Disconnected incidence components of the current core hypergraph can be solved independently, and their optimal costs add.
assumptions_latex: I_1,\ldots,I_p\text{ are pairwise disjoint and cover }I.
\forall K\in\mathcal K\;\exists!j\text{ such that }K\subseteq I_j.
The objective is additive: \(w(S)=\sum_{i\in S}w_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v(\mathcal K)=\sum_{j=1}^p v(\mathcal K_j).

notation.meaning: Cores wholly contained in incidence component j.
Minimum hitting-set weight for component j.

knowledge_statements.title: Component Decomposition of the Current-Core Master

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact binary formulation and lower-bound interpretation for the currently known cores.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For finite soft index set \(I\), weights \(w_i\ge0\), and valid current core family \(\mathcal K\), define \[v(\mathcal K)=\min\left\{\sum_{i\in I}w_i z_i:z_i\in\{0,1\},\ \sum_{i\in K}z_i\ge1\ \forall K\in\mathcal K\right\}.\] Feasible incidence vectors correspond exactly to hitting sets \(S(z)=\{i:z_i=1\}\). Every feasible MaxSAT removal set hits every valid core, so \(v(\mathcal K)\) lower-bounds the full removal optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary variables select a minimum-weight set intersecting every known core, and the resulting value lower-bounds the full MaxSAT removal cost.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) and \(\mathcal K\) are finite.
Every \(K\in\mathcal K\) is a valid soft-index core.
\(w_i\ge0\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v(\mathcal K)=\min_{S:\,S\cap K\ne\varnothing\ \forall K\in\mathcal K}\sum_{i\in S}w_i\le\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{MaxSAT}}.

notation.meaning: Indicator selecting soft clause i for removal.

knowledge_statements.title: Binary Current-Core Minimum-Weight Hitting-Set Master

assumptions_latex: \(I\) is finite and each soft clause has weight \(w_i>0\).
\(\mathcal K\) is the current finite family of extracted soft-clause cores.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An optimizer \(S^*=\{i:z_i^*=1\}\) is a minimum-weight set intersecting every core currently known to the master.

notation.meaning: Binary selection variable for removing soft clause i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integer master problem over the finite core family accumulated so far.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The minimum-weight hitting-set master associated with \(\mathcal K\) is \[\min_{z\in\{0,1\}^{I}}\ \sum_{i\in I}w_i z_i\qquad\text{subject to}\qquad \sum_{i\in K}z_i\geq1\quad\text{for every }K\in\mathcal K.\] For any feasible vector \(z\), the set \(S(z)=\{i\in I:z_i=1\}\) intersects every known core. Conversely, the incidence vector of every hitting set of \(\mathcal K\) is feasible. Hence the master optimum equals the minimum total weight of a hitting set for the currently extracted cores; it is a lower bound on the full MaxSAT removal cost until the oracle validates its optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A binary integer program selects a minimum-weight set of soft clauses intersecting every extracted core. Its value lower-bounds the full MaxSAT optimum until oracle validation.
knowledge_statements.title: Minimum-Weight Hitting-Set Master

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is a correct finite minimum-weight hitting-set master for the currently known cores, but its nontrivial connection to IHS MaxSAT is unsupported by a cited source.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case oracle-call bound for the finite abstract-core loop.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let E be finite. If every rejection of S\subseteq E returns a permanently retained conflict K\subseteq E\setminus S, then S violates the new master constraint S\cap K\ne\varnothing and cannot recur. Hence at most 2^{|E|} distinct candidates are submitted to the oracle, including the final accepted candidate when one exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every retained conflict permanently excludes the rejected candidate, so there is at most one oracle call per subset of the finite ground set.
assumptions_latex: |E|<\infty.
Every returned conflict is retained.
Every later master candidate hits every retained conflict.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{oracle}}\leq 2^{|E|}.

notation.meaning: finite ground set of removable constraints

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Candidate-Exclusion Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal families witnessing the two independent exactness failures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let E=\{a,b\} with w_a<w_b. If both \{a\} and \{b\} are acceptable, adding the invalid conflict K=\{b\} excludes the optimal acceptable set \{a\}. Separately, with the valid retained conflict \{a,b\}, a master that returns the feasible hitting set \{b\} may be oracle-accepted although the acceptable hitting set \{a\} has smaller cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With two weighted elements, an invalid singleton conflict can exclude the cheaper acceptable solution, and a nonoptimizing master can choose the costlier acceptable solution.
assumptions_latex: 0\leq w_a<w_b.
\{a\},\{b\}\in\mathcal A.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Either an invalid conflict or nonoptimal master selection can destroy the global-optimality conclusion.}
knowledge_statements.title: Conflict-Validity and Master-Optimality Counterexamples

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exactness Boundaries of the Abstract-Core Loop
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions needed for the framework's general global-optimality guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \mathcal A\subseteq 2^E be the acceptable sets. Every returned conflict K must satisfy A\cap K\ne\varnothing for all A\in\mathcal A, and the terminal candidate must minimize weight over all sets hitting the retained conflicts. Violating conflict validity can exclude an optimal acceptable set; using only a feasible hitting set can yield an accepted but nonminimum acceptable set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Invalid conflicts can remove the true optimum, while a merely feasible master can return an acceptable but suboptimal set.
assumptions_latex: E\text{ is finite}.
w_e\geq 0\text{ for every }e\in E.
Oracle acceptance is equivalent to membership in \mathcal A.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Conflict validity and exact master minimization suffice for the framework's stated global-optimality guarantee; dropping either condition permits failure in general.}
knowledge_statements.title: Exactness Boundaries of the Abstract-Core Loop
Abstract-Core Framework
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite abstract conflict-hitting framework underlying implicit hitting-set MaxSAT.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(\mathcal K=\varnothing\). Repeatedly compute \[S\in\operatorname*{argmin}\left\{\sum_{e\in T}w_e:T\subseteq E,\ T\cap K\neq\varnothing\text{ for all }K\in\mathcal K\right\}.\] Submit \(S\) to the oracle. If the oracle accepts it, return \(S\). Otherwise receive a conflict \(K\subseteq E\setminus S\) and replace \(\mathcal K\) by \(\mathcal K\cup\{K\}\). The new conflict excludes the current candidate because \(S\cap K=\varnothing\). Since every acceptable set hits every returned conflict, the accepted master optimizer has cost no greater than any acceptable set and is therefore globally minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly solve a minimum-weight hitting-set master and ask an oracle to validate its candidate. Rejected candidates yield new conflicts; provided an acceptable removal set exists, an accepted master optimum is globally optimal.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) is a finite set of removable constraints with positive costs \((w_e)_{e\in E}\).
At least one acceptable removal set \(S\subseteq E\) exists.
An oracle accepts exactly acceptable removal sets and, upon rejecting \(S\subseteq E\), returns a conflict \(K\subseteq E\setminus S\) that every acceptable removal set intersects.
The master solves minimum-weight hitting sets of all returned conflicts exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The framework terminates after finitely many distinct conflicts and returns a minimum-cost acceptable removal set.

children.title: Cooperative IHS Variants
children.top_down_role: IHS architectures coordinating multiple solving components or information sources.

assumptions_latex: A finite weighted partial MaxSAT instance is feasible.
The master communicates candidate removal sets, bounds, and cores through a reliable shared state.
Every accepted core is valid and every reported model satisfies the hard clauses.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When a candidate is oracle-validated and its cost equals the shared lower bound, the cooperative procedure may terminate with a globally optimal model.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cooperative IHS template with concurrent master, oracle, and incumbent information exchange.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain shared \(\mathcal K\), \(L\), and \(U\). A master worker repeatedly solves the minimum-weight hitting-set problem over a snapshot of \(\mathcal K\), publishes its optimizer \(S\), and raises \(L\) only using a valid master optimum. Oracle workers test published sets \(S\); an unsatisfiable test publishes a valid core \(K\) for insertion into \(\mathcal K\), while a satisfiable test publishes a model and lowers \(U\) to its cost. Messages may be processed asynchronously, but stale results may update the state only when their core, bound, or model remains independently valid. Terminate when an oracle-validated candidate has cost \(L=U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Master and oracle workers exchange candidates, cores, and incumbents concurrently. Only independently valid stale information is retained, and equality of certified bounds proves optimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Cooperative IHS Variants

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cooperative algorithm template preserves plausible validity invariants, but no source supports the named variant or its asynchronous stale-result rules.

children.title: Hybrid IHS Variants
children.top_down_role: IHS variants combined with alternative exact-search paradigms.

assumptions_latex: The instance is finite, weighted, and has a hard-feasible assignment.
The IHS and auxiliary exact MaxSAT procedures share only valid cores, models, and objective bounds.
At least one component remains complete if the other component is suspended.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The hybrid returns an optimal model once shared valid bounds coincide; exchanging valid information does not compromise exactness.

notation.meaning: Global lower and upper objective bounds

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact IHS combined with another complete MaxSAT search mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Run an implicit hitting-set process together with an auxiliary exact procedure, such as core-guided or branch-and-bound search. Both components may add valid cores to \(\mathcal K\), raise \(L\) using certified lower bounds, and lower \(U\) using hard-feasible models. The IHS component proposes minimum-weight hitting sets and validates them by a SAT oracle; the auxiliary component searches under the current bounds. Scheduling may alternate, race, or suspend components, provided no uncertified bound is shared and at least one enabled component guarantees finite exact progress. Return the incumbent \(x^*\) when \(L=U\), or when an IHS candidate is validated with cost equal to the certified lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An IHS solver and another exact MaxSAT method share valid cores, bounds, and models. Flexible scheduling preserves exactness when one component guarantees completion.
knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid IHS Variants

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the hybrid-variant leaf, but the claimed completion condition under flexible scheduling and component suspension requires literature support.

children.title: Oracle-Master Coordination Regimes
children.top_down_role: Information-flow regimes between the core oracle and hitting-set master.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of termination based on a component-local master that omits an outstanding core.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let unit-weight elements be \(a,b\), with valid cores \(K_1=\{a\}\) and \(K_2=\{b\}\). A component containing only \(K_1\) has master value \(1\) and candidate \(\{a\}\), while the master containing both cores has value \(2\). Thus a local value match at \(1\) does not certify global feasibility or optimality unless the candidate and bound are validated against the globally relevant coordination state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stale component can appear to close its local gap while its candidate misses an outstanding core.
assumptions_latex: The terminating component has not incorporated the valid outstanding core \(K_2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L_{\mathrm{local}}=1\not\Rightarrow L_{\mathrm{local}}=\operatorname{OPT}.

notation.meaning: Valid cores present in different coordination states

knowledge_statements.title: Stale-Master Gap-Closure Failure

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower-bound invariant for delayed incorporation of globally valid IHS cores.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal K_t\subseteq\mathcal K_{t+1}\) be incorporated valid core families, and let \(v_t\) be the exact minimum weight of a hitting set of \(\mathcal K_t\). Then \(v_t\le v_{t+1}\le\operatorname{OPT}\). A hitting set for \(\mathcal K_t\) need not hit cores delivered later.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding valid cores can only strengthen the master and raise its sound lower bound, but a stale candidate may fail to hit later cores.
assumptions_latex: Every core in \(\mathcal K_{t+1}\) must be hit by every feasible removal set.
Each stated master value is exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v_t\le v_{t+1}\le\operatorname{OPT}.

notation.meaning: Core family incorporated at coordination state t
Exact hitting-set value for that family

knowledge_statements.title: Monotone Core-Family Coordination

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient checkable termination condition for distributed or asynchronous IHS coordination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A termination certificate consists of a removal set \(S\), a hard-feasible model whose violated soft clauses are contained in \(S\), a certified lower bound \(L\) from the master over a globally committed family of valid cores, and evidence that the certificate refers to one closed coordination snapshot. If \(w(S)=L\), then the model and \(S\) are globally optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Termination is safe when a validated feasible candidate matches a certified global lower bound computed for a closed coordination snapshot.
assumptions_latex: Every core used by the certified master is globally valid.
The master lower-bound certificate is checkable.
The feasibility model and lower-bound certificate refer to a consistent closed snapshot.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: w(S)=L\land S\text{ is oracle-validated}\Longrightarrow w(S)=\operatorname{OPT}.
knowledge_statements.title: Quiescent Global Termination Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combinatorial bound on nonrepeated oracle validations in coordinated IHS.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With \(m\) soft-clause indices there are exactly \(2^m\) removal sets. Therefore, any coordination protocol that submits each removal set to the complete oracle at most once performs at most \(2^m\) distinct candidate validations. This counting bound alone does not establish progress, fair delivery, or termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duplicate-free coordination can validate at most one candidate per soft-clause subset, hence at most 2^m candidates.
assumptions_latex: The soft-clause index set has cardinality \(m\).
No removal set is submitted for complete validation more than once.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{validate}}\le 2^m.

notation.meaning: Number of distinct complete candidate validations.

knowledge_statements.title: Distinct Candidate-Validation Bound

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Versioned IHS Coordination States and Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational protocol schema distinguishing nonoverlapping, barrier-batched, and asynchronous oracle-master coordination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A versioned coordination state is \(Q_q=(q,\mathcal K_q,V_q,O_q)\), where \(q\) is a committed version, \(\mathcal K_q\) is its monotone family of valid cores, \(V_q\) records completed candidate validations, and \(O_q\) records outstanding requests with their generating versions. In the synchronous schema no oracle round overlaps the next committed master state; in the batched schema a finite batch generated from one committed state is installed at a barrier; in the asynchronous schema requests from different versions may overlap and every globally valid returned core may be installed despite staleness. In all three schemas, a stale candidate must be validated against a closed current snapshot before supporting termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Versioned states record committed cores, validations, and outstanding work; the three schemas differ in overlap and commit barriers, while stale candidates never certify termination without current-snapshot validation.
assumptions_latex: Every installed core is globally valid.
Core-family updates are monotone.
Each request and response carries an unambiguous candidate identifier and generating version.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal K_q\subseteq\mathcal K_{q+1},\qquad\text{stale valid cores may strengthen later states, but stale candidates cannot alone certify termination}.

notation.meaning: Committed coordination state at version q.

knowledge_statements.title: Versioned IHS Coordination States and Regimes

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Barrier-synchronous coordination between an exact current-core master and a complete MaxSAT oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(\mathcal K\leftarrow\varnothing\). Repeatedly solve the current-core master exactly to obtain a minimum-weight hitting set \(S\), then submit \(S\) to a complete oracle for \(H\land\bigwedge_{i\notin S}C_i\). If the oracle returns a model, terminate with that model and \(S\). If it returns a globally valid core \(K\subseteq I\setminus S\), commit \(K\) to \(\mathcal K\) before the next master solve. If \(H\) itself is certified unsatisfiable, report hard infeasibility. With finite \(I\) and no repeated submitted removal set, at most \(2^{|I|}\) oracle submissions occur.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Synchronous IHS alternates exact master solves and complete oracle calls, committing each returned core before generating another candidate.
assumptions_latex: The soft index set \(I\) is finite.
Every master solve is exact.
Every oracle call terminates with a checked model, a globally valid core, or a certificate that \(H\) is unsatisfiable.
No removal set is submitted more than once.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{oracle}}\le 2^{|I|}\quad\text{and termination returns an optimal removal solution or certified hard infeasibility}.

notation.meaning: Committed family of globally valid soft-clause cores.

knowledge_statements.title: Synchronous Oracle–Master IHS Coordination

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asynchronous transition system with eventual delivery and quiescent termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain a monotone committed core family \(\mathcal K\), pending versioned requests \(P\), completed candidate validations \(V\), and the best checked incumbent. Fairly solve the current master and dispatch its optimizer when no equivalent request is pending or complete. Process responses in arbitrary order, remove completed identifiers from \(P\), install every new globally valid returned core, and record checked feasible models. Every dispatched request remains pending until processed. A snapshot is closed only when \(P=\varnothing\) and no delivered response awaits commit. Terminate on checked hard infeasibility or when a closed-snapshot exact master value equals a checked incumbent cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Asynchronous coordination suppresses duplicate validations, processes every dispatched response, installs valid cores monotonically, and closes the gap only at quiescence.
assumptions_latex: The soft index set is finite.
Exact master solves and dispatched oracle calls terminate.
Every dispatched response is eventually delivered and processed.
Every installed core is globally valid.
Eligible current master optimizers are eventually dispatched.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{A quiescent equality }L=U\text{ certifies optimality}.
knowledge_statements.title: Duplicate-Suppressing Asynchronous IHS Coordination

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-batch IHS transition system with versioned commits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At committed version \(q\), solve the exact master over \(\mathcal K_q\) and form a finite duplicate-free batch \(B_q\) containing a current master optimizer. Tag requests by \((q,S)\), wait until every request returns checked evidence, discard duplicate responses, and commit all new globally valid cores simultaneously to \(\mathcal K_{q+1}\). Generate no new batch before the commit. Terminate only on checked hard infeasibility or when a validated feasible candidate matches the exact master value of a closed committed state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A barrier-batched regime validates a finite versioned batch, commits all returned cores together, and terminates only against a closed state.
assumptions_latex: Every master solve is exact.
Every request terminates with checkable evidence.
Every installed core is globally valid.
Each batch contains a current exact-master optimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Every committed lower bound is valid, and every accepted gap closure certifies optimality}.

notation.meaning: Finite candidate batch generated at version q.
Core family committed at version q.

knowledge_statements.title: Barrier-Batched Oracle–Master Coordination

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Termination of Duplicate-Suppressing Asynchronous IHS
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-progress theorem for the specified asynchronous transition system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose there are \(m\) soft indices, every dispatched validation is eventually processed, every eligible current master optimizer is eventually dispatched, and every rejected candidate returns a valid core not hit by that candidate. Duplicate suppression permits at most \(2^m\) completed candidate validations. Each rejected optimizer is permanently excluded by its committed core; a feasible optimizer matches a valid master lower bound and is optimal. Thus the system reaches optimality or certified hard infeasibility after finitely many validations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eventual delivery, fair optimizer dispatch, valid excluding cores, and duplicate suppression give finite asynchronous IHS termination.
assumptions_latex: The specified asynchronous transition system is followed.
The soft index set has size \(m<\infty\).
Every rejected candidate yields a committed core that it fails to hit.
Every dispatched validation is eventually processed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{validate}}\le2^m\quad\text{and the terminal result is optimality or certified hard infeasibility}.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Termination of Duplicate-Suppressing Asynchronous IHS

assumptions_latex: The master produces candidate removal sets and lower-bound certificates.
The oracle returns models or valid conflicts for submitted candidates.
Messages carry sufficient version information to identify the core family used by each master solve.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any synchronous, batched, or asynchronous regime satisfying the validity and fairness conditions preserves the correctness of IHS termination.

notation.meaning: Core family known at coordination time t

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correctness conditions common to synchronous, batched, and asynchronous IHS coordination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A coordination regime is admissible when: \(1\) every submitted \(S_t\) is feasible for the master built from its recorded \(\mathcal K_t\); \(2\) every returned conflict is globally valid, even if generated from a stale candidate; \(3\) an upper bound is updated only from a hard-feasible model; \(4\) a lower bound is updated only from a certified relaxation or master bound valid for the current problem; and \(5\) fairness ensures that a candidate generated from every persistently current core family is eventually tested, or that another complete component makes progress. Termination is permitted only when a validated candidate attains the certified lower bound, equivalently when \(L=U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coordination may be synchronous or asynchronous, but cores and bounds must remain globally valid, current candidates must eventually be tested, and termination requires matching certified bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Oracle-Master Coordination Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A condition record is appropriate here, but the asserted sufficiency of the stated validity and fairness conditions for all synchronous, batched, and asynchronous regimes is unsupported.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Termination under Fair Core Delivery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed finite-progress conditions for coordinated IHS over a finite soft-clause set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume finitely many soft clauses, exact master solves, complete oracle calls, globally valid returned cores, eventual delivery of every returned core, and a fair policy that eventually validates or supersedes every persistently current minimum-weight master candidate. If duplicate coordination states are not processed indefinitely, coordinated IHS terminates after finitely many distinct candidate validations with an optimum or hard infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proposal claims finite termination from a finite candidate space, exact components, eventual valid-core delivery, fairness, and duplicate suppression.
assumptions_latex: The soft-clause index set is finite.
Master and oracle calls terminate and are exact.
Every returned core is eventually incorporated or rendered redundant.
Persistently current candidates are eventually validated or superseded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{finite domain}+\text{exactness}+\text{validity}+\text{fair delivery}+\text{duplicate suppression}\Longrightarrow\text{finite correct termination}.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Termination under Fair Core Delivery

intermediate_metadata.reason: This leaf owns coordination-state invariants, stale-state failures, fairness and delivery obligations, and global termination certificates. Cooperative and hybrid solver designs were excluded as sibling-owned, and master duality and core extraction remain in their own leaves. The proposed general termination theorem is deferred as insufficiently operational, so expansion remains necessary.

children.title: Variable Branching
children.top_down_role: Branching regimes centered on variable assignments.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correctness invariant separating exhaustive binary branching from its selection heuristic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At every nonterminal node with partial assignment \(\alpha\), choose any variable \(v\notin\operatorname{dom}(\alpha)\) and represent both children \(\alpha\cup\{v=0\}\) and \(\alpha\cup\{v=1\}\), except children removed by sound infeasibility or bound certificates. The choice of \(v\) and the value order may change tree size and discovery order, but not the represented total completions or the final optimum under exhaustive fair processing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any unfixed variable and either value order preserve completeness when both branches are represented and only sound pruning is used.
assumptions_latex: The Boolean variable set is finite.
Every live node is eventually processed or soundly pruned.
Every pruning certificate is valid for all completions of its node.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{OPT}\) is invariant under variable-selection and value-order heuristics.
knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Choice Independence of Completeness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combinatorial size bound when each Boolean variable is branched on at most once per path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With \(n\) initially unfixed Boolean variables, binary variable branching has depth at most \(n\), at most \(2^n\) leaves, and at most \(2^{n+1}-1\) nodes. Equality holds for the full unpruned tree with no additional propagated fixings.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pure binary variable branching has depth at most n, at most 2^n leaves, and at most 2^(n+1)−1 nodes.
assumptions_latex: There are \(n\) initially unfixed Boolean variables.
No variable is branched on twice along a path.
Both values are represented at every unpruned branch.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d\le n,\qquad N_{\mathrm{leaves}}\le2^n,\qquad N_{\mathrm{nodes}}\le2^{n+1}-1.

notation.meaning: Number of initially unfixed Boolean variables

knowledge_statements.title: Unpruned Binary Variable-Branching Tree Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Completeness failure when an uncertified truth-value child is omitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a node branching on unfixed \(v\), omitting one child without a sound exclusion certificate destroys coverage. For example, with hard clause \(v\), exploring only \(v=0\) reports infeasibility although the parent is feasible at \(v=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Omitting an uncertified truth-value branch can miss the only feasible solution.
assumptions_latex: \(v\) is unfixed at the parent.
The omitted child has no valid pruning certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Omitting an uncertified child can make the search incomplete}.
knowledge_statements.title: One-Sided Branch Omission

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Locally defining operation of Boolean variable branching.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a partial assignment \(\alpha\), branching on an unfixed Boolean variable \(v\) creates the two children \(\alpha\cup\{v=0\}\) and \(\alpha\cup\{v=1\}\). Their sets of total completions are disjoint and their union is the parent’s completion set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Variable branching fixes an unfixed Boolean variable to zero and one in two exhaustive children.
assumptions_latex: \(v\notin\operatorname{dom}(\alpha)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Ext}(\alpha)=\operatorname{Ext}(\alpha\cup\{v=0\})\mathbin{\dot\cup}\operatorname{Ext}(\alpha\cup\{v=1\}).

notation.meaning: Total Boolean extensions of the partial assignment

knowledge_statements.title: Binary Variable Split

assumptions_latex: A branch-and-bound node fixes a partial Boolean assignment \(\alpha\).
The chosen variable \(v\) is unassigned under \(\alpha\).
The node lower bound is valid for every completion of its partial assignment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two children partition all completions of \(\alpha\); pruning both children or solving them exactly therefore resolves the parent node.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary variable branching within exact MaxSAT branch-and-bound search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Select an unassigned variable \(v\) at node \(\alpha\) and create children \(\alpha_0=\alpha\cup\{v=0\}\) and \(\alpha_1=\alpha\cup\{v=1\}\). Apply Boolean propagation and compute a valid lower bound \(B(\alpha_b)\) on the violation cost of every total assignment extending each child. Prune child \(b\in\{0,1\}\) when it is inconsistent with the hard clauses or when \(B(\alpha_b)\geq U\), where \(U\) is the incumbent cost; otherwise continue search from that child. Update \(U\) whenever a hard-feasible total assignment of smaller cost is found. Stop when no live node remains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branch on an unassigned Boolean variable, propagate each truth value, and prune a child when it is hard-infeasible or cannot improve the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.title: Variable Branching

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The binary branching partition and pruning rules are coherent and the algorithm kind fits, but no authoritative MaxSAT branch-and-bound source is cited.

children.title: Clause Branching
children.top_down_role: Branching regimes centered on clause satisfaction choices.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary clause-level branching over optimum-preserving normalized relaxation assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(C=\ell_1\lor\cdots\lor\ell_k\) encoded as \(C\lor r_C\) with positive objective term \(w_Cr_C\), restrict attention to normalized representatives satisfying \(r_C=1\) exactly when \(C\) is false. Branch into \(C\land(r_C=0)\) and \((\bigwedge_{j=1}^k\neg\ell_j)\land(r_C=1)\). These children are disjoint and cover all normalized representatives. Normalization is optimum-preserving because any model with \(C\) true and \(r_C=1\) can lower its cost by setting \(r_C=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After normalizing the relaxation variable to record actual violation, branch into satisfying the clause without charge or falsifying it with the relaxation charge.
assumptions_latex: \(r_C\) is fresh and clause-specific.
The objective contains \(w_Cr_C\) with \(w_C>0\).
Search is over normalized representatives or applies the stated optimum-preserving normalization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal N=\operatorname{Mod}(C\land\neg r_C)\ \dot\cup\ \operatorname{Mod}\!\left((\bigwedge_j\neg\ell_j)\land r_C\right),

notation.meaning: Relaxation variable for soft clause C
Normalized assignments for the relaxed clause

knowledge_statements.title: Normalized Soft-Clause Satisfaction–Violation Split

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Immediate child count for ordered first-true clause branching.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an unresolved clause with \(k\) eligible literals, ordered first-true branching creates exactly \(k\) satisfaction children. If violation is permitted and represented explicitly, the all-false violation child gives \(k+1\) children. Each satisfaction child fixes at most \(k\) clause literals; the violation child fixes all \(k\) literals and its relaxation variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A k-literal ordered clause branch has k satisfaction children, or k+1 children with an explicit violation branch.
assumptions_latex: All listed literals are unresolved at the parent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: m=k\text{ for mandatory satisfaction},\qquad m=k+1\text{ with an explicit violation child}.
knowledge_statements.title: Ordered Clause-Branch Arity
Clause Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordered, disjoint branching on the literals of a clause in exact MaxSAT search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(j=1,\ldots,k\), create the ordered branch \[\alpha_j=\alpha\cup\{\ell_1=0,\ldots,\ell_{j-1}=0,\ell_j=1\}.\] Propagate each \(\alpha_j\), discard hard-inconsistent children, and prune any child whose valid lower bound is at least the incumbent cost. Continue exact search on the remaining children. Every total extension of \(\alpha\) satisfying \(C\) has a unique first true literal in the chosen ordering and therefore belongs to exactly one \(\alpha_j\). If violation of \(C\) is permitted through a relaxation variable, add a separate branch fixing all \(\ell_j=0\) and charging or activating that relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Order a clause's literals and branch on which is first true. The resulting children are disjoint and cover all satisfying completions, with an optional violation branch.
assumptions_latex: A search node has partial assignment \(\alpha\), and clause \(C=\ell_1\lor\cdots\lor\ell_k\) is not satisfied by \(\alpha\).
Each literal \(\ell_j\) is currently unassigned and the literals are ordered.
Child-node bounds are valid for all completions represented by those children.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The ordered clause branches are pairwise disjoint and cover exactly the completions of \(\alpha\) that satisfy \(C\).

children.top_down_role: Higher-level decompositions of the optimization search space.

assumptions_latex: \(V\) is a finite set of Boolean variables containing every variable occurring in \(H\) and \(S\).
Every \(w_i\) is strictly positive.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{OPT}(H,S\mid\alpha)=\min_{1\le j\le q}\operatorname{OPT}(H,S\mid\beta_j)\).

notation.meaning: Finite set of Boolean variables for the instance.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact partition of a residual weighted partial-MaxSAT search space into branch-and-bound children.

source_refs.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\) be a finite set of Boolean variables, let \(H\) be a set of hard clauses over \(V\), let \(S=\{(C_i,w_i)\}_{i=1}^m\) be soft clauses over \(V\) with \(w_i>0\), and let \(\alpha\) be a partial assignment on \(V\). A valid branching family \(\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_q\) consists of partial assignments extending \(\alpha\) such that the sets of hard-feasible total completions form the disjoint partition \[\{\tau:V\to\{0,1\}\mid \tau\supseteq\alpha,\ \tau\models H\}=\mathop{\dot\bigcup}_{j=1}^q\{\tau:V\to\{0,1\}\mid \tau\supseteq\beta_j,\ \tau\models H\}.\] Consequently, when an infeasible child is assigned value \(+\infty\), \[\operatorname{OPT}(H,S\mid\alpha)=\min_{1\le j\le q}\operatorname{OPT}(H,S\mid\beta_j).\] Thus exhaustive processing or sound pruning of every child preserves exactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid branch creates disjoint children covering every hard-feasible total completion of the parent assignment; the parent optimum is the minimum child optimum, with infeasible children valued at infinity.
knowledge_statements.title: Search-Space Partitioning

source_witnesses.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Covering Children Suffice for the Optimum Identity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact parent–child optimum relation when child regions may overlap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_\alpha\) be the hard-feasible total completions of a parent node and let \(X_1,\ldots,X_q\subseteq X_\alpha\) satisfy \(X_\alpha=\bigcup_{j=1}^qX_j\), without requiring disjointness. For any cost function \(c:X_\alpha\to\mathbb{R}\), with \(\min\varnothing=+\infty\), \[\min_{\tau\in X_\alpha}c(\tau)=\min_{1\le j\le q}\min_{\tau\in X_j}c(\tau).\] Overlap preserves exactness but may duplicate search; disjointness is not required for this optimum identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Child regions need only cover the parent to preserve its optimum; disjointness prevents duplicate search but is not required for correctness.
assumptions_latex: \(X_j\subseteq X_\alpha\) for every \(j\).
\(X_\alpha=\bigcup_{j=1}^qX_j\).
\(q<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{\tau\in X_\alpha}c(\tau)=\min_j\min_{\tau\in X_j}c(\tau)\).

notation.meaning: Hard-feasible completion set of the parent node.
Completion region represented by child j.

children.title: Branching Granularity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes distinguished by the unit used to partition search.

knowledge_statements.title: Branching Granularity Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classification by the number and form of Boolean decisions imposed at one search node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a residual MaxSAT instance under partial assignment \(\alpha\), the granularity of a branch is the maximum number of previously unset variables fixed by any child condition. Variable branching has granularity one and uses the two conditions \(x=0\) and \(x=1\). Block branching has granularity \(k>1\) and partitions completions using mutually exclusive assignments or predicates over a selected set \(B\) with \(|B|=k\). Clause branching partitions on mutually exclusive conditions derived from a clause or constraint and may have nonuniform effective granularity. Every regime is admissible only when its child conditions are disjoint and exhaustive over completions of \(\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branching may decide one variable, a variable block, or clause-derived conditions; regardless of granularity, children must be mutually exclusive and exhaustive.
assumptions_latex: \(\alpha\) is a partial Boolean assignment.
Every branching condition concerns variables unset by \(\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The branching regime is classified by its child predicates and their maximum number of newly fixed variables.

notation.meaning: Selected block of previously unset Boolean variables.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the branching-granularity leaf and is internally coherent, but no citation supports the proposed variable, block, and clause branching taxonomy or the particular maximum-newly-fixed-variables definition of granularity.

children.title: Propagation Lower Bounds
children.top_down_role: Lower bounds derived from propagation outcomes.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison of propagation lower bounds obtained from nested sets of forced relaxation variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the same residual weighted MaxSAT node, let two sound propagation procedures force relaxation-variable index sets \(F\) and \(F'\), respectively, with \(F\subseteq F'\). If all weights are positive and each index is charged once, then \[\sum_{i\in F}w_i\leq\sum_{i\in F'}w_i.\] Whenever both forced sets are logical consequences of the residual node and each forced relaxation variable represents a distinct objective charge, both sums are valid lower bounds. A non-entailed force or duplicate charge invalidates that conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sound propagator forcing a superset of distinctly charged relaxation variables gives a bound at least as strong.
assumptions_latex: Both forced sets are logical consequences of the same residual node.
\(F\subseteq F'\).
Every \(w_i>0\), and each objective charge is counted once.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_F\leq L_{F'}\leq\operatorname{OPT}.\)

notation.meaning: Nested sets of relaxation variables forced true by sound propagation.
Total distinct weight charged by forced set F.

knowledge_statements.title: Monotonicity Under Stronger Sound Propagation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal propagation-bound failure caused by charging one forced relaxation variable twice.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the hard clause be \(\neg x\), and encode the unit-weight soft clause \(x\) as \(x\lor r\) with objective \(r\). Sound propagation forces \(x=0\) and then \(r=1\), so the residual optimum and the distinct forced-charge bound are both \(1\). Counting the same forced variable twice reports \(2>\operatorname{OPT}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A forced relaxation variable contributes one objective charge; counting that force twice can exceed the true optimum.
assumptions_latex: The sole soft clause has weight one.
Both reported charges refer to the same relaxation variable \(r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 2>1=\operatorname{OPT}.

notation.meaning: Relaxation variable for the sole soft clause.

knowledge_statements.title: Duplicate Forced-Charge Failure

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-node procedure for extracting a propagation witness without duplicate objective charges.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a residual relaxation encoding under partial assignment \(\alpha\), initialize \(F\leftarrow\varnothing\) and run a sound propagation engine to closure. Whenever propagation first derives \(r_i=1\), insert \(i\) into \(F\); later derivations of the same fact do not change \(F\). If propagation derives a contradiction from the residual mandatory constraints and recorded node assumptions, return its derivation. Otherwise return \((F,L)\), where \(L=\sum_{i\in F}w_i\), together with a derivation of every recorded force.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Propagate to closure, record each forced relaxation variable once, and return its total weight and force derivations, or return a checked residual-node contradiction.
assumptions_latex: Every propagation step is a sound consequence of the residual node.
Each \(r_i\) denotes one objective charge of weight \(w_i\ge0\).
The set representation suppresses duplicate indices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L=\sum_{i\in F}w_i\text{ and every }i\in F\text{ has a recorded derivation of }r_i=1.

notation.meaning: Set of distinctly charged relaxation-variable indices forced true.
Total weight of the recorded forced charges.

knowledge_statements.title: Distinct Forced-Charge Collection

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Checkable node lower-bound certificate formed from distinct propagation-forced objective charges.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a residual relaxation encoding \(E\mid\alpha\), a forced-charge witness consists of a duplicate-free index set \(F\), the encoded weights \((w_i)_{i\in F}\), and a sound derivation of \(E\mid\alpha\models r_i\) for every \(i\in F\). A checker validates each derivation and the distinctness of \(F\), then recomputes \(L=\sum_{i\in F}w_i\) exactly. If each \(r_i\) denotes one nonnegative objective charge, the accepted witness certifies that every feasible completion of \(\alpha\) has cost at least \(L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Derivations of distinct forced relaxation variables and their exact weight sum form a checkable propagation lower-bound witness.
assumptions_latex: Every force derivation is checked in the residual-node context.
The index set \(F\) is duplicate-free.
Each \(r_i\) contributes exactly one objective term of weight \(w_i\ge0\).
Arithmetic is exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: E\mid\alpha\models\bigwedge_{i\in F}r_i\quad\Longrightarrow\quad L=\sum_{i\in F}w_i\le\operatorname{OPT}(E\mid\alpha).

notation.meaning: Duplicate-free set of forced relaxation-variable indices.
Certified sum of forced objective charges.
Residual encoding under the node assignment.

knowledge_statements.title: Propagation Forced-Charge Witness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Checked propagation contradiction proving that a MaxSAT search node has no hard-feasible completion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E_{\mathrm{mand}}\mid\alpha\) contain the hard constraints, recorded node assumptions, and every other constraint mandatory for all admissible completions of node \(\alpha\). If a sound checker accepts a contradiction derived from this residual system, then the node has no admissible completion, its residual optimum is \(+\infty\), and it may be pruned independently of soft-objective charges.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A checked contradiction from constraints mandatory at the residual node certifies node infeasibility and an infinite lower bound.
assumptions_latex: Every derivation premise is mandatory for every completion of the node.
The propagation or proof checker is sound.
Node assumptions are recorded exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: E_{\mathrm{mand}}\mid\alpha\vdash\bot\Longrightarrow\operatorname{Feas}(E\mid\alpha)=\varnothing\text{ and }\operatorname{OPT}(E\mid\alpha)=+\infty.

notation.meaning: Residual constraints mandatory at node alpha.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual Mandatory-Conflict Infeasibility Certificate
Propagation Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower bound obtained from soft cost forced by sound propagation at a search node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Encode each soft clause \((C_i,w_i)\) by \(C_i\lor r_i\), where \(r_i\) is a relaxation variable, and minimize \(\sum_i w_i r_i\). Under a partial assignment \(\alpha\), apply sound Boolean and pseudo-Boolean propagation to the hard clauses, relaxed clauses, and any globally valid learned constraints. If propagation forces \(r_i=1\) for every \(i\) in a set \(F_\alpha\), then \[L_{\mathrm{prop}}(\alpha)=\sum_{i\in F_\alpha}w_i\] is a lower bound on the cost of every hard-feasible completion of \(\alpha\). A propagation conflict in the hard constraints gives lower bound \(+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The total weight of relaxation variables forced true by sound propagation lower-bounds every feasible completion; a hard conflict makes the node infeasible.
assumptions_latex: All propagation rules preserve logical consequence.
Each relaxation variable \(r_i\) is charged at most once.
Every \(w_i>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_{\mathrm{prop}}(\alpha)\leq\operatorname{OPT}(H,S\mid\alpha)\).

notation.meaning: Relaxation variable indicating payment for soft clause i.
Indices whose relaxation variables propagation forces true.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits the propagation-lower-bound leaf, and the forced-relaxation-variable inequality is plausible under sound propagation. An authoritative MaxSAT or pseudo-Boolean source is required to support the encoding and lower-bound formulation.

children.title: Consistency Lower Bounds
children.top_down_role: Lower bounds derived from local consistency processing.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of summing group minima when inconsistent soft-clause groups overlap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=\{\neg x\}\) and let the unit-weight soft clauses be \(C_1=x\), \(C_2=y\), and \(C_3=y\lor z\). The groups \(I_1=\{1,2\}\) and \(I_2=\{1,3\}\) are each inconsistent with \(H\), but both inconsistency arguments can be discharged by falsifying the shared clause \(C_1\). The assignment \(x=0,y=1\) has cost \(1\), whereas summing the two group minima gives \(2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Overlapping inconsistent groups may be hit by one falsified soft clause, so summing their minimum weights can overestimate the optimum.
assumptions_latex: All displayed soft clauses have unit weight.
The inconsistent groups share soft clause \(C_1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{j=1}^2\min_{i\in I_j}w_i=2>1=\operatorname{OPT}.\)

notation.meaning: Overlapping soft-clause groups individually inconsistent with the hard clauses.
The shared soft clause whose falsification satisfies both group requirements.
