knowledge_statements.scope_note: Verification contract for an inconsistent-group packing bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A certificate gives hard-inconsistent groups \(G\in\mathcal G\), a checked refutation of \(H_\alpha\land\bigwedge_{i\in G}C_i\) for every positively charged group, and rational charges \(y_G\ge0\) satisfying \(\sum_{G\ni i}y_G\le w_i\). Verification certifies the lower bound \(\sum_Gy_G\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Checked group refutations plus a feasible charge packing certify the resulting consistency lower bound.
assumptions_latex: The refutation checker is sound.
Rational charges and capacity inequalities are checked exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{check}(\mathcal G,y)=\mathrm{valid}\Longrightarrow\sum_Gy_G\le\operatorname{OPT}(H,S\mid\alpha).

notation.meaning: Charge assigned to inconsistent group G
Residual hard formula at the current node

knowledge_statements.title: Checkable Consistency-Packing Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Overlap-safe consistency bound using soft-weight capacities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let every \(G\in\mathcal G\) satisfy \(H_\alpha\land\bigwedge_{i\in G}C_i\) unsatisfiable. If \(y_G\ge0\) and \(\sum_{G\ni i}y_G\le w_i\) for every soft index \(i\), then \(\sum_{G\in\mathcal G}y_G\) is a valid residual lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Charges packed on inconsistent groups under soft-clause weight capacities give a valid bound even when groups overlap.
assumptions_latex: Every \(G\in\mathcal G\) is inconsistent with \(H_\alpha\).
\(\sum_{G\ni i}y_G\le w_i\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_{G\in\mathcal G}y_G\le\operatorname{OPT}(H,S\mid\alpha).

notation.meaning: Family of hard-inconsistent residual soft-clause groups
Packed charge assigned to group G
Residual weight capacity of soft clause i

knowledge_statements.title: Fractional Packing of Inconsistent Groups
Consistency Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Packing lower bound from disjoint hard-inconsistent groups of residual soft clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H_\alpha\) be the hard clauses residual under \(\alpha\), and let \(I_1,\ldots,I_t\) be pairwise disjoint sets of soft-clause indices. Suppose \(H_\alpha\cup\{C_i:i\in I_j\}\) is unsatisfiable for every \(j\). Every hard-feasible completion must therefore falsify at least one soft clause from each \(I_j\). Hence \[L_{\mathrm{cons}}(\alpha)=\sum_{j=1}^t\min_{i\in I_j}w_i\] is a valid lower bound. Pairwise disjointness is essential for this additive formula unless a separate accounting argument prevents charging the same soft weight more than once.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each disjoint group that cannot jointly coexist with the hard clauses forces a payment; summing the minimum group weights gives a lower bound.
assumptions_latex: The index sets \(I_j\) are pairwise disjoint.
Each \(H_\alpha\cup\{C_i:i\in I_j\}\) is unsatisfiable.
Every \(w_i>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_{\mathrm{cons}}(\alpha)\leq\operatorname{OPT}(H,S\mid\alpha)\).

notation.meaning: Hard clauses simplified by the current partial assignment.
A packed set of jointly inconsistent residual soft clauses.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits the consistency-lower-bound leaf, and disjoint inconsistent soft-clause groups plausibly yield the stated packing bound. No source is supplied for this MaxSAT-specific formulation or its accounting conditions.

children.title: Inference Lower Bounds
children.top_down_role: Lower bounds derived from optimization-preserving inference.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accounting failure when one unavoidable cost is recorded both as an extracted offset and as retained empty-clause weight.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the residual weighted MaxSAT instance consist of the single soft empty clause \((\square,1)\), so \(\operatorname{OPT}=1\). Suppose an alleged inference step records its weight as an offset \(c=1\) while retaining \((\square,1)\) with weight \(\lambda=1\). The reported bound is then \(c+\lambda=2>\operatorname{OPT}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extracting an empty clause into an offset while retaining and charging that clause double-counts the same unavoidable cost.
assumptions_latex: The original residual instance contains exactly one unit-weight soft empty clause.
The transformation records its weight as an offset without removing or zeroing the residual charge.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: c+\lambda=2>1=\operatorname{OPT}.
knowledge_statements.title: Offset–Empty-Clause Double Counting

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Verification contract for a compositional weighted-inference lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A certificate records residual instances \(F_k\), offsets \(\delta_k\), locally checkable pointwise cost identities between successive instances, and a checked terminal lower bound \(L_m\). Exact verification certifies \(\sum_k\delta_k+L_m\) for \(F_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Checking every cost transformation, extracted offset, and terminal bound certifies their composition for the original instance.
assumptions_latex: The selected inference calculus has sound local step checkers.
Offsets and weights are represented exactly.
The terminal lower-bound certificate is sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{check}(F_0\to\cdots\to F_m,c,L_m)=\mathrm{valid}\Longrightarrow c+L_m\le\operatorname{OPT}(F_0).

notation.meaning: Certified lower bound for the terminal residual instance

knowledge_statements.title: Stepwise Inference Accounting Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Empty-clause specialization of the compositional cost-offset invariant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the terminal residual instance \(F_m\) contains soft empty clauses of weights \(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_t\), and those weights remain in the terminal residual cost rather than having already been extracted into \(c\), then \(L_m=\sum_j\lambda_j\) is valid and \(c+\sum_j\lambda_j\le\operatorname{OPT}(F_0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Derived empty-clause weights may be added to extracted offsets only when they have not already been charged by those offsets.
assumptions_latex: Every displayed empty clause is necessarily falsified.
No \(\lambda_j\) is already represented in the accumulated offset \(c\).
The compositional pointwise cost identity holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: c+\sum_{j=1}^t\lambda_j\le\operatorname{OPT}(F_0).

notation.meaning: Weight of a terminal soft empty clause

knowledge_statements.title: Terminal Empty-Clause Lower Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise accounting invariant for weighted-MaxSAT inference transformations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let residual instances \(F_0,\ldots,F_m\) and offsets \(\delta_1,\ldots,\delta_m\) satisfy \(\operatorname{cost}_{F_{k-1}}(x)=\delta_k+\operatorname{cost}_{F_k}(x)\) for every hard-feasible completion \(x\). Then \(\operatorname{cost}_{F_0}(x)=c+\operatorname{cost}_{F_m}(x)\), where \(c=\sum_k\delta_k\), and every lower bound \(L_m\) on \(F_m\) gives \(c+L_m\le\operatorname{OPT}(F_0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pointwise cost-preserving inference steps compose, so accumulated offsets plus a terminal residual bound lower-bound the original instance.
assumptions_latex: Every transformation preserves the relevant hard-feasible completions.
Each step satisfies the stated pointwise cost identity.
Offsets and costs are represented exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: c+L_m\le\operatorname{OPT}(F_0).

notation.meaning: Residual weighted-MaxSAT instance after k steps
Cost offset extracted at step k

knowledge_statements.title: Compositional Cost-Offset Invariant
Inference Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A checkable lower-bound certificate produced by sound weighted MaxSAT inference.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At node \(\alpha\), let a sound weighted inference derivation transform the residual instance into an equivalent residual instance containing empty soft clauses \((\square,\lambda_1),\ldots,(\square,\lambda_t)\), where \(\lambda_j>0\). Equivalence means that every total completion has the same soft cost before and after the transformation, possibly plus an explicitly recorded constant offset \(c\geq0\). Because an empty clause is necessarily falsified, the derivation certifies \[L_{\mathrm{inf}}(\alpha)=c+\sum_{j=1}^t\lambda_j\leq\operatorname{OPT}(H,S\mid\alpha).\] The derivation and all weight-accounting steps constitute a mechanically checkable certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cost-preserving inference deriving weighted empty clauses certifies their total weight, plus any recorded offset, as a node lower bound.
assumptions_latex: Every inference step preserves the cost of each completion up to its recorded offset.
All derived empty-clause weights are positive.
The derivation is checkable from the residual instance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_{\mathrm{inf}}(\alpha)\leq\operatorname{OPT}(H,S\mid\alpha)\).

notation.meaning: Weight of a derived empty clause.
Explicit constant cost offset accumulated by inference.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A checkable inference derivation is suitable for the certificate leaf, but a weighted MaxSAT calculus source is needed to determine the exact equivalence convention and whether the constant offset and derived empty-clause weights are accounted for without duplication.

children.title: Combined Lower-Bound Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes integrating multiple lower-bound sources.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal failure of unconditional additive lower-bound combination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the weighted MaxSAT instance containing the unit soft clauses \((x,1)\) and \((\neg x,1)\), with no hard clauses. Its optimum is \(1\). If the same inconsistency certificate is reported twice, it gives two individually sound bounds \(L_1=L_2=1\). Then \(\max\{L_1,L_2\}=1\) is sound, whereas \(L_1+L_2=2>\operatorname{OPT}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Individually sound bounds derived from the same unavoidable cost cannot be added without non-overlap accounting.
assumptions_latex: The two lower-bound reports may charge the same soft-clause weights.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L_1\leq\operatorname{OPT}\land L_2\leq\operatorname{OPT}\not\Rightarrow L_1+L_2\leq\operatorname{OPT}.

notation.meaning: Individually sound but overlapping lower-bound certificates.

knowledge_statements.title: Overlapping-Bound Double Counting

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Checkable sufficient condition for adding heterogeneous MaxSAT lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_1,\ldots,P_p\) be pairwise disjoint residual soft-index sets. If certificate \(j\) proves that every hard-feasible completion incurs cost at least \(L_j\) from indices in \(P_j\), then \(\sum_jL_j\) is a residual lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounds can be added when each is certified against disjoint residual cost resources.
assumptions_latex: \(P_j\cap P_k=\varnothing\) for \(j\ne k\).
Each \(L_j\) lower-bounds the cost contributed by \(P_j\) for every hard-feasible completion.
Residual weights are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_{j=1}^pL_j\le\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{res}}.

notation.meaning: Certified lower bound on block-j cost

knowledge_statements.title: Partitioned-Cost Additive Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Maximum and Convex Aggregation of Common-Scope Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe aggregation when all bounds refer to the same residual optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(L_j\le V\) for every \(j\), then \(\max_jL_j\le V\). If also \(\theta_j\ge0\) and \(\sum_j\theta_j=1\), then \(\sum_j\theta_jL_j\le\max_jL_j\le V\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The maximum of common-scope lower bounds is valid; convex averaging is valid but never stronger.
assumptions_latex: Every \(L_j\) bounds the same residual optimum \(V\).
For the convex form, \(\theta_j\ge0\) and \(\sum_j\theta_j=1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_j\theta_jL_j\le\max_jL_j\le V.
knowledge_statements.title: Maximum and Convex Aggregation of Common-Scope Bounds

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combination of separately fixed cost with a bound on uncharged residual cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If every completion extending node \(\alpha\) incurs an irrevocably fixed cost \(c(\alpha)\), and \(L(\alpha)\) lower-bounds only the remaining cost not represented in \(c(\alpha)\), then \(c(\alpha)+L(\alpha)\) is a valid node lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Already fixed cost may be added to a residual bound only when the two terms charge disjoint cost.
assumptions_latex: \(c(\alpha)\) is incurred by every completion of \(\alpha\).
\(L(\alpha)\) excludes every cost unit already included in \(c(\alpha)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: c(\alpha)+L(\alpha)\le\operatorname{OPT}(H,S\mid\alpha).

notation.meaning: Irrevocably paid and separately accounted cost
Lower bound on remaining uncharged cost

knowledge_statements.title: Paid-Cost plus Residual-Bound Accounting
Combined Lower-Bound Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe max-combination and conditionally safe additive combination of node lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L_1(\alpha),\ldots,L_p(\alpha)\) be sound lower bounds on the residual optimum. Without further conditions, \[L_{\max}(\alpha)=\max_{1\leq j\leq p}L_j(\alpha)\] is sound. The sum \(\sum_jL_j(\alpha)\) is sound only when the certificates use pairwise disjoint cost resources, or when a joint certificate explicitly proves that no unit of soft weight is charged more than once. If \(c(\alpha)\) is cost already irrevocably paid and every \(L_j\) bounds only the remaining uncharged cost, then \(c(\alpha)+\max_jL_j(\alpha)\) is also sound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The maximum of sound bounds is always sound; sums require disjoint weight accounting, and already-paid cost may be added to a residual bound.
assumptions_latex: Each \(L_j(\alpha)\) is a sound bound on the same residual objective.
Any additive combination has a valid non-overlap certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max_jL_j(\alpha)\leq\operatorname{OPT}(H,S\mid\alpha)\), with addition valid only under non-overlapping cost accounting.

notation.meaning: A sound lower bound at search node alpha.
Soft cost already forced and separately accounted for.

children.title: MaxSAT Resolution Calculi
children.top_down_role: Resolution-centered calculi for MaxSAT reasoning.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Classical Resolvent Alone Is Not MaxSAT Cost Preserving
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal pivot example demonstrating the need for residual or compensation clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Take unit-weight clauses \(C_1=x\lor a\) and \(C_2=\neg x\lor b\). Classical resolution replaces them by \(R=a\lor b\). Under the assignment \(x=1,a=1,b=0\), the parent multiset has falsification cost \(1\), because \(C_2\) is false, while \(R\) is true and has cost \(0\). Therefore replacing the parents solely by their classical resolvent does not preserve assignment-wise MaxSAT cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ordinary resolution can change MaxSAT falsification cost when the parent clauses are replaced only by their resolvent.
assumptions_latex: All three clauses have unit weight.
Replacement deletes both parent clauses and retains only the classical resolvent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{cost}_{\{C_1,C_2\}}(1,1,0)=1\ne0=\operatorname{cost}_{\{R\}}(1,1,0).\)
knowledge_statements.title: Classical Resolvent Alone Is Not MaxSAT Cost Preserving
MaxSAT Resolution Calculi
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic definition of weighted resolution rules with explicit compensation for objective preservation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A weighted MaxSAT resolution calculus is a set of pivot-indexed rewrite rules. For a pivot variable \(x\), a rule replaces a finite multiset \(P_x\) of weighted clauses containing both polarities of \(x\) by a multiset \(R_x\) containing at least one resolvent not containing \(x\), together with residual or compensation clauses. The rule is admissible when, for every total assignment \(\tau\), \[\sum_{(C,w)\in P_x}w\,\mathbf{1}[\tau\not\models C]=\sum_{(D,v)\in R_x}v\,\mathbf{1}[\tau\not\models D].\] A derivation is a finite sequence of admissible rewrites; derived weighted empty clauses expose unavoidable objective cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A MaxSAT resolution rule resolves on a pivot while adding residual or compensation clauses so every assignment retains exactly the same falsification cost.
assumptions_latex: All clause weights are nonnegative.
Zero-weight clauses may be deleted.
Assignments are total on variables occurring in the rewritten clauses.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every admissible resolution rewrite preserves the pointwise weighted falsification cost.

notation.meaning: Parent and replacement weighted-clause multisets for pivot x.
Indicator that assignment tau falsifies clause C.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the resolution-calculi leaf, but the proposed pointwise cost-preservation criterion and required pivot, resolvent, residual, and compensation structure need an exact weighted MaxSAT resolution reference.

children.title: MaxSAT Transformation Calculi
children.top_down_role: Calculi based on objective-preserving formula transformations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equisatisfiability Does Not Preserve Assignment Costs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between SAT-preserving rewrites and MaxSAT cost-preserving transformations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=\{(x,1)\}\) and \(G=\{(
eg x,1)\}\). Both are satisfiable and have optimum cost \(0\), but \(\operatorname{cost}_F(0)=1
e0=\operatorname{cost}_G(0)\) and \(\operatorname{cost}_F(1)=0
e1=\operatorname{cost}_G(1)\). Thus equisatisfiability, even together with equality of optimum values, does not imply pointwise cost preservation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equisatisfiable weighted formulas can have equal optima while assigning different costs to corresponding assignments.
assumptions_latex: Both clauses are soft and have weight one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{OPT}(F)=\operatorname{OPT}(G)=0\) but \(\operatorname{cost}_F\not\equiv\operatorname{cost}_G\).
knowledge_statements.title: Equisatisfiability Does Not Preserve Assignment Costs

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Projected Cost Preservation with Auxiliary Variables
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact semantics for transformations that introduce fresh variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) use variables \(X\), let \(G\) use \(X\cup Y\) with \(X\cap Y=\varnothing\), and let \(c_F,c_G\) be offsets. The transformation preserves projected costs exactly when, for every \(x\in\{0,1\}^X\), \[c_F+\operatorname{cost}_F(x)=\min_{y\in\{0,1\}^Y}\bigl(c_G+\operatorname{cost}_G(x,y)\bigr).\] This implies equality of optimum values, and every optimal assignment of \(G\) projects to an optimal assignment of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With fresh auxiliaries, exact preservation means that minimizing transformed cost over extensions recovers each original assignment's cost.
assumptions_latex: \(X\cap Y=\varnothing\).
The Boolean auxiliary domain is finite.
Weights and offsets are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{OPT}(F,c_F)=\operatorname{OPT}(G,c_G)\), and optimal transformed assignments project to original optima.
knowledge_statements.title: Projected Cost Preservation with Auxiliary Variables
MaxSAT Transformation Calculi
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-preserving rewrite systems for weighted MaxSAT clause multisets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A weighted MaxSAT transformation calculus consists of rules \((F,c)\rightsquigarrow(F',c')\), where \(F\) and \(F'\) are weighted-clause multisets and \(c,c'\geq0\) are explicit objective offsets. A rule is cost-preserving when every total assignment \(\tau\) satisfies \[c+\sum_{(C,w)\in F}w\,\mathbf{1}[\tau\not\models C]=c'+\sum_{(D,v)\in F'}v\,\mathbf{1}[\tau\not\models D].\] Rules may split weights, remove zero-weight clauses, extract weighted empty clauses into the offset, or introduce compensation clauses, provided this identity remains valid. Any finite sequence of such rules preserves the optimum and the cost of every assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A MaxSAT transformation calculus rewrites weighted clauses and offsets while preserving every assignment's objective value, and therefore preserves the optimum.
assumptions_latex: All transformed formulas use a common assignment domain or explicitly quantified auxiliary variables.
Every rule satisfies the displayed cost identity.
All weights and offsets are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_\tau\operatorname{cost}_{F,c}(\tau)=\min_\tau\operatorname{cost}_{F',c'}(\tau)\) after every transformation sequence.

notation.meaning: Weighted-clause multisets before and after transformation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the transformation-calculi leaf. A source is required for the claimed calculus and for the semantics of transformations that introduce auxiliary variables, since pointwise equality over a common assignment domain is not by itself a complete convention when domains change.

children.title: Resolution-Transformation Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural relationships between resolution inferences and formula transformations.

knowledge_statements.title: Resolution-Transformation Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted MaxSAT resolution is an objective-preserving transformation with a pivot-resolvent structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every admissible weighted MaxSAT resolution step is a cost-preserving transformation step: its parent multiset and its resolvent, residual, and compensation multiset satisfy the same pointwise cost identity. Hence a resolution derivation \(F_0\Rightarrow F_1\Rightarrow\cdots\Rightarrow F_t\) induces a transformation derivation with \[\operatorname{cost}_{F_0}(\tau)=\operatorname{cost}_{F_t}(\tau)\] for every total assignment \(\tau\), and therefore \(\operatorname{OPT}(F_0)=\operatorname{OPT}(F_t)\). Conversely, a transformation step corresponds to a resolution step only if it admits the calculus's required pivot, resolvent, and compensation decomposition; arbitrary cost-preserving transformations need not do so.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Resolution derivations are cost-preserving transformation derivations; the converse holds only for transformations admitting the required pivot and compensation structure.
assumptions_latex: Every resolution rule satisfies pointwise cost preservation.
All intermediate weights are nonnegative.
The assignment domain is unchanged throughout the derivation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{cost}_{F_0}(\tau)=\operatorname{cost}_{F_t}(\tau)\) for all \(\tau\), so \(\operatorname{OPT}(F_0)=\operatorname{OPT}(F_t)\).

notation.meaning: Successive weighted formulas in a resolution derivation.
Total weight of clauses in F falsified by tau.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits the correspondence leaf, and the forward implication follows from the candidate definitions. A source is still required to establish that those definitions match an accepted MaxSAT resolution and transformation calculus and to delimit the claimed converse.

children.title: MaxCDCL Solver Architecture
children.top_down_role: Conflict-driven MaxSAT search architectures.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete bounded-CDCL calls required by standard integral threshold schedules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the integral optimum lies in \([L_0,U_0]\), ascending threshold search needs at most \(U_0-L_0+1\) complete calls. Binary threshold search that preserves an inclusive certified interval needs at most \(\lceil\log_2(U_0-L_0+1)\rceil\) complete calls to determine the optimal value, excluding any separate call needed to construct an incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear threshold search uses at most the initial gap plus one calls, while binary threshold search uses logarithmically many.
assumptions_latex: Objective values are integral.
Every threshold call is complete and maintains a valid interval containing the optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{linear}}\le U_0-L_0+1,\qquad N_{\mathrm{binary}}\le\lceil\log_2(U_0-L_0+1)\rceil.
knowledge_statements.title: Threshold-Call Bounds

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unified primal and threshold-refutation certificate for an integral MaxSAT objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\) be a correct relaxation-variable encoding with nonnegative integral objective \(f(r)\). A final certificate consists of a model \(M\models E\) with \(f(M)=U\) and a checkable unsatisfiability refutation of \(E\land(f(r)\le U-1)\). The model certifies \(\operatorname{OPT}\le U\), the refutation certifies \(\operatorname{OPT}\ge U\), and hence \(U=\operatorname{OPT}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible model of cost U and a checked refutation of all solutions of cost at most U−1 certify exact optimality.
assumptions_latex: The objective is integral and bounded below.
\(E\) preserves MaxSAT feasibility and costs.
The model and refutation checkers are sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M\models E\land f(M)=U\land\operatorname{UNSAT}(E\land f\le U-1)\Longrightarrow U=\operatorname{OPT}.
knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-CDCL Final Optimality Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of lower-bound updates after an inconclusive bounded search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a search of \(E\land(f\le B)\) ends without a model or a sound unsatisfiability certificate, then \(L\leftarrow B+1\) is unjustified. An unknown or interrupted result cannot exclude costs at most \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Only certified unsatisfiability may raise the lower bound; timeout or unknown may not.
assumptions_latex: The bounded call returns neither a checked model nor a sound unsatisfiability certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{UNKNOWN}(E\land f\le B)\not\Rightarrow\operatorname{OPT}\ge B+1.
knowledge_statements.title: Incomplete Threshold-Call Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correctness invariant for threshold updates in bounded-CDCL search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(L\le\operatorname{OPT}\le U\) and \(L\le B<U\). A complete unsatisfiable query \(E\land(f\le B)\) permits \(L\leftarrow B+1\); a returned model of cost \(c\le B\) permits \(U\leftarrow\min\{U,c\}\). Either update preserves an interval containing the integral optimum, and \(L=U\) determines its value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complete threshold results update one certified endpoint while preserving an interval containing the optimum.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is integer-valued.
\(E\) preserves feasible costs.
The threshold query is complete.
\(L\le B<U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L'\le\operatorname{OPT}\le U'.
knowledge_statements.title: Certified Interval Invariant

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Architecture-level interface among the permanent encoding, bounded solver, learned database, and objective controller; learning derivation and retention policy remain sibling-owned.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent a MaxCDCL state by \(\Sigma=(E,L,U,M,\mathcal D,\Gamma_B)\), where \(E\) is a permanent cost-preserving relaxation encoding, \([L,U]\) is a certified integral objective interval, \(M\) is absent or is a model of \(E\) of cost \(U\), \(\mathcal D\) contains learned constraints with recorded assumption scopes, and \(\Gamma_B\) is the temporary frame encoding \(f\le B\). A bounded invocation on \(E\cup\mathcal D\cup\Gamma_B\) returns a checked model, a checked refutation under \(\Gamma_B\), or an inconclusive result. Only a checked model or refutation authorizes a bound update; withdrawing \(\Gamma_B\) leaves \(E\) unchanged and every retained learned item subject to its recorded scope.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: MaxCDCL maintains a permanent cost encoding, certified objective interval, incumbent, scope-tagged learned database, and temporary threshold frame; only checked models or refutations update bounds.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) preserves all feasible MaxSAT costs.
\(f\) is integer-valued.
Every learned item records the assumptions under which it is valid.
Model and refutation checkers are sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{OPT}(E)\in[L,U]\text{ is preserved by every authorized controller transition}.
knowledge_statements.title: MaxCDCL Persistent-State Interface

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Architecture-level solve–propagate–learn–update loop; learning derivation and retention policies remain sibling-owned.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Construct \(E\), obtain a checked feasible incumbent of cost \(U\) or certify hard infeasibility, and initialize a valid integral lower bound \(L\). While \(L<U\), choose \(B\in[L,U-1]\), install a temporary frame \(\Gamma_B\) encoding \(f\le B\), and run CDCL/PB search. A checked model of cost \(c\le B\) permits \(U\leftarrow\min\{U,c\}\); a checked refutation under \(\Gamma_B\) permits \(L\leftarrow B+1\); an inconclusive result changes neither bound. Withdraw \(\Gamma_B\), retaining learned information only with its valid scope. At \(L=U\), return the incumbent and lower-bound evidence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: MaxCDCL performs objective-bounded CDCL/PB searches, updates bounds only from checked outcomes, manages threshold scopes, and stops when the certified interval closes.
assumptions_latex: The permanent encoding preserves feasible costs.
The objective is nonnegative and integral.
The upper endpoint is attained by a checked incumbent.
Every bound-changing outcome has a checkable model or refutation.
Learning and retention follow sound sibling-owned regimes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Termination at }L=U\text{ returns an incumbent of cost }\operatorname{OPT}=L=U.

notation.meaning: Certified lower bound and attained incumbent value.

knowledge_statements.title: Complete Bounded-CDCL MaxCDCL Controller

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Syntactically valid permanent relaxation encoding used by the architecture.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given hard clauses \(H\) and weighted soft clauses \((C_i,w_i)\), introduce a fresh Boolean variable \(r_i\) for each soft clause and define \[E=H\land\bigwedge_i(C_i\lor r_i),\qquad f(r)=\sum_iw_i r_i.\] Every hard-feasible assignment extends with equal violation cost by setting \(r_i=1\) exactly for falsified soft clauses. Every model of \(E\) projects to a hard-feasible assignment whose violation cost is at most \(f(r)\). Therefore minimizing \(f\) gives the weighted partial-MaxSAT optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fresh clause-specific relaxation variables produce a permanent formula whose minimum weighted relaxation cost equals the MaxSAT optimum.
assumptions_latex: Every \(r_i\) is fresh and clause-specific.
Hard clauses are mandatory.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_{M\models E}f(M)=\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{MaxSAT}}.

notation.meaning: Relaxation variable for soft clause i.

knowledge_statements.title: Cost-Preserving Permanent MaxCDCL Encoding
MaxCDCL Solver Architecture
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact bound-search architecture coupling CDCL reasoning with a weighted relaxation objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given hard clauses \(H\) and soft clauses \((C_i,w_i)\), introduce \(r_i\) and form \(E=H\cup\{C_i\lor r_ifloor_i\}\), interpreting the subscript only as the associated index, with objective \(f(r)=\sum_iw_ir_i\). Initialize a valid lower bound \(L\) and incumbent upper bound \(U\). While \(L<U\), choose an integer \(B\) with \(L\leq B<U\) and run CDCL with pseudo-Boolean propagation on \(E\land(f(r)\leq B)\). If satisfiable, set \(U\) to the smaller of \(U\) and the model cost; if unsatisfiable, set \(L=B+1\). Retain globally valid learned constraints, and guard bound-local constraints. Stop at \(L=U\) and return an incumbent of cost \(U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: MaxCDCL repeatedly solves objective-bounded relaxation encodings with CDCL, learns valid constraints, updates lower or upper bounds, and terminates when they coincide.
assumptions_latex: Weights and objective bounds are nonnegative integers.
Initial bounds satisfy \(L\leq\operatorname{OPT}\leq U\).
Each bounded CDCL call is complete.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Upon termination, the returned incumbent has cost \(L=U=\operatorname{OPT}(H,S)\).

notation.meaning: Relaxation variable for soft clause i.
Lower bound, incumbent upper bound, and tested objective bound.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the solver-architecture leaf, but the encoding contains the malformed expression \(C_i\lor r_i\rfloor_i\), including an unmatched \(\rfloor\). A MaxCDCL source is also required to support the architecture, bound-update policy, and learned-constraint retention conditions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Validity Scope of Learned Constraints across Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed retention rule for learned information between objective-threshold calls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A learned constraint \(D\) may be retained unguarded across all threshold calls only if \(E\models D\). If it is justified only under \(f(r)\le B\), it must be discarded when that assumption is withdrawn or stored as \((f(r)\le B)\Rightarrow D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Globally implied learned constraints persist across bounds; threshold-local constraints require guards or deletion.
assumptions_latex: E\text{ is the permanent relaxation encoding}.
Each learned constraint has a checkable derivation under its recorded assumptions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: E\models D\Rightarrow D\text{ is globally reusable};\quad E\land(f\le B)\models D\not\Rightarrow E\models D.
knowledge_statements.title: Validity Scope of Learned Constraints across Bounds

intermediate_metadata.reason: This leaf owns the overall bounded-CDCL solver architecture, objective-bound state, threshold scheduling, and final optimality interface. Objective-conflict derivation and learned-constraint retention policies were excluded as sibling-owned; accordingly, the proposed retention record is deferred as misplaced. The malformed central seed and missing certificate contract require expansion.

children.title: Objective-Conflict Learning
children.top_down_role: Learning mechanisms derived from conflicts involving objective bounds.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal failure caused by retaining a threshold-local consequence after relaxing the threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\) impose no restriction on \(r\in\{0,1\}\). Under \(r\le0\), the clause \(D=\neg r\) is entailed. Under \(r\le1\), the assignment \(r=1\) is feasible but is removed if \(D\) persists unguarded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lemma forcing a relaxation variable false at threshold zero becomes invalid when the threshold is relaxed to one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
E\land(r\le0)\models
eg r,\qquad E\land(r\le1)
ot\models
eg r.
knowledge_statements.title: Unguarded Bound-Lemma Failure

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity and lifetime criterion for a constraint derived from an objective-bound conflict.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\) be the bound-independent encoding and \(A_B\) an activated encoding of \(f(r)\le B\). If sound conflict analysis derives \(D\) with \(E\land A_B\models D\), adding \(D\) preserves the bounded instance. It may persist unguarded after deactivating \(A_B\) when \(E\models D\); otherwise the persistent consequence must retain its dependency, for example as \(A_B\rightarrow D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bound-derived constraint is valid under that bound; it survives unguarded only if the base encoding entails it, otherwise its bound dependency must remain guarded.
assumptions_latex: Conflict analysis is implication-sound.
\(A_B\) is satisfiability-equivalent to the intended active threshold in the encoded space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: E\land A_B\models D,\qquad E\models D\text{ or }E\models(A_B\rightarrow D)\text{ for persistent retention}.
knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Dependent Learning Validity
Objective-Conflict Learning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Learned clauses or inequalities explaining conflicts caused by the active objective bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\) be a relaxation encoding and let the active objective constraint be \(f(r)\leq B\). If propagation under a partial assignment \(\alpha\) yields a conflict, conflict analysis may derive a clause or pseudo-Boolean inequality \(D\) satisfying \[E\land(f(r)\leq B)\models D\quad\text{and}\quad\alpha\not\models D.\] A derivation trace from the conflicting constraints certifies that \(D\) excludes the conflicting state without removing any model of the bounded instance. If \(D\) depends on \(B\), it must be guarded by that bound or discarded when the bound changes; an unguarded constraint may persist only when \(E\models D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Objective-conflict learning derives a checkable clause or inequality that blocks a bound-induced conflict while preserving every model allowed by the active bound.
assumptions_latex: Propagation and conflict-analysis rules are implication-sound.
The active bound is represented as a checkable pseudo-Boolean constraint.
Bound-dependent learned constraints are guarded or scoped.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D\) is a valid learned constraint for \(E\land(f(r)\leq B)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind is appropriate for a trace-justified learned constraint, but \(\alpha\not\models D\) does not mean that a partial assignment falsifies or is excluded by \(D\); it may merely leave \(D\) undecided. The statement needs a source-backed correction using the proper falsification or entailment condition and precise guarded-learning semantics.

children.title: Objective-Learning Integration Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes governing integration of objective information into learned constraints.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incremental integration of objective thresholds without making them permanent base constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain a bound-independent database \(E\). For each threshold \(B\), add an exact activation-controlled encoding \(a_B\rightarrow(f(r)\le B)\) and solve under assumption \(a_B\). On a bound change, retract the assumption. Unconditional consequences entailed by \(E\) may persist; every bound-dependent consequence must retain its activation dependency.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Install objective bounds through assumptions so global learning persists while threshold-local learning remains guarded.
assumptions_latex: Each activated bound encoding is exact under its activation literal.
Learned constraints retain every activation dependency used in their derivation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{SAT}(E\land a_B)\iff\operatorname{SAT}(E\land(f(r)\le B)).
knowledge_statements.title: Assumption-Activated Objective Integration

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Soundness condition for replacing an integrated objective threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose threshold \(B\) is replaced by \(B'\) while a constraint \(D\), known only from \(E\land(f(r)\le B)\models D\), remains active. If \(E\land(f(r)\le B')\not\models D\), the retained state is not equivalent to the intended new bounded instance. Sound replacement requires retraction, guarding, or an independent proof that \(E\models D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Changing a threshold is unsound when old threshold-local lemmas remain active without valid guards.
assumptions_latex: The new threshold need not imply the old threshold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: E\land(f\le B')\not\models D\Rightarrow E\land(f\le B')\land D\text{ is not an equivalent replacement state}.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective-State Replacement Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe reuse of an old threshold consequence under a stronger minimization threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(E\land(f(r)\le B)\models D\) and a replacement threshold satisfies \(B'\le B\), then \(E\land(f(r)\le B')\models D\). Thus an old bound-local consequence remains logically valid under monotone tightening, although its recorded dependency is still needed if the solver may later relax or remove the threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lemma valid under an objective upper bound remains valid under every tighter bound, but not automatically after relaxation or withdrawal.
assumptions_latex: The objective uses a minimization upper-bound convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl(E\land(f\le B)\models D\bigr)\land B'\le B\Longrightarrow E\land(f\le B')\models D.
knowledge_statements.title: Monotone-Tightening Reuse of Bound-Local Consequences

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct integration when objective upper bounds only strengthen.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain one solver state and permanently conjoin bounds \(f(r)\le B_1,f(r)\le B_2,\ldots\), where \(B_{k+1}\le B_k\). Every consequence entailed by an earlier active formula remains valid after tightening. Later relaxation or withdrawal requires rebuilding or dependency guards.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Permanently installed bounds are safe when thresholds only tighten; relaxation requires rebuilding or guards.
assumptions_latex: The objective uses a minimization upper-bound convention.
\(B_{k+1}\le B_k\) at every update.
Each learned constraint is entailed by the formula active when learned.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: E\land(f\le B_k)\models D\Longrightarrow E\land(f\le B_{k+1})\models D.
knowledge_statements.title: Permanent Monotone-Tightening Regime

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational regime using independent bounded solver calls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each threshold \(B\), construct or reset a solver for \(E\land(f(r)\le B)\), solve it, export only its model or checked refutation and constraints independently certified as consequences of \(E\), and discard all other call-local state before changing \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The external regime solves thresholds independently and carries across only globally justified information.
assumptions_latex: Every bounded call used for a certified update is complete.
Every persistent exported constraint is independently entailed by \(E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Call-local learning does not alter the semantics of a later threshold call}.
knowledge_statements.title: Externally Rebuilt Threshold Regime
Objective-Learning Integration Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classification by how objective bounds participate in propagation, conflict analysis, and learned-constraint retention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a relaxation encoding \(E\) with objective \(f(r)\), objective learning has three integration regimes. In an external regime, a controller changes \(B\) while CDCL reasons primarily over \(E\), and bound-specific information is scoped to each call. In an integrated regime, \(f(r)\leq B\) participates directly in propagation and conflict analysis, producing guarded objective-conflict constraints. In a hybrid regime, both mechanisms are used, with selected globally entailed consequences retained across bounds. Exactness requires every persistent learned constraint \(D\) to satisfy \(E\models D\), while a bound-specific constraint need only satisfy \(E\land(f(r)\leq B)\models D\) if it remains correctly guarded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Objective learning may be external, fully integrated, or hybrid; persistent constraints must be globally entailed, while bound-specific constraints require correct guarding.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) is a sound relaxation encoding.
Every learned constraint has a checkable implication justification.
Bound-local constraints carry an enforceable scope guard.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Learned-constraint retention is sound precisely under the stated global-entailment or guarded-bound entailment condition.

notation.meaning: Relaxation encoding independent of the current objective bound.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A representation is a reasonable kind for an integration-regime classification, but no source supports the external, integrated, and hybrid taxonomy. The word 'precisely' also overstates necessity unless the allowed retention mechanisms and guard semantics are formally fixed by a cited framework.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural and binary-size bound for the direct pseudo-Boolean encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With \(n\) propositional variables, \(|S|\) soft clauses, \(|H|\) hard clauses, and \(L\) literal occurrences, the direct indicator encoding uses \(n+|S|\) Boolean variables, \(|H|+|S|\) PB inequalities, and \(O(L+|S|)\) nonzero coefficients. Copying binary-encoded weights into the objective yields polynomial output length.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The direct MaxSAT-to-PB encoding is linear in clause structure and polynomial in full binary input size.
assumptions_latex: The instance is explicitly encoded.
Weights are copied in binary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |T(I)|=O(L+n+|H|+|S|+\text{weight-bit-length}).

notation.meaning: Direct pseudo-Boolean encoding of instance I.

knowledge_statements.title: Polynomial-Size Clause-to-PB Reduction

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Negative Soft Weights Break One-Sided Violation Semantics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weight-sign boundary for the usual soft-clause indicator constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In \(\sum_{\ell\in C_j}t(\ell)+u_j\ge1\), a positive objective coefficient makes an optimum choose \(u_j=0\) whenever \(C_j\) is satisfied. If \(w_j<0\), minimization instead favors \(u_j=1\) even for a satisfied clause, so the one-sided constraint no longer makes \(u_j\) its violation indicator. Exact reification or a reformulation is then required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negative penalties invalidate the usual one-sided violation-indicator semantics.
assumptions_latex: Only the usual lower-linking clause inequality is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: w_j<0\Longrightarrow u_j\text{ need not equal }[\neg C_j].

notation.meaning: Proposed violation indicator for soft clause j.

knowledge_statements.title: Negative Soft Weights Break One-Sided Violation Semantics

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent objective conventions for the pseudo-Boolean reduction of weighted partial MaxSAT.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W=\sum_{j\in S}w_j\). For every hard-feasible assignment \(x\), \[\sum_{j\in S:C_j(x)=0}w_j=W-\sum_{j\in S:C_j(x)=1}w_j.\] Consequently, minimizing falsified soft weight is equivalent to maximizing satisfied soft weight, and \(\operatorname{OPT}_{\min}=W-\operatorname{OPT}_{\max}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimizing violated soft weight and maximizing satisfied soft weight select the same assignments, with values complementary to total soft weight.
assumptions_latex: S\text{ is finite}.
The two objectives use the same soft-clause weights.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname*{argmin}_{x}\sum_{j:C_j(x)=0}w_j=\operatorname*{argmax}_{x}\sum_{j:C_j(x)=1}w_j.
knowledge_statements.title: Satisfied-Weight and Violation-Cost Equivalence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pseudo-Boolean reification of a soft clause’s violation independently of objective-coefficient signs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a soft clause \(C_j\), introduce \(u_j\in\{0,1\}\) and impose \[u_j\ge 1-\sum_{\ell\in C_j}t(\ell),\qquad u_j\le 1-t(\ell)\quad(\ell\in C_j).\] Then \(u_j=1\) if and only if every literal of \(C_j\) is false. Hence \(\sum_j w_j u_j\) equals the signed weighted violation cost for arbitrary real coefficients \(w_j\); hard clauses remain represented by \(\sum_{\ell\in C_j}t(\ell)\ge1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One lower inequality and one upper inequality per literal exactly reify clause violation, including when violation coefficients are nonpositive.
assumptions_latex: \(t(\ell)\in\{0,1\}\) is the truth value of literal \(\ell\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: u_j=1\iff C_j\text{ is false}.

notation.meaning: Exact violation indicator for soft clause j.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Two-Sided Violation Reification

knowledge_statements.statement_title: MaxSAT Cost-Threshold Correspondence in the Two-Sided PB Encoding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decision-threshold preservation under exact soft-clause violation reification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the exact two-sided reification \(u_j=1\iff C_j\text{ is false}\), for every threshold \(B\), a hard-feasible MaxSAT assignment falsifying soft clauses of total weight at most \(B\) exists if and only if the corresponding PB system has a feasible solution satisfying \(\sum_{j\in S}w_j u_j\le B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact violation reification preserves every weighted MaxSAT decision threshold in the PB formulation.
assumptions_latex: Every hard clause is encoded exactly.
Each \(u_j\) is exactly reified as the violation indicator of soft clause \(C_j\).
Weights and the threshold are represented exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists x:\operatorname{cost}_{\mathrm{MaxSAT}}(x)\le B\iff\exists(x,u):\operatorname{PB}(x,u)\land\sum_jw_ju_j\le B.

notation.meaning: Exact violation indicator for soft clause j.

knowledge_statements.title: MaxSAT Cost-Threshold Correspondence in the Two-Sided PB Encoding
MaxSAT via Pseudo-Boolean Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact weighted partial MaxSAT encoding as a pseudo-Boolean minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let soft clauses be indexed by \(S\), hard clauses by \(H\), and let \(w_j>0\) for \(j\in S\). For Boolean variables \(x_i\in\{0,1\}\), define \(t(x_i)=x_i\) and \(t(\neg x_i)=1-x_i\). Introduce \(u_j\in\{0,1\}\) for each soft clause. Then weighted partial MaxSAT is represented by
\[\min \sum_{j\in S}w_j u_j\]
subject to
\[\sum_{\ell\in C_j}t(\ell)\ge 1\quad(j\in H),\qquad \sum_{\ell\in C_j}t(\ell)+u_j\ge1\quad(j\in S).\]
For every feasible assignment, minimizing over \(u\) gives \(u_j=1\) exactly when soft clause \(C_j\) is false; hence the optimum equals the minimum total weight of falsified soft clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clause-violation indicators turn weighted partial MaxSAT into a pseudo-Boolean problem whose objective is exactly the total weight of falsified soft clauses.
assumptions_latex: \(C_j\) is a finite disjunction of literals for every \(j\in H\cup S\).
\(w_j>0\) for every \(j\in S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{PB}}=\min_x\sum_{j\in S:C_j(x)=0}w_j\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is mathematically precise and fits the terminal container, but the cited generic integer-programming-models chapter is indirect and does not inspectably support this specific weighted partial MaxSAT pseudo-Boolean encoding. An authoritative MaxSAT or pseudo-Boolean source with a specific encoding locator is required.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural size of the direct clause formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(n\) source variables, \(|H|\) hard clauses, \(|S|\) soft clauses, and \(L\) literal occurrences, the violation-variable formulation has \(n+|S|\) binary variables, \(|H|+|S|\) clause inequalities, and \(O(L+|S|)\) nonzero coefficients. Copying binary-encoded weights gives polynomial total encoding length.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The direct 0–1 IP reduction has linear structural size and polynomial binary encoding length.
assumptions_latex: Clauses and weights are explicit.
Weights are copied in binary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{var}}=n+|S|,\quad N_{\mathrm{con}}=|H|+|S|,\quad N_{\mathrm{nz}}=O(L+|S|).
knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Size Direct Formulation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Continuous Relaxation Is Not Generally Exact
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integrality boundary of the direct formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For three unit-weight soft clauses \((x)\), \((y)\), and \((\neg x\vee\neg y)\), every Boolean assignment violates at least one clause, so the integer optimum is \(1\). After replacing binary domains by unit intervals, \(x=y=1/2\) and all three violation variables equal to zero satisfy the relaxation, giving value \(0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dropping integrality can create a strict objective gap, so the direct LP relaxation is not an exact MaxSAT solver.
assumptions_latex: The violation-variable formulation is used.
Binary domains are relaxed to [0,1].
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{LP}}<\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{IP}}\text{ is possible}.
knowledge_statements.title: Continuous Relaxation Is Not Generally Exact

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact minimization-oriented 0–1 IP formulation of weighted partial MaxSAT.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each soft clause \(C_j\), introduce \(u_j\in\{0,1\}\), impose \(\sum_{\ell\in C_j}t(\ell)+u_j\ge1\), impose \(\sum_{\ell\in C_h}t(\ell)\ge1\) for every hard clause, and minimize \(\sum_{j\in S}w_j u_j\). With \(w_j>0\), every optimum sets \(u_j=1\) exactly when \(C_j\) is false.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary violation variables yield an exact 0–1 IP minimizing falsified soft-clause weight while enforcing hard clauses.
assumptions_latex: w_j>0\text{ for every soft clause}.
t(x_i)=x_i,\quad t(\neg x_i)=1-x_i.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min\sum_{j\in S}w_j u_j=\min_{x\text{ hard-feasible}}\sum_{j:C_j(x)=0}w_j.

notation.meaning: Violation variable for soft clause j.
Linear truth-value expression for literal ell.

knowledge_statements.title: Violation-Variable 0–1 Formulation
MaxSAT via 0–1 Integer Programming
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact weighted partial MaxSAT encoding as a binary linear integer program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) and \(S\) index hard and soft clauses, with \(w_j>0\) for \(j\in S\). For each propositional variable use \(x_i\in\{0,1\}\), and define \(t(x_i)=x_i\), \(t(\neg x_i)=1-x_i\). Introduce \(z_j\in\{0,1\}\) for each soft clause and solve
\[\max \sum_{j\in S}w_jz_j\]
subject to
\[\sum_{\ell\in C_j}t(\ell)\ge1\quad(j\in H),\qquad z_j\le\sum_{\ell\in C_j}t(\ell)\quad(j\in S).\]
At an optimum, positivity of \(w_j\) makes \(z_j=1\) exactly for satisfied soft clauses. Thus optimal assignments and optimal satisfied weight agree with weighted partial MaxSAT.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary truth and clause-satisfaction variables yield a 0–1 linear program maximizing exactly the satisfied soft-clause weight while enforcing every hard clause.
assumptions_latex: \(C_j\) is a finite clause for every \(j\in H\cup S\).
\(w_j>0\) for every \(j\in S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{IP}}=\max_{x:\,C_j(x)=1\ \forall j\in H}\sum_{j\in S:C_j(x)=1}w_j\).

notation.meaning: Linear binary expression giving the truth value of literal \(\ell\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The binary linear formulation is mathematically sound and the representation content kind fits the leaf, but the cited generic integer-programming chapter does not inspectably establish this MaxSAT encoding. A specific MaxSAT-to-0–1-IP source locator is required.

children.title: MaxSAT via Weighted CSP
children.top_down_role: Encodings of MaxSAT instances as weighted constraint satisfaction problems.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Succinct-versus-tabular size boundary for clause cost functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If each clause cost is represented intensionally by its literals and exceptional falsifying tuple, the reduction has \(m\) local functions and \(O(L+m+n)\) structural size. If an arity-\(k\) function is tabulated over all Boolean tuples, its table can require \(2^k\) entries; polynomial size then requires bounded arity or a succinct representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The WCSP reduction is linear with succinct clause costs but may be exponential when high-arity costs are fully tabulated.
assumptions_latex: Variables have Boolean domains.
L\text{ is the total clause-literal count}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |T(I)|=O(L+m+n)\text{ intensionally, while an arity-}k\text{ table can have }2^k\text{ entries}.

notation.meaning: Arity of a clause cost function.

knowledge_statements.title: Clause-Scope WCSP Encoding Size

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of a finite penalty intended to represent a hard clause.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a hard-clause violation receives a finite penalty \(M\le W=\sum_{j\in S}w_j\), there are instances in which a hard-violating assignment costs no more than every hard-feasible assignment. Consequently such an \(M\) does not generally enforce hard semantics; an absorbing top or a penalty exceeding every attainable soft cost is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nominal hard penalty no larger than the possible soft cost can permit a hard-violating optimum.
assumptions_latex: W=\sum_{j\in S}w_j.
Hard violations remain target-feasible and receive penalty M.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M\le W\centernot\implies\arg\min F\subseteq\{a:a\text{ satisfies all hard clauses}\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Insufficient Top Cost Violates Hardness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation of hard clauses by an absorbing infeasibility cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W=\sum_{j\in S}w_j\) and choose \(\top>W\). Assign cost \(w_j\) to falsifying soft clause \(C_j\), zero otherwise, and cost \(\top\) to falsifying hard clause \(C_h\), zero otherwise. If aggregation caps sums at the absorbing value \(\top\), then \(F(a)<\top\) exactly when \(a\) satisfies every hard clause, and below \(\top\), \(F(a)\) equals the falsified soft-clause weight.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An absorbing top cost larger than every attainable soft penalty exactly represents hard clauses in a weighted CSP.
assumptions_latex: w_j\ge0.
\top>\sum_{j\in S}w_j.
Cost aggregation is capped at the absorbing value \top.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F(a)<\top\iff a\text{ satisfies all hard clauses},\qquad F(a)=\sum_{j:C_j(a)=0}w_j\text{ below }\top.
knowledge_statements.title: Top-Cost Weighted-CSP Variant
MaxSAT via Weighted CSP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost-function representation of weighted partial MaxSAT over binary domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Give each propositional variable \(X_i\) domain \(\{0,1\}\). For every hard clause \(C_j\), impose the relation containing exactly the local tuples that satisfy \(C_j\). For every soft clause \(C_j\) of weight \(w_j>0\), define a cost function on its variables by
\[f_j(a)=\begin{cases}0,&C_j(a)=1,\\ w_j,&C_j(a)=0.\end{cases}\]
The weighted CSP minimizes \(F(a)=\sum_{j\in S}f_j(a)\) over assignments satisfying every hard relation. Its feasible assignments are precisely the hard-clause-satisfying assignments, and \(F(a)\) is precisely their falsified soft-clause weight. Consequently, decoding is the identity on Boolean assignments and preserves all optimal solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Represent hard clauses as relations and soft clauses as zero-or-weight cost functions; minimizing total cost is exactly weighted partial MaxSAT.
assumptions_latex: All propositional variables have binary domains.
Every soft-clause weight satisfies \(w_j>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{WCSP}}=\min_{a:\,C_j(a)=1\ \forall j\in H}\sum_{j\in S:C_j(a)=0}w_j\).

notation.meaning: Local cost function associated with soft clause \(C_j\).
Sum of all soft-clause cost functions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cost-function construction is coherent, objective preserving, and correctly classified as a representation, but no citation supports the weighted-CSP semantics or reduction. Supply an authoritative source with a specific section, theorem, or page locator.

children.title: MaxSAT via Answer-Set Optimization
children.top_down_role: Encodings of MaxSAT objectives in answer-set optimization frameworks.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Size of the direct finite-ground answer-set reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(n\) variables, \(m\) clauses, and \(L\) literal occurrences, a direct ground encoding uses \(O(n+m)\) atoms and rules and \(O(L+m+n)\) rule-literal occurrences. Copying binary weights and priorities gives polynomial total output length.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The direct ground answer-set reduction is linear in explicit clause structure and polynomial in full input length.
assumptions_latex: The MaxSAT instance is finite and already ground.
Weights and priorities are copied in binary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |T(I)|=O(L+m+n+\text{weight-and-priority bit length}).

notation.meaning: Ground answer-set optimization encoding of instance I.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear Ground Encoding Size

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Default Negation Requires a Controlled Assignment Module
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary for interpreting atom absence as falsity of a source variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under stable-model semantics, \(\mathtt{not\ x}\) succeeds when \(x\) is absent from the candidate stable model. It represents falsity of the source Boolean variable only relative to an assignment module whose projected stable models cover exactly the intended choices for \(x\); additional rules that restrict or derive assignment atoms can otherwise destroy the required assignment correspondence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Default negation can encode a false Boolean literal only relative to a controlled module that preserves the intended assignment projections.
assumptions_latex: Stable-model semantics is used.
Source assignments are decoded from designated assignment atoms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathtt{not\ x}\text{ represents source falsity only under exact assignment-projection semantics}.

notation.meaning: Default negation in an answer-set rule body.

knowledge_statements.title: Default Negation Requires a Controlled Assignment Module

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lexicographic answer-set optimization variant for stratified soft clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition soft clauses into priority levels \(S_p\). Assign each clause \(j\in S_p\) a weak-constraint penalty of weight \(w_j\) at priority \(p\). Under a fixed lexicographic priority convention, optimal answer sets minimize the violation-cost vector by priority order. Ordinary weighted MaxSAT is the single-priority special case.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weak-constraint priorities encode lexicographically stratified MaxSAT; ordinary weighted MaxSAT uses one priority level.
assumptions_latex: The selected answer-set language uses the stated lexicographic priority convention.
Clauses, weights, and priorities are finite and ground.
The base assignment and violation encoding is faithful.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{cost}(M)=\operatorname{lex}_{p}\left(\sum_{j\in S_p}w_j[\neg C_j(M)]\right).

notation.meaning: Soft clauses at priority level p.
Stable model encoding a Boolean assignment.

knowledge_statements.title: Priority-Level MaxSAT Encoding
MaxSAT via Answer-Set Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ground answer-set encoding using choice rules, violation atoms, constraints, and weak constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each Boolean variable introduce an atom \(x_i\) and the choice rule \(\mathtt{\{x_i\}.}\), interpreting membership of \(x_i\) in a stable model as truth. For each clause \(C_j=\ell_{j1}\vee\cdots\vee\ell_{jk}\), add
\[\mathtt{viol(j)\ :-\ F(\ell_{j1}),\ldots,F(\ell_{jk}).}\]
where \(F(x_i)=\mathtt{not\ x_i}\) and \(F(\neg x_i)=\mathtt{x_i}\). Add \(\mathtt{:-viol(j).}\) for \(j\in H\), and the weak constraint \(\mathtt{: \!\sim viol(j).\ [w_j@1,j]}\) for \(j\in S\). Stable models correspond to hard-clause-satisfying assignments, and their weak-constraint cost is the total weight of falsified soft clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choice rules encode assignments; violation atoms detect false clauses, hard constraints reject them, and weak constraints minimize weighted soft violations.
assumptions_latex: The MaxSAT instance and resulting answer-set program are finite and ground.
Every soft-clause weight \(w_j\) is a positive integer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{ASO}}=\min_{x:\,C_j(x)=1\ \forall j\in H}\sum_{j\in S:C_j(x)=0}w_j\).

notation.meaning: Answer-set body literal true exactly when propositional literal \(\ell\) is false.
Atom indicating that clause \(C_j\) is violated.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed finite ground encoding fits the representation leaf, but its stable-model correspondence and version-sensitive weak-constraint syntax have no cited support. An authoritative answer-set optimization source with a precise locator is required before the syntax and objective claim can be relied upon.

children.title: Reduction-Fidelity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits involving objective preservation, weights, or representational overhead.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Succinctness Is Part of Reduction Fidelity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between semantic equivalence and a polynomial reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Even with exact feasible-set projection and pointwise cost preservation, a translation is not a polynomial reduction if constructing or writing the target instance, representing its weights or tables, or decoding its solutions requires superpolynomial time or output length in the source encoding size.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Semantic exactness does not imply a polynomial reduction when representation or decoding overhead is superpolynomial.
assumptions_latex: Source size is measured by full binary encoding length.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{semantic fidelity}\centernot\implies\text{polynomial reduction}.
knowledge_statements.title: Succinctness Is Part of Reduction Fidelity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary for replacing lexicographic levels by one scalar objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the total possible variation below priority \(p\) is at most \(R_{<p}\), a scalar coefficient for one unit at level \(p\) preserves lexicographic dominance when it exceeds \(R_{<p}\), after accounting for all lower-level scaling. A coefficient no larger than that range can reverse the lexicographic order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scalarizing priorities is faithful only when each higher-level unit dominates every possible lower-level cost change.
assumptions_latex: All level costs are finite nonnegative integers.
The priority order and minimization convention are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M_p>R_{<p}\text{ is sufficient for level-}p\text{ dominance; }M_p\le R_{<p}\text{ can fail}.

notation.meaning: Maximum aggregate variation below priority p.

knowledge_statements.title: Priority Flattening Requires Dominating Multipliers

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Optimizer Preservation Is Weaker than Cost Preservation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation of decoded optimizer agreement from pointwise objective fidelity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A reduction may satisfy \(\pi(\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in Y}g(y))=\operatorname*{argmin}_{a\in A}f(a)\) while assigning incorrect costs to nonoptimal objects. Optimizer preservation alone therefore does not preserve optimal values, thresholds, approximation gaps, or near-optimal solution sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matching optimizers does not imply preservation of objective values or suboptimality structure.
assumptions_latex: f\text{ and }g\text{ are minimization objectives}.
\pi:Y\to A\text{ is a decoder}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \pi(\arg\min g)=\arg\min f\centernot\implies g(y)=\alpha+\beta f(\pi(y)).

notation.meaning: Decoder from target objects to source assignments.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimizer Preservation Is Weaker than Cost Preservation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Auxiliary Target Models Require Projection Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplicity, spurious-model, and missing-representative boundaries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Several target models may decode to one source assignment without harming optimization, provided every target model decodes to a source-feasible assignment and every source-feasible assignment has a representative with the required cost. A spurious decoded model or a source assignment with no representative violates exact feasible-set fidelity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Target-model multiplicity is harmless, but spurious models and missing source representatives are not.
assumptions_latex: \pi\text{ is defined on target-feasible models}.
Costs are compared after projection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Multiplicity is allowed, whereas exact coverage requires }\pi(Y)=A.
knowledge_statements.title: Auxiliary Target Models Require Projection Control

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Decision-Threshold Transfer under Positive Affine Cost
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer of exact cost-threshold queries through a faithful objective transformation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(g(y)=\alpha+\beta f(\pi(y))\) for every \(y\in Y\), where \(\beta>0\) and \(\pi(Y)=A\), then for every source threshold \(k\), \[\exists a\in A:f(a)\le k\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\exists y\in Y:g(y)\le\alpha+\beta k.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive affine cost correspondence transfers every source decision threshold to the corresponding target threshold.
assumptions_latex: \pi(Y)=A.
g(y)=\alpha+\beta f(\pi(y))\text{ for every }y\in Y.
\beta>0.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_{a\in A}f(a)\le k\iff\min_{y\in Y}g(y)\le\alpha+\beta k.
knowledge_statements.title: Decision-Threshold Transfer under Positive Affine Cost

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonpositive Objective Scale Does Not Preserve Minimizers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp sign boundary for affine objective correspondence in a minimizing reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the source feasible set be \(A=\{a_0,a_1\}\) with \(f(a_0)=0\) and \(f(a_1)=1\), and let the target contain corresponding objects \(y_0,y_1\). If \(g(y)=\alpha+\beta f(\pi(y))\), then \(\beta=0\) makes both target costs equal, while \(\beta<0\) makes \(y_1\) strictly preferable. Thus preservation of source minimizers by an affine cost map requires positive scale, except when the source cost is constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero affine scale loses optimizer distinctions, and negative scale reverses the minimization order.
assumptions_latex: Source and target use minimization.
The source objective is nonconstant on its feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \beta\le0\Longrightarrow\arg\min g\text{ need not decode to }\arg\min f.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonpositive Objective Scale Does Not Preserve Minimizers
Reduction-Fidelity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational conditions under which an optimization reduction preserves feasibility, objective values, and optimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\) be the feasible MaxSAT assignments, \(Y\) the feasible objects of a target formalism, and \(\pi:Y\to A\) a polynomial-time decoder. An objective-faithful reduction satisfies
\[\pi(Y)=A,\qquad g(y)=\alpha+\beta f(\pi(y))\quad\text{for every }y\in Y,\qquad \beta>0,\]
where \(f\) and \(g\) are minimized source and target costs. These conditions ensure that target optima decode to source optima and that every source optimum has an optimal target representative. Fidelity is not guaranteed if hard-feasibility coverage, soft-weight multiplicity, objective direction, priority levels, or the target formalism's model semantics violate either displayed condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reduction is faithful when decoding covers exactly the feasible assignments and target cost is a positive affine transform of source cost.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) and \(Y\) are the respective feasible sets.
Both \(f\) and \(g\) use minimization conventions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi(\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in Y}g(y))=\operatorname*{argmin}_{a\in A}f(a)\).

notation.meaning: Decoder from target feasible objects to MaxSAT assignments.
Affine objective constants with positive scale \(\beta\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated coverage and positive-affine objective conditions do imply the displayed optimizer correspondence and fit a condition container, but no source supports this reduction-fidelity criterion or its listed failure boundaries.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed closure of exact polynomial optimization reductions under composition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(R_1\) has decoder \(\pi_1:Y\to A\) with \(\pi_1(Y)=A\) and \(g(y)=\alpha_1+\beta_1f(\pi_1(y))\), and \(R_2\) has decoder \(\pi_2:Z\to Y\) with \(\pi_2(Z)=Y\) and \(h(z)=\alpha_2+\beta_2g(\pi_2(z))\), where \(\beta_1,\beta_2>0\). Then \(\pi_1\circ\pi_2\) is onto and \[h(z)=(\alpha_2+\beta_2\alpha_1)+(\beta_2\beta_1)f((\pi_1\circ\pi_2)(z)).\] Polynomial translations and decoders remain polynomial under composition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Onto positive-affine faithful reductions compose, but this is a general reduction theorem rather than a boundary specific to the WCSP–answer-set pair.
assumptions_latex: Both component translations and decoders have polynomial time and output bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R_2\circ R_1\text{ is an objective-faithful polynomial reduction}.
knowledge_statements.title: Composition of Faithful Reductions

intermediate_metadata.reason: This leaf locally owns pair-specific feasible-set, cost, optimizer, threshold, priority, and succinctness boundaries. Concrete MaxSAT-via-WCSP and MaxSAT-via-Answer-Set encodings were excluded as adjacent sibling scopes. The proposed composition theorem is mathematically sound but deferred because its canonical home is general reduction theory. The unified definition and instantiated checklist remain missing.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Additive-Approximation Transfer under Positive Affine Cost
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed general consequence of positive-affine objective correspondence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(\pi(Y)=A\) and \(g(y)=\alpha+\beta f(\pi(y))\) for every \(y\in Y\), with \(\beta>0\). If \(g(y)\le\operatorname{OPT}_g+\varepsilon\), then \(f(\pi(y))\le\operatorname{OPT}_f+\varepsilon/\beta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A target additive error of epsilon becomes a source additive error of epsilon divided by the positive cost scale.
assumptions_latex: \pi(Y)=A.
g(y)=\alpha+\beta f(\pi(y))\text{ pointwise}.
\beta>0.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: g(y)-\operatorname{OPT}_g\le\varepsilon\Rightarrow f(\pi(y))-\operatorname{OPT}_f\le\varepsilon/\beta.
knowledge_statements.title: Additive-Approximation Transfer under Positive Affine Cost

intermediate_metadata.reason: The locally owned inventory covers feasible-set projection failures, target-model multiplicity, pointwise-cost consequences, threshold transfer, priority scalarization, optimizer-only weakness, and succinctness. The additive-approximation claim is sound but deferred as general reduction theory, consistently with the previously deferred composition theorem. The pair-specific unified definition and a two-target checklist remain missing, so expansion is required. Concrete WCSP and answer-set encodings were excluded as sibling scopes.
