knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arithmetic-operation cost from a fixed partial assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an explicitly stored normalized inequality with \(n\) terms, computing the attainable maximum \(U\), testing \(U-b<0\), and scanning unassigned coefficients for \(a_i>U-b\) takes \(O(n)\) arithmetic operations. Enqueuing a forced true literal does not alter \(U\), since its coefficient was already included. Incrementally falsifying \(\ell_i\) updates \(U\leftarrow U-a_i\) in \(O(1)\) arithmetic operations; locating newly critical coefficients has the additional cost of the chosen watched or ordered structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full slack scan is linear in the number of terms, while falsifying one literal updates the attainable maximum with one subtraction.
assumptions_latex: \text{Arithmetic operations are counted at unit cost.}
\text{The inequality is explicitly stored with }n\text{ terms.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_{\mathrm{scan}}(n)=O(n),\qquad T_{\mathrm{activity\ update}}=O(1)\text{ per falsified literal}.
review_flags: Bit complexity also depends on coefficient encoding length; watched-location costs belong to the watched-incremental sibling.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Time Single-Constraint Slack Scan

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Propagation completeness for one normalized monotone PB lower-bound inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(C:\sum_i a_i\ell_i\ge b\), where \(a_i\ge0\) and the literals use distinct underlying Boolean variables, let \(U\) be the maximum attainable left-hand side under a partial assignment and \(s=U-b\). Then \(s<0\) exactly when the partial assignment has no extension satisfying \(C\). If \(s\ge0\), an unassigned literal \(\ell_k\) is true in every extension satisfying \(C\) exactly when \(a_k>s\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For one normalized monotone PB inequality, negative slack exactly identifies conflict and coefficient excess exactly identifies a forced true literal.
assumptions_latex: a_i\ge0\text{ for every }i.
\text{Each underlying variable occurs in at most one literal.}
\text{All variables are Boolean.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: s<0\iff\text{no satisfying extension of }C;\qquad s\ge0\Rightarrow(\ell_k\text{ is forced by }C\iff a_k>s).
review_flags: Exactness is for this single inequality; other active constraints may force additional literals.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Forced-Literal Characterization by Slack
Slack-Based Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact propagation for a normalized pseudo-Boolean lower-bound constraint under a partial assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\sum_{i=1}^n a_i\ell_i\ge b\), where \(a_i\ge0\) and each \(\ell_i\) is Boolean. Under a partial assignment, initialize the attainable upper sum
\[U=\sum_{\ell_i\text{ true}}a_i+\sum_{\ell_i\text{ unassigned}}a_i\]
and slack \(s=U-b\). If \(s<0\), report conflict. Otherwise, for every unassigned \(\ell_k\) with \(a_k>s\), enqueue \(\ell_k=1\), because assigning it false would leave \(U-a_k<b\). After each assignment, update \(U\) and repeat until no new literal is enqueued. The output is either a conflict or the propagation fixpoint of this single inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maintain the maximum still-attainable sum: negative slack is conflict, while any unassigned literal whose coefficient exceeds slack must become true.
assumptions_latex: The inequality is normalized with \(a_i\ge0\).
Every \(\ell_i\) has value true, false, or unassigned.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s<0\Rightarrow\bot\), and \(a_k>s\Rightarrow\ell_k=1\) for every unassigned \(\ell_k\).

notation.meaning: Maximum left-hand side attainable by extending the partial assignment.
A Boolean literal occurring in the inequality.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The normalized nonnegative-coefficient slack tests are mathematically consistent and the algorithm content kind fits the leaf. No authoritative pseudo-Boolean propagation source or inspectable locator is supplied.

children.title: Watched PB Propagation
children.top_down_role: Watched-data structures for pseudo-Boolean propagation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Watch-safety certificate, replacement, and exact fallback for a normalized PB inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P:\sum_i a_i\ell_i\ge b\), let \(N\) be the nonfalse literals and maintain \(W\subseteq N\). The sufficient safety invariant \(\sum_{i\in W}a_i\ge b+\max_{i\in N}a_i\) implies that \(P\) is neither conflicting nor propagating. When a watched literal becomes false, add nonwatched members of \(N\) until safety is restored. If restoration fails, compute \(U=\sum_{i\in N}a_i\), report conflict when \(U<b\), and force each unassigned \(\ell_k\) with \(U-a_k<b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted watches suppress exact scans while a sufficient coefficient-sum certificate holds; failed repair triggers exact conflict and forcing tests.
assumptions_latex: a_i\ge0
\text{Every watched-literal falsification triggers repair or dirty processing.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_{i\in W}a_i\ge b+\max_{i\in N}a_i\Rightarrow\text{no conflict and no forced unassigned literal}.

notation.meaning: Indices of true or unassigned literals

review_flags: The invariant is sufficient, not asserted necessary.
knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Watched PB Propagation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weighted Watch Repair and Fallback Cost
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case local work without stronger amortization assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a constraint with \(m\) stored terms, a replacement search or exact fallback scan costs \(O(m)\) coefficient inspections in the worst case. Across \(q\) triggering events the unconditional bound is \(O(qm)\); monotone scan cursors can improve branch-local replacement scanning, but backtracking and watch restoration require separate accounting.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weighted watch repair or fallback scan is linear in constraint length in the worst case.
assumptions_latex: \text{Terms are explicitly stored.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_{\mathrm{event}}=O(m),\qquad T_q=O(qm)\text{ without additional amortization invariants}.

notation.meaning: Number of stored terms in the constraint

knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Watch Repair and Fallback Cost

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Two Arbitrary Watches Do Not Ensure Weighted PB Safety
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating ordinary clause watching from weighted PB watching.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P:2x+y+z\ge3\) with all literals unassigned, two nonfalse watched literals exist, but \(x\) is already forced because the exact attainable sum is \(U=4\) and \(U-2=2<3\). Thus merely counting two nonfalse watches does not certify absence of weighted PB propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unlike a clause, a weighted PB constraint may propagate even while two watched literals remain nonfalse.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Two nonfalse literals alone are not a valid weighted watch certificate.}
knowledge_statements.title: Two Arbitrary Watches Do Not Ensure Weighted PB Safety

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Two-Watched-Literal Propagation Is the Clausal Special Case
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unit-coefficient specialization of weighted watch safety.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent \(\ell_1\lor\cdots\lor\ell_m\) by \(\sum_i\ell_i\ge1\). Two nonfalse watched literals have total weight \(2=b+\max_i a_i\), so they certify that the clause is neither conflicting nor unit. Failure to find a replacement leaves exact inspection to report conflict or unit propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a clause, weighted coefficient watching reduces to the ordinary two-watched-literal rule.
assumptions_latex: a_i=1
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Two nonfalse watches certify clause safety.}
knowledge_statements.title: Two-Watched-Literal Propagation Is the Clausal Special Case
Watched PB Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Watch-based filtering with exact slack evaluation when the watch safety invariant fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(P:\sum_i a_i\ell_i\ge b\), let \(N\) contain the currently nonfalse literals and maintain \(W\subseteq N\). A sufficient watch-safety invariant is
\[\sum_{i\in W}a_i\ge b+\max_{i\in N}a_i.\]
When a watched literal becomes false, scan nonwatched members of \(N\) and add replacements until the invariant is restored. While it holds, neither conflict nor propagation is possible for \(P\). If restoration fails, compute \(U=\sum_{i\in N}a_i\) exactly: report conflict when \(U<b\), and enqueue every unassigned \(\ell_k\) satisfying \(U-a_k<b\). Continue until the trail and all affected watch sets reach a fixpoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Watched coefficients suppress unnecessary scans; failure of the safety invariant triggers an exact slack scan for conflicts and forced literals.
assumptions_latex: Watch updates are triggered whenever a watched literal becomes false.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm reports only valid conflicts and enqueues exactly the literals found by the exact test \(U-a_k<b\) whenever scanning occurs.

notation.meaning: Indices of literals that are true or unassigned.
Currently watched subset of nonfalse literals.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed watch-safety invariant is sufficient for suppressing conflict and propagation scans, and the record fits an algorithm leaf, but this particular invariant and maintenance procedure require an authoritative watched pseudo-Boolean propagation citation.

children.title: Incremental PB Propagation
children.top_down_role: Propagation maintenance across evolving pseudo-Boolean states.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact attainable-sum maintenance across assignments and chronological backtracking.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P:\sum_i a_i\ell_i\ge b\), maintain \(U_P=\sum_{\ell_i\text{ true or unassigned}}a_i\). When a trail event makes \(\ell_k\) false, decrement \(U_P\) by \(a_k\) in every affected occurrence and record the decrement for undo; a true assignment causes no decrement. Chronological backtracking restores every recorded decrement. Report conflict when \(U_P<b\), and force each unassigned \(\ell_k\) with \(U_P-a_k<b\). Processing newly affected constraints to quiescence yields the same propagation fixpoint as full recomputation from the current trail.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maintain attainable sums occurrence by occurrence, undo them on backtracking, and use the exact conflict and forcing tests.
assumptions_latex: a_i\ge0
\text{Every forward and undo event is applied exactly once to every affected occurrence.}
\text{Affected constraints are processed to quiescence.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: U_P=\sum_{\ell_i\text{ true or unassigned}}a_i\text{ at every trail state, and incremental propagation equals full recomputation.}

notation.meaning: Maximum attainable left-hand side for constraint P

knowledge_statements.title: Trail-Based Incremental PB Propagation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward and undo cost excluding separately triggered exact rescans.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\operatorname{occ}(\ell)\) is the number of stored PB occurrences of literal \(\ell\), a forward falsification or its undo costs \(O(\operatorname{occ}(\ell))\) arithmetic updates. Across trail events \(T\), update work is \(O(\sum_{e\in T}\operatorname{occ}(\ell_e))\). Exact rescans add the lengths of the constraints scanned; arbitrary-precision implementations additionally pay the bit cost of coefficient-sized additions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Incremental state updates cost time proportional to affected literal occurrences, plus any explicitly triggered exact scans.
assumptions_latex: \text{Occurrence lists identify affected constraints directly.}
\text{Each occurrence is updated exactly once per event.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_{\mathrm{updates}}=O\!\left(\sum_{e\in T}\operatorname{occ}(\ell_e)\right).

notation.meaning: Stored occurrence count of literal ℓ

knowledge_statements.title: Occurrence-Proportional Trail Update Cost

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Missed Update or Undo Corrupts Incremental Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal correctness boundary for occurrence-complete trail maintenance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P:x+y\ge1\), start with \(U_P=2\). If assigning \(x=0\) fails to decrement \(U_P\), the maintained value remains \(2\) and misses the forced assignment \(y=1\). Conversely, after correctly decrementing to \(1\), backtracking without restoring the decrement leaves \(U_P=1\) although both literals are again unassigned, so later propagation uses a false state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Omitting either a forward occurrence update or its undo can miss propagation or create spurious deductions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Occurrence-complete forward updates and undo are necessary for the maintained invariant.}
knowledge_statements.title: Missed Update or Undo Corrupts Incremental Propagation
Incremental PB Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trail-based maintenance of pseudo-Boolean slack without recomputing each constraint from scratch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each constraint \(P:\sum_i a_i\ell_i\ge b\), initialize \(U_P=\sum_i a_i\). Whenever the trail makes an unassigned literal \(\ell_k\) false, set \(U_P\leftarrow U_P-a_k\) for every occurrence in an affected constraint; a true assignment leaves \(U_P\) unchanged. Record each decrement with its decision level and undo it on backtracking. After an update, report conflict if \(U_P<b\); otherwise enqueue each unassigned \(\ell_k\) for which \(U_P-a_k<b\). Processing affected constraints until no enqueue occurs produces the same fixpoint as recomputing attainable sums from the current trail.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Update each attainable sum only when a literal becomes false, undo updates on backtracking, and apply the ordinary conflict and forcing tests.
assumptions_latex: All constraints have normalized form \(\sum_i a_i\ell_i\ge b\) with \(a_i\ge0\).
Every trail update and undo is applied once to each affected occurrence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At every trail state, \(U_P=\sum_{\ell_i\text{ true or unassigned}}a_i\), so incremental and full-scan propagation agree.

notation.meaning: Maximum left-hand side attainable for constraint \(P\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The trail-based attainable-sum invariant and undo rule are coherent and correctly presented as an algorithm, but the equivalence with full recomputation lacks an authoritative source with a precise locator.

children.title: Watch-Maintenance Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes for maintaining watched pseudo-Boolean constraints incrementally.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Implementation-independent comparison of eager, coalesced lazy, and hybrid scheduling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(r_P\) is the cost of repairing or exactly checking constraint \(P\), eager scheduling can pay \(r_P\) after every invalidating event. A coalescing lazy queue pays at most one such cost per dirty interval before \(P\) is processed, while hybrid scheduling lies between these event choices. No unconditional asymptotic dominance follows without bounds on invalidation frequency, repair success, and queue coalescing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lazy scheduling can coalesce several invalidations into one repair, but no regime universally dominates without workload assumptions.
assumptions_latex: \text{A dirty flag coalesces repeated enqueues for the same constraint.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: W_{\mathrm{eager}}\le\sum_P e_Pr_P,\qquad W_{\mathrm{lazy}}\le\sum_P d_Pr_P,\quad d_P\le e_P.

notation.meaning: Number of invalidating events for P
Number of processed dirty intervals for P

knowledge_statements.title: Maintenance-Regime Work Accounting

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sound Eager, Lazy, and Hybrid Watch Maintenance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regime definitions and sufficient conditions for exact PB propagation fixpoints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Eager maintenance repairs or checks a watch certificate immediately after each invalidating event; lazy maintenance marks the constraint dirty and repairs or checks it when dequeued; hybrid maintenance may do either per event. All three yield the exact propagation fixpoint provided that certificate validity implies absence of conflict and forcing, every potentially invalidating event either triggers processing or marks the constraint dirty, every dirty constraint is processed before quiescence, and processing restores a valid certificate or performs the exact conflict and forcing tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eager, lazy, and hybrid repair schedules are fixpoint-equivalent when invalidations are never lost, dirty work is processed fairly, and fallback checks are exact.
assumptions_latex: \text{The watch certificate is sound.}
\text{Dirty processing is fair within each propagation phase.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Fixpoint}_{\mathrm{eager}}=\operatorname{Fixpoint}_{\mathrm{lazy}}=\operatorname{Fixpoint}_{\mathrm{hybrid}}=\operatorname{Fixpoint}_{\mathrm{exact}}.
review_flags: The theorem concerns propagation results, not equality of work or processing order.
knowledge_statements.title: Sound Eager, Lazy, and Hybrid Watch Maintenance

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Missed Dirty Marking Makes Lazy Maintenance Unsound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal failure witness for lost certificate invalidation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P:x+y\ge1\), suppose a lazy regime initially regards \(P\) as safe. If \(x=0\) and \(y=0\) invalidate that state but neither event marks \(P\) dirty, the queue may terminate without processing \(P\), although its exact attainable sum is \(0<1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lazy regime that loses invalidation events can terminate while overlooking an immediate conflict.
assumptions_latex: \text{Only dirty constraints are processed before quiescence.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Fixpoint}_{\mathrm{lazy}}\ne\operatorname{Fixpoint}_{\mathrm{exact}}\text{ may result.}
knowledge_statements.title: Missed Dirty Marking Makes Lazy Maintenance Unsound
Watch-Maintenance Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Soundness boundary shared by eager, lazy, and hybrid pseudo-Boolean watch maintenance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Associate each pseudo-Boolean constraint \(P\) with a watch certificate \(I_P\) whose validity implies that \(P\) is neither conflicting nor propagating. A watch-maintenance regime may repair \(I_P\) eagerly after each falsification, lazily when \(P\) is dequeued, or by any hybrid schedule. It is propagation-sound and fixpoint-complete provided that: every event capable of invalidating \(I_P\) marks \(P\) dirty; every dirty \(P\) is processed before termination of propagation; and processing either restores a valid certificate or performs the exact tests \(U_P<b\) and \(U_P-a_k<b\). The timing of repairs may change work performed, but not the resulting propagation fixpoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eager and lazy watch repair are equivalent when every invalidation is recorded and every dirty constraint receives exact checking before propagation terminates.
assumptions_latex: A valid \(I_P\) implies absence of conflict and forced literals for \(P\).
Dirty constraints are processed fairly within each propagation phase.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Fixpoint}_{\mathrm{watched}}=\operatorname{Fixpoint}_{\mathrm{exact}}\).

notation.meaning: Coefficient of an unassigned candidate literal.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The dirty-marking, fairness, and exact-check conditions form a plausible soundness boundary and fit the condition container. The claimed eager/lazy/hybrid fixpoint equivalence is nontrivial and has no supporting citation.

children.title: PB Branching Regimes
children.top_down_role: Decision-selection regimes for pseudo-Boolean search.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coverage and fairness conditions separating heuristic selection from exhaustive search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a nonterminal state, branch on an unassigned Boolean variable \(x\) using children \(x=0\) and \(x=1\). Their completion sets are disjoint and cover the parent's completion set. Thus variable-selection and polarity-order heuristics preserve exhaustive coverage provided every unpruned child is eventually processed. Coverage or progress fails if one value is omitted, an already assigned variable is repeatedly selected without state reduction, or an unpruned child is postponed forever.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branching heuristics preserve completeness only when both Boolean values cover the parent and every surviving child is eventually explored.
assumptions_latex: \text{Variables are Boolean.}
\text{Pruning is sound.}
\text{Every unpruned child is eventually processed.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Comp}(S)=\operatorname{Comp}(S\land x=0)\;\dot\cup\;\operatorname{Comp}(S\land x=1).

notation.meaning: Satisfying total extensions of search state S.

review_flags: This is a branching-local condition; restart-induced fairness is owned by the restart and interaction leaves.
knowledge_statements.title: Completeness Boundary for PB Branching
PB Branching Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: State-dependent variable and polarity selection for pseudo-Boolean conflict-driven search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let a pseudo-Boolean search state be \(S=(F,\tau,D)\), where \(F\) is the active constraint database, \(\tau\) the propagation-closed trail, and \(D\) auxiliary statistics. A branching regime is a map
\[B(S)=(x,p),\]
where \(x\) is unassigned on \(\tau\) and \(p\in\{0,1\}\) is the chosen polarity. Applying the branch appends the decision \(x=p\) at a new decision level and invokes pseudo-Boolean propagation. Static order, activity-based order, coefficient/slack scores, and phase saving are instances obtained by changing the map \(B\). A regime is total when \(B(S)\) is defined for every nonterminal propagation-closed state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A PB branching regime maps each nonterminal propagated state to an unassigned variable and a polarity, then starts a new decision level.
assumptions_latex: The trail \(\tau\) is consistent and closed under the selected propagation procedure.
A state is terminal when it is conflicting or assigns every variable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B:S\mapsto(x,p)\) with \(x\notin\operatorname{dom}(\tau)\) and \(p\in\{0,1\}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The state-to-variable-and-polarity map is an appropriate definition for the branching-regime leaf, with explicit domains and terminal-state qualifications. An authoritative PB search source with a specific locator is still required.

children.title: PB Restart Regimes
children.top_down_role: Restart policies used during pseudo-Boolean solving.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fixed, Geometric, and Luby Restart Schedules
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical conflict-budget sequences for restart epochs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(c\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), a fixed schedule uses \(r_k=c\), while a geometric schedule uses \(r_k=\lceil c\gamma^{k-1}\rceil\) with \(\gamma>1\). A scaled Luby schedule uses \(r_k=cu_k\), where \(u_{2^m-1}=2^{m-1}\) and, for \(2^{m-1}\le k<2^m-1\), \(u_k=u_{k-2^{m-1}+1}\). Hence \((u_k)=(1,1,2,1,1,2,4,\ldots)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Standard restart schedules use constant, geometrically growing, or recursively universal epoch budgets.
assumptions_latex: c\in\mathbb Z_{>0}.
\gamma>1\text{ for the geometric schedule.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r_k\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\text{ for every }k.

notation.meaning: Conflict budget of restart epoch k.

review_flags: No policy-independent runtime dominance for PB solving is asserted.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed, Geometric, and Luby Restart Schedules

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions separating semantic preservation from complete restarted search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Restarting to decision level zero preserves the feasible set when retained learned constraints are valid consequences. Termination and completeness additionally require progress or fairness: every unrefuted finite decision prefix must eventually be extended far enough to find a model or derive a refutation. A regime that repeatedly restarts before such progress and reproduces the same decisions without a blocking consequence may loop forever even on a finite instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restarts may preserve all solutions while an unfair schedule repeatedly revisits the same prefix and prevents termination.
assumptions_latex: \text{All retained learned constraints are entailed by the original instance.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{semantic preservation}\not\Rightarrow\text{termination};\qquad\text{fair progress is required for complete restarted search}.
knowledge_statements.title: Fairness Boundary for Restart Completeness
PB Restart Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conflict-budgeted restart control for pseudo-Boolean conflict-driven search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose a sequence of positive conflict budgets \((r_k)_{k\ge1}\). In restart epoch \(k\), run pseudo-Boolean propagation, branching, conflict analysis, and learning until a solution or root conflict is found, or until \(r_k\) new conflicts have occurred. On budget exhaustion, cancel every trail assignment above decision level zero, retain the original constraints and all retained learned constraints, update search statistics according to the chosen policy, increment \(k\), and resume propagation. A restart changes neither the feasible set nor the validity of learned constraints; it changes only the subsequent traversal order and retained heuristic state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After a scheduled number of conflicts, backtrack to level zero while retaining sound learned constraints and then resume search with updated heuristic state.
assumptions_latex: Every learned pseudo-Boolean constraint is entailed by the original instance.
Each restart budget \(r_k\) is a positive integer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Sol}(F\cup L)=\operatorname{Sol}(F)\) before and after every restart.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conflict-budgeted restart procedure is appropriately classified as an algorithm, and solution preservation follows under the stated entailment assumption. No authoritative pseudo-Boolean restart source or precise locator is supplied.

children.title: PB Database-Management Regimes
children.top_down_role: Retention, deletion, and prioritization regimes for learned constraints.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Semantic and Proof Boundaries of Constraint Deletion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Model-preserving learned-constraint deletion and its operational boundaries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the retained original PB database and suppose \(F\models C\) for every \(C\in L\). Then for every \(L'\subseteq L\), \(F\land L'\equiv F\); deleting learned consequences may weaken propagation but cannot change the feasible set. Deleting a retained constraint not entailed by the remaining database can enlarge that set. Separately, semantically safe deletion may invalidate a proof trace when its proof format or later derivations require the deleted object.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deleting entailed learned constraints preserves solutions but may weaken propagation; nonredundant deletion is unsound, and proof logging imposes a separate dependency condition.
assumptions_latex: F\models C\text{ for every }C\in L.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L'\subseteq L\Rightarrow\operatorname{Sol}(F\land L')=\operatorname{Sol}(F).

notation.meaning: Database of consequences entailed by F.

review_flags: Proof-trace safety depends on the particular proof system and deletion rules.
knowledge_statements.title: Semantic and Proof Boundaries of Constraint Deletion
PB Database-Management Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound retention and deletion policies for learned pseudo-Boolean constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain an immutable original database \(F\) and a learned database \(L\) of constraints entailed by \(F\). At each reduction event, mark as protected every learned constraint currently serving as a trail reason and any constraint required by the solver's proof-logging discipline. Rank the remaining constraints by a policy using quantities such as activity, size, age, or coefficient complexity, and delete any selected subset. Add newly derived constraints to \(L\), update their ranks after use, and reconsider protected constraints only after they cease to be reasons. Because deletion removes only consequences of \(F\), it preserves the feasible set, although it may weaken subsequent propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Keep original and currently indispensable learned constraints; rank and delete other entailed constraints, preserving solutions while trading memory against propagation strength.
assumptions_latex: Every member of \(L\) is logically entailed by \(F\).
Constraints needed as active reasons or proof dependencies remain protected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Sol}(F\cup L')=\operatorname{Sol}(F)\) for every retained subset \(L'\subseteq L\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The learned-constraint retention and deletion procedure fits the database-management algorithm leaf, and feasible-set preservation is correctly conditioned on entailment. Its operational protection requirements and PB-specific management policy lack an authoritative cited source.

children.title: Search-Control Interaction
children.top_down_role: Interactions among branching, restart, and database policies.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correct feasible-set invariant for composed branching, restart, and database actions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the original PB formula and \(L\) a retained learned database with \(F\models C\) for every \(C\in L\). Branching restricts only the current search region; backtracking or restarting removes trail restrictions; adding or deleting members of \(L\) leaves \(F\land L\equiv F\). Consequently these controls may alter traversal, propagation, and heuristic state, but the persistent database never admits or excludes a model of \(F\). Individual learned constraints need not be equivalent to \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Soundly composed search controls change the explored state but not the models of the original formula; learned consequences need not individually equal the formula.
assumptions_latex: F\models C\text{ for every retained learned constraint }C.
\text{Branching children cover the parent region when exhaustive search is required.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\land L\equiv F.
review_flags: Corrects the deferred seed's overstated conclusion that each learned constraint has the same feasible assignments as F.
knowledge_statements.title: Semantic Invariant Under Search-Control Composition

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Noncommutativity of Restart and Database Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trail-dependent interaction between restart and learned-constraint protection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\) clear all assignments above decision level zero, and let \(D\) delete low-ranked learned constraints except active trail reasons. If an entailed low-ranked constraint \(C\) is locked as a reason before restart, then applying \(D\) before \(R\) retains \(C\), whereas applying \(R\) before \(D\) may remove its lock and permit deletion. Hence \(R\circ D\ne D\circ R\) for some solver states, although both orders preserve the models of \(F\). The resulting databases may induce different later propagation and branching scores.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restart and database reduction need not commute because restart can unlock a learned reason before deletion.
assumptions_latex: C\text{ is an entailed learned constraint.}
D\text{ protects active reasons and may delete unlocked low-ranked constraints.}
R\text{ removes the assignment for which }C\text{ is a reason.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R(D(S))\ne D(R(S))\text{ for some valid states }S.

notation.meaning: A low-ranked learned constraint initially locked as a reason.

knowledge_statements.title: Noncommutativity of Restart and Database Reduction

assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite set of pseudo-Boolean constraints over Boolean variables.
Propagation, decisions, conflicts, learning, backjumping, restarts, and constraint deletion preserve all models of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\) and every constraint learned by the procedure have the same feasible assignments before and after each search-control action.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic invariant coupling PB propagation, learning, and search control.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a finite pseudo-Boolean constraint set and let \(\alpha\) be the current partial assignment. Search control may choose a decision literal, restart, backjump, or delete learned constraints. Propagation extends \(\alpha\) only by literals logically implied by the active constraints; conflict analysis adds only constraints entailed by \(F\); backjumping and restarting remove assignments but not constraints; deletion removes only redundant learned constraints. Consequently, search control changes the explored search tree without introducing a feasible assignment outside \(F\) or excluding any model of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sound propagation and learning let branching, restarts, backjumping, and learned-constraint deletion alter the search tree without changing the original feasible set.
knowledge_statements.title: Search-Control Interaction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No citation or inspectable locator supports this solver-level invariant. The conclusion incorrectly suggests that each learned constraint has the same feasible assignments as F; an entailed learned constraint need only contain all models of F, while the conjunction of F with learned constraints remains equivalent to F.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Clausal Explanations for a PB Lower-Bound Constraint
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient coefficient tests for lazy conflict and propagation clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C:\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_i\ell_i\ge b\), where \(a_i\ge0\), the literals have distinct underlying variables, and \(A=\sum_i a_i\). For an index set \(T\), \[A-\sum_{i\in T}a_i<b\ \Longrightarrow\ C\models\bigvee_{i\in T}\ell_i.\] For \(q\notin T\), \[A-a_q-\sum_{i\in T}a_i<b\ \Longrightarrow\ C\models\ell_q\lor\bigvee_{i\in T}\ell_i.\] If all literals indexed by \(T\) are currently false, the first clause explains conflict and the second is unit and forces \(\ell_q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A maximum-activity deficit yields an entailed conflict clause or unit propagation explanation.
assumptions_latex: a_i\ge0\text{ for every }i.
\text{Underlying variables are pairwise distinct.}
T\text{ indexes currently false literals when used operationally.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A-\sum_{i\in T}a_i<b\Rightarrow C\models\bigvee_{i\in T}\ell_i;\quad A-a_q-\sum_{i\in T}a_i<b\Rightarrow C\models\ell_q\lor\bigvee_{i\in T}\ell_i.

notation.meaning: Indices selected for the explanatory clause.

review_flags: This validates one explanation family but does not identify a canonical lazy-translation algorithm or explanation-selection policy.
knowledge_statements.title: Clausal Explanations for a PB Lower-Bound Constraint

assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a pseudo-Boolean constraint over finitely many Boolean literals.
The explanation oracle returns only clauses logically entailed by \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every generated clause \(E\) satisfies \(C\models E\), so adding \(E\) preserves the models of the active pseudo-Boolean formula.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: On-demand clause generation while retaining the native PB constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a native pseudo-Boolean constraint \(C\) and a partial assignment \(\alpha\). Keep \(C\) unexpanded. Whenever propagation on \(C\) detects a conflict or forces a literal \(q\), invoke an explanation oracle. In the conflict case it returns a clause \(E\) with \(C\models E\) that is falsified by \(\alpha\); in the propagation case it returns \(E\) with \(C\models E\), with \(q\in E\), and with every other literal of \(E\) false under \(\alpha\). Add \(E\) to the clausal database and apply ordinary clausal propagation or conflict analysis. Terminate with the SAT, UNSAT, or optimization result produced by the combined search.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retain each PB constraint natively and generate an entailed conflict or propagation clause only when the current assignment requires one.
knowledge_statements.title: Lazy Clausal Translation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits this procedural leaf, and the stated entailment conditions are coherent, but no source identifies or supports this particular lazy clausal translation procedure, explanation policy, or termination/result claim.

assumptions_latex: Each reason and conflict is represented as a clause inequality over Boolean literals.
Complementary occurrences of a pivot variable are available at each resolution step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The final learned inequality is entailed by the reason and conflict inequalities used in its derivation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clausal resolution embedded in pseudo-Boolean conflict analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent clauses as inequalities. Given reason inequalities \(x+A\ge 1\) and \((1-x)+B\ge 1\), eliminate the pivot \(x\) and derive the resolvent inequality \(A+B\ge 1\), followed by duplicate-literal normalization to its clausal form. Starting from the conflicting inequality, repeatedly resolve the most recently assigned eligible literal against its reason. Stop when the selected assertiveness criterion is met, and output the resulting inequality \(L\). Each resolution step is logically sound; hence the conjunction of the inequalities used during analysis entails \(L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Resolve complementary pivot literals in clausal PB inequalities, normalize duplicates, and repeat until the chosen learned-constraint stopping criterion is reached.
knowledge_statements.title: Resolution-Style PB Learning

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits conflict learning, but the record describes ordinary clausal resolution embedded in PB notation rather than a clearly sourced resolution-style PB learning regime. A source must establish the intended variant, normalization rule, and stopping criterion.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Builder-proposed rule deferred because it duplicates the cutting-planes cancellation rule rather than identifying the intended resolution-style PB variant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: From \(a x+A\ge r\) and \(b(1-x)+B\ge s\), the proposed rule aligns coefficients and eliminates the pivot by a cutting-planes combination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proposed generalized resolvent is sound arithmetic, but its canonical home is Cutting-Planes Conflict Learning unless a narrower resolution-style calculus is specified.
assumptions_latex: \(a,b>0\) and \(x\) is Boolean.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Local publication is deferred pending a distinct resolution-style rule and normalization convention.}
knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient-Aligned Generalized PB Resolution

intermediate_metadata.reason: The builder's accepted-looking records duplicate the cutting-planes sibling and therefore fail the canonical-home test. The immutable seed instead describes only clausal resolution embedded in PB notation. Until the intended distinct calculus is fixed, the topic and its essential claims are deferred.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local verification criterion for learned PB consequences and contradictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A finite derivation whose initial rows are active PB constraints and whose later rows follow from declared sound scaling, addition, complementary-pivot cancellation, or division rules certifies its final row as an entailed inequality; a final row \(0\ge c\) with \(c>0\) certifies infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proof log of locally checkable cutting-planes steps certifies every learned row and certifies infeasibility when it ends in contradiction.
assumptions_latex: Every step names its premises and arithmetic parameters.
Arithmetic is exact and every normalization rule used is sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigwedge_{C\in\mathcal C}C\Rightarrow L;\quad L\equiv(0\ge c),\ c>0\Rightarrow\mathcal C\text{ is infeasible}.

notation.meaning: initial PB rows used by the derivation

knowledge_statements.title: Checkable Cutting-Planes Derivation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coefficient Flooring Is Not a General Division Rule
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of independent downward rounding during PB division.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Dividing \(x+y\ge1\) by two and independently flooring its coefficients while rounding the threshold upward produces \(0x+0y\ge1\), which is not entailed by the satisfiable premise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Downward coefficient rounding can turn a satisfiable PB inequality into contradiction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x+y\ge1\not\Rightarrow\lfloor1/2\rfloor x+\lfloor1/2\rfloor y\ge\lceil1/2\rceil.
knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient Flooring Is Not a General Division Rule

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound elimination of one Boolean pivot after exact coefficient alignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: From \(a x+A\ge r\) and \(b(1-x)+B\ge s\), with \(a,b>0\) and \(g=\gcd(a,b)\), infer \(\frac bgA+\frac agB\ge\frac bg r+\frac ag s-\frac{ab}{g}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scale two PB inequalities to equal complementary pivot coefficients, add them, and remove the resulting constant pivot contribution.
assumptions_latex: \(a,b\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\).
\(A,B\) are integer linear forms not containing the displayed pivot.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (a x+A\ge r)\wedge(b(1-x)+B\ge s)\Rightarrow\frac bgA+\frac agB\ge\frac bg r+\frac ag s-\frac{ab}{g}.

notation.meaning: greatest common divisor of the pivot coefficients

knowledge_statements.title: Complementary-Pivot Cutting-Planes Cancellation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound positive-integer division of a nonnegative PB inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), \(\sum_i a_i l_i\ge q\) entails \(\sum_i\lceil a_i/d\rceil l_i\ge\lceil q/d\rceil\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Divide a nonnegative PB inequality by a positive integer and round every retained coefficient and the threshold upward.
assumptions_latex: \(a_i,q\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\).
\(d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_i a_i l_i\ge q\Rightarrow\sum_i\lceil a_i/d\rceil l_i\ge\lceil q/d\rceil.
knowledge_statements.title: Cutting-Planes Division Rule

assumptions_latex: All active constraints are valid integer inequalities over Boolean literals.
Inference multipliers are nonnegative integers, and rounding rules used after combination are sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The learned constraint \(L\) is satisfied by every Boolean assignment satisfying the constraints used to derive it.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conflict learning by sound cutting-planes elimination steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(D\) to a pseudo-Boolean inequality violated by the current assignment. Select an assigned pivot literal and its reason inequality \(R\). Multiply \(D\) and \(R\) by nonnegative integers so that complementary pivot coefficients can be canceled, add the scaled inequalities, eliminate the pivot, and apply only sound weakening, saturation, or division-rounding normalization. Repeat while the chosen stopping condition is false. Output the normalized inequality \(L=D\). Because scaling, addition, cancellation using Boolean complementarity, and the admitted normalization rules preserve logical consequence, every assignment satisfying the constraints used in the derivation satisfies \(L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Combine the conflict with reason inequalities, cancel pivots, normalize soundly, and learn the resulting entailed pseudo-Boolean constraint.
knowledge_statements.title: Cutting-Planes Conflict Learning

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf, but the admitted weakening, saturation, division-rounding, and complement-cancellation operations are not stated precisely enough to verify soundness as one algorithmic regime, and no supporting locator is supplied.

children.title: PB Assertiveness Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes classified by the propagation effect of learned PB constraints.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational assertiveness of one normalized nonnegative PB inequality at a retained trail level.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(L:\sum_i a_i l_i\ge q\), let \(M(\alpha)=\sum_{l_i\text{ true in }\alpha}a_i+\sum_{l_i\text{ unassigned in }\alpha}a_i\) and \(s(\alpha)=M(\alpha)-q\). At a nonconflicting partial assignment \(\alpha\), meaning \(s(\alpha)\ge0\), \(L\) is assertive exactly when some unassigned \(l_j\) satisfies \(a_j>s(\alpha)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonviolated PB inequality is assertive when at least one unassigned literal has a coefficient larger than the remaining slack and is therefore forced true.
assumptions_latex: \(a_i,q\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\).
Each \(l_i\) is a normalized Boolean literal and \(\alpha\) is a partial assignment.
\(s(\alpha)\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L\text{ propagates an unassigned literal under }\alpha\Longleftrightarrow\exists j\;(l_j\text{ unassigned and }a_j>s(\alpha)).

notation.meaning: maximum attainable activity under the partial assignment

knowledge_statements.title: Slack Characterization of PB Assertiveness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between consistency and propagation at a retained trail level.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(L:x+y\ge1\) at the empty assignment, \(s=1\) and both coefficients equal \(1\); hence \(L\) is nonviolated but propagates neither literal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A PB constraint can remain consistent after backtracking without becoming assertive.
assumptions_latex: \(x,y\in\{0,1\}\) are unassigned.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: s\ge0\ \not\Rightarrow\ \exists j\;(a_j>s).
knowledge_statements.title: Nonviolation Does Not Imply Assertiveness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniqueness variant of propagation assertiveness for a normalized nonnegative PB inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(L:\sum_i a_i l_i\ge q\) at a nonconflicting retained assignment \(\alpha\), let \(s(\alpha)\) be the maximum-activity slack and \(F(\alpha)=\{j:l_j\text{ is unassigned and }a_j>s(\alpha)\}\). Ordinary propagation assertiveness means \(F(\alpha)\ne\varnothing\). A uniqueness-restricted regime accepts exactly when \(|F(\alpha)|=1\); a multiple-force state has \(|F(\alpha)|>1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ordinary assertiveness permits one or more forced literals, while a uniqueness-restricted regime requires exactly one.
assumptions_latex: \(a_i,q\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\).
\(s(\alpha)\ge0\).
Propagation uses the maximum-activity slack test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{uniqueness-restricted assertiveness}\Longleftrightarrow |F(\alpha)|=1.

notation.meaning: Set of literals forced true by the inequality at alpha.

knowledge_statements.title: Uniqueness-Restricted PB Assertiveness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pivot-sensitive assertiveness predicate independent of backjump selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a designated learned literal \(l_p\), a normalized PB inequality is pivot-assertive at retained assignment \(\alpha\) exactly when it is nonviolated, \(l_p\) is unassigned, and \(a_p>s(\alpha)\), equivalently \(p\in F(\alpha)\). Uniqueness is an additional condition and is not implied by pivot assertiveness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pivot-sensitive regime requires the designated pivot, rather than merely some literal, to be forced after trail truncation.
assumptions_latex: The inequality is normalized with nonnegative coefficients.
\(s(\alpha)\ge0\).
The pivot is designated by the chosen conflict calculus and is unassigned at \(\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L\text{ is pivot-assertive at }\alpha\Longleftrightarrow a_p>s(\alpha).
knowledge_statements.title: Designated-Pivot PB Assertiveness

assumptions_latex: \(L\) is a learned pseudo-Boolean constraint produced at conflict level \(d\).
\(\alpha_{\le b}\) retains exactly the assignments at decision levels at most \(b<d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The assertiveness regime accepts \(b\) exactly when propagation of \(L\) under \(\alpha_{\le b}\) forces at least one previously unassigned literal.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational assertiveness condition after truncating the assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a learned constraint \(L\) obtained at conflict level \(d\), an assertiveness regime specifies admissible levels \(b<d\). A level \(b\) is assertive for \(L\) when \(L\) is not violated by the restricted assignment \(\alpha_{\le b}\) and pseudo-Boolean propagation on \(L\) under \(\alpha_{\le b}\) forces at least one literal that is unassigned there. Different regimes may additionally require a unique forced literal or select a designated pivot literal, but every accepted regime must satisfy this propagation predicate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A learned PB constraint is assertive at a retained level when it is consistent there and immediately forces an unassigned literal.
knowledge_statements.title: PB Assertiveness Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits an assertiveness predicate, but the conclusion omits the statement's nonviolation requirement while claiming an exact characterization. The assertion that every regime must satisfy this particular propagation predicate also requires a source distinguishing the relevant PB assertiveness variants.

children.title: PB Backjumping Regimes
children.top_down_role: Nonchronological return regimes following pseudo-Boolean conflict analysis.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic nonchronological return rule parameterized by an explicitly declared assertiveness predicate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a conflict at level \(d\) and an entailed learned inequality \(L\), choose a declared admissible level \(b<d\) at which \(L\) is nonviolated and propagating under the retained trail \(\alpha_{\le b}\). Remove assignments above \(b\), retain \(L\), and resume propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Return to an earlier level where the learned PB inequality is consistent and immediately propagating, erase later assignments, and propagate it.
assumptions_latex: \(L\) is entailed by the active PB constraints.
The chosen \(b<d\) satisfies the declared assertiveness predicate.
Trail truncation removes only temporary assignments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Models}(F\wedge L)=\operatorname{Models}(F),\quad L\text{ propagates under }\alpha_{\le b}.
knowledge_statements.title: Assertion-Preserving PB Backjump

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Missing Assertive Level Requires a Declared Fallback
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Totality boundary for assertion-driven return-level selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A rule defined only as choosing a nonroot level at which \(L\) is assertive is partial when no such level exists; it must explicitly permit root return, chronological return, further conflict reduction, or another sound fallback.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An assertion-driven backjump regime is incomplete unless it specifies what happens when no eligible earlier level exists.
assumptions_latex: Candidate return levels are restricted by a declared assertiveness predicate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{b:0<b<d,\ L\text{ assertive at }b\}=\varnothing\Rightarrow\text{a fallback rule is required}.
knowledge_statements.title: Missing Assertive Level Requires a Declared Fallback

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic selection over a declared set of assertive return levels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B=\{b\in\{0,\ldots,d-1\}:L\text{ satisfies the declared assertiveness predicate under }\alpha_{\le b}\}\). If \(B\ne\varnothing\), choose \(b^*=\max B\), delete trail assignments above \(b^*\), retain \(L\), and propagate. If \(B=\varnothing\), invoke the regime's separately declared sound fallback.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Return to the greatest level satisfying the declared assertiveness predicate, with an explicit fallback when no such level exists.
assumptions_latex: \(L\) is entailed by the active PB constraint system.
The assertiveness predicate and empty-set fallback are fixed parts of the regime.
The trail has finite decision levels \(0,\ldots,d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: B\ne\varnothing\Longrightarrow b^*=\max B<d\text{ and }L\text{ is assertive under }\alpha_{\le b^*}.

notation.meaning: set of admissible assertive return levels

knowledge_statements.title: Greatest-Admissible Assertive Backjump

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Chronological return as a baseline PB backtracking regime following conflict analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After a conflict at decision level \(d>0\), chronological backtracking selects \(b=d-1\), deletes every trail assignment above \(b\), retains any globally entailed learned PB constraint \(L\), and resumes propagation or conflict processing. The retained \(L\) need not be assertive or nonviolated under \(\alpha_{\le b}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Chronological PB backtracking returns one decision level and does not guarantee that the learned inequality propagates or is consistent there.
assumptions_latex: The conflict occurs at decision level \(d>0\).
Any retained learned constraint is entailed by the active PB model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: b=d-1,\qquad \operatorname{Models}(F\wedge L)=\operatorname{Models}(F).
knowledge_statements.title: Chronological PB Backtrack Regime

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Chronological and Assertive Return Levels Can Differ
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation of chronological return from an assertiveness-driven return rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a conflict is analyzed at level \(d=2\), the retained level-one trail contains \(x=0\), and the learned entailed inequality is \(L:2x+y\ge2\). Chronological return selects \(b=1\), where the maximum attainable activity of \(L\) is \(1\), so \(L\) is violated. At level \(0\), both literals are unassigned, the slack is \(1\), and \(2>1\), so \(L\) forces \(x=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Chronological return can leave a learned PB inequality conflicting while a lower nonchronological return level makes it assertive.
assumptions_latex: \(L\) is entailed by the active model.
The learned constraint is installed after analysis of the level-two conflict.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L\text{ is violated under }\alpha_{\le1}\quad\text{and assertive under }\alpha_{\le0}.
knowledge_statements.title: Chronological and Assertive Return Levels Can Differ

assumptions_latex: A conflict occurs at decision level \(d>0\).
\(L\) is a learned constraint entailed by the active pseudo-Boolean formula.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Backjumping to any admissible \(b<d\) preserves all models and permits propagation of \(L\) from \(\alpha_{\le b}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonchronological PB backtracking governed by the learned constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input the conflict level \(d\), the trail, and an entailed learned constraint \(L\). Compute candidate levels \(b<d\) by restricting the trail to \(\alpha_{\le b}\). A regime may choose the greatest level at which \(L\) is assertive, the greatest level below the highest retained coefficient-relevant assignment, or another level satisfying its declared propagation condition. Delete every trail assignment above \(b\), retain \(L\), and resume propagation. The output is the truncated trail together with the consequences of \(L\); model preservation follows from \(L\) being entailed and from backtracking only removing temporary assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose an admissible earlier level from the learned PB constraint, erase later trail assignments, retain the constraint, and resume propagation.
knowledge_statements.title: PB Backjumping Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: An algorithmic regime is appropriate here, but the candidate-level alternatives are not formally defined, especially the phrase 'highest retained coefficient-relevant assignment.' No citation supports the proposed family of PB backjump selection rules.

children.title: Assertiveness-Backjump Coupling
children.top_down_role: Structural dependence between learned-constraint assertiveness and return level.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic coupling procedure without imposing a universal level-selection policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Evaluate candidate levels \(b<d\) using the assertive backjump coupling condition. If an eligible level is chosen, remove assignments above \(b\), install \(L\), and perform its forced propagation. If no eligible level exists, \(L\) cannot support assertive backjumping under the current trail and another learned constraint or return policy is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose an eligible assertive level, backtrack to it, and propagate the learned constraint; otherwise use a fallback policy.
assumptions_latex: The trail has finitely many decision levels.
Conflict and PB propagation tests for \(L\) are available under retained prefixes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b\in\{j<d:L\text{ is nonconflicting and propagating under }\alpha_{\le j}\}\) permits immediate propagation after backjumping.
knowledge_statements.title: Assertive-Level Selection and Propagation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coupling a learned PB constraint's propagation state to a return level.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L:\sum_i a_i\ell_i\ge B\) be learned at conflict level \(d\), and let \(\alpha_{\le b}\) be the trail retained at a level \(b<d\). The level \(b\) is assertive for \(L\) when \(L\) is nonconflicting under \(\alpha_{\le b}\) and PB propagation on \(L\) forces at least one currently unassigned literal. Backjumping to such a level makes \(L\) immediately active.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An assertive backjump returns to a level where the learned PB constraint is consistent and immediately propagating.
assumptions_latex: \(a_i\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\).
Assignments above level \(b\) are removed before testing propagation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{nonconflicting}(L,\alpha_{\le b})\land\operatorname{propagating}(L,\alpha_{\le b})\) makes \(b\) an assertive return level for \(L\).

notation.meaning: trail restricted to levels at most b

knowledge_statements.title: Assertive Backjump Coupling Condition

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additional condition needed to certify immediate incompatibility with the removed conflicting continuation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If an assertive learned constraint \(L\) forces a literal \(\ell\) after backjumping to \(b\), and the removed conflicting suffix assigned \(\ell=0\), then propagation forces the opposite of that removed assignment and the same suffix cannot be replayed unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Immediate blocking of the old suffix requires the learned constraint to force a value incompatible with that suffix.
assumptions_latex: \(L\) satisfies the assertive backjump coupling condition at level \(b\).
The removed suffix assigned the forced literal false.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L\text{ forces }\ell=1\land\alpha_{>b}(\ell)=0\Rightarrow\alpha_{>b}\text{ cannot be replayed unchanged}.

notation.meaning: assignments removed by backjumping below their levels

knowledge_statements.title: Immediate Suffix-Blocking Condition

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Propagation Alone Does Not Certify Immediate Suffix Blocking
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes ordinary assertiveness from a specific replay-blocking witness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: That \(L\) propagates after a backjump establishes assertiveness, but does not by itself identify an assignment in the removed suffix that is immediately contradicted. A suffix-blocking claim additionally requires a forced value incompatible with that suffix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Assertiveness alone does not certify immediate opposite-polarity blocking of a specified removed suffix.
assumptions_latex: \(L\) is propagating under the retained trail prefix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{propagating}(L,b)\not\Rightarrow\operatorname{immediateSuffixBlockingWitness}(L,b)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Propagation Alone Does Not Certify Immediate Suffix Blocking

assumptions_latex: \(L\) is learned from a conflict at level \(d\).
At least one level \(b<d\) makes \(L\) consistent and propagating under \(\alpha_{\le b}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Choosing such a level \(b\) makes \(L\) assertive immediately after the backjump and prevents immediate repetition of the same conflicting trail prefix.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coupling the learned constraint's propagation profile to level selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L\) be a learned pseudo-Boolean constraint at conflict level \(d\). Select a backjump level \(b<d\) for which the restricted assignment \(\alpha_{\le b}\) satisfies \(L\), while pseudo-Boolean propagation on \(L\) forces a literal that was assigned above \(b\) on the conflicting trail. After deleting assignments above \(b\), insert \(L\) and propagate that literal. Thus the assertiveness test determines an admissible backjump level, and the chosen level determines whether \(L\) becomes immediately active.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Backjump to a level where the learned PB constraint becomes consistent but unit-propagating, so it immediately blocks the conflicting continuation.
knowledge_statements.title: Assertiveness-Backjump Coupling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle kind fits the interaction leaf, but forcing a literal that happened to be assigned above b does not by itself show that the conflicting continuation is blocked; the forced value must be incompatible with that continuation. The precise assertiveness-backjump coupling also lacks a source.

children.title: Irrelevant-Literal Management
children.top_down_role: Detection and treatment of literals irrelevant to learned PB constraints.

assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a pseudo-Boolean constraint over finitely many Boolean literals.
Irrelevance is evaluated with respect to a declared domain \(D\) of partial or total assignments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Deleting \(l_j\) from the representation is exact on \(D\) precisely when \(C(\alpha,l_j=0)=C(\alpha,l_j=1)\) for every compatible \(\alpha\in D\).

notation.meaning: assignment domain used for the test

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic criterion for safely eliminating a PB literal on a declared domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A literal \(l_j\) is irrelevant to a pseudo-Boolean constraint \(C\) on an assignment domain \(D\) when, for every assignment \(\alpha\in D\) compatible with both values of its variable, \(C(\alpha,l_j=0)\) and \(C(\alpha,l_j=1)\) have the same truth value. Management may delete, ignore, or avoid watching \(l_j\) only on a domain for which this condition has been established. Under this condition, replacing \(C\) by either restriction with respect to \(l_j\) preserves exactly the satisfying assignments projected onto the remaining variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A literal may be eliminated on a domain when changing its value never changes whether the PB constraint is satisfied there.
knowledge_statements.title: Irrelevant-Literal Management

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind is plausible, but D mixes partial and total assignments without defining the truth evaluation of C on partial assignments. The notation also assigns values to a literal rather than explicitly to its underlying variable, which is ambiguous for complemented literals. No PB-specific source or locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Builder-proposed global semantic criterion, deferred because its canonical home and intended conflict-analysis domain are unresolved.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a normalized threshold row, the proposed criterion declares \(l_j\) irrelevant when no sum of the other coefficients lies in \([b-a_j,b-1]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proposed test characterizes global Boolean independence in a restricted normalized row, not necessarily the intended trail-relative irrelevant-literal notion of PB conflict analysis.
assumptions_latex: Other literals would need to correspond to independently valued distinct variables.
All coefficients would need to be nonnegative integers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Publication is deferred pending a definition of the leaf's intended irrelevance domain.}
knowledge_statements.title: Global Reachable-Sum Irrelevance Criterion

intermediate_metadata.reason: The topic is materially ambiguous: the immutable seed mixes assignment domains, while the builder substitutes a restricted global subset-sum notion that may belong to general PB preprocessing rather than conflict-analysis literal management. Coefficient normalization and post-deletion algebra are excluded as sibling scopes.

children.title: Coefficient Management
children.top_down_role: Control of coefficient size, representation, and numerical burden.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerical-growth boundary for exact coefficient management.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Eliminating unequal positive pivot coefficients \(a\) and \(b\) by integral alignment can require the common coefficient \(\operatorname{lcm}(a,b)\) and can multiply nonpivot coefficients by \(b/\gcd(a,b)\) or \(a/\gcd(a,b)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact pivot alignment can enlarge nonpivot coefficients, so normalization alone provides no monotone magnitude bound.
assumptions_latex: Integral scaling is used for exact complementary-pivot alignment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{exact normalization does not imply that every derived coefficient is at most }\max\{a,b\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Pivot Alignment Can Increase Coefficients

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact reduction of a PB row whose coefficients share a positive divisor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(d>0\) divides every \(a_i\), then \(\sum_i a_i l_i\ge b\) is equivalent to \(\sum_i(a_i/d)l_i\ge\lceil b/d\rceil\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Divide all coefficients by a common positive divisor and round the threshold upward without changing Boolean satisfaction.
assumptions_latex: \(a_i,b\in\mathbb Z\).
\(d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\) divides every \(a_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_i a_i l_i\ge b\Longleftrightarrow\sum_i(a_i/d)l_i\ge\lceil b/d\rceil.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Common-Divisor Normalization

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Arbitrary Coefficient Clipping Changes the Feasible Set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary for clipping a learned-row coefficient below an exact sound cap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(C:2x+y\ge2\), clipping the coefficient of \(x\) to \(1\) gives \(C':x+y\ge2\). The Boolean assignment \((x,y)=(1,0)\) satisfies \(C\) but violates \(C'\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Arbitrary coefficient clipping can remove satisfying assignments.
assumptions_latex: The threshold remains unchanged.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 2x+y\ge2\not\equiv x+y\ge2.
knowledge_statements.title: Arbitrary Coefficient Clipping Changes the Feasible Set

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Single-Step Bit Growth Under Exact Pivot Alignment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bit-length accounting for one exact complementary-pivot alignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For positive pivot coefficients \(a,b\), exact integral alignment uses \(m=\operatorname{lcm}(a,b)\le ab\). Consequently, \(\operatorname{bits}(m)\le \operatorname{bits}(a)+\operatorname{bits}(b)\). A nonpivot coefficient \(c\) scaled by \(b/\gcd(a,b)\) has bit length \(O(\operatorname{bits}(c)+\operatorname{bits}(b))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One exact pivot-alignment step has additive bit-length growth, although repeated steps may accumulate it.
assumptions_latex: \(a,b,c\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\).
Exact integral scaling is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{bits}(\operatorname{lcm}(a,b))\le\operatorname{bits}(a)+\operatorname{bits}(b),\quad \operatorname{bits}\!\left(c\frac b{\gcd(a,b)}\right)=O(\operatorname{bits}(c)+\operatorname{bits}(b)).

notation.meaning: binary bit length of a positive integer

knowledge_statements.title: Single-Step Bit Growth Under Exact Pivot Alignment

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rounded Division Produces a Valid PB Weakening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coefficient control by sound, generally inexact division of a nonnegative learned PB row.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(C:\sum_i a_i\ell_i\ge b\) with \(a_i,b\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) and \(d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), define \(C_d:\sum_i\lceil a_i/d\rceil\ell_i\ge\lceil b/d\rceil\). Every Boolean assignment satisfying \(C\) satisfies \(C_d\). The converse need not hold, so this operation is generally a weakening.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rounding coefficients and the threshold upward after division gives an entailed, generally weaker PB inequality.
assumptions_latex: \(a_i,b\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\).
\(d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C\models C_d,\qquad C_d\not\models C\text{ in general}.
knowledge_statements.title: Rounded Division Produces a Valid PB Weakening

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Ordered Coefficient-Control Policy for PB Conflict Analysis
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound ordering of exact and weakening coefficient operations on learned PB inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Normalize each antecedent to a nonnegative-literal integer inequality and remove any common coefficient divisor. To cancel complementary pivot literals with positive coefficients \(a,b\), multiply the rows by \(b/\gcd(a,b)\) and \(a/\gcd(a,b)\), add them, replace the aligned complementary literals by their resulting constant, and normalize the bound. Then apply exact saturation and gcd normalization. Rounded division may be applied only as an explicitly marked weakening. Every emitted row must be checked as entailed by its registered antecedents.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalize rows, align and cancel complementary pivots exactly, apply exact reductions, and label any rounded division as weakening.
assumptions_latex: All arithmetic is exact and integral.
Every antecedent is valid for the current PB problem.
Rounded division uses a sound directed-rounding rule and is not labeled equivalent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Every emitted learned row is entailed by its registered antecedents.}

notation.meaning: positive coefficients of complementary pivot literals

knowledge_statements.title: Ordered Coefficient-Control Policy for PB Conflict Analysis

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Derivation-Wide Bit Growth Under Exact Alignment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case accumulated coefficient growth under repeated exact pivot alignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B_t\) bound the bit length of every coefficient and threshold entering alignment step \(t\), and suppose each row contains at most \(n\) terms. Exact lcm alignment, scaling, addition, and canonicalization satisfy \(B_{t+1}\le2B_t+O(\log n)\). Consequently, after \(s\) consecutive unreduced alignments, \(B_s\le2^sB_0+O((2^s-1)\log n)\). Arithmetic checking is polynomial in the explicit intermediate bit length, but need not be polynomial in \(B_0+s\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated exact alignments can double coefficient bit length per step; checking is output-polynomial but intermediate derivations can be large.
assumptions_latex: Each row contains at most \(n\) nonzero terms.
Arithmetic cost is charged by operand bit length.
No independent global coefficient cap is assumed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: B_s\le2^sB_0+O((2^s-1)\log n).

notation.meaning: maximum coefficient or threshold bit length before alignment step t
number of consecutive exact alignment steps

knowledge_statements.title: Derivation-Wide Bit Growth Under Exact Alignment

assumptions_latex: \(a_i\) and \(b\) are nonnegative integers, and each \(l_i\in\{0,1\}\).
The constraint is \(\sum_i a_i l_i\ge b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Replacing every \(a_i\) by \(\min\{a_i,b\}\) yields a constraint equivalent on \(\{0,1\}^n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coefficient saturation for nonnegative threshold PB constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(C:\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_i l_i\ge b\), where \(a_i,b\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) and \(l_i\in\{0,1\}\). Define \(a_i'=\min\{a_i,b\}\) and \(C':\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_i'l_i\ge b\). Then \(C\) and \(C'\) have identical Boolean satisfying assignments. Indeed, any selected literal whose coefficient exceeds \(b\) already supplies the entire threshold, while assignments selecting no such literal have unchanged activity. Thus saturation controls coefficient magnitude without changing the represented Boolean constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a nonnegative threshold PB constraint, capping every coefficient at the threshold preserves exactly the same Boolean assignments.
knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient Management

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The coefficient-saturation property is mathematically precise for nonnegative threshold PB constraints and fits the leaf, but the record has no citation or inspectable locator. The unrelated local inventory cannot support candidate-review acceptance.

children.title: Literal-Coefficient Interaction
children.top_down_role: Effects of literal removal on coefficient structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between exact restriction or proven irrelevance and syntactic erasure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The row \(2x+y\ge2\) is satisfied by \((x,y)=(1,0)\), whereas deleting \(2x\) without adjusting the threshold yields the unsatisfiable Boolean row \(y\ge2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero literal term cannot generally be erased while leaving the threshold unchanged.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 2x+y\ge2\not\equiv y\ge2.
knowledge_statements.title: Unadjusted Literal Deletion Is Unsound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact combination of coefficients attached to opposite literals of one variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in\{0,1\}\), \(p x+q(1-x)+A\ge b\) is equivalent to \((p-q)x+A\ge b-q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Opposite literals can be merged by extracting their common constant contribution and retaining the coefficient difference.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) contains neither \(x\) nor \(1-x\).
\(p,q,b\in\mathbb Z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p x+q(1-x)+A\ge b\Longleftrightarrow(p-q)x+A\ge b-q.
knowledge_statements.title: Complementary-Literal Coefficient Normalization

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Restriction by a Literal Value
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coefficient-threshold transformation caused by fixing one PB literal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(C:a_jl_j+\sum_{i\ne j}a_il_i\ge b\), restriction to \(l_j=v\in\{0,1\}\) is \(\sum_{i\ne j}a_il_i\ge b-a_jv\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixing a literal removes its term and subtracts its realized contribution from the threshold.
assumptions_latex: The restriction fixes the literal's truth value rather than merely deleting its term.
All literals have Boolean truth values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C\!\restriction_{l_j=v}\equiv\sum_{i\ne j}a_il_i\ge b-a_jv.

notation.meaning: constraint restricted to literal value v

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Restriction by a Literal Value

assumptions_latex: \(C\) has nonnegative coefficients and Boolean literals.
\(l_j\) is unassigned under the current partial assignment \(\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Constraint \(C\) forces \(l_j=1\) under \(\alpha\) exactly when \(a_j>s(\alpha)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact coefficient-slack test for PB propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C:\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_i l_i\ge b\), with \(a_i\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\), and let \(U(\alpha)\) and \(T(\alpha)\) be the unassigned and true literals under \(\alpha\). Define the maximum residual slack by \(s(\alpha)=\sum_{i\in T(\alpha)}a_i+\sum_{i\in U(\alpha)}a_i-b\). For an unassigned literal \(l_j\), assigning \(l_j=0\) reduces the maximum attainable left-hand side by \(a_j\). Therefore \(C\) forces \(l_j=1\) exactly when \(s(\alpha)-a_j<0\), equivalently when \(a_j>s(\alpha)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unassigned literal is forced true exactly when its coefficient exceeds the constraint's current maximum residual slack.
knowledge_statements.title: Literal-Coefficient Interaction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The coefficient-slack formula is standard for a nonconflicting propagation state, but the record does not assume s(alpha) is nonnegative. If the current assignment is already conflicting, the solver reports conflict rather than treating every coefficient exceeding negative slack as a forced literal. No source is supplied to fix the intended operational convention.
