knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact normalization of a linear combination containing both polarities of one variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If an added PB inequality contains \(px+q(1-x)\) with \(p,q\ge0\), then \[px+q(1-x)=\min\{p,q\}+|p-q|\ell,\] where \(\ell=x\) if \(p\ge q\), and \(\ell=1-x\) otherwise. Moving the constant to the threshold gives an equivalent normalized PB inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After adding PB inequalities, opposite literals of a variable can be consolidated exactly into a constant and one remaining polarity.
assumptions_latex: \(p,q\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(px+q(1-x)\equiv\min\{p,q\}+|p-q|\ell\).

notation.meaning: the polarity with the larger coefficient

knowledge_statements.title: Complementary-Literal Elimination After Addition

assumptions_latex: \(C_k\) are valid inequalities over a common Boolean domain.
All multipliers \(\lambda_k\) are nonnegative integers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every common Boolean solution of the premises satisfies \(\sum_k\lambda_k L_k(x)\ge\sum_k\lambda_k b_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonnegative linear combination rule in cutting-planes calculus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_k:L_k(x)\ge b_k\) for \(k=1,\ldots,m\) be integer linear inequalities valid for every feasible \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\), and choose \(\lambda_k\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\). The linear-combination inference rule derives \(\sum_{k=1}^{m}\lambda_kL_k(x)\ge\sum_{k=1}^{m}\lambda_kb_k\). Every Boolean assignment satisfying all premises satisfies the derived inequality because multiplication by a nonnegative scalar preserves inequality direction and the scaled inequalities may be added. Zero multipliers simply omit premises; negative multipliers are not admitted by this rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any nonnegative integer linear combination of valid PB inequalities is itself valid for all common Boolean solutions.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Combination Inference

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The mathematical rule is precise, but an inference-rule leaf is better represented as a principle than as a generic property. No cited source or specific locator supports its formulation in the PB cutting-planes calculus.

children.title: PB Division Families
children.top_down_role: Division-based inference families for pseudo-Boolean constraints.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain restriction for the standard division inference schema.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The standard \(\ge\)-preserving PB division schema requires \(d>0\). Division by zero is undefined, and division by a negative number reverses the inequality direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The standard PB division rule permits only positive divisors.
assumptions_latex: The constraint is written with relation \(\ge\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\) is required by the stated schema.
knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Divisor Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence-preserving exact division of an integral PB inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\) divides every \(a_i\) and \(b\), then over Boolean assignments, \[\sum_i a_i\ell_i\ge b\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\sum_i(a_i/d)\ell_i\ge b/d.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dividing every coefficient and the threshold by a common positive divisor preserves the satisfying assignments exactly.
assumptions_latex: \(a_i,b\in\mathbb Z\).
\(d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\) divides every \(a_i\) and \(b\).
Each \(\ell_i\in\{0,1\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Sol}(C)=\operatorname{Sol}(C/d)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Common-Divisor Reduction

assumptions_latex: \(a_i,b\in\mathbb Z\), each \(l_i\in\{0,1\}\), and \(d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\).
The premise is \(\sum_i a_i l_i\ge b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The ceiling-division inequality \(\sum_i\lceil a_i/d\rceil l_i\ge\lceil b/d\rceil\) is a valid consequence of the premise.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound ceiling-division member of the PB division family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: From the pseudo-Boolean inequality \(\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_i l_i\ge b\), choose a positive integer divisor \(d\). Ceiling division derives \(\sum_{i=1}^{n}\lceil a_i/d\rceil l_i\ge\lceil b/d\rceil\). This rule is sound because, for every Boolean assignment satisfying the premise, \(\sum_i\lceil a_i/d\rceil l_i\ge\lceil(\sum_i a_i l_i)/d\rceil\ge\lceil b/d\rceil\). Exact division is the special case in which every retained coefficient and the threshold are divisible by \(d\); other PB division regimes combine weakening or saturation with a declared rounding convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dividing a PB inequality by a positive integer and rounding coefficients and threshold upward produces a valid consequence.
knowledge_statements.title: PB Division Families

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed ceiling-division consequence is mathematically coherent, but a named inference-family leaf should be a principle or representation rather than a generic property. The claims about exact division and other PB division regimes require an authoritative source with a specific locator.

children.title: PB Rounding Families
children.top_down_role: Rounding conventions associated with coefficient division.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rounded Division Need Not Preserve Equivalence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict weakening caused by coefficient-wise ceiling division.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(C:x_1+x_2\ge2\) and \(d=2\), ceiling division yields \(x_1+x_2\ge1\). The assignment \((x_1,x_2)=(1,0)\) satisfies the rounded constraint but not \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sound ceiling-rounded division can introduce new satisfying assignments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Sol}(C)\subsetneq\operatorname{Sol}(C/2)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Rounded Division Need Not Preserve Equivalence
PB Rounding Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coefficient-wise division and upward rounding for normalized pseudo-Boolean inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\). From the normalized constraint \(C:\sum_{i=1}^n a_i\ell_i\ge b\), derive
\[C/d:\quad \sum_{i=1}^n \left\lceil\frac{a_i}{d}\right\rceil\ell_i\ge \left\lceil\frac{b}{d}\right\rceil.\]
For every Boolean assignment \(x\), satisfaction of \(C\) implies satisfaction of \(C/d\). Consequently, the rounded inequality is a sound pseudo-Boolean consequence, although it need not be equivalent to the original constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dividing a PB inequality by a positive integer and rounding every coefficient and the threshold upward yields a valid, generally weaker consequence.
assumptions_latex: \(a_i,b\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) and \(d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\).
Each \(\ell_i\) is a Boolean literal evaluated in \(\{0,1\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C\models C/d\).

notation.meaning: Boolean literal, either a variable or its complement

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The coefficient-wise ceiling division rule is mathematically plausible, correctly scoped to normalized nonnegative PB inequalities, and appropriately classified as a principle, but the record supplies no citation. A direct PB proof-system source with a section, rule, theorem, or page locator is required.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rejected here because it primarily concerns compatibility between coefficient and threshold rounding conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(C:x\ge1\) and \(d=2\), combining coefficient flooring with threshold ceiling gives \(0x\ge1\), which is false at the satisfying assignment \(x=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coefficient flooring paired with threshold ceiling is unsound, but that pairing is owned by Division-Rounding Compatibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C\not\models(\lfloor1/2\rfloor x\ge\lceil1/2\rceil)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient-Flooring Failure

intermediate_metadata.reason: The leaf owns upward coefficient and threshold rounding and the fact that sound rounding may strictly weaken a constraint. Divisor selection was excluded as PB Division Families scope, and the proposed mixed floor/ceiling counterexample was deferred to Division-Rounding Compatibility.

children.title: Division-Rounding Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Compatibility regimes linking divisors with rounding conventions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: General sufficient compatibility condition for normalized nonnegative PB division.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C:\sum_i a_i\ell_i\ge b\), with \(a_i,b\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\), Boolean literals, and \(d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\). If \(\bar a_i\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) satisfies \(\bar a_i\ge a_i/d\) and \(\bar b\le\lceil b/d\rceil\), then \(C\models\sum_i\bar a_i\ell_i\ge\bar b\). The coefficient-wise ceiling rule \(\bar a_i=\lceil a_i/d\rceil\), \(\bar b=\lceil b/d\rceil\), is the componentwise smallest coefficient choice at the strongest threshold supplied by this sufficient condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rounding divided coefficients upward and using no threshold above the divided ceiling gives a sound pseudo-Boolean consequence.
assumptions_latex: a_i,b,\bar a_i\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}.
d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C\models\sum_i\bar a_i\ell_i\ge\bar b.
review_flags: condition is sufficient; it is not asserted to characterize every sound rounded consequence
knowledge_statements.title: Sound Division-Rounding Compatibility

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Flooring Coefficients With an Up-Rounded Threshold Can Lose Entailment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of an incompatible mixed rounding rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For Boolean \(x,y\), \(C:x+y\ge1\) and \(d=2\), flooring coefficients while rounding the threshold upward gives \(0x+0y\ge1\), which is false at \((x,y)=(1,0)\), a model of \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Flooring divided coefficients while ceiling the threshold can reject a model of the original constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x+y\ge1\not\models0x+0y\ge1.
knowledge_statements.title: Flooring Coefficients With an Up-Rounded Threshold Can Lose Entailment

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence case requiring no rounding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\) divides every coefficient \(a_i\) and the threshold \(b\), then \[\sum_i a_i\ell_i\ge b\iff\sum_i(a_i/d)\ell_i\ge b/d.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Division by a positive common divisor preserves the inequality exactly.
assumptions_latex: a_i,b\in\mathbb Z.
d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}.
d\mid a_i\text{ for every }i.
d\mid b.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_i a_i\ell_i\ge b\iff\sum_i\frac{a_i}{d}\ell_i\ge\frac bd.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Division Under Common Divisibility
Division-Rounding Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions ensuring that division and rounding define a sound PB inference.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a normalized inequality \(C:\sum_i a_i\ell_i\ge b\), a division-rounding map \(R_d\) is admissible when \(d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\) and its rounded data satisfy
\[\bar a_i\ge a_i/d\quad\text{and}\quad \bar b=\lceil b/d\rceil,\]
with \(\bar a_i\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\). Under these conditions, \(R_d(C):\sum_i\bar a_i\ell_i\ge\bar b\) is entailed by \(C\). Choosing \(\bar a_i=\lceil a_i/d\rceil\) gives the canonical coefficient-wise rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Division and rounding are compatible when the divisor is positive, coefficients are rounded no lower than their quotients, and the threshold is rounded upward.
assumptions_latex: \(a_i,b,\bar a_i\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) and \(d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\).
All literals take values in \(\{0,1\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C\models R_d(C)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated sufficient conditions imply integer transformed coefficients at least as large as the coefficient-wise ceilings and therefore give the claimed consequence. The condition content kind fits the leaf, but no source supports this generalized admissibility formulation or the assertion that the ceiling choice is canonical.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Flooring the Threshold Can Be Unsound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Builder proposal rejected because an infeasible premise entails every constraint and therefore cannot witness failed entailment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The proposed premise \(2x\ge3\) has no Boolean model. Consequently \(2x\ge3\models x\ge1\) holds vacuously, contrary to the proposed conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proposed infeasible-premise example does not show unsoundness and is deferred.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 2x\ge3\models x\ge1.
review_flags: downward threshold rounding is weaker, not inherently unsound, under upward coefficient rounding
knowledge_statements.title: Flooring the Threshold Can Be Unsound

intermediate_metadata.reason: The leaf owns the soundness relationship between division and rounding, including a general sufficient condition, exact divisible scaling, a genuine mixed-rounding failure, and a checkable compatibility test. The false infeasible-premise counterexample was deferred. Individual division calculi and rounding-family catalogues were excluded as sibling scopes.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applicability limits of the standard coefficient-capping formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The formula \(a_i\mapsto\min\{a_i,b\}\) is the standard saturation rule for a normalized \(\ge\) constraint with \(a_i\ge0\) and \(b>0\). Signed coefficients must first be normalized; when \(b\le0\), a nonnegative normalized inequality is already tautological.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Threshold capping applies to normalized nonnegative PB inequalities with a positive threshold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a_i\ge0\) and \(b>0\) are the applicability conditions for the standard capping formula.
knowledge_statements.title: Normalization Boundary for Threshold Capping

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical closure property of coefficient capping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(S_b(a)_i=\min\{a_i,b\}\) with \(b>0\), applying saturation twice changes nothing: \(S_b(S_b(a))=S_b(a)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Threshold saturation is idempotent.
assumptions_latex: \(a_i\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\).
\(b\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_b\circ S_b=S_b\).
knowledge_statements.title: Idempotence of Saturation
Saturation-Based Inference
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Saturation of coefficients at the threshold in normalized PB constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the normalized pseudo-Boolean constraint
\[C:\quad \sum_{i=1}^n a_i\ell_i\ge b,\]
with \(b>0\), define its saturation by
\[\operatorname{sat}(C):\quad \sum_{i=1}^n\min\{a_i,b\}\ell_i\ge b.\]
Then \(C\) and \(\operatorname{sat}(C)\) have exactly the same satisfying Boolean assignments. Thus every coefficient exceeding the threshold may be replaced by the threshold without changing the represented constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Capping each nonnegative coefficient at the positive threshold preserves exactly the Boolean solutions of a normalized PB constraint.
assumptions_latex: \(a_i\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) and \(b\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\).
Each \(\ell_i\) has Boolean value zero or one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C\equiv\operatorname{sat}(C)\) over Boolean assignments.

notation.meaning: constraint obtained by capping coefficients at the threshold

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The saturation equivalence is precise under the stated nonnegative-coefficient and positive-threshold assumptions, and principle is suitable for this topic. The record nevertheless has no inspectable citation for PB saturation.

children.title: PB Weakening Families
children.top_down_role: Constraint-relaxing transformations within pseudo-Boolean calculi.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary parameter-monotone weakenings of a normalized PB inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: From \(C:\sum_i a_i\ell_i\ge b\), one may derive \[\sum_i(a_i+\delta_i)\ell_i\ge b-\eta\] for arbitrary \(\delta_i,\eta\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Increasing nonnegative literal coefficients or lowering the threshold yields a valid weaker PB constraint.
assumptions_latex: \(a_i\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\).
\(\delta_i,\eta\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\).
Each \(\ell_i\in\{0,1\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C\models\sum_i(a_i+\delta_i)\ell_i\ge b-\eta\).
knowledge_statements.title: Monotone Coefficient and Threshold Weakening

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recognition of a weakening that has lost all constraining force.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a normalized inequality \(\sum_i c_i\ell_i\ge r\) with \(c_i\ge0\), if \(r\le0\), every Boolean assignment satisfies the inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normalized nonnegative PB inequality with a nonpositive threshold is tautological.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Sol}(\sum_i c_i\ell_i\ge r)=\{0,1\}^n\).
knowledge_statements.title: Tautological Weakening Boundary
PB Weakening Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Literal deletion with compensating threshold reduction for PB inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C:\sum_{i=1}^n a_i\ell_i\ge b\), and choose \(S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\). The weakening of \(C\) on \(S\) is
\[W_S(C):\quad \sum_{i\notin S}a_i\ell_i\ge b-\sum_{i\in S}a_i.\]
Every Boolean assignment satisfying \(C\) satisfies \(W_S(C)\). If the new threshold is nonpositive, the weakened constraint is tautological. Taking \(S\) to be a singleton gives elementary literal weakening.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deleting selected nonnegative PB terms and subtracting their maximum possible contribution from the threshold yields a sound weaker constraint.
assumptions_latex: \(a_i\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) and \(b\in\mathbb Z\).
Each \(\ell_i\) takes a value in \(\{0,1\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C\models W_S(C)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The deletion rule correctly compensates for the maximum contribution of the removed Boolean terms and is appropriately presented as a weakening principle. No source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: PB Strengthening Families
children.top_down_role: Constraint-tightening transformations within pseudo-Boolean calculi.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of threshold strengthening across an attainable left-hand-side value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(C:x_1+x_2\ge1\), raising the threshold to \(2\) excludes the satisfying assignment \((1,0)\). Thus threshold raising is not equivalence-preserving when the skipped interval contains an attainable left-hand-side value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A PB threshold cannot be raised arbitrarily without excluding valid assignments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Sol}(x_1+x_2\ge2)\subsetneq\operatorname{Sol}(x_1+x_2\ge1)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Unjustified Threshold Raising Is Unsound
PB Strengthening Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integrality strengthening by rounding a threshold to the coefficient lattice.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C:\sum_{i=1}^n a_i\ell_i\ge b\), and let \(g=\gcd(a_1,\ldots,a_n)>0\). Since every value of the left-hand side is an integer multiple of \(g\), the strengthened constraint
\[S_g(C):\quad \sum_{i=1}^n a_i\ell_i\ge g\left\lceil\frac{b}{g}\right\rceil\]
has exactly the same Boolean solutions as \(C\). The threshold is thereby raised to the least attainable lattice value not below \(b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A PB threshold can be raised to the next multiple of the coefficient gcd without changing the Boolean feasible set.
assumptions_latex: \(a_i\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\), not all zero, and \(b\in\mathbb Z\).
Each \(\ell_i\) is Boolean-valued.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C\equiv S_g(C)\).

notation.meaning: greatest common divisor of the coefficients

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The gcd-lattice threshold adjustment preserves the Boolean solution set under the stated assumptions and fits the strengthening-family leaf as a principle. A direct source for this PB integrality-strengthening rule is missing.

children.title: Transformation Admissibility Regimes
children.top_down_role: Contexts governing admissible weakening or strengthening transformations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact replacement criterion in the presence of unchanged ambient constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Gamma\) be the unchanged ambient PB constraints. Replacing \(C\) by \(T(C)\) preserves the ambient feasible set exactly if and only if \[\operatorname{Sol}(\Gamma\land C)=\operatorname{Sol}(\Gamma\land T(C)).\] This contextual equality may hold even when \(C\) and \(T(C)\) are not globally equivalent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A transformed constraint may replace the original when they are equivalent relative to the unchanged ambient constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(\Gamma\), \(C\), and \(T(C)\) use a common Boolean assignment space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Gamma\land C\equiv\Gamma\land T(C)\) is necessary and sufficient for contextual replacement.
knowledge_statements.title: Context-Relative Replacement Admissibility
Transformation Admissibility Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic admissibility criteria for PB weakening and strengthening transformations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T\) map a PB constraint \(C\) to \(T(C)\), both interpreted over the same Boolean variables. The transformation is consequence-admissible precisely when
\[\operatorname{Sol}(C)\subseteq\operatorname{Sol}(T(C)),\]
and equivalence-admissible precisely when equality holds. A transformation used to replace \(C\) without retaining it must be equivalence-admissible; a transformation used only to derive an additional valid constraint need only be consequence-admissible. A strict strengthening with \(\operatorname{Sol}(T(C))\subsetneq\operatorname{Sol}(C)\) requires an independent justification preserving the ambient feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: PB transformations are admissible as derived constraints under entailment, but replacing an original constraint requires equality of Boolean solution sets.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) and \(T(C)\) use a common Boolean assignment space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Replacement requires \(\operatorname{Sol}(C)=\operatorname{Sol}(T(C))\); derivation requires \(\operatorname{Sol}(C)\subseteq\operatorname{Sol}(T(C))\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The distinction between consequence-preserving derivation and equivalence-preserving replacement is coherent, and condition is the correct role for the admissibility-regime leaf. The record has no cited PB proof-system or transformation-semantics source for these criteria.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Number of Strict Improvement Calls
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iteration bound after a feasible incumbent is known for integer-valued linear improvement search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U_0\) be the initial feasible objective value and let \(L\in\mathbb Z\) satisfy \(L\le f(x)\) for every feasible \(x\). If every successful call returns a solution with \(f(x)\le U-1\), then there are at most \(U_0-L\) successful improvements and at most \(U_0-L+1\) post-incumbent feasibility calls, including the final unsuccessful call.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each successful call lowers the integer incumbent by at least one, so a finite integer lower bound limits the number of calls.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) has a feasible assignment with initial value \(U_0\).
\(f(x)\in\mathbb Z\) for every feasible assignment.
\(L\in\mathbb Z\) is a valid global lower bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{success}}\le U_0-L,\qquad N_{\mathrm{calls}}\le U_0-L+1.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Number of Strict Improvement Calls

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact strict-incumbent cutoff for a rational linear PB objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=c^Tx\) with \(c_i\in\mathbb Q\), and let \(D>0\) be a common multiple of their denominators. Then every Boolean objective value lies in \(D^{-1}\mathbb Z\). For an incumbent value \(U\), the strict condition \(f(x)<U\) is equivalent on \(\{0,1\}^n\) to \(f(x)\le U-1/D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a rational objective on a denominator lattice, subtract one lattice step rather than one to encode strict improvement.
assumptions_latex: \(Dc_i\in\mathbb Z\) for every objective coefficient.
\(U=f(\bar x)\) for a Boolean incumbent \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f(x)<U\Longleftrightarrow f(x)\le U-\frac1D\quad\text{for Boolean }x.

notation.meaning: common denominator multiple defining an objective-value lattice

knowledge_statements.title: Rational-Lattice Strict-Improvement Cutoff

knowledge_statements.statement_title: No Universal Unit Cutoff for Nonintegral Objectives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the integer \(U-1\) cutoff outside an integer objective lattice.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x)=x/2\) and incumbent \(U=1/2\), the Boolean assignment \(x=0\) is a strict improvement, but it does not satisfy \(f(x)\le U-1=-1/2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subtracting one can discard valid improvements when objective values are nonintegral.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f(x)<U\not\Longleftrightarrow f(x)\le U-1\quad\text{for general rational }f.
knowledge_statements.title: No Universal Unit Cutoff for Nonintegral Objectives
Linear Solution-Improvement Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict incumbent improvement for an integer-valued linear PB objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given PB constraints \(F\) and objective \(f(x)=c^Tx\) with integer coefficients, first obtain a feasible assignment \(x^0\); if none exists, report infeasibility. Set \(U=f(x^0)\). Repeatedly call a complete PB feasibility solver on
\[F\cup\{f(x)\le U-1\}.\]
If it returns \(x^{k+1}\), set \(U=f(x^{k+1})\) and continue. If it reports infeasibility, stop and output the incumbent \(x^k\) and value \(U\), which are globally optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly require an integer objective value strictly better than the incumbent; the last incumbent is optimal when the next improvement constraint is infeasible.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) is handled by a complete PB feasibility solver.
\(c\in\mathbb Z^n\), so every strict improvement is expressible as \(f(x)\le U-1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned incumbent satisfies \(f(x^k)=\min\{f(x):x\models F\}\).

source_refs.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

source_witnesses.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The integer-objective improvement loop is mathematically standard and algorithm is the correct content kind, but the cited section on primal bounds, greedy methods, and local search does not specifically support the repeated complete-feasibility calls or the optimality conclusion. In addition, the assumption writing F as a subset of {0,1}^n conflicts with the statement's use of F as a PB constraint system. A source directly covering linear-search optimization and corrected typing of F are required.

children.title: PB Search-Space Branching
children.top_down_role: Branching organizations for pseudo-Boolean optimization search.

knowledge_statements.title: PB Search-Space Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary branching that partitions a PB search node by a literal value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At a search node with residual PB system \(F_N\), choose an unfixed variable \(x_j\). Create children
\[F_{N,0}=F_N\cup\{x_j=0\},\qquad F_{N,1}=F_N\cup\{x_j=1\}.\]
Propagate and simplify PB constraints in each child, discarding any child proved infeasible. Continue until every surviving leaf is infeasible, pruned by an objective bound, or supplies a complete feasible assignment. The two children form a disjoint and exhaustive partition of the parent node's Boolean assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branching fixes an unfixed Boolean variable to zero and one, producing disjoint children whose union equals the parent search space.
assumptions_latex: \(x_j\in\{0,1\}\) is unfixed at the parent node.
Propagation and infeasibility tests are sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Sol}(F_N)=\operatorname{Sol}(F_{N,0})\mathbin{\dot\cup}\operatorname{Sol}(F_{N,1})\).

notation.meaning: residual PB system at node N

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Disjoint exhaustive branching on an integer-valued pseudo-Boolean linear form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h(x)=\sum_i a_i\ell_i\) have integer coefficients and Boolean literals, and let \(\beta\in\mathbb Z\). From residual system \(F_N\), create children \[F_N\cup\{h(x)\ge\beta\},\qquad F_N\cup\{h(x)\le\beta-1\}.\] Because \(h(x)\) is integer-valued, the children are disjoint and cover every Boolean assignment represented by the parent. Binary variable branching is the special case \(h(x)=x_j\) and \(\beta=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An integer PB inequality and its complementary threshold form a disjoint exhaustive branch pair.
assumptions_latex: \(a_i,\beta\in\mathbb Z\).
Each \(\ell_i\) is Boolean-valued.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Sol}(F_N)=\operatorname{Sol}(F_N\land h\ge\beta)\mathbin{\dot\cup}\operatorname{Sol}(F_N\land h\le\beta-1).
knowledge_statements.title: Complementary PB-Inequality Branching

children.title: PB Objective Bounds
children.top_down_role: Upper-bound and lower-bound sources used during exact PB search.

knowledge_statements.title: PB Objective Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nodewise lower and incumbent upper bounds for minimization PB search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a minimization PB problem at node \(N\), a number \(L_N\) is a valid lower bound when
\[L_N\le f(x)\quad\text{for every }x\in\operatorname{Sol}(F_N).\]
A feasible incumbent \(\hat x\) supplies the upper bound \(U=f(\hat x)\). The pair \((L_N,U)\) brackets every improving solution in the node. A relaxation optimum is a verifiable lower-bound certificate whenever the relaxation contains every Boolean solution represented by \(F_N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A node lower bound underestimates every feasible objective there, while a feasible incumbent provides a global upper bound for minimization.
assumptions_latex: The problem minimizes \(f\) over Boolean assignments.
\(\hat x\) satisfies the original PB system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(x\in\operatorname{Sol}(F_N)\), \(L_N\le f(x)\), and the global optimum is at most \(U\).

notation.meaning: valid lower bound at node N
objective value of a feasible incumbent
residual PB constraints at node N

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct node lower bound from fixed variables and independent minimization of unfixed linear objective terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At node \(N\), let \(x_i=v_i\in\{0,1\}\) for \(i\in I_N\). For \(f(x)=c_0+\sum_{i=1}^n c_i x_i\), define \[L_N^{\mathrm{lit}}=c_0+\sum_{i\in I_N}c_i v_i+\sum_{i\notin I_N}\min\{0,c_i\}.\] Then \(L_N^{\mathrm{lit}}\le f(x)\) for every completion represented by the node. Additional sound Boolean fixings cannot decrease this bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Add fixed-variable contributions and minimize each unfixed objective term over its Boolean domain to obtain a valid node lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(x_i\in\{0,1\}\) for every objective variable.
All node fixings are sound for the represented completions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L_N^{\mathrm{lit}}\le \min\{f(x):x\in\operatorname{Sol}(F_N)\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Literal-Wise Residual Objective Bound

children.title: PB Bound-Based Pruning
children.top_down_role: Search pruning based on incumbent values or relaxation bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: PB Bound-Based Pruning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe node elimination using a valid objective lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider minimization with incumbent value \(U\) and a valid node lower bound \(L_N\). The node \(N\) may be pruned without losing any solution strictly improving the incumbent whenever
\[L_N\ge U.\]
If objective values are integral and the search seeks a solution satisfying \(f(x)\le U-1\), the equivalent pruning test is \(L_N>U-1\). An infeasible node is also prunable, independently of objective bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A minimization node is safely pruned when its valid lower bound is no better than the incumbent, or when the node is infeasible.
assumptions_latex: \(L_N\le f(x)\) for every feasible assignment in node \(N\).
\(U\) is the value of a feasible incumbent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_N\ge U\) implies that node \(N\) contains no assignment with objective value below \(U\).

notation.meaning: valid lower bound for node N

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invariant-preserving core-guided variant using an exact hitting-set master and PB feasibility oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Solve the accumulated core master exactly, obtaining a selected violation set \(S\). Query \(H\wedge\bigwedge_{i\notin S}p_i\). If infeasible, add a returned core not hit by \(S\); if feasible with assignment \(x\), then \(f(x)\le\sum_{i\in S}w_i\), and the master lower bound implies that \(x\) is globally optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternate an exact weighted core-hitting master with PB feasibility checks until the master-selected relaxations admit a hard-feasible assignment.
assumptions_latex: The hard constraints \(H\) are feasible.
The master is solved exactly.
Every infeasible oracle response returns a valid core not hit by the current \(S\).
Weights are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{feasible query at master value }L\Rightarrow f(x)=L=\operatorname{OPT}_{H}.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Implicit-Hitting-Set Core-Guided Optimization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Checkable lower bound for possibly overlapping cores.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(y_K\ge0\) for valid cores so that \(\sum_{K\ni i}y_K\le w_i\) for every preference \(i\). Then every hard-feasible assignment has cost at least \(\sum_Ky_K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Core prices form a valid lower-bound certificate when their total charge to each preference does not exceed its weight.
assumptions_latex: Every priced core satisfies \(H\models\sum_{i\in K}z_i\ge1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{OPT}_{H}\ge\sum_{K\in\mathcal K}y_K.

notation.meaning: nonnegative packing price assigned to core K

knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Core-Packing Lower-Bound Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case iteration bound for the exact implicit-hitting-set variant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Each infeasible iteration adds a core not hit by the current violation set, so that same set cannot recur. With \(m\) preferences, at most \(2^m\) infeasible violation sets can be encountered.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The exact implicit-hitting-set variant terminates on finitely many preferences but can require exponentially many iterations.
assumptions_latex: There are \(m\) Boolean violation indicators.
Every infeasible iteration excludes its current violation set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{infeasible}}\le2^m.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Core-Enumeration Termination

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Overlapping Core Minima Cannot Be Added Naively
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Double-counting boundary for weighted core lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With one unit-weight preference incompatible with \(H\), two duplicate reported cores \(K_1=K_2=\{1\}\) each have minimum weight one, but their naive sum is two while the optimum violation cost is one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Overlapping cores can charge the same soft weight repeatedly, so their separate minimum weights cannot be summed without capacity accounting.
assumptions_latex: The sole preference is incompatible with \(H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 1+1>\operatorname{OPT}_{H}=1.
knowledge_statements.title: Overlapping Core Minima Cannot Be Added Naively

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Core object used in core-guided PB optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For hard PB constraints \(H\), preferred conditions \(p_i\), and violation indicators \(z_i\), a set \(K\) is an objective-assumption core when \(H\wedge\bigwedge_{i\in K}p_i\) is infeasible; consequently \(H\models\sum_{i\in K}z_i\ge1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An objective core is a set of preferences that cannot all hold with the hard constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(z_i=1\) exactly when preference \(p_i\) is violated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H\models\sum_{i\in K}z_i\ge1.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Assumption Core

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact master relaxation induced by accumulated valid objective cores.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For valid cores \(\mathcal K\), solve \(\min\{\sum_iw_iz_i:\sum_{i\in K}z_i\ge1\ (K\in\mathcal K),\ z_i\in\{0,1\}\}\). Its optimum is a lower bound on the original hard-constrained objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accumulated cores define a minimum-weight hitting-set master whose value lower-bounds the true optimum.
assumptions_latex: Every \(K\in\mathcal K\) is a valid objective core.
The master and original objective use the same violation indicators and weights.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{master}}(\mathcal K)\le\operatorname{OPT}_{H}.
knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Core Hitting-Set Master
Core-Guided Pseudo-Boolean Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimization driven by unsatisfiable cores of guarded objective requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent the objective as \(f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m w_i\ell_i\) with \(w_i\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), and guard each preferred condition \(\ell_i=0\) by an assumption literal. Invoke a PB solver under the active assumptions. If satisfiable, record the assignment and its cost. If unsatisfiable, extract an assumption core \(K\), derive a PB relaxation constraint requiring positive weighted violation within \(K\), update the certified lower bound by the extracted minimum core weight, split larger weights when necessary, and repeat. Stop when the lower bound equals the best feasible cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Core-guided PB optimization repeatedly relaxes an unsatisfiable set of objective assumptions, raises a certified lower bound, and stops when it meets a feasible cost.
assumptions_latex: \(w_i\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\) and all \(\ell_i\) are Boolean literals.
Each reported core is genuinely unsatisfiable with the hard PB constraints.
Every relaxation and weight split preserves the represented weighted objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At termination, \(L=U\) and the recorded assignment minimizes \(f\) subject to the hard constraints.

notation.meaning: certified lower bound and best feasible cost

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the appropriate content kind, but the description combines weighted core extraction, minimum-weight bound updates, weight splitting, and PB relaxation without specifying one exact invariant-preserving variant. Different core-guided algorithms use materially different relaxation constraints and accounting rules, so the assumptions do not by themselves make the claimed lower-bound update reliable. A direct source for the intended weighted PB variant is required.

children.title: PB–LP Hybrid Solving
children.top_down_role: Pseudo-Boolean solving integrated with linear-programming relaxations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Acceptance test for an integral optimum of a valid PB LP relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) be the feasible set of a minimization PB model and let \(P\subseteq[0,1]^n\) satisfy \(F\subseteq P\). If \(x^*\) is optimal for \(\min\{c^Tx:x\in P\}\), is integral, and an exact PB check confirms \(x^*\in F\), then \[c^Tx^*=\min_{x\in F}c^Tx.\] Integrality alone is insufficient when the relaxation omits or weakens original constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An integral LP optimum is globally optimal for the PB model only after exact PB feasibility is confirmed.
assumptions_latex: The objective is minimization of \(c^Tx\).
\(F\subseteq P\).
\(x^*\) is LP-optimal over \(P\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: LP-Dual Lower-Bound Certificate for a PB Model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer of a verified LP dual bound to the original PB minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be an LP relaxation of PB feasible set \(F\), so \(F\subseteq P\), and consider minimization of \(c^Tx\). If \(y\) is feasible for the dual of the LP over \(P\) and has dual value \(d(y)\), then \[d(y)\le \min_{x\in P}c^Tx\le \min_{x\in F}c^Tx.\] Thus a verified dual-feasible solution supplies a valid PB lower bound even when the primal LP optimum is fractional.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A verified dual-feasible LP solution gives a lower bound for the original PB minimization problem through relaxation containment.

The primal and dual use a consistent minimization formulation.
\(y\) is verified dual-feasible.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Exhaustive Branching Bound for a PB–LP Tree
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite tree-size bound for a PB–LP hybrid using exhaustive Boolean variable-fixing branches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a PB–LP minimization search on \(n\) Boolean variables. Suppose processing of every generated node terminates; each unresolved node either closes by a sound LP or PB certificate or branches into \(x_j=0\) and \(x_j=1\) for a previously unfixed variable; cuts preserve every PB-feasible assignment; and every generated node is eventually processed or soundly dominated. Then every root-to-leaf path has at most \(n\) branches, at most \(2^{n+1}-1\) tree nodes are generated, and exhaustive processing returns a globally optimal incumbent or global infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With terminating node processing and exhaustive variable fixing, a PB–LP tree has depth at most n and at most 2^(n+1)-1 nodes.
assumptions_latex: The model has \(n\) Boolean variables.
Processing of every generated node terminates.
Every branch fixes a previously unfixed variable and covers both Boolean values.
Every cut and node closure is sound.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Separation over a Fixed Cut Pool
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Termination of within-node LP reoptimization when separation draws from a fixed finite family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be a finite family of inequalities valid for the PB feasible set. At one search node, repeatedly solve the current LP and, whenever separation continues, add at least one previously absent member of \(K\) violated by the current LP solution. Then at most \(|K|\) cut-addition rounds and at most \(|K|+1\) LP solves occur before the procedure stops or exhausts \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A separation loop drawing new cuts from a fixed finite pool terminates after at most one addition round per available cut.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is finite.
Every inserted inequality is valid for the PB feasible set.
Every continuing round inserts a previously absent violated member of \(K\).
Each LP solve and separation call terminates.

If \(L\ge U\), then no point of \(F_N\) improves the incumbent, and the node may be closed.

assumptions_latex: \(F_N\subseteq P_N\).
\(U=c^T\bar x\) for an incumbent verified feasible for the original PB model.
\(L\le\min_{x\in P_N}c^Tx\).

PB–LP Hybrid Solving
knowledge_statements.scope_note: PB search combined with LP relaxation bounds and cut exchange.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given PB constraints \(F\) and a linear objective, replace \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\) by \(0\le x\le1\) to form an LP relaxation \(P\). At each search node, solve the current LP. Prune if it is infeasible or its minimization bound is at least the incumbent value. Otherwise, test the LP solution against PB constraints, add any valid separating PB or linear cuts, and reoptimize; if no useful cut is found and the solution is fractional, branch on a Boolean variable. Return the best integral PB-feasible incumbent after all nodes are resolved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A PB–LP hybrid uses LP relaxations for bounds, exchanges valid cuts, checks integral candidates in the PB model, and branches when relaxation remains fractional.
assumptions_latex: Every added cut is valid for all Boolean solutions of \(F\).
LP solves and PB feasibility checks are sound.
The branching rule exhaustively partitions every unresolved node.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Upon exhaustive termination, the returned incumbent is globally optimal, or infeasibility is certified if no incumbent exists.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited LP-based branch-and-bound section plausibly supports relaxation bounds, pruning, and branching, but it does not establish the stated PB-specific cut-exchange procedure. The algorithm also invokes a minimization bound without explicitly declaring a minimization objective at the outset. A source specifically covering PB-LP cut exchange and a precise optimization direction are required before this algorithm can be accepted.

children.title: PB–MIP Hybrid Solving

assumptions_latex: The pseudo-Boolean model has binary variables \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\), linear objective \(c^\top x\), and constraints \(Ax\ge b\).

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every exchanged inequality is valid for the original pseudo-Boolean feasible set, and every reported incumbent is feasible for that set; hence termination with matching global lower and upper bounds certifies optimality.

Dedicated pseudo-Boolean hybrid-solving source and exact algorithmic variant are still required
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic exact minimization interface between a native PB engine and a MIP branch-and-cut engine.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(F=\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:Ax\ge b\}\), initialize \(L=-\infty\), \(U=+\infty\), and no incumbent. Repeatedly let the PB component propagate constraints, derive valid pseudo-Boolean cuts, and identify branching information; translate each selected cut into a linear inequality valid on \(F\) and submit it to the MIP component. Let the MIP component solve its current relaxation or search tree, return a certified lower bound, valid cuts, or an integer incumbent, and translate these objects back to the PB component when representable. Update \(L\) and \(U\). Stop with an optimal incumbent when \(L=U\), with infeasibility when a valid global contradiction is derived, or otherwise return the incumbent and certified gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A PB-MIP hybrid exchanges valid cuts, bounds, branching information, and incumbents; equality of certified lower and upper bounds proves global optimality.

children.title: Relaxation-Exchange Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Information exchanged between PB reasoning and mathematical-programming components.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Receiver-side validity condition for importing cuts and bounds between PB and mathematical-programming components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\) be the original-model region on which a received object will be used. An imported inequality may be installed only if its translated form is valid for every original feasible point in \(Q\). An imported minimization lower bound \(L\) may be used only if \(L\le f(x)\) for every original feasible \(x\in Q\). Such an object may be treated as global only when \(Q\) is the root feasible region; otherwise its node assumptions and model mapping must be retained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Imported cuts and bounds are sound only on the original-model region covered by their translated validity and retained scope metadata.
assumptions_latex: Sender and receiver provide a defined mapping to the same original decision and objective space.
The receiver can validate the object's model, node, and assumption scope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Use on }Q\text{ is sound only if translated validity holds for all original feasible points in }Q.

notation.meaning: original-model region covered by the imported object's scope

knowledge_statements.title: Scope-Preserving Relaxation Import

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Receiver protocol for validating, installing, retaining, and invalidating exchanged objects.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each received object \(o\), the receiver checks its model version, variable mapping, optimization direction, validity certificate or trusted provenance, and scope \(Q(o)\). It rejects \(o\) if any check fails; otherwise it installs \(o\) only at nodes whose original-model regions are contained in \(Q(o)\). When backtracking, model revision, or assumption removal makes that containment false, the receiver removes or deactivates \(o\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Validate every exchanged object and keep it active only while its mapping and validity scope cover the current search region.

Node regions and active assumptions are identifiable by the receiver.

A partial assignment may be imported only as scoped assumptions or as fixings justified for every original feasible completion in its declared region.

assumptions_latex: Both components represent the same binary feasible set, possibly through different relaxations.
Every translator preserves validity in the receiving component's variable space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The interface is sound: adding any translated object cannot delete a feasible binary point of the original model, and imported bounds remain certified for the stated optimization direction.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound bidirectional exchange of relaxation information for a shared binary optimization model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) and let \(R_1,R_2\subseteq[0,1]^n\) satisfy \(F\subseteq R_1\cap R_2\). A sound relaxation-exchange interface consists of maps \(T_{12}\) and \(T_{21}\) acting on cuts, variable bounds, objective bounds, partial assignments, or incumbents. If an inequality \(a^\top x\ge\beta\) produced by component \(i\) is valid for \(F\), its translation must define an inequality valid for \(F\) in component \(j\). A translated partial assignment must preserve exactly its fixed binary values, an incumbent must remain in \(F\), and an objective bound must retain its direction and validity. Exchange may strengthen \(R_1\) or \(R_2\) but must not alter \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxation-exchange interface translates cuts, bounds, assignments, and incumbents between components without excluding any feasible binary solution or invalidating objective bounds.
