children.title: PB Constraint Normalization
children.top_down_role: Standardization of pseudo-Boolean constraint orientation and representation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence-preserving syntactic normalization of one integral PB inequality into positive-literal greater-than-or-equal form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Orient an integral PB inequality as \(\sum_i a_i\ell_i\ge b\). For each \(a_i<0\), write \(a_i\ell_i=(-a_i)(1-\ell_i)+a_i\), thereby replacing the term by a positive coefficient on the complementary literal and replacing \(b\) by \(b-a_i\). Collect repeated literals. If both \(x\) and \(1-x\) have coefficients \(\alpha,\beta\), subtract \(m=\min\{\alpha,\beta\}\) from both and replace \(b\) by \(b-m\). Delete zeros. If \(g\) is the gcd of the remaining coefficients, divide them by \(g\) and replace \(b\) by \(\lceil b/g\rceil\). Constant outcomes are tautological when the normalized threshold is nonpositive and infeasible when it exceeds the sum of all coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalize orientation and signs, collect repeated and complementary literals, delete zeros, and divide coefficient gcds using ceiling on the threshold.
assumptions_latex: a_i,b\in\mathbb Z
\ell_i\in\{x_j,1-x_j\}
\bar x_j=1-x_j
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Sat}(P)=\operatorname{Sat}(\operatorname{Norm}(P)).

notation.meaning: Greatest common divisor of the remaining nonzero coefficients
Constant removable from a complementary-literal pair

review_flags: Normalization fixes cleaned syntax but does not select among all possible canonical representatives.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact PB Inequality Normalization

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Termination and Bit Complexity of Normalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complexity under sorted or hash-based literal collection and binary integer encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(m\) input terms of maximum bit length \(L\), sign conversion and collection require one finite pass plus literal aggregation; sorting gives \(O(m\log m)\) identifier comparisons, while hashing gives expected \(O(m)\) dictionary operations. Integer additions and gcd computations are polynomial in \(m\) and \(L\), and every rewrite phase strictly reduces the number of unprocessed terms or complementary pairs, so normalization terminates in polynomial bit time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalization terminates and is polynomial in the number of terms and the binary lengths of its integers.
assumptions_latex: \text{Coefficients and thresholds use binary encoding.}
\text{Exact integer arithmetic is used.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_{\mathrm{Norm}}\in\operatorname{poly}(m,L).
review_flags: Exact constants depend on the integer-arithmetic and dictionary implementations.
knowledge_statements.title: Termination and Bit Complexity of Normalization

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Floor Division Does Not Preserve a PB Threshold
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp failure boundary for coefficient-gcd scaling with a nondivisible threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(2x\ge1\), coefficient division by \(2\) with floor rounding gives \(x\ge0\), which accepts \(x=0\). Ceiling gives the equivalent inequality \(x\ge1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rounding a divided threshold downward can turn a nontrivial PB constraint into a tautology.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 2x\ge1\not\equiv x\ge\lfloor1/2\rfloor,\qquad 2x\ge1\equiv x\ge\lceil1/2\rceil.
knowledge_statements.title: Floor Division Does Not Preserve a PB Threshold

assumptions_latex: The input is an integer pseudo-Boolean inequality \(\sum_i a_i\ell_i\ge b\), where each \(\ell_i\) is a Boolean literal.
Complementary literals satisfy \(\bar x_i=1-x_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output inequality has the same satisfying Boolean assignments as the input and has nonnegative coefficients, distinct literals, and a consistently scaled integer right-hand side.

notation.meaning: Boolean literal, either a variable or its complement
Greatest common divisor of nonzero coefficients and right-hand side

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: literal complementation, coefficient collection, sign removal, and common-factor division are exact integer PB transformations
A dedicated pseudo-Boolean preprocessing reference is required
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact syntactic normalization of one integer pseudo-Boolean inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: To normalize \(\sum_i a_i\ell_i\ge b\), first replace every term with \(a_i<0\) by \((-a_i)(1-\ell_i)\) and increase the right-hand side by \(-a_i\). Expand constants, combine repeated occurrences of each literal, and use \(x_j+(1-x_j)=1\) to eliminate simultaneous occurrences of complementary literals by subtracting their common coefficient and adjusting the right-hand side. Delete zero coefficients. If the remaining coefficients and right-hand side possess a positive common divisor \(g\), divide them by \(g\); if division of the right-hand side is not exact after a coefficient-only common divisor is chosen, replace it by the appropriate ceiling. Return the resulting equivalent inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalization removes negative coefficients, combines literals, eliminates complementary pairs, and divides common factors while preserving exactly the satisfying Boolean assignments.
knowledge_statements.title: PB Constraint Normalization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits PB constraint normalization and its transformations are mathematically plausible, but no PB-specific source fixes the normalization convention, complementary-literal reduction, or rounded common-factor division rule.

children.title: PB Constraint Canonicalization
children.top_down_role: Selection of canonical forms among equivalent constraint representations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Syntactic Rules Need Not Canonicalize Semantic Threshold Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary separating deterministic syntactic normalization from semantic canonicalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The inequalities \(x+y+z\ge2\) and \(2x+2y+z\ge3\) define the same Boolean function: each holds exactly when at least two of \(x,y,z\) are true. Both have positive coefficients, primitive coefficient gcd, fixed \(\ge\) orientation, and coefficients no larger than their thresholds, yet their ordered coefficient-threshold tuples differ. Therefore these local syntactic rules do not select one representative for every semantic equivalence class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distinct primitive, ordered, saturated inequalities can represent the same threshold function, so routine normalization is not complete semantic canonicalization.
assumptions_latex: x\prec y\prec z
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Sat}(x+y+z\ge2)=\operatorname{Sat}(2x+2y+z\ge3),\qquad(1,1,1;2)\ne(2,2,1;3).
knowledge_statements.title: Local Syntactic Rules Need Not Canonicalize Semantic Threshold Functions

assumptions_latex: The constraint has already been normalized to \(\sum_{i=1}^m a_i\ell_i\ge b\) with positive integer coefficients.
A fixed total order on literals is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The canonical representative is uniquely determined by the normalized inequality and chosen literal order, and it defines the same Boolean satisfying set.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: canonicalization requires an explicit ordering and deterministic exact transformations to select one representative
Different PB solvers use different canonical conventions; a source is needed to fix the intended regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A deterministic canonical representative after exact PB normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a normalized inequality \(\sum_{i=1}^m a_i\ell_i\ge b\), order the distinct literals by a fixed total order \(\prec\), remove coefficients that are zero, divide all coefficients and \(b\) by their greatest common divisor when exact, and orient the relation as \(\ge\). In the positive-coefficient regime, replace each coefficient by \(\min\{a_i,b\}\), since values above \(b\) are indistinguishable on Boolean assignments. The ordered tuple \(C=(a_1,\ldots,a_m;b)\), together with its ordered literal list, is the canonical representative. Two constraints are canonically identical under this convention exactly when these ordered data coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Canonicalization applies deterministic ordering, scaling, orientation, and coefficient saturation so syntactically different PB inequalities receive one comparable representative.
knowledge_statements.title: PB Constraint Canonicalization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role fits the canonicalization leaf, but canonical representatives depend on the selected transformation order and convention. No cited source establishes this particular ordering, scaling, orientation, and saturation regime.

children.title: Canonical-Form Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes distinguished by the chosen canonical representation.

assumptions_latex: Constraints are finite integer inequalities over Boolean literals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each regime has a stated invariant, and conversions using the displayed identities preserve the satisfying Boolean assignments.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: PB inequalities admit equivalent signed-variable, nonnegative-literal, threshold, and equality-oriented representations
The taxonomy's intended list of canonical regimes is ambiguous without a PB-specific source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Common exact representation regimes for integer pseudo-Boolean constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A pseudo-Boolean constraint may be maintained in one of four exact regimes: signed-variable form \(\sum_i a_i x_i\ge b\) with \(a_i\in\mathbb Z\); positive-literal form \(\sum_i a_i\ell_i\ge b\) with \(a_i>0\); upper-bound form \(\sum_i a_i\ell_i\le b\); or equality form \(\sum_i a_i\ell_i=b\). Signed-variable and positive-literal forms are interconverted using \(x_i=1-(1-x_i)\). An upper-bound inequality becomes a lower-bound inequality by multiplying both sides by \(-1\) and then normalizing literals. An equality denotes the conjunction of its lower- and upper-bound inequalities. A canonical-form regime fixes one such orientation, a literal order, and a primitive scaling convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Canonical-form regimes fix orientation, literal polarity, ordering, and scaling; standard algebraic identities convert among regimes without changing Boolean solutions.
knowledge_statements.title: Canonical-Form Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role fits the leaf, but the proposed four-regime classification is convention-dependent, and equality form is not a general single-constraint replacement for an inequality without additional structure. A PB-specific source is needed to establish the intended classification.

children.title: PB Constraint Dominance
children.top_down_role: Dominance relations among pseudo-Boolean constraints.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order-theoretic structure of semantic PB dominance for a fixed background formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(B\) and define \(C_1\succeq_B C_2\) by \(B\land C_1\models C_2\). Then \(\succeq_B\) is reflexive and transitive. Mutual dominance is an equivalence relation, and the induced relation on equivalence classes is a partial order. Strict dominance, defined by \(C_1\succeq_B C_2\) and not \(C_2\succeq_B C_1\), is irreflexive and transitive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed background, semantic dominance forms a preorder; quotienting mutually dominant constraints gives a partial order.
assumptions_latex: B\text{ is fixed for every comparison}
B,C_1,C_2,C_3\text{ share one Boolean assignment universe}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C_1\succeq_B C_2\land C_2\succeq_B C_3\Longrightarrow C_1\succeq_B C_3.

notation.meaning: Semantic dominance relative to background B

knowledge_statements.title: Background-Relative Dominance Is a Preorder
PB Constraint Dominance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic dominance relative to an optional background PB formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\), \(C_1\), and \(C_2\) be pseudo-Boolean formulas over the same Boolean variables. Constraint \(C_1\) dominates \(C_2\) relative to \(B\) when \[\operatorname{Sat}(B)\cap\operatorname{Sat}(C_1)\subseteq\operatorname{Sat}(B)\cap\operatorname{Sat}(C_2).\] Dominance is strict when this inclusion is proper. Unconditional dominance is obtained when \(B\) is the identically true formula. Mutual dominance relative to \(B\) is equality of the two displayed intersections.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One PB constraint dominates another relative to a background formula when every background-feasible assignment satisfying the first also satisfies the second; dominance is strict when the reverse implication fails within that background.
assumptions_latex: Both constraints are interpreted over the same Boolean variables.
Dominance is evaluated relative to an optional background formula \(B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(C_1\) dominates \(C_2\) relative to \(B\), then replacing \(C_2\) by \(C_1\) within the background cannot introduce an assignment feasible for \(B\land C_2\), although it may remove assignments unless relative equivalence also holds.

notation.meaning: Sets of Boolean assignments satisfying the indicated formulas

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: semantic dominance is implication relative to a background constraint set
A PB-specific source is required because some literature uses dominance for narrower coefficientwise relations

children.title: PB Constraint Subsumption
children.top_down_role: Subsumption relations used to remove weaker constraints.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coefficientwise Subsumption Is Not Necessary for Semantic Implication
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary of the proposed sufficient coefficientwise comparison.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_1:2x+y\ge2\) and \(C_2:x+y\ge1\). Every Boolean assignment satisfying \(C_1\) has \(x=1\), hence satisfies \(C_2\); therefore \(C_1\models C_2\). Nevertheless \(a_{1x}\le a_{2x}\) fails because \(2\nleq1\). Thus the coefficientwise condition is sufficient at most, not necessary for semantic implication.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A PB constraint can imply another even when the coefficientwise subsumption comparison fails.
assumptions_latex: C_1,C_2\text{ use the same ordered positive-literal universe}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C_1\models C_2\quad\text{but}\quad a_{1x}>a_{2x}.
knowledge_statements.title: Coefficientwise Subsumption Is Not Necessary for Semantic Implication

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cost of an Aligned Coefficientwise Subsumption Check
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sparse and dense checking costs after the subsumption convention and literal universe are fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For sorted sparse lists with \(m_1,m_2\) nonzero coefficients and maximum integer bit length \(L\), alignment and comparison take \(O(m_1+m_2)\) identifier comparisons and \(O((m_1+m_2)L)\) bit operations, plus one threshold comparison. A dense representation over \(n\) literals takes \(O(nL)\) bit operations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sorted sparse constraints admit a linear merge-and-compare subsumption check.
assumptions_latex: \text{Sparse lists are sorted by a common literal identifier.}
\text{Integers use binary encoding.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_{\mathrm{sparse}}=O((m_1+m_2)L),\qquad T_{\mathrm{dense}}=O(nL).
knowledge_statements.title: Cost of an Aligned Coefficientwise Subsumption Check

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A fixed syntactic subsumption convention for normalized positive-literal PB inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_1:\sum_i a_{1i}\ell_i\ge b_1\) and \(C_2:\sum_i a_{2i}\ell_i\ge b_2\) share an ordered literal universe, with missing coefficients equal to zero. Define coefficientwise subsumption by \(a_{1i}\le a_{2i}\) for every \(i\) and \(b_1\ge b_2\). Then \(C_1\models C_2\), so \(C_2\) may be removed from any conjunction containing \(C_1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint with no larger coefficients and no smaller threshold syntactically subsumes the weaker aligned constraint.
assumptions_latex: a_{ki}\ge0
\text{Both constraints use the same literal meanings.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\forall i\ a_{1i}\le a_{2i})\land b_1\ge b_2\Longrightarrow C_1\models C_2.
review_flags: This record explicitly fixes one syntactic convention; semantic implication is broader.
knowledge_statements.title: Coefficientwise PB Subsumption
PB Constraint Subsumption
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sufficient syntactic subsumption test for normalized positive-literal PB inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_1:\sum_i a_{1i}\ell_i\ge b_1\) and \(C_2:\sum_i a_{2i}\ell_i\ge b_2\), where all coefficients are nonnegative and the same literal \(\ell_i\) occupies position \(i\), with missing literals assigned coefficient zero. Under the coefficientwise convention, \(C_1\) syntactically subsumes \(C_2\) if \[a_{1i}\le a_{2i}\quad\text{for every }i,\qquad b_1\ge b_2.\] These conditions imply \(C_1\models C_2\), so \(C_2\) is redundant in any conjunction that already contains \(C_1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under this coefficientwise convention, a normalized PB inequality subsumes another when every coefficient of the first is no larger and its threshold is no smaller; this guarantees implication and makes the second constraint removable when both occur in a conjunction.
assumptions_latex: Constraints are in positive-literal form over a common ordered literal universe.
Missing literals are assigned coefficient zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(a_{1i}\le a_{2i}\) for every \(i\) and \(b_1\ge b_2\), then \(C_1\models C_2\), and \(C_2\) is removable from any conjunction already containing \(C_1\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: coefficientwise comparison supplies a directly checkable sufficient implication condition for positive-literal threshold inequalities
A PB-specific source is required to confirm that this sufficient test is called syntactic subsumption

children.title: PB Redundancy Detection
children.top_down_role: Identification of constraints dispensable from the represented feasible region.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Complexity of General PB Redundancy Detection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case complexity of deciding redundancy of one PB constraint relative to an arbitrary finite PB background.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a finite conjunction \(B\) of pseudo-Boolean constraints and a PB constraint \(C\), deciding whether \(B\models C\) is coNP-complete under polynomial-time many-one reductions for standard binary encodings of integral coefficients. A Boolean assignment satisfying \(B\land\neg C\) is a polynomially checkable certificate of nonredundancy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: General PB redundancy detection is coNP-complete, while a violating Boolean assignment certifies nonredundancy.
assumptions_latex: B\text{ and }C\text{ are explicitly encoded using binary integral coefficients}
\text{All variables are Boolean}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \textsc{PB-Redundancy}=\{(B,C):B\models C\}\text{ is coNP-complete}.
knowledge_statements.title: Complexity of General PB Redundancy Detection

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Checkable Certificates for PB Redundancy and Nonredundancy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proof-system-independent finite certificates for the semantic redundancy decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A satisfying Boolean assignment of \(B\land\neg C\) certifies nonredundancy. A proof-system-independent redundancy certificate may enumerate all \(2^n\) assignments to the variables of \(B\cup\{C\}\) and, for each assignment, identify either a falsified constraint of \(B\) or satisfaction of \(C\). Checking every listed assignment and verifying complete, duplicate-free enumeration certifies \(B\models C\). The redundancy certificate may be exponential but is independently checkable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A violating assignment certifies nonredundancy; exhaustive assignment coverage gives a precise, independently checkable redundancy certificate without assuming a particular PB proof calculus.
assumptions_latex: n\text{ is the number of distinct Boolean variables.}
\text{Every PB evaluation uses exact integer arithmetic.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The stated certificates respectively imply }B\not\models C\text{ and }B\models C.
review_flags: The exhaustive redundancy certificate is not claimed to be compact.
knowledge_statements.title: Checkable Certificates for PB Redundancy and Nonredundancy

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact redundancy of one PB constraint relative to a finite PB background.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A constraint \(C\) is redundant relative to \(B\) exactly when \(\operatorname{Sat}(B)=\operatorname{Sat}(B\land C)\), equivalently \(B\models C\), equivalently \(B\land\neg C\) is unsatisfiable. For integral \(C:\sum_i a_i\ell_i\ge b\), \(\neg C\) is \(\sum_i a_i\ell_i\le b-1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A PB constraint is redundant exactly when the remaining formula entails it, or equivalently when the remaining formula together with its discrete negation is infeasible.
assumptions_latex: \text{All variables are Boolean.}
a_i,b\in\mathbb Z
B\text{ is a finite PB conjunction.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Sat}(B)=\operatorname{Sat}(B\land C)\iff B\models C\iff B\land\neg C\text{ is unsatisfiable}.
knowledge_statements.title: Semantic PB Redundancy

assumptions_latex: The formula \(B\) and candidate constraint \(C\) use finitely many Boolean variables.
Satisfiability of pseudo-Boolean formulas is interpreted over \(\{0,1\}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Unsatisfiability of \(B\land\neg C\) is a verifiable semantic certificate that adding or deleting \(C\) does not change the feasible assignments of \(B\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: redundancy is semantic entailment, equivalently unsatisfiability after conjoining the negation
A source is required for the intended proof-log or checker format
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic redundancy and its unsatisfiability certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A pseudo-Boolean constraint \(C\) is redundant with respect to a background formula \(B\) exactly when \[\operatorname{Sat}(B)=\operatorname{Sat}(B\land C),\] equivalently when \(B\models C\). Thus redundancy detection reduces to deciding whether \(B\land
eg C\) is unsatisfiable. For an integer inequality \(C:\sum_i a_i\ell_i\ge b\), its Boolean negation is \(
eg C:\sum_i a_i\ell_i\le b-1\). Any independently checkable derivation of contradiction from \(B\land
eg C\) certifies redundancy; a satisfying assignment of that formula certifies nonredundancy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A PB constraint is redundant exactly when the remaining formula entails it; an unsatisfiability derivation for the formula plus its negation certifies redundancy.
knowledge_statements.title: PB Redundancy Detection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role fits redundancy detection, and entailment via unsatisfiability of the negated constraint is mathematically standard. No source supports the intended PB proof system or independently checkable contradiction format.

children.title: Preprocessing Relation Hierarchy
children.top_down_role: Structural relationships among dominance, subsumption, and redundancy.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Contextual Redundancy Without a Single-Constraint Witness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict separation between joint semantic redundancy and implication by one PB constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_1:x+y\ge1\), \(C_2:(1-x)+z\ge1\), and \(C_3:y+z\ge1\) over \(x,y,z\in\{0,1\}\). Then \(C_1\land C_2\models C_3\), but \(C_1\not\models C_3\) and \(C_2\not\models C_3\). Thus \(C_3\) is redundant in \(C_1\land C_2\land C_3\) without a single-constraint implication witness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two PB constraints may jointly make a third redundant even though neither alone implies it.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C_1\land C_2\models C_3,\quad C_1\not\models C_3,\quad C_2\not\models C_3.
review_flags: This establishes joint redundancy without a single implication witness but does not resolve the field-dependent meaning or direction of PB dominance and subsumption.
knowledge_statements.title: Contextual Redundancy Without a Single-Constraint Witness

assumptions_latex: All relations compare PB constraints over a common Boolean domain.
Subsumption denotes a sound syntactic sufficient test for implication.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Subsumption implies dominance, dominance of \(C_1\) over \(C_2\) makes \(C_2\) redundant in any conjunction containing \(C_1\), and semantic redundancy need imply neither syntactic subsumption nor single-constraint dominance.

notation.meaning: Semantic dominance relative to background formula

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: syntactic subsumption is a sufficient implication test, while dominance and redundancy are progressively more contextual semantic relations
A PB preprocessing reference is required to confirm the intended naming and strictness of the hierarchy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical ordering of subsumption, dominance, and contextual redundancy tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For PB constraints \(C_1,C_2\) and background formula \(B\), a sound syntactic subsumption relation satisfies \[C_1\preceq_s C_2\;\Longrightarrow\; C_1\models C_2\;\Longrightarrow\; B\land C_1\models C_2.\] Hence subsumption is a sufficient test for unconditional dominance, and unconditional dominance is sufficient for dominance relative to every \(B\). If \(C_1\) occurs in \(B\) and dominates \(C_2\), then \(C_2\) is redundant in \(B\land C_2\). Conversely, \(B\models C_2\) may result from several constraints jointly, so redundancy need not be witnessed by a single dominating constraint or by syntactic subsumption.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Syntactic subsumption implies semantic dominance, which can establish redundancy; contextual redundancy may instead arise jointly and need not have either simpler witness.
knowledge_statements.title: Preprocessing Relation Hierarchy

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property role fits the hierarchy leaf and the logical ordering is plausible under the record's definitions, but those definitions and the strictness of the named hierarchy require a PB preprocessing source.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Davis–Putnam Elimination as a Clausal PB Special Case
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact elimination of one Boolean variable from CNF represented by clausal PB inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write \(F=R\land\bigwedge_{i=1}^{p}(x\lor A_i)\land\bigwedge_{j=1}^{q}(\neg x\lor B_j)\), where \(R,A_i,B_j\) contain no \(x\). Delete the clauses containing \(x\) or \(\neg x\) and insert every non-tautological resolvent \(A_i\lor B_j\): \[\operatorname{DP}_x(F)=R\land\bigwedge_{i=1}^{p}\bigwedge_{j=1}^{q}(A_i\lor B_j).\] Then \(\operatorname{DP}_x(F)\equiv\exists x\,F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Resolving every positive occurrence against every negative occurrence and deleting the parents exactly projects a CNF over the remaining variables.
assumptions_latex: F\text{ is a finite CNF.}
A_i\text{ and }B_j\text{ contain no }x.
\text{Tautological resolvents are discarded.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{DP}_x(F)\equiv\exists x\,F.

notation.meaning: Clauses not containing the eliminated variable.
A resolvent after removing complementary occurrences of the eliminated variable.

review_flags: This is the clausal special case, not a complete account of elimination directly on general PB inequalities.
knowledge_statements.title: Davis–Putnam Elimination as a Clausal PB Special Case

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Output-size boundary for explicit resolution-based Boolean elimination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(x\) occurs positively in \(p\) clauses and negatively in \(q\) clauses, one Davis–Putnam step creates at most \(pq\) candidate resolvents before tautology and subsumption deletion. Repeated exact elimination can produce exponentially many explicitly stored clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One step forms a Cartesian product of positive and negative occurrences, and repeated elimination can have exponential output size.
assumptions_latex: \text{All candidate resolvents are explicitly materialized before deletion.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{cand}}\le pq,\qquad N_{\mathrm{output}}\text{ may be exponential under repeated elimination.}

notation.meaning: Counts of positive- and negative-occurrence clauses for the eliminated variable.

knowledge_statements.title: Elimination Fill-In and Size Blowup

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resolvent-free Davis–Putnam special case.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(F=R\land\bigwedge_i(x\lor A_i)\) and \(x\) occurs nowhere negatively, then \(\exists x\,F\equiv R\); symmetrically, if all occurrences are negative, set \(x=0\) and delete their clauses. No resolvents are generated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pure-polarity variable can be eliminated by satisfying and deleting all clauses containing it.
assumptions_latex: F\text{ is finite CNF.}
x\text{ occurs in at most one polarity.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists x\,F\equiv R.

notation.meaning: Clauses not containing the eliminated variable

knowledge_statements.title: Pure-Polarity Variable Elimination in CNF

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Parity Projection Forces Exponential CNF Size
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit family witnessing exponential output under elimination into CNF.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Encode the parity relation \(z=x_1\oplus\cdots\oplus x_n\) by a linear chain of auxiliary XOR variables, using a constant number of CNF clauses per XOR, and fix \(z=1\). The extended CNF has \(O(n)\) clauses and auxiliaries. Eliminating all auxiliaries projects to odd parity on \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\). Every equivalent CNF over only the \(x_i\) requires one length-\(n\) clause excluding each even-parity assignment, hence at least \(2^{n-1}\) clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear-size extended parity encoding can project to a relation requiring exponentially many clauses over the retained variables.
assumptions_latex: n\ge2
\text{The output is required to be CNF over retained variables only.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |F_{\mathrm{extended}}|=O(n),\qquad |\exists\text{ auxiliaries }F|_{\mathrm{CNF}}\ge2^{n-1}.
knowledge_statements.title: Parity Projection Forces Exponential CNF Size

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Objective-Dependent Elimination Requires a Value Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimization-preserving elimination when the removed variable affects cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(h(y)=\min\{f(x,y):x\in\{0,1\},F(x,y)\}\), with \(h(y)=+\infty\) when no extension exists. Then \(\min_{x,y:F(x,y)}f(x,y)=\min_y h(y)\). Feasibility projection alone preserves objective values without additional information when the objective is constant across feasible extensions, in particular when \(f(x,y)=g(y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the eliminated variable affects cost, exact elimination must retain the best extension cost as a value function.
assumptions_latex: F\text{ has a finite Boolean domain.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_{x,y:F(x,y)}f(x,y)=\min_y h(y).

notation.meaning: Best feasible extension cost for retained assignment y

knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Dependent Elimination Requires a Value Function

knowledge_statements.scope_note: General exact elimination of one Boolean variable from an arbitrary PB formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any PB formula \(F(x,y)\), exact elimination of \(x\) is \(G(y)=\exists x\,F(x,y)\equiv F(0,y)\lor F(1,y)\). Thus \(G(\hat y)\) holds exactly when \(\hat y\) has a feasible extension. The cofactor disjunction is always exact, although converting it back to a conjunction of PB inequalities can require exponential size.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating a Boolean variable is existential projection, equivalently the disjunction of its zero and one cofactors.
assumptions_latex: F\text{ is finite.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G(y)\equiv\exists x\,F(x,y)\equiv F(0,y)\lor F(1,y).
review_flags: Exact projection need not remain compact in conjunctive PB syntax.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Boolean Cofactor Elimination

assumptions_latex: The PB formula \(F(x,y)\) has finitely many Boolean variables.
Elimination is required to preserve feasibility of every assignment to the retained variables \(y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The eliminated formula is the exact projection of \(F\) onto \(y\): it preserves feasibility and, with an objective independent of \(x\), preserves the optimal value.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Boolean variable elimination is existential quantification and equals disjunction of the two cofactors
A PB-specific source is required for concrete elimination rules and size controls
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact elimination as existential projection of a Boolean PB formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a pseudo-Boolean formula \(F(x,y)\) with \(x\in\{0,1\}\), exact elimination of \(x\) produces \[G(y)\;\equiv\;\exists x\in\{0,1\}\,F(x,y)\;\equiv\;F(0,y)\lor F(1,y).\] Consequently, for every retained assignment \(\hat y\), \(G(\hat y)\) holds if and only if at least one extension \((x,\hat y)\) satisfies \(F\). If an objective \(f(y)\) does not involve \(x\), then minimizing \(f(y)\) subject to \(G(y)\) has the same feasible objective values and optimum as minimizing \(f(y)\) subject to \(F(x,y)\). Repeated elimination applies this projection successively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating a binary variable existentially projects the PB formula, equivalently disjoining its zero and one cofactors, while preserving extendable retained assignments.
knowledge_statements.title: Variable Elimination

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Existential projection is a suitable representation of exact variable elimination and the objective-preservation qualification is correct, but no PB-specific citation supplies concrete elimination rules or establishes this as the intended terminal content.

children.title: PB Coefficient Reduction
children.top_down_role: Reduction of coefficient magnitude or representation cost.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: GCD Normalization of a PB Threshold
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact common-divisor reduction for an integer pseudo-Boolean threshold inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[\sum_{i=1}^n a_i\ell_i\ge b,\] where \(a_i,b\in\mathbb Z\), \(\ell_i\in\{0,1\}\), and \(g=\gcd(|a_1|,\ldots,|a_n|)>0\). The inequality is equivalent over Boolean assignments to \[\sum_{i=1}^n (a_i/g)\ell_i\ge \left\lceil b/g\right\rceil.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Divide all coefficients by their gcd and round the threshold upward to preserve exactly the same Boolean solutions.
assumptions_latex: All coefficients and the threshold are integers.
At least one coefficient is nonzero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \left(\sum_i a_i\ell_i\ge b\right)\Longleftrightarrow\left(\sum_i \frac{a_i}{g}\ell_i\ge\left\lceil\frac bg\right\rceil\right).
knowledge_statements.title: GCD Normalization of a PB Threshold

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Raw Threshold Capping Is Unsafe with Signed Coefficients
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary requiring normalization to nonnegative literals before elementary saturation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(C:5x-4y\ge1\), naively replacing the positive coefficient \(5\) by the threshold \(1\) gives \(C':x-4y\ge1\). The Boolean assignment \((x,y)=(1,1)\) satisfies \(C\) but violates \(C'\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Threshold capping is not sound on an unnormalized row containing signed coefficients.
assumptions_latex: The raw signed representation is capped without conversion to a nonnegative-literal threshold form.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 5x-4y\ge1\not\equiv x-4y\ge1.
knowledge_statements.title: Raw Threshold Capping Is Unsafe with Signed Coefficients

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tautology and contradiction tests for a normalized nonnegative PB row.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(C:\sum_i a_i\ell_i\ge b\) with \(a_i\ge0\), let \(A=\sum_i a_i\). If \(b\le0\), then \(C\) is tautological. If \(b>A\), then \(C\) is contradictory. Only \(0<b\le A\) requires positive-threshold coefficient reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Discharge nonpositive-threshold rows as tautologies and thresholds above total activity as contradictions before reducing coefficients.
assumptions_latex: \(a_i\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: b\le0\Rightarrow C\text{ tautological},\qquad b>\sum_i a_i\Rightarrow C\text{ contradictory}.
knowledge_statements.title: Row-Status Tests Before Positive-Threshold Reduction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conversion of a signed Boolean linear inequality into nonnegative-literal threshold form before coefficient reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition \(\sum_i c_i x_i\ge b\) into \(P=\{i:c_i\ge0\}\) and \(N=\{i:c_i<0\}\), and put \(a_i=-c_i>0\) for \(i\in N\). Over Boolean variables the row is equivalent to \[\sum_{i\in P}c_i x_i+\sum_{i\in N}a_i(1-x_i)\ge b+\sum_{i\in N}a_i,\] which has nonnegative literal coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace each negative variable coefficient by a positive coefficient on its complemented literal and shift the threshold accordingly.
assumptions_latex: \(c_i,b\in\mathbb Z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_i c_i x_i\ge b\Longleftrightarrow\sum_{i\in P}c_i x_i+\sum_{i\in N}(-c_i)(1-x_i)\ge b+\sum_{i\in N}(-c_i).

notation.meaning: indices of nonnegative and negative original coefficients

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Normalization to Nonnegative Literals

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bit Complexity of a Fixed PB Numerical-Reduction Pass
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arithmetic cost of normalization, row-status evaluation, coefficient capping, and gcd normalization on one PB row.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a PB row contain \(m\) terms and have total input bit length \(S\). A pass that complements negative coefficients, aggregates exact threshold shifts, computes total activity, caps coefficients at a positive normalized threshold, computes their gcd, and performs directed threshold division uses polynomially many bit operations in \(S\). After capping, every surviving coefficient is at most the positive threshold, and subsequent gcd division cannot increase it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One fixed numerical coefficient-reduction pass is polynomial in the row's binary length and does not enlarge coefficients after threshold capping.
assumptions_latex: Integers use exact binary encoding.
The stated finite sequence is applied without structural search.
Standard polynomial-time integer addition, comparison, gcd, and division algorithms are used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_{\mathrm{pass}}=\operatorname{poly}(S),\qquad a_i^{\mathrm{out}}\le b_{\mathrm{positive}}.

notation.meaning: total binary encoding length of the input row

knowledge_statements.title: Bit Complexity of a Fixed PB Numerical-Reduction Pass

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact coefficient reduction for a normalized nonnegative at-most pseudo-Boolean inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C:\sum_{i=1}^n a_i\ell_i\le b\), where \(a_i\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\), \(b\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\), and \(\ell_i\in\{0,1\}\). Define \(a_i'=\min\{a_i,b+1\}\). Then \[\sum_i a_i\ell_i\le b\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\sum_i a_i'\ell_i\le b.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a nonnegative at-most PB inequality, every coefficient exceeding the bound may be replaced by b+1 without changing the satisfying Boolean assignments.
assumptions_latex: a_i\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}.
b\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_i a_i\ell_i\le b\iff\sum_i\min\{a_i,b+1\}\ell_i\le b.
knowledge_statements.title: Upper-Bound Coefficient Truncation

assumptions_latex: The constraint is \(\sum_i a_i\ell_i\ge b\) with \(a_i\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\), \(b>0\), and Boolean literals \(\ell_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Replacing every \(a_i\) by \(a_i'=\min\{a_i,b\}\) yields an equivalent inequality and never increases any coefficient.

A dedicated PB preprocessing citation is required
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact coefficient saturation for positive-literal threshold inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C:\sum_i a_i\ell_i\ge b\), where \(a_i\ge0\), \(b>0\), and \(\ell_i\in\{0,1\}\). Define \(a_i'=\min\{a_i,b\}\) and \(C':\sum_i a_i'\ell_i\ge b\). Then \(C\) and \(C'\) have identical satisfying Boolean assignments. In particular, if some selected literal has \(a_i\ge b\), that literal alone reaches the threshold both before and after reduction; if no such literal is selected, every selected term is unchanged. Thus coefficient saturation is an exact reduction, not merely a relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a nonnegative PB threshold inequality, every coefficient may be capped at the threshold without changing any satisfying Boolean assignment.

children.title: PB Constraint Simplification
children.top_down_role: Simplification of constraint structure while preserving intended semantics.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Literal propagation after fixed assignments have been substituted into a normalized positive-coefficient PB inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\sum_{i\in U}a_i\ell_i\ge b'\), with \(a_i>0\), and let \(W=\sum_{i\in U}a_i\). If \(W-a_j<b'\), every satisfying residual assignment has \(\ell_j=1\). Substituting \(\ell_j=1\) and replacing \(b'\) by \(b'-a_j\) preserves exactly the satisfying assignments on the remaining literals. Repetition to a fixpoint is sound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A residual literal is forced true when all other unfixed literals together cannot reach the threshold.
assumptions_latex: a_i>0\quad(i\in U)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: W-a_j<b'\Longrightarrow\left(\sum_{i\in U}a_i\ell_i\ge b'\Rightarrow\ell_j=1\right).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact simplification of one normalized positive-coefficient PB inequality under a partial assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P:\sum_i a_i\ell_i\ge b\), delete terms fixed false and subtract from \(b\) every coefficient whose literal is fixed true. Writing the residual as \(\sum_{i\in U}a_i\ell_i\ge b'\) and \(W=\sum_{i\in U}a_i\), return tautology if \(b'\le0\), contradiction if \(W<b'\), and otherwise force every \(\ell_j\) satisfying \(W-a_j<b'\). These operations preserve exactly the extensions consistent with the partial assignment and can be repeated after newly fixed literals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Substitute fixed literals, adjust the threshold, detect tautology or contradiction, and force any literal whose omission makes the residual threshold unattainable.
assumptions_latex: a_i>0

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{j\in U:W-a_j<b'\}\). After substituting any \(j\in F\), the test for \(k\ne j\) becomes \((W-a_j)-a_k<b'-a_j\), which is equivalent to \(W-a_k<b'\). Hence all currently forced literals can be found in one scan and substituted in any order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All literals forced by the residual-slack test can be found simultaneously, and their substitution order is immaterial.
assumptions_latex: a_i>0

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(\sum_i a_i\ell_i\ge b\), substitute fixed literals, delete terms fixed to zero, and set \(b'=b-\sum_{i:\ell_i=1}a_i\). Let \(U\) index the unfixed literals and let \(W=\sum_{i\in U}a_i\). If \(b'\le0\), output the tautology; if \(W<b'\), output contradiction. Otherwise replace each residual coefficient by \(\min\{a_i,b'\}\), combine repeated or complementary literals by exact normalization, and delete zeros. Output the resulting inequality over \(U\). Every step preserves precisely the extensions consistent with the supplied fixed assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Simplification substitutes fixed literals, adjusts the threshold, detects tautology or contradiction, and saturates residual coefficients while preserving consistent solutions.

children.title: Reduction-Simplification Interaction
children.top_down_role: Effects of coefficient reduction on subsequent structural simplification.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Threshold Reduction Can Enable New Coefficient Saturation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Syntactic interaction between substitution and threshold-dependent coefficient saturation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P:\sum_i a_i\ell_i\ge b\) with positive coefficients, saturation replaces \(a_i\) by \(\min\{a_i,b\}\). If fixed true literals contribute weight \(t\), substitution gives residual threshold \(b'=b-t\), so saturation must be reconsidered against \(b'\). For example, \(5x+4y\ge6\) with \(y=1\) becomes \(5x\ge2\), then \(2x\ge2\). Each transformation is equivalent under the partial assignment, but the syntactic results of the two stages need not commute.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Substitution can lower the threshold and expose additional coefficient saturation, so reduction may need to be repeated after simplification.
assumptions_latex: a_i\in\mathbb Z_{>0}
t\text{ is the weight of literals fixed true}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: b'=b-t<b\text{ may imply }\min\{a_i,b'\}<\min\{a_i,b\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Threshold Reduction Can Enable New Coefficient Saturation

assumptions_latex: All literals take values in \(\{0,1\}\).
Each reduction and simplification step is equivalence-preserving on the current partial assignment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two transformation orders define the same set of extendable Boolean assignments, although their resulting coefficient vectors may differ.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic interaction of coefficient reduction and simplification under a fixed partial assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be a pseudo-Boolean constraint, let \(\rho\) be a partial Boolean assignment, and let \(R\) and \(S_\rho\) preserve exactly the extensions of the current assignment satisfying their input constraint. Then, for every total assignment \(x\supseteq\rho\), \[x\models S_\rho(R(P))\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x\models P\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x\models R(S_\rho(P)).\] Thus reduction followed by simplification and simplification followed by renewed reduction are semantically interchangeable. Their syntactic outputs need not coincide, so any coefficient reduction applied before substitution may require normalization against the simplified right-hand side.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equivalence-preserving coefficient reduction and partial-assignment simplification may be composed in either order without changing feasible extensions, though the resulting constraints may look different.
knowledge_statements.title: Reduction-Simplification Interaction

assumptions_latex: The MaxSAT objective is minimized over assignments satisfying all hard clauses.
All soft-clause weights are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every feasible assignment supplies a valid upper bound on the optimal cost.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Upper bounds for weighted partial MaxSAT obtained directly from feasible assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be the hard clauses and \(S=\{(C_i,w_i)\}_{i=1}^m\) the soft clauses with \(w_i\ge 0\). For an assignment \(x\models H\), define \[c(x)=\sum_{i:x\not\models C_i}w_i.\] If \(z^*=\min\{c(y):y\models H\}\), then \(z^*\le c(x)\). Consequently, the best value among any collection \(F\) of feasible assignments, \(U_F=\min_{x\in F}c(x)\), is also a valid upper bound whenever \(F\ne\varnothing\). No assignment violating a hard clause yields such a bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The cost of any assignment satisfying every hard clause is an upper bound on the optimal weighted MaxSAT cost; the best observed feasible cost is the tightest such bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasible-Assignment Bounds

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The upper-bound property is mathematically standard and matches the leaf, but the record supplies no MaxSAT citation with a specific locator.

children.title: Incumbent Improvement
children.top_down_role: Progress of assignment-derived upper bounds through better feasible solutions.

assumptions_latex: Both the current incumbent and the candidate assignment satisfy all hard clauses.
The objective is minimization of total violated soft-clause weight.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Accepting a strictly cheaper candidate preserves upper-bound validity and strictly decreases the incumbent bound.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict incumbent update rule for a minimization-form weighted MaxSAT problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize with a feasible assignment \(x^{\mathrm{inc}}\) and set \(U=c(x^{\mathrm{inc}})\). Given another feasible assignment \(y\), apply the update \[(x^{\mathrm{inc}},U)\leftarrow\begin{cases}(y,c(y)),&c(y)<U,\\(x^{\mathrm{inc}},U),&c(y)\ge U.\end{cases}\] After every update, \(U=c(x^{\mathrm{inc}})\) and \(z^*\le U\). An accepted update strictly decreases \(U\); a tie may replace the stored assignment without improving the numerical bound. The output is the final incumbent and its valid upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace the incumbent only when a feasible candidate has lower cost. Each accepted replacement strictly lowers the valid upper bound while retaining a feasible witness.
knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Improvement

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and strict incumbent-update rule fit the leaf, but no specifically located MaxSAT or exact-search source is cited.

children.title: Incumbent Dominance
children.top_down_role: Dominance relations used to compare or discard incumbent candidates.

assumptions_latex: The compared assignments satisfy all hard clauses.
The objective is minimization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A no-more-expensive incumbent dominates the other feasible assignment for objective-value bounding.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-value dominance between feasible MaxSAT assignments, without asserting structural assignment dominance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For feasible assignments \(x\) and \(y\), define incumbent dominance by \[x\preceq_c y\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad c(x)\le c(y).\] If \(x\preceq_c y\), retaining \(y\) cannot yield a tighter assignment-derived upper bound than retaining \(x\). In particular, with \(U=c(x)\), any search state whose certified lower bound \(L\) satisfies \(L\ge U\) may be pruned independently of \(y\). This condition concerns objective values only and does not imply that \(x\) satisfies every soft clause satisfied by \(y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible assignment dominates another for bounding when its cost is no larger. The dominated assignment cannot provide a better upper bound, though their satisfied clauses may differ.
knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Dominance

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition correctly limits dominance to objective-value bounding and fits the leaf, but it lacks an inspectable MaxSAT source for the dominance and pruning claims.

children.title: Improvement-Dominance Interaction
children.top_down_role: Interaction between incumbent replacement and dominance filtering.

assumptions_latex: The incumbent upper bound comes from a feasible assignment.
Every search-state lower bound is valid for all feasible completions of that state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Incumbent improvement can only enlarge the set of states dominated by the upper bound and preserves exact pruning.

notation.meaning: A valid lower bound for search state q.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interaction between decreasing feasible upper bounds and lower-bound dominance in exact MaxSAT search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an incumbent improvement changes \(U\) to \(U'\) with \(z^*\le U'<U\). A search state \(q\) is objective-dominated whenever \(L(q)\ge U'\), because every feasible completion of \(q\) has cost at least \(U'\) and therefore cannot improve the incumbent. Moreover, \[\{q:L(q)\ge U\}\subseteq\{q:L(q)\ge U'\}.\] Hence improvement never revives a previously dominated state and may create additional dominated states. If a global lower bound \(L\) satisfies \(L\ge U'\), then \(U'=z^*\) and the incumbent is optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lowering a feasible incumbent bound preserves all earlier dominance pruning and may justify more pruning. Equality of the global lower and upper bounds certifies optimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Improvement-Dominance Interaction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle correctly describes the interaction of an improved upper bound with valid state lower bounds, but no exact-search or MaxSAT source with a specific locator is provided.

Its decision form is NP-complete, and remains NP-complete when every candidate core has three clauses.

assumptions_latex: Every listed core is jointly unsatisfiable with the hard clauses.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unweighted lower-bound certificate from pairwise disjoint soft unsatisfiable cores.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let each \(K_j\) be a subset of the soft clauses such that \(H\cup K_j\) is unsatisfiable, and suppose \(K_j\cap K_k=\varnothing\) whenever \(j\ne k\). Every assignment \(x\models H\) must violate at least one clause from each \(K_j\). Because the cores are disjoint, these required violations are distinct, so \[c(x)=\bigl|\{C\in S:x\not\models C\}\bigr|\ge t.\] Therefore \(t\) is a verifiable lower bound on the optimum. The certificate consists of the cores, their pairwise disjointness, and their unsatisfiability relative to \(H\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each disjoint unsatisfiable core forces a distinct soft-clause violation. Thus, in unweighted MaxSAT, the number of pairwise disjoint cores lower-bounds the optimum.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal K\) be soft-clause cores satisfying \(H\cup K\) unsatisfiable for every \(K\in\mathcal K\). Choose multipliers \(\lambda_K\ge0\) satisfying the clause-capacity inequalities \[\sum_{K\in\mathcal K:C_i\in K}\lambda_K\le w_i\qquad(i=1,\ldots,m).\] Every feasible assignment violates at least one clause in every core. Summing these requirements with multipliers and using the capacity inequalities gives \[c(x)\ge\sum_{K\in\mathcal K}\lambda_K.\] Hence any feasible multiplier vector certifies the displayed lower bound despite core overlap; assigning unit value independently to overlapping cores need not be valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Overlapping cores can be packed fractionally. When the total charge placed on each clause does not exceed its weight, the total core charge is a valid lower bound.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a family \(\mathcal K\) of soft cores, define the minimum-weight core cover value \[L_{\mathrm{cover}}=\min\left\{\sum_{i=1}^m w_i z_i:\ z_i\in\{0,1\},\ \sum_{i:C_i\in K}z_i\ge1\ \text{for every }K\in\mathcal K\right\}.\] If \(x\models H\), its violation indicators \(z_i(x)=1\) exactly when \(x\not\models C_i\) form a feasible cover, because each core contains a violated clause. Therefore \(c(x)\ge L_{\mathrm{cover}}\) for every feasible \(x\), and consequently \(z^*\ge L_{\mathrm{cover}}\).

If \(A\) is totally unimodular, then for every nonnegative weight vector \(w\), \[\min\{w^Tz:Az\ge\mathbf1,\ z\ge0\}=\min\{w^Tz:Az\ge\mathbf1,\ z\in\{0,1\}^m\}.\] Hence the packing, fractional-cover, and integer-cover values coincide.

The right-hand side is \(\mathbf1\).

A hard-feasible assignment can satisfy one soft clause, so \[L_{\mathrm{pack}}=L_{\mathrm{frac}}=\tfrac32<2=L_{\mathrm{int}}=z^*.\]

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the core-clause incidence matrix \(A\), fractional covering and core packing are the primal-dual pair \[L_{\mathrm{frac}}=\min\{w^Tz:A z\ge\mathbf1,\ z\ge0\},\qquad L_{\mathrm{pack}}=\max\{\mathbf1^T\lambda:A^T\lambda\le w,\ \lambda\ge0\}.\] Feasibility and boundedness hold when every core is nonempty and \(w\ge0\), so finite-dimensional linear-programming duality gives \(L_{\mathrm{pack}}=L_{\mathrm{frac}}\). Restricting \(z\) to \(\{0,1\}^m\) yields the integer cover value \(L_{\mathrm{int}}\), and \[L_{\mathrm{pack}}=L_{\mathrm{frac}}\le L_{\mathrm{int}}\le z^*.\] Thus overlap is handled by clause capacities in the packing dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fractional covering of all known cores is dual to capacity-constrained core packing. Their common value is no larger than the integer cover or the true optimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Overlap-Cover Interaction

For a finite valid core family \(\mathcal K\) and weights \(w_i\ge0\), the strongest admissible split-weight charge is
\[\max_{\delta\ge0}\left\{\sum_{K\in\mathcal K}\delta_K:\sum_{K\ni C_i}\delta_K\le w_i\ (i\in S)\right\}.\]

and the two finite optimal values are equal.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(r_i\leftarrow w_i\) and \(L\leftarrow0\). knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clause-based linear-programming relaxation of weighted partial MaxSAT.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Introduce \(x_j\in[0,1]\) for each Boolean variable and \(r_i\in[0,1]\) for each soft clause. children.title: Hitting-Set Lower Bounds
children.top_down_role: Lower bounds obtained from transversals of accumulated conflict structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Core-generation procedure that monotonically refines an integral hitting-set lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a collected core family \(\mathcal C\), compute a minimum-weight hitting set \(R\), then test the hard clauses together with all soft clauses outside \(R\). If the residual formula is satisfiable, \(R\) is a minimum-weight correction set and \(w(R)=\operatorname{OPT}\). If it is unsatisfiable, add a returned core contained among the retained clauses and repeat; that core is not hit by \(R\), so the hitting-set lower bound cannot decrease.

children.top_down_role: Search regimes combining multiple bound-progression strategies.

assumptions_latex: The weighted partial MaxSAT instance has hard formula \(H\), positive integer weights \(w_i\), and objective \(f(x)=\sum_{i\in I}w_i[\neg C_i(x)]\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact adaptive search using any mixture of lower, upper, and interior bound queries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain the invariant \(L\le\operatorname{OPT}\le U\). While \(L<U\), select by any history-dependent regime a bound \(b\in\{L,\ldots,U-1\}\), and query \(H\land(f\le b)\). If the query is unsatisfiable, set \(L\leftarrow b+1\). If it is satisfiable with model \(x\), set \(U\leftarrow\min\{U,f(x)\}\) and retain the best model. The selection rule may alternate among bottom-up queries \(b=L\), top-down queries \(b=U-1\), and interior queries. Each iteration strictly reduces \(U-L\); hence the procedure terminates with \(L=U=\operatorname{OPT}\), and the retained model has that cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adaptively query any bound between the current lower and upper bounds. Exact SAT and UNSAT responses shrink the interval until its common endpoint is the optimum.

children.title: Regime-Switching Criteria
children.top_down_role: Structural conditions governing transitions between search regimes.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: General correctness and termination condition allowing bounded or otherwise well-founded stuttering between strict bracket reductions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A history-dependent switching policy preserves exactness if every certified update maintains \(L_t\le\operatorname{OPT}\le U_t\). It terminates whenever its nonterminal transitions admit no infinite execution; for a finite integer bracket, sufficient instances include strict contraction at every iteration and policies allowing noncontracting steps but guaranteeing a strict contraction after finitely many such steps. Therefore per-iteration strict contraction is sufficient but not necessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Switching must preserve the certified bracket and make well-founded progress; occasional nonshrinking steps are harmless when strict contraction is guaranteed to recur.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A regime-switching rule is correctness-admissible when, for every nonterminal history \(\mathcal H_t\), it selects \(b_t\in\{L_t,\ldots,U_t-1\}\), interprets satisfiable and unsatisfiable oracle answers without weakening their logical meaning, and updates bounds so that the new interval contains \(\operatorname{OPT}\) and is a strict subinterval of \([L_t,U_t]\). Switching may depend on elapsed time, core size, model quality, or estimated query cost; these quantities affect efficiency but not correctness. Conversely, permitting \(b_t\notin[L_t,U_t-1]\), accepting an inexact answer as certified, or allowing a nonshrinking update invalidates the general termination guarantee.

notation.meaning: Relaxation variable associated with soft clause i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global, core-local, and duplicated relaxation-variable regimes for weighted partial MaxSAT.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the global regime, replace every soft clause \(C_i\) by \(C_i\lor r_i\) and minimize \(g(r)=\sum_i w_i r_i\) subject to \(H\). For each fixed hard-feasible assignment \(x\), minimizing over \(r\) sets \(r_i=[\neg C_i(x)]\), so \(\min_r g(r)=f(x)\). In a core-local regime, variables are introduced only for clauses occurring in processed cores; exactness additionally requires every unrelaxed clause to retain its original soft semantics. In a duplicated regime, multiple variables representing one original violation must be linked or charged so that their minimum total contribution equals \(w_i[\neg C_i(x)]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One paid relaxation variable per soft clause is exact. Partial or duplicated relaxation remains exact only when uncovered clauses and duplicate costs preserve every original violation charge.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Regimes
