The original and reformulated objectives are \(f(x)\) and \(g(x,z)\), respectively.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reformulation preserves the optimal value and projects every reformulated optimum to an original optimum.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise value-function criterion for objective-preserving core-guided reformulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A relaxation reformulation is objective-preserving precisely when, for every assignment \(x\) satisfying the original hard clauses, \(R(x)\ne\varnothing\) and \(f(x)=\min_{z\in R(x)}g(x,z)\), while every reformulation-feasible pair \((x,z)\) projects to a hard-feasible \(x\). Under these conditions, \[\min_{x\models H}f(x)=\min\{g(x,z):x\models H,\ z\in R(x)\}.\] Moreover, if \((x^*,z^*)\) is reformulation-optimal, then \(x^*\) is original-optimal whenever auxiliary variables at \(x^*\) are minimized. Thus feasibility projection, pointwise minimum-cost equality, and complete accounting of constants and split weights are jointly sufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reformulation preserves the objective when its feasible solutions project correctly and the cheapest auxiliary extension of every original assignment has exactly the original cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Preservation Conditions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The pointwise value-function criterion is plausible and the condition kind fits, but no source supports the stated precise characterization and optimal-solution projection conclusion.

children.title: Preservation Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where relaxation changes objective meaning or admissible costs.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counterexample family for spurious transformed assignments and missing lifts of original assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Projection can fail in either direction. First, the original instance \(H=\{x\}\), \(S=\{(\neg x,1)\}\) has optimum one; a transformed model that admits \(x=0\) has a spurious zero-cost optimum. Second, the original instance \(H=\varnothing\), \(S=\{(x,1)\}\) has optimum zero; a transformed model that permits only \(x=0\) has optimum one. Thus admitting a non-hard-feasible projection or omitting all extensions of an original assignment can change the optimum even when the copied soft coefficient is correct.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A transformed model can lower the optimum by admitting spurious projections or raise it by losing all extensions of an original low-cost assignment.
assumptions_latex: \text{In the first instance the transformed model admits }x=0
\text{In the second instance the transformed model permits only }x=0
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{OPT}'<\operatorname{OPT}\text{ can result from spurious projections, and }\operatorname{OPT}'>\operatorname{OPT}\text{ can result from missing lifts}
knowledge_statements.title: Two-Sided Feasibility-Projection Failures

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Overcharging Can Increase the Reformulated Optimum
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost-distortion failure complementary to omission and undercharging.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=\{\neg x\}\) and let the sole soft clause be \((x,1)\), so \(\operatorname{OPT}=1\). Replacing it by \(x\lor r\) and charging \(\alpha r\) with \(\alpha>1\) gives \(\operatorname{OPT}'=\alpha>1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Charging a relaxation variable more than the original clause weight can make the transformed optimum strictly too large.
assumptions_latex: H=\{\neg x\}
\alpha>1
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{OPT}'=\alpha>\operatorname{OPT}=1
knowledge_statements.title: Overcharging Can Increase the Reformulated Optimum

assumptions_latex: Boolean variable \(x\) is constrained by the hard clause \(\neg x\).
The sole soft clause is \(x\) with weight \(1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Omitting or undercharging a relaxation variable can strictly reduce the optimum, so objective preservation fails.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp undercharging failure caused by relaxing a forced-false soft clause without preserving its cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The original instance \(H=\{\neg x\}\) with soft clause \((x,1)\) has \(\operatorname{OPT}=1\). Replace the soft clause by the hard relaxed clause \(x\lor r\), but omit \(r\) from the objective, or assign it any charge \(\alpha<1\). The assignment \(x=0,r=1\) is reformulation-feasible and has cost \(0\), or \(\alpha\), respectively. Hence \(\operatorname{OPT}'<1=\operatorname{OPT}\). The same failure mechanism occurs when split or duplicated relaxation variables permit an original violation while their minimum combined charge is less than its original weight.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A forced-false unit soft clause costs one originally, but costs less after relaxation if its activation variable is omitted or undercharged. This strictly changes the optimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Preservation Failure Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure example is internally coherent and fits the failure-boundary container, but it has no cited source or inspectable locator supporting its use as a MaxSAT preservation boundary.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of additive weight splitting when a violation need activate only one independently weighted piece.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(w=a+b\), where \(a,b>0\), and let \(y=[\neg C(x)]\). Replace \(wy\) by \(az_1+bz_2\), with \(z_1,z_2\in\{0,1\}\) and only \(z_1+z_2\ge y\). At any fixed assignment with \(y=1\), the minimum feasible split contribution is \(\min\{a,b\}<a+b=w\). Thus this linking regime can change assignment costs and the optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Merely requiring one split indicator to activate under a violation undercharges the original clause.
assumptions_latex: w=a+b
z_1+z_2\ge y
knowledge_statements.title: Undercounting under At-Least-One Split Linking

assumptions_latex: Each soft-clause weight satisfies \(w_i>0\).
For every \(i\), positive pieces \(w_{ij}\) satisfy \(w_i=\sum_{j=1}^{k_i}w_{ij}\).
Each split indicator \(z_{ij}\) is constrained to equal the original violation indicator \(y_i=[\neg C_i(x)]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Weight splitting preserves every assignment cost and therefore preserves the optimum and optimal assignments.

notation.meaning: Original violation indicator for clause i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact additive splitting of weighted soft-clause penalties under shared violation semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any hard-feasible assignment \(x\), the original contribution of soft clause \(i\) is \(w_i y_i\). Replace it by \(k_i\) positive-weight pieces with contribution \(\sum_{j=1}^{k_i}w_{ij}z_{ij}\). If \(w_i=\sum_jw_{ij}\) and the reformulation enforces \(z_{ij}=y_i\) for every \(j\), then \[\sum_{j=1}^{k_i}w_{ij}z_{ij}=\left(\sum_{j=1}^{k_i}w_{ij}\right)y_i=w_i y_i.\] Summing over all soft clauses gives pointwise equality of the original and split objectives. The same conclusion holds with weaker linking constraints exactly when their minimum feasible split contribution at each fixed \(x\) equals \(w_i y_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Splitting a soft weight preserves the problem when the pieces sum to the original weight and collectively charge exactly the same clause-violation event.
knowledge_statements.title: Weight-Splitting Preservation Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The additive equality is plausible and the representation kind is acceptable for the regime container, but the exact linking and weaker-linking characterization lacks a direct source.

assumptions_latex: At an OLL iteration, \(B\) is a constant lower-bound offset and \(g\) is a nonnegative residual objective.
A detected residual core \(K\) implies \(\sum_{i\in K}y_i\ge1\) for every feasible residual assignment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Incrementing the offset and subtracting the certified core unit from the residual objective preserves the original objective value.

notation.meaning: Violation indicators in the detected core

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract objective-offset invariant underlying unit-cost OLL core reformulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the current reformulation satisfies \(f(x)=B+g(x,z)\) after minimizing admissible auxiliaries for every hard-feasible \(x\). If a valid core \(K\) certifies \(s_K(z)=\sum_{i\in K}y_i\ge1\), define \(B'=B+1\) and \(g'=g-1\) on the feasible region, implementing \(g'\) with exact Boolean or cardinality auxiliaries. Then \(g'\ge0\) and \(B'+g'=B+g=f\) pointwise after auxiliary minimization. Consequently, repeated OLL reformulations preserve the original optimum provided every extracted unit is valid, all residual multiplicities are represented, and each auxiliary encoding is projection-exact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: OLL preserves the objective when each core justifies one unit of unavoidable residual cost, that unit moves to a constant offset, and the residual encoding remains exact.
knowledge_statements.title: OLL Objective-Reformulation Preservation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source defines the intended OLL variant. Moreover, the stated assumptions do not establish that the residual objective contains the certified unit, so the conclusions that g-1 is nonnegative and exactly implementable are not reliable as written.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of feasibility inference when the recorded family omits a minimal core.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=\top\), \(C_1=p\), \(C_2=\neg p\), and let the recorded core family be \(\mathcal V=\varnothing\), omitting the minimal core \(\{1,2\}\). Then \(S=\varnothing\) hits every member of \(\mathcal V\) vacuously, but \(H\land C_1\land C_2\) is unsatisfiable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hitting a recorded family is insufficient when that family omits a minimal contradictory soft-clause set.
assumptions_latex: H=\top
C_1=p
C_2=\neg p
\mathcal V=\varnothing
S=\varnothing
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \left(\forall U\in\mathcal V,\ S\cap U\ne\varnothing\right)\land\operatorname{UNSAT}(H\land C_1\land C_2)
knowledge_statements.title: Incomplete Core Families Are Insufficient

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Converse direction complementing sufficiency of complete minimal-core coverage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq I\). If some assignment satisfies \(H\) and every \(C_i\) with \(i\in I\setminus S\), then \(S\cap U\ne\varnothing\) for every \(U\subseteq I\) such that \(H\land\bigwedge_{i\in U}C_i\) is unsatisfiable. In particular, every feasible removal set hits every inclusion-minimal soft core.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every feasible removal set intersects every unsatisfiable soft core.
assumptions_latex: S\subseteq I
\exists x:\ H(x)\land\bigwedge_{i\in I\setminus S}C_i(x)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall U\subseteq I,\quad \operatorname{UNSAT}\!\left(H\land\bigwedge_{i\in U}C_i\right)\Rightarrow U\cap S\ne\varnothing

notation.meaning: Soft clauses permitted to be removed or violated
Soft-clause core relative to the hard formula

knowledge_statements.title: Core-Hitting Necessity

assumptions_latex: The soft-clause index set \(I\) is finite and every \(w_i>0\).
The family \(\mathcal U\) contains every inclusion-minimal set \(U\subseteq I\) for which \(H\land\bigwedge_{i\in U}C_i\) is unsatisfiable.
A set \(S\subseteq I\) intersects every \(U\in\mathcal U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists an assignment satisfying \(H\) and every soft clause indexed by \(I\setminus S\).

notation.meaning: Family of all minimal unsatisfiable soft-clause cores relative to H
Candidate set of violated or removed soft clauses

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficiency of hitting all minimal soft cores relative to the hard formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume, toward the stated feasibility conclusion, that \(H\land\bigwedge_{i\in I\setminus S}C_i\) were unsatisfiable. Because \(I\setminus S\) is finite, it would contain an inclusion-minimal subset \(U\) such that \(H\land\bigwedge_{i\in U}C_i\) is unsatisfiable. By completeness, \(U\in\mathcal U\). But \(U\subseteq I\setminus S\) gives \(U\cap S=\varnothing\), contradicting that \(S\) hits every member of \(\mathcal U\). Therefore hitting all minimal cores is sufficient for the unhit soft clauses to be jointly satisfiable with \(H\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a candidate violation set intersects every minimal unsatisfiable soft core, all unselected soft clauses are jointly satisfiable with the hard clauses.
knowledge_statements.title: Core-Coverage Sufficiency

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem fits Core-Coverage Sufficiency and is mathematically standard for a finite complete family of minimal cores, but it has no citation and the statement field contains proof text, which must be removed after sourcing.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient oracle outcome forcing a valid core-hitting lower bound to meet a feasible upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a master containing only valid core-hitting constraints have optimal selector \(S=\{i:y_i=1\}\) and value \(L=\sum_{i\in S}w_i\), where \(w_i\ge0\). If an oracle returns a hard-feasible assignment \(x\) satisfying every \(C_i\) for \(i\notin S\), its violation cost \(U\) satisfies \(U\le L\). Together with master validity \(L\le\operatorname{OPT}\) and feasibility \(\operatorname{OPT}\le U\), this yields \(L=U=\operatorname{OPT}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If an oracle realizes every clause left unselected by an optimal valid hitting-set solution, the bounds coincide at the optimum.
assumptions_latex: w_i\ge0
L=\min\{\sum_iw_i y_i:y\text{ satisfies all master core constraints}\}
S=\{i:y_i=1\}\text{ for an optimal master solution}
x\models H\land\bigwedge_{i\notin S}C_i
\text{Every master core constraint is valid}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L=U=\operatorname{OPT}

notation.meaning: Soft clauses selected by an optimal hitting-set master solution
Violation cost of the oracle assignment

knowledge_statements.title: Master-Set Realizability Forces Bound Closure

assumptions_latex: The master minimizes \(\sum_{i\in I}w_i y_i\) over hitting constraints for certified cores, producing value \(L\).
The oracle tests the master-selected violation set and, when feasible, returns an assignment of cost \(U\).
All weights are nonnegative and all core constraints are valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When \(L=U\), the oracle assignment is MaxSAT-optimal and the common value equals \(\operatorname{OPT}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality certificate from equality of a core-hitting lower bound and a feasible MaxSAT upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every feasible MaxSAT assignment violates at least one soft clause in each certified core, so its violation vector satisfies every master hitting constraint. Therefore the optimal master value obeys \(L\le\operatorname{OPT}\). Any assignment returned feasible by the oracle has cost \(U\), hence \(\operatorname{OPT}\le U\). If \(L=U\), these inequalities give \(L=\operatorname{OPT}=U\). The master solution and oracle assignment need not have identical violation vectors; equality of their certified objective values suffices. If \(L<U\), disagreement alone is not an optimality certificate and requires another core, a better incumbent, or a stronger master.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified cores make the hitting-set master a lower bound, while an oracle model supplies an upper bound. Equality of those bounds certifies global optimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Master–Oracle Bound Agreement

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind fits the bound-agreement container and the bound-equality claim is plausible, but no source supports the master–oracle formulation and the statement includes derivational proof text.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal witness showing that abstract unsatisfiability alone does not validate a concrete hitting constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=\top\), let \(C_1=p\), and let an abstract element \(a\) be tested by \(P_a=p\land\neg p\) but instantiated as \(B_a=\{1\}\). Although \(H\land P_a\) is unsatisfiable, \(H\land C_1\) is satisfiable. Instantiating the abstract singleton core as \(y_1\ge1\) therefore excludes the valid assignment \(p=\top\), for which \(y_1=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without a sound implication from the abstract certificate to concrete block unsatisfiability, instantiation can exclude valid solutions.
assumptions_latex: H=\top
C_1=p
P_a=p\land\neg p
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{UNSAT}(H\land P_a)\not\Rightarrow\operatorname{UNSAT}(H\land C_1),\quad y_1\ge1\text{ is invalid}

notation.meaning: Predicate used by the abstract core oracle
Claimed concrete block represented by the abstract element

knowledge_statements.title: Unsound Instantiation without Concretization Implication

assumptions_latex: The abstract elements \(a\in A\) index soft-clause blocks \(B_a\subseteq I\).
An abstract core \(A_0\subseteq A\) certifies unsatisfiability of \(H\land\bigwedge_{a\in A_0}\bigwedge_{i\in B_a}C_i\).
Concrete indicators satisfy \(y_i=[\neg C_i(x)]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The instantiated union is a valid concrete core and its hitting inequality is valid for every hard-feasible assignment.

notation.meaning: Set of abstract block indices in the core
Soft-clause block represented by abstract element a

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound instantiation of a block-based abstract unsatisfiable core into a concrete hitting constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U=\bigcup_{a\in A_0}B_a\). The abstract-core certificate states exactly that \(H\land\bigwedge_{i\in U}C_i\) is unsatisfiable, so no assignment satisfying \(H\) can satisfy every clause indexed by \(U\). Consequently every hard-feasible assignment has \(y_i=1\) for at least one \(i\in U\), and therefore satisfies \(\sum_{i\in U}y_i\ge1\). Thus adding this instantiated hitting constraint cannot remove any feasible MaxSAT violation vector. Correctness fails without the block-conjunction semantics or another sound implication from the abstract certificate to concrete unsatisfiability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An abstract block core instantiates soundly when the union of its represented soft clauses is unsatisfiable with the hard clauses; its concrete hitting constraint is then valid.
knowledge_statements.title: Abstract-Core Instantiation Correctness

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem matches the terminal title under the explicitly stated block-conjunction semantics, but that abstraction semantics is uncited and the statement includes proof text.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit objective-range bound for nonnegative integer-weighted partial MaxSAT.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For soft weights \(w_i\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\) and \(W=\sum_i w_i\), every assignment cost lies in \(\{0,1,\ldots,W\}\). Therefore a sound procedure deleting at least one still-possible cost at every nonterminal iteration makes at most \(W\) such iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An integer-weighted MaxSAT objective has at most total-weight plus one possible costs.
assumptions_latex: The soft-clause weights are nonnegative integers.
Every nonterminal iteration soundly eliminates at least one currently possible objective value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |V|\leq W+1,\qquad N_{\mathrm{nonterminal}}\leq W.
knowledge_statements.title: Weighted-Integer Objective-Range Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finiteness alone does not imply algorithmic termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V=\{0,1\}\) and suppose an iteration repeats forever with \(V_t=V\). The objective range is finite but the process does not terminate. A strict reduction rule or another well-founded progress measure is therefore necessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An algorithm can cycle forever while retaining the same finite set of unresolved costs.
assumptions_latex: No strict-elimination or anti-repetition condition is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |V|<\infty\not\Rightarrow\text{termination}.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Range Without Progress

assumptions_latex: The set \(V=\{f(x):x\models H\}\) of attainable objective values is finite and nonempty.
Whenever the algorithm does not terminate, it deletes at least one value from the currently possible subset of \(V\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm terminates after at most \(|V|-1\) nonterminal objective-range reductions.

notation.meaning: Finite set of attainable objective values

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Termination from strict elimination within the finite set of attainable MaxSAT costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V_t\subseteq V\) be the objective values still consistent with all certificates after iteration \(t\). Assume \(V_0=V\), every update is sound so that \(\operatorname{OPT}\in V_t\), and each nonterminal iteration satisfies \(V_{t+1}\subsetneq V_t\). Since a strictly descending chain of nonempty subsets obtained by deleting at least one value has length at most \(|V|-1\), some iteration must be terminal. At termination, if the stopping rule requires a singleton possible-value set, then \(V_t=\{\operatorname{OPT}\}\). For integer-weighted MaxSAT, finiteness follows directly from finitely many assignments, and also from \(V\subseteq\{0,,,,,,,,,	,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,\ldots,\sum_iw_i\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact MaxSAT method terminates when every nonterminal step eliminates at least one attainable cost and only finitely many costs exist.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Objective-Range Termination

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-descent termination idea fits the container, but no source is cited. The displayed characterization of integer objective values is corrupted, the statement contains proof text, and identification of the optimum remains conditional on an additional singleton stopping rule.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharper finite core-space bound when only distinct inclusion-minimal cores are accumulated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(|I|=n\). The family \(\mathcal M\) of distinct inclusion-minimal unsatisfiable cores is an antichain in \(2^I\), so \(|\mathcal M|\leq\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}\). A procedure adding a previously absent minimal core after every nonterminal oracle call therefore makes at most this many core additions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distinct minimal cores form an antichain, so Sperner's bound limits their number.
assumptions_latex: \(|I|=n<\infty\).
Every accumulated core is inclusion-minimal and previously absent.
All work between successive core additions terminates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{core}}\leq\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}.
knowledge_statements.title: Minimal-Core Antichain Bound

assumptions_latex: The soft-clause index set \(I\) is finite.
Every nonterminal unsatisfiable oracle call adds a previously absent core \(U\subseteq I\).
All other phases between core additions terminate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure performs at most \(2^{|I|}-1\) core additions and therefore terminates.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite termination bound for algorithms that never add the same soft-clause core twice.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every core is a nonempty subset of \(I\), so at most \(2^{|I|}-1\) distinct cores exist. If each nonterminal unsatisfiable oracle call produces \(U\notin\mathcal U_t\) and updates \(\mathcal U_{t+1}=\mathcal U_t\cup\{U\}\), the number of such calls is at most \(2^{|I|}-1\). Hence an algorithm whose remaining work terminates between core additions cannot generate cores indefinitely. If only inclusion-minimal cores are stored, the same finite bound remains valid, though sharper antichain bounds may apply. Duplicate generation without a progress-producing strengthening is outside this termination condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: There are finitely many soft-clause cores. A procedure that adds a new core after every nonterminal UNSAT call can therefore make only finitely many such calls.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Core-Space Termination

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind is defensible because the record gives an explicit bound, and the finite-count argument is plausible under the stated uniqueness assumption. A direct MaxSAT termination source is absent, however, and the statement includes proof text.

assumptions_latex: \(L_t\leq f^*\leq U_t\) for every iteration \(t\).
\(L_t,U_t\in V\), where \(V\subset\mathbb{R}\) is finite and totally ordered.
At every nonterminal iteration, \(L_{t+1}\geq L_t\), \(U_{t+1}\leq U_t\), and at least one of these inequalities is strict.
The procedure terminates whenever \(L_t=U_t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists T<\infty:\ L_T=U_T=f^*\).

notation.meaning: valid lower and upper bounds at iteration t
finite set of attainable bound values

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient termination condition for an exact bound-driven MaxSAT procedure.

source_refs.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a minimization procedure maintaining valid bounds \(L_t\leq f^*\leq U_t\) and terminating whenever \(L_t=U_t\). Suppose \(L_t,U_t\in V\) for a finite totally ordered set \(V\subset\mathbb{R}\). At every nonterminal iteration, suppose \(L_{t+1}\geq L_t\), \(U_{t+1}\leq U_t\), and at least one inequality is strict. Then only finitely many nonterminal iterations are possible, so the procedure terminates at some \(T<\infty\) with \(L_T=U_T=f^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Valid bounds drawn from a finite ordered set terminate exactly when neither bound regresses and at least one bound strictly improves at every nonterminal iteration.
knowledge_statements.title: Strict Bound-Progress Termination

source_witnesses.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iteration bound induced by monotone strict movement in a finite ordered bound set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\) be a finite totally ordered set of size \(m\). If \(L_t,U_t\in V\), \(L_t\) never decreases, \(U_t\) never increases, and every nonterminal iteration changes at least one bound strictly, then there are at most \(2(m-1)\) nonterminal iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each bound can move through the finite ordered set at most size-minus-one times.
assumptions_latex: \(|V|=m<\infty\).
\(L_{t+1}\geq L_t\) and \(U_{t+1}\leq U_t\).
Every nonterminal iteration changes at least one bound strictly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{nonterminal}}\leq2(m-1).

notation.meaning: Lower and upper bounds at iteration \(t\).

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Bound-Movement Count

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict numerical progress need not terminate over an infinite value set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f^*=1\), let \(L_t=1-2^{-t}\) and \(U_t=1+2^{-t}\). Both bounds improve strictly and remain valid, but \(L_t\neq U_t\) for every finite \(t\). Thus strict monotone progress over an infinite value set does not ensure finite termination by bound equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounds can improve strictly forever while converging to the optimum without meeting.
assumptions_latex: Bound values may range over an infinite ordered set.
Termination requires exact equality of the bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl(L_{t+1}>L_t\land U_{t+1}<U_t\bigr)\not\Rightarrow\exists T:\ L_T=U_T.
knowledge_statements.title: Infinite-Value Asymptotic-Gap Counterexample

assumptions_latex: The rooted search tree has finite depth and finite branching, and no node is generated twice.
At every branched node, the children collectively cover all feasible assignments represented by their parent.
Every node-processing operation terminates, and every generated open node is eventually selected.
A node is fathomed only after infeasibility is established, its subproblem is solved, or a valid lower bound proves that it cannot improve the incumbent.
The root subproblem is feasible, and every incumbent is a feasible assignment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure terminates after processing finitely many nodes, and its final incumbent has objective value \(f^*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-tree sufficient condition for exact MaxSAT branch-and-bound termination.

source_refs.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a MaxSAT branch-and-bound procedure explore a rooted tree of subproblems. Assume the tree has finite depth and finite branching, no node is generated twice, and the children of every branched node collectively cover all feasible assignments represented by that node. Assume each node-processing operation terminates, every generated open node is eventually selected, and a node is fathomed only after infeasibility is established, its subproblem is solved, or a valid lower bound proves that it cannot improve the incumbent. If the root subproblem is feasible and every incumbent is feasible, then the procedure processes finitely many nodes, terminates, and returns an incumbent of value \(f^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite search tree with exhaustive branching, terminating and fair node processing, valid fathoming, and a feasible root terminates with a globally optimal incumbent.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Search-Tree Termination

source_witnesses.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Node bound for a search tree of bounded depth and branching factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a rooted search tree has depth at most \(d\) and every internal node has at most \(b\) children, it has at most \(\sum_{k=0}^{d}b^k\) nodes. Processing each generated node at most once therefore requires at most that many node-processing steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded depth and branching give the standard geometric bound on processed search nodes.
assumptions_latex: \(d<\infty\) and \(b<\infty\).
Each generated node is processed at most once.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{nodes}}\leq\sum_{k=0}^{d}b^k.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Branching Node Bound

children.title: Weighted Break Scores
children.top_down_role: Weighted measures used to assess candidate local-search flips.

assumptions_latex: The weighted CNF formula is finite.
All clause weights are fixed and finite.
\(a\) is a complete Boolean assignment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f(a^{\oplus x})<f(a)\iff\operatorname{make}_w(x;a)>\operatorname{break}_w(x;a).

notation.meaning: weight of violated clauses made satisfied by flipping x
weight of satisfied clauses broken by flipping x
assignment a with variable x flipped

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact decomposition of the one-flip change in weighted violation cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f(a)=\sum_{C:a
ot\models C}w_C\). Define \(\operatorname{make}_w(x;a)=\sum_{C:a
ot\models C,\,a^{\oplus x}\models C}w_C\) and \(\operatorname{break}_w(x;a)=\sum_{C:a\models C,\,a^{\oplus x}
ot\models C}w_C\). Then \[f(a)-f(a^{\oplus x})=\operatorname{make}_w(x;a)-\operatorname{break}_w(x;a).\] Hence the flip strictly improves the weighted objective exactly when its make score exceeds its break score.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The objective improvement from a flip equals made-clause weight minus broken-clause weight.
knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Flip Gain Decomposition

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clause-local characterization of clauses contributing to a variable's break score.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume each scored clause contains no repeated variable and no complementary literal pair. For a complete assignment \(a\), a satisfied clause \(C\) becomes unsatisfied after flipping \(x\) exactly when the literal of \(x\) is the unique true literal of \(C\). Hence \[\operatorname{break}_w(x;a)=\sum_{C:\,\operatorname{TrueLit}_a(C)=\{\ell_x\}}w_C.\] In particular, \(\operatorname{break}_w(x;a)=0\) exactly when no positive-weight clause is uniquely supported by \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For ordinary non-tautological clauses, a clause contributes to a variable's break score exactly when that variable supplies its only true literal.
assumptions_latex: F\text{ is a finite CNF formula whose scored clauses contain no repeated variable or complementary literal pair}.
a\text{ is a complete assignment}.
w_C>0\text{ for every scored clause }C.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{break}_w(x;a)=0\iff\nexists C\text{ of positive weight uniquely satisfied by the literal of }x.

notation.meaning: literals of C true under a
literal of x true under a

knowledge_statements.title: Unique-Support Representation of Weighted Break

assumptions_latex: F\text{ is a finite CNF formula}.
\text{Clause-variable incidence lists and true-literal counts are maintained}.
\text{Arithmetic on stored clause weights has unit cost}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_{\mathrm{update}}(x)=O\!\left(\sum_{C\ni x}|C|\right).

notation.meaning: number of literal occurrences in clause C
time to update maintained break scores after flipping x

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incremental maintenance cost after one variable flip using clause incidence and true-literal counts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain each clause's number of true literals and every variable's weighted break score. After flipping \(x\), only clauses containing \(x\) can change truth status or unique true support, and only variables occurring in those clauses can have break contributions changed. With incidence lists, all affected scores can be updated in time \(O\!\left(\sum_{C\ni x}|C|\right)\), without inspecting unaffected clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A flip changes break-score contributions only in incident clauses, permitting an update proportional to their total size.
knowledge_statements.title: Clause-Local Incremental Break-Score Update

assumptions_latex: C=(x\lor\neg x)\text{ has positive finite weight }w_C.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{TrueLit}_a(C)=\{x\}\quad\text{but}\quad a^{\oplus x}\models C.

notation.meaning: literals of C true under a

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal witness showing that unique true-literal support does not characterize break contributions for tautological clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=(x\lor\neg x)\) and let \(a_x=1\). Then \(x\) is the unique literal of \(C\) true under \(a\), but after flipping \(x\), the literal \(\neg x\) becomes true, so \(C\) remains satisfied and contributes zero to \(\operatorname{break}_w(x;a)\). Thus the unique-true-literal characterization fails when a clause contains a complementary literal pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tautological clause can have one true literal before a flip and remain satisfied afterward, invalidating the unique-support break test.
knowledge_statements.title: Tautological Clause Defeats Unique-Support

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary range and equality conditions for ordinary finite weighted break scores.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For positive finite clause weights and a complete assignment, \[0\leq\operatorname{break}_w(x;a)\leq\sum_{C:\,x\in\operatorname{var}(C)}w_C.\] Equality on the left holds exactly when no positive-weight clause changes from satisfied to unsatisfied after flipping \(x\). Equality on the right holds exactly when every positive-weight clause containing \(x\) is satisfied before the flip and unsatisfied afterward.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weighted break score lies between zero and the total weight of clauses containing the flipped variable, with equality determined by which incident clauses break.
assumptions_latex: F\text{ is a finite weighted CNF formula}.
0<w_C<\infty.
a\text{ is a complete assignment}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\leq\operatorname{break}_w(x;a)\leq\sum_{C:\,x\in\operatorname{var}(C)}w_C.

notation.meaning: total weight of clauses changed from satisfied to unsatisfied by flipping x

knowledge_statements.title: Incident-Weight Bounds for Weighted Break

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weighted Break Is Additive and Positively Homogeneous
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic behavior of ordinary weighted break scores under clause-family decomposition and weight scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(F=F_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}F_2\), then \(\operatorname{break}_{F,w}(x;a)=\operatorname{break}_{F_1,w}(x;a)+\operatorname{break}_{F_2,w}(x;a)\). For \(\alpha\geq0\), \(\operatorname{break}_{\alpha w}(x;a)=\alpha\operatorname{break}_w(x;a)\); consequently every common positive scaling preserves break-score orderings and ties.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted break scores add over disjoint clause groups and scale linearly with a common nonnegative weight multiplier.
assumptions_latex: F\text{ is finite}.
F=F_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}F_2.
w_C\geq0.
\alpha\geq0.
a\text{ is a complete assignment}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{break}_{F,w}=\operatorname{break}_{F_1,w}+\operatorname{break}_{F_2,w},\qquad \operatorname{break}_{\alpha w}=\alpha\operatorname{break}_w.

notation.meaning: disjoint partition of the scored clause family

knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Break Is Additive and Positively Homogeneous
Weighted Break Scores
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Break cost of flipping one variable in weighted MaxSAT local search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a weighted CNF formula with positive clause weights \(w_C\), and let \(a\) be a complete Boolean assignment. For a variable \(x\), write \(a^{\oplus x}\) for the assignment obtained by flipping \(x\). The weighted break score is \[\operatorname{break}_w(x;a)=\sum_{C\in F:\,a\models C,\ a^{\oplus x}\not\models C} w_C.\] Thus it is exactly the total weight of clauses changed from satisfied to unsatisfied by the flip. Hard clauses may instead be assigned an overriding lexicographic weight.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The weighted break score is the total weight of currently satisfied clauses that become unsatisfied when a variable is flipped.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite weighted CNF formula.
Each ordinary clause has weight \(w_C>0\).
\(a\) is a complete Boolean assignment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{break}_w(x;a)=\sum_{C:\,a\models C,\ a^{\oplus x}\not\models C}w_C\).

notation.meaning: assignment a with variable x flipped
weighted break score of flipping x at a

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The ordinary weighted-break formula is precise and the definition content kind fits the leaf. No citation supports the MaxSAT terminology or the additional lexicographic hard-clause convention, so source review is required before acceptance.

assumptions_latex: All soft weights are nonnegative and finite.
At least one assignment satisfies every hard clause.
Each violated hard clause incurs penalty \(H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H>\sum_{C\in F_s}w_C\Rightarrow\arg\min f_H\subseteq\{a:a\models F_h\}.

notation.meaning: penalty for each violated hard clause

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-weight encoding of lexicographic hard-clause priority; primary ownership lies outside this scoring leaf.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W=\sum_{C\in F_s}w_C\). If every violated hard clause receives penalty \(H>W\) and a hard-feasible assignment exists, every minimizer of total penalized violation cost is hard-feasible. When \(H\leq W\), this enforcement is not guaranteed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hard-clause penalty greater than total soft weight enforces hard priority, but this is a hard-feasibility representation result rather than a weighted-break-score result.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Penalty for Hard-Clause Priority

intermediate_metadata.reason: This leaf locally owns weighted break, make, and net-gain quantities and their exact relation to one-flip objective change. Weighted Flip Gain Decomposition is accepted. The proposed finite hard-penalty condition is deferred as canonically belonging to the Hard Feasibility Layer, and the foundational weighted-break definition remains missing. Flip-Selection Policies, Score-Selection Coupling, and Degenerate Tie Regimes were excluded as sibling scopes.

children.title: Flip-Selection Policies
children.top_down_role: Policy families for choosing among candidate variable flips.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is finite and nonempty.
Every score \(s_x\) is finite.
The inverse temperature satisfies \(\beta\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p_0(x)=|X|^{-1},\qquad \lim_{\beta\to\infty}p_\beta(x)=\begin{cases}|M|^{-1},&x\in M,\\0,&x\notin M,\end{cases}\quad M=\arg\max_{y\in X}s_y.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limiting exploration and exploitation behavior of finite-set softmax flip selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(p_\beta(x)=e^{\beta s_x}/\sum_{y\in X}e^{\beta s_y}\), \(p_0\) is uniform on \(X\). As \(\beta\to\infty\), \(p_\beta\) converges to the uniform distribution on \(M=\arg\max_{x\in X}s_x\), with limiting probability zero for every nonmaximizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Softmax is uniform at zero inverse temperature and approaches uniform choice among maximum-score flips as inverse temperature grows.
knowledge_statements.title: Softmax Temperature Limits

assumptions_latex: \(X(a)\) is finite and nonempty.
\(g(\cdot\mid a)\) is a probability distribution on \(X(a)\).
\(0\leq\varepsilon\leq1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p(x\mid a)\geq\varepsilon/|X(a)|\quad\forall x\in X(a).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum per-step selection probability under uniform exploration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The mixture \(p(x\mid a)=(1-\varepsilon)g(x\mid a)+\varepsilon/|X(a)|\) is a probability distribution and satisfies \(p(x\mid a)\geq\varepsilon/|X(a)|\) for every candidate. If \(\varepsilon>0\), every candidate has positive probability; at \(\varepsilon=0\), positive support is inherited only from \(g\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mixing any base policy with uniform exploration gives every candidate a probability floor of epsilon divided by the candidate-set size.
knowledge_statements.title: Exploration Floor of Epsilon Mixtures

assumptions_latex: S\text{ is finite}.
X(a)\neq\varnothing\text{ for every }a\in S.
\text{The permitted-flip digraph is strongly connected}.
\eta>0.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p(x\mid a)\geq\eta\ \forall a\in S,\ x\in X(a)\Longrightarrow\text{the induced chain is irreducible}.

notation.meaning: permitted flip set at assignment a

knowledge_statements.scope_note: State-space reachability induced by a state-based exploration-mixed flip policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be a finite assignment state space and let \(X(a)\) be the permitted flips at \(a\). Assume the directed graph with arcs \(a\to a^{\oplus x}\) for \(x\in X(a)\) is strongly connected. If a state-based selection policy satisfies \(p(x\mid a)\geq\eta>0\) for every permitted flip, then its assignment Markov chain is irreducible. This does not imply aperiodicity: a chain containing only single-bit flips on the full Boolean cube has period two unless a self-loop or another parity-breaking transition is introduced.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive probability floor on every edge of a strongly connected flip graph makes a state-based search chain irreducible, but not necessarily aperiodic.
knowledge_statements.title: Irreducibility from Uniform Exploration

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lazy Exploration Gives Finite-State Ergodic Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stationary convergence for a finite irreducible state-based flip policy augmented by a positive self-loop.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be the transition matrix of a finite irreducible state-based flip policy. For \(0<\lambda<1\), define \(P_\lambda=\lambda I+(1-\lambda)P\). Then \(P_\lambda\) is irreducible and aperiodic, has a unique stationary distribution \(\pi\), and \(\mu P_\lambda^t\to\pi\) for every initial distribution \(\mu\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding a positive stay-put probability makes a finite irreducible flip chain aperiodic and ensures convergence to its unique stationary distribution.
assumptions_latex: P\text{ is a transition matrix on a finite state space}.
P\text{ is irreducible}.
0<\lambda<1.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists!\pi:\pi P_\lambda=\pi,\qquad \lim_{t\to\infty}\mu P_\lambda^t=\pi.
knowledge_statements.title: Lazy Exploration Gives Finite-State Ergodic Convergence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mappings from a finite candidate set and its scores to a selected flip distribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A flip-selection policy assigns each state \(a\) a probability distribution \(p(\cdot\mid a)\) on a finite nonempty candidate set \(X(a)\). Uniform selection has \(p(x\mid a)=1/|X(a)|\). A deterministic greedy policy selects one member of \(M(a)=\arg\max_{x\in X(a)}s(x;a)\) using a specified tie order; randomized greedy selection may use any specified distribution supported on \(M(a)\). Softmax with \(\beta\geq0\) uses \(p_\beta(x\mid a)\propto e^{\beta s(x;a)}\). An \(\varepsilon\)-exploration mixture with \(0\leq\varepsilon\leq1\) combines a base distribution \(g\) with uniform selection as \((1-\varepsilon)g+\varepsilon/|X(a)|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A flip policy maps candidates to a distribution, including uniform, greedy with explicit tie handling, softmax, and epsilon-exploration mappings.
assumptions_latex: X(a)\text{ is finite and nonempty}.
s(x;a)\in\mathbb R\quad\forall x\in X(a).
\beta\geq0.
0\leq\varepsilon\leq1.
\text{Any deterministic greedy tie order is specified}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_{x\in X(a)}p(x\mid a)=1,\qquad p(x\mid a)\geq0.

notation.meaning: softmax inverse temperature and uniform-exploration probability

knowledge_statements.title: Flip-Selection Policy Interface
Flip-Selection Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Score-based variable selection within stochastic local search for weighted MaxSAT.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a current assignment \(a\), form a nonempty candidate set \(X(a)\) of flippable variables and compute a score \(s(x;a)\) for every \(x\in X(a)\). Select \(x\) using a specified policy, for example greedily from \(\arg\max_{y\in X(a)}s(y;a)\), by softmax probability \[p(x\mid a)=\frac{\exp(\beta s(x;a))}{\sum_{y\in X(a)}\exp(\beta s(y;a))},\] or by an \(\varepsilon\)-mixture of greedy and uniform selection. Replace \(a\) by \(a^{\oplus x}\), update scores, and stop under the prescribed budget or target-cost rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A flip policy maps candidate scores to a variable choice, using greedy, softmax, or exploration-mixed selection, then updates the assignment.
assumptions_latex: \(X(a)\neq\varnothing\) at every executed step.
Scores \(s(x;a)\) are finite for all candidates.
The stopping budget or target-cost rule is specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The policy defines a probability distribution on \(X(a)\) and the update \(a\leftarrow a^{\oplus x}\).

notation.meaning: softmax inverse temperature and exploration probability

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm content kind fits, but no source supports the asserted family of greedy, softmax, and epsilon-mixture MaxSAT policies. The admissible range of epsilon and the tie rule for greedy selection also need specification once an authoritative policy source is selected.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact relationship between score differences and relative flip probabilities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(p_\beta(x)=e^{\beta s_x}/\sum_{z\in X}e^{\beta s_z}\), every pair \(x,y\in X\) satisfies \(p_\beta(x)/p_\beta(y)=e^{\beta(s_x-s_y)}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under softmax, pairwise probability odds are determined by score differences and inverse temperature.
assumptions_latex: X\text{ is finite and nonempty}.
s_x\in\mathbb R\text{ for all }x\in X.
\beta\geq0.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \frac{p_\beta(x)}{p_\beta(y)}=\exp\!\bigl(\beta(s_x-s_y)\bigr).
knowledge_statements.title: Softmax Pairwise Odds

The proposed pairwise-odds record is deferred to Score–Selection Coupling. The umbrella policy definition remains missing; score definitions and tie pathology were excluded.

children.title: Score–Selection Coupling
children.top_down_role: Interactions between score semantics and flip-selection behavior.

assumptions_latex: Lower break cost denotes a more desirable flip.
The selection policy favors numerically larger inputs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: b(x;a)<b(y;a)\not\Rightarrow p(x\mid a)\geq p(y\mid a)\text{ under positive-direction coupling to }b.

notation.meaning: break cost of flipping x at assignment a

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure caused by coupling a cost score to a desirability-maximizing policy without reversing its order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(b(x;a)\) is a break cost for which smaller values are preferred, coupling it directly to argmax or to \(p(x\mid a)\propto e^{\beta b(x;a)}\) with \(\beta>0\) favors larger break costs. Order-consistent coupling uses \(-b\), argmin, or a negative exponent. Score orientation is therefore part of the coupling semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A break cost must be minimized or sign-reversed; feeding it unchanged to a larger-is-better policy reverses the intended preference.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Score Sign Must Match Policy Direction
knowledge_statements.title: Score Sign Must Match Policy Direction

assumptions_latex: The candidate set is finite and nonempty.
All scores and parameters are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p_\beta(s+c\mathbf 1)=p_\beta(s),\qquad p_\beta(\alpha s)=p_{\alpha\beta}(s).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transformations of scores that preserve or reparameterize softmax selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(p_\beta(x)=e^{\beta s_x}/\sum_y e^{\beta s_y}\), adding a common constant \(c\) to every score leaves the distribution unchanged. Multiplying every score by \(\alpha>0\) gives the same distribution as replacing \(\beta\) by \(\alpha\beta\). Thus softmax depends on score differences and the product of score scale with inverse temperature.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Softmax ignores common score offsets, and positive score scaling is equivalent to inverse-temperature scaling.
knowledge_statements.title: Softmax Score-Transformation Invariance

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of uniform exploration on an already score-monotone base policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g(\cdot\mid a)\) be score-monotone on finite \(X(a)\), and set \(p_\varepsilon(x\mid a)=(1-\varepsilon)g(x\mid a)+\varepsilon/|X(a)|\) for \(0\leq\varepsilon\leq1\). Then \(p_\varepsilon\) is score-monotone. If \(g\) is strictly score-monotone and \(\varepsilon<1\), then \(p_\varepsilon\) is strictly score-monotone; at \(\varepsilon=1\), all score discrimination is lost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform exploration preserves weak score ordering and preserves strict ordering unless the policy becomes completely uniform.
assumptions_latex: X(a)\text{ is finite and nonempty}.
g(\cdot\mid a)\text{ is score-monotone}.
0\leq\varepsilon\leq1.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: s_x>s_y\Rightarrow p_\varepsilon(x\mid a)\geq p_\varepsilon(y\mid a),\quad\text{strict if }g\text{ is strict and }\varepsilon<1.
knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Exploration Preserves Score Monotonicity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Greedy Coupling Is Invariant Under Strictly Increasing Score Transforms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order-theoretic invariance of argmax selection and its contrast with magnitude-sensitive coupling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be finite and nonempty and \(\phi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) strictly increasing. Then \(\arg\max_{x\in X}\phi(s_x)=\arg\max_{x\in X}s_x\). Greedy coupling therefore depends only on score order, whereas fixed-temperature softmax generally changes under nonlinear transformations because it depends on score differences.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Greedy selection depends only on score order, while fixed-temperature softmax generally also depends on score magnitudes.
assumptions_latex: X\text{ is finite and nonempty}.
s_x\in\mathbb R\text{ for all }x\in X.
\phi\text{ is strictly increasing}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \arg\max_{x\in X}\phi(s_x)=\arg\max_{x\in X}s_x.
knowledge_statements.title: Greedy Coupling Is Invariant Under Strictly Increasing Score Transforms

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weak, Strict, and Full-Support Score Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinct consistency notions linking candidate scores to selection probabilities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For finite nonempty \(X(a)\), a selection distribution \(p(\cdot\mid a)\) is weakly score-monotone when \(s(x;a)>s(y;a)\Rightarrow p(x\mid a)\geq p(y\mid a)\). It is strictly score-discriminating when the concluding inequality is strict, and it has full support when \(p(x\mid a)>0\) for every candidate. These notions are independent in general: deterministic argmax is weakly monotone without full support, finite-temperature softmax with \(\beta>0\) is strict with full support, and the uniform distribution has full support but is not strictly discriminating when unequal scores occur.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weak ordering, strict discrimination, and positive probability for every candidate are separate score–selection coupling properties.
assumptions_latex: X(a)\text{ is finite and nonempty}.
s(x;a)\in\mathbb R\quad\forall x\in X(a).
p(\cdot\mid a)\text{ is a probability distribution on }X(a).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{weak monotonicity},\ \text{strict discrimination},\ \text{and full support are distinct conditions}.

notation.meaning: score of candidate flip x at assignment a

knowledge_statements.title: Weak, Strict, and Full-Support Score Coupling
Score–Selection Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency condition linking flip scores to stochastic variable-selection probabilities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each assignment \(a\), let \(s(\cdot;a)\) score the finite candidate set \(X(a)\), and let \(p(\cdot\mid a)\) be the flip-selection distribution. The selection is score-monotone when, for all \(x,y\in X(a)\), \[s(x;a)>s(y;a)\Longrightarrow p(x\mid a)\geq p(y\mid a).\] It is strictly score-monotone when the concluding inequality is strict. A softmax rule with finite \(\beta>0\) is strictly score-monotone and assigns positive probability to every candidate; deterministic argmax selection is score-monotone but not strictly positive on nonmaximizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Score–selection coupling is monotone when a higher-scoring flip never receives lower selection probability; softmax is strict, while greedy selection can exclude candidates.
assumptions_latex: \(X(a)\) is finite and nonempty.
All scores are real and all selection probabilities are defined.
For softmax strictness, \(0<\beta<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s(x;a)>s(y;a)\Rightarrow p(x\mid a)\geq p(y\mid a)\), with strict inequality under strict coupling.

notation.meaning: score of flipping x at assignment a
probability of selecting x at assignment a

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The monotonicity condition and the softmax consequence are mathematically coherent, and condition is an appropriate content kind. However, the named coupling is identified as a local formalization and has no source establishing its role in MaxSAT score-based selection.

children.title: Degenerate Tie Regimes
children.top_down_role: Selection behavior when candidates receive indistinguishable scores.

assumptions_latex: \(M\) is finite and nonempty.
Every member of \(M\) has the same score.
Permutation invariance means invariance under every permutation of \(M\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p\text{ is permutation-invariant on }M\iff p(x)=1/|M|\quad\forall x\in M.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetry behavior of selection rules on equal-score candidates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a finite set of tied maximum-score candidates. A probability rule on \(M\) is invariant under every permutation of \(M\) exactly when it assigns probability \(1/|M|\) to every member. A deterministic rule on a nonsingleton \(M\) must therefore use information external to the tied scores and breaks this full permutation symmetry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform random tie-breaking preserves full symmetry among tied candidates; deterministic selection from a nonsingleton tie uses external information and breaks it.
knowledge_statements.title: Tie-Breaking and Permutation Symmetry

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equal Scores Receive Equal Softmax Probability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact effect of a partial score tie under finite-temperature softmax selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(p_\beta(x)=e^{\beta s_x}/\sum_{z\in X}e^{\beta s_z}\) with finite scores, \(s_x=s_y\) implies \(p_\beta(x)=p_\beta(y)\) for every finite \(\beta\). If \(\beta>0\), the converse also holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite-temperature softmax gives equal probabilities to tied scores, and at positive inverse temperature only tied scores have equal probability.
assumptions_latex: X\text{ is finite and nonempty}.
s_z\in\mathbb R\text{ for all }z\in X.
0\leq\beta<\infty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: s_x=s_y\Rightarrow p_\beta(x)=p_\beta(y),\qquad \beta>0\Rightarrow\bigl(p_\beta(x)=p_\beta(y)\iff s_x=s_y\bigr).
knowledge_statements.title: Equal Scores Receive Equal Softmax Probability

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical partition of maximum-score and complete-tie regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite nonempty candidate set \(X(a)\), let \(M(a)=\arg\max_{x\in X(a)}s(x;a)\). The state has maximum-score degeneracy when \(|M(a)|>1\), and complete score degeneracy when \(s(x;a)=c\) for every \(x\in X(a)\), equivalently \(M(a)=X(a)\). In either case scores alone do not select a unique maximizer. Under complete degeneracy, finite-temperature softmax is uniform on \(X(a)\), while deterministic argmax requires an external tie rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partial tie has several maximum-score candidates; a complete tie gives every candidate the same score and makes softmax uniform.
assumptions_latex: X(a)\text{ is finite and nonempty}.
s(x;a)\in\mathbb R\quad\forall x\in X(a).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |M(a)|>1\Rightarrow\arg\max s\text{ is nonunique},\qquad M(a)=X(a)\Rightarrow p_\beta(x\mid a)=|X(a)|^{-1}.
knowledge_statements.title: Partial and Complete Score Degeneracy
Degenerate Tie Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of score discrimination when multiple candidate flips tie.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M(a)=\arg\max_{x\in X(a)}s(x;a)\). A degenerate tie regime occurs when \(|M(a)|>1\), or, in the complete-degeneracy case, when \(s(x;a)=c\) for every \(x\in X(a)\). Scores alone then do not determine a unique flip. Under complete degeneracy, softmax selection is uniform on \(X(a)\) for every finite inverse temperature, while deterministic argmax requires an external tie-breaking rule. Consequently, any claimed preference among tied variables must arise from tie-breaking information not contained in the score.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When best scores tie, scores do not identify one flip; complete ties make softmax uniform and force greedy methods to use an external tie-breaker.
assumptions_latex: \(X(a)\) is finite and nonempty.
The selection rule depends on candidates through their scores, apart from explicit tie-breaking.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(s(x;a)=c\) for all \(x\in X(a)\), then softmax gives \(p(x\mid a)=1/|X(a)|\), and argmax is set-valued.

notation.meaning: common score in the completely degenerate case

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient probabilistic-completeness condition for an indefinitely continued focused random walk.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose there exist \(L\in\mathbb{N}\) and \(\delta>0\) such that, from every non-target state and after every history, the conditional probability of reaching target set \(G\) within the next \(L\) steps is at least \(\delta\). Then after \(kL\) steps the probability of not having reached \(G\) is at most \((1-\delta)^k\), and the indefinitely continued walk reaches \(G\) with probability one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniformly positive bounded-horizon chance of reaching the target gives geometric failure decay and almost-sure eventual hitting.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reachability property of a pure clause-focused walk when a satisfying assignment exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a CNF formula on \(n\) variables, let \(b\models F\), and let the current assignment \(a\not\models F\). Every clause \(C\) unsatisfied by \(a\) contains a variable \(x\in\operatorname{var}(C)\) with \(a_x\ne b_x\). Flipping such a variable decreases \(d_H(a,b)\) by one. Repeating this choice either reaches a satisfying assignment earlier or reaches \(b\), and therefore succeeds within at most \(n\) flips. If each focused clause contains at most \(k\) variables and its variable is chosen uniformly, the conditional probability of following one such successful sequence is at least \(k^{-n}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every unsatisfied clause contains a flip moving toward a fixed satisfying assignment; suitable focused flips therefore find some satisfying assignment within n steps, with positive probability under uniform choices.
assumptions_latex: F\text{ is a finite CNF formula on }n\text{ variables}.
b\models F.
1\leq|\operatorname{var}(C)|\leq k\text{ for every focused clause }C.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\text{ a focused sequence reaching }\{a:a\models F\}\text{ in at most }n\text{ flips},\qquad \Pr(\text{follow it})\geq k^{-n}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Success amplification for repeated finite-budget focused random walks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose each independently randomized focused-walk run reaches a target set \(G\) within its budget with probability at least \(p\). After \(r\) independent runs, the probability that none reaches \(G\) is at most \((1-p)^r\), so success probability is at least \(1-(1-p)^r\). For \(0<p<1\), failure probability at most \(\delta\in(0,1)\) is ensured by \(r\geq\lceil\log(\delta)/\log(1-p)\rceil\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent restarts turn a per-run success probability into geometric failure decay.

Other clauses may simultaneously become unsatisfied; therefore this local effect does not imply nonincreasing total MaxSAT cost.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an initial assignment \(a_0\), budget \(T\), objective \(f\), clause-focus distributions \(\mu_t(\cdot\mid a_t,H_t)\) supported on currently unsatisfied eligible clauses, and variable distributions \(\nu_t(\cdot\mid C_t,a_t,H_t)\) supported on \(\operatorname{var}(C_t)\), repeat while \(t<T\) and the stopping condition is false: sample \(C_t\sim\mu_t\), sample \(x_t\sim\nu_t\), and set \(a_{t+1}=a_t^{\oplus x_t}\). If \(\tau\leq T\) is the number of executed flips, return one assignment \(a^*\in\arg\min_{0\leq t\leq\tau}f(a_t)\), selected by the prescribed incumbent tie rule.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit focused-walk variant with break-count and noise conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a CNF formula \(F\), assignment \(a_t\), and \(p\in[0,1]\), choose an unsatisfied clause \(C_t\) uniformly. For \(x\in\operatorname{var}(C_t)\), let \(\operatorname{break}_{a_t}(x)\) be the number of currently satisfied clauses made unsatisfied by flipping \(x\). If some variable has break count zero, select uniformly among those variables; otherwise, with probability \(p\) select uniformly from \(\operatorname{var}(C_t)\), and with probability \(1-p\) select uniformly among its minimum-break variables. Flip the selected variable, repeat until satisfaction or the budget is reached, and retain a best visited assignment when used for MaxSAT.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This WalkSAT convention focuses on an unsatisfied clause and prefers zero-break moves, otherwise mixing uniform and minimum-break choices.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Random-walk MaxSAT search focused on a currently unsatisfied clause.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a weighted CNF formula \(F\), an assignment \(a_0\), and an iteration budget \(T\), repeat for \(t<T\): if \(a_t\) satisfies the target criterion, stop; otherwise choose an unsatisfied clause \(C_t\), possibly with probability proportional to its weight, and choose a variable \(x_t\in\operatorname{var}(C_t)\). knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of scaling and common-offset normalization on adaptive weighted flip scores.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a signed flip score \(s_q=\sum_C\sigma_Cq_C\), positive scaling \(q'_C=\alpha q_C\) with \(\alpha>0\) preserves all score orderings. A common offset \(q'_C=\alpha q_C+\gamma\) contributes \(\gamma\sum_C\sigma_C\); it preserves a particular score when that signed clause count is zero, but can change rankings when the compared flips have different signed clause counts.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Additive Clause Weights Encode Unsatisfied-Update Counts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed form of unsmoothed additive clause-weight updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose clause \(C\) starts with search weight \(q_C^{(0)}>0\), and at each designated update time \(t\) receives increment \(\eta_t>0\) exactly when it is unsatisfied. With no smoothing, decay, clipping, or normalization, \[q_C^{(T)}=q_C^{(0)}+\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\eta_t\mathbf 1\{a_t\not\models C\}.\] For constant \(\eta_t=\eta\), differences in accumulated increments equal \(\eta\) times differences in unsatisfied-update counts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without smoothing, an additive dynamic weight is its initial value plus increments accumulated at updates when its clause was unsatisfied.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract interface separating adaptive search penalties from the fixed MaxSAT objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A dynamic clause-weighting policy maintains positive search weights \(q^{(t)}=(q_C^{(t)})_{C\in F}\). At each designated update time it applies a specified map \(q^{(t+1)}=U_t(q^{(t)},a_t,H_t)\), where \(a_t\) is the current assignment and \(H_t\) is the available search history. The resulting weights may guide flip selection, but incumbents are compared using the fixed original objective weights \(w_C\). Additive penalties, multiplicative updates, decay or smoothing, clipping, and normalization are distinct choices of \(U_t\), not equivalent by definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dynamic clause weighting updates temporary search penalties through a specified rule while retaining the original clause weights for incumbent evaluation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weight boundedness for a specified exponential-smoothing update within dynamic clause weighting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(0<\rho_t\leq1\) and \(q_C^{(t+1)}=(1-\rho_t)q_C^{(t)}+\rho_t b_C^{(t)}\), where \(m\leq b_C^{(t)}\leq M\) for every \(C,t\). Then \[\min\{q_C^{(0)},m\}\leq q_C^{(t)}\leq\max\{q_C^{(0)},M\}\quad\text{for all }t.\] Thus this smoothing rule prevents the unbounded growth possible under unsmoothed additive penalties, although bounded weights imply neither assignment-search convergence nor target hitting.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convex-combination smoothing with bounded targets keeps adaptive clause weights bounded but does not ensure search convergence.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dynamic Weighting Alone Gives No Target-Hitting Guarantee
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absence of a generic convergence guarantee when the Boolean move policy is unrestricted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F=\{(x\lor y),(x\lor\neg y)\} and initialize (x,y)=(0,0). A policy that flips y at every iteration alternates between (0,0) and (0,1), never sets x=1, and therefore never satisfies both clauses. Arbitrary positive dynamic updates of currently unsatisfied clause weights do not change this conclusion. Hence dynamic weighting alone does not imply eventual target attainment; a hitting theorem requires assumptions on move selection, randomization, restarts, or state-space reachability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dynamic clause weights do not ensure target attainment when the move policy can cycle while ignoring a necessary variable.
assumptions_latex: Weight updates do not themselves change the Boolean assignment.
The move policy is otherwise unrestricted and flips only y.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Pr(\exists t:\,a_t\models F)=0\text{ for this deterministic policy, regardless of the positive weight-update sequence}.

Dynamic Clause-Weighting Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local-search family that adaptively penalizes persistently unsatisfied clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize positive search weights \(q_C^{(0)}\) for clauses \(C\in F\) and an assignment \(a_0\). At iteration \(t\), score candidate flips using \(q^{(t)}\), select and apply one flip, and obtain \(a_{t+1}\). If a designated stagnation or local-minimum condition holds, update \[q_C^{(t+1)}=q_C^{(t)}+\eta_t\mathbf{1}\{a_{t+1}\not\models C\},\] optionally followed by a specified smoothing or normalization operation; otherwise retain the weights. Stop at the target cost or budget, and return the best assignment measured using the original MaxSAT weights, not the adaptive search weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dynamic clause weighting raises penalties on unsatisfied clauses during stagnation, uses them to redirect flips, and evaluates incumbents with the original objective.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is finite and initial search weights satisfy \(q_C^{(0)}>0\).
Each increment satisfies \(\eta_t>0\).
Stagnation, smoothing, flip selection, and stopping rules are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Adaptive weights guide search, while returned-solution quality is evaluated by the fixed original objective \(f\).
