Neighborhood Reoptimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact or bounded reoptimization over a Boolean neighborhood of an incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a weighted MaxSAT instance with objective \(f\), incumbent assignment \(a\), and neighborhood \(N(a)\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) containing \(a\), solve or approximately solve \[b\in\arg\min_{z\in N(a)} f(z).\] Accept \(b\) whenever \(f(b)<f(a)\); otherwise retain \(a\). Neighborhoods may be defined by freeing selected variables and fixing all others, or by a Hamming-radius constraint. Repeat under a specified neighborhood schedule and stop at its budget. Exact neighborhood solution makes every accepted step strictly improving and certifies neighborhood optimality when no improving \(b\) exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reoptimize the MaxSAT objective inside a chosen neighborhood, accept strict improvement, and certify local optimality when that neighborhood is solved exactly.
assumptions_latex: The Boolean instance and objective \(f\) are fixed.
Each neighborhood contains its incumbent.
Every neighborhood subproblem is solved exactly when a local-optimality certificate is claimed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact solution with \(f(b)\geq f(a)\) certifies \(f(a)=\min_{z\in N(a)}f(z)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The leaf appropriately contains an algorithm, but the displayed argmin requires exact solution while the prose simultaneously permits approximate solution. A MaxSAT neighborhood-search source is needed to separate the exact certificate-bearing variant from bounded or approximate variants.

children.title: Relaxation-Guided Search
children.top_down_role: Search families guided by relaxed objective or feasibility information.

assumptions_latex: \(R(a)\) is a tractable relaxation of the Boolean MaxSAT formulation at incumbent \(a\).
The relaxation produces a solution \(r\) and associated information used by a specified rule to select \(S\).
Every neighborhood candidate is evaluated by the original objective \(f\).
The acceptance and stopping rules are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted incumbent \(a^+\) satisfies \(f(a^+)<f(a)\), while information from \(R(a)\) determines the searched neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Neighborhood selection guided by a tractable relaxation of Boolean MaxSAT.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an incumbent \(a\), construct a tractable relaxation \(R(a)\) of the Boolean MaxSAT formulation and compute a relaxation solution \(r\), together with any reduced-cost, marginal, or violation information supplied by the relaxation. Use this information under a specified rule to choose a variable set \(S\), define \[N_S(a)=\{z\in\{0,1\}^n:z_i=a_i\text{ for every }i\notin S\},\] and reoptimize the original objective \(f\) over \(N_S(a)\). Accept a candidate \(a^+\) only when \(f(a^+)<f(a)\), update the relaxation if prescribed, and repeat until the target or budget is reached. Relaxation information guides neighborhood selection but does not replace evaluation by \(f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve a tractable relaxation, use its signals to select free variables, and reoptimize the original MaxSAT objective in the resulting neighborhood, accepting only strict improvements.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Guided Search

assumptions_latex: The original objective \(f\) is evaluated exactly.
The entire neighborhood \(N_S(a)\) is optimized rather than sampled.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f(a)=\min_{z\in N_S(a)}f(z).

notation.meaning: neighborhood obtained by fixing variables outside S

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate supplied by exact exhaustion of the relaxation-selected neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For incumbent \(a\) and selected free-variable set \(S\), let \(N_S(a)=\{z\in\{0,1\}^n:z_i=a_i\text{ for }i\notin S\}\). If exact optimization over \(N_S(a)\) returns no \(z\) with \(f(z)<f(a)\), then \(a\) minimizes \(f\) over that neighborhood. This is a global-optimality certificate only if the neighborhood contains every feasible assignment of the original problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact failure to improve over the entire selected neighborhood certifies neighborhood-local optimality, becoming global only when that neighborhood covers the full feasible set.
knowledge_statements.title: Neighborhood-Local Optimality at Exhaustion

assumptions_latex: \(n<\infty\).
Every accepted replacement satisfies \(f(a_{t+1})<f(a_t)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \#\{t:a_{t+1}\text{ is accepted}\}\leq 2^n-1.

notation.meaning: original objective minimized by the search

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bound on accepted strict-improvement moves in the finite Boolean assignment space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb{R}\). If relaxation-guided search replaces its incumbent only by \(a_{t+1}\) satisfying \(f(a_{t+1})<f(a_t)\), no incumbent can repeat and at most \(2^n-1\) replacements can be accepted. This bounds accepted moves, not the work spent generating or solving neighborhoods.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict improvement prevents repeated incumbents, so at most 2^n minus 1 moves are accepted; neighborhood-solving time is not thereby bounded.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Strict-Improvement Termination

assumptions_latex: No independent valid bound, infeasibility certificate, or exhaustive coverage argument applies to assignments outside the searched neighborhoods.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{relaxation guidance alone}\not\Rightarrow\text{sound pruning or global optimality}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between heuristic neighborhood guidance and certified exclusion of assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A relaxation solution, reduced cost, marginal, or violation signal may rank variables or neighborhoods, but without a valid implication for the original Boolean problem it proves neither infeasibility nor nonimprovement of excluded assignments. A search restricted to relaxation-selected neighborhoods is therefore generally incomplete, and its terminal incumbent need not be globally optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relaxation signals can guide neighborhood choice but cannot by themselves justify pruning or global optimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Guidance Does Not Certify Pruning

children.title: Partition-Based Search
children.top_down_role: Search families organized around decomposed clause or variable regions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block-coordinate reoptimization of a finite Boolean minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition the variables into nonempty blocks \(S_1,\ldots,S_k\). From feasible assignment \(a\), visit a block \(S_j\), fix every variable outside \(S_j\), solve the induced subproblem exactly, and replace \(a\) only by a strict improvement under the original objective. If an exact full sweep visits every block and accepts no update, then no feasible assignment differing from \(a\) only within one block has smaller objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exactly reoptimize one variable block at a time, accept strict improvements, and certify blockwise local optimality after an unimproving exact full sweep.
assumptions_latex: S_1,\ldots,S_k\text{ partition the finite Boolean variable set}.
Every visited block subproblem is solved exactly when blockwise local optimality is claimed.
Only strict improvements under the original objective are accepted.
A full sweep visits every block.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f(a)\leq f(z)\text{ for every feasible }z\text{ differing from }a\text{ only within one }S_j.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Partition-Based Search

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counts accepted incumbent changes, not exact block-solve effort or unsuccessful visits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Because every accepted update strictly decreases \(f\) and \(F\) is finite, partition-based search accepts at most \(|\{f(x):x\in F\}|-1\) updates. This gives no polynomial runtime bound: an exact block subproblem may be exponentially hard, and an unspecified schedule may perform arbitrarily many nonimproving visits.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strictly improving block search accepts finitely many updates, although exact block solves can remain computationally hard.
assumptions_latex: F\text{ is finite}.
Every accepted block update strictly decreases }f.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{accepted}}\leq|\{f(x):x\in F\}|-1.

notation.meaning: Set of distinct attainable objective values

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Blockwise Local Optimality Is Not Global Optimality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite Boolean objective representable as a pseudo-Boolean function or weighted Boolean optimization instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_1=\{1\}\), \(S_2=\{2\}\), and set \(f(0,0)=1\), \(f(1,0)=f(0,1)=2\), and \(f(1,1)=0\). At \((0,0)\), changing either block alone increases the objective, so an exact strict-improvement sweep accepts no update; nevertheless \((1,1)\) is globally better.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Singleton-block search can stop where either one-variable change is worse even though changing both variables is globally better.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (0,0)\text{ is blockwise locally optimal but not globally optimal.}
knowledge_statements.title: Blockwise Local Optimality Is Not Global Optimality

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between block reoptimization and neighborhood reoptimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For block \(S_j\), define \(N_j(a)=\{z\in F:z_i=a_i\text{ for every }i\notin S_j\}\). Exact block reoptimization is exactly minimization of \(f\) over \(N_j(a)\); partition-based search is neighborhood reoptimization with neighborhood family \(\{N_1,\ldots,N_k\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reoptimizing a block is neighborhood optimization over feasible assignments agreeing with the incumbent outside that block.
assumptions_latex: S_1,\ldots,S_k\text{ are variable blocks}.
a\in F.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min\{f(z):z\in F,\ z_i=a_i\ \forall i\notin S_j\}=\min_{z\in N_j(a)}f(z).

notation.meaning: Feasible assignments reachable by changing only block j

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Induced Neighborhood Representation

assumptions_latex: \(S_1,\ldots,S_k\) partition the finite Boolean variable set.
For each visited block, the induced subproblem is solved exactly while variables outside that block are fixed to the current incumbent.
The incumbent is replaced only by a strict improvement under the original objective \(f\).
A full sweep visits every block.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If a full exact sweep leaves \(a\) unchanged, then \(f(a)\leq f(z)\) for every \(z\) differing from \(a\) only within one block \(S_j\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Search by reoptimizing blocks of Boolean variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition the Boolean variables into nonempty blocks \(S_1,\ldots,S_k\). Starting from an assignment \(a\), select a block \(S_j\), fix every variable outside \(S_j\) to its value in the current assignment, and solve the induced weighted MaxSAT subproblem over \(S_j\) exactly. Replace \(a\) only when the resulting assignment has strictly smaller original objective value, and continue according to a specified block schedule. If a full sweep visits every block and leaves \(a\) unchanged, then \(a\) is blockwise locally optimal: no assignment differing from \(a\) only within one block has lower cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partition variables into blocks, exactly reoptimize one block at a time while fixing the others, accept only strict improvements, and obtain blockwise local optimality when a full sweep leaves the incumbent unchanged.
knowledge_statements.title: Partition-Based Search

children.title: Cross-Partition Coordination
children.top_down_role: Information exchange and consistency across search partitions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency condition for combining complete assignments proposed on overlapping variable subsets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_1,\ldots,S_k\) cover the variables and let \(a^{(j)}\in\{0,1\}^{S_j}\). A global assignment having each \(a^{(j)}\) as its restriction exists exactly when \(a_i^{(j)}=a_i^{(\ell)}\) for every \(i\in S_j\cap S_\ell\). When it exists it is unique on the covered variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Assignments proposed by overlapping partitions combine exactly when they agree on every shared variable.
assumptions_latex: \bigcup_{j=1}^kS_j\text{ is the global variable set}.
a^{(j)}\text{ assigns every variable in }S_j.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists!a:\ a|_{S_j}=a^{(j)}\ \forall j\iff a_i^{(j)}=a_i^{(\ell)}\ \forall i\in S_j\cap S_\ell,\forall j,\ell.
knowledge_statements.title: Overlap-Agreement Composability

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient structural separability test for clause, pseudo-Boolean-factor, or other finite Boolean factor representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent each hard constraint and each nonconstant objective factor by a hyperedge equal to its variable scope. If disjoint blocks \(S_1,\ldots,S_k\) cover the variables and every hyperedge is contained in one block, feasibility and objective value separate by block, so independently optimal block assignments combine to a global optimum. A hyperedge intersecting multiple blocks is a syntactic coordination factor; ignoring it need not preserve feasibility or optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When every constraint and objective factor is contained in one disjoint block, independent block optimization is exact; cross-block factors require treatment by coordination or reformulation.
assumptions_latex: The Boolean model is expressed as hard-constraint and objective factors with explicit variable scopes.
S_1,\ldots,S_k\text{ are disjoint and cover all variables}.
Every factor scope is contained in one block.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_{x\in F}f(x)=\sum_{j=1}^k\min_{x_{S_j}\in F_j}f_j(x_{S_j})\text{ under the stated factorization.}
knowledge_statements.title: Interaction-Hypergraph Coordination Boundary
Cross-Partition Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency condition for combining assignments proposed by interacting partitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let variable subsets \(S_1,\ldots,S_k\) cover the variables and let local assignments \(a^{(j)}\in\{0,1\}^{S_j}\) be proposed by partition subproblems. They are directly composable exactly when \[a_i^{(j)}=a_i^{(\ell)}\quad\text{for every }i\in S_j\cap S_\ell.\] Under this agreement condition there is a unique global assignment on the covered variables whose restriction to each \(S_j\) equals \(a^{(j)}\). If agreement fails, coordination must reconcile shared variables or reoptimize coupling clauses; independently concatenating the local assignments is not well-defined and need not preserve their predicted objective improvements.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Overlapping partition solutions combine consistently only when they agree on shared variables; otherwise shared variables or coupling clauses require reconciliation.
assumptions_latex: \(S_1,\ldots,S_k\) cover the global variable set.
Each \(a^{(j)}\) assigns every variable in \(S_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A global assignment with restrictions \(a^{(j)}\) exists exactly when all overlap equalities hold, and it is then unique.

notation.meaning: variables shared by partitions j and ell

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The overlap-agreement criterion is mathematically precise, plain text matches the formulas, and condition fits the leaf. No source is provided for its use as a cross-partition coordination statement in this MaxSAT search family.

assumptions_latex: The Boolean optimization problem is a minimization problem with feasible set \(F\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) and objective \(f:F\to\mathbb{R}\).
Reports are indexed by nondecreasing times \(t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every reported incumbent is feasible, and its value is a valid nonincreasing upper bound on the optimum.

Incumbent solution and its reported objective value at time t

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimization convention; maximization reverses the bound direction.

source_refs.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An anytime incumbent report at time \(t\) is either the symbol “no incumbent” with value \(U(t)=+\infty\), or a pair \((x^{\mathrm{inc}}(t),U(t))\) satisfying \(x^{\mathrm{inc}}(t)\in F\) and \(U(t)=f(x^{\mathrm{inc}}(t))\). Consequently \(f^*\leq U(t)\). An incumbent-management interface retains the best reported value, so for \(t_1\leq t_2\) it satisfies \(U(t_2)\leq U(t_1)\). Reporting an incumbent asserts feasibility and its attained objective value, but does not assert optimality unless a matching valid lower bound is also available.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An anytime incumbent is a feasible solution whose value upper-bounds the minimum. Retaining the best incumbent makes reported values nonincreasing, without implying optimality by itself.
knowledge_statements.title: Anytime Incumbent Reporting

source_witnesses.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

assumptions_latex: The Boolean optimization problem is a minimization problem with optimum \(f^*=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\).
Each reported bound is justified by a sound relaxation, dual certificate, or exhaustive search argument.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The retained lower bound satisfies \(L(t)\leq f^*\) and may be made nondecreasing over time.

notation.meaning: Valid lower bound reported at time t
Best incumbent value reported at time t

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covers certified bounds for minimization, including incomplete runs.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 7. Cuts, Lower Bounds and Box Reduction p. 83
source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A lower-bound report at time \(t\) is a number \(L(t)\in\mathbb{R}\cup\{-\infty\}\) accompanied by a sound justification that \(L(t)\leq f^*\). The management interface may retain \(L(t)=\max_{s\leq t}\widehat L(s)\), where every raw report \(\widehat L(s)\) is valid; hence \(L(t)\) is nondecreasing and remains valid. If an incumbent value \(U(t)\) is available, \(L(t)\leq f^*\leq U(t)\). Equality \(L(t)=U(t)\) certifies optimality, while an incomplete run need not make the gap vanish.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reported lower bound must be sound for the current minimization problem. Taking the maximum of all valid reports preserves validity and yields a nondecreasing bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Anytime Lower-Bound Reporting

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 7. Cuts, Lower Bounds and Box Reduction p. 83
source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aggregation of global or conditional lower-bound reports for a fixed minimization objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose report \(i\) certifies \(L_i\leq\inf_{x\in F\cap R_i}f(x)\). For a current region \(R\), \(L=\max_i L_i\) is valid whenever every included report applies throughout \(R\), in particular when \(R\subseteq R_i\) for every \(i\). A report restricted to a proper subregion, another model version, or another objective convention cannot be promoted to a bound for \(R\) merely by taking a maximum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximum aggregation is sound only for lower bounds whose validity scopes all contain the current search region.
assumptions_latex: L_i\leq\inf_{x\in F\cap R_i}f(x)\text{ for every included report }i.
R\subseteq R_i\text{ for every included report }i.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \max_i L_i\leq\inf_{x\in F\cap R}f(x).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Objective Lower Bounds Do Not Certify Infeasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates an objective lower-bound report from a certificate that the feasible set is empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the convention \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\), every finite \(L\) satisfies \(L\leq f^*\) when \(F=\varnothing\), but the same inequality can hold for a feasible problem. Thus a lower-bound report alone cannot certify infeasibility; a separate certificate that \(F=\varnothing\) is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid objective lower bound alone cannot distinguish infeasibility from a feasible problem with a larger optimum.
assumptions_latex: f^*=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\text{ with }\inf\varnothing=+\infty.
L\in\mathbb{R}\text{ and }L\leq f^*.

children.title: Independent Portfolio Search
children.top_down_role: Portfolio configurations whose constituent searches operate without shared search state.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aggregation applies only to verified reports for the same instance and validity scope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Run workers without inter-worker feedback. At stopping time \(T\), return the feasible incumbent having value \(\min_i U_i(T)\) among workers that reported one, and the bound \(\max_i L_i(T)\) among compatible globally valid lower-bound reports. If no worker reported an incumbent, report no incumbent; if no worker reported a compatible finite lower bound, retain the designated trivial bound such as \(-\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Run configured solvers without communication and aggregate only their compatible final incumbent and lower-bound reports.
assumptions_latex: Every worker solves the same minimization instance.
Every aggregated incumbent is verified feasible and every aggregated lower bound is globally valid for that instance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f^*\leq\min_i U_i(T),\qquad \max_i L_i(T)\leq f^*\text{ whenever the corresponding report sets are nonempty.}

notation.meaning: Incumbent value reported by worker i at stopping
Compatible global lower bound reported by worker i at stopping

knowledge_statements.title: Independent Run-and-Aggregate Portfolio

knowledge_statements.scope_note: No-communication definition; common read-only input and final report collection are permitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An independent portfolio has factorized worker evolution: \(\sigma_i(0{:}T)\) is determined by the common instance, worker \(i\)'s configuration, private randomness, and allocated resources, but not by another worker's state or reports before stopping. Concurrent and time-sliced execution are variants when they preserve those allocations and introduce no feedback.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent workers share the input but no mutable search information; each trajectory depends only on its own setup, randomness, and resources.
assumptions_latex: Worker configurations, seeds, and resource allocations are fixed independently of other workers' search reports.
Final collection does not feed information back into an active worker.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sigma_i(0{:}T)\perp\!\!\!\perp\{\sigma_j(0{:}T):j\neq i\}\mid(I,c_i,\omega_i,r_i)\text{ in the operational no-feedback sense.}

notation.meaning: Common instance, configuration, private randomness, and resources of worker i

knowledge_statements.title: Independent Portfolio State Factorization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case boundary; it does not deny empirical diversification benefits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Independent diversification has no unconditional speedup or success dominance. A solver may require more resources than any individual allocation but no more than the total portfolio budget; then every split run fails while one uninterrupted run with the total budget succeeds. Performance guarantees require assumptions on runtime distributions, allocations, or complementarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Splitting a fixed budget among independent workers can be worse than assigning it to one uninterrupted run.
assumptions_latex: A fixed total budget is divided among at least two workers.
Success may require an uninterrupted resource threshold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Independent portfolio execution does not universally dominate a single full-budget run.}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed success criterion and allocations; correlated outcomes require their actual union probability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the within-budget success events \(E_1,\ldots,E_k\) are mutually independent and \(\Pr(E_i)=p_i\), then \(\Pr(\bigcup_iE_i)=1-\prod_i(1-p_i)\). Without stochastic independence, the product expression need not hold.

assumptions_latex: E_1,\ldots,E_k\text{ are mutually independent}.
\Pr(E_i)=p_i.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Pr\!\left(\bigcup_{i=1}^kE_i\right)=1-\prod_{i=1}^k(1-p_i).

Within-allocation success probability of worker i

assumptions_latex: A finite portfolio contains solvers \(S_1,\ldots,S_k\) for the same Boolean optimization instance.
Each solver has a resource allocation and independently maintained internal state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The portfolio returns the best valid incumbent and bound among completed reports, without exchanging search information between solvers.

notation.meaning: Incumbent and lower-bound reports produced by solver i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent parallel or interleaved search with only final report aggregation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize each \(S_i\) on the same instance with its assigned configuration or random seed and with no shared mutable search state. Execute the solvers concurrently or by a fixed resource schedule. During search, solver \(S_i\) may emit valid reports \((U_i(t),L_i(t))\), but no learned constraints, branching data, incumbents, bounds, or state are sent to another solver. At a stopping time \(T\), return an incumbent attaining \(\min_i U_i(T)\) when one exists, together with the valid aggregate lower bound \(\max_i L_i(T)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Run differently configured solvers on the same instance without communication, then aggregate their valid reports by taking the best incumbent and strongest lower bound.

children.title: Cooperative Portfolio Search
children.top_down_role: Portfolio configurations whose constituent searches exchange useful state.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic cooperative search loop; message schemas and validation mechanisms are owned by Information-Sharing Interfaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize workers on the common problem and repeatedly allocate resources, collect exported search information, admit only messages whose semantics and validity conditions are preserved for the receiver, and allow workers to continue from their updated states. At interruption, return the best verified incumbent and any compatible certified bound obtained by the workers. Shared information used only as guidance need not be a certificate, but information used for pruning or certified conclusions must be valid in the receiver's scope.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cooperative workers exchange information during search, validating every message used for pruning or certification and aggregating only compatible final reports.
assumptions_latex: Workers use a common model or validity-preserving translations.
Every imported claim used for pruning or certification is validated for the receiver's current model and scope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Validated imports preserve the correctness guarantees of the receiving searches.}
knowledge_statements.title: Validated Cooperative Portfolio Loop

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Behavioral definition of cooperation, independent of a particular message transport or solver technology.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A portfolio is cooperative when there exist distinct workers \(i\neq j\), a time \(t\), and information \(m_j\) produced by worker \(j\) such that importing \(m_j\) can change worker \(i\)'s subsequent search state or decisions before final result collection. Mere final aggregation of independently produced reports is not cooperation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A portfolio is cooperative when information produced by one worker can influence another worker during search.
assumptions_latex: At least two workers solve a common instance or explicitly translated equivalent instances.
Information may be exchanged before final result collection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists i\neq j,t,m_j:\ \sigma_i(t^+;m_j)\neq\sigma_i(t^+;\varnothing).

notation.meaning: Search state of worker i at time t

knowledge_statements.title: Cooperative Portfolio Search

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correctness boundary for certificate-affecting imports.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If an imported bound, learned constraint, core, or incumbent is valid only on region \(R\), under assumptions \(A\), or for model version \(v\), it may affect certified search only where those conditions remain true. Unvalidated promotion to a global claim can remove feasible solutions, overstate a lower bound, or accept an infeasible incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Using a local, stale, or incompatible message outside its validity conditions can make cooperative search unsound.
assumptions_latex: A received message has conditional scope, assumptions, or model-version metadata.
The receiver proposes to use the message for pruning or certification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Validity outside the message's certified conditions is not guaranteed.}

notation.meaning: Model version under which the message was established

knowledge_statements.title: Unsafe Cooperative Import Boundary

children.title: Information-Sharing Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Interfaces for exchanging incumbents, bounds, cores, or search guidance.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract semantic contract independent of serialization and transport.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An information-sharing interface specifies an encoder, decoder, message schema, and admission rule. A decoded claim may affect certified search only when its claim type, model and objective version, validity scope, asserted content, and required witness or certificate are preserved and applicable to the receiver's current state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sharing interface must preserve message meaning, model identity, scope, and validation evidence before a claim affects certified search.
assumptions_latex: Sender and receiver use the same instance or an explicit validity-preserving translation.
Messages carry sufficient metadata to determine type, model version, objective convention, scope, and validation requirements.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Admitted certificate-affecting messages retain their asserted semantics for the receiver.}
knowledge_statements.title: Semantic Information-Sharing Interface

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional bounds retain their scopes and cannot automatically enter a global maximum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For one minimization instance, verified feasible incumbent reports merge by \(U=\min_iU_i\), and compatible globally valid lower-bound reports merge by \(L=\max_jL_j\). Both operations are associative, commutative, idempotent, and monotone in information content. A conditional lower bound may participate only in an aggregate whose target region is contained in its validity region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compatible incumbent values merge by minimum and compatible global lower bounds by maximum; conditional information retains its scope.
assumptions_latex: Every U_i\text{ is attained by a verified feasible solution of the common instance}.
Every L_j\text{ is a compatible globally valid lower bound for the common instance}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L=\max_jL_j\leq f^*\leq U=\min_iU_i.
knowledge_statements.title: Validity-Preserving Report Merge

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic representation; concrete wire formats are interchangeable only when decoding preserves every component.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A search-information message can be represented as \(m=(\tau,v,s,c,w)\), where \(\tau\) is the claim type, \(v\) the model and objective version, \(s\) its global or conditional validity scope, \(c\) the asserted incumbent, bound, learned constraint, core, or guidance datum, and \(w\) any witness required for validation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A shareable search message identifies its claim type, model version, validity scope, asserted content, and validation evidence.
assumptions_latex: The message communicates a mathematical claim or search-guidance datum.
Sender and receiver may use different internal representations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: m=(\tau,v,s,c,w).

notation.meaning: Typed message containing claim type, version, scope, content, and witness

knowledge_statements.title: Typed Search-Information Message

assumptions_latex: Sender and receiver agree on the optimization instance or on an explicit variable and objective translation.
Messages carry enough metadata to determine their scope, version, and validity conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A message is admissible exactly when decoding, compatibility, and semantic validation preserve the claim it communicates.

notation.meaning: Encoding and decoding maps for shared messages

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic contract for exchanging search information across heterogeneous workers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An information-sharing interface consists of an encoder \(E\), decoder \(D\), message schema, and admissibility predicate \(A(m,\sigma_s,\sigma_r)\). A message \(m\) may affect the receiver only if decoding succeeds, referenced variables and objective conventions agree, the message is applicable to the receiver’s current state, and its claimed semantics are independently checked or follow from a trusted certificate. For every admitted incumbent, decoded feasibility and objective value must be preserved; for every admitted bound or learned constraint, validity for the common instance must be preserved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sharing interface must decode messages unambiguously and verify instance, representation, scope, and semantic validity before shared information can alter another worker’s search.
knowledge_statements.title: Information-Sharing Interfaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition is locally appropriate, but the claimed exact admissibility contract and its sufficiency depend on a formally specified interface or proof protocol for which no source is supplied.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polynomial-Time Verification in Explicit Proof Length
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Checking complexity for explicitly encoded cutting-planes derivations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an explicitly encoded cutting-planes derivation \(\pi\), each line can be checked by exact integer arithmetic against its cited premises and declared rule. For a fixed polynomial-time checkable rule encoding, verification runs in time polynomial in the total bit length \(|F|+|\pi|\). This output-sensitive bound does not imply that every unsatisfiable pseudo-Boolean instance has a polynomial-length refutation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An explicit cutting-planes proof is checkable in polynomial time in its bit length, even though proofs need not have polynomial length.
assumptions_latex: Premise indices, multipliers, divisors, and coefficients are explicitly binary encoded.
Every declared local rule is polynomial-time checkable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_{\mathrm{verify}}(F,\pi)\le\operatorname{poly}(|F|+|\pi|).

notation.meaning: Total binary encoding length of the derivation.

knowledge_statements.title: Polynomial-Time Verification in Explicit Proof Length

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete failure of division without the prescribed coefficient rounding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: From the valid Boolean inequality \(x+y\ge1\), dividing by \(2\), rounding the right-hand side upward, but rounding the coefficients downward would produce \(0x+0y\ge1\). This conclusion is false at the satisfying assignment \((x,y)=(1,0)\). Hence arbitrary coefficient rounding is not a sound cutting-planes division rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Naively dividing and rounding coefficients downward can turn a satisfiable inequality into a contradiction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x+y\ge1\not\models 0\ge1.
knowledge_statements.title: Unsound Naive Division

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete rule schema for nonnegative pseudo-Boolean inequalities over literals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write normalized inequalities as \(\sum_j a_j\ell_j\ge A\), where \(a_j\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) and \(\ell_j\in\{x_i,1-x_i\}\). The cutting-planes rules include nonnegative integer combination and positive integer division. From \(C,D\), derive \(\lambda C+\mu D\) for \(\lambda,\mu\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\). From \(\sum_j a_j\ell_j\ge A\) and \(d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), derive \(\sum_j\lceil a_j/d\rceil\ell_j\ge\lceil A/d\rceil\). Together with Boolean axioms and exact normalization, these rules preserve truth under every Boolean assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalized cutting planes combines inequalities with nonnegative integer multipliers and divides using upward rounding of coefficients and the right-hand side.
assumptions_latex: All literals take values in \(\{0,1\}\).
Coefficients are normalized to nonnegative integers before applying the displayed division rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C_1,\ldots,C_k\models_{\{0,1\}^n}D\text{ for every inequality }D\text{ produced by these rules}.

notation.meaning: A positive or complemented Boolean literal.

knowledge_statements.title: Normalized Cutting-Planes Inference Rules

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Refutational Completeness of Boolean Cutting Planes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Completeness of the fixed standard cutting-planes variant over finite Boolean systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every finite unsatisfiable set \(F\) of integer pseudo-Boolean inequalities, the standard cutting-planes system with Boolean axioms, sound nonnegative combination, and sound integer division with rounding admits a finite derivation of a contradictory constant inequality. Thus the system is refutationally complete over \(\{0,1\}^n\); this assertion gives no polynomial bound on refutation length.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every unsatisfiable finite pseudo-Boolean system has a finite cutting-planes refutation, although the refutation need not be short.
assumptions_latex: The fixed rule set is the standard refutationally complete Boolean cutting-planes calculus.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{x\in\{0,1\}^n:x\models F\}=\varnothing\Longrightarrow F\vdash_{\mathrm{CP}}0\ge1.

notation.meaning: Derivability in the fixed cutting-planes calculus.

knowledge_statements.title: Refutational Completeness of Boolean Cutting Planes

assumptions_latex: Variables are Boolean and initial constraints are integer linear inequalities.
Every inference uses a declared sound cutting-planes rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Deriving \(0\geq1\) is a checkable certificate that the initial pseudo-Boolean constraints are infeasible.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Refutational cutting-planes system over Boolean inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A cutting-planes derivation from \(F\) is a finite sequence of integer linear inequalities in which each line is an initial constraint, a Boolean axiom \(x_i\geq0\) or \(-x_i\geq-1\), or follows from earlier lines by a declared sound rule. Core rules include addition after multiplication by nonnegative integers and sound integer division with rounding. Every derived line is valid for all Boolean assignments satisfying \(F\). A cutting-planes refutation ends with the contradictory inequality \(0\geq1\), thereby certifying that no assignment in \(\{0,1\}^n\) satisfies \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cutting-planes proof derives valid integer inequalities from pseudo-Boolean constraints and Boolean axioms. Reaching the contradiction zero at least one certifies infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Cutting-Planes Proofs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The refutational idea is standard and the certificate kind fits, but the exact cutting-planes rules—especially integer division and rounding—must be fixed and supported by an authoritative proof-system source.

children.title: RUP Proofs
children.top_down_role: RUP-style justification within pseudo-Boolean certification workflows.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polynomial-Time Verification of a RUP Addition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case verification cost for one abstract clausal RUP check.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an explicit clause database containing \(L\) literal occurrences, a candidate clause \(C\) can be RUP-checked by adding the temporary assumptions \(\{\neg\ell:\ell\in C\}\) and running indexed unit propagation. A queue-and-occurrence implementation takes \(O(L+|C|)\) time per fresh check, including initialization or reset work.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One RUP addition is polynomial-time checkable; a fresh indexed propagation check is linear in the explicit clause data and candidate length.
assumptions_latex: The clause database is finite and explicit.
Propagation maintains occurrence counters or equivalent linear-time indexing.
The bound includes initialization or restoration of propagation state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_{\mathrm{RUP}}(F,C)=O(L+|C|).

notation.meaning: Number of literal occurrences in the current clause database.

knowledge_statements.title: Polynomial-Time Verification of a RUP Addition

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Deletion Can Destroy Future RUP Admissibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational effect of deleting clauses needed by later propagation checks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: There exist \(F\), \(D\in F\), and \(C\) such that \(C\) is RUP relative to \(F\) but not relative to \(F\setminus\{D\}\). Thus deletion preserves the logical soundness of the remaining database but can invalidate a later RUP check.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deleting a clause can make a later addition fail RUP because admissibility is tested against the current database.
assumptions_latex: RUP admissibility is evaluated against the current clause database.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists F,D,C:\operatorname{RUP}_F(C)\land\neg\operatorname{RUP}_{F\setminus\{D\}}(C).

notation.meaning: Clause C passes reverse unit propagation relative to F.

knowledge_statements.title: Deletion Can Destroy Future RUP Admissibility

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistence of a RUP propagation contradiction under database strengthening.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If exhaustive unit propagation derives contradiction from \(F\land\bigwedge_{\ell\in C}\neg\ell\), then it also derives contradiction from \((F\land G)\land\bigwedge_{\ell\in C}\neg\ell\) for every conjunction of clauses \(G\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding clauses cannot invalidate an existing RUP propagation contradiction.
assumptions_latex: F\text{ and }G\text{ are conjunctions of clauses}.
C\text{ is a clause}.
\operatorname{UP}(F\land\bigwedge_{\ell\in C}\neg\ell)=\bot.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{UP}((F\land G)\land\bigwedge_{\ell\in C}\neg\ell)=\bot.
knowledge_statements.title: RUP Monotonicity under Clause Addition

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Format-independent operational checker for clause additions and deletions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize the current database with the input CNF. For an addition record \(C\), temporarily assume every literal of \(C\) false, run exhaustive unit propagation, and insert \(C\) only if contradiction is reached; then restore the temporary propagation state. For a deletion, validate its identifier and remove that live occurrence. Accept an unsatisfiability claim only after a checked addition of the empty clause.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The checker processes records in order, RUP-checks additions against the current database, validates deletions, and accepts unsatisfiability only at a checked empty clause.
assumptions_latex: \text{Identifiers select unambiguous live clause occurrences}.
\text{Parsing rejects malformed literals and records}.
\text{Temporary propagation state is restored soundly after each check}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{AcceptRefutation}(F,T)\Rightarrow F\text{ is unsatisfiable}.

notation.meaning: Ordered RUP addition and deletion sequence.

knowledge_statements.title: Abstract RUP Sequence Checker

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unsatisfiability certificate produced by an accepted RUP sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_0\) be the input CNF. If every added clause in a finite sequence is RUP-admissible relative to the database at its addition point, every deletion merely removes an identified live clause, and the sequence accepts addition of the empty clause, then \(F_0\) is unsatisfiable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An accepted RUP sequence ending with the empty clause certifies unsatisfiability of the original CNF.
assumptions_latex: \text{Every addition is checked against the current database}.
\text{Every deletion identifies an existing clause and adds no consequence}.
\text{The final accepted addition is the empty clause}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F_0\models\bot.
knowledge_statements.title: Empty-Clause RUP Refutation Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract clausal reverse-unit-propagation proof system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a current finite clause database \(F\) and clause \(C=\ell_1\lor\cdots\lor\ell_r\), \(C\) is RUP-admissible exactly when exhaustive unit propagation on \(F\land\neg\ell_1\land\cdots\land\neg\ell_r\) derives contradiction. A RUP sequence processes additions against the database then current and may delete identified live clause occurrences; every addition must pass at its position.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A clause passes RUP when assuming all its literals false makes unit propagation contradict the current database.
assumptions_latex: F\text{ is a finite conjunction of clauses}.
\text{Clause and literal syntax is well formed}.
\text{Unit propagation is exhaustive and sound}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{RUP}_F(C)\iff\operatorname{UP}\!\left(F\land\bigwedge_{\ell\in C}\neg\ell\right)=\bot.

notation.meaning: RUP admissibility of C relative to F.

knowledge_statements.title: RUP Admissibility and Proof-Sequence Semantics

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical implication certified by a successful RUP check.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If sound unit propagation derives contradiction from \(F\land\neg C\), then \(F\land\neg C\) is unsatisfiable and therefore \(F\models C\). Consequently \(F\) and \(F\land C\) have identical satisfying assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every RUP-admissible clause is logically implied by the current database.
assumptions_latex: \operatorname{RUP}_F(C).
\text{Unit propagation is sound}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\models C\quad\text{and}\quad\operatorname{Mod}(F)=\operatorname{Mod}(F\land C).
knowledge_statements.title: Soundness of RUP Addition

assumptions_latex: The current formula \(F\) is a conjunction of clauses over Boolean literals.
Unit propagation is performed on \(F\) together with temporary assumptions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A clause \(C\) is RUP-admissible when unit propagation on \(F\land\neg C\) derives contradiction.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard clausal reverse-unit-propagation admissibility test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The clause \(C=\ell_1\lor\cdots\lor\ell_r\) has the reverse unit propagation property relative to \(F\) if unit propagation from \(F\) under the temporary assumptions \(\neg\ell_1,\ldots,\neg\ell_r\) derives the empty clause. This propagation contradiction establishes \(F\models C\), so adding \(C\) preserves the satisfying assignments of \(F\). A RUP proof is a sequence of clause additions passing this test, optionally with deletions that do not affect soundness; deriving the empty clause certifies unsatisfiability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A clause passes RUP when assuming all its literals false makes unit propagation contradict the current formula. Such a clause is implied and can be added soundly.
knowledge_statements.title: RUP Proofs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The clausal RUP test is stated coherently and the certificate role fits, but no inspectable source supports the precise proof sequence and deletion semantics.

children.title: Clausal PB Proofs
children.top_down_role: Clausal proof representations for pseudo-Boolean reasoning.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Not Every PB Inequality Is One Clausal Line
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expressiveness boundary of unit-coefficient, right-hand-side-one constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x,y,z\in\{0,1\}\), the threshold \(x+y+z\geq2\) is not equivalent to any single clause. It is equivalent to \((x\lor y)\land(x\lor z)\land(y\lor z)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A general PB threshold may require several clauses; the two-of-three threshold is a simple example.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x+y+z\geq2\equiv(x\lor y)\land(x\lor z)\land(y\lor z),\quad\text{but not one clause}.
knowledge_statements.title: Not Every PB Inequality Is One Clausal Line

assumptions_latex: Each Boolean literal \(\ell\) has value in \(\{0,1\}\).
Clauses are represented as pseudo-Boolean inequalities with unit coefficients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequality \(\sum_{j=1}^r\ell_j\geq1\) is satisfied exactly when the corresponding clause is satisfied.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clause-as-inequality fragment of pseudo-Boolean proof logging.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Encode a positive literal \(x_i\) by \(x_i\), a negative literal \(\neg x_i\) by \(1-x_i\), and a clause \(C=\ell_1\lor\cdots\lor\ell_r\) by \(P(C):\sum_{j=1}^r\ell_j\geq1\). For every Boolean assignment \(\alpha\), \(\alpha\models C\) if and only if \(\alpha\models P(C)\). A clausal pseudo-Boolean proof restricts logged constraints to these unit-coefficient inequalities and admits a new line only through its specified sound clausal or pseudo-Boolean check. The contradictory empty clause is represented by \(0\geq1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A clause is exactly the pseudo-Boolean inequality requiring at least one of its literal values to equal one. The empty clause becomes the contradictory inequality zero at least one.
knowledge_statements.title: Clausal PB Proofs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The clause-to-inequality equivalence is correct, but the broader definition of a clausal pseudo-Boolean proof is format-dependent and unsupported. Because the terminal title is a proof family, certificate may fit better than representation once the intended system is sourced.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed algebraic realization of clausal resolution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Adding \(S_A+x\geq1\) and \(S_B+(1-x)\geq1\) yields \(S_A+S_B\geq1\). Identifying this result with the clausal resolvent requires format-specific weakening, coefficient saturation, duplicate removal, and tautology normalization when nonpivot literals overlap or complement one another.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: PB addition eliminates the pivot, but obtaining the ordinary resolvent may require normalization rules not fixed by this terminal title.
assumptions_latex: All literal values are Boolean.
The intended format specifies the required normalization rules.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{A resolution correspondence is valid only after the format's permitted normalization is fixed.}
knowledge_statements.title: Resolution as Pseudo-Boolean Addition

intermediate_metadata.reason: The reliable local inventory is clause-as-PB semantics, the empty contradictory line, and the failure of one clause to express every PB threshold. The Builder's direct resolution claim was deferred because overlaps require unspecified normalization. The exact calculus, checker, and complexity remain unresolved; RUP and translation compatibility were excluded to sibling leaves.

children.title: Translation Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Compatibility boundaries between RUP-style records and clausal PB records.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Size-and-time requirement for computationally meaningful proof compatibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Pi\) be a source proof of \(F\), and let \(S(\Pi)\) be a target proof for \(T(F)\). If \(T\) and \(S\) are polynomial-time computable and \(|S(\Pi)|\le p(|F|+|\Pi|)\) for a fixed polynomial \(p\), then this translation is a polynomial proof simulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proof translation is polynomial when translation time and target-proof growth are polynomially bounded.
assumptions_latex: T\text{ and }S\text{ are total on the stated classes}.
p\text{ is a fixed polynomial}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T,S\in\mathrm{FP}\land |S(\Pi)|\le p(|F|+|\Pi|)\Longrightarrow\text{polynomial simulation}.
knowledge_statements.title: Polynomial Simulation Criterion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinction between local derivation translation and completed-refutation translation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A stepwise simulation maps every source derivation prefix to a checkable target derivation of its translated current conclusion. A refutation simulation need only map completed source refutations to target refutations. Stepwise simulation implies refutation simulation, whereas the converse is not guaranteed by the definitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Translating every proof step is a stronger guarantee than translating only completed refutations.
assumptions_latex: P\text{ and }Q\text{ have explicit derivations}.
T\text{ translates instances and conclusions}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{stepwise simulation}\Longrightarrow\text{refutation simulation}.
knowledge_statements.title: Stepwise Simulation versus Refutation Simulation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equisatisfiability Does Not Imply Proof Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between semantic instance translation and proof-system simulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The condition \(F\in\mathrm{SAT}\iff T(F)\in\mathrm{SAT}\) alone provides neither a translation of source derivations into checkable target derivations nor a polynomial bound on translated proof size.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Preserving satisfiability does not by itself preserve proof steps, checkability, or proof size.
assumptions_latex: T\text{ is an equisatisfiable instance translation}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{SAT}(F)\iff\operatorname{SAT}(T(F))\centernot\implies P\preceq Q.

notation.meaning: Q simulates P under the chosen translation.

knowledge_statements.title: Equisatisfiability Does Not Imply Proof Compatibility

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closure of semantic and proof compatibility under consecutive representation translations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \((T_1,\pi_1,S_1)\) is satisfaction- and proof-compatible from \(P\) to \(Q\), and \((T_2,\pi_2,S_2)\) is satisfaction- and proof-compatible from \(Q\) to \(R\), then \((T_2\circ T_1,\pi_1\circ\pi_2,S_2\circ S_1)\) is compatible from \(P\) to \(R\). If both simulations are polynomial, their composition is polynomial.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compatible instance, assignment, and proof translations compose; polynomial simulations remain polynomial.
assumptions_latex: \operatorname{codom}(T_1)=\operatorname{dom}(T_2),\quad \operatorname{codom}(\pi_2)=\operatorname{dom}(\pi_1),\quad \operatorname{codom}(S_1)=\operatorname{dom}(S_2).
Each component translation satisfies the same stated semantic and proof-compatibility predicates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P\preceq Q\land Q\preceq R\Longrightarrow P\preceq R.
knowledge_statements.title: Composition of Compatible Translations

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stepwise semantic compatibility of clausal RUP with the clausal pseudo-Boolean fragment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Translate each nonempty clause \(C=\ell_1\vee\cdots\vee\ell_r\) to \(T(C):\sum_{j=1}^r\ell_j\ge1\), interpreting each literal by its Boolean truth value. On this fragment, clausal unit propagation and exact PB slack propagation make the same literal deductions and detect the same conflicts. Consequently, if unit propagation refutes \(F\land\bigwedge_{\ell\in C}\neg\ell\), then PB propagation refutes \(T(F)\) under the corresponding literal-falsifying assumptions, certifying addition of \(T(C)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The standard clause inequality preserves unit-propagation deductions, so a clausal RUP check translates to PB propagation on the clausal fragment.
assumptions_latex: The target represents Boolean literals with exact complement semantics.
The target checker supports clausal inequalities, literal-falsifying assumptions, and exhaustive exact slack propagation.
The source-to-target variable and literal maps are validated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{UP}\!\left(F\land\bigwedge_{\ell\in C}\neg\ell\right)=\bot\Rightarrow\operatorname{PBProp}\!\left(T(F)\mid\{\ell=0:\ell\in C\}\right)=\bot.

notation.meaning: Exhaustive exact slack propagation in the clausal-PB fragment.

knowledge_statements.title: Clause-to-PB Preservation of RUP Propagation

assumptions_latex: A source representation and target representation have explicitly defined assignment translations.
Both proof systems have mechanically checkable inference relations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Compatibility requires preservation of satisfaction, refutation, and checkability under translation.

notation.meaning: Instance translation from the source to target representation
Assignment projection from target variables to source variables

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility between clausal and pseudo-Boolean instances and proof logs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A translation \((T,\pi)\) is satisfaction-compatible if, for every source instance \(F\), \(F\) is satisfiable exactly when \(T(F)\) is satisfiable, and every satisfying assignment of \(T(F)\) projects under \(\pi\) to a satisfying assignment of \(F\). It is proof-compatible from system \(P\) to system \(Q\) if every checkable \(P\)-derivation of a constraint or contradiction can be transformed into a checkable \(Q\)-derivation of the translated conclusion. Polynomial compatibility additionally requires polynomial-time translation and polynomially bounded proof-size increase.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compatible translation preserves satisfiability and turns valid source proof steps or refutations into checkable target proofs; polynomial compatibility also controls translation time and proof growth.
knowledge_statements.title: Translation Compatibility

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the leaf, but satisfaction compatibility, proof simulation, and polynomial proof-size control combine several distinct notions whose intended formal standard requires a direct source.

children.title: Redundance Proofs
children.top_down_role: Certification of transformations justified through redundancy.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of bare equisatisfiability to survive arbitrary later conjunctions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For Boolean \(x\), let \(F=\top\), \(C=(x=1)\), and \(D=(x=0)\). Then \(F\) and \(F\land C\) are both satisfiable, but \(F\land D\) is satisfiable while \(F\land C\land D\) is not. Thus current equisatisfiability alone is not compositional under later constraint addition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint can preserve current satisfiability yet become destructive after another constraint is added.
assumptions_latex: Redundancy means only preservation of whether the current formula is satisfiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\simeq_{\mathrm{sat}}F\land C\not\Rightarrow F\land D\simeq_{\mathrm{sat}}F\land C\land D.
knowledge_statements.title: Satisfiability Redundancy Is Context-Sensitive

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical redundancy special case stronger than satisfiability preservation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(F\models C\), then \(F\equiv F\land C\). Thus any sound derivation of \(C\) from \(F\) certifies a redundant addition that preserves the complete model set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A logically implied constraint is redundant in the strongest sense: adding it preserves every model.
assumptions_latex: \(F\models C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Mod}(F)=\operatorname{Mod}(F\land C).
knowledge_statements.title: Entailed Constraints Are Model-Preserving Redundancies

assumptions_latex: The current pseudo-Boolean constraint set is \(F\), and \(C\) is a proposed additional constraint.
The proof format specifies a checkable witness relation for redundancy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A certified redundant constraint may be added without changing whether the current formula is satisfiable.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic core of witness-based pseudo-Boolean redundancy addition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A redundance certificate for adding \(C\) to \(F\) supplies a mechanically checkable witness \(\omega\) such that every assignment \(\alpha\) satisfying \(F\) but violating \(C\) can be transformed into an assignment \(\omega(\alpha)\) satisfying \(F\land C\). Hence \(F\) satisfiable implies \(F\land C\) satisfiable, while the reverse implication follows from conjunction elimination. Therefore \(F\) and \(F\land C\) are equisatisfiable. The concrete proof system must specify how the witness obligation is reduced to permitted derivations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A redundance proof witnesses how any model violating the added constraint can be converted into a model satisfying it. This makes the addition equisatisfiability-preserving.
knowledge_statements.title: Redundance Proofs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The semantic witness argument yields equisatisfiability, but the exact mechanically checkable witness obligation depends on the pseudo-Boolean proof format and has no cited source.

children.title: Constraint Strengthening Proofs
children.top_down_role: Certification of transformations that replace constraints with stronger forms.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Format-independent sufficient condition for model-preserving constraint replacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the current formula be \(G\land C\). If \(C'\models C\) and \(G\land C\models C'\), then \(G\land C\equiv G\land C'\). Replacing \(C\) by \(C'\) consequently preserves every model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stronger replacement preserves all models when the surrounding formula already implies it and it implies the old constraint.
assumptions_latex: \(C'\models C\).
\(G\land C\models C'\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G\land C\equiv G\land C'.
knowledge_statements.title: Contextual Implication Criterion for Strengthening

assumptions_latex: The current formula contains a constraint \(C\), and \(C'\) is intended to replace it.
The relation \(C'\models C\) and preservation of satisfiability are mechanically certified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Replacing \(C\) by \(C'\) is admissible when the resulting formula is equisatisfiable with the original formula.

notation.meaning: Constraints other than the one being replaced

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certified replacement by a logically stronger pseudo-Boolean constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A constraint-strengthening step replaces \(G\land C\) by \(G\land C'\), where \(C'\models C\). Soundness for satisfiability additionally requires a checkable certificate that \(G\land C\) satisfiable implies \(G\land C'\) satisfiable. The reverse implication follows from \(C'\models C\), so the two formulas are equisatisfiable. Operationally, a proof log may first add \(C'\) using an admissible redundance or derivation rule and then delete \(C\); deletion alone cannot justify the strengthening.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replacing a constraint by a stronger one requires both implication back to the original constraint and a certificate that no last satisfying assignment is lost.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Strengthening Proofs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role and equisatisfiability requirement are appropriate, but the add-then-delete realization and admissibility conditions are proof-format-specific and unsupported.

children.title: Strengthening Admissibility Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits governing when strengthening remains certifiably sound.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic hierarchy separating satisfiability, model, and optimization preservation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A strengthening is admissible only relative to the conclusion certified by the proof system. Equisatisfiability is sufficient for a terminal satisfiability conclusion; preservation of the entire model set requires logical equivalence; and an optimization conclusion requires a certified correspondence preserving the claimed optimum, bound, or objective values to the extent asserted by that conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The required certificate depends on whether the log claims satisfiability, model equivalence, or an optimization result.
assumptions_latex: The proof system specifies the semantic conclusion certified by its log.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The strengthening must preserve the invariant needed for the declared conclusion.}
knowledge_statements.title: Required Invariant Determines Admissibility

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equisatisfiability Does Not Preserve an Objective
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimization boundary for satisfiability-preserving strengthening.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\{0,1\}\), minimize \(x\), take \(C:(x\geq0)\), and replace it by \(C':(x\geq1)\). Both constraints are satisfiable and \(C'\models C\), but their optimal values are \(0\) and \(1\), respectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A replacement may preserve satisfiability while changing the optimum, so optimization logs need an optimization-preserving invariant.
assumptions_latex: The transformation is used to certify the optimization problem \(\min x\), not merely satisfiability.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{sat}(C)=\operatorname{sat}(C')=\mathrm{true},\qquad\operatorname{opt}(C)=0\neq1=\operatorname{opt}(C').
knowledge_statements.title: Equisatisfiability Does Not Preserve an Objective

assumptions_latex: Variables are Boolean.
A strengthening step replaces an existing constraint by a strictly stronger constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Logical strength alone does not make replacement admissible; equisatisfiability or a stronger required invariant must also be certified.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp failure of uncertified strengthening under Boolean semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The condition \(C'\models C\) is insufficient for admissible replacement. Let \(x\in\{0,1\}\), let \(C\) be \(x\geq0\), and let \(C'\) be \(x\geq2\). Then \(C'\models C\), but \(C\) is satisfiable whereas \(C'\) is not. Thus replacing \(C\) by \(C'\) can destroy satisfiability even though the new constraint is logically stronger. An admissible strengthening rule must additionally certify equisatisfiability, implication from the surrounding formula, or the specific invariant required by the proof system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stronger constraint can eliminate every model: replacing the valid Boolean constraint x at least zero by x at least two makes the formula infeasible. Strength alone is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.title: Strengthening Admissibility Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample correctly shows that logical strengthening alone can destroy satisfiability, and failure_boundary is the correct role. A specifically located source or explicit standard-field rationale is still required.

children.title: Proof-System Strength
children.top_down_role: Comparative expressive power of pseudo-Boolean proof systems.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order-theoretic structure of size-based proof-system strength.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under a fixed common contradiction language and polynomially compatible encodings, size-based strength is reflexive and transitive. Mutual strength is therefore an equivalence relation, and the induced relation on equivalence classes is a partial order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Size-based proof strength is a preorder; quotienting by mutual strength gives a partial order.
assumptions_latex: All comparisons use a common language and polynomially compatible formula and proof encodings.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P\preceq P,\qquad(P\preceq Q\land Q\preceq R)\Rightarrow P\preceq R.
knowledge_statements.title: Size Strength Is a Preorder
Proof-System Strength
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Size-based comparison of pseudo-Boolean refutation systems on encoded contradictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) and \(Q\) be sound and complete proof systems for unsatisfiable pseudo-Boolean formulas, and let \(|\pi|\) denote proof length under fixed polynomially related encodings. Define \(P\preceq Q\) when there exists a polynomial \(p\) such that, for every unsatisfiable formula \(F\), \[\min_{\pi\in Q(F)}|\pi|\le p\!\left(|F|+\min_{\rho\in P(F)}|\rho|\right).\] Thus \(Q\) is at least as strong as \(P\); they have equivalent strength when both \(P\preceq Q\) and \(Q\preceq P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One proof system is at least as strong as another when it always has polynomial-size refutations whenever the other does, under compatible encodings.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) and \(Q\) are sound and complete for the same pseudo-Boolean contradiction language.
Proof and formula encodings are polynomially related.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\preceq Q\) defines the size-based strength preorder.

notation.meaning: Q is at least as strong as P

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard proof-complexity size preorder specialized to pseudo-Boolean refutations
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The size-based strength preorder is mathematically coherent and fits the definition container, but no inspectable citation supports this pseudo-Boolean specialization.

children.title: Proof Rank
children.top_down_role: Rank-based structural complexity of pseudo-Boolean derivations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural relation between inference depth and the size of a pruned single-conclusion derivation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\pi\) have one designated conclusion, maximum inference fan-in \(b\geq 1\), rank \(r\), and only lines ancestral to that conclusion. If \(s\) is the number of inferred lines, then \(r\leq s\) and \(|\pi|\leq\sum_{i=0}^{r}b^i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank is at most the number of inference steps, and a pruned bounded-fan-in proof of rank r has at most geometrically many lines.
assumptions_latex: Axioms have rank zero and each inferred line has rank one plus the maximum premise rank.
Every retained line is ancestral to the unique designated conclusion.
Every inference has at most \(b\) premises.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r\leq s\quad\text{and}\quad |\pi|\leq\sum_{i=0}^{r}b^i.
knowledge_statements.title: Rank–Size Bounds under Bounded Fan-In

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rank Alone Does Not Bound Logged Proof Length
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of depth to control length without pruning and bounded fan-in.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If rank is measured only at designated conclusions, arbitrarily many nonancestral valid lines can be added without changing rank. Even after ancestral pruning, unbounded fan-in permits rank-one conclusions with arbitrarily many premises. Hence no function of rank alone bounds logged proof length under either convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed rank does not bound proof length when irrelevant lines or unbounded-fan-in inferences are permitted.
assumptions_latex: Rank is measured at designated conclusions.
The proof format does not require both ancestral pruning and bounded inference fan-in.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nexists f\;\forall\pi\;\bigl(|\pi|\leq f(\operatorname{rank}(\pi))\bigr).
knowledge_statements.title: Rank Alone Does Not Bound Logged Proof Length
Proof Rank
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Derivation-depth measure for rule-based pseudo-Boolean proofs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\pi\) be a directed acyclic derivation whose source vertices are input axioms and whose other vertices are inferred lines. Assign rank zero to every axiom and define the rank of an inferred line \(v\) by \[r(v)=1+\max\{r(u):u\text{ is a premise used to infer }v\}.\] The rank of \(\pi\) is the maximum rank of any designated conclusion line. For a formula \(F\), its \(P\)-rank is the minimum rank among all \(P\)-refutations of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proof rank is the minimum possible maximum inference depth of a refutation, with input axioms placed at rank zero.
assumptions_latex: The proof is represented as an acyclic derivation with explicit premise edges.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}_P(F)=\min_{\pi\in P(F)}\max_v r(v)\).

notation.meaning: minimum rank of a P-refutation of F

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard inference-depth definition of proof rank
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The inference-depth definition is plausible, but proof-rank conventions can differ regarding conclusion rank and overall derivation rank; an authoritative source with a precise locator is required.

children.title: Simulation Relations
children.top_down_role: Relationships in which one proof system efficiently represents another.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonuniform Size Strength Does Not Supply a Simulation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniformity boundary between minimum-size comparison and proof translation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The assertion that every formula having a short \(P\)-refutation has some short \(Q\)-refutation does not itself give an algorithm constructing the \(Q\)-refutation from a supplied \(P\)-refutation. Polynomial simulation therefore requires a uniform polynomial-time translator or an equivalent constructive result.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Existence of short target proofs is weaker than an efficient method for translating source proofs.
assumptions_latex: The size comparison supplies only bounds on minimum proof sizes and no translator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{nonuniform size strength}\not\Rightarrow\text{polynomial simulation}.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonuniform Size Strength Does Not Supply a Simulation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identity and composition laws for uniform polynomial proof translations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every proof system polynomially simulates itself through the identity translator. If \(Q\) polynomially simulates \(P\) through \(T_1\) and \(R\) polynomially simulates \(Q\) through \(T_2\), then \(T_2\circ T_1\) polynomially simulates \(P\) in \(R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polynomial simulation is reflexive and transitive because polynomial translators compose.
assumptions_latex: Formula and proof encodings are polynomially compatible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P\leq_{\mathrm{sim}}Q\land Q\leq_{\mathrm{sim}}R\Rightarrow P\leq_{\mathrm{sim}}R.
knowledge_statements.title: Polynomial Simulation Is a Preorder
Simulation Relations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polynomial-time translation between pseudo-Boolean proof systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A pseudo-Boolean proof system \(Q\) polynomially simulates a system \(P\) if there are a polynomial \(p\) and an algorithm \(T\) such that, for every \(P\)-refutation \(\pi\) of every encoded formula \(F\), \(T(F,\pi)\) is a valid \(Q\)-refutation of \(F\), runs in time at most \(p(|F|+|\pi|)\), and satisfies \[|T(F,\pi)|\le p(|F|+|\pi|).\] Mutual polynomial simulation defines polynomial equivalence of the systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A system polynomially simulates another when every refutation can be translated into a valid refutation with polynomial time and size overhead.
assumptions_latex: Both systems use polynomially intertranslatable encodings of formulas and proof lines.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The translator \(T\) establishes a polynomial simulation of \(P\) by \(Q\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard polynomial-simulation definition for proof systems
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The polynomial-simulation definition is internally consistent and fits the container, but it has no inspectable source.

children.title: Proof-System Separations
children.top_down_role: Regimes exhibiting limits between proof-system families.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resource-specific separation by minimum refutation rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A polynomial-size contradiction family \((F_n)\) separates \(P\) from \(Q\) by rank in favor of \(Q\) if \(\operatorname{rank}_Q(F_n)\leq n^{O(1)}\) while \(\operatorname{rank}_P(F_n)=n^{\omega(1)}\). Such a family excludes any translation whose output rank is polynomially bounded in the input encoding length and input rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rank separation gives polynomial-rank refutations in one system and forces superpolynomial rank in the other.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) and \(Q\) use a common contradiction language and compatible rank conventions.
