knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{rank}_Q(F_n)\leq n^{O(1)}\quad\land\quad\operatorname{rank}_P(F_n)=n^{\omega(1)}.

notation.meaning: minimum rank of a P-refutation of F

knowledge_statements.title: Rank Separation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-way failure of polynomial simulation witnessed by oppositely oriented families.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If one contradiction family separates \(P\) from \(Q\) in favor of \(Q\), and another separates \(Q\) from \(P\) in favor of \(P\), under the same size conventions, then neither system polynomially simulates the other.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Oppositely oriented separation families establish incomparability under polynomial simulation.
assumptions_latex: Both separations use fixed polynomially compatible formula and proof encodings.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P\not\leq_{\mathrm{sim}}Q\quad\land\quad Q\not\leq_{\mathrm{sim}}P.
knowledge_statements.title: Proof-System Incomparability
Proof-System Separations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Size separation witnessed by a family of pseudo-Boolean contradictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) and \(Q\) be proof systems for the same pseudo-Boolean language. A family \((F_n)_{n\ge 1}\) separates \(P\) from \(Q\) in favor of \(Q\) if every \(F_n\) is unsatisfiable, \(|F_n|\) is polynomially bounded in \(n\), some \(Q\)-refutation of \(F_n\) has size polynomial in \(n\), and, for every polynomial \(p\), all sufficiently large \(n\) satisfy \[\min_{\pi\in P(F_n)}|\pi|>p(n).\] Such a family proves that \(P\) does not polynomially simulate \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A separation in favor of Q consists of polynomial-size Q-refutations but superpolynomial minimum P-refutation size, which rules out P polynomially simulating Q.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) and \(Q\) are sound and complete for a common encoded language.
The family \((F_n)\) has polynomial encoding size.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\) does not polynomially simulate \(Q\).

notation.meaning: set of P-refutations of the nth formula

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: a superpolynomial P-size lower bound against polynomial-size Q-refutations rules out P simulating Q
A proof-complexity source is required for the terminology and orientation.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct witness certificates for pseudo-Boolean feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a pseudo-Boolean system \(F=\{a_i^{\mathsf T}x\ge b_i:i=1,\ldots,m\}\) with \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\), a feasibility certificate is a vector \(\hat x\in\{0,1\}^n\). Verification recomputes every integer scalar product and accepts exactly when \[a_i^{\mathsf T}\hat x\ge b_i\qquad(i=1,\ldots,m).\] Acceptance certifies that \(F\) is feasible because the certificate itself is an element of the feasible set. Its verification uses polynomially many integer-arithmetic operations in the encoded instance size.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A binary assignment certifies feasibility when direct substitution verifies every pseudo-Boolean inequality.
assumptions_latex: All coefficients and right-hand sides are finitely encoded integers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Acceptance implies \(\hat x\in\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:a_i^{\mathsf T}x\ge b_i\ \forall i\}\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: feasibility is directly certified by a satisfying binary assignment
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A satisfying binary assignment is the appropriate feasibility certificate, and the statement fits the container, but no citation with a specific locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical limit of failing to submit or verify a refutation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be a sound pseudo-Boolean proof system. If a submitted derivation is absent or rejected, no feasibility conclusion follows: failure to establish \(P\vdash_F0\ge1\) may mean that \(F\) is feasible, that \(P\) is incomplete, or merely that proof search did not find an available refutation. Inferring feasibility requires an independently justified completeness-and-exhaustion argument or a direct satisfying assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Failure to produce an accepted contradiction is not a feasibility certificate.
assumptions_latex: The proof system is sound but is not assumed complete.
Proof search is not assumed exhaustive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P\nvdash_F0\ge1\not\Longrightarrow \exists x\in\{0,1\}^n\;(x\models F).

notation.meaning: No accepted refutation has been established from F in P.

knowledge_statements.title: Absence-of-Refutation Boundary
Infeasibility Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Checkable refutations of pseudo-Boolean constraint systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a pseudo-Boolean system \(F\), an infeasibility certificate in a sound proof system \(P\) is a finite derivation \(\pi=(L_1,\ldots,L_t)\) whose lines are input constraints or follow from earlier lines by locally checkable rules of \(P\), and whose final line is an explicit contradiction such as \(0\ge1\). A verifier checks every rule application and the final contradiction. If all checks succeed, soundness of \(P\) certifies that no binary assignment satisfies \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A checked derivation of contradiction certifies that a pseudo-Boolean constraint system has no feasible binary assignment.
assumptions_latex: Every inference rule of \(P\) is sound over binary assignments.
The encoding makes each inference step decidable by the verifier.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\vdash_F 0\ge1\) implies \(\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:x\models F\}=\varnothing\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: sound checked refutation is the canonical infeasibility certificate
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The checked-refutation formulation is mathematically standard and has the correct certificate role, but an inspectable pseudo-Boolean proof-system source is absent.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conclusions supported by only one side of an objective-bound certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimization, a checked refutation of \(F\cup\{c^{\mathsf T}x<L\}\) establishes \(c^{\mathsf T}x\ge L\) for every feasible \(x\), but does not establish feasibility or attainment. A verified feasible witness of value \(U\) establishes an upper bound \(\operatorname{OPT}(F,c)\le U\), but does not exclude a better feasible solution. Exact finite optimality follows only when feasibility is established and valid lower and upper bounds meet.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lower-bound refutation alone does not prove feasibility or attainment, and an upper-bound witness alone does not prove optimality.
assumptions_latex: Objective evaluation and checker comparisons use exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{lower-bound evidence alone}\not\Longrightarrow\text{attainment},\qquad \text{upper-bound evidence alone}\not\Longrightarrow\text{optimality}.

notation.meaning: Certified lower and upper objective bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: One-Sided Bound Boundary
Objective-Bound Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificates of valid lower or upper bounds for pseudo-Boolean objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimizing \(c^{\mathsf T}x\) over binary assignments satisfying a pseudo-Boolean system \(F\). A lower-bound certificate for \(L\) is a checked refutation of \[F\cup\{c^{\mathsf T}x\le L-1\}\] when the objective is integer-valued; it certifies \(c^{\mathsf T}x\ge L\) for every feasible \(x\). An upper-bound certificate for \(U\) is a feasible assignment \(\hat x\) satisfying \(c^{\mathsf T}\hat x=U\). The analogous inequality directions apply to maximization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A refutation below a threshold certifies a lower bound, while a feasible assignment with known value certifies an upper bound for minimization.
assumptions_latex: The objective coefficients are integers.
The refutation system is sound and its proof log is accepted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L\le \operatorname{OPT}(F,c)\le U\).
review_flags: The locator supports bound-based optimality generally; pseudo-Boolean proof-log specialization needs confirmation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bound logic is coherent, but the cited general integer-optimization section does not establish the pseudo-Boolean proof-log certificate formulation. A domain-specific source is needed.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp distinction between finite optimality and incomplete one-sided evidence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization pseudo-Boolean problem, a finite value \(z\) is certified optimal only when a verified feasible assignment attains \(z\) and independently checked evidence excludes every feasible value below \(z\). Lower-bound evidence without attainment does not certify an optimizer, while an attaining assignment without exclusion of smaller values certifies only an upper bound. If \(F\) is infeasible, the appropriate terminal certificate is a refutation of \(F\), not a finite optimum certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact finite optimality requires both attainment and exclusion of every better value; infeasibility is a different terminal claim.
assumptions_latex: Objective evaluation and comparison are exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{finite optimality certificate}=\text{verified attainment}+\text{verified exclusion of improvement}.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility-and-Zero-Gap Boundary
Pseudo-Boolean Optimality Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal witness plus matching proof-derived bound for integer-valued minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the problem \(z^*=\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:x\in\{0,1\}^n,\ x\models F\}\) with integer \(c\), an optimality certificate for value \(z\) consists of a feasible assignment \(\hat x\) with \(c^{\mathsf T}\hat x=z\) and an accepted pseudo-Boolean refutation of \[F\cup\{c^{\mathsf T}x\le z-1\}.\] Feasibility gives \(z^*\le z\), while soundness of the refutation gives \(z^*\ge z\); therefore the verifier certifies \(z^*=z\) and the optimality of \(\hat x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimality is certified by a feasible solution of value z and a checked refutation showing that no feasible solution has smaller value.
assumptions_latex: The objective is integer-valued.
The pseudo-Boolean refutation system is sound.
Both the assignment and refutation pass verification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z^*=z=c^{\mathsf T}\hat x\).
review_flags: The exact pseudo-Boolean refutation formulation requires a domain-specific source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The primal-witness plus matching refutation construction correctly expresses optimality for an integer-valued objective, but the cited general bounds section does not support the exact pseudo-Boolean certificate model.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic direct checker.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Evaluate every hard clause and reject on the first false clause. Otherwise evaluate all soft clauses, add exactly the weights of false clauses, and accept \((\alpha,U)\) only if the recomputed sum equals \(U\). With direct clause storage, time is linear in inspected literal occurrences plus exact weight-addition bit cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Check all hard clauses and accept only an exactly recomputed soft cost.
assumptions_latex: Clause identities and declared weights are fixed and finitely encoded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{accept}(\alpha,U)\Rightarrow\alpha\models H\land U=U(\alpha).
knowledge_statements.title: Feasible-Witness Verification

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct primal certificate for weighted partial MaxSAT.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A total Boolean assignment \(\alpha\) is a feasible witness when it satisfies every hard clause. Its checked cost is \(U(\alpha)=\sum_{C\in S:\alpha\not\models C}w_C\). Acceptance after direct clause evaluation and exact summation certifies \(\operatorname{OPT}\le U(\alpha)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hard-feasible assignment certifies an upper bound equal to the weight of its falsified soft clauses.
assumptions_latex: The objective minimizes falsified soft-clause weight.
Weights and arithmetic conventions are exact and fixed.
\alpha is total.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \alpha\models H\Rightarrow\operatorname{OPT}\le U(\alpha).
knowledge_statements.title: Feasible Assignment Witness

knowledge_statements.statement_title: A Primal Witness Does Not Prove Optimality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical limit of feasible-assignment evidence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Acceptance of \((\alpha,U)\) establishes only \(\operatorname{OPT}\le U\). Without a certified lower bound \(L\ge U\), or equivalent exhaustive exclusion of all lower costs, it does not establish \(U=\operatorname{OPT}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible witness is an upper-bound certificate, not an optimality certificate by itself.
assumptions_latex: The objective is minimization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{accept}(\alpha,U)\not\Rightarrow U=\operatorname{OPT}.
knowledge_statements.title: A Primal Witness Does Not Prove Optimality
Feasible Assignment Witnesses
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal certificates for weighted partial MaxSAT.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a weighted partial MaxSAT instance have hard clauses \(H\), soft clauses \(S\), and positive weights \(w_C\). A feasible-assignment witness is a Boolean assignment \(\alpha\) satisfying every clause in \(H\). Its certified cost is \[U(\alpha)=\sum_{C\in S:\,\alpha\not\models C}w_C.\] Direct evaluation of all clauses verifies feasibility and cost. For the minimization form of MaxSAT, acceptance certifies the upper bound \(\operatorname{OPT}\le U(\alpha)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An assignment satisfying all hard clauses certifies a MaxSAT upper bound equal to the total weight of its falsified soft clauses.
assumptions_latex: Every soft-clause weight is positive and finitely encoded.
The MaxSAT objective minimizes the weight of falsified soft clauses.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha\models H\) implies \(\operatorname{OPT}\le U(\alpha)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct primal witness for weighted partial MaxSAT
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The feasible-assignment witness and resulting MaxSAT upper bound are precise and correctly classified as a certificate, but no inspectable source is cited.

knowledge_statements.title: Lower-Bound Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proof-log certificates excluding MaxSAT solutions below a claimed cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a weighted partial MaxSAT instance encoded by a pseudo-Boolean formula \(F\) with integer cost function \(f(x)\), a lower-bound certificate for an integer \(L\) is an accepted refutation of \[F\cup\{f(x)\le L-1\}.\] Soundness implies that every assignment satisfying the hard constraints has cost at least \(L\), hence \(L\le\operatorname{OPT}\). The certificate is independently checkable when each logged inference and the terminal contradiction are verifiable in polynomial time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A checked refutation of every solution below L certifies that the MaxSAT optimum is at least L.
assumptions_latex: The MaxSAT cost is integer-valued.
The pseudo-Boolean encoding preserves feasible assignments and their costs.
The logging proof system is sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\vdash f(x)\ge L\), and therefore \(L\le\operatorname{OPT}\).

notation.meaning: pseudo-Boolean encoding of the MaxSAT instance

review_flags: A MaxSAT proof-logging source is needed to validate the encoding-specific formulation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact rational extension of the accepted integer threshold certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an exact feasibility-and-cost encoding \(F\) with rational cost \(f\) and \(L\in\mathbb Q\), an accepted refutation of \(F\land(f<L)\) certifies \(L\le\operatorname{OPT}\). Multiplication by a common positive denominator \(d\) yields an equivalent exact integer threshold obligation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Refuting all feasible solutions below a rational threshold certifies that threshold as a lower bound.
assumptions_latex: The encoding preserves feasible assignments and exact costs.
Scaling and strict comparison introduce no rounding.
The refutation system is sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\land(f<L)\vdash\bot\Rightarrow L\le\operatorname{OPT}.
knowledge_statements.title: Rational-Cost Threshold Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Encoding or Threshold Mismatch Invalidates the Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic identity required for bound transfer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sound refutation does not certify a reported MaxSAT lower bound when it concerns a non-equivalent encoding, different objective or direction, inexactly rounded threshold, or different instance version. A separately certified cost-preserving transformation is required for transfer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid proof of the wrong model, objective, threshold, or instance is not a lower-bound certificate for the reported problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \neg\operatorname{Equivalent}(F,f,\text{reported instance})\Rightarrow\text{the refutation does not certify the reported }L.
knowledge_statements.title: Encoding or Threshold Mismatch Invalidates the Bound

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Downward Closure of Certified Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order property of valid lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(L\le\operatorname{OPT}\) is certified and \(L'\le L\) uses the same model, objective, and numerical convention, then \(L'\le\operatorname{OPT}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every weaker threshold below a certified lower bound is also valid.
assumptions_latex: Both bounds refer to the identical model and objective semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L'\le L\le\operatorname{OPT}\Rightarrow L'\le\operatorname{OPT}.
knowledge_statements.title: Downward Closure of Certified Lower Bounds

children.title: Unsatisfiable-Core Certificates
children.top_down_role: Certificate structures centered on conflicting soft-clause subsets.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Checked conflicting soft-clause subset and its induced hitting inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For hard clauses \(H\) and soft clauses \(C_i\), a certificate for \(K\subseteq I\) is an accepted refutation of \(H\land\bigwedge_{i\in K}C_i\). Hence every hard-feasible assignment falsifies at least one \(C_i\) with \(i\in K\); under relaxation indicators \(y_i\), every feasible relaxation satisfies \(\sum_{i\in K}y_i\ge1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A checked refutation of a soft-clause subset proves that every feasible solution must relax at least one clause in it.
assumptions_latex: The refutation calculus is sound.
y_i=1 denotes permission to violate C_i.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H\land\bigwedge_{i\in K}C_i\text{ unsatisfiable}\Rightarrow\sum_{i\in K}y_i\ge1\text{ for every feasible relaxation}.
knowledge_statements.title: Unsatisfiable Soft-Core Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Empty Soft Core Certifies Hard Infeasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary where soft relaxation cannot restore feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(H\) is unsatisfiable, \(K=\varnothing\) is a core and its formal hitting inequality is \(0\ge1\). This certifies absence of any hard-feasible assignment, not a finite soft-cost lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An empty soft core proves that the hard layer itself is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H\text{ unsatisfiable}\Rightarrow\text{no soft-clause relaxation restores feasibility}.
knowledge_statements.title: Empty Soft Core Certifies Hard Infeasibility

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity and minimality of certified cores.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(K\) is a core, every \(K'\supseteq K\) is also a core. A core is inclusion-minimal exactly when every proper subset \(J\subsetneq K\) leaves \(H\land\bigwedge_{i\in J}C_i\) satisfiable. Minimality is unnecessary for validity of \(\sum_{i\in K}y_i\ge1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cores need not be minimal; minimality strengthens their description but is unnecessary for a valid hitting inequality.
assumptions_latex: Clause identities and H are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K\text{ core}\land K\subseteq K'\Rightarrow K'\text{ core}.
knowledge_statements.title: Core Minimality Is Optional
Unsatisfiable-Core Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Checked unsatisfiable subsets used in core-guided MaxSAT reasoning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For hard clauses \(H\) and soft clauses indexed by \(I\), an unsatisfiable-core certificate for \(K\subseteq I\) is a checked refutation of \[H\cup\{C_i:i\in K\}.\] Soundness certifies that every assignment satisfying \(H\) must falsify at least one clause indexed by \(K\). Equivalently, if \(y_i=1\) denotes relaxation of \(C_i\), every feasible relaxation vector obeys \[\sum_{i\in K}y_i\ge1.\] Thus each certified core supplies a valid hitting constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A checked refutation of a soft-clause subset proves that every feasible MaxSAT solution must relax at least one clause in that subset.
assumptions_latex: The refutation system is sound for the clause or pseudo-Boolean encoding.
Relaxation variable \(y_i=1\) permits soft clause \(C_i\) to be violated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H\cup\{C_i:i\in K\}\) unsatisfiable implies \(\sum_{i\in K}y_i\ge1\) for every feasible relaxation.

notation.meaning: index set of a certified unsatisfiable core
relaxation indicator for soft clause i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: an unsatisfiable core induces a mandatory hitting constraint
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The core-to-hitting-constraint implication is coherent provided feasible relaxations enforce each relaxed clause, but no source documents the certificate or the assumed relaxation encoding.

children.title: Hitting-Set Certificates
children.top_down_role: Certificate structures centered on weighted transversals of conflict families.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: MaxSAT lower bound obtained from a certified core hypergraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal K\) be a family of soft-clause index sets, each with an accepted unsatisfiable-core certificate. A checked proof that \(y_i\in\{0,1\}\), \(\sum_{i\in K}y_i\ge1\) for \(K\in\mathcal K\), and \(\sum_iw_i y_i<L\) is infeasible certifies \(L\le\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{MaxSAT}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified cores plus a proof that no cheaper transversal exists certify a MaxSAT lower bound.
assumptions_latex: Every K\in\mathcal K is a certified core.
w_i\ge0 and all comparisons are exact.
The hitting-set infeasibility proof system is sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \neg\exists y\in\{0,1\}^I:\bigwedge_{K\in\mathcal K}\sum_{i\in K}y_i\ge1\land\sum_iw_i y_i<L\Rightarrow L\le\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{MaxSAT}}.
knowledge_statements.title: Certified Hitting-Set Lower Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Provenance requirement for hitting constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A correct hitting-set proof is not a MaxSAT lower-bound certificate if any hyperedge it uses lacks a sound core certificate, because an arbitrary hyperedge may exclude feasible MaxSAT relaxation vectors and spuriously increase the hitting-set optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every hyperedge used in a MaxSAT hitting-set certificate must have certified core provenance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists K\in\mathcal K\text{ without certified core provenance}\Rightarrow h(\mathcal K)\text{ is not thereby a certified MaxSAT bound}.
knowledge_statements.title: Uncertified Hyperedges Invalidate Bound Transfer

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strengthening by additional certified cores.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For certified core families \(\mathcal K_1\subseteq\mathcal K_2\), define \(h(\mathcal K)=\min\{\sum_iw_i y_i:y\in\{0,1\}^I,\sum_{i\in K}y_i\ge1\ (K\in\mathcal K)\}\). Then \(h(\mathcal K_1)\le h(\mathcal K_2)\le\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{MaxSAT}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding certified cores can only strengthen the hitting-set lower bound without exceeding the MaxSAT optimum.
assumptions_latex: Every hyperedge is a valid certified core.
w_i\ge0.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal K_1\subseteq\mathcal K_2\Rightarrow h(\mathcal K_1)\le h(\mathcal K_2)\le\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{MaxSAT}}.
knowledge_statements.title: Monotonicity of Certified Hitting-Set Bounds
Hitting-Set Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certified lower bounds from hitting a verified family of MaxSAT cores.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal K\) be a family of soft-clause index sets, each accompanied by a valid unsatisfiable-core certificate, and let \(w_i>0\). A hitting-set lower-bound certificate for \(L\) additionally provides a checked proof that the integer system \[y_i\in\{0,1\},\qquad \sum_{i\in K}y_i\ge1\ \ (K\in\mathcal K),\qquad \sum_i w_i y_i\le L-1\] is infeasible. Every feasible MaxSAT relaxation hits every certified core, so its cost is at least \(L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Verified cores plus a proof that no hitting set costs below L certify a MaxSAT lower bound of L.
assumptions_latex: Every member of \(\mathcal K\) has an accepted unsatisfiable-core certificate.
Soft-clause relaxation costs are positive integers.
The hitting-set infeasibility proof system is sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L\le\min\{\sum_iw_i y_i:y\text{ is a feasible MaxSAT relaxation}\}\).
review_flags: A domain-specific source is needed for the formal core–hitting-set certificate construction and verification model.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The construction gives a valid lower bound when all cores and the hitting-set infeasibility proof are certified, but the formal certificate construction and polynomial-time verification model lack an inspectable source.

children.title: Core–Transversal Consistency
children.top_down_role: Consistency between recorded cores and the corresponding hitting-set evidence.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint consistency of certified cores, a transversal, and a feasible assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For certified cores \(\mathcal U\), a set \(T\subseteq I\), and assignment \(x\), consistency requires \(T\cap U\ne\varnothing\) for every \(U\in\mathcal U\), \(x\models H\), and \(x\models C_i\) for every \(i\notin T\). Then \(x\) is a feasible MaxSAT assignment whose falsified-clause cost is at most \(\sum_{i\in T}w_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A consistent certificate hits every recorded core and realizes the proposed relaxation by a hard-feasible assignment.
assumptions_latex: Every U\in\mathcal U has a checked unsatisfiability certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T\in\operatorname{Tr}(\mathcal U)\land x\models H\land\bigwedge_{i\notin T}C_i\Rightarrow\operatorname{cost}(x)\le\sum_{i\in T}w_i.
knowledge_statements.title: Core–Transversal Consistency Test

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Incomplete Core Families Give Only Necessity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between hitting recorded cores and feasible relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an incomplete certified family \(\mathcal K\), every feasible relaxation hits \(\mathcal K\), but a transversal of \(\mathcal K\) can leave an unrecorded unsatisfiable residual subset. Thus recorded-core consistency alone proves neither feasibility nor exact optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hitting an incomplete core family is necessary but need not be sufficient for MaxSAT feasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{FeasRelax}\subseteq\operatorname{Tr}(\mathcal K),\quad\operatorname{Tr}(\mathcal K)\not\subseteq\operatorname{FeasRelax}\text{ in general}.
knowledge_statements.title: Incomplete Core Families Give Only Necessity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact correspondence for the complete minimal-core hypergraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(H\) is satisfiable and \(\mathcal U\) contains every inclusion-minimal \(K\subseteq I\) such that \(H\land\bigwedge_{i\in K}C_i\) is unsatisfiable. Then \(T\) hits every member of \(\mathcal U\) if and only if \(H\land\bigwedge_{i\notin T}C_i\) is satisfiable. With positive weights, minimum-weight feasible relaxations and minimum-weight transversals have the same value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hitting every minimal soft core is exactly equivalent to leaving a satisfiable residual formula.
assumptions_latex: H\text{ is satisfiable}.
\mathcal U\text{ contains all inclusion-minimal soft cores}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T\in\operatorname{Tr}(\mathcal U)\Longleftrightarrow H\land\bigwedge_{i\notin T}C_i\text{ is satisfiable}.
knowledge_statements.title: Complete-Core Transversal Correspondence
Core–Transversal Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency condition linking certified unsatisfiable cores to a feasible weighted hitting-set witness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be the hard clauses and let soft clause \(C_i\) have positive weight \(w_i\), for \(i\in I\). A core–transversal consistency certificate consists of a family \(\mathcal U\subseteq 2^I\), a set \(T\subseteq I\), and an assignment \(x\). For every \(U\in\mathcal U\), the formula \(H\land\bigwedge_{i\in U}C_i\) has a checkable unsatisfiability certificate; \(T\cap U\ne\varnothing\); and \(x\) satisfies \(H\) and every \(C_i\) with \(i\notin T\). Thus \(T\) is a transversal of the certified cores and \(x\) realizes a feasible MaxSAT solution of cost at most \(\sum_{i\in T}w_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified cores are all hit by a proposed transversal, while a feasible assignment satisfies every soft clause outside that transversal.
assumptions_latex: \(w_i>0\) for every \(i\in I\).
Every asserted core has a separately checkable unsatisfiability certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T\) hits every \(U\in\mathcal U\), and \(x\) has soft-clause cost at most \(\sum_{i\in T}w_i\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate statement is mathematically coherent and fits the leaf, but no inspectable source supports this specialized MaxSAT core–transversal formulation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximate primal–lower-bound agreement for weighted partial MaxSAT.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\) satisfy all hard clauses, let its recomputed soft-clause cost be \(U\), and let a sound certificate establish \(z^*\ge L\). Then \(0\le U-z^*\le U-L\). Hence \(U-L\le\varepsilon\) certifies additive \(\varepsilon\)-optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible assignment whose verified cost is within epsilon of a certified lower bound is additively epsilon-optimal.
assumptions_latex: \(x\) satisfies every hard clause.
\(U\) is the exactly recomputed weighted soft-clause cost of \(x\).
The lower-bound certificate soundly establishes \(z^*\ge L\).
\(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: U-L\le\varepsilon\Longrightarrow 0\le U-z^*\le\varepsilon.

notation.meaning: Verified cost of the feasible assignment.

knowledge_statements.title: Certified Additive Optimality Gap

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Agreement Requires a Common Instance and Objective
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scope-consistency requirement for composing primal and lower-bound evidence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Numerical equality \(U=L\) proves optimality only when the primal witness and lower-bound derivation concern the same hard clauses, soft clauses, weights, and objective convention, or are connected by a checked equivalence transformation. Otherwise equality alone does not establish \(L\le z^*\le U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matching numbers certify optimality only when both certificates concern the same instance and objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: U=L\text{ alone does not imply }z^*=U\text{ without common-scope validation}.
knowledge_statements.title: Agreement Requires a Common Instance and Objective
Primal–Lower-Bound Agreement Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality certificate obtained by equality of independently checkable feasible cost and lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a weighted partial MaxSAT instance, let \(z^*\) denote the minimum total weight of falsified soft clauses. A primal–lower-bound agreement certificate is a triple \((x,U,L)\) such that \(x\) satisfies every hard clause, its checked soft cost is \(U\), and a sound independently checkable derivation establishes \(z^*\ge L\). If \(U=L\), then weak bounding gives \(L\le z^*\le U\), hence \(z^*=U=L\), and \(x\) is optimal. The certificate checker must verify feasibility, recompute \(U\), validate the lower-bound derivation, and compare the two bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible assignment is optimal when its verified cost equals a separately certified lower bound.
assumptions_latex: The instance has finitely many soft clauses with nonnegative weights.
The lower-bound derivation is sound for the encoded MaxSAT instance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U=L\Longrightarrow z^*=U=L\), so \(x\) is optimal.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Primal–lower-bound equality is a sound optimality certificate and the content kind fits, but the record has no cited source for its MaxSAT certificate formulation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle-query complexity of midpoint certified bound search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the certified optimum interval initially contains \(N=U_0-L_0+1\) integers. At each iteration query \(k=\lfloor(L+U)/2\rfloor\), replace \(L\) by \(k+1\) after checked UNSAT, and replace \(U\) by any checked feasible cost \(u\leq k\) after SAT. Then the interval becomes a singleton after at most \(\lceil\log_2 N\rceil\) threshold queries.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Midpoint threshold search needs at most the ceiling of log base two of the initial number of candidate objective values.
assumptions_latex: All objective values and interval endpoints are integral.
Every SAT or UNSAT response is soundly checked.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T\leq\lceil\log_2(U_0-L_0+1)\rceil\).
knowledge_statements.title: Bisection Query Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of bound certification when a queried encoding is not tied to the declared objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A SAT model or UNSAT refutation for an auxiliary formula \(E_k\) justifies an objective-bound update only if checked encoding evidence establishes that \(E_k\) is equisatisfiable with \(F\land(f\leq k)\), with model projection and objective evaluation preserved. Without this link, UNSAT of \(E_k\) need not imply \(z^*>k\), and SAT of \(E_k\) need not provide a feasible assignment of cost at most \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proofs for threshold formulas certify objective bounds only when the formulas are checked encodings of the declared threshold problem.
assumptions_latex: Objective bounds are inferred from independently encoded threshold queries.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E_k\not\equiv_{\mathrm{sat}}F\land(f\leq k)\) implies that SAT or UNSAT evidence for \(E_k\) alone does not certify the claimed objective bound.

notation.meaning: Auxiliary encoding submitted to the proof-producing solver.

knowledge_statements.title: Threshold-Encoding Certification Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonicity underlying certified search over an integral minimization objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q(k)=F\land(f\leq k)\). If \(Q(k)\) is satisfiable, then \(Q(k')\) is satisfiable for every \(k'\geq k\). If \(Q(k)\) is unsatisfiable, then \(Q(k')\) is unsatisfiable for every \(k'\leq k\). Therefore a checked refutation of \(Q(k)\) and a checked feasible assignment of cost \(u\) certify \(k<z^*\leq u\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Threshold satisfiability is monotone, so checked UNSAT and SAT results bracket the optimum.
assumptions_latex: The threshold encoding is equisatisfiable with \(F\land(f\leq k)\).
The objective is minimized over assignments satisfying \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q(k)\text{ UNSAT}\) and a feasible cost \(u\) imply \(k<z^*\leq u\).

notation.meaning: Feasibility query at objective threshold k.

knowledge_statements.title: Threshold Monotonicity and Optimum Bracketing
Certified Bound Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone search over objective thresholds with a checked SAT or UNSAT result at every query.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an integer-valued MaxSAT cost \(f\) with initial bounds \(L\le z^*\le U\), repeatedly choose an integer threshold \(k\) with \(L\le k<U\) and query the encoding \(F\land(f\le k)\). If it is satisfiable, record the model, recompute its cost \(u\le k\), and set \(U\leftarrow u\). If it is unsatisfiable, require a checkable refutation and set \(L\leftarrow k+1\). Stop when \(L=U\); output a recorded model of cost \(U\), all refutations used to raise \(L\), and the equality \(L=U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Search objective thresholds, checking every model or refutation, until the certified lower and upper bounds coincide.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is integer-valued and bounded on feasible assignments.
Each threshold encoding is equisatisfiable with \(F\land(f\le k)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At termination, \(L=U=z^*\), and the recorded model of cost \(U\) is optimal.

notation.meaning: Boolean encoding of the hard feasibility constraints

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The threshold-search algorithm is coherent, but the cited branch-and-bound section does not adequately support the specific SAT/UNSAT threshold encodings and proof-logging protocol.

children.title: Certified Core-Guided Solving
children.top_down_role: Certification interfaces for core-guided MaxSAT solvers.

knowledge_statements.title: Certified Core-Guided Solving
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Core-guided MaxSAT iteration in which every extracted core and objective reformulation is checkable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize the working formula with the hard clauses and selector-controlled soft clauses, and initialize the certified lower bound to zero. Solve under the current selectors. A satisfying result supplies a checked feasible assignment and upper bound. An unsatisfiable result must supply a checked core \(U\); relax the clauses indexed by \(U\), add a sound cardinality or pseudo-Boolean constraint expressing the required relaxation cost, update the lower bound, and log an objective-preserving reformulation. Continue until a checked feasible cost equals the accumulated certified lower bound, then output the assignment, core refutations, and reformulation trace.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly certify unsatisfiable cores, relax them with logged constraints, and stop when the feasible cost meets the certified lower bound.
assumptions_latex: All soft weights are nonnegative.
Every core refutation and reformulation step is accepted by a sound checker.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Equality of the checked feasible cost and accumulated lower bound certifies global optimality.

notation.meaning: an extracted unsatisfiable core of selector assumptions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the leaf, but weighted core-guided updates have materially different rules; an authoritative source is needed to determine the exact relaxation, bound-update, and reformulation conditions.

children.title: Certified OLL Solving
children.top_down_role: Certification interfaces for OLL-style MaxSAT solvers.

knowledge_statements.title: Certified OLL Solving
knowledge_statements.scope_note: OLL-style optimization with certified cores and logged cardinality-bound strengthening.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Encode each soft clause using a relaxation literal and maintain an ordered collection of cardinality constraints with current bounds. Solve the hard clauses under assumptions representing the current objective bound. For a satisfying result, check the model and update the upper bound. For an unsatisfiable result, check the returned assumption core, introduce or strengthen the corresponding cardinality constraint by one level, increase the certified lower bound by the justified amount, and log the encoding transformation. Terminate when the checked model cost equals the certified lower bound; output the model, refutations, cardinality encodings, and transformation log.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: OLL solving strengthens logged cardinality bounds from checked assumption cores until a verified model meets the lower bound.
assumptions_latex: The cardinality encodings preserve their stated Boolean constraints.
Each bound increase is justified by a checked unsatisfiable core.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When the checked upper and lower bounds agree, the returned MaxSAT assignment is optimal.

notation.meaning: relaxation literal associated with soft clause \(i\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed algorithm has the correct general role, but the precise OLL variant, acronym, cardinality strengthening, and weighted lower-bound increments require a specialized source.

children.title: Reformulation Trace Certification
children.top_down_role: Evidence connecting intermediate reformulations to the original objective.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp boundary between one-way simulation and objective-equivalent reformulation traces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimization formulations \((F,f)\) and \((G,g)\), a cost-preserving extension of every \(F\)-feasible assignment into \(G\) implies \(\operatorname{opt}(G)\leq\operatorname{opt}(F)\), while a cost-preserving projection of every \(G\)-feasible assignment into \(F\) implies \(\operatorname{opt}(F)\leq\operatorname{opt}(G)\). Either inequality can be strict: feasible cost sets \(\{1\}\) and \(\{0,1\}\) witness failure of the missing direction. Bidirectional maps imply equality of feasible cost sets and optima.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One-way cost-preserving assignment maps prove only one optimum inequality; examples with cost sets {1} and {0,1} show that the missing direction is essential.
assumptions_latex: Both formulations are minimization problems.
Each stated assignment map is total on its source feasible set and preserves cost exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\to G\Rightarrow\operatorname{opt}(G)\leq\operatorname{opt}(F),\qquad G\to F\Rightarrow\operatorname{opt}(F)\leq\operatorname{opt}(G).

notation.meaning: every feasible assignment of F has a cost-preserving feasible extension in G

knowledge_statements.title: One-Way Reformulation Guarantees

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composition rule for successive certified reformulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If every adjacent trace step \((F_j,f_j)\leftrightarrow(F_{j+1},f_{j+1})\) has total cost-preserving extension and projection maps, their compositions give such maps between any two trace positions. Hence all trace positions have the same feasible objective-value set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bidirectional checked maps compose, so every segment of the reformulation trace preserves all feasible objective values.
assumptions_latex: Every adjacent map is total on feasible assignments.
Every adjacent map preserves objective values exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{f_j(x):x\models F_j\}=\{f_k(y):y\models F_k\}\quad(0\leq j,k\leq m).

notation.meaning: formulation and objective at trace position j

knowledge_statements.title: Compositionality of Checked Trace Steps
Reformulation Trace Certification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stepwise certificate that solver-introduced relaxations preserve the represented objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((F_0,f_0),\ldots,(F_m,f_m)\) be successive Boolean optimization formulations. A reformulation trace certificate provides, for each \(j<m\), checkable extension and projection rules between assignments of \(F_j\) and \(F_{j+1}\). Every feasible assignment of \(F_j\) must extend to one of \(F_{j+1}\) with equal objective value, and every feasible assignment of \(F_{j+1}\) must project to one of \(F_j\) with equal objective value. Consequently the feasible objective-value sets, and hence the optima, agree at every step. A final certificate for \((F_m,f_m)\) therefore transfers to \((F_0,f_0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each logged reformulation has objective-preserving extension and projection checks, so the final optimum transfers to the original instance.
assumptions_latex: Every trace step supplies total checkable extension and projection rules.
Objective values are exactly preserved in both directions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min\{f_0(x):x\models F_0\}=\min\{f_m(y):y\models F_m\}\).

notation.meaning: formula and objective after reformulation step j

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bidirectional objective-preservation condition is precise and sufficient, but no source supports this particular reformulation-trace certificate or its checker rules.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Progress by Separating the Current Transversal
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coarse iteration bound for exact implicit hitting-set solving.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If an unsuccessful iteration testing \(T\subseteq I\) returns a certified core \(U\subseteq I\setminus T\), then \(T\) does not hit the enlarged core family and cannot be selected again. Thus at most \(2^{|I|}\) distinct transversals are tested, provided every master and satisfiability call terminates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every new core excludes the current transversal, giving finite termination over a finite soft-clause universe.
assumptions_latex: The soft-clause index set \(I\) is finite.
Every master and satisfiability subproblem terminates.
Every returned core is disjoint from the current transversal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{iterations}}\leq2^{|I|}.

notation.meaning: transversal tested in the current iteration

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Progress by Separating the Current Transversal

knowledge_statements.statement_title: A Nonoptimal Transversal Does Not Close the Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessity of a checked optimum for the hitting-set master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A checked MaxSAT assignment with violation set \(T\) certifies the upper bound \(w(T)\), and the fact that \(T\) hits every accumulated core establishes only master feasibility. Global optimality follows when \(w(T)\) matches a certified lower bound such as \(h(\mathcal U)\); hitting all known cores without master-optimality evidence does not exclude a cheaper transversal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hitting every known core is insufficient: the feasible violation cost must also match a certified lower bound.
assumptions_latex: The instance is weighted partial MaxSAT with nonnegative soft-clause weights.
The assignment and its incurred violation cost are checked.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T\text{ hits }\mathcal U\not\Rightarrow w(T)=\operatorname{OPT};\qquad w(T)=h(\mathcal U)\Rightarrow w(T)=\operatorname{OPT}.

notation.meaning: total weight of the soft clauses indexed by T

knowledge_statements.title: A Nonoptimal Transversal Does Not Close the Gap

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Certified Cores Give Hitting-Set Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fundamental lower-bound invariant of implicit hitting-set MaxSAT.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal U\) be a family of certified soft-clause cores relative to the hard clauses. The violation set of every hard-feasible assignment intersects every \(U\in\mathcal U\). Therefore the minimum weight \(h(\mathcal U)\) of a hitting set of \(\mathcal U\) is a lower bound on the weighted MaxSAT optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every feasible violation set hits every certified core, so the optimal master hitting-set value is a valid MaxSAT lower bound.
assumptions_latex: Each member of \(\mathcal U\) has a checked unsatisfiability certificate relative to the hard clauses.
Soft-clause weights are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: h(\mathcal U)\leq\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{MaxSAT}}.

notation.meaning: family of certified unsatisfiable soft-clause cores
minimum weight of a set intersecting every certified core

knowledge_statements.title: Certified Cores Give Hitting-Set Lower Bounds
Certified Implicit Hitting-Set Solving
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Alternation between certified core discovery and a checked minimum-weight hitting-set subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain a family \(\mathcal U\) of certified soft-clause cores, initially empty. Compute a minimum-weight hitting set \(T\) of \(\mathcal U\), together with a certificate of its hitting-set optimality, and test whether the hard clauses together with all soft clauses outside \(T\) are satisfiable. If satisfiable, check the assignment and output it with \(T\). If unsatisfiable, check a refutation, extract a new core \(U\subseteq I\setminus T\), add \(U\) to \(\mathcal U\), and repeat. At successful termination, every feasible violation set hits \(\mathcal U\), while the returned assignment violates only \(T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve certified hitting-set relaxations and add checked cores until the selected transversal admits a feasible MaxSAT assignment.
assumptions_latex: Soft-clause weights are nonnegative.
Each hitting-set optimum and each reported core is independently checkable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At successful termination, the returned assignment and \(T\) have minimum possible soft-clause weight.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The iteration and optimality conclusion are mathematically consistent, but the specialized certified implicit-hitting-set method and its hitting-set optimality certificate lack an inspectable source.

children.title: Certified Branch Search
children.top_down_role: Certification structure associated with branch-based MaxSAT exploration.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coverage, Not Disjointness, Is Required for Sound Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local branch-generation condition for certified branch search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a parent region \(R\), feasible set \(X\), and child regions \(R_1,\ldots,R_q\subseteq R\), sound exhaustive branching requires \(R\cap X\subseteq\bigcup_jR_j\). Pairwise disjointness is unnecessary for soundness, although it prevents duplicate exploration. If coverage fails, closing all recorded children says nothing about an uncovered feasible assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Children must cover every feasible parent completion; overlap is sound but a coverage gap is fatal.
assumptions_latex: Every child region is contained in its parent.
Every leaf conclusion is applied only to assignments represented by that leaf.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R\cap X\subseteq\bigcup_jR_j\text{ is required, while }R_i\cap R_j=\varnothing\text{ is optional}.
knowledge_statements.title: Coverage, Not Disjointness, Is Required for Sound Branching
Certified Branch Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branch search whose child disjunctions and node outcomes are independently checkable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Start with a root node representing all assignments satisfying the hard clauses. At an open node with region \(R\), choose branching predicates \(B_1,\ldots,B_q\) and log a checkable coverage statement \(R\subseteq\bigcup_{j=1}^q(R\cap B_j)\). Create the nonempty child regions \(R\cap B_j\). A leaf is closed only by a checked infeasibility refutation, a checked bound-pruning certificate, or complete enumeration with verified objective values. Maintain the best checked feasible assignment as incumbent. When every generated leaf is validly closed, return the incumbent together with the branch and leaf certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every branch covers its parent, and every leaf is closed by a checked infeasibility, bound, or exhaustive-evaluation certificate.
assumptions_latex: The Boolean search space is finite.
Each branching coverage statement and leaf certificate is decidable by the checker.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If all leaves are validly closed, no feasible assignment has cost below the returned incumbent.

notation.meaning: assignment region represented by a search node

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm captures certified branch coverage and leaf closure, but the cited general branch-and-bound chapter does not specifically substantiate the formal checker and certificate requirements.

children.title: Certified Bound Pruning
children.top_down_role: Evidence supporting exclusion of subproblems through objective bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Certified Bound Pruning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local certificate proving that a search node cannot improve the incumbent objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider a minimization search node whose region is \(R
eq\varnothing\), and let \(U\) be the cost of a checked incumbent. A bound-pruning certificate supplies a checkable number \(L_R\) and a sound derivation that \(f(x)\ge L_R\) for every feasible \(x\in R\). If \(L_R\ge U\), then no assignment represented by the node has objective value strictly smaller than the incumbent, so the entire node may be closed. If enumeration of all optimal solutions is required, pruning on equality additionally requires a stated tie policy or evidence that the node contains no unreported optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A node can be pruned when its verified lower bound is at least the cost of the checked incumbent.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem.
\(U\) is the recomputed cost of a feasible incumbent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_R\ge U\Longrightarrow \nexists x\in R\text{ feasible with }f(x)<U\).

notation.meaning: certified lower bound over the node

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Prevents a valid node bound from being applied outside its certified region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A derivation of \(f(x)\geq L_R\) for every feasible \(x\in R\) permits pruning a node region \(S\) when \(S\subseteq R\) and \(L_R\geq U\). It gives no pruning justification when \(S\) contains feasible assignments outside \(R\). The certificate must therefore identify its assumptions, and the checker must verify that the pruned node entails them.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A node bound may prune only the certified region or one of its subregions.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem.
U is the recomputed value of a checked feasible incumbent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S\subseteq R\land L_R\geq U\Rightarrow S\text{ is prunable};\qquad S\nsubseteq R\text{ gives no such implication}.

notation.meaning: region on which the lower-bound derivation is valid

knowledge_statements.title: Node Bounds Are Scope-Local

children.title: Search-Tree Completeness Certificates
children.top_down_role: Evidence that the relevant branch space has been exhaustively covered.

knowledge_statements.title: Search-Tree Completeness Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-tree certificate that all feasible assignments are covered and every terminal region is validly resolved.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A search-tree completeness certificate is a finite rooted tree whose root contains the full feasible search domain. Each internal node labeled by region \(R\) has children labeled by regions \(R_1,
\ldots,R_q\), with a checkable inclusion \(R\subseteq\bigcup_{j=1}^qR_j\). Every leaf is accompanied by either a checked infeasibility refutation, a checked bound-pruning certificate relative to the incumbent, or an exhaustive feasible evaluation. If all local coverage and closure checks succeed, every feasible assignment lies in a closed leaf; consequently the tree omits no assignment capable of improving the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Checked parent-to-child coverage and valid closure of every leaf prove that the finite search examined all potentially improving assignments.
assumptions_latex: The root region contains every feasible assignment.
The certificate tree is finite and every leaf has a valid closure record.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every feasible assignment belongs to a validly closed leaf, so none omitted by the search can improve the incumbent.

notation.meaning: region represented by an internal node

source_refs.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

source_witnesses.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Incomplete Child Coverage Invalidates Tree Closure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of completeness when recorded children omit part of a parent region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let R=\{0,1\} and let the only child be R_1=\{0\}. Even if R_1 is validly closed, R\nsubseteq R_1; therefore assignment 1 remains unaccounted for and may improve the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Closing every recorded leaf is insufficient if a branching step omits part of its parent region.
assumptions_latex: The root domain is \(R=\{0,1\}\).
Only \(R_1=\{0\}\) is recorded as a child.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R\nsubseteq\bigcup_jR_j,\text{ so completeness is not certified.}
knowledge_statements.title: Incomplete Child Coverage Invalidates Tree Closure

children.title: Certified Lexicographic MaxSAT
children.top_down_role: Certification for objectives ordered by strict priority levels.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact level-by-level solver paradigm for certified lexicographic MaxSAT.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For objectives \(f_1,\ldots,f_p\) in priority order, optimize \(f_1\) to a certified value \(v_1\), impose \(f_1=v_1\), and continue similarly through level \(p\). If every stage supplies a feasible witness and checked evidence excluding smaller values under all earlier optimum equalities, the final witness is lexicographically optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimize and certify each priority level exactly, fixing its value before proceeding to the next.
assumptions_latex: There are finitely many priority levels.
Every stage is solved exactly under all previously certified optimum equalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f(x^*)=\min_{\mathrm{lex}}\{f(x):x\in X\}.

notation.meaning: certified optimum at level k under the earlier optimum equalities

knowledge_statements.title: Sequential Certified Lexicographic Optimization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer of a scalar optimality certificate to bounded integer lexicographic costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(0\leq f_k(x)\leq M_k\) are integer-valued, set \(W_p=1\), and choose \(W_k>\sum_{j>k}W_jM_j\). Then a checked global-optimality certificate for \(\sum_kW_kf_k\), together with checked component bounds and arithmetic, certifies lexicographic optimality. If a dominance inequality is violated, lower-priority improvements can outweigh a one-unit higher-priority degradation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dominant mixed-radix weights let a checked scalar optimum certify lexicographic optimality; inadequate weights can reverse priorities.
assumptions_latex: Every component is integer-valued with a checked finite upper bound \(M_k\).
The scalar objective and arithmetic are represented exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \arg\min_X\sum_kW_kf_k=\arg\min_{\mathrm{lex},X}(f_1,\ldots,f_p).

notation.meaning: scalar weight for priority level k
checked upper bound for component k

knowledge_statements.title: Certified Mixed-Radix Scalarization
Certified Lexicographic MaxSAT
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential certificate of optimality at each priority level under all previously fixed optimum values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a feasible Boolean assignment have cost vector \(f(x)=(f_1(x),\ldots,f_p(x))\), ordered from highest to lowest priority. A lexicographic optimality certificate supplies an assignment \(x^*\) and, for each level \(k\), a checked proof that no feasible \(x\) satisfying \(f_j(x)=f_j(x^*)\) for every \(j<k\) also satisfies \(f_k(x)<f_k(x^*)\). The checker verifies feasibility, recomputes the complete vector, and validates every conditional lower-bound or unsatisfiability proof. These levelwise statements imply that no feasible vector is lexicographically smaller than \(f(x^*)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At every priority level, certify that no solution matching all earlier optimum values can improve the current value.
assumptions_latex: The number of priority levels is finite.
Each objective component is exactly evaluable on Boolean assignments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x^*)\le_{\mathrm{lex}} f(x)\) for every feasible assignment \(x\).

notation.meaning: lexicographic order from level 1 to level p

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The levelwise exclusion conditions correctly certify lexicographic optimality and the certificate role fits, but no source supports the specialized MaxSAT formulation and conditional proof encoding.

children.title: Certified Multiobjective MaxSAT
children.top_down_role: Certification for MaxSAT instances with multiple objective components.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A second sound route for certifying one Pareto-optimal MaxSAT assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\lambda_i>0\) for all objective components and a checked certificate proves that \(x^*\) globally minimizes \(\sum_i\lambda_if_i(x)\), then \(x^*\) is Pareto optimal. If \(\lambda\geq0\) is nonzero but has zero components, scalar optimality guarantees only weak Pareto optimality in general.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certified optimum of a strictly positive weighted sum is Pareto optimal; zero weights weaken the guarantee.
assumptions_latex: The scalarized problem is solved globally with a sound certificate.
All scalar arithmetic and objective evaluations are exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda\in\mathbb R_{>0}^p,\ x^*\in\arg\min_X\lambda^Tf(x)\Rightarrow x^*\in\operatorname{Pareto}(X).
knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Weight Scalar Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weighted-Sum Certificates Are Incomplete for Discrete Pareto Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limit of scalarization-based single-point certification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the attainable minimization vectors \((0,3),(2,2),(3,0)\), every vector is Pareto optimal, but \((2,2)\) minimizes no scalarization \(\lambda_1y_1+\lambda_2y_2\) with \(\lambda_1,\lambda_2>0\). Thus positive-weight scalar certificates certify supported Pareto vectors but need not reach every Pareto vector of a finite MaxSAT objective image.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Discrete Pareto sets may contain unsupported points that no positive weighted sum can certify by scalar optimality alone.
assumptions_latex: The displayed vectors are attainable and no additional attainable vector dominates them.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{SupportedPareto}(X)\subsetneq\operatorname{Pareto}(X)\text{ can occur}.

notation.meaning: Pareto vectors optimal for some strictly positive weighted sum

knowledge_statements.title: Weighted-Sum Certificates Are Incomplete for Discrete Pareto Sets
Certified Multiobjective MaxSAT
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pareto-optimality certificate based on exclusion of every feasible assignment that dominates the witness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f=(f_1,\ldots,f_p)\) be minimized componentwise over the feasible assignments of a MaxSAT encoding. A Pareto certificate for a feasible assignment \(x^*\) contains a checked refutation of the formula requiring \(f_i(x)\le f_i(x^*)\) for every \(i\) and \(f_j(x)<f_j(x^*)\) for at least one \(j\). The checker verifies feasibility of \(x^*\), recomputes its objective vector, validates the comparison encoding, and checks the refutation. Unsatisfiability of this dominance query proves that no feasible assignment dominates \(x^*\), so its objective vector is Pareto optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Refuting the existence of any feasible assignment that weakly improves every objective and strictly improves one certifies Pareto optimality.
assumptions_latex: The number of objectives is finite.
All componentwise comparison encodings are exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nexists x\text{ feasible}: (\forall i,\ f_i(x)\le f_i(x^*))\land(\exists j,\ f_j(x)<f_j(x^*))\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The dominance-query refutation correctly certifies one Pareto-optimal witness and does not overclaim front completeness, but the specialized multiobjective MaxSAT certificate lacks a source.

children.title: Priority-Level Certificates
children.top_down_role: Evidence preserving optimality across successive priority levels.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conditional Proof Context Must Cover the Exact Prefix Region
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Soundness boundary for lower-priority evidence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For level \(k\), the required domain is \(C_k=X\cap\bigcap_{j<k}\{f_j=v_j\}\). A proof established on any superset of \(C_k\), including all of \(X\), is sufficient, but a proof valid only on an unrelated subset need not exclude every lexicographically relevant assignment. The checker must verify that the proof assumptions entail the claimed bound throughout \(C_k\) and must separately validate the earlier values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A level bound must hold throughout the exact earlier-optimum region; a global stronger bound is valid, but a bound on an unrelated restriction is not.
assumptions_latex: Priority levels are ordered from highest to lowest.
The checker validates the active assumptions and earlier certified values of every conditional proof.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C_k\subseteq D_k\land(\forall x\in D_k,\ f_k(x)\geq v_k)\Rightarrow(\forall x\in C_k,\ f_k(x)\geq v_k).

notation.meaning: feasible region satisfying all earlier certified optimum equalities
domain on which the supplied level-k bound is proved

knowledge_statements.title: Conditional Proof Context Must Cover the Exact Prefix Region

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inductive invariant for reusable priority-level certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v_1,\ldots,v_p\) be claimed priority optima. If, for each \(k\), a checked derivation proves \(f_k(x)\geq v_k\) for every feasible \(x\) satisfying \(f_j(x)=v_j\) for all \(j<k\), and one checked feasible witness attains every \(v_k\), then every prefix \((v_1,\ldots,v_k)\) is lexicographically minimal. Hence the full vector is lexicographically minimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each checked level extends an already certified optimal prefix, so the per-level certificates compose.
assumptions_latex: One feasible witness attains all claimed level values.
Every lower-bound derivation is valid on the exact conditional region determined by earlier optimum equalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall k\leq p:\ (v_1,\ldots,v_k)=\min_{\mathrm{lex}}\{(f_1(x),\ldots,f_k(x)):x\in X\}.

notation.meaning: certified optimum value at priority level k

knowledge_statements.title: Prefix Compositionality of Priority Certificates
Priority-Level Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate for lexicographic MaxSAT optimality across finitely many priority levels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a satisfiable MaxSAT instance whose soft clauses are partitioned into ordered priority levels \(1,\ldots,p\), and let \(c_i(\alpha)\) be the cost incurred by assignment \(\alpha\) at level \(i\). A priority-level certificate consists of a feasible assignment \(\alpha^*\) and, for each \(i\), a checkable derivation showing \(c_i(\alpha)\ge c_i(\alpha^*)\) for every feasible \(\alpha\) satisfying \(c_j(\alpha)=c_j(\alpha^*)\) for all \(j<i\). Acceptance certifies that \((c_1(\alpha^*),\ldots,c_p(\alpha^*))\) is lexicographically minimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible assignment and sequential lower-bound derivations certify that every priority level is optimal after all higher-priority costs have been fixed.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) has finitely many Boolean variables and priority levels.
Each supplied derivation is checked by a sound proof checker.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((c_1(\alpha^*),\ldots,c_p(\alpha^*))=\min_{\mathrm{lex}}\{(c_1(\alpha),\ldots,c_p(\alpha)): \alpha\models F_{\mathrm{hard}}\}\).

notation.meaning: cost of assignment alpha at priority level i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role fits the leaf and the sequential optimality claim is plausible, but no citation or inspectable locator supports the certificate format. The hard-clause set F_{\mathrm{hard}} is also not introduced explicitly, and the concrete proof system needed to validate the universal lower-bound derivations is unspecified.

children.title: Pareto-Front Certificates
children.top_down_role: Evidence concerning nondominated outcomes in multiobjective regimes.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite construction and certification of all nondominated objective vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Repeatedly obtain and certify a Pareto vector \(y^r\) with a feasible witness, then constrain subsequent searches to objective vectors not weakly dominated by any recorded vector. When the residual formula is refuted, checked witnesses, pointwise Pareto certificates, exact blocking encodings, and the final refutation certify that the distinct recorded vectors are the complete Pareto front. Finiteness of the attainable objective image gives termination when every search call terminates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certify Pareto vectors, block their dominated regions, and refute the residual problem to certify front completeness.
assumptions_latex: The feasible Boolean assignment set and hence its objective image are finite.
Every witness, dominance encoding, blocking constraint, point certificate, and final refutation is checked exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Min}_{\leq}f(X)=\{y^1,\ldots,y^m\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Certified Dominance-Blocking Front Enumeration

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Output-Size Bound for Explicit Front Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary representation and verification cost of an explicitly listed Pareto front.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An explicit certificate listing \(m\) distinct vectors of dimension \(q\) contains \(mq\) objective coordinates, so reading and checking those coordinates requires \(\Omega(mq)\) operations before feasibility and coverage proofs are checked. Finite Boolean instances can have exponentially many nondominated vectors, so explicit complete-front certificates can be exponentially large.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Explicit front certificates require at least linear work in their listed coordinates and can have exponential size.
assumptions_latex: Every Pareto vector is represented explicitly in the certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_{\mathrm{verify}}=\Omega(mq).

notation.meaning: number of distinct listed Pareto vectors

knowledge_statements.title: Output-Size Bound for Explicit Front Certificates

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pointwise Pareto Evidence Is Not Front Completeness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes individual nondominance certificates from a complete-front certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Feasible witnesses and valid dominance-query refutations for every listed vector prove that all listed vectors are Pareto optimal, but do not prove that none was omitted. Completeness additionally requires checked evidence that every feasible objective vector is dominated by or equal to a listed vector, equivalently a refutation of the residual region outside all listed dominated regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proving every listed point Pareto optimal does not prove that the list contains every Pareto point.
assumptions_latex: All objectives are minimized componentwise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\forall y\in Y,\ y\text{ is Pareto})\not\Rightarrow Y=\operatorname{Min}_{\leq}f(X).
knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise Pareto Evidence Is Not Front Completeness
Pareto-Front Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete certificate for a finite multiobjective MaxSAT Pareto front.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite feasible assignment set \(X\) and minimization objective map \(f:X\to\mathbb{Z}^q\), a Pareto-front certificate is a finite list \((x^1,y^1),\ldots,(x^m,y^m)\) together with checkable evidence that \(x^r\in X\), \(y^r=f(x^r)\), no distinct \(y^r,y^s\) weakly dominates the other, and every \(x\in X\) satisfies \(y^r\le f(x)\) componentwise for some \(r\). Acceptance certifies that the distinct vectors \(y^1,\ldots,y^m\) are exactly all nondominated attainable objective vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasible witnesses, pairwise nondominance checks, and a global coverage derivation certify the complete set of Pareto-optimal objective vectors.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is finite.
All feasibility, objective, and coverage evidence is checked soundly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{y^1,\ldots,y^m\}=\operatorname{Min}_{\le}\{f(x):x\in X\}\).

notation.meaning: set of nondominated vectors under componentwise minimization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role and finite Pareto-front characterization fit the leaf, but the global coverage evidence is the substantive completeness certificate and has no authoritative citation, locator, or specified proof calculus.

children.title: Certified Cardinality Encodings
children.top_down_role: Certification concerns specific to cardinality-constraint encodings.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cardinality-specific boundary between implication and exact projected encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For C(x_1,x_2)\equiv x_1+x_2\le1, the CNF E(x_1,x_2,y)=(\neg x_1\lor\neg x_2)\land y satisfies E\Rightarrow C, but the feasible assignment x_1=x_2=0 has no extension satisfying E when y=0 is forced externally. Thus soundness alone does not establish C(x)\iff\exists y\,E(x,y) in the surrounding formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cardinality encoding that only implies the constraint may exclude feasible source assignments once auxiliary-variable conditions are considered.
assumptions_latex: The auxiliary variable is required to be fresh for standalone projection semantics.
The surrounding formula may constrain a nonfresh auxiliary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: E\Rightarrow C\text{ does not alone certify }C\iff\exists y\,E.
knowledge_statements.title: One-Sided Cardinality Encoding Is Insufficient

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cardinality-specific reductions among at-most, at-least, and exact constraints that certified encodings may check.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For x_i\in\{0,1\},\quad \sum_{i=1}^n x_i\ge k\iff\sum_{i=1}^n(1-x_i)\le n-k,\qquad \sum_{i=1}^n x_i=k\iff\left(\sum_i x_i\le k\right)\land\left(\sum_i x_i\ge k\right).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At-least constraints reduce to at-most constraints on complemented variables, and exact cardinality is the conjunction of at-most and at-least constraints.
assumptions_latex: 0\le k\le n
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Mod}(\sum_i x_i=k)=\operatorname{Mod}(\sum_i x_i\le k)\cap\operatorname{Mod}(\sum_i x_i\ge k).
knowledge_statements.title: Cardinality Variant Reductions

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sequential-Counter Certificate Size and Checking Time
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Size and verification bounds for the stated sequential-counter construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The construction has O(n(k+1)) auxiliary variables and constant-size gate templates. Its CNF and construction trace therefore have O(n(k+1)) size, and a checker validating indices, boundaries, freshness, every gate template, and \neg s_{n,k+1} runs in time linear in the emitted CNF and trace length.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The sequential-counter certificate has O(nk) size and is checkable in linear output time.
assumptions_latex: Gate templates have constant encoded size.
The trace explicitly identifies every recurrence and emitted clause.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |E_{n,k}|=O(n(k+1)),\qquad T_{\mathrm{check}}=O(|E_{n,k}|+|T|).
knowledge_statements.title: Sequential-Counter Certificate Size and Checking Time

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection-exact sequential-counter CNF for an at-most-k constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For C(x)\equiv\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\le k with 0\le k<n, introduce s_{i,j} for 1\le i\le n and 1\le j\le k+1. Encode s_{i,j}\leftrightarrow(s_{i-1,j}\lor(x_i\land s_{i-1,j-1})) by complete Tseitin equivalences, using s_{i,0}=1 and s_{0,j}=0, and assert \neg s_{n,k+1}. The resulting CNF E_{n,k}(x,s) satisfies C(x)\leftrightarrow\exists s\,E_{n,k}(x,s).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A prefix counter with complete gate definitions exactly encodes an at-most-k constraint after auxiliary variables are projected away.
assumptions_latex: 0\le k<n
All auxiliary variables are fresh.
Every recurrence is encoded in both directions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_i x_i\le k\iff\exists s\,E_{n,k}(x,s).
