knowledge_statements.scope_note: Construction-dependent output and checking bounds for certified cardinality encodings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A standard truncated totalizer retaining counts through \(k+1\) has \(O(nk)\) explicit auxiliary incidences and clauses. A full sorting network with \(O(n\log^2 n)\) comparators yields the same asymptotic number of constant-size comparator templates, while standard cardinality-network constructions specialized to threshold \(k\) can use \(O(n\log^2 k)\) comparators. Each explicit construction trace is checkable in time linear in its serialized topology and emitted CNF, after identifier validation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Standard truncated totalizers have O(nk) output, while selected comparator-network constructions have O(n log² n) or O(n log² k) output and output-linear checking.
assumptions_latex: \text{The selected totalizer or network construction has the stated topology}.
\text{Every gate or merge template has constant encoded size}.
\text{The trace explicitly records all topology and wire identifiers}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |E_{\mathrm{tot}}|=O(nk),\quad |E_{\mathrm{sort}}|=O(n\log^2n),\quad |E_{\mathrm{card}}|=O(n\log^2k).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection-exact unary totalizer encoding of an at-most-k constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Construct a binary tree over \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\). At each internal node, introduce a unary vector whose entries represent the attainable lower bounds on the number of true leaves below that node, and encode a complete, fixed merge relation between the two child vectors and the parent vector. Truncate values above \(k\) into an overflow entry. Asserting that the root overflow entry is false yields \(E_{n,k}(x,y)\) with \[\sum_i x_i\le k\iff\exists y\,E_{n,k}(x,y).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A completely specified unary totalizer tree with a forbidden overflow output exactly encodes an at-most-k constraint.
assumptions_latex: 0\le k<n.
\text{All auxiliary variables are fresh}.
\text{The certificate fixes and checks every forward and reverse merge clause required by its totalizer semantics}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_i x_i\le k\iff\exists y\,E_{n,k}(x,y).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection-exact comparator-network encoding of cardinality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a checked sorting or \(k\)-selection network map Boolean inputs to outputs \(z_1\ge\cdots\ge z_n\). Encode each comparator \((p,q)\mapsto(p\lor q,p\land q)\) by complete Tseitin equivalences on fresh wires. Then \(\neg z_{k+1}\) encodes \(\sum_i x_i\le k\), while \(z_k\) encodes \(\sum_i x_i\ge k\), under existential projection of the internal wires.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A validated comparator network reduces a cardinality constraint to a designated sorted output wire.
assumptions_latex: \text{The trace certifies a valid sorting or selection-network topology}.
\text{Every comparator is encoded in both directions using fresh internal wires}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_i x_i\le k\iff\exists y\,(E(x,y)\land\neg z_{k+1}).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Input Propagation Completeness of the Full Sequential Counter
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Input-level unit-propagation guarantee for the stated complete-equivalence sequential-counter encoding of an at-most-k constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E_{n,k}(x,s)\) be the complete-equivalence prefix-counter encoding with \(s_{i,0}=1\), \(s_{0,j}=0\), and \(\neg s_{n,k+1}\). For every partial assignment \(\rho\) to the input variables, unit propagation derives contradiction if \(\rho\) sets at least \(k+1\) inputs true. If it sets exactly \(k\) inputs true, unit propagation derives \(\neg x_j\) for every remaining unassigned input.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The full sequential counter detects too many true inputs and, after exactly k true inputs, forces every other input false.
assumptions_latex: 0\le k<n.
Every recurrence is encoded by a propagation-correct complete Tseitin template.
All counter variables are fresh and all boundary constants are encoded correctly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |\rho^{-1}(1)|\ge k+1\Rightarrow\operatorname{UP}(E_{n,k}\mid\rho)=\bot,\qquad |\rho^{-1}(1)|=k\Rightarrow\operatorname{UP}(E_{n,k}\mid\rho)\vdash\neg x_j\text{ for every unassigned }x_j.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact output-size and checking bound for the auxiliary-free subset encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The subset-clause encoding of \(\sum_i x_i\le k\) has exactly \(\binom{n}{k+1}\) clauses and \((k+1)\binom{n}{k+1}\) literal occurrences. A trace listing each \((k+1)\)-subset exactly once is checkable in time polynomial in its serialized output length. For \(k=\lfloor n/2\rfloor\), its size is exponential in \(n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The direct subset encoding is output-checkable but can contain exponentially many clauses.
assumptions_latex: Subsets and variable identifiers use an unambiguous serialization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |E_{n,k}|_{\mathrm{clauses}}=\binom{n}{k+1}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Auxiliary-free exact cardinality encoding and its input-level propagation behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(C(x)\equiv\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\le k\), define \[E_{n,k}(x)=\bigwedge_{I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\},\ |I|=k+1}\left(\bigvee_{i\in I}\neg x_i\right).\] Then \(C(x)\iff E_{n,k}(x)\). Under any partial input assignment, unit propagation derives contradiction after \(k+1\) inputs are true and derives \(\neg x_j\) for every remaining input after exactly \(k\) inputs are true.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Forbidding every set of k+1 true inputs gives an exact auxiliary-free encoding with complete input propagation for the at-most-k constraint.
assumptions_latex: 0\le k<n.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_i x_i\le k\iff E_{n,k}(x),\qquad |\rho^{-1}(1)|=k\Rightarrow\operatorname{UP}(E_{n,k}\mid\rho)\vdash\neg x_j\text{ for every unassigned }x_j.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact boundary handling for certified at-most-k cardinality encodings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For Boolean variables \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\), the constraint \(C(x)\equiv\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\le k\) is inconsistent when \(k<0\), tautological when \(k\ge n\), and nontrivial only when \(0\le k<n\). A certified encoder may emit the one-clause CNF containing the empty clause in the first case and the empty conjunction in the second.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An at-most-k constraint is impossible below zero and tautological at or above the number of inputs, giving constant-size certified encodings.
assumptions_latex: x_i\in\{0,1\}\quad(1\le i\le n).
n\in\mathbb N.

Certified Cardinality Encodings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection-equivalence certificate for a CNF encoding of a cardinality constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\) be Boolean literals and let \(C(x)\) denote \(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\le k\). A certified cardinality encoding comprises a CNF formula \(E(x,y)\), with auxiliary variables \(y\), and checkable derivations establishing both projection directions: every model of \(E\) satisfies \(C\), and every assignment to \(x\) satisfying \(C\) has an extension in \(y\) satisfying \(E\). Consequently, eliminating \(y\) from \(E\) yields exactly the models of the original cardinality constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The certificate proves that the CNF encoding has exactly the cardinality-feasible assignments after auxiliary variables are projected away.
assumptions_latex: The two projection derivations are checked soundly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C(x)\iff \exists y\,E(x,y)\).

notation.meaning: its CNF encoding with auxiliary variables

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inexact Coefficient Arithmetic Invalidates PB Encoding Certification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: PB-specific failure boundary for overflow or truncation during encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If an encoding computes a partial sum or bound modulo 2^w rather than over the declared integers, the encoded comparison can differ from \sum_i a_i x_i\le b. For example, with w=2, the exact inequality 3x_1+3x_2\le3 rejects (1,1), whereas reducing the sum modulo 4 yields 2\le3 and accepts it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed-width overflow can make a PB encoding accept an assignment rejected by the exact inequality.
assumptions_latex: The source inequality uses exact integer semantics.
The purported encoding uses unsigned arithmetic modulo \(2^w\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Mod}(E)\not\subseteq\operatorname{Mod}(P).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact preprocessing of signed coefficients before certified PB encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For x_i\in\{0,1\},\quad a_i x_i=-a_i(1-x_i)+a_i.\text{ Hence a negative-coefficient term can be replaced by a nonnegative coefficient on the complemented literal with the bound shifted by the same constant.}
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Signed pseudo-Boolean inequalities can be normalized exactly by complementing literals and shifting the bound.
assumptions_latex: All coefficients and bounds are represented by exact integers.
Variables are Boolean.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_i a_i x_i\le b\text{ is equivalent to its exactly shifted nonnegative-literal form.}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A serial ripple-adder implementation uses O(nB) constant-fan-in gates and therefore O(nB) auxiliary variables and Tseitin clauses. A checker validating coefficient bits, accumulator width, connectivity, freshness, complete gate templates, and the comparator assertion runs in O(nB+L) bit operations apart from standard costs of exact integer parsing, where L is the total source-coefficient bit length.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The serial binary-adder encoding has O(nB) structural size and polynomial, output-linear certificate checking after integer parsing.
assumptions_latex: Coefficients are binary encoded.
Every gate uses a fixed constant-size CNF template.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let P(x)\equiv\sum_{i=1}^n a_i\ell_i\le b, where a_i\ge0, S=\sum_i a_i\ge1, and 0\le b<S. With B=\lceil\log_2(S+1)\rceil, build a B-bit circuit computing the exact sum, append a comparator with b, encode every gate by a complete Tseitin equivalence, and assert the comparator output. The resulting CNF E_P(x,y) satisfies P(x)\leftrightarrow\exists y\,E_P(x,y).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sufficiently wide exact adder and comparator with complete gate definitions gives a projection-exact PB encoding.

a_i\ge0

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coefficient-Sensitive Bounds for BDD and Generalized-Totalizer PB Encodings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pseudo-polynomial size boundary for explicit reachable-sum encodings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=\sum_i a_i\). A straightforward layered partial-sum decision diagram for \(\sum_i a_i\ell_i\le b\), with all values above \(b\) merged into overflow, has at most \(O(n\min\{S+1,b+2\})\) states before further semantic reduction. A generalized totalizer has size polynomial in its explicitly retained sum states and merge pairs. These are pseudo-polynomial bounds: for binary-encoded coefficients, \(S\) and the retained-state set may be exponential in the source bit length. Checking is linear in the explicit diagram or merge trace plus exact-integer parsing and arithmetic costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reachable-sum BDD and generalized-totalizer encodings may be pseudo-polynomial in coefficient magnitude despite output-sensitive certificate checking.
assumptions_latex: a_i\text{ are binary-encoded nonnegative integers}.
\text{The trace explicitly lists retained states, transitions, or merge pairs}.
\text{All arithmetic is exact}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |E_{\mathrm{BDD}}|=O(n\min\{S+1,b+2\})\text{ for the stated unreduced construction, which need not be polynomial in binary input length}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact reachable-sum tree encoding of a normalized PB inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At each node of a binary coefficient tree, record the exactly retained attainable sums of its subtree and introduce indicators governed by a fixed complete merge relation. For \(\sum_i a_i\ell_i\le b\), all sums exceeding \(b\) may be mapped to a distinguished overflow state, which is forbidden at the root. When the capping policy, retained sums, and all merge relations are checked, the resulting CNF is projection equivalent to the source inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A checked generalized totalizer combines weighted reachable sums and forbids the root overflow state.
assumptions_latex: a_i\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}.
\text{The retained sums, capping policy, and merge arithmetic are exact}.
\text{The fixed merge encoding is complete for its declared state semantics}.
\text{Auxiliary variables are fresh}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_i a_i\ell_i\le b\iff\exists y\,E_{\mathrm{GT}}(x,y).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection-exact ordered-decision-diagram encoding of a normalized pseudo-Boolean inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P(x)\equiv\sum_i a_i\ell_i\le b\) with \(a_i\ge0\), build an ordered decision diagram whose states record sufficient exact residual-sum information to determine feasibility. Encode every decision node by a complete equivalence selecting its low or high successor according to \(\ell_i\), assert the root, and forbid the false terminal. If every transition and state merge is checked, the resulting CNF satisfies \[P(x)\iff\exists y\,E_P(x,y).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A correctly checked PB decision diagram with complete node definitions is projection equivalent to the source inequality.
assumptions_latex: a_i\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}.
\text{All state arithmetic and residual-feasibility merges are exact}.
\text{The variable order and all transitions are recorded}.
\text{Auxiliary node variables are fresh}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Output-sensitive checking and exponential-size boundary of the minimal-cover encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A listed minimal-cover family is checkable by exact coefficient summation and single-element deletion tests in time polynomial in its explicit trace and coefficient bit lengths. There are at most \(2^n\) minimal covers, and exponentially many are possible: for \(a_i=1\) and \(b=\lfloor n/2\rfloor\), every subset of size \(b+1\) is a minimal cover. Hence the exact cover CNF is not generally polynomial-size in the binary source encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimal-cover clauses are individually easy to check, but their complete family can be exponentially large.
assumptions_latex: Coefficients and bounds use exact binary integer representations.
The trace explicitly lists the claimed covers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |\mathcal C_{\min}|\le2^n\quad\text{and}\quad |\mathcal C_{\min}|=2^{\Omega(n)}\text{ for some instances}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Minimal-Cover CNF Encoding of a PB Inequality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Auxiliary-free encoding of a normalized nonnegative pseudo-Boolean inequality by all inclusion-minimal overweight covers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P(\ell)\equiv\sum_{i=1}^n a_i\ell_i\le b\), where \(a_i\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\). A set \(C\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) is a minimal cover when \(\sum_{i\in C}a_i>b\) and every proper subset has weight at most \(b\). If \(\mathcal C_{\min}\) contains every minimal cover, then \[P(\ell)\iff\bigwedge_{C\in\mathcal C_{\min}}\left(\bigvee_{i\in C}\neg\ell_i\right).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative PB inequality is encoded exactly by forbidding every inclusion-minimal set of selected literals whose weight exceeds the bound.
assumptions_latex: a_i\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}.
\mathcal C_{\min}\text{ contains every inclusion-minimal overweight cover}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_i a_i\ell_i\le b\iff\bigwedge_{C\in\mathcal C_{\min}}\bigvee_{i\in C}\neg\ell_i.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constant-size certified outcomes for normalized nonnegative pseudo-Boolean inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P(\ell)\equiv\sum_{i=1}^n a_i\ell_i\le b\), where \(a_i\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\), \(\ell_i\in\{0,1\}\), and \(S=\sum_i a_i\). If \(b<0\), then \(P\) is inconsistent; if \(b\ge S\), then \(P\) is tautological. A certified encoder may therefore emit the one-clause CNF containing the empty clause for \(b<0\), the empty conjunction for \(b\ge S\), and a nontrivial encoding only for \(0\le b<S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normalized nonnegative PB inequality is impossible below zero and tautological once its bound reaches the sum of all coefficients.
assumptions_latex: a_i\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}.
S=\sum_i a_i\text{ is computed exactly}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unit-Propagation Consistency Detection for a Fixed BDD Encoding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Input-level inconsistency detection for an ordered PB decision diagram encoded by four-clause ITE equivalences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) be an ordered binary decision diagram exactly representing a pseudo-Boolean predicate \(P\). Give its accepting and rejecting terminals fixed values \(z_1=1\) and \(z_0=0\). For every node \(v\) testing literal \(\ell_i\), with low child \(l(v)\) and high child \(h(v)\), encode \[z_v\leftrightarrow((\neg\ell_i\land z_{l(v)})\lor(\ell_i\land z_{h(v)}))\] using all four ITE implication clauses, and assert the root variable. For every partial input assignment \(\rho\), unit propagation derives contradiction exactly when \(P\mid\rho\) has no satisfying completion. This consistency result does not generally imply that unit propagation derives every input literal entailed by \(P\mid\rho\), because an entailed value may require resolution across distinct live BDD branches.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The complete four-clause ITE encoding detects partial assignments with no feasible completion, but it is not generally generalized-arc-consistent on all input literals.
assumptions_latex: D\text{ exactly represents }P\text{ and respects a fixed variable order}.
\text{Terminal values, the root assertion, and all four ITE clauses are present}.
\text{BDD node variables are fresh}.
\text{Every state merge preserves an identical residual predicate}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P\mid\rho\equiv\bot\iff\operatorname{UP}(E_D\mid\rho)=\bot.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection-equivalence certificate for encoding a pseudo-Boolean inequality into CNF.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P(x)\) be the pseudo-Boolean inequality \(\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i\le b\), where \(x_i\in\{0,1\}\) and \(a_i,b\in\mathbb{Z}\). A certified pseudo-Boolean encoding comprises a CNF formula \(E(x,y)\) and checkable derivations proving that every model of \(E\) projects to an assignment satisfying \(P\), while every assignment satisfying \(P\) extends through the auxiliary variables \(y\) to a model of \(E\). Thus the encoding preserves precisely the feasible assignments on the original variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Checked projection in both directions certifies that a CNF encoding preserves exactly the solutions of the pseudo-Boolean inequality.
assumptions_latex: The coefficients and bound have a fixed finite integer representation.
The projection derivations are checked by a sound proof system.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact GCD Reduction of Integer PB Inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed coefficient preprocessing rather than a PB-to-CNF encoding or encoding certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P(x)\equiv\sum_{i=1}^n a_i\ell_i\leq b\), where \(a_i\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\), and let \(d=\gcd\{a_i:a_i>0\}\). If at least one coefficient is positive, then \[\sum_i a_i\ell_i\leq b\iff\sum_i\frac{a_i}{d}\ell_i\leq\left\lfloor\frac bd\right\rfloor.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The identity is correct, but greatest-common-divisor coefficient compression is primarily a pseudo-Boolean preprocessing transformation, not a certified PB encoding family.
assumptions_latex: a_i\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}.
\exists i\;a_i>0.
d=\gcd\{a_i:a_i>0\}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Mod}(P)=\operatorname{Mod}\!\left(\sum_i(a_i/d)\ell_i\leq\lfloor b/d\rfloor\right).

notation.meaning: greatest common divisor of the positive coefficients

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If C(x)\leftrightarrow\exists y\,E(x,y) and f depends only on x, then the two nonempty feasible sets have the same minimum value and the same projected optimal assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact projection equivalence preserves optimal values and projected optimizers for objectives over original variables.
assumptions_latex: C(x)\leftrightarrow\exists y\,E(x,y)
f=f(x)
The feasible set is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_{C(x)}f(x)=\min_{E(x,y)}f(x).
knowledge_statements.title: Projection Equivalence Preserves Original-Variable Optimization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic checker for the stated definitional certificate class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The checker validates freshness, acyclic dependency order, recorded replacement sites, and every complete local equivalence template, then constructs an extension witness by evaluating definitions in order. With indexed occurrences and adjacency lists, checking and witness construction take O(|C|+|E|+|T|) time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Acyclic definitional-extension certificates can be checked and extended in linear serialized-input time.
assumptions_latex: Formula and trace references use a validated finite serialization.
Each local definition has a fixed checkable template.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_{\mathrm{check}}=O(|C|+|E|+|T|).
knowledge_statements.title: Checker for Definitional-Extension Certificates

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Definitional Tseitin Extensions Are Projection Equivalent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete projection-equivalence certificate for acyclic Boolean definitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let E(x,y) be obtained from C(x) by introducing fresh variables y_1,\ldots,y_m in acyclic dependency order, replacing selected subformulas consistently, and conjoining complete definitions y_i\leftrightarrow\varphi_i(x,y_1,\ldots,y_{i-1}). Every model of E projects to a model of C, and every model of C has the extension obtained by evaluating the definitions in order. Hence C(x)\leftrightarrow\exists y\,E(x,y).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fresh acyclic two-direction definitions preserve exactly the original-variable models.
assumptions_latex: Every y_i is fresh.
Definitions are acyclic and encoded in both directions.
All replacement sites are recorded and consistent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{x:C(x)\}=\{x:\exists y\,E(x,y)\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Definitional Tseitin Extensions Are Projection Equivalent

knowledge_statements.scope_note: General two-component certificate schema combining soundness evidence with an extension witness generator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a source constraint \(C(x)\) and encoding \(E(x,y)\), a certificate may contain (i) an accepted refutation of \(E(x,y)\land\neg C(x)\), and (ii) an extension circuit \(W(x)\) with an accepted derivation of \(C(x)\Rightarrow E(x,W(x))\). If both proof checkers are sound and the variable maps are validated, acceptance establishes \[C(x)\iff\exists y\,E(x,y).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A soundness refutation plus a certified extension circuit proves projection equivalence.
assumptions_latex: \text{Both derivations are accepted by specified sound proof checkers}.
W\text{ has outputs corresponding exactly to the auxiliary variables}.
\text{Source, encoded, and auxiliary variable maps are validated}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C(x)\iff\exists y\,E(x,y).

notation.meaning: Circuit producing auxiliary values from a source assignment.

knowledge_statements.title: Proof-and-Extension Encoding Equivalence Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Checking and Witness Bound for Proof-and-Extension Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional verification and witness-generation cost for the two-component certificate schema.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the soundness derivation is checked in time \(T_s\), the extension derivation in time \(T_e\), the extension circuit has serialized size \(|W|\), and the variable map has size \(|M|\), then total checking time is \(O(T_s+T_e+|W|+|M|)\). For a source model, evaluating \(W\) computes an auxiliary witness in \(O(|W|)\) Boolean-gate operations; its length is the number of auxiliary outputs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The two proof checks, variable map, and extension circuit have additive verification cost, and the circuit generates explicit auxiliary witnesses.
assumptions_latex: \text{The selected proof checkers terminate with costs }T_s\text{ and }T_e.
\text{Circuit gates have constant encoded size and evaluation cost}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_{\mathrm{check}}=O(T_s+T_e+|W|+|M|).

notation.meaning: Validated source, encoded, and auxiliary variable map.

knowledge_statements.title: Checking and Witness Bound for Proof-and-Extension Certificates
Encoding Equivalence Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General certificate of existential projection equivalence between an original constraint and its encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C(x)\) be a Boolean constraint and \(E(x,y)\) an encoding using fresh auxiliary variables \(y\). An encoding equivalence certificate contains checkable derivations of soundness, \(E(x,y)\Rightarrow C(x)\), and completeness under extension, \(C(x)\Rightarrow\exists y\,E(x,y)\). If both derivations are accepted, then projection of the model set of \(E\) onto the original variables equals the model set of \(C\); hence replacing \(C\) by \(E\) preserves satisfiability and all assignments over \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two checked implications certify that projecting the encoding’s models onto the original variables gives exactly the original constraint’s models.
assumptions_latex: The auxiliary variables \(y\) are fresh.
Both implications are expressed in a sound checkable proof system.

notation.meaning: encoding over original and auxiliary variables

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role and existential-projection equivalence match the leaf. However, no source, locator, or concrete proof system supports the proposed general certificate, particularly its completeness-under-extension component.

children.title: Certified MaxSAT Preprocessing
children.top_down_role: Certified preprocessing transformations specialized to MaxSAT instances.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Two-Sided Criterion for MaxSAT Optimum Preservation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions sufficient for optimum transfer after weighted partial MaxSAT preprocessing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose every feasible \beta of F' reconstructs to feasible R(\beta) of F with \operatorname{cost}_F(R(\beta))=\operatorname{cost}_{F'}(\beta)+\delta. This gives \operatorname{opt}(F)\le\operatorname{opt}(F')+\delta. Equality follows if every feasible \alpha of F has a feasible representative \beta in F' with \operatorname{cost}_{F'}(\beta)+\delta\le\operatorname{cost}_F(\alpha).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transformed-to-original reconstruction yields one optimum inequality; a converse representation condition yields equality.
assumptions_latex: Both instances use exact minimization semantics.
Hard-clause feasibility is preserved.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{opt}(F)=\operatorname{opt}(F')+\delta.
knowledge_statements.title: Two-Sided Criterion for MaxSAT Optimum Preservation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: One-Sided Reconstruction Can Lose the Original Optimum
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counterexample to optimum preservation from reconstruction alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F have feasible assignments a_0,a_1 of costs 0,1, and let F' have one feasible assignment b of cost 1. With R(b)=a_1 and \delta=0, reconstruction preserves feasibility and cost for every transformed solution, but \operatorname{opt}(F)=0\ne1=\operatorname{opt}(F').
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A transformed instance may omit the best original solution even though all its solutions reconstruct correctly.
assumptions_latex: The finite cost tables are represented by weighted partial MaxSAT instances.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall\beta\;\operatorname{cost}_F(R(\beta))=\operatorname{cost}_{F'}(\beta)\not\Rightarrow\operatorname{opt}(F)=\operatorname{opt}(F').
knowledge_statements.title: One-Sided Reconstruction Can Lose the Original Optimum

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Checking Bound for Elementary MaxSAT Reductions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bit-complexity bound for the stated elementary rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With canonically serialized clauses, a trace of tautology deletions and duplicate-soft-clause merges is checked by validating clause references, a complementary-literal pair, equality of merged clauses, and exact weight addition. Sorting or collision-safe indexed hashing yields time polynomial in the instance and trace bit lengths.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The elementary MaxSAT reduction trace is checkable in polynomial bit time.
assumptions_latex: Integer addition is charged by operand bit length.
Clause occurrences have unambiguous identifiers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_{\mathrm{check}}=\operatorname{poly}(|F|+|T|).
knowledge_statements.title: Checking Bound for Elementary MaxSAT Reductions

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Certified MaxSAT Tautology and Duplicate-Soft-Clause Reductions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two elementary cost-preserving weighted partial MaxSAT preprocessing rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under minimization of falsified soft weight: a tautological hard or soft clause may be deleted; and identical soft clauses of weights w_1,w_2\ge0 may be replaced by one copy of weight w_1+w_2. Both rules preserve every assignment's hard feasibility and objective value, hence preserve the optimum with identity reconstruction and zero offset.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deleting tautologies and merging duplicate soft clauses by adding their weights preserve every assignment and cost.
assumptions_latex: Soft weights are exact nonnegative integers.
Clause identity and tautology are checked syntactically.
The objective is total falsified soft weight.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{cost}_{F}(\alpha)=\operatorname{cost}_{F'}(\alpha),\qquad\operatorname{opt}(F)=\operatorname{opt}(F').

notation.meaning: Source and reduced weighted partial MaxSAT instances.

knowledge_statements.title: Certified MaxSAT Tautology and Duplicate-Soft-Clause Reductions

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Certified Hard-Unit Propagation in Weighted Partial MaxSAT
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact elimination rule forced by a hard unit clause.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under minimization of falsified soft weight, if the hard formula contains the unit clause \((\ell)\), set \(\ell=1\), delete clauses thereby satisfied, and remove \(\neg\ell\) from the remaining clauses. Each soft clause that becomes empty contributes its exact weight to an objective offset \(\delta\). If a hard clause becomes empty, hard infeasibility is certified. Otherwise reinserting \(\ell=1\) reconstructs every reduced model, and its original cost is its reduced cost plus \(\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hard unit fixes its literal; exact simplification and the recorded weights of newly falsified soft clauses preserve the objective.
assumptions_latex: \text{The unit clause is hard}.
\text{The objective is total falsified soft weight}.
\text{Soft weights are exact nonnegative integers}.
\text{All affected occurrences and weight shifts are recorded}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{opt}(F)=\operatorname{opt}(F')+\delta\text{, unless an empty hard clause certifies infeasibility}.

notation.meaning: Total weight of soft clauses made empty by the forced assignment.

knowledge_statements.title: Certified Hard-Unit Propagation in Weighted Partial MaxSAT

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Certified Hard-Clause Subsumption in Weighted Partial MaxSAT
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact deletion of a hard or soft clause subsumed by a hard clause.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a hard clause and \(C\ne H\) another hard or soft clause with \(H\subseteq C\) as sets of literals. Every hard-feasible assignment satisfies \(H\), and therefore satisfies \(C\). Deleting \(C\) preserves hard feasibility and every feasible assignment's falsified-soft-weight objective; if \(C\) is soft, its cost contribution was identically zero on the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A clause subsumed by a hard clause is redundant, including a soft clause that is necessarily satisfied on every feasible assignment.
assumptions_latex: Clauses use set semantics after duplicate-literal normalization.
The objective is the exact total nonnegative weight of falsified soft clauses.
The subsuming clause \(H\) is hard.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Feas}(F)=\operatorname{Feas}(F\setminus\{C\}),\qquad \operatorname{cost}_F(\alpha)=\operatorname{cost}_{F\setminus\{C\}}(\alpha)\text{ for every feasible }\alpha.

notation.meaning: Every literal of the hard subsuming clause occurs in the deleted clause.

knowledge_statements.title: Certified Hard-Clause Subsumption in Weighted Partial MaxSAT

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary weight-sensitive reductions for weighted partial MaxSAT preprocessing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under minimization of falsified soft weight, an empty soft clause of weight \(w\ge0\) is false under every assignment and may be deleted while adding \(w\) to the objective offset. A soft clause of weight zero may be deleted with zero offset. Both transformations preserve hard feasibility and satisfy \(\operatorname{opt}(F)=\operatorname{opt}(F')+\delta\) with identity reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An empty soft clause contributes a constant offset, while a zero-weight soft clause contributes nothing; both can be deleted exactly.
assumptions_latex: Soft weights are exact nonnegative integers.
The objective is total falsified soft weight.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \delta=w\text{ for an empty weight-}w\text{ soft clause, and }\delta=0\text{ for a zero-weight soft clause}.
knowledge_statements.title: Empty and Zero-Weight Soft-Clause Reductions

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Certified Pure-Literal Assignment in Weighted Partial MaxSAT
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact MaxSAT preprocessing when a variable occurs in only one polarity throughout the current instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\ell\) be a literal such that its complement \(\bar\ell\) occurs in no hard or soft clause of a weighted partial MaxSAT instance \(F\). Assign \(\ell=1\), delete every clause containing \(\ell\), and remove its variable. Every reduced assignment extends by \(\ell=1\) with identical hard feasibility and falsified-soft weight, while changing any original assignment to \(\ell=1\) cannot falsify a previously satisfied clause. Hence the transformation preserves the optimum with zero offset.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A variable occurring in only one polarity can be fixed to satisfy that polarity and removed without changing the optimum.
assumptions_latex: \(\bar\ell\) occurs in no current hard or soft clause.
Soft weights are exact and nonnegative.
The objective is total falsified soft weight.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{opt}(F)=\operatorname{opt}(F'),\qquad \delta=0.

notation.meaning: Instance after pure-literal assignment and simplification.

knowledge_statements.title: Certified Pure-Literal Assignment in Weighted Partial MaxSAT

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact weight-sensitive preprocessing of two interacting complementary soft unit clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a weighted partial MaxSAT instance contains soft unit clauses \((x,w_+)\) and \((\neg x,w_-)\), where \(w_+,w_-\ge0\). Let \(m=\min\{w_+,w_-\}\). Replace their weights by \(w_+-m\) and \(w_--m\), delete any resulting zero-weight copy, and add \(m\) to the objective offset. Every assignment violates exactly one of the two original units, so its original cost equals its transformed cost plus \(m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subtracting the smaller weight from complementary soft units extracts a constant objective offset without changing assignment rankings.
assumptions_latex: w_+,w_-\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}.
\text{The objective is total falsified soft weight}.
\text{All other hard and soft clauses are retained unchanged}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{cost}_{F}(\alpha)=\operatorname{cost}_{F'}(\alpha)+m\quad\forall\alpha,\qquad \operatorname{opt}(F)=\operatorname{opt}(F')+m.

notation.meaning: common weight extracted as an objective offset

knowledge_statements.title: Certified Complementary Soft-Unit Weight Cancellation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Terminating trace-producing driver over the fixed elementary rule registry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a deterministic priority order on the elementary registry. Starting from \(F_0\), repeatedly select the first applicable rule and its lexicographically first canonical witness, emit and check its trace record, and replace the current instance by the recorded result. Stop on certified hard infeasibility or when no rule applies. Every nonterminal step deletes at least one current clause or eliminates at least one current variable and introduces no new variable. If the final feasible instance is \(F_m\), then \[\operatorname{opt}(F_0)=\operatorname{opt}(F_m)+\sum_{i=1}^{m}\delta_i,\] and reverse replay of recorded forced literals reconstructs an original optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A deterministic saturation loop over the fixed elementary rules terminates, accumulates exact offsets, and reconstructs an original optimum by reverse replay.
assumptions_latex: \text{Only rules in the Elementary Certified MaxSAT Trace Grammar are used}.
\text{Each application passes its local checker before mutation}.
\text{Canonical witness selection and rule priority are fixed}.
\text{All weight and offset arithmetic is exact}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: m\leq n_0+m_0,\qquad \operatorname{opt}(F_0)=\operatorname{opt}(F_m)+\sum_{i=1}^{m}\delta_i\text{ unless hard infeasibility is certified}.

notation.meaning: initial numbers of variables and clauses

knowledge_statements.title: Saturating Elementary Certified MaxSAT Preprocessor

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Total Trace Bound for Elementary Saturation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Total serialization and checking bounds for the fixed noncreating elementary preprocessing driver.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N\) be the initial serialized instance length and \(q=n_0+m_0\). The elementary saturation driver emits at most \(q\) records. If every record lists or validly indexes each affected clause occurrence, its total trace length is polynomial in \(N\): the registry introduces no variables or literals, and merged weights have at most the bit length of the initial total soft weight. Deterministic replay, exact arithmetic, and local rule validation therefore run in time polynomial in \(N+|T|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The noncreating elementary saturation run has at most variables-plus-clauses steps and a polynomial-size, polynomial-time-checkable trace.
assumptions_latex: \text{The driver uses only the fixed elementary registry}.
\text{Every affected occurrence is serialized or referenced by a validated index}.
\text{Exact integer operations are charged by operand bit length}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |T|=\operatorname{poly}(N),\qquad T_{\mathrm{check}}=\operatorname{poly}(N+|T|).
knowledge_statements.title: Total Trace Bound for Elementary Saturation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Executable trace grammar for the represented elementary weighted-partial-MaxSAT preprocessing rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An elementary MaxSAT preprocessing trace is a sequence of records \(t_i=(r_i,I_i,D_i,A_i,\delta_i,W_i)\). Here \(r_i\) is one of \{tautology deletion, duplicate-soft merge, hard-unit propagation, hard-clause subsumption, empty/zero-soft deletion, pure-literal assignment, complementary-soft-unit cancellation\}; \(I_i\) lists canonical input-clause identifiers; \(D_i\) and \(A_i\) list deleted and added canonical clauses with exact binary weights; \(\delta_i\geq0\) is the objective-offset increment; and \(W_i\) records a forced literal or identity reconstruction witness. A checker replays records in order and accepts exactly when the referenced current clauses satisfy the selected rule's syntactic, arithmetic, feasibility, reconstruction, and offset conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The trace language uses canonical clause references and a finite registry of represented elementary MaxSAT rules, permitting deterministic local replay.
assumptions_latex: \text{Clauses have canonical literal ordering and persistent identifiers}.
\text{Weights and offsets are exact binary nonnegative integers}.
\text{Each rule identifier has the local judgment stated by its accepted rule theorem}.
\text{The checker rejects stale identifiers and arithmetic overflow}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Check}(F_0,T)=F_m\text{ is a deterministic executable judgment, and every accepted step satisfies its local reconstruction and offset contract}.

notation.meaning: elementary rule identifier at trace step i
referenced, deleted, and added clause records

knowledge_statements.title: Elementary Certified MaxSAT Trace Grammar
Certified MaxSAT Preprocessing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trace-producing preprocessing with certified optimum and model preservation for weighted partial MaxSAT.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a weighted partial MaxSAT instance \(F_0\). Initialize \(F\leftarrow F_0\) and an empty trace \(T\). Repeatedly select an applicable preprocessing rule, emit its parameters and a locally checkable preservation certificate, and replace \(F\) by the transformed instance. Output \((F',T,R,\delta)\), where \(R\) reconstructs an original feasible assignment from any feasible assignment of \(F'\), and \(\delta\) is the accumulated objective offset. Accept only if every trace step checks and reconstructed assignments satisfy \(\operatorname{cost}_{F_0}(R(eta))=\operatorname{cost}_{F'}(\beta)+\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each preprocessing step is logged and checked, while reconstruction and an objective offset transfer solutions and optimal values back to the original MaxSAT instance.
assumptions_latex: All soft weights are nonnegative integers.
Every applied transformation has a sound local checking rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{opt}(F_0)=\operatorname{opt}(F')+\delta\), with optimal models recoverable by \(R\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is an appropriate content kind, but the statement contains the undefined expression R(eta) while quantifying a transformed assignment beta. More importantly, reconstruction from every feasible transformed assignment plus an objective equation supplies only one preservation direction and does not by itself establish equality of optimum values; authoritative rule semantics and the missing converse or optimality-preservation condition are needed.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed driver over tautology deletion, duplicate merging, and hard-unit propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The proposal repeatedly applies the first applicable rule from a fixed ordered elementary rule set and emits its record. Conditional on every accepted step strictly decreasing a finite measure and satisfying a concrete two-sided preservation contract, the loop terminates and the composed offsets preserve the optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A measure-decreasing saturation loop would terminate, but the supplied proposal lacks the concrete trace language and full rule contracts needed for an accepted algorithm.
assumptions_latex: \text{A concrete rule registry and checker exist}.
\text{Every accepted step strictly decreases a well-founded measure}.
\text{Every emitted step satisfies two-sided optimum preservation}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{opt}(F_0)=\operatorname{opt}(F_m)+\sum_i\delta_i\text{ only under the unstated concrete contracts}.
knowledge_statements.title: Saturating Trace-Producing MaxSAT Preprocessor

The abstract trace schema and saturation driver were deferred as nonexecutable. A concrete trace language, weight-sensitive rule, and complete driver remain. PB transformations and generic trace composition were excluded as sibling scopes.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed abstract trace schema for weighted partial MaxSAT preprocessing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A trace is proposed as a sequence \((F_{i-1},r_i,p_i,w_i,F_i)\), where \(r_i\) names a rule, \(p_i\) gives clause and weight references, and \(w_i\) gives reconstruction data. The proposal declares a step acceptable when an associated rule contract establishes the required two preservation directions and objective offset.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proposal describes the fields of a MaxSAT preprocessing trace but does not fix an executable rule registry or local judgments.
assumptions_latex: \text{Clauses and weights would require canonical identifiers}.
\text{Every rule would require a fixed local checking contract}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{No concrete acceptance relation follows until the rule grammar and contracts are fixed}.
knowledge_statements.title: MaxSAT Preprocessing Trace Judgment

children.title: Certified Pseudo-Boolean Preprocessing
children.top_down_role: Certified preprocessing transformations specialized to pseudo-Boolean instances.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic condition required of certified PB preprocessing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If every feasible z of P' reconstructs to feasible R(z) of P with f(R(z))=f'(z)+\delta, then \operatorname{opt}(P)\le\operatorname{opt}(P')+\delta. Equality additionally requires that every feasible x of P have a feasible representative z of P' satisfying f'(z)+\delta\le f(x).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: PB preprocessing needs transformed-to-original reconstruction and a converse representation condition to preserve the optimum.
assumptions_latex: All arithmetic is exact.
Both instances use minimization semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{opt}(P)=\operatorname{opt}(P')+\delta.
knowledge_statements.title: Two-Sided PB Optimum-Preservation Criterion

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inexact PB Preprocessing Can Change Feasibility and Optimum
knowledge_statements.scope_note: PB-specific failure boundary for coefficient rounding or overflow during preprocessing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For P:\min x_1+x_2\text{ subject to }3x_1+3x_2\ge4, the exact feasible set requires x_1=x_2=1 and has optimum 2. Replacing coefficient 3 by 2 through unjustified rounding gives 2x_1+2x_2\ge4, which happens to preserve this example, whereas replacing it by 1 gives x_1+x_2\ge4 and makes the instance infeasible. Therefore coefficient rewriting requires an exact checked equivalence or a certified directional preservation condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uncertified coefficient rounding can change PB feasibility and therefore the optimum.
assumptions_latex: Variables are Boolean.
The source coefficients use exact integer semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Unjustified coefficient replacement need not preserve }\operatorname{Feas}(P)\text{ or }\operatorname{opt}(P).
knowledge_statements.title: Inexact PB Preprocessing Can Change Feasibility and Optimum

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bit Complexity of Elementary PB Trace Checking
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Checking bound for fixed-variable substitution and gcd normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A checker validates substitution by scanning affected coefficients and recomputing exact bound and objective shifts. It validates gcd normalization by recomputing the gcd, exact quotients, and directed bound rounding. Both checks run in time polynomial in the total binary length of the affected constraints and trace data.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The two elementary PB preprocessing certificates are checkable in polynomial bit time.
assumptions_latex: Integers are binary encoded.
Any forcing premise has an independently checkable certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_{\mathrm{check}}=\operatorname{poly}(|P|+|T|).
knowledge_statements.title: Bit Complexity of Elementary PB Trace Checking

knowledge_statements.statement_title: GCD Normalization of an Integer PB Inequality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact coefficient normalization for one nonzero integer PB inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \sum_i a_i\ell_i\le b with integers a_i\ge0 and g=\gcd\{a_i:a_i>0\}>0, the left side is a multiple of g, so the inequality is equivalent on Boolean assignments to \sum_i(a_i/g)\ell_i\le\lfloor b/g\rfloor. For a greater-than-or-equal inequality, the corresponding bound is \lceil b/g\rceil.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dividing PB coefficients by their positive gcd and rounding the bound in the correct direction preserves feasibility.
assumptions_latex: a_i,b\in\mathbb Z
a_i\ge0
At least one coefficient is positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_i a_i\ell_i\le b\iff\sum_i(a_i/g)\ell_i\le\lfloor b/g\rfloor.
knowledge_statements.title: GCD Normalization of an Integer PB Inequality

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Certified Fixed-Variable Substitution in PB Instances
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact PB preprocessing rule for a globally forced variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a checked premise establishes x_j=c\in\{0,1\} for every feasible solution, substitute c for x_j in every constraint and the objective, shift bounds by the resulting constants, and record the removed objective constant as \delta. Deletion and reinsertion of x_j=c preserve feasibility, and \operatorname{opt}(P)=\operatorname{opt}(P')+\delta.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A globally forced Boolean variable can be substituted exactly when all bound and objective shifts are recorded.
assumptions_latex: All arithmetic is exact.
The premise x_j=c is certified for the entire current feasible set.
Source and target use the same optimization direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{opt}(P)=\operatorname{opt}(P')+\delta.
knowledge_statements.title: Certified Fixed-Variable Substitution in PB Instances

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coefficient Saturation for a Normalized PB Constraint
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact coefficient-capping rule for a nonnegative at-least pseudo-Boolean inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\sum_i a_i\ell_i\ge b\) with integers \(a_i\ge0\) and \(b>0\), replacing each coefficient by \(a_i'=\min\{a_i,b\}\) preserves the satisfying Boolean assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a nonnegative at-least PB inequality, every coefficient larger than the bound may be capped at the bound exactly.
assumptions_latex: a_i,b\in\mathbb Z.
a_i\ge0.
\ell_i\text{ are Boolean literals}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_i a_i\ell_i\ge b\iff\sum_i\min\{a_i,b\}\ell_i\ge b.
knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient Saturation for a Normalized PB Constraint

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deletion of a PB constraint implied by the remaining system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=Q\land A\). If a specified sound PB proof checker accepts a derivation of \(Q\models A\), then deleting \(A\) preserves exactly the feasible assignments. With the objective unchanged, all objective values and the optimum are preserved using identity reconstruction and zero offset.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A PB constraint can be deleted when a checked derivation proves it implied by the remaining system.
assumptions_latex: \text{The implication }Q\models A\text{ is accepted by a specified sound PB proof checker}.
\text{The objective is unchanged}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Feas}(Q\land A)=\operatorname{Feas}(Q),\qquad\operatorname{opt}(Q\land A)=\operatorname{opt}(Q).
knowledge_statements.title: Certified PB Redundancy Deletion

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Certified Range Simplification of a Normalized PB Constraint
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact tautology and infeasibility tests from the attainable range of one nonnegative PB inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n a_i\ell_i\), where \(a_i\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\), and let \(S=\sum_i a_i\). Since \(0\le L(x)\le S\), the constraint \(L(x)\ge b\) is tautological for \(b\le0\) and infeasible for \(b>S\); dually, \(L(x)\le b\) is infeasible for \(b<0\) and tautological for \(b\ge S\). Exact validation of \(S\) therefore certifies deletion of a tautology or immediate infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The exact attainable range of a nonnegative PB sum identifies trivial constraints and immediate infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: All coefficients and the bound are exact integers.
a_i\ge0.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\le L(x)\le S\text{ yields the stated tautology and infeasibility cases}.

notation.meaning: Exact sum of the nonnegative coefficients.

knowledge_statements.title: Certified Range Simplification of a Normalized PB Constraint

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Complementary-Literal Aggregation in a PB Constraint
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact within-constraint simplification of coefficients on a variable and its complement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) contain no occurrence of \(x\). For integers \(a,c,b\), \[A+a x+c(1-x)\le b\iff A+(a-c)x\le b-c.\] The same identity holds with \(\ge\) or \(=\). Applied to an objective, removing the constant \(c\) records \(c\) as the objective offset. Thus duplicate and complementary occurrences can be aggregated using exact integer arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coefficients on a variable and its complement can be combined exactly while shifting the bound or objective constant.
assumptions_latex: All coefficient, bound, and objective arithmetic is exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A+a x+c(1-x)\bowtie b\iff A+(a-c)x\bowtie b-c,\qquad \bowtie\in\{\le,\ge,=\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Complementary-Literal Aggregation in a PB Constraint

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Optimal Elimination of an Unconstrained PB Variable
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-aware elimination of a Boolean variable absent from every PB constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a minimization PB instance whose objective is \(f(x)=c x_j+g(x_{-j})\), and suppose \(x_j\) occurs in no constraint. Set \(x_j=0\) when \(c\ge0\) and \(x_j=1\) when \(c<0\), remove the term \(c x_j\), and record \(\delta=\min\{0,c\}\). The reduced feasible set is the projection of the original feasible set, every reduced optimum extends by the prescribed value, and \(\operatorname{opt}(P)=\operatorname{opt}(P')+\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unconstrained Boolean variable is fixed to its cheaper objective value and eliminated with the corresponding constant offset.
assumptions_latex: The instance is a minimization problem.
\(x_j\) occurs in no constraint.
The objective coefficient \(c\) is represented exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{opt}(P)=\operatorname{opt}(P')+\min\{0,c\}.

notation.meaning: Boolean variable absent from all constraints.
Objective coefficient of the eliminated variable.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimal Elimination of an Unconstrained PB Variable

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Sign Normalization by Literal Complementation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certified normalization of a negative coefficient in a linear pseudo-Boolean constraint or objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in\{0,1\}\) and \(a<0\), \(ax=a+(-a)(1-x)\). Hence \(A+ax\bowtie b\) is equivalent to \(A+(-a)(1-x)\bowtie b-a\), for \(\bowtie\in\{\le,\ge,=\}\). In a minimization objective, the replacement records the constant \(a\) as an objective offset.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A negative coefficient can be made positive by complementing its literal and exactly recording the resulting bound or objective shift.
assumptions_latex: a\in\mathbb Z_{<0}.
All arithmetic and recorded shifts are exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A+ax\bowtie b\iff A+(-a)(1-x)\bowtie b-a,\qquad \bowtie\in\{\le,\ge,=\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Sign Normalization by Literal Complementation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact redundancy rule for normalized pseudo-Boolean inequalities having identical left-hand sides.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L(x)\) be an exact integer pseudo-Boolean form. If the system contains \(L(x)\ge b_1\) and \(L(x)\ge b_2\) with \(b_1\ge b_2\), then \(L(x)\ge b_2\) is redundant. Dually, if it contains \(L(x)\le b_1\) and \(L(x)\le b_2\) with \(b_1\le b_2\), then \(L(x)\le b_2\) is redundant. Exact normalized-LHS equality and bound comparison certify either deletion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For identical normalized PB left-hand sides, the inequality with the weaker bound can be deleted exactly.
assumptions_latex: All coefficients and bounds are exact integers.
The compared left-hand sides are identical after certified normalization.
The objective is unchanged.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Feas}(P)=\operatorname{Feas}(P')\quad\text{and}\quad\operatorname{opt}(P)=\operatorname{opt}(P').
knowledge_statements.title: Certified Duplicate-LHS PB Subsumption

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic fixed-point driver over the elementary trace registry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: First canonicalize every constraint and objective by exact literal complementation, duplicate aggregation, and constant removal, producing nonnegative literal coefficients and recorded objective offsets. Thereafter scan in fixed identifier order and emit the first applicable range deletion, coefficient saturation, nontrivial gcd normalization, certified fixed-variable substitution, unconstrained-variable elimination, or duplicate-LHS deletion. Accept a step only when it strictly decreases \[\mu(P)=(n_{\mathrm{active}},N_{\mathrm{constraints}},N_{\mathrm{occurrences}},\sum a).\] Stop when a full scan emits no line and sum all recorded offsets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After exact canonicalization, repeatedly apply the first certified elementary reduction that strictly decreases a finite lexicographic measure.
assumptions_latex: The input instance is finite.
All rule selection and identifier ordering are deterministic.
Every post-canonicalization step strictly decreases the displayed nonnegative-integer measure.
Every forcing-premise check terminates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The algorithm terminates and }\operatorname{opt}(P_0)=\operatorname{opt}(P_m)+\sum_{t\in T}\delta_t.
knowledge_statements.title: Terminating Elementary Certified PB Preprocessor

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Output-Sensitive Checking Bound for the Elementary PB Registry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Total bit complexity of checking an explicit elementary trace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B_t\) be the binary length of all exact data in trace line \(t\), and let \(D_t\) be the cost of checking any attached forcing derivation. Exact comparison, addition, division, gcd computation, directed rounding, aggregation, and coefficient capping take time polynomial in \(B_t\). Hence \[T_{\mathrm{check}}=O\!\left(\sum_{t\in T}\operatorname{poly}(B_t)+\sum_{t\in T}D_t\right).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The elementary trace is checkable in time polynomial in its explicit binary length plus the explicitly charged costs of forcing proofs.
assumptions_latex: Integers are binary encoded.
Every line contains all data required by its local checker.
Each attached forcing proof has a terminating checker charged as \(D_t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_{\mathrm{check}}=O\!\left(\sum_t\operatorname{poly}(B_t)+\sum_tD_t\right).

notation.meaning: Explicit binary length of trace line t.
Cost of checking the forcing derivation attached to line t.

knowledge_statements.title: Output-Sensitive Checking Bound for the Elementary PB Registry

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Executable Elementary PB Preprocessing Trace Registry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete trace language for fixed exact-integer PB transformations, excluding general proof-calculus redundancy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An elementary trace is a sequence of records \(t=(r,J,p,q,\delta)\), where \(r\in\{\mathrm{canonicalize},\mathrm{range},\mathrm{gcd},\mathrm{saturate},\mathrm{forced},\mathrm{free},\mathrm{duplicate}\}\), \(J\) identifies the affected constraints or objective, \(p\) and \(q\) contain their exact pre-state and claimed post-state data, and \(\delta\) is the objective-constant change. The checker requires the recorded pre-state to equal the current state and exactly recomputes the declared rule. A forced-variable record additionally contains a checked derivation of its global forcing premise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each trace line names a fixed elementary rule and records exact before-and-after data; acceptance requires exact local recomputation and any required forcing certificate.
assumptions_latex: All integers have finite exact binary encodings.
Constraint and variable identifiers are unambiguous.
The forcing-premise checker is sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Check}(P_0,T)=P_m\Longrightarrow\text{every accepted line satisfies its declared exact transformation contract}.

notation.meaning: Objective offset contributed by one trace line.

knowledge_statements.title: Executable Elementary PB Preprocessing Trace Registry

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Executable Nonnegative-Combination Certificate for PB Implication
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound but incomplete exact-integer certificate for implication and redundancy of normalized greater-than-or-equal PB inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\) contain normalized inequalities \(A_j(x)=\sum_i a_{ji}\ell_i\ge b_j\). A certificate supplies referenced lines and multipliers \(\lambda_j\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\). Exact addition derives \[\sum_j\lambda_jA_j(x)\ge B:=\sum_j\lambda_jb_j.\] After exact aggregation of duplicate and complementary literals, let the normalized left-hand side be \(A(x)\). If the proposed target is \(A(x)\ge d\) with \(d\le B'\), where \(B'\) is the bound after all normalization-induced constant shifts, the certificate proves \(Q\models A(x)\ge d\). The target is therefore redundant in \(Q\land\{A(x)\ge d\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact nonnegative integer combination, normalization, and bound weakening provide a checkable but incomplete certificate of a pseudo-Boolean consequence.
assumptions_latex: \lambda_j\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\quad\forall j.
\text{All products, sums, complementary-literal shifts, and comparisons are computed as exact integers}.
\text{Every referenced inequality is present or was previously derived}.
\text{The target has the normalized combined left-hand side and a bound no stronger than the normalized derived bound}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{CheckComb}(Q,\pi,A\ge d)=\mathrm{accept}\Longrightarrow Q\models A(x)\ge d.

notation.meaning: nonnegative integer multiplier for referenced inequality j
combined right-hand-side bound after normalization-induced constant shifts

knowledge_statements.title: Executable Nonnegative-Combination Certificate for PB Implication

assumptions_latex: All variables, coefficients, and bounds have finite exact representations.
Every transformation has a sound local checking rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{opt}(P_0)=\operatorname{opt}(P')+\delta\), and \(R\) reconstructs original optimal solutions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trace-producing preprocessing for pseudo-Boolean optimization with certified reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a pseudo-Boolean optimization instance \(P_0\). Initialize \(P\leftarrow P_0\) and an empty trace \(T\). At each iteration, apply a declared simplification to constraints or objective, append its data and a locally checkable preservation certificate, and update \(P\). Output \((P',T,R,\delta)\), where \(R\) maps each feasible solution of \(P'\) to one of \(P_0\), and \(\delta\) is an objective offset. Acceptance requires every step to check and \(f_0(R(z))=f'(z)+\delta\) for reconstructed solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A checked transformation trace, reconstruction map, and objective offset certify that pseudo-Boolean preprocessing preserves feasibility and optimal solutions.
knowledge_statements.title: Certified Pseudo-Boolean Preprocessing

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed driver over exact PB simplifications.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The proposal repeatedly applies normalization, certified fixed-variable substitution, gcd division, eligible coefficient saturation, and proof-backed redundancy deletion until a full pass changes nothing. Conditional on a concrete rule language, exact local checkers, and a componentwise nonincreasing finite measure with a strict decrease at every accepted step, such a loop terminates and composed offsets preserve the optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A suitably measure-decreasing PB saturation loop would terminate, but the proposed algorithm lacks a concrete trace language and fixed redundancy calculus.
assumptions_latex: \text{A concrete trace format and rule registry exist}.
\text{All arithmetic is exact}.
\text{Every accepted step is componentwise nonincreasing in the finite measure and strictly decreases at least one component}.
\text{Every semantic premise is independently certified}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{opt}(P_0)=\operatorname{opt}(P_m)+\sum_i\delta_i\text{ only under the unstated concrete contracts}.
knowledge_statements.title: Saturating Trace-Producing PB Preprocessor

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Executable Cutting-Planes Certificate for PB Redundancy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed implication certificate for proof-backed PB redundancy transformations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\) be a system of integer PB inequalities and \(A\) a proposed consequence. The proposal accepts \(Q\models A\) when a finite derivation from \(Q\land\neg A\) ends in contradiction using nonnegative integer combination, normalization, rounded division, and saturation rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cutting-planes refutation could certify PB redundancy, but the proposal does not fix an executable rule registry or serialization.
assumptions_latex: All arithmetic is exact.
The negation of the target uses integer semantics.
Every inference belongs to a fixed sound rule registry.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{CheckCP}(Q\land\neg A,\pi)=\mathrm{accept}\Longrightarrow Q\models A.
knowledge_statements.title: Executable Cutting-Planes Certificate for PB Redundancy

children.title: Transformation Trace Composition
children.top_down_role: Composition of evidence across multiple preprocessing transformations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Partial Reconstruction Domains Do Not Compose
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary for concatenating traces with incompatible reconstruction domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If R_1 is certified only on D_1\subsetneq\operatorname{Feas}(P_1) and R_2 can return a model in \operatorname{Feas}(P_1)\setminus D_1, then R_1\circ R_2 is undefined on that terminal model. Thus local acceptance of the two partial traces does not certify their concatenation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partial reconstruction traces compose only when the later trace's entire output lies in the earlier trace's certified domain.
assumptions_latex: R_1\text{ and }R_2\text{ may be partial reconstruction relations}.
\operatorname{range}(R_2)\nsubseteq\operatorname{dom}(R_1).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R_1\circ R_2\text{ is not a total terminal-model reconstruction}.

notation.meaning: certified domain of the first reconstruction

knowledge_statements.title: Partial Reconstruction Domains Do Not Compose

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composition checker for typed homogeneous or heterogeneous traces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given typed component traces T_1,\ldots,T_m, the checker invokes each declared sound component checker, verifies exact adjacent instance identity, checks syntactic type compatibility of reconstruction domains and ranges, verifies common objective semantics, and adds offsets exactly. It then emits the concatenated trace, reverse reconstruction order, and \delta_{\mathrm{tot}}=\sum_i\delta_i.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A composed trace is checked componentwise plus typed interface compatibility, with reverse reconstruction and exact offset accumulation.
assumptions_latex: Each component checker is sound for its declared trace language.
The trace contract makes required reconstruction domains and ranges explicit.
Instance and numeric serializations are unambiguous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \delta_{\mathrm{tot}}=\sum_{i=1}^m\delta_i.
knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic Concatenated-Trace Checker

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Additive Size and Checking Cost of Trace Composition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational overhead for explicit typed trace concatenation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For component traces of encoded lengths L_i and checking times C_i, payload-preserving concatenation has length \Theta(\sum_iL_i). Checking costs O(\sum_iC_i+I+A), where I is adjacent-interface validation and A is exact offset addition; every checker has reading cost \Omega(\sum_iL_i).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Composed-trace size is additive, and checking cost is the sum of component, interface, and offset-processing costs.
assumptions_latex: Concatenation does not duplicate component payloads.
Offsets have finite exact encodings.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L=\Theta\!\left(\sum_iL_i\right),\qquad C=O\!\left(\sum_iC_i+I+A\right).
knowledge_statements.title: Additive Size and Checking Cost of Trace Composition

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Identity and Associativity of Certified Trace Composition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic laws for compatible trace contracts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent a certified trace contract by a reconstruction relation R, an additive offset \delta, and its declared source and target instances. The empty trace is (\operatorname{id},0). For compatible contracts, (R_1,\delta_1)\circ(R_2,\delta_2)=(R_1\circ R_2,\delta_1+\delta_2). When reconstruction range-domain and objective conventions match, the empty trace is a two-sided identity and composition is associative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compatible trace contracts compose associatively by relational composition and exact offset addition, with the empty trace as identity.
assumptions_latex: Adjacent target and source instances match exactly.
Each reconstruction is total on feasible outputs admitted by the following contract.
Objective directions and numeric semantics agree.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: ((R_1,\delta_1)\circ(R_2,\delta_2))\circ(R_3,\delta_3)=(R_1,\delta_1)\circ((R_2,\delta_2)\circ(R_3,\delta_3)).
knowledge_statements.title: Identity and Associativity of Certified Trace Composition
Transformation Trace Composition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compositional preservation and reconstruction for sequential certified transformations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a checked trace transforms \(P_0\) to \(P_1\) with reconstruction \(R_1\) and objective offset \(\delta_1\), and another transforms \(P_1\) to \(P_2\) with reconstruction \(R_2\) and offset \(\delta_2\). If each trace preserves feasibility and satisfies \(f_{i-1}(R_i(z))=f_i(z)+\delta_i\), their concatenation is certified by the composed reconstruction \(R_1\circ R_2\) and offset \(\delta_1+\delta_2\). Therefore any finite sequence of accepted traces can be checked and reconstructed compositionally.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified traces compose by concatenating their steps, composing reconstruction maps, and adding their objective offsets.
assumptions_latex: The codomain instance of the first trace equals the domain instance of the second.
Both component traces have been accepted by sound checkers.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Property is the correct role, and the affine-offset composition equation follows under compatible reconstruction domains. No source or formal trace semantics establishes that feasibility preservation and checker acceptance compose as claimed across the referenced preprocessing families.

children.title: Certified Model Reconstruction
children.top_down_role: Certified recovery of source-level assignments from transformed solutions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Feasibility Reconstruction Alone Does Not Transfer Optimality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation of model reconstruction from objective reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A checked chain proving z_0\models P_0 establishes source feasibility only. Even if z_m is optimal for P_m, optimality of z_0 does not follow without objective-preservation evidence and a condition excluding omitted better source solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reconstructing a feasible original model does not by itself prove that it is optimal.
assumptions_latex: The reconstruction checker validates feasibility only.
No objective-preservation or converse coverage certificate is assumed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: z_m\in\operatorname{argmin}P_m\land z_0\models P_0\not\Rightarrow z_0\in\operatorname{argmin}P_0.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility Reconstruction Alone Does Not Transfer Optimality

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nondeterministic inverse reconstruction with checked predecessor witnesses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each transformation P_{i-1}\to P_i, let Q_i(z_i,z_{i-1}) be total on feasible outputs and guarantee z_{i-1}\models P_{i-1}. Then any supplied chain Q_m(z_m,z_{m-1}),\ldots,Q_1(z_1,z_0) certifies z_0\models P_0; uniqueness of predecessors is unnecessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inverse reconstruction may be nondeterministic when the supplied predecessor chain is locally checked and feasible.
assumptions_latex: Each Q_i is total on feasible outputs.
Every accepted predecessor satisfies the preceding instance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: z_m\models P_m\land\bigwedge_{i=1}^mQ_i(z_i,z_{i-1})\Rightarrow z_0\models P_0.
knowledge_statements.title: Certified Reconstruction May Be Relational

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reverse traversal of accepted local reconstruction relations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an accepted trace P_0\to\cdots\to P_m and a checked model z_m\models P_m, process steps in reverse. At step i, obtain a predecessor z_{i-1}, check the declared local relation Q_i(z_i,z_{i-1}), and reject on failure. Finally evaluate every constraint of P_0 on z_0. Acceptance certifies z_0\models P_0.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Model reconstruction traverses the accepted trace backward, checks every predecessor witness, and validates the final source model.
assumptions_latex: The forward trace is accepted.
z_m\models P_m.
Each Q_i is total on the feasible outputs admitted by its transformation contract.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: z_m\models P_m\land\bigwedge_{i=1}^mQ_i(z_i,z_{i-1})\Rightarrow z_0\models P_0.
knowledge_statements.title: Reverse Certified Model Reconstruction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Size and checking complexity for an explicit reconstruction chain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If step i supplies a predecessor witness of length W_i and Q_i is checked in time C_i, the explicit chain has length \Theta(\sum_iW_i) and is checked in O(\sum_iC_i+C_0), where C_0 is final source-constraint evaluation. Reading the witnesses costs \Omega(\sum_iW_i).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reconstruction size and checking cost are additive across inverse steps, plus final source validation.
assumptions_latex: Intermediate witnesses are explicitly serialized.
Source constraints are evaluated under exact source semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: W=\Theta\!\left(\sum_iW_i\right),\qquad C=O\!\left(\sum_iC_i+C_0\right).
knowledge_statements.title: Model-Reconstruction Witness and Checking Cost

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit separation of model reconstruction from objective reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let P_0 minimize x over x\in\{0,1\}, and let P_1 have the single feasible model z_1=1. The feasibility-only reconstruction R(1)=1 produces a model of P_0, and z_1 is optimal for P_1, but R(z_1) is not optimal for P_0, whose optimum is attained at x=0.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A transformed optimum can reconstruct to a feasible but nonoptimal source model when a better source assignment was omitted.
assumptions_latex: Only transformed-to-source feasibility is certified.
No objective-preservation or converse-coverage certificate is present.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: z_1\in\operatorname{argmin}P_1\land R(z_1)\models P_0\not\Rightarrow R(z_1)\in\operatorname{argmin}P_0.
knowledge_statements.title: Concrete Feasible but Nonoptimal Reconstruction

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inverse Rule for Projection and Variable Elimination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic reconstruction contract for a transformation that projects out variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an accepted forward contract for \(P_{i-1}(x,y)\to P_i(x)\) guarantees \(P_i(x)\Rightarrow\exists y\,P_{i-1}(x,y)\).
