Reconstruction supplies values \(\widehat y\), and the checker directly validates \(P_{i-1}(x,\widehat y)\). Acceptance certifies \((x,\widehat y)\) as a feasible predecessor.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reconstruction after projection supplies and directly checks values for every eliminated variable.
assumptions_latex: P_i(x)\Rightarrow\exists y\,P_{i-1}(x,y).
x\models P_i.
\widehat y\text{ is explicitly supplied or produced by a checked witness procedure}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P_{i-1}(x,\widehat y).
knowledge_statements.title: Inverse Rule for Projection and Variable Elimination

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inverse Rule for Introduced Definitional Auxiliaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reconstruction contract when preprocessing introduced fresh variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(P_i(x,y)\) extends \(P_{i-1}(x)\) only by accepted fresh acyclic definitions of \(y\), source reconstruction projects away \(y\) and retains the checked original-variable assignment \(x\). The checker validates the variable map and source constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fresh definitional auxiliaries are discarded after validating the original-variable map and source model.
assumptions_latex: y\text{ are fresh auxiliary variables}.
P_{i-1}(x)\iff\exists y\,P_i(x,y).
\text{The original-variable map is injective and checked}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P_i(x,y)\Rightarrow P_{i-1}(x).
knowledge_statements.title: Inverse Rule for Introduced Definitional Auxiliaries

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inverse Rules for Substitution and Forced Values
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Typed semantic reconstruction contracts for eliminated fixed or defined variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If an accepted forward step removes \(x_j\) after certifying \(x_j=c\), reconstruction sets \(x_j=c\). If it removes \(x_j\) using an accepted equivalence \(x_j\leftrightarrow\psi(x_{-j})\), reconstruction evaluates the recorded total Boolean expression \(\psi\) on the surviving assignment. Checking the accepted premise, variable map, and affected source constraints certifies a feasible predecessor.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Forced variables are reinserted at certified values, while definitionally substituted variables are recomputed from their accepted definitions.
assumptions_latex: \psi\text{ is a total checked Boolean expression on surviving variables}.
\text{The forward forcing premise or defining equivalence was accepted}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: z_i\models P_i\land Q_i(z_i,z_{i-1})\Rightarrow z_{i-1}\models P_{i-1}.
knowledge_statements.title: Inverse Rules for Substitution and Forced Values
Certified Model Reconstruction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate that a transformed model reconstructs to a feasible model of the original instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a checked transformation trace map an original instance \(P_0\) to \(P_m\). Given a model \(z_m\models P_m\), a certified model reconstruction supplies intermediate assignments \(z_{m-1},\ldots,z_0\) and step records showing that each \(z_{i-1}\) is the prescribed inverse image of \(z_i\) under transformation \(i\). A checker validates every local reconstruction condition and the original constraints. Acceptance certifies \(z_0\models P_0\); if the trace is optimization-preserving and \(z_m\) is optimal, the associated objective certificate transfers optimality to \(z_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Checked inverse steps reconstruct a transformed model into a feasible original model, with optimality transferred when objective preservation is also certified.
assumptions_latex: The forward transformation trace has been accepted.
\(z_m\) satisfies the final transformed instance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_0\models P_0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Certificate fits the leaf, and the stated local checks support the displayed feasibility conclusion. The additional optimality-transfer claim depends on an unspecified associated objective certificate, while no reconstruction language, rule set, citation, or locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reconstruction Rules for Projection, Substitution, and Fresh Definitions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed omnibus statement of common inverse rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Projection, substitution, forced-variable elimination, and fresh definitional extension are claimed to admit standard locally checkable inverse witnesses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proposal groups several inverse transformations without specifying their distinct forward contracts and local judgments.
knowledge_statements.title: Reconstruction Rules for Projection, Substitution, and Fresh Definitions

intermediate_metadata.reason: The leaf covers relational reconstruction semantics, reverse traversal, additive certificate complexity, direct source feasibility validation, and a concrete failure of optimality transfer. The proposed omnibus inverse-rule theorem was deferred because projection, substitution, forced-value, and auxiliary cases require separate typed contracts. Objective reconstruction and general reconstruction-trace validation were excluded as sibling scopes.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed abstract record for one inverse transformation step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The proposal records a transformation identifier, the stage assignment, a typed predecessor witness, and references to affected variables and constraints, and declares acceptance when an associated rule-specific relation \(Q_i(z_i,z_{i-1})\) holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proposed record fields do not define an executable syntax or the rule-specific inverse judgments.
assumptions_latex: \text{The corresponding forward step has been accepted}.
\text{Identifiers would need an unambiguous serialization}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{No concrete acceptance judgment follows until the inverse-rule registry is fixed}.
knowledge_statements.title: Typed Model-Reconstruction Record

intermediate_metadata.reason: The accepted local inventory contains relational reconstruction, reverse traversal, separate inverse contracts for projection, forced values, definitional substitution and auxiliaries, additive checking cost, final source feasibility validation, and the failure of feasibility-only optimality transfer. The proposed typed record was deferred because it is not an executable certificate language. Objective reconstruction and generic reconstruction-trace validation were excluded as sibling scopes.

children.title: Certified Objective Reconstruction
children.top_down_role: Certified recovery of source-level objective values from transformed solutions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise and optimum-value consequences of checked affine objective relations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For feasible sets \(X_i\), reconstruction maps \(R_i:X_i\to X_{i-1}\), and checked relations \(f_{i-1}(R_i(z))=a_i f_i(z)+b_i\) with \(a_i>0\), composition gives \(f_0(R(z))=Af_m(z)+B\), where \(A=\prod_i a_i>0\). This certifies values and ordering on \(R(X_m)\). If \(R(X_m)\) contains an optimizer of \(f_0\) over \(X_0\), then \(\operatorname{OPT}_0=A\operatorname{OPT}_m+B\); surjectivity of \(R\) is sufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Checked positive-affine step relations compose, but global optimum transfer additionally requires the reconstructed image to contain an original optimizer.
assumptions_latex: R_i(X_i)\subseteq X_{i-1}
a_i>0
All coefficients and objective values are checked exactly.
The relevant optima are attained when optimum equality is asserted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f_0(R(z))=Af_m(z)+B;\quad R(X_m)\cap\operatorname*{argopt}_{x\in X_0}f_0(x)\ne\varnothing\Rightarrow\operatorname{OPT}_0=A\operatorname{OPT}_m+B.

notation.meaning: composed positive scale and affine offset

knowledge_statements.title: Composed Objective-Reconstruction Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp failure of optimum transfer without optimizer coverage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact reconstruction on every transformed solution can miss a better original solution.
assumptions_latex: No optimizer-coverage or lifting condition is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f_0\circ R=Af_m+B\not\Rightarrow\operatorname{OPT}_0=A\operatorname{OPT}_m+B.
knowledge_statements.title: Missing-Image Counterexample
Certified Objective Reconstruction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate relating objective values before and after certified transformations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an accepted transformation trace from optimization instance \(P_0\) to \(P_m\), an objective-reconstruction certificate supplies exact step relations \(f_{i-1}(R_i(z_i))=a_i f_i(z_i)+b_i\), with \(a_i>0\), for every reconstructible feasible \(z_i\). A checker validates these relations and composes them to obtain \(f_0(R(z_m))=A f_m(z_m)+B\), where \(A=\prod_i a_i>0\) and \(B\) is the induced affine offset. Acceptance certifies preservation of objective ordering and permits reconstruction of the original optimum value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Checked positive affine relations compose to recover original objective values and preserve the ordering of feasible solutions.
assumptions_latex: Each transformation has a total reconstruction map on its feasible outputs.
All scaling and offset values are represented exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_0(R(z_m))=A f_m(z_m)+B\) with \(A>0\), so \(\operatorname{opt}(P_0)=A\operatorname{opt}(P_m)+B\).

notation.meaning: composed positive scale and affine offset

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Certificate is the appropriate content kind, but positive affine relations along a total map from transformed feasible solutions to original ones preserve ordering only among reconstructed images. They do not alone imply equality of the two global optima without an appropriate lifting, coverage, or optimal-solution correspondence condition. A source is needed to determine the intended semantics and hypotheses.

children.title: Reconstruction Trace Validation
children.top_down_role: Validation of reconstruction records across transformation sequences.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract deterministic validator for an identified transformation trace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(P_0,\ldots,P_m\), an ordered trace \(T\), and final model \(z_m\), check trace syntax, identifiers, scopes, and adjacency; check \(z_m\models P_m\); then traverse backward, accepting \(z_{i-1}\) and each objective relation only through the validator for the identified rule. Finally check \(z_0\models P_0\) and the composed objective equation. Reject at the first failed check.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Validate trace linkage and walk backward through sound local reconstruction rules, rejecting any invalid step.
assumptions_latex: Every admitted rule has a deterministic sound local validator.
All trace data are finitely and unambiguously represented.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Validate}(P_0,\ldots,P_m,T,z_m)=\operatorname{accept}\Rightarrow z_0\models P_0\text{ and the accepted objective relation holds}.
knowledge_statements.title: Backward Reconstruction-Trace Validation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure caused by omitted, reordered, or context-mismatched records.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Individually valid records cannot be composed when an output instance, namespace, objective convention, or transformation identifier fails to equal the corresponding input of the adjacent record.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Valid isolated records do not certify reconstruction when adjacent stages or scopes fail to match.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists i:\operatorname{out}(t_i)\ne\operatorname{in}(t_{i-1})\Rightarrow T\text{ is not a valid compositional trace}.
knowledge_statements.title: Broken Trace Link Invalidates Composition

knowledge_statements.scope_note: End-to-end soundness inherited from linked sound local validators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If every accepted local judgment \(V_i(P_{i-1},P_i,z_i,z_{i-1})\) soundly establishes the declared reconstruction and objective relation, and all adjacent stage identities agree, then acceptance of every step composes to a valid source model and objective relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sound, correctly linked local reconstruction judgments compose into a sound end-to-end certificate.
assumptions_latex: Each V_i is sound for its identified rule.
Adjacent instance identities, namespaces, scopes, and numerical conventions agree.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: z_m\models P_m\land\bigwedge_{i=1}^m V_i=\operatorname{accept}\Rightarrow z_0\models P_0.
knowledge_statements.title: Compositional Trace-Validation Soundness
Reconstruction Trace Validation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic checking procedure for model and objective reconstruction traces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an original instance \(P_0\), a transformed instance \(P_m\), a transformation trace \(T\), a final model \(z_m\), and claimed intermediate models and objective relations. Check the syntax and adjacency of all trace steps; then traverse \(T\) backward, validating each local inverse rule, each reconstructed assignment, and each objective relation. Finally check \(z_0\models P_0\) and the composed objective equation. Output accept with \((z_0,f_0(z_0))\) only if every check succeeds; otherwise output reject at the first invalid step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The validator walks backward through the trace, checks every reconstruction and objective relation, and accepts only a valid original model and value.
assumptions_latex: Every transformation rule has a deterministic local validator.
All instances, models, and numerical data are finitely represented.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Validate}(P_0,P_m,T,z_m)=\operatorname{accept}\Rightarrow z_0\models P_0\) and the reported objective relation holds.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm fits this validation leaf, and its plain and mathematical statements agree. Its soundness is conditional on an unspecified trace format and local validators, with no authoritative citation or inspectable locator supporting those rules.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract command-processing procedure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(S_0\) from \(F_0\). Process commands in order, validating additions before activation, applying only admissible deletions, opening or closing scopes according to the declared lifetime rules, and accepting a query only from live validated objects. Reject at the first invalid transition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Process each log command against the current state and accept queries only from live validated evidence.
assumptions_latex: Each command class has a sound validator and state-transition rule.
The log is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{accept}(L)\Rightarrow\text{every accepted query follows from its prefix state}.
knowledge_statements.title: Sequential Incremental-Log Checking

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Calculus-independent state semantics for an incremental proof log.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After prefix \(L_{\le k}\), let \(S_k=(A_k,D_k,\Gamma_k)\), where \(A_k\) is the active validated constraint set, \(D_k\) records live derived objects and dependencies, and \(\Gamma_k\) records open assumptions. A query at position \(k\) may use only objects live in \(S_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An incremental proof log denotes an ordered sequence of active constraints, dependencies, and assumption scopes.
assumptions_latex: Identifiers have unique live meanings.
Scope and deletion lifetimes are formally specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{meaning}(q_k)\text{ is evaluated relative to }S_k.
knowledge_statements.title: Incremental Checker-State Semantics

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lifetime failures invalidating incremental certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A checker must reject use of a deleted object, or of a dependent object whose continuing validity was not established, and must reject export of a conclusion after an assumption closes unless an accepted discharge rule justifies it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use-after-deletion and undisclosed assumption leakage invalidate incremental query certificates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{invalid lifetime use or undischarged scope escape}\Rightarrow\operatorname{reject}.
knowledge_statements.title: Unsafe Deletion and Scope Leakage

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inductive soundness invariant for stateful checking.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If initialization is sound and every accepted transition preserves that each live derived constraint follows from \(F_0\) and the currently open assumptions, then every accepted query \(Q_k\) satisfies \(F_0\land\bigwedge\Gamma_k\models Q_k\). Later commands do not alter the meaning of the accepted prefix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sound state invariant makes each accepted query valid under the assumptions active at that query.
assumptions_latex: Initialization and every transition preserve the entailment invariant.
Queries are tied immutably to their log positions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{accept}(q_k)\Rightarrow F_0\land\bigwedge\Gamma_k\models Q_k.
knowledge_statements.title: Prefix Soundness of Accepted Queries
Incremental Proof Logging
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stateful proof logging across additions, deletions, assumptions, and repeated solver queries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize the checker state with a base constraint set \(F_0\). For each event, append a log command that either adds a constraint with a derivation from the active state, deletes a previously validated constraint, opens or closes a scoped assumption, or records a query conclusion. The checker processes commands in order and updates the active set only after validation. A query claiming unsatisfiability or an objective bound is accepted only when its derivation uses constraints active in that query's scope. The output is the sequence of accepted query conclusions or rejection at the first invalid command.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stateful checker validates logged changes and accepts each query result only from constraints active in that query’s scope.
assumptions_latex: Command identifiers and assumption scopes are unambiguous.
The underlying derivation checker is sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{accept}(L)\Rightarrow\) every logged query conclusion follows from its active constraint state.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is suitable for the Incremental Proof Logging topic, but additions, deletions, scoped assumptions, and objective-bound queries require precise calculus-specific semantics. No citation, locator, command format, or concrete proof system is provided, so the soundness claim cannot be reviewed reliably.

knowledge_statements.title: Independent PB Proof Checkers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound acceptance criterion for a checker implemented independently of the proof-producing PB solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\) be a pseudo-Boolean instance, \(P\) a purported refutation, and \(C\) a deterministic checker developed without reusing the solver's inference implementation. The checker is sound when
\[C(F,P)=\mathsf{accept}\;\Longrightarrow\;F\text{ has no assignment in }\{0,1\}^n.\]
For an optimization claim with objective \(f\) and bound \(b\), acceptance must instead imply that the separately encoded bound claim follows from \(F\). Thus \((F,P)\), together with the fixed checker specification, is a mechanically verifiable certificate; implementation independence supplies diversity, not soundness by itself.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An independent checker certifies unsatisfiability or an objective bound only when acceptance soundly implies the claimed property of the original PB instance.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) and \(P\) have unambiguous finite encodings.
\(C\) implements the specified proof rules and rejects malformed steps.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C(F,P)=\mathsf{accept}\Rightarrow F\text{ is unsatisfiable}\), with the analogous implication for encoded optimization bounds.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the PB-specific soundness contract or independence claim. The statement also describes a checker soundness condition rather than a certificate itself; the exact proof calculus and optimization-bound encoding must be instantiated.

knowledge_statements.title: Formally Verified PB Checkers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: End-to-end soundness contract for a PB checker connected to a machine-checked semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\llbracket F\rrbracket\) denote the Boolean semantics of a parsed pseudo-Boolean instance and let \(V(F,P)\) be an executable checker extracted from, or refinement-verified against, a formal specification. A formally verified checker provides a machine-checked theorem
\[V(F,P)=\mathsf{accept}\;\Longrightarrow\;\neg\exists x\in\{0,1\}^n:\llbracket F\rrbracket(x)=\mathsf{true}.\]
The certificate is end-to-end only if verified parsing connects the input bytes to \(F\), verified arithmetic excludes overflow discrepancies, and the executed binary is related to the verified checker artifact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A formally verified checker certifies a PB refutation through a machine-checked soundness theorem, provided parsing, arithmetic, and executable refinement remain within scope.
assumptions_latex: The formal semantics covers every accepted proof command.
Parsing, arithmetic, and executable refinement satisfy their stated verification contracts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V(F,P)=\mathsf{accept}\Rightarrow \llbracket F\rrbracket\text{ is unsatisfiable}.\)

notation.meaning: Formal Boolean semantics of the parsed instance.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A formal-verification source is required to substantiate the claimed end-to-end theorem and its parsing, arithmetic, extraction, and binary-refinement scope. The record concerns checker soundness rather than a certificate object.

children.title: Proof Elaboration
children.top_down_role: Expansion of compact proof records into checker-ready evidence.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Soundness condition for expanding compact commands into primitive checker steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let each source macro \(m\), invoked in derivation state \(S\), have a finite expansion \(E(m,S)\) into primitive rules of calculus \(R\). If checking each expansion succeeds whenever the macro precondition holds, and the expansion preserves the macro's exposed conclusion, identifier environment, and every state invariant consumed by later commands, sequential replacement of all macros yields a primitive log \(Q\) with the same terminal claim as the compact log \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite macro expansions compose correctly when each expansion preserves the source command's conclusion and externally visible derivation state.
assumptions_latex: Every supported expansion is finite.
Each expansion preserves exposed conclusions, identifiers, and later-state invariants.
The primitive checker accepts each generated rule application.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{check}_R(F,Q)=\mathsf{accept}\land \operatorname{claim}(Q)=\operatorname{claim}(P).

notation.meaning: Primitive expansion of macro m in derivation state S.

knowledge_statements.title: Compositional Soundness of Macro Expansion
Proof Elaboration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expansion of abbreviated PB proof steps into primitive steps accepted by a target checker.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given an instance \(F\), a compact proof log \(P=(s_1,\ldots,s_m)\), and a primitive checker calculus \(R\), initialize \(Q\) as the empty sequence. Process each \(s_i\) in order: resolve every reference against the current derivation state, expand each macro or omitted witness into a finite sequence of rules from \(R\), and append those rules to \(Q\). Reject if expansion fails or a generated premise is unavailable. Stop after \(s_m\) and output \(Q\), requiring
\[\operatorname{check}_R(F,Q)=\mathsf{accept}\]
whenever elaboration reports success.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Elaboration replaces every abbreviated proof command with explicit primitive inferences while preserving references and requiring the target checker to accept the result.
assumptions_latex: Every supported macro has a finite expansion into rules of \(R\).
All identifiers and numeric coefficients have exact encodings.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Successful elaboration outputs \(Q\) with \(\operatorname{check}_R(F,Q)=\mathsf{accept}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the Proof Elaboration leaf, but no cited proof format or calculus establishes finite macro expansion, reference handling, or the stated success contract.

children.title: Proof Compression
children.top_down_role: Reduction of proof-record size while preserving checkability.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient interface condition for replacing a proof subderivation by a smaller derivation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an accepted proof be decomposed as \(P=A D B\). Suppose the externally visible results of \(D\) used by \(B\) form an interface \(I\), every external premise used by \(D\) remains available after \(A\), and \(D'\) derives the identical interface \(I\) without changing checker state consumed by \(B\). After consistently updating identifiers, \(P'=A D' B\) is a valid replacement whenever the fixed checker accepts it. If \(|D'|<|D|\) under the declared size measure, the replacement is a strict local compression.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proof segment may be replaced by a smaller segment deriving the same externally visible results, provided later references and checker state remain valid and the result is rechecked.
assumptions_latex: The target checker accepts every inference in \(D'\).
No unrepresented state produced only by \(D\) is consumed by \(B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C(F,A D' B)=\mathsf{accept}\land |D'|<|D|\Longrightarrow A D' B\text{ is a strict valid local compression}.

notation.meaning: Prefix, replaced subderivation, and suffix of the original log.
Externally visible interface of the replaced subderivation.

knowledge_statements.title: Compositional Subderivation Replacement
Proof Compression
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantics-preserving reduction of a PB proof log relative to a fixed checker calculus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given an instance \(F\), an accepted proof \(P\), and checker \(C\), initialize \(Q:=P\). Repeatedly apply a terminating sequence of transformations that may delete unreachable derived constraints, replace a derivation by a shorter admissible derivation of the same constraint, or rename identifiers consistently. After each transformation, preserve the final claimed contradiction or bound and validate all remaining dependencies. Stop when no selected transformation applies, then output \(Q\) only if
\[C(F,Q)=\mathsf{accept}.\]
Otherwise return the original accepted proof or report compression failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compression removes redundant proof material or shortens derivations, but outputs a compressed log only after the fixed checker accepts it.
assumptions_latex: \(C(F,P)=\mathsf{accept}\).
The transformation schedule terminates and preserves well-formed references.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned compressed proof \(Q\) satisfies \(C(F,Q)=\mathsf{accept}\).

children.title: Checker-Oriented Normalization
children.top_down_role: Normalization of proof records for specific checker interfaces.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact normalization of a PB inequality containing both polarities of one variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in\{0,1\}\), an inequality \(a x+b\bar x+R\ge d\) is equivalent to \((a-b)x+R\ge d-b\). Repeating this substitution and deleting zero coefficients yields at most one polarity of each variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Opposite literals of a Boolean variable can be combined exactly by substituting its complement and shifting the threshold.
assumptions_latex: a,b,d\in\mathbb Z.
Arithmetic is exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: a x+b\bar x+R\ge d\iff(a-b)x+R\ge d-b.
knowledge_statements.title: Complementary-Literal Coefficient Normalization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary on checker-acceptance preservation by normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Canonical sorting or reserialization does not establish \(C(F,P)=C(F,N(P))\) unless every algebraic rewrite preserves constraint semantics and every structural rewrite preserves command order, identifiers, references, arithmetic semantics, and rule versions wherever those features affect checking.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Canonical-looking output need not preserve proof acceptance when normalization changes references, rule versions, command order, or arithmetic semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Syntactic canonicality does not imply checker-acceptance equivalence}.
knowledge_statements.title: Semantic Normalization versus Canonical Printing

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence-preserving reduction of an integer-valued PB inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L(x)=\sum_i a_i\ell_i(x)\), where \(a_i\in\mathbb Z\), \(\ell_i(x)\in\{0,1\}\), and \(g>0\) divides every \(a_i\). Then \[L(x)\ge d\iff\sum_i(a_i/g)\ell_i(x)\ge\lceil d/g\rceil.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dividing all coefficients by a common divisor preserves an integer PB inequality when the threshold is rounded upward.
assumptions_latex: a_i,d\in\mathbb Z.
g\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\text{ and }g\mid a_i\text{ for all }i.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_i a_i\ell_i\ge d\iff\sum_i(a_i/g)\ell_i\ge\lceil d/g\rceil.

notation.meaning: Positive common divisor of the left-hand coefficients.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Common-Divisor Reduction
Checker-Oriented Normalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonicalization of PB constraints and proof commands before checking.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a PB proof artifact \(P\), parse every constraint into an exact integer-coefficient form. For each constraint, move terms to the designated side, combine coefficients of identical literals, eliminate zero coefficients, apply the specified sign convention, divide by an allowed common divisor only when the calculus validates the resulting constraint, and order terms canonically. Normalize identifiers and rule arguments without changing their references. Output \(N(P)\) only when the target checker confirms
\[C(F,P)=\mathsf{accept}\;\Longleftrightarrow\;C(F,N(P))=\mathsf{accept}\]
for artifacts in the supported language.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Checker-oriented normalization canonicalizes coefficients, literals, identifiers, and commands while preserving acceptance under the specified PB calculus.
assumptions_latex: Arithmetic is exact and normalization rules belong to the supported calculus.
\(P\) is well formed in the declared input language.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Normalization yields a canonical \(N(P)\) whose checker acceptance agrees with that of \(P\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The leaf and algorithm role fit, but the bidirectional acceptance claim is format-specific and unsupported. Division, sign conventions, identifier normalization, and canonicality require an explicit PB calculus and format source.

children.title: Compression Trust Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Trust assumptions surrounding compressed proof representations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trust boundary when compression output is checked against a different instance or command semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the intended instance, while checker \(C\) interprets instance \(\widehat F\) and rule semantics \(\widehat R\). Acceptance \(C(\widehat F,Q)=\mathsf{accept}\) certifies the intended claim only if the trusted input path establishes \(\widehat F=F\) and \(\widehat R=R\), where \(R\) is the intended sound semantics. Otherwise the parser, translator, or semantic adapter establishing that correspondence belongs to the trusted computing base.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent rechecking protects against a faulty compressor only when the checker receives the intended instance and interprets every command with the intended sound semantics.
assumptions_latex: The intended calculus \(R\) is sound for the certified claim.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C(\widehat F,Q)=\mathsf{accept}\land \widehat F=F\land \widehat R=R\Longrightarrow Q\text{ certifies the intended claim about }F.

notation.meaning: Instance actually interpreted by the checker.
Rule semantics actually implemented by the checker.

knowledge_statements.title: Instance-and-Semantics Alignment Boundary
Compression Trust Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between untrusted compression and transformations requiring independent semantic validation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) transform an accepted proof \(P\) into \(Q=T(P)\). If a trusted checker \(C\) rechecks \(Q\) from the original instance \(F\), then correctness need not rely on \(T\): acceptance is justified by \(C(F,Q)=\mathsf{accept}\). If checking resumes from an unverified cached state, accepts opaque macro steps introduced by \(T\), or checks only that \(Q\) is syntactically related to \(P\), a faulty transformation can delete a necessary premise while still passing the weakened interface. Thus the compressor leaves the trust boundary only under complete independent rechecking.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compression may remain untrusted only when the compressed proof is independently rechecked from the original instance without opaque transformations or unverified cached state.
assumptions_latex: The trusted checker is sound for every command allowed in \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Complete rechecking makes \(T\) untrusted; weakened checking places the omitted semantic obligations inside the trusted boundary.

children.title: Proof Archival Formats
children.top_down_role: Persistent formats for storing proof artifacts and associated records.

knowledge_statements.title: Proof Archival Formats
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Self-describing archival representation of PB instances, claims, proofs, and interpretation rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A PB proof archive is represented by a finite tuple
\[A=(F,G,P,S,M),\]
where \(F\) is the exact input instance, \(G\) is the claimed contradiction or objective bound, \(P\) is the proof log, \(S\) identifies the syntax and inference semantics, and \(M\) records decoding metadata. The representation is archival only if each component has a versioned, deterministic byte-level encoding and decoding reconstructs the same integers, literals, command order, and references. A conforming consumer must reject unknown mandatory fields or unsupported semantic versions rather than reinterpret them silently.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An archival format stores the exact instance, claim, proof, semantics, and decoding metadata in a deterministic, versioned representation.
assumptions_latex: All integer coefficients and identifiers admit finite exact encodings.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Decoding \(A\) uniquely determines \((F,G,P,S,M)\), or fails explicitly.

notation.meaning: Instance, certified claim, and proof log.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role fits, but the five-component tuple and mandatory deterministic, versioned behavior are proposed architectural requirements rather than a sourced PB archival format or standard.

children.title: Reproducibility Metadata
children.top_down_role: Metadata needed to reproduce certified solver results.

knowledge_statements.title: Reproducibility Metadata
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metadata sufficient to reconstruct a deterministic PB proof-checking experiment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an archived PB run, reproducibility metadata is a record
\[M=(h_F,h_P,v_S,v_C,o,e,r),\]
where \(h_F\) and \(h_P\) identify the exact instance and proof bytes, \(v_S\) identifies the proof semantics, \(v_C\) identifies the checker source or binary, \(o\) is the complete option vector, \(e\) describes the execution environment, and \(r\) records the expected verdict and diagnostics. The metadata is sufficient relative to a repository when every identifier resolves uniquely and rerunning the identified checker on those bytes reconstructs the declared checking invocation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reproducibility metadata uniquely identifies the instance, proof, semantics, checker, options, environment, and expected verdict needed to repeat checking.
assumptions_latex: Referenced artifacts remain resolvable in the designated repository.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\) uniquely determines the intended proof-checking invocation and its expected result.

notation.meaning: Content identifiers for instance and proof bytes.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed metadata tuple is plausible, but no reproducibility standard supports its completeness or the claim that it uniquely determines a repeatable invocation and expected result.

children.title: Artifact Integrity Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Mechanisms for identifying and validating archived certification artifacts.

knowledge_statements.title: Artifact Integrity Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Content-authentication contract linking archived PB artifacts to the bytes actually checked.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let an archive manifest contain pairs \((n_i,d_i)\), where \(n_i\) names a required artifact and \(d_i=H(b_i)\) is its recorded digest. An integrity interface validates supplied bytes \(b_i'\) by recomputing \(H(b_i')\), requiring equality with \(d_i\) for every mandatory artifact, and validating any authenticated manifest signature under its declared key policy. Successful validation certifies byte identity relative to the digest assumptions:
\[\forall i,\ H(b_i')=d_i.\]
It does not by itself certify PB proof soundness, semantic correctness, provenance, or freedom from malicious content.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The integrity interface certifies that checked bytes match authenticated archive digests, but it does not certify proof soundness or provenance.
assumptions_latex: The digest and signature schemes satisfy the declared security assumptions.
The manifest itself is obtained through the stated authentication policy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Successful validation establishes \(H(b_i')=d_i\) for every mandatory artifact \(i\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The digest comparison is mathematically clear, but its authentication guarantees depend on an unstated hash, signature, and key-policy model. This is primarily an integrity-validation condition or interface property, not a PB certificate.

children.title: Long-Term Checker Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Compatibility concerns for archived proofs across checker generations.

knowledge_statements.title: Long-Term Checker Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility condition for replaying archived PB proofs under later checker implementations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\) declare proof-language version \(v\), and let \(C_t\) be a checker available at a later time. Long-term compatibility holds when \(C_t\) either implements the complete semantics \(S_v\) or applies a validated translator \(T_{v\to w}\) into a supported semantics \(S_w\), with
\[\operatorname{Valid}_{S_v}(F,P,G)\;\Longleftrightarrow\;\operatorname{Valid}_{S_w}\bigl(T_{v\to w}(F,P,G)\bigr).\]
The archive must also preserve exact numeric encodings and version identifiers. Merely accepting the old syntax is insufficient if rule meanings, overflow behavior, defaults, or objective conventions have changed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A future checker is compatible only if it preserves the archived proof semantics directly or through a validated semantics-preserving translation.
assumptions_latex: The archive identifies its syntax, semantics, and numeric conventions unambiguously.
Translation failure is reported rather than repaired heuristically.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Replay preserves \(\operatorname{Valid}(F,P,G)\) across the declared semantic versions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits, but the equivalence imposed on version translation is format-specific and unsupported. A versioning specification must define validity, numeric semantics, and the translator's validation obligation.

children.title: Solver Engineering Interface Hierarchy
children.top_down_role: Implementation families affecting MaxSAT and PB solving without descending to procedural steps.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Iterative and Core-Guided MaxSAT Solving: A Survey and Assessment
top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Implementation details and empirical solver classification
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Iterative and Core-Guided MaxSAT Solving: A Survey and Assessment

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Practically Feasible Proof Logging for Pseudo-Boolean Optimization
top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: RoundingSat, Sat4j, VeriPB, and checker integration
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Practically Feasible Proof Logging for Pseudo-Boolean Optimization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Infeasibility result for an assumption-based incremental query.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a persistent database \(F\) and assumptions \(A\), a failed-assumption core is a subset \(U\subseteq A\) such that \(F\land\bigwedge U\) is infeasible. Consequently \(F\models\bigvee_{u\in U}\neg u\). Minimality of \(U\) is not required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An infeasible subset of the current assumptions certifies the call as infeasible and induces a consequence of the persistent database.
assumptions_latex: The database and assumption semantics remain fixed during the call.
The reported subset is checked against the persistent database.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: U\subseteq A\land\operatorname{UNSAT}(F\land\bigwedge U)\Rightarrow F\models\bigvee_{u\in U}\neg u.
knowledge_statements.title: Failed-Assumption Core

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Temporary CNF groups implemented through assumptions over a persistent clause database.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(G=\bigwedge_{j=1}^r C_j\), introduce a fresh selector \(s\) and permanently add \(\neg s\lor C_j\) for every \(j\). Solving under \(s\) projects to solving the previous database with \(G\); solving under \(\neg s\), or existentially leaving \(s\) unrestricted, projects to the previous database without requiring \(G\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fresh selector guards a temporary clause group: assuming it activates the group, while setting it false disables the group.
assumptions_latex: \(s\) is fresh outside its guards and query assumptions.
Every clause of \(G\) is guarded with the same polarity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Mod}(F\land s\land\bigwedge_j(\neg s\lor C_j))|_V=\operatorname{Mod}(F\land G).
knowledge_statements.title: Activation-Literal Encoding of Temporary Constraints
Assumption-Based Incrementality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incremental PB or SAT solving through temporary assumptions over a persistent base instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a persistent constraint database \(F\) and query sequence \(A_1,\ldots,A_k\), initialize one solver state with \(F\). For query \(j\), temporarily require every literal or supported PB assumption in \(A_j\), propagate and search using the persistent state, and return \(\mathsf{SAT}\) with a model satisfying \(F\land A_j\), or \(\mathsf{UNSAT}\) with a valid conflict certificate relative to \(A_j\). Afterward retract the temporary assumptions while retaining only learned information logically implied by \(F\), or information guarded so that it is active only under the assumptions that justify it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A persistent solver answers successive temporary-assumption queries while retaining only unconditional or correctly guarded learned information.
assumptions_latex: Each query assumption has a defined solver-level encoding.
Learned constraints carry sufficient dependency information for safe reuse.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each answer is correct for \(F\land A_j\), and retained unguarded information is implied by \(F\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm matches the leaf, but SAT-literal assumptions and general PB assumptions are blended without an instantiated solver interface. Safe retention of learned information also needs a source defining dependency or guarding semantics.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact feasibility-query bounds for an integer objective with finite bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the integer optimum lies in \([L,U]\cap\mathbb Z\), where \(U\) is attained. Unit-step cutoff search needs at most \(U-L\) cutoff decisions. Dichotomic search using exact queries \(f\le m\) needs at most \(\lceil\log_2(U-L+1)\rceil\) cutoff decisions, apart from any initial call used to obtain an incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unit-step tightening is linear in the objective range, while exact binary search uses logarithmically many cutoff decisions.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is integer-valued.
Every cutoff query is exact.
\(L\) is valid and \(U\) is a feasible finite upper bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{linear}}\le U-L,\qquad N_{\mathrm{binary}}\le\lceil\log_2(U-L+1)\rceil.

notation.meaning: Valid lower bound and feasible upper bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear and Dichotomic Objective-Bound Search

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinction between integer and general objective cutoffs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For incumbent value \(U\), the general improving constraint is \(f(x)<U\). It is equivalent to \(f(x)\le U-1\) only for an integer-valued objective. Without a known positive value lattice, using \(U-1\) for a real- or rational-valued objective can exclude improving solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The U-minus-one cutoff is exact for integer objectives; general objectives require a strict cutoff or a justified value gap.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) is the value of a feasible incumbent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\in\mathbb Z\Rightarrow(f<U\Longleftrightarrow f\le U-1);\quad\text{otherwise this equivalence need not hold}.
knowledge_statements.title: Strict-Improvement Cutoff Boundary
Incremental Objective Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone objective-bound updates implemented through an incremental feasibility oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a minimization problem with base constraints \(F\), integer-valued objective \(f\), and incumbent value \(U\), maintain a solver state containing \(F\). At iteration \(t\), activate an encoding of
\[f(x)\le b_t,\qquad b_t<U,\]
using an assumption literal or a monotonically added constraint. If feasible, obtain \(x_t\), set \(U:=f(x_t)\), and choose a stricter bound. If infeasible and all smaller objective values are excluded, return the incumbent as optimal. Learned information may persist only when implied by the permanent database or correctly guarded by the active bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Incremental optimization repeatedly activates stricter objective bounds, updates the incumbent on feasibility, and proves optimality when all improving values are infeasible.
assumptions_latex: The objective has a discrete ordered range and an incumbent exists.
Every activated bound is encoded exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Infeasibility of the final improving bound certifies that no feasible \(x\) has \(f(x)<U\).

notation.meaning: Incumbent value and active trial bound.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unsound Reuse after Removing a Dependency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal failure of untracked reuse after permanent-clause deletion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_0=(p)\), so \(F_0\models(p)\). After deleting the sole base clause, \(F_1=\top\) admits \(p=0\). Retaining the learned unit \((p)\) therefore removes a valid model of the new database.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Learning p from the base clause p and then deleting that clause shows that an untracked learned consequence may become unsound.
assumptions_latex: The deletion changes the intended permanent database from \((p)\) to \(\top\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F_0\models p\quad\text{but}\quad F_1\not\models p.
knowledge_statements.title: Unsound Reuse after Removing a Dependency

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistence of learned consequences when permanent constraints are only added.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(F_0\models L\) and \(F_1=F_0\land G\), then \(F_1\models L\). Under deletion, \(L\) may remain unconditional only if the remaining database entails it; otherwise its supporting dependency must remain guarded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A learned consequence survives permanent additions automatically, while removal of supporting constraints requires revalidation or dependency guards.
assumptions_latex: \(L\) is entailed by the earlier permanent database.
Added constraints retain their declared semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F_0\models L\Rightarrow F_0\land G\models L.
knowledge_statements.title: Reuse under Monotone Database Extension

assumptions_latex: The persistent base formula is \(F\), and each incremental call uses a finite set \(A\) of assumption literals.
Every retained learned clause is a logical consequence of the clauses and assumptions recorded in its derivation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A learned clause may be reused unconditionally exactly when \(F\models L\); assumption-dependent information must retain its dependency guard.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: logical consequence characterizes sound reuse across changing assumption sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound clause reuse across assumption-based incremental SAT calls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be fixed while assumption sets vary. If a learned clause \(L\) satisfies \(F\models L\), then adding \(L\) preserves satisfiability for every future call \(F\land A'\). If instead \(F\land A\models L\) is known only under \(A=\{a_1,\ldots,a_k\}\), sound reusable information is the guarded clause \(\neg a_1\lor\cdots\lor\neg a_k\lor L\), provided the derivation establishes \(F\models(\bigwedge A)\rightarrow L\). Discarding the guard without proving \(F\models L\) can change a later call's satisfiability status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unconditional reuse requires implication by the persistent formula; facts depending on temporary assumptions remain sound only with guards recording those dependencies.
knowledge_statements.title: Learned-Information Reuse

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The guarded-reuse claim is mathematically plausible and fits the property container, but no inspectable source supports the incremental-SAT dependency semantics or the unconditional-reuse characterization.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condition for translating an assumption core back to uniquely identified input constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose each selectable input constraint \(G_i\) is guarded by a distinct selector \(s_i\) through \(s_i\Rightarrow G_i\), and the extraction call assumes selectors in \(A\) true. A returned core \(U\subseteq A\) identifies \(\{G_i:s_i\in U\}\) as unsatisfiable with the unguarded base formula when selectors uniquely and exclusively activate their associated constraints. Shared, omitted, or semantically reused selectors need not identify a unique constraint core.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An assumption core maps unambiguously to input constraints only when selectors uniquely and exclusively activate those constraints.
assumptions_latex: Each selectable constraint is activated by an assumption literal.
The base formula and guarding implications preserve the intended constraint semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A unique exclusive selector mapping makes an assumption core identify a corresponding constraint core.
knowledge_statements.title: Selector-to-Constraint Core Mapping

assumptions_latex: The Boolean formula \(F\) is queried under a finite set \(A\) of assumption literals.
The solver reports that \(F\land\bigwedge_{a\in A}a\) is unsatisfiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A valid extraction result is any \(U\subseteq A\) for which \(F\land\bigwedge_{u\in U}u\) is unsatisfiable.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: assumption-core interfaces return an unsatisfiable subset of submitted assumptions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic contract for an assumption-based unsatisfiable-core interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An unsatisfiable-core extraction interface accepts \((F,A)\) and, after an unsatisfiable result, returns \(U\subseteq A\) such that \(F\land\bigwedge_{u\in U}u\) is unsatisfiable. The interface need not return an inclusion-minimal or minimum-cardinality core unless that stronger guarantee is stated separately. The result is externally checkable by submitting exactly \(U\) as assumptions and confirming unsatisfiability; membership in \(A\) checks that the reported core refers only to selectable input constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After an unsatisfiable assumption call, the interface returns a subset of submitted assumptions that remains unsatisfiable with the base formula.
knowledge_statements.title: Core Extraction Interfaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The returned unsatisfiable subset is appropriately described as a certificate-like interface result, but the record has no citation for the assumed-core interface contract or its checking guarantees.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The claim is already contained in the immutable extraction-interface seed and is therefore not republished.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Validity of \(U\subseteq A\) requires only that \(F\land\bigwedge_{u\in U}u\) be unsatisfiable; it implies neither inclusion minimality nor minimum cardinality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid extracted core may contain redundant assumptions.
assumptions_latex: \(U\subseteq A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Core validity alone implies neither inclusion minimality nor minimum cardinality.
knowledge_statements.title: Core Validity Is Not Minimality

intermediate_metadata.reason: The local inventory comprises the assumption-core extraction contract, membership and unsatisfiability rechecking, the validity-versus-minimality boundary already present in the seed, and faithful selector provenance. The duplicate minimality proposal is deferred. Core reduction quality and all grouping or clustering operations remain in sibling topics.

children.title: Core Trimming
children.top_down_role: Reduction of extracted cores without requiring full minimality.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Anytime Validity of Monotone Core Trimming
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity of every completed step of a sound shrinking process.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(C_{k+1}\subseteq C_k\) and \(F\land\bigwedge C_{k+1}\) is unsatisfiable at every accepted trimming step, every intermediate \(C_k\) is a valid core. Interruption after any completed step therefore returns a sound core. Strict accepted shrinkage can occur at most \(|C_0|-1\) times, although oracle calls can dominate runtime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every accepted trimming step leaves a valid core, and only finitely many strict cardinality reductions are possible.
assumptions_latex: \(C_0\) is a finite unsatisfiable core.
Every accepted replacement is a sound unsatisfiable subset of the current core.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C_k\text{ is a core for all }k,\qquad\#\{k:C_{k+1}\subsetneq C_k\}\le |C_0|-1.
knowledge_statements.title: Anytime Validity of Monotone Core Trimming

assumptions_latex: An initial core \(C_0\) satisfies \(F\land\bigwedge C_0\) unsatisfiable.
Each trimming call on \(C_k\) returns a core \(D_k\subseteq C_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output \(C_T\) remains unsatisfiable and satisfies \(C_T\subseteq C_0\), but need not be inclusion-minimal.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: repeated core extraction preserves unsatisfiability while monotonically shrinking the core
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterative shrinking without a minimality guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input \((F,C_0,B)\), where \(C_0\) is an unsatisfiable core and \(B\) is a call or time budget. Initialize \(k=0\). While budget remains, solve \(F\) under assumptions \(C_k\); from the unsatisfiable response obtain \(D_k\subseteq C_k\). If \(D_k\subsetneq C_k\), set \(C_{k+1}=D_k\) and continue; otherwise stop. Output the last core \(C_T\). Every iterate is unsatisfiable with \(F\), and cardinalities decrease on successful iterations, but termination caused by budget exhaustion or a nonshrinking response does not certify minimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly re-extract a smaller core within a budget. The result remains unsatisfiable but is not necessarily minimal.
knowledge_statements.title: Core Trimming

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The monotone shrinking procedure is coherent and algorithm is the correct content kind, but a domain source is required to establish that this procedure and stopping rule constitute core trimming in the intended SAT/MaxSAT sense.

children.title: Core Minimization
children.top_down_role: Core-processing families targeting irreducible conflict subsets.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle-call bound for one complete deletion pass.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Starting from a core of size \(n\), a deletion procedure that schedules every initial element for at most one test makes at most \(n\) satisfiability-oracle calls. Its bookkeeping is polynomial in the explicit core size; this does not imply polynomial total runtime because an oracle call may be intractable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A complete deletion pass makes at most one SAT call per initial core element, though the calls themselves may be expensive.
assumptions_latex: Each initial element is scheduled for at most one deletion test.
Oracle cost is measured separately from bookkeeping.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{SAT}}\le n.
knowledge_statements.title: Deletion Minimization Oracle Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinction between standard core minimization and globally smallest-core optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An unsatisfiable core \(M\subseteq C\) is inclusion-minimal when every proper subset is satisfiable with the base formula; by monotonicity it suffices to test every single-element deletion. It is minimum-cardinality when \(|M|\le |U|\) for every unsatisfiable \(U\subseteq C\). Every minimum-cardinality core is inclusion-minimal, but the converse fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deletion minimization finds an inclusion-minimal core, which need not be a smallest-cardinality core.
assumptions_latex: Unsatisfiability is monotone under adding constraints.
\(C\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{minimum-cardinality}\Rightarrow\text{inclusion-minimal},\qquad\text{not conversely}.
knowledge_statements.title: Inclusion-Minimal Versus Minimum-Cardinality Core

assumptions_latex: The finite set \(C\) is an unsatisfiable core of the base formula \(F\).
The satisfiability oracle is sound and complete for every tested subset.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The deletion procedure outputs an inclusion-minimal unsatisfiable core \(M\subseteq C\).

notation.meaning: current candidate and final minimal core

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: deletion-based minimization is the standard constructive test for inclusion-minimal unsatisfiable subsets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deletion-based inclusion minimization of an assumption core.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input \((F,C)\) with \(F\land\bigwedge C\) unsatisfiable. Set \(M=C\). Process each element \(c\) that remains in \(M\): query satisfiability of \(F\land\bigwedge(M\setminus\{c\})\). If the query is unsatisfiable, replace \(M\) by \(M\setminus\{c\}\); if it is satisfiable, retain \(c\). After every remaining element has been tested against the current set, output \(M\). Then \(F\land\bigwedge M\) is unsatisfiable, while \(F\land\bigwedge(M\setminus\{c\})\) is satisfiable for every \(c\in M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Delete each core element whenever unsatisfiability survives. A complete pass yields an inclusion-minimal, though not necessarily minimum-cardinality, core.
knowledge_statements.title: Core Minimization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The deletion procedure correctly targets inclusion-minimal rather than minimum-cardinality cores and fits an algorithm leaf, but no authoritative source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Minimality Certification
children.top_down_role: Evidence and checks associated with claimed core minimality.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Verification obligations for a finite candidate core.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(|M|=k\), inclusion minimality is checkable from one accepted UNSAT certificate for \(F\land\bigwedge M\) and \(k\) indexed SAT-witness obligations: for every \(m\in M\), an assignment \(x^{(m)}\) satisfying \(F\land\bigwedge(M\setminus\{m\})\). Witness assignments for different deletions need not be distinct. Missing any deletion witness leaves the corresponding member's necessity uncertified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A checkable package contains one whole-core UNSAT certificate and one indexed SAT-witness obligation per deletion.
assumptions_latex: The UNSAT proof format has a sound checker.
Formula evaluation under an explicit assignment is exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{UNSAT}}=1,\qquad N_{\mathrm{deletion\ obligations}}=|M|.

notation.meaning: Witness satisfying the formula after deleting \(m\).

knowledge_statements.title: Locally Checkable Inclusion-Minimality Evidence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between irreducibility and globally smallest size.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The inclusion-minimality package certifies only that no member of \(M\) can be deleted. Certifying that \(M\) has minimum cardinality \(k\) additionally requires evidence that no unsatisfiable subset of the candidate universe has cardinality below \(k\). Single-deletion SAT witnesses do not establish this global lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deletion witnesses certify irreducibility, not that no smaller unrelated core exists.
assumptions_latex: The candidate universe may contain unsatisfiable subsets not contained in \(M\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{inclusion-minimality certificate}\not\Rightarrow\text{minimum-cardinality certificate}.
knowledge_statements.title: Minimum-Cardinality Certification Is Stronger
Minimality Certification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate for inclusion minimality, not minimum cardinality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A minimality certificate for \(M\) consists of an accepted certificate or trusted complete-oracle result that \(F\land\bigwedge M\) is unsatisfiable and, for every \(m\in M\), a satisfying assignment \(x^{(m)}\) for \(F\land\bigwedge(M\setminus\{m\})\). These conditions certify that \(M\) is inclusion-minimal; they do not certify that \(M\) has minimum cardinality among all unsatisfiable subsets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certify the whole set unsatisfiable and provide a satisfying assignment for every single-element deletion. This certifies inclusion minimality, not minimum cardinality.
assumptions_latex: The candidate \(M\) is a finite subset of selectable constraints or assumption literals for the base Boolean formula \(F\).
Unsatisfiability certificates are accepted by a specified checker, or unsatisfiability is reported by a trusted sound and complete oracle.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The UNSAT evidence for \(F\land\bigwedge M\), together with SAT witnesses for every \(F\land\bigwedge(M\setminus\{m\})\), certifies inclusion minimality of \(M\).

notation.meaning: a member of the candidate core
satisfying assignment for the formula obtained by deleting m

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: inclusion minimality is characterized by unsatisfiability of the full set and satisfiability after every single deletion

children.title: Cost–Quality Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Computational tradeoffs between core reduction effort and resulting core quality.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational cost-quality comparison under a fixed reduction budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For budget \(B\), let \(\mathcal A_B=\{P:t(P)\le B\}\). Choosing \(P^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{P\in\mathcal A_B}q(P)\) is optimal only relative to the declared effort measure \(t\), quality loss \(q\), candidate family, and available performance data. Smaller output cardinality alone does not imply better downstream solving performance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under a fixed budget, optimize the declared quality measure among admissible reducers; core size is not a universal proxy for downstream benefit.
assumptions_latex: A common effort measure, budget, quality loss, and reducer family are fixed.
Every candidate satisfies the required core-validity guarantee.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}\{q(P):t(P)\le B\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Budget-Constrained Core-Quality Selection

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Qualification under which dominated core reducers may be discarded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let reducer \(P\) have effort \(t(P)\) and quality loss \(q(P)\), both minimized. If selection utility \(U(t,q)\) is nondecreasing in each argument, then componentwise dominance of \(P_2\) by \(P_1\) implies \(U(t(P_1),q(P_1))\le U(t(P_2),q(P_2))\). A strictly dominated reducer therefore cannot be uniquely preferred under such preferences. Without monotonicity or when relevant criteria are omitted, Pareto dominance is not decisive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pareto filtering is justified only when preferences worsen monotonically with effort and declared quality loss.
assumptions_latex: Compared reducers address the same input and correctness requirement.
The selection utility is componentwise nondecreasing in effort and quality loss.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (t_1\le t_2\land q_1\le q_2)\Rightarrow U(t_1,q_1)\le U(t_2,q_2).

notation.meaning: Selection utility over effort and quality loss.

knowledge_statements.title: Monotone-Preference Pareto Criterion

assumptions_latex: Each reduction procedure returns an unsatisfiable subcore of the same initial core.
Resource cost and output quality are measured by fixed functions \(t\) and \(q\), with smaller values preferred.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A procedure is nondominated exactly when no alternative has both weakly lower cost and weakly better quality, with one strict improvement.

notation.meaning: core-quality loss, such as output cardinality

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Pareto dominance formalizes the solver-cost versus core-quality tradeoff
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pareto formulation of reduction effort versus core quality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Associate each valid reduction procedure \(P\) with \((t(P),q(P))\), where \(t(P)\) may count oracle calls or runtime and \(q(P)\) may be output cardinality or another fixed loss measure. Procedure \(P_1\) dominates \(P_2\) when \(t(P_1)\le t(P_2)\) and \(q(P_1)\le q(P_2)\), with at least one strict inequality. A rational cost-quality choice lies on the nondominated frontier. Minimality requirements constrain feasible procedures; without such a requirement, additional computation has value only when it improves the selected quality measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compare reducers by solver effort and a fixed core-quality loss. Relevant choices lie on the Pareto frontier of these two measures.
knowledge_statements.title: Cost–Quality Tradeoffs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Pareto dominance is a suitable principle for the leaf, but the operational quality measure and the claim that a rational choice lies on the frontier require a source or explicit monotonic-preference assumptions.

children.title: Core Partitioning
children.top_down_role: Organization of cores into explicit disjoint or structured partitions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalence-Relation Representation of a Core Partition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical representation of a partition of indexed core occurrences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a core partition \(\mathcal P\) of \(I\), define \(i\sim_{\mathcal P}j\) exactly when \(i\) and \(j\) lie in the same block. Then \(\sim_{\mathcal P}\) is an equivalence relation whose classes are the blocks of \(\mathcal P\). Conversely, the equivalence classes of every equivalence relation on \(I\) form a unique partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Core partitions correspond exactly to equivalence relations on indexed core occurrences.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) is a finite index set of core occurrences.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{\text{partitions of }I\}\longleftrightarrow\{\text{equivalence relations on }I\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Equivalence-Relation Representation of a Core Partition
Core Partitioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-theoretic partitioning of a finite set of indexed core occurrences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I=\{1,\ldots,m\}\) index the extracted cores \((C_i)_{i\in I}\). A core partition is a family \(\mathcal P=\{P_1,\ldots,P_r\}\) of subsets of \(I\) such that \(P_j\ne\varnothing\) for every \(j\), \(P_i\cap P_j=\varnothing\) whenever \(i\ne j\), and \(\bigcup_{j=1}^{r}P_j=I\). Thus every indexed core occurrence belongs to exactly one block. A rule based on variables, weights, or provenance is additional structure and does not alter these partition axioms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A core partition assigns every indexed core occurrence to exactly one nonempty block, with distinct blocks disjoint.
assumptions_latex: The extracted cores form a finite indexed family \((C_i)_{i\in I}\) with \(I=\{1,\ldots,m\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A core partition is a family of nonempty, pairwise disjoint subsets of \(I\) whose union is \(I\).

notation.meaning: finite index set for extracted core occurrences
partition blocks on the index set

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: a partition is a disjoint exhaustive grouping of a finite ground set

children.title: Core Clustering
children.top_down_role: Grouping of cores using similarity or shared-conflict structure.

assumptions_latex: The finite core family is \(\mathcal C=\{C_1,\ldots,C_m\}\).
A symmetric dissimilarity \(d(C_i,C_j)\ge0\) and an admissible class of partitions are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A core clustering is an admissible partition minimizing a stated within-cluster loss, possibly approximately.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: clustering is specified by objects, a dissimilarity or objective, and an admissible partition class
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-based clustering of cores under a fixed dissimilarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(\mathcal C\), dissimilarity \(d\), and admissible partitions \(\Pi\), a core clustering is a partition \(\mathcal P\in\Pi\) selected to minimize an explicitly declared loss. One representative choice is \(J(\mathcal P)=\sum_{P\in\mathcal P}|P|^{-1}\sum_{C_i,C_j\in P}d(C_i,C_j)\). An exact clustering belongs to \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{\mathcal P\in\Pi}J(\mathcal P)\); an approximate clustering must state its tolerance or approximation criterion. The definition depends on \(d\), so different variable-, clause-, weight-, or provenance-based dissimilarities can yield different clusterings.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Core clustering partitions cores by minimizing a declared within-group dissimilarity objective; the result depends on the chosen similarity model.
knowledge_statements.title: Core Clustering

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The objective-based formulation is internally coherent, but it selects one particular meaning of core clustering without evidence that this is the intended local concept. The dissimilarity, admissible partitions, and approximation criterion require domain-specific sourcing.

children.title: Overlap-Aware Grouping
children.top_down_role: Grouping regimes that retain shared clauses or variables across groups.

assumptions_latex: The core family \(\mathcal C\) is finite.
A nonnegative overlap score \(s(C,D)\) and threshold \(\tau\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Threshold overlap groups are the connected components of the graph joining pairs with \(s(C,D)\ge\tau\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: connected components give a canonical partition induced by thresholded pairwise overlap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Graph representation of grouping induced by pairwise core overlap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Construct \(G_\tau=(\mathcal C,E_\tau)\), where \(\{C,D\}\in E_\tau\) exactly when \(C\ne D\) and \(s(C,D)\ge\tau\). The overlap-aware grouping induced by \((s,\tau)\) is the set of connected components of \(G_\tau\). Thus cores may share a group through a chain of substantial overlaps even when their direct overlap is below threshold. For set-valued cores, a normalized choice is \(s(C,D)=|C\cap D|/|C\cup D|\), with the convention stated for two empty sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Threshold a chosen overlap score, form the core-overlap graph, and use its connected components as groups.
knowledge_statements.title: Overlap-Aware Grouping

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The threshold-graph representation is well defined and fits a representation leaf, but connected-component grouping is a specific single-linkage choice rather than an intrinsic consequence of overlap awareness. A source must support this intended grouping rule and overlap score.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed multiple-membership interpretation of overlap-aware grouping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) index a finite core family. A proposed overlap-aware grouping is a family \(\mathcal G\) of nonempty subsets covering \(I\), without requiring disjointness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This proposal interprets overlap awareness as allowing core occurrences to belong to several groups.
assumptions_latex: The intended meaning of overlap is multiple membership of indexed core occurrences.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigcup_{G\in\mathcal G}G=I.

notation.meaning: Proposed family of possibly overlapping groups.

knowledge_statements.title: Overlapping Core Cover

intermediate_metadata.reason: The proposed new records are deferred because they silently equate overlap awareness with multiple membership, while the supplied sibling scope instead emphasizes shared clauses or variables across groups. The deferred seed also canonizes connected components without establishing the score or linkage rule. Partition semantics, general clustering policy, and temporal stability are excluded to their named siblings; the local semantic ambiguity requires deferral.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed boundary for score-threshold grouping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a symmetric score \(s\), the relation \(C R_\tau D\iff s(C,D)\ge\tau\) need not be transitive. Connected components, maximal cliques, and neighborhoods can therefore produce different groupings from the same threshold graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Thresholded pairwise overlap generally requires an additional grouping policy.
assumptions_latex: A symmetric pairwise overlap score and threshold are part of the intended grouping regime.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R_\tau\text{ need not be an equivalence relation}.
knowledge_statements.title: Pairwise-Threshold Nontransitivity Boundary

Partition semantics, general clustering policy, and temporal stability are excluded to their named siblings; the local semantic ambiguity requires deferral.

children.title: Cluster Stability Regimes
children.top_down_role: Persistence of core groupings as new conflicts are discovered.

assumptions_latex: Two core families \(\mathcal C\) and \(\mathcal C'\) are clustered into partitions \(\mathcal P\) and \(\mathcal P'\).
A block similarity \(s(P,Q)\in[0,1]\) and tolerance \(\varepsilon\in[0,1]\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The clustering is \(\varepsilon\)-stable when its blocks admit a bijective matching with similarity at least \(1-\varepsilon\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: matched-block similarity provides a checkable perturbation-stability condition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matched-cluster stability under a specified perturbation of the core family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(|\mathcal P|=|\mathcal P'|\). The pair is in an \(\varepsilon\)-stable regime when there exists a bijection \(\pi:\mathcal P\to\mathcal P'\) such that \(s(P,\pi(P))\ge1-\varepsilon\) for every \(P\in\mathcal P\). With Jaccard block similarity, \(s(P,Q)=|P\cap Q|/|P\cup Q|\). A sequence of perturbations is uniformly stable when the same bound holds for every allowed perturbation. Failure of equal cluster counts or of every admissible matching to meet the threshold places the pair outside this stability regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A clustering is stable when original and perturbed clusters can be matched bijectively, with every matched pair exceeding a fixed similarity threshold.
knowledge_statements.title: Cluster Stability Regimes
