intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The matched-block condition is checkable and condition is a plausible content kind, but it is an unsupported proposed definition. The allowed perturbations, treatment of unequal cluster counts, and intended notion of stability require a source.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient and box-sharp condition for replacing a scalar stratified objective by lexicographic minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\prod_{k=1}^K\{0,\ldots,M_k\}\) and \(F(c)=\sum_{k=1}^Ka_kc_k\), where lower indices have higher priority. If \(a_k>\sum_{\ell>k}a_\ell M_\ell\) for every \(k<K\), then the ordering induced by \(F\) on \(C\) agrees with lexicographic ordering, so their minimizer sets coincide. If this inequality fails, the equivalence is not guaranteed over the full box: lower strata can tie or outweigh a one-unit improvement at level \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scalar and lexicographic stratum optimization agree when every level outweighs the maximum possible contribution of all lower levels.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\prod_k\{0,\ldots,M_k\}\) is the attainable set of integer stratum-count vectors.
\(a_k>0\), ordered from highest to lowest priority.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a_k>\sum_{\ell>k}a_\ell M_\ell\ \forall k<K\Longrightarrow\operatorname*{argmin}_{c\in C}F(c)=\operatorname*{lexmin}_{c\in C}(c_1,\ldots,c_K)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Dominance Criterion for Lexicographic Strata

assumptions_latex: The objective is \(f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^{n}w_i x_i\), where \(x_i\in\{0,1\}\) and \(w_i\ge0\).
The distinct positive weights satisfy \(0=\lambda_0<\lambda_1<\cdots<\lambda_K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The weighted objective equals a sum of nested threshold-layer counts weighted by successive differences.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: discrete layer-cake identity exactly decomposes a nonnegative weighted Boolean objective
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact threshold-layer decomposition of a nonnegative Boolean objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each level define \(S_k=\{i:w_i\ge\lambda_k\}\) and \(\Delta_k=\lambda_k-\lambda_{k-1}\). Since \(w_i=\sum_{k:w_i\ge\lambda_k}\Delta_k\), the objective has the exact stratified representation \[f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^{n}w_i x_i=\sum_{k=1}^{K}\Delta_k\sum_{i\in S_k}x_i.\] The sets are nested, \(S_1\supseteq\cdots\supseteq S_K\). Hence processing strata in descending weight order preserves the objective only when all layer contributions and their coefficients remain represented.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any nonnegative weighted Boolean sum decomposes exactly into nested threshold layers weighted by differences between consecutive weight levels.
knowledge_statements.title: Weight Stratification

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite layer-cake identity is mathematically precise, and representation is the correct kind, but no cited source establishes this decomposition as the intended weight-stratification concept in Boolean optimization.

children.title: Weight Splitting
children.top_down_role: Objective transformations that distribute clause weights across solver structures.

assumptions_latex: A Boolean objective term has weight \(w_i\ge0\).
The split coefficients satisfy \(\alpha_{ij}\ge0\) and \(\sum_{j=1}^{r_i}\alpha_{ij}=w_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Replacing \(w_i x_i\) by linked pieces \(\sum_j\alpha_{ij}x_{ij}\) preserves every feasible objective value.

notation.meaning: Boolean copies used by the split

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: coefficient splitting is objective-equivalent when copied indicators are linked to the original indicator
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact splitting of a weighted Boolean objective term into linked pieces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(r_i\ge1\) and coefficients \(\alpha_{i1},\ldots,\alpha_{ir_i}\) with \(\alpha_{ij}\ge0\) and \(\sum_{j=1}^{r_i}\alpha_{ij}=w_i\). Introduce Boolean copies \(x_{ij}\) together with linking constraints \(x_{ij}=x_i\) for every \(j\). Then \[w_i x_i=\sum_{j=1}^{r_i}\alpha_{ij}x_{ij}\] for every feasible assignment. Applying this construction termwise preserves the objective and its optimum. If the linking constraints are omitted or weakened, the split model can admit unequal copies and need not be objective-equivalent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Split a weight into nonnegative pieces attached to Boolean copies constrained equal to the original variable; this exactly preserves the objective.
knowledge_statements.title: Weight Splitting

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The linked-copy construction is objective-equivalent, but it may be a generic reformulation rather than the intended MaxSAT weight-splitting operation under the Weight-Splitting-Hardening Coupling branch. A domain-specific source is needed before fixing the mathematical version and content role.

children.title: Clause Hardening
children.top_down_role: Regimes that promote selected weighted clauses to hard status.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hardening certificate based on a lower bound conditional on violating the candidate clause.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be the penalty over assignments satisfying \(H\), let \(\bar x\models H\land C\) have cost \(U=P(\bar x)\), and let \(B_C\) satisfy \(P(x)\geq B_C\) for every \(x\models H\land\neg C\). If \(B_C\geq U\), making \(C\) hard preserves the optimal value and leaves at least one optimum. If \(B_C>U\), every original optimum satisfies \(C\), so the complete optimizer set is preserved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certified lower bound for violating a clause can justify hardening it; strict domination preserves every optimum.
assumptions_latex: \(\bar x\models H\land C\) and \(P(\bar x)=U\).
\(B_C\leq P(x)\) for every \(x\models H\land\neg C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_C\geq U\) preserves the optimal value and an optimum; \(B_C>U\) preserves the full optimizer set.

notation.meaning: Lower bound conditional on violating C
Cost of a known incumbent satisfying C

knowledge_statements.title: Conditional-Lower-Bound Hardening Certificate

assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a satisfiable set of hard clauses and \(S=\{(C_i,w_i)\}_{i=1}^m\) has \(w_i>0\).
\(U\) is the penalty of a known assignment satisfying \(H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{OPT}(H,S)=\operatorname{OPT}(H\cup\{C_i:w_i>U\},S\setminus\{(C_i,w_i):w_i>U\})\).

notation.meaning: Optimal soft-clause penalty subject to hard clauses

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: a soft clause whose violation alone exceeds a valid incumbent penalty cannot be violated by an optimum
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient incumbent-based hardening rule for weighted partial MaxSAT.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \((C_i,w_i)\in S\) with \(w_i>U\), every optimal assignment satisfies \(C_i\). Consequently, all such clauses may be moved from the soft set to the hard set without changing the optimal penalty or the set of optimal assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any soft clause weighted above a valid incumbent penalty is satisfied by every optimum and may therefore be made hard.
knowledge_statements.title: Clause Hardening

children.title: Threshold Interaction
children.top_down_role: Interaction between split weights and hardening thresholds.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Componentwise Threshold Tests Are Not Split-Invariant
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of individual-piece testing to detect domination by the aggregate weight of one violation event.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose one penalty event of weight \(w\) is split into \(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_r\geq0\) with \(\sum_j\alpha_j=w\). The implication \(w>\Delta\Rightarrow\exists j\,\alpha_j>\Delta\) is false; for example, \(w=10\), \(\Delta=6\), and \(\alpha_1=\alpha_2=5\). Hardening after such a split must therefore compare the aggregate conditional penalty for the common event, not only individual pieces.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact splitting can hide an aggregate hardening opportunity from componentwise threshold tests.
assumptions_latex: \(w=\sum_j\alpha_j\) with \(\alpha_j\geq0\).
All pieces encode the same violation event.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(w>\Delta\not\Rightarrow\max_j\alpha_j>\Delta\).
knowledge_statements.title: Componentwise Threshold Tests Are Not Split-Invariant

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Growth of the strictly hardenable set as consistently normalized bounds tighten.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For valid bounds \(L\leq\operatorname{OPT}\leq U\), let \(\Delta=U-L\) and \(S(\Delta)=\{i:w_i>\Delta\}\). If \(L'\geq L\) and \(U'\leq U\) remain valid in the same objective normalization, then \(\Delta'=U'-L'\leq\Delta\) and \(S(\Delta)\subseteq S(\Delta')\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tightening valid bounds can only enlarge the set certified by the strict residual-weight hardening test.
assumptions_latex: \(L\leq L'\leq\operatorname{OPT}\leq U'\leq U\).
All bounds and residual weights use the same objective normalization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U'-L'\leq U-L\) and \(\{i:w_i>U-L\}\subseteq\{i:w_i>U'-L'\}\).

notation.meaning: Clauses whose residual weights strictly exceed the gap

knowledge_statements.title: Monotonicity of the Hardening Threshold

assumptions_latex: \(L\leq \operatorname{OPT}(H,S)\leq U\).
\(L\) is represented as a fixed objective offset and all remaining penalties are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(w_i>U-L\Longrightarrow C_i\text{ is satisfied by every optimum}\).

notation.meaning: Current lower and upper objective bounds

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: hardening thresholds must be applied to the residual objective after accounting for a lower-bound offset
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interaction between hardening weights and a maintained lower-bound offset.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After extracting the fixed lower-bound contribution \(L\), an assignment with objective at most \(U\) has residual penalty at most \(\Delta=U-L\). Hence a residual soft clause of weight \(w_i>\Delta\) cannot be violated by an optimum and may be hardened. The comparison must use residual weights and the residual gap in the same objective normalization; comparing a transformed weight directly with the unadjusted bound \(U\) is not generally valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With lower-bound offset L, hardening compares residual clause weights against the residual gap U-L, using one consistent objective normalization.
knowledge_statements.title: Threshold Interaction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The residual-gap condition is coherent only under the stated fixed-offset normalization and fits Threshold Interaction. No inspectable source is supplied for the MaxSAT-specific threshold rule, so the record remains source-dependent.

children.title: Objective-Preservation Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits within which splitting or hardening retains objective semantics.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient conditions for preserving value or the complete optimizer set after hardening.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a finite nonempty feasible set, let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\), and put \(X_C=\{x\in X:x\models C\}\). If \(X_C=\varnothing\), hardening destroys feasibility. Otherwise it preserves the optimal value exactly when \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}f(x)\cap X_C\neq\varnothing\), and it preserves the complete original optimizer set exactly when \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}f(x)\subseteq X_C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hardening preserves value iff some original optimum satisfies the clause, and preserves every optimizer iff all original optima satisfy it.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is finite and nonempty.
\(f:X\to\mathbb R\) is minimized and \(X_C=\{x\in X:x\models C\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X_C\neq\varnothing\Rightarrow[\min_{X_C}f=\min_Xf\iff\operatorname*{argmin}_Xf\cap X_C\neq\varnothing]\), with full-set preservation iff \(\operatorname*{argmin}_Xf\subseteq X_C\).

notation.meaning: Original feasible assignments satisfying the clause to be hardened

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Hardening-Preservation Criterion

assumptions_latex: \(L\leq\operatorname{OPT}(H,S)\leq U\) and residual penalties are nonnegative.
A transformed clause \(C_i\) has residual weight \(w_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(w_i>U-L\) is sufficient; without this strict inequality, hardening is not guaranteed to preserve all optima.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: strict domination by the admissible residual gap is the generic sufficient boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of the generic weight-versus-gap hardening guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The generic preservation guarantee holds when \(w_i>\Delta\), because every assignment violating \(C_i\) then has objective greater than \(U\). At \(w_i=\Delta\), a violating assignment can attain objective \(U\), so hardening may delete an optimal assignment even when it preserves the optimal value. For \(w_i<\Delta\), it may also increase the optimal value. Thus equality is insufficient for preservation of the complete optimal-solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strictly exceeding the residual gap preserves all optima; equality can remove tied optima, and a smaller weight can change the optimum value.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Preservation Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the leaf, and the distinction between strict inequality, equality, and smaller weights is mathematically plausible. A source supporting the claimed sharp MaxSAT boundary is absent.

children.title: Objective Reformulation
children.top_down_role: Alternative representations of weighted objectives for solver use.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are finite Boolean feasible sets with objectives \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) and \(g:Y\to\mathbb{R}\).
\(T:X\to Y\) maps feasible assignments and \(f(x)=a g(T(x))+b\) for constants \(a>0\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}f(x))\subseteq\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in T(X)}g(y)\) and \(\min_X f=a\min_{T(X)}g+b\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-affine objective reformulation on finite Boolean feasible sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A reformulation is objective preserving on the represented feasible assignments when there exist \(a>0\) and \(b\) such that \(f(x)=a g(T(x))+b\) for every \(x\in X\). The positive affine relation preserves all strict and tied objective comparisons. Therefore minimizers correspond through \(T\) on \(T(X)\), and the original optimal value is reconstructed as \(a\min_{y\in T(X)}g(y)+b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-affine relation between original and transformed costs preserves objective ordering and permits exact recovery of the original optimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective Reformulation

children.title: Objective Compression
children.top_down_role: Reduction of objective representation size or coefficient diversity.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact compression of integer coefficient magnitudes by a common divisor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\sum_i w_i p_i(x)\), where \(w_i\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\), and let \(d=\gcd\{w_i:w_i>0\}>0\). With \(\widetilde w_i=w_i/d\) and \(\widetilde f(x)=\sum_i\widetilde w_i p_i(x)\), one has \(f=d\widetilde f\) pointwise on \(X\). Thus \(\operatorname*{argmin}_X f=\operatorname*{argmin}_X\widetilde f\) and \(\min_X f=d\min_X\widetilde f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dividing nonzero integer weights by their gcd reduces coefficient magnitudes without changing minimizers.
assumptions_latex: \(f(x)=\sum_iw_ip_i(x)\) on a nonempty feasible set \(X\).
\(w_i\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\), with at least one positive weight.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_X f=\operatorname*{argmin}_X\widetilde f\) and \(\min_Xf=d\min_X\widetilde f\).

notation.meaning: Greatest common divisor of the positive weights

knowledge_statements.title: Common-Factor Weight Normalization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deletion of penalties constant on the feasible set while retaining one reconstruction offset.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m w_ip_i(x)\), define \(I_0=\{i:p_i\equiv0\text{ on }X\}\), \(I_1=\{i:p_i\equiv1\text{ on }X\}\), and \(b=\sum_{i\in I_1}w_i\). Then \(f(x)=b+\sum_{i\notin I_0\cup I_1}w_ip_i(x)\) for every \(x\in X\). The constant terms may be removed without changing minimizers, provided \(b\) is retained when source objective values are required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Identically zero penalties can be deleted, while identically one penalties can be replaced by a stored constant offset.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x)=b+\sum_{i\notin I_0\cup I_1}w_ip_i(x)\) on \(X\), with unchanged minimizers.

notation.meaning: Indices of identically zero and identically one penalties

knowledge_statements.title: Constant-Penalty Elimination

assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) is the feasible set.
Each objective term has the form \(w_i p_i(x)\), where \(w_i\geq0\) and \(p_i:X\to\{0,1\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_i w_i p_i(x)=\sum_{E\in\mathcal E}W_E p_E(x)\) for every \(x\in X\).

notation.meaning: Equivalence classes of terms having identical penalty indicators on X

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: identical Boolean penalty indicators can be merged by summing coefficients
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact compression by merging objective terms identical on the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(i\sim j\) when \(p_i(x)=p_j(x)\) for every \(x\in X\). For each equivalence class \(E\in\mathcal E\), choose its common indicator \(p_E\) and set \(W_E=\sum_{i\in E}w_i\). Replacing all terms indexed by \(E\) with the single term \(W_Ep_E(x)\) preserves the objective pointwise on \(X\), hence preserves its value and every optimal assignment while reducing the number of distinct penalty terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Objective terms with identical violation behavior on all feasible assignments may be merged by summing their weights.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective Compression

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Merging terms whose Boolean penalty indicators agree on the entire feasible set is pointwise objective preserving and fits Objective Compression. The record supplies only standard-field rationale and no inspectable source for this Boolean-optimization formulation.

children.title: Cost-Preservation Criteria
children.top_down_role: Criteria relating transformed objective costs to source-level costs.

assumptions_latex: \(T:X\to Y\) maps original feasible assignments into transformed feasible assignments.
\(R:Y\to X\) reconstructs an original feasible assignment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(R(y))=a g(y)+b\) on relevant transformed assignments, with \(a>0\), is the cost-preservation criterion.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise and positive-affine criteria for preserving Boolean objective comparisons.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Exact pointwise preservation requires \(g(T(x))=f(x)\) for every \(x\in X\). For optimization alone, the more general relation \(f(R(y))=a g(y)+b\), with \(a>0\) and constant \(b\), preserves cost order on the transformed assignments under consideration. If either the scale is nonpositive or the offset depends on the assignment, preservation of minimizers does not follow without additional structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Costs are preserved exactly by pointwise equality, or for minimization by a fixed positive scaling and fixed additive offset.
knowledge_statements.title: Cost-Preservation Criteria

knowledge_statements.scope_note: General scalar criterion preserving all comparisons on relevant transformed assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y_0\) be the relevant transformed feasible set. All pairwise weak and strict comparisons between \(g(y)\) and reconstructed costs \(f(R(y))\) are preserved exactly if and only if there is a strictly increasing function \(h\) on the attained set \(g(Y_0)\) such that \(f(R(y))=h(g(y))\) for every \(y\in Y_0\). Positive-affine recovery \(h(t)=at+b\), \(a>0\), is sufficient and numerically reconstructible but is not necessary for ordinal preservation alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Preserving every attained scalar-cost comparison is equivalent to a strictly increasing relabeling; positive-affine recovery is a stronger special case.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are scalar-valued on the relevant assignments.
\(R\) maps every assignment in \(Y_0\) to an original feasible assignment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: [\forall y,z\in Y_0:\ g(y)\le g(z)\iff f(R(y))\le f(R(z))]\iff[\exists h\text{ strictly increasing}:f\circ R=h\circ g].

notation.meaning: Strictly increasing relabeling of attained costs.

knowledge_statements.title: Order-Isomorphism Criterion on Attained Costs

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coverage condition required to transfer global optimization claims between feasible spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A cost relation stated only for reconstructed transformed assignments does not preserve the original global optimum unless transformed representatives cover all relevant original alternatives. It suffices that for every original feasible \(x\in X\) there is \(y\in Y_0\) whose reconstructed cost has the declared relation to \(f(x)\), while every \(y\in Y_0\) reconstructs feasibly. Without this coverage, a lower-cost original assignment may be absent from the transformed problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cost-order preservation on transformed assignments must be paired with representative completeness to preserve the original global optimum.
assumptions_latex: \(R(Y_0)\subseteq X\).
The declared cost relation holds on \(Y_0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{cost relation on }Y_0+\text{representative completeness}\Rightarrow\text{global optimum transfer}.
knowledge_statements.title: Representative-Completeness Requirement

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Optimizer Preservation Is Weaker Than Cost Preservation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between retaining optimizers and retaining comparisons or values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On feasible assignments \(p,q,r\), let \(f=(0,1,2)\) and \(g=(0,2,1)\). The objectives have the same unique minimizer \(p\) but reverse the order of \(q\) and \(r\). Thus equality of reconstructed optimizer sets does not imply preservation of nonoptimal cost order or recoverability of source costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Objectives may share all minimizers while disagreeing on comparisons among nonoptimal solutions.
assumptions_latex: The three assignments are feasible in both representations and reconstruction is the identity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname*{argmin}f=\operatorname*{argmin}g\not\Rightarrow\text{cost-order preservation}.
knowledge_statements.title: Optimizer Preservation Is Weaker Than Cost Preservation

children.title: Objective Reconstruction Requirements
children.top_down_role: Information required to recover source-level objective values.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fiber Criterion for Exact Objective Reconstruction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient information condition for deterministic source-cost decoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R:Y\to X\) reconstruct assignments and let \(E:Y\to Z\) contain all retained information available for cost decoding. A map \(D:Z\to\mathbb R\) satisfying \(D(E(y))=f(R(y))\) for every \(y\in Y\) exists if and only if \(E(y_1)=E(y_2)\) implies \(f(R(y_1))=f(R(y_2))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact cost decoding is possible exactly when reconstructed source cost is constant on each fiber of the retained transformed information.
assumptions_latex: \(R:Y\to X\) is the assignment-reconstruction map.
\(E:Y\to Z\) is all information exposed to the objective decoder.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists D\;\forall y,\ D(E(y))=f(R(y))\iff\forall y_1,y_2,\ E(y_1)=E(y_2)\Rightarrow f(R(y_1))=f(R(y_2))\).
knowledge_statements.title: Fiber Criterion for Exact Objective Reconstruction

assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are the original and transformed feasible sets with objectives \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) and \(g:Y\to\mathbb{R}\).
\(R:Y\to X\) is total and computable, and constants \(a>0\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}\) satisfy \(f(R(y))=a g(y)+b\) for every \(y\in Y\).
For every \(x\in X\), there exists \(y\in Y\) such that \(R(y)=x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in Y}g(y)\Longrightarrow R(y^\star)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}f(x)\), and \(\min_{x\in X}f(x)=a\min_{y\in Y}g(y)+b\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: preprocessing is optimization preserving only when transformed solutions and objective values can be mapped back
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Requirements for recovering original solutions and costs after objective transformation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A complete objective reconstruction supplies a total computable map \(R:Y\to X\), constants \(a>0\) and \(b\in\mathbb{R}\) satisfying \(f(R(y))=a g(y)+b\) for every \(y\in Y\), and a transformed representative of every \(x\in X\). Under these requirements, every transformed optimum reconstructs to an original optimum and the original optimal value is recovered by the stated positive-affine formula. Every original optimum is recoverable from a transformed optimum when it lies in the image of \(R\) restricted to \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in Y}g(y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reconstruction must recover feasible original assignments and their costs, represent every original feasible assignment, and map transformed optima to original optima; recovering every original optimum requires coverage by transformed optima.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective Reconstruction Requirements

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unit Propagation and Subsumption on Hard Clauses
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical simplifications of the hard CNF layer with reconstruction data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If hard CNF \(H\) contains unit \((\ell)\), assign \(\ell=1\), delete satisfied clauses, delete \(\neg\ell\) from remaining clauses, and record the forced assignment. If hard clauses \(C,D\) satisfy \(C\subseteq D\), deleting \(D\) preserves the hard-model set. Deriving an empty hard clause certifies hard-layer infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unit propagation applies forced hard literals, subsumption removes redundant hard clauses, and an empty hard clause certifies infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: All affected clauses belong to the hard CNF.
Forced assignments are retained for reconstruction and for evaluating affected soft clauses.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H\text{ and the simplified hard formula are equisatisfiable; subsumption preserves the complete hard-model set}.

notation.meaning: Every literal of clause C occurs in clause D.

knowledge_statements.title: Unit Propagation and Subsumption on Hard Clauses

knowledge_statements.scope_note: SAT-level elimination of a hard-CNF variable; MaxSAT use additionally requires objective-compatible reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write \(H=H_0\land\bigwedge_i(x\lor A_i)\land\bigwedge_j(\neg x\lor B_j)\). Replacing clauses mentioning \(x\) by all non-tautological resolvents \(A_i\lor B_j\) produces an equisatisfiable hard formula \(H'\), and a model of \(H'\) can be extended by a suitable value of \(x\). At most \(pq\) resolvents arise from \(p\) positive and \(q\) negative occurrences. This SAT-level fact alone does not preserve a MaxSAT objective when \(x\) affects soft clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hard-variable elimination by complete resolution preserves hard satisfiability, but MaxSAT use requires reconstruction that also preserves soft penalties.
assumptions_latex: All required non-tautological resolvents are retained unless the step is rejected.
Any occurrence of the eliminated variable in the soft objective is handled by an objective-preserving reconstruction rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{SAT}(H)\Longleftrightarrow\operatorname{SAT}(H'),\qquad |\mathcal R|\le pq.

notation.meaning: Positive and negative hard-clause occurrence counts of x.

knowledge_statements.title: Resolution-Based Hard-Variable Elimination

knowledge_statements.scope_note: SAT-level blocked-clause deletion with reverse reconstruction; MaxSAT objective compatibility remains an additional obligation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A hard clause \(C\) is blocked by \(\ell\in C\) in the current hard formula when every resolvent of \(C\) with a clause containing \(\neg\ell\) is tautological. Deleting \(C\) preserves hard satisfiability, and deleted clauses can be restored in reverse order. If the blocking variable occurs in soft clauses, this hard-level reconstruction is insufficient unless the selected extension also preserves the declared penalty relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Blocked hard clauses may be removed for satisfiability, but MaxSAT reconstruction must additionally account for the soft cost of any changed variable.
assumptions_latex: Blocking is tested in the current hard formula.
Deleted clauses and blocking literals are recorded in reverse reconstruction order.
Soft-objective effects of reconstruction are separately preserved.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{SAT}(H)\Longleftrightarrow\operatorname{SAT}(H\setminus\{C\}).
knowledge_statements.title: Blocked Hard-Clause Elimination

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equisatisfiability Is Insufficient for MaxSAT Preprocessing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between SAT-correct hard preprocessing and objective-correct MaxSAT preprocessing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Replacing hard formula \(H\) by an equisatisfiable \(H'\) is insufficient for MaxSAT correctness when reconstruction can choose original assignments with different soft penalties. Sound MaxSAT preprocessing additionally requires that transformed optima reconstruct to hard-feasible original assignments with the declared penalty relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Preserving only hard satisfiability does not preserve a MaxSAT optimum when reconstruction choices have different soft costs.
assumptions_latex: The MaxSAT instance contains a soft penalty function over original assignments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{SAT}(H)\Longleftrightarrow\operatorname{SAT}(H')\ \not\Rightarrow\ \operatorname{OPT}(H,S)=\operatorname{OPT}(H',S').

notation.meaning: Hard formula and weighted soft family.

knowledge_statements.title: Equisatisfiability Is Insufficient for MaxSAT Preprocessing

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Substitution using an equivalence entailed by the hard layer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If H\models(\ell\leftrightarrow m), replace occurrences of \ell by m in the hard formula and record a reconstruction rule for the eliminated literal. The transformed hard models correspond to projections of original hard models under that equivalence. For MaxSAT correctness, affected soft clauses must undergo the same semantic substitution or be handled by an objective-reconstruction rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hard-entailed equivalent literals may be merged, but affected soft occurrences must be transformed consistently to preserve MaxSAT costs.
assumptions_latex: H\models(\ell\leftrightarrow m).
The eliminated literal's reconstruction rule is recorded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Mod}(H')=\pi(\operatorname{Mod}(H))\quad\text{and}\quad R(\operatorname{Mod}(H'))\subseteq\operatorname{Mod}(H).

notation.meaning: Projection or substitution map from original assignments to transformed assignments.

knowledge_statements.title: Hard-Equivalent Literal Substitution

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Failed-Literal Probing on the Hard Formula
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hard-CNF probing with forced-literal reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an unassigned literal \ell, temporarily assume \ell and apply sound hard-clause propagation. If this derives the empty clause, then H\models
eg\ell; permanently assign 
eg\ell, simplify H, and record the forced value. If probing both \ell and 
eg\ell derives contradiction, H is unsatisfiable. Any forced assignment must also be applied when evaluating or transforming affected soft clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A contradictory hard-clause probe forces the opposite literal; contradictions in both directions prove hard infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: Propagation is sound for H.
Probe assumptions are rolled back unless logically forced.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H\land\ell\models\bot\Rightarrow H\models\neg\ell;\qquad(H\land\ell\models\bot)\land(H\land\neg\ell\models\bot)\Rightarrow H\models\bot.
knowledge_statements.title: Failed-Literal Probing on the Hard Formula

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Criterion for safely eliminating hard variables that occur in soft clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let y be a transformed hard model and E(y) its nonempty set of original hard-model extensions. Reconstruction is objective-correct when it returns R(y)\in\arg\min_{x\in E(y)}p(x) and the transformed objective satisfies q(y)=p(R(y))+\kappa for a fixed declared offset \kappa. Then every transformed optimum reconstructs to an original optimum. Choosing an arbitrary member of E(y) is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When eliminated variables affect soft clauses, reconstruction must choose a minimum-penalty hard extension and preserve its cost up to a fixed offset.
assumptions_latex: E(y)\ne\varnothing for every transformed hard model y.
p is the original soft-penalty function.
\kappa is independent of y.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R(y)\in\arg\min_{x\in E(y)}p(x),\ q(y)=p(R(y))+\kappa\Rightarrow R(\arg\min q)\subseteq\arg\min p.

notation.meaning: Original hard-model extensions of transformed model y.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Aware Extension Criterion

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hard-Equisatisfiable Elimination Can Change Soft Cost
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal explicit failure of arbitrary model reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let H=(x\lor y)\land(\neg x\lor y), which is equivalent to y, and let the unit-weight soft clause be (\neg x). Eliminating x from the hard layer yields H'=(y). The transformed model y=1 has two hard-model extensions: x=0 has penalty 0, whereas x=1 has penalty 1. A reconstruction rule choosing x=1 therefore returns a nonoptimal original solution although H and H' are equisatisfiable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One transformed hard model can have original extensions with different soft costs, so arbitrary reconstruction can destroy optimality.
assumptions_latex: Violation of soft clause (\neg x) costs one.
The hard-only transformed instance does not encode the extension cost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{pen}(x=0,y=1)=0<1=\operatorname{pen}(x=1,y=1).
knowledge_statements.title: Hard-Equisatisfiable Elimination Can Change Soft Cost

assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a hard CNF over variables \(V\), and \(H'\) is a preprocessed CNF over \(V'\).
There are maps \(T:\operatorname{Mod}(H)\to\operatorname{Mod}(H')\) and \(R:\operatorname{Mod}(H')\to\operatorname{Mod}(H)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H\text{ is satisfiable}\Longleftrightarrow H'\text{ is satisfiable}\), and models returned from \(H'\) reconstruct through \(R\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equisatisfiable preprocessing of the hard component with model reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Hard-clause preprocessing is reconstruction preserving when \(H\) and \(H'\) are equisatisfiable, every \(x\in\operatorname{Mod}(H)\) has an encoded model \(T(x)\in\operatorname{Mod}(H')\), and every \(y\in\operatorname{Mod}(H')\) yields \(R(y)\in\operatorname{Mod}(H)\). In a MaxSAT instance, changing only the hard component under these conditions is sound only if the soft-clause penalty of reconstructed assignments is also related to the transformed objective by the declared reconstruction rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hard preprocessing must preserve satisfiability and provide model reconstruction; MaxSAT soundness also requires compatibility with the soft objective.
knowledge_statements.title: Hard-Clause Preprocessing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated bidirectional model conditions are a plausible reconstruction-preserving preprocessing criterion, but the cited hard-versus-soft-constraints section does not inspectably support SAT preprocessing or model reconstruction. A dedicated preprocessing source is required; condition or principle may also be more exact than representation for this statement.

children.title: Soft-Clause Transformations
children.top_down_role: Preprocessing transformations acting on soft-clause structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Removal of soft clauses whose truth value is fixed by the hard formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a positive-weight soft clause \((C,w)\), if \(H\models C\), deleting it changes no hard-feasible penalty. If \(H\models\neg C\), deleting it and adding \(w\) to the global offset preserves every hard-feasible penalty. Tautological and empty soft clauses are unconditional special cases.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hard-implied soft clause is free; a hard-refuted soft clause is always violated and becomes a constant penalty offset.
assumptions_latex: The entailment test is sound for the current hard formula.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P(x)=P'(x)\text{ or }P(x)=P'(x)+w\quad\text{for every }x\models H.
knowledge_statements.title: Hard-Entailed Soft-Clause Simplification

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Converting a soft clause to a hard clause using a strict penalty comparison.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\) be the penalty of a hard-feasible assignment. If soft clause \((C,w)\) has \(w>U\), every optimum satisfies \(C\), so hardening \(C\) preserves all optima. Equality is insufficient: the two soft clauses \((x,U)\) and \((\neg x,U)\) make both assignments optimal with penalty \(U\), while hardening either clause removes one optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A soft clause heavier than a feasible total penalty may be hardened; equality is insufficient when tied optima exist.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) is the exact penalty of a hard-feasible incumbent.
All penalty contributions are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: w>U\Rightarrow\operatorname*{argmin}P\subseteq\{x:x\models C\};\qquad w=U\text{ is insufficient}.
knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent-Based Soft-Clause Hardening

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consolidation of identical weighted soft clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Copies \((C,w_1),\ldots,(C,w_k)\) may be replaced by \((C,\sum_iw_i)\), because all copies have the same violation indicator and therefore the replacement preserves every assignment's penalty exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Identical soft clauses can be merged by summing their weights without changing any assignment's cost.
assumptions_latex: The clauses have the same violation indicator under the current variable interpretation.
Weights are finite and nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_iw_i\mathbf1[x\not\models C]=\left(\sum_iw_i\right)\mathbf1[x\not\models C].
knowledge_statements.title: Duplicate Soft-Clause Merging

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weighted MaxSAT Resolution with Compensation Clauses
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Penalty-preserving structural resolution of complementary weighted soft clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((x\lor A,u)\) and \((
eg x\lor B,w)\) be weighted soft clauses and let \(m=\min\{u,w\}>0\). Replace them by \((x\lor A,u-m)\), \((
eg x\lor B,w-m)\), \((A\lor B,m)\), \((x\lor A\lor
eg B,m)\), and \((
eg x\lor
eg A\lor B,m)\), omitting zero-weight clauses and simplifying tautologies. For every assignment, the replacement penalty equals the penalty of the two premises.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted MaxSAT resolution transfers the common weight to a resolvent and compensation clauses while preserving every assignment's penalty.
assumptions_latex: \(u,w\) are finite positive weights.
\(A\) and \(B\) do not contain the displayed pivot occurrences.
Simplification preserves each remaining clause's violation indicator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
u\mathbf1[
eg(x\lor A)]+w\mathbf1[
eg(
eg x\lor B)]=\sum_{(D,q)\in S'}q\mathbf1[
eg D].

notation.meaning: Common premise weight transferred by the rule.

knowledge_statements.title: Weighted MaxSAT Resolution with Compensation Clauses

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Ordinary Clause Subsumption Is Unsafe for Soft Clauses
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of hard-clause subsumption when applied to independently weighted soft clauses without compensation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the hard formula be \(H=\{\neg x\}\) and the soft clauses be \((x,1)\) and \((x\lor y,100)\). Although \(x\) subsumes \(x\lor y\) as an ordinary clause, deleting \((x\lor y,100)\) changes the optimum set: originally \((x,y)=(0,1)\) has penalty \(1\), whereas \((0,0)\) has penalty \(101\); after deletion both hard-feasible assignments have penalty \(1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deleting a subsumed soft clause can change optimal assignments because the clause carries an independent violation penalty.
assumptions_latex: Soft-clause weights are charged upon violation.
The subsumed soft clause is deleted without compensation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\operatorname*{argmin}_{H}\!\left(\mathbf1[
eg x]+100\mathbf1[
eg(x\lor y)]ight)=\{(0,1)\}
e\{(0,0),(0,1)\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Ordinary Clause Subsumption Is Unsafe for Soft Clauses

assumptions_latex: \(H\) is the hard formula and \(S=\{(C_i,w_i)\}\) is the original weighted soft family.
\((H',S')\) is a transformed instance with a reconstruction map \(R\).
Every original feasible assignment has a transformed representative satisfying the declared penalty relation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(P(R(y))=P'(y)+b\) for every relevant \(y\models H'\) and representative completeness holds, then transformed optima reconstruct to original optima and \(\operatorname{OPT}(H,S)=\operatorname{OPT}(H',S')+b\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: soft-clause transformations are characterized by reconstructible penalty equivalence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract exact transformation rule for weighted soft clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A soft-clause transformation replaces \((H,S)\) with \((H',S')\) together with reconstruction data. It is penalty preserving when there is a constant \(b\) such that, for every transformed feasible assignment \(y\models H'\), the original penalty of \(R(y)\) satisfies \(P(R(y))=P'(y)+b\), and every original feasible assignment has a transformed representative obeying the same equality. Then transformed optima reconstruct to original optima and \(\operatorname{OPT}(H,S)=\operatorname{OPT}(H',S')+b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A soft-clause transformation is exact when reconstructed penalties differ by one fixed offset and every original feasible assignment has a transformed representative.
knowledge_statements.title: Soft-Clause Transformations

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed generic projected-cost criterion for elimination of a variable occurring in soft clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q(z)=\min\{P(0,z):H(0,z),\;P(1,z):H(1,z)\}\). A transformed instance is declared exact when its projected penalty equals \(Q(z)-b\) for every retained assignment and an attaining value of the eliminated variable can be reconstructed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proposal characterizes variable elimination through projected-cost equality and reconstruction.
assumptions_latex: The transformed representation realizes the stated projected-cost equality.
An attaining extension can be reconstructed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{OPT}(H,P)=\operatorname{OPT}(H',P')+b.

notation.meaning: minimum original penalty over hard-feasible extensions of the eliminated variable

review_flags: This is an abstract projected-cost preservation criterion rather than a concrete soft-clause transformation; its canonical home is Penalty-Preservation Criteria.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Objective-Aware Soft-Variable Elimination

intermediate_metadata.reason: This leaf locally owns concrete structural transformations of weighted soft clauses: removal of hard-fixed clauses, duplicate merging, strict hardening, and weighted MaxSAT resolution, together with their unsafe boundaries. Weight-only changes are excluded to Weight Transformations, abstract projected-cost preservation and variable-elimination criteria to Penalty-Preservation Criteria, and combined structural-weight behavior to Transformation Interaction. Ordinary subsumption is now sharply excluded; a separate positive generic subsumption rule is not core because none exists without additional equivalence or compensation assumptions already covered by the preservation sibling.

children.title: Weight Transformations
children.top_down_role: Preprocessing transformations acting on penalty weights.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact normalization of nonnegative integral soft-clause weights by their greatest common divisor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m w_i p_i(x)\), where \(w_i\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\), \(p_i(x)\in\{0,1\}\), and some \(w_i>0\). For \(g=\gcd\{w_i:w_i>0\}\), set \(w_i'=w_i/g\). Then \(c'(x)=\sum_iw_i'p_i(x)=c(x)/g\) for every assignment. Hence \(\arg\min c'=\arg\min c\), and \(z^*=gz'^*\). Division by a number that does not divide every positive weight does not preserve an integral-weight representation without an additional numeric convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dividing all integral soft weights by their positive greatest common divisor uniformly scales every cost, preserves all optimizers, and permits recovery of the original optimum by multiplication.
assumptions_latex: w_i\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}
\exists i:\ w_i>0
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: c'(x)=c(x)/g,\quad \arg\min c'=\arg\min c,\quad z^*=gz'^*.

notation.meaning: Greatest common divisor of the positive weights
Violation indicator of soft clause i

knowledge_statements.title: Common-Factor Weight Normalization

assumptions_latex: Penalty indicators \(p_i(x)\in\{0,1\}\) are evaluated on the same feasible assignment set.
All weights are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(w p(x)=\sum_{j=1}^k w_j p(x)\) exactly when \(\sum_{j=1}^k w_j=w\).

notation.meaning: Violation indicator of a soft condition

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: coefficient splitting and merging follow directly from distributivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact splitting and merging of weights attached to identical penalties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A weighted penalty term \(w p(x)\) may be split into terms \(w_1p(x),\ldots,w_kp(x)\), with \(w_j\geq0\), precisely when \(\sum_{j=1}^k w_j=w\). Conversely, terms sharing the same penalty indicator may be merged by summing their weights. These operations preserve the penalty pointwise. Merging terms whose indicators merely agree at a current assignment, rather than on the entire feasible set, has no general preservation guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weights may be split or merged exactly when the associated violation indicator is unchanged and the component weights sum to the original weight.
knowledge_statements.title: Weight Transformations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The split-and-merge identity is pointwise correct when all terms share the same penalty indicator, and representation fits the leaf. No inspectable weighted-MaxSAT source is supplied.

children.title: Penalty-Preservation Criteria
children.top_down_role: Criteria preserving the intended penalty semantics after transformation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimizer preservation without affine numerical penalty recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R:Y\to X\) map transformed feasible assignments to original feasible assignments. Suppose some \(y^*\in Y\) reconstructs to an original minimizer and, for all \(y,z\in Y\), \(P'(y)<P'(z)\) if and only if \(P(R(y))<P(R(z))\), with equality under \(P'\) implying equality of reconstructed penalties. Then every transformed minimizer reconstructs to an original minimizer. This ordinal condition need not recover numerical original penalties.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Preserving the complete ordering and ties of reconstructed penalties, together with representation of an original optimum, preserves transformed minimizers but not numerical costs.
assumptions_latex: \(R\) maps transformed feasible assignments to original feasible assignments.
At least one transformed assignment reconstructs to an original minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R(\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in Y}P'(y))\subseteq\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}P(x).
knowledge_statements.title: Order-Preservation Criterion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of replacing a fixed reconstruction offset by assignment-dependent offsets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P'(y_0)=0\), \(P'(y_1)=1\), while \(P(R(y_0))=2\) and \(P(R(y_1))=1\). Each equality has the form \(P(R(y))=P'(y)+b_y\), but the assignment-dependent offsets reverse the optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Per-assignment offsets provide no preservation guarantee because they can reverse which assignment is optimal.
assumptions_latex: Both transformed assignments and their reconstructions are feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname*{argmin}P'=\{y_0\},\qquad\operatorname*{argmin}P=\{R(y_1)\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Assignment-Dependent Offset Can Reverse Optima

assumptions_latex: \(R:Y\to X\) reconstructs original feasible assignments from transformed feasible assignments.
\(P:X\to\mathbb{R}_{\geq0}\) and \(P':Y\to\mathbb{R}_{\geq0}\) are the two penalties.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P(R(y))=aP'(y)+b\) with \(a>0\), together with representative completeness, preserves optimum penalties and minimizers.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: positive-affine penalty equivalence plus bidirectional representability preserves optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Penalty-level correctness criterion for soft-clause and weight transformations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Penalty preservation requires constants \(a>0\), \(b\) such that \(P(R(y))=aP'(y)+b\) for every relevant \(y\in Y\). It also requires representative completeness: for every \(x\in X\), some \(y\in Y\) satisfies \(R(y)=x\) or at least has the same original penalty. Under these conditions, \(\min_{x\in X}P(x)=a\min_{y\in Y}P'(y)+b\), and every transformed minimizer reconstructs to an original minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A transformation preserves penalties when reconstruction gives a fixed positive-affine cost relation and transformed assignments represent every relevant original cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Penalty-Preservation Criteria

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The positive-affine penalty relation plus representative completeness is a coherent preservation condition and matches the leaf. Its MaxSAT preprocessing interpretation lacks an inspectable source.

children.title: Transformation Interaction
children.top_down_role: Interactions between structural soft-clause changes and weight changes.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe orchestration when one preprocessing rule can enable or invalidate another.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Associate each transformation with a validity predicate on the current instance. After a rewrite changes clauses, weights, hard implications, offsets, or incumbent bounds, re-evaluate every affected predicate before applying its rule. If a single well-founded measure \(\mu\) strictly decreases on every nontrivial accepted step, repeated processing terminates at a fixpoint. Individual rule soundness alone does not guarantee termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Interacting rules must recheck affected side conditions, and fixpoint termination requires a common well-founded decreasing measure.
assumptions_latex: Dependency tracking conservatively identifies every affected predicate.
\(\mu\) is well founded and strictly decreases on every nontrivial accepted rewrite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Every applied rule is valid on its actual input, and the rewrite loop terminates}.

notation.meaning: Well-founded measure of preprocessing state I.

knowledge_statements.title: Side-Condition Revalidation and Fixpoint Processing

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-pass order dependence between merging and incumbent-based hardening.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a feasible incumbent have penalty \(U=1\), and let the soft family contain \((C,1)\) twice. Testing either copy first cannot harden it because \(1\not>U\). Merging first produces \((C,2)\), after which \(2>U\) justifies hardening. Thus the two one-pass orders yield different reduced instances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Merging duplicate weights can make a clause heavy enough to harden, so one-pass preprocessing order can matter.
assumptions_latex: \(U=1\) is the penalty of a hard-feasible incumbent.
Both copies have the same violation indicator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_{\mathrm{merge}}\circ T_{\mathrm{harden}}(I)\ne T_{\mathrm{harden}}\circ T_{\mathrm{merge}}(I).
knowledge_statements.title: Duplicate Merging Can Enable Hardening

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient condition for order-independent preprocessing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(T_1,T_2\) have disjoint write sets and fresh auxiliaries, neither changes any validity predicate or reconstruction datum used by the other, and their reconstruction updates act independently. Then both compositions are defined and yield isomorphic transformed instances with the same accumulated penalty relation, up to renaming fresh auxiliaries.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transformations commute when their effects, side conditions, and reconstruction updates are independent.
assumptions_latex: The write sets and fresh auxiliary sets are disjoint.
Each validity predicate is invariant under the other transformation.
The reconstruction updates commute on their common domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_2(T_1(I))\cong T_1(T_2(I))\quad\text{with the same reconstructed penalty relation}.

notation.meaning: Isomorphism preserving clauses, weights, offsets, and reconstruction.

knowledge_statements.title: Commutation of Independent Transformations

assumptions_latex: Transformations \(T_1\) and \(T_2\) have reconstruction maps \(R_1\) and \(R_2\).
Their penalty relations are \(P_0(R_1(y))=a_1P_1(y)+b_1\) and \(P_1(R_2(z))=a_2P_2(z)+b_2\), with \(a_1,a_2>0\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: positive-affine reconstruction invariants compose algebraically
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composition law for sequential penalty-preserving transformations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Sequential transformations remain penalty preserving when their reconstruction domains match and each individual invariant holds on every assignment passed to the preceding reconstruction. The composite reconstruction is \(R_1\circ R_2\); its scale is \(a_1a_2\), and its offset is \(a_1b_2+b_1\). Thus transformation order is interchangeable only when both orders are defined and yield the same composite feasible representation and penalty relation; individual soundness alone does not imply commutativity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Penalty-preserving transformations compose with multiplied scales and adjusted offsets, but they commute only when both composite representations and costs agree.
knowledge_statements.title: Transformation Interaction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The affine composition formula is algebraically correct, the domain qualifications are stated, and property fits Transformation Interaction. No inspectable source supports the preprocessing-composition and noncommutativity claims.

children.title: Solution Reconstruction
children.top_down_role: Recovery of source-instance assignments from preprocessed solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Solution Reconstruction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reconstructs an original MaxSAT assignment from a preprocessed-instance assignment and an ordered transformation trace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a weighted partial MaxSAT instance, let \(F'\) be obtained from \(F\) by transformations \(T_1,\ldots,T_k\), and let \(y\) satisfy every hard clause of \(F'\). Initialize \(a_k:=y\). For \(i=k,k-1,\ldots,1\), apply the recorded inverse extension rule \(E_i\) and set \(a_{i-1}:=E_i(a_i)\). Each \(E_i\) must preserve already assigned original variables and extend eliminated variables so that the clauses represented before \(T_i\) have the satisfaction status prescribed by its reconstruction record. Output \(x:=a_0\). Reconstruction succeeds exactly when every \(E_i\) is defined and \(x\) satisfies all hard clauses of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replay recorded preprocessing transformations backward, extending the reduced assignment at each step. Success yields an original-variable assignment satisfying every original hard clause.
assumptions_latex: \(F'\) is produced from \(F\) by the recorded ordered transformations \(T_1,\ldots,T_k\).
\(y\) satisfies all hard clauses of \(F'\).
Each transformation record supplies a deterministic or admissibly chosen inverse extension rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x=E_1(E_2(\cdots E_k(y)\cdots))\) is an assignment of the original variables satisfying every hard clause of \(F\).

notation.meaning: Inverse assignment-extension rule recorded for the ith transformation.
Partial reconstruction state after reversing transformations later than i.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: reverse replay of logged, solution-preserving preprocessing transformations is the standard reconstruction interface
Authoritative MaxSAT preprocessing source with explicit reconstruction semantics is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf, but the inverse-extension obligations and exact success criterion depend on the preprocessing system. No source or inspectable locator supports them.

children.title: Objective Reconstruction
children.top_down_role: Recovery of source-instance objective values from transformed costs.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compositional recovery of original cost through a sequence of preprocessing transformations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_0,F_1,\ldots,F_k\) be successive instances. Suppose reverse reconstruction gives \(a_{i-1}=E_i(a_i)\) and \(c_{F_{i-1}}(a_{i-1})=c_{F_i}(a_i)+\delta_i(a_i)\) for every \(i\). Then every reconstructible \(a_k\) satisfies \[c_{F_0}(a_0)=c_{F_k}(a_k)+\sum_{i=1}^k\delta_i(a_i).\] If every \(\delta_i\) is constant, their sum is a constant total offset; otherwise replacing the state-dependent sum by a constant is not generally valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Per-transformation objective corrections add during reverse reconstruction. State-dependent corrections must be evaluated at the corresponding reconstructed intermediate states.
assumptions_latex: a_{i-1}=E_i(a_i)\text{ is defined for every }i
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: c_{F_0}(a_0)=c_{F_k}(a_k)+\sum_{i=1}^k\delta_i(a_i).

notation.meaning: Inverse reconstruction map for transformation i
Objective correction contributed by transformation i

knowledge_statements.title: Composition of Objective Corrections
Objective Reconstruction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovers the original weighted MaxSAT objective from a reduced assignment and preprocessing metadata.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a weighted partial MaxSAT instance \(F\), define \(c_F(x)\) as the total weight of soft clauses falsified by assignment \(x\). A preprocessing trace has an objective reconstruction pair \((R,\Delta)\) when \(R\) maps each hard-feasible reduced assignment \(y\) to an original hard-feasible assignment and \(\Delta\) is a trace-recorded correction satisfying \[c_F(R(y))=c_{F'}(y)+\Delta(y).\] If all removed objective contributions are assignment-independent, then \(\Delta(y)=\delta\) is a constant offset. Consequently, the reported original objective for \(y\) is \(c_{F'}(y)+\Delta(y)\), not merely the reduced-instance cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The original cost equals the reduced assignment’s cost plus the correction recorded during preprocessing; the correction may be a constant or assignment-dependent.
assumptions_latex: \(y\) satisfies every hard clause of the reduced instance \(F'\).
The preprocessing trace records a reconstruction map \(R\) and every removed objective contribution.

notation.meaning: Total weight of original soft clauses falsified by x.
Solution reconstruction map from reduced to original assignments.
Objective correction encoded by the preprocessing trace.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: cost-preserving MaxSAT preprocessing commonly records an additive or computable objective correction
A source specifying objective reconstruction for the intended preprocessing system is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits, but the claimed constant-or-assignment-dependent correction model requires a MaxSAT preprocessing source specifying the applicable objective-reconstruction semantics.

children.title: Reconstruction Consistency
children.top_down_role: Consistency between reconstructed assignments and reconstructed costs.

knowledge_statements.title: Reconstruction Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility condition coupling reconstructed assignments with reconstructed objective values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y\) be the set of assignments satisfying all hard clauses of a reduced MaxSAT instance \(F'\), let \(R:Y\to\{0,1\}^{V(F)}\), and let \(q:Y\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}\) be the reported original objective. The solution-objective reconstruction pair \((R,q)\) is consistent precisely when, for every \(y\in Y\), \[R(y)\models F_{\mathrm{hard}}\qquad\text{and}\qquad q(y)=c_F(R(y)).\] If \(q(y)=c_{F'}(y)+\Delta(y)\), consistency therefore requires \(c_F(R(y))=c_{F'}(y)+\Delta(y)\) for every hard-feasible reduced assignment, including assignments tied at the reduced objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reconstruction pair is consistent when every feasible reduced assignment becomes a hard-feasible original assignment and its reported value equals that assignment’s actual original cost.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) and \(F'\) are the original and reduced weighted partial MaxSAT instances.
\(R\) and \(q\) are defined on every hard-feasible assignment of \(F'\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall y\in Y:\ R(y)\models F_{\mathrm{hard}}\ \land\ q(y)=c_F(R(y))\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: feasibility and exact objective agreement are the defining consistency obligations
A MaxSAT preprocessing reference formalizing both obligations is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind and formulas fit the leaf, but no cited source formalizes this universal feasibility-and-objective consistency requirement for the intended reconstruction system.

children.title: Reconstruction Failure Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Diagnostic categories for incomplete or inconsistent reconstruction records.

knowledge_statements.title: Reconstruction Failure Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Checkable witnesses localizing failure in solution or objective reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a reduced assignment \(yunderset{}{}\), a reconstruction trace, and claimed output \((x,q)\), a failure diagnostic is one of: \(D_i=(i,a_i)\), showing that inverse rule \(E_i\) is undefined on reconstruction state \(a_i\); \(D_H=C\), where \(C\) is an original hard clause falsified by \(x\); or \(D_O=(x,q,S)\), where \(S\) is the set of original soft clauses falsified by \(x\) and \(q\ne\sum_{C\in S}w_C\). Each witness is verified by replaying the indicated trace step, evaluating one hard clause, or recomputing the displayed weighted sum, respectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A diagnostic identifies an undefined inverse step, a falsified original hard clause, or a mismatch between reported cost and the weights of falsified soft clauses.
assumptions_latex: The preprocessing trace and claimed reconstructed pair \((x,q)\) are available.
Original clauses and soft-clause weights are available to the checker.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any valid \(D_i\), \(D_H\), or \(D_O\) certifies that the claimed reconstruction is not a consistent solution-objective reconstruction.

notation.meaning: Witness of failure at inverse reconstruction step i.
Witness consisting of a falsified original hard clause.
Witness of disagreement between claimed and recomputed objective.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: these witnesses directly negate the reconstruction consistency predicates
The exact diagnostic format is an interface design choice requiring system-specific documentation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind is plausible, but the diagnostic formats are system-specific and uncited. The expression "yunderset{}{}" is also malformed and fails to introduce the intended reduced assignment y.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Native PB Conflict and Literal Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Propagation by the PB component for a normalized inequality with nonnegative coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q:\sum_{i=1}^m a_i\ell_i\ge b\), where \(a_i\ge0\). Under a partial assignment \(\alpha\), let \(M_\alpha\) be the sum of coefficients whose literals are true or unassigned. If \(M_\alpha<b\), then \(Q\land\alpha\) is infeasible. If \(\ell_k\) is unassigned and \(M_\alpha-a_k<b\), then \(Q\land\alpha\models\ell_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A PB constraint conflicts when its maximum attainable value misses the threshold and forces a literal when omitting that literal would make the threshold unattainable.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\) has nonnegative coefficients and Boolean literals.
\(\alpha\) is a consistent partial assignment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M_\alpha<b\Rightarrow Q\land\alpha\text{ is infeasible};\quad M_\alpha-a_k<b\Rightarrow Q\land\alpha\models\ell_k.

notation.meaning: Maximum left-hand side attainable under the partial assignment.

knowledge_statements.title: Native PB Conflict and Literal Propagation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical contract for returning PB conflicts and propagations to the SAT component.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_{PB}\) be the active PB constraints and \(A=\{a_1,\ldots,a_k\}\). If \(F_{PB}\land\bigwedge A\) is infeasible, then \(F_{PB}\models\bigvee_i\neg a_i\). If \(F_{PB}\land\bigwedge A\models\ell\), then \(F_{PB}\models\bigvee_i\neg a_i\lor\ell\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Assumptions sufficient for a PB conflict or propagation yield an entailed SAT clause that can serve as its explanation.
assumptions_latex: The SAT and PB components share the same literal interpretation.
The explanation includes every active dependency needed for the entailment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F_{PB}\models\bigvee_i\neg a_i\quad\text{or}\quad F_{PB}\models\bigvee_i\neg a_i\lor\ell.
knowledge_statements.title: Clausal Explanations for PB Inferences
SAT–PB Integration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic interface combining clauses with pseudo-Boolean constraints over shared Boolean variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A SAT–PB instance over Boolean variables \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\) is a pair \((\mathcal C,\mathcal P)\), where \(\mathcal C\) is a CNF clause set and \(\mathcal P\) contains normalized pseudo-Boolean inequalities \(a_j^{\mathsf T}x\ge b_j\). Its feasible set is \[F=\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:x\models\mathcal C\}\cap\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:a_j^{\mathsf T}x\ge b_j\ \text{for every }j\}.\] An integrated solver may encode constraints eagerly or query a PB propagator lazily, but every propagated literal or learned clause returned to SAT must be logically implied by the active PB constraints under the current assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SAT and pseudo-Boolean components share Boolean variables; feasible assignments satisfy both, and every PB-derived propagation or learned clause must be logically valid.
assumptions_latex: All SAT and PB components use a common Boolean variable interpretation.
PB explanations are generated relative to the current SAT assumptions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The integrated feasible set is exactly the intersection of the CNF and PB feasible sets, and exchanged explanations preserve it.

notation.meaning: CNF clause set handled by the SAT component.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: SAT–PB integration uses intersection semantics and implication-valid exchanged explanations
No supplied locator directly supports the hybrid SAT–PB interface.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the integration topic, and the intersection semantics are plausible, but no source with a locator supports the PB propagation and explanation-validity interface.

children.title: PB–MIP Integration
children.top_down_role: Interfaces connecting pseudo-Boolean reasoning with mixed-integer optimization.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact binary embedding need not remain exact after integrality is relaxed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \min\{x_1+x_2:2x_1+2x_2\ge3,\ x\in\{0,1\}^2\}. Its integer optimum is 2. Replacing integrality by 0\le x\le1 admits (1,1/2) with value 3/2, which is optimal for the relaxation. Thus the direct PB–MIP embedding is exact at binary points but can have a positive LP integrality gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A direct binary-linear embedding preserves PB solutions, but its continuous relaxation can admit cheaper fractional points.
assumptions_latex: The objective is minimization.
The relaxation replaces x\in\{0,1\}^2 by 0\le x\le1.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: z_{\mathrm{IP}}=2>3/2=z_{\mathrm{LP}}.
knowledge_statements.title: Integrality-Relaxation Gap

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Checkable obligations for direct or extended integration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F be the PB feasible set and Q_I the integral feasible set of a MIP formulation in variables (x,y). Exact integration requires \operatorname{proj}_x(Q_I)=F. For optimization, define v_Q(x)=\inf\{g(x,y):(x,y)\in Q_I\}. Objective equivalence up to declared constant \kappa requires v_Q(x)=f(x)+\kappa for every x\in F. Together with exact coefficient representation, binary enforcement of original Boolean coordinates, and validated decoding, these equalities certify preservation of feasible assignments, optimal values, and optimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact PB–MIP integration requires equality of integral projections and equality of the lifted value function with the PB objective up to a declared offset.
assumptions_latex: F is the intended PB feasible set.
Q_I is the integral feasible set of the direct or extended MIP formulation.
All infima used in v_Q are attained or interpreted in the extended-real sense.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{proj}_x(Q_I)=F,\quad v_Q(x)=f(x)+\kappa\ \forall x\in F\Rightarrow\operatorname{proj}_x(\arg\min_{Q_I}g)=\arg\min_F f.

notation.meaning: Integral feasible set of the MIP formulation.
Best lifted MIP objective among extensions of x.

knowledge_statements.title: PB–MIP Embedding Exactness Test
PB–MIP Integration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact embedding of pseudo-Boolean constraints into a mixed-integer linear model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a pseudo-Boolean model contain constraints \(a_j^{\mathsf T}x\ge b_j\) over \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\) and objective \(c^{\mathsf T}x\). Its direct MIP integration declares the same variables binary and inserts the same linear inequalities and objective. Hence \[\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:a_j^{\mathsf T}x\ge b_j\ \forall j\}=\{x\in\mathbb Z^n:0\le x\le1,\ a_j^{\mathsf T}x\ge b_j\ \forall j\}.\] Auxiliary-variable reformulations are exact only when projection onto the original \(x\)-coordinates equals this set and the projected objective agrees with \(c^{\mathsf T}x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A PB model embeds directly as binary linear constraints in MIP; any extended reformulation is exact only if projection preserves feasible assignments and objective values.
assumptions_latex: All pseudo-Boolean coefficients and bounds are represented exactly.
The MIP solver enforces integrality of every original Boolean variable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The PB feasible set and the projected integral feasible set of its exact MIP integration coincide.

notation.meaning: Vector of shared Boolean or binary variables.
Coefficients and bound of pseudo-Boolean constraint j.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: pseudo-Boolean inequalities are 0–1 linear inequalities and embed directly in MIP
The supplied MIP locators do not specifically document the PB–MIP integration interface.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits. The direct 0–1 linear embedding is standard, but no cited source supports the full PB–MIP integration and exact projected-objective claims.

children.title: Cut-Callback Integration
children.top_down_role: Interfaces exposing pseudo-Boolean cuts through solver callbacks.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient finite-refinement condition for rejecting infeasible integer candidates with permanent callback cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n be finite and F\subseteq X. If every encountered \bar x\in X\setminus F causes permanent addition, throughout its validity domain, of a valid inequality excluding \bar x, then no infeasible assignment can trigger refinement twice. Hence at most |X\setminus F| distinct infeasible integer candidates are refined. Full solver termination additionally requires termination of the underlying search between callback additions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Permanent valid cuts that exclude each triggering infeasible binary assignment permit at most one refinement per infeasible assignment; overall termination still depends on the host search.
assumptions_latex: X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\text{ is finite.}
Every generated inequality is valid for F and excludes its triggering candidate.
Each inequality remains active wherever its validity assumptions hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{reject}}\le |X\setminus F|.

notation.meaning: Number of distinct infeasible candidates refined.

review_flags: Clarified that the counting result alone does not prove termination of the host branch-and-bound search.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Callback Refinement Termination

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinct callback responsibilities at integer candidates and fractional relaxation points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At an integral candidate \bar x, a lazy-constraint callback tests membership in the intended PB feasible set F and, when \bar x\notin F, adds an admissible constraint valid for F that excludes \bar x. At a fractional relaxation point \bar x, a separation callback may add a valid inequality violated by \bar x. The first variant enforces omitted feasibility constraints; the second strengthens the relaxation and cannot substitute for candidate validation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lazy callbacks reject infeasible integer candidates; separation callbacks cut fractional relaxation points and cannot replace final feasibility checks.
assumptions_latex: Each submitted inequality is valid on its declared domain.
The callback context establishes the supplied point's status.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar x\in\mathbb Z^n\setminus F\Rightarrow\text{candidate rejection};\qquad \bar x\notin\mathbb Z^n\Rightarrow\text{optional relaxation separation}.
knowledge_statements.title: Lazy-Constraint and Relaxation-Separation Variants

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Candidate Refinement Does Not Bound Host Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between callback refinement counts and end-to-end search complexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Even when at most |X\setminus F| infeasible integer candidates are permanently rejected, that count alone does not bound the number of branch-and-bound nodes, fractional separation calls, or wall-clock time. Full termination requires the host search and every invoked separation procedure to terminate under their own assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite number of integer-candidate rejections does not by itself bound fractional cuts, search nodes, or runtime.
assumptions_latex: X is finite.
No independent host-search or fractional-separation bound is assumed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{reject}}\le|X\setminus F|\not\Rightarrow\text{a bound on }N_{\mathrm{nodes}},N_{\mathrm{sep}},\text{ or }T.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Candidate Refinement Does Not Bound Host Search
Cut-Callback Integration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adds PB-derived valid inequalities through a MIP solver callback.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an exact MIP relaxation \(P\supseteq\operatorname{conv}(F)\) of the Boolean feasible set \(F\). Whenever the solver invokes a callback at point \(\bar x\in P\), query the PB separator. If it returns \((\alpha,\beta)\) satisfying \(\alpha^{\mathsf T}x\ge\beta\) for every \(x\in F\) and \(\alpha^{\mathsf T}\bar x<\beta\), submit that inequality through a callback channel permitted at the current search state; otherwise submit nothing. Continue until the MIP solver terminates. Return an incumbent only after checking its PB feasibility, and accept infeasibility only when all added inequalities were globally valid or were used solely within their valid local domains.
