knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At callback points, add violated PB-derived inequalities only after establishing validity for the relevant feasible set, and independently check the final incumbent’s PB feasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) contains the convex hull of the intended Boolean feasible set \(F\).
The PB separator supplies a validity domain for every returned inequality.
The solver documents which callback channels accept global or local cuts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No feasible point of \(F\) is removed by an admissibly submitted callback inequality.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: separation callbacks require validity and violation checks before adding a cut
Solver-specific callback semantics and an authoritative PB–MIP source are required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but admissible callback channels, local validity domains, and termination behavior are solver-dependent and lack an authoritative source and locator.

children.title: Relaxation Exchange Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Exchange of relaxation information across PB and MIP components.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of accepting globally valid inequalities into a minimization relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F\subseteq P_k and let H_k be a halfspace containing F. With P_{k+1}=P_k\cap H_k, one has F\subseteq P_{k+1}\subseteq P_k. Therefore, for minimization, L_k=\inf_{x\in P_k}c^{\mathsf T}x satisfies L_k\le L_{k+1}\le z^*=\inf_{x\in F}c^{\mathsf T}x. Equality L_{k+1}=L_k may hold when the new inequality is redundant or leaves a relaxation optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accepting a valid inequality preserves feasible points and cannot weaken a minimization lower bound, though it need not improve the bound strictly.
assumptions_latex: F\subseteq P_k.
F\subseteq H_k.
The objective is the same minimization objective on F and P_k.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\subseteq P_{k+1}\subseteq P_k\quad\text{and}\quad L_k\le L_{k+1}\le z^*.

notation.meaning: Receiver relaxation after k accepted inequalities.
Halfspace supplied by exchanged inequality k.
Optimal value over the common feasible set.

knowledge_statements.title: Monotone Relaxation Tightening

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separate validation and application rules for canonical exchange classes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under a verified semantic coordinate map \phi between compatible models: (1) import a cut only on a receiver domain contained in its certified validity domain; (2) import a minimization lower bound only for the same objective and a contained scope, combining compatible bounds by maximum; (3) import an incumbent only with a complete feasible witness, combining values by minimum; and (4) import a variable bound only when its justification is valid on the receiver scope, intersecting the receiver domain after applying \phi. Reject messages with unknown model, objective, scope, version, or coordinate semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cuts, lower bounds, incumbents, and variable bounds have distinct admission rules and all require verified model, scope, version, objective, and coordinate metadata.
assumptions_latex: \phi preserves the semantics of every exchanged coordinate.
The sender attaches artifact type and validity metadata.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Every admitted message preserves the feasible set or a valid primal or lower bound, according to type.}

notation.meaning: Verified semantic coordinate map between PB and MIP representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Typed Relaxation-Message Admission

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of finite convergence under infinitely many valid exchanges.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F=\{1\}\subset\mathbb R and P_k=[1-1/k,1] for k\ge1. Each update satisfies F\subseteq P_{k+1}\subseteq P_k. For objective \min x, the relaxation bounds L_k=1-1/k increase to z^*=1, but L_k<z^* for every finite k.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An infinite sequence of valid nested relaxations can converge to the exact bound without attaining it at any finite exchange.

Relaxation Exchange Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound exchange of relaxation constraints and bounds between PB and MIP components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) be the common feasible set, and let \(P_{\mathrm{PB}}\) and \(P_{\mathrm{MIP}}\) be relaxations containing \(F\). A relaxation exchange interface accepts from either component only inequalities \(h(x)\ge0\) valid for every \(x\in F\), then intersects the receiver's relaxation with their halfspaces. For minimization, a transmitted lower bound \(L\) is admissible only if \(L\le\min_{x\in F}c^{\mathsf T}x\); a transmitted incumbent value \(U\) is admissible only with a feasible witness \(x^I\in F\) satisfying \(U=c^{\mathsf T}x^I\). Thus exchanged information can tighten relaxations without changing \(F\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correctness conditions for transformed models and restricted callback contexts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A deduction expressed in original variables may be submitted to a transformed model only through a verified translation that preserves its truth on corresponding feasible points. A callback may perform only operations admitted in its invocation context, and mutable shared callback data require synchronization or immutable snapshots. Missing semantic translation, a forbidden operation, reentrant mutation, or a data race invalidates any correctness inference based solely on the original expression.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes globally valid callback deductions from node-local deductions requiring contextual enforcement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the global feasible set and \(F_N=F\cap D_N\) the feasible set under branch-and-bound node domain \(D_N\). An inequality \(a^{\mathsf T}x\ge b\) may be installed globally only if it holds for every \(x\in F\). If it is known only for every \(x\in F_N\), it may be used solely at node \(N\) and its descendants while \(D_N\) remains active. Promoting such a local inequality globally can delete a feasible point \(x^*\in F\setminus D_N\) with \(a^{\mathsf T}x^*<b\), invalidating feasibility, optimality, or infeasibility conclusions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Global callbacks require globally valid deductions. A cut valid only under a node’s branching assumptions must remain local, or it may remove legitimate solutions elsewhere.
assumptions_latex: The solver distinguishes global and node-local callback channels.
The validity domain of each generated inequality is known.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Local validity on \(F_N\) does not imply global validity on \(F\); global promotion is unsound whenever a violating \(x^*\in F\setminus D_N\) exists.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Parallel Integration Has No Unconditional Speedup Guarantee

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(p\) deterministic workers that execute the same effective search trajectory and exchange no information that changes pruning, branching, or termination. Hence parallel integration alone guarantees neither speedup nor reduced aggregate work.

Shared-State Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Typed shared state for sound communication among parallel Boolean-optimization workers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a common minimization instance with feasible set \(F\), a shared-state interface is a tuple \(\Sigma=(\mathcal L,L,x^*,U)\). Here every learned constraint \(C\in\mathcal L\) is globally valid on \(F\); \(L\) is a certified global lower bound satisfying \(L\le\min_{x\in F}f(x)\); and either \((x^*,U)=\bot\) or \(x^*\in F\) with \(U=f(x^*)\). knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eventual-consistency condition for finitely many monotone asynchronous updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose finitely many updates u_k are published, every update reaches every nonterminated worker after finite delay, and workers merge updates using an associative, commutative, idempotent join \sqcup. Then every nonterminated worker eventually holds S^*=\bigsqcup_k u_k. Without eventual delivery, convergence to the same joined state is not guaranteed.

Every update is delivered to every nonterminated worker after finite delay.
\sqcup\text{ is associative, commutative, and idempotent.}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In synchronous round r with worker computation times t_{ir}, the barrier cannot release before \max_i t_{ir}; excluding communication overhead, aggregate idle waiting is W_r=\sum_i(\max_j t_{jr}-t_{ir}). An asynchronous regime removes mandatory barrier waiting but incurs messaging, contention, and stale-information costs. Without bounded delivery delay or another freshness assumption, no finite staleness bound follows.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A barrier inherits the slowest worker's round time; asynchronous exchange removes mandatory barriers but has no finite staleness guarantee without delivery assumptions.
assumptions_latex: Round boundaries are well defined for the synchronous calculation.
The waiting identity excludes communication and barrier-processing overhead.

Local idleness, an empty local queue, or a temporarily unchanged incumbent is insufficient. knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract synchronization semantics for parallel Boolean-optimization workers sharing deductions and feasible incumbents.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p\ge 1\) workers solving a common minimization instance have local states \(S_1,\ldots,S_p\), a shared set \(K_t\) of valid deductions, and a shared incumbent value \(U_t\), where every finite \(U_t\) is the objective value of a feasible assignment. A synchronous regime partitions execution into rounds: every worker completes round \(r\), exchanges selected deductions and feasible incumbents at a barrier, and starts round \(r+1\) using the resulting shared information. An asynchronous regime permits workers to publish or consume such information without a global barrier. Either regime preserves validity of the shared information when every imported deduction is valid for the common instance, \(K_{t+1}\supseteq K_t\), and each incumbent update is \(U_{t+1}=\min\{U_t,f(x_{t+1})\}\) for some feasible assignment \(x_{t+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Synchronous workers exchange deductions and feasible incumbents at barriers, whereas asynchronous workers exchange them independently. Valid deductions may be accumulated, and the incumbent may decrease only to the objective value of another feasible assignment.

children.title: Weighted-CNF Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Syntax and metadata interfaces for weighted conjunctive-normal-form instances.

knowledge_statements.title: Weighted-CNF Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mathematical interchange representation for weighted partial CNF under minimization semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A weighted-CNF interface represents an instance by \(I=(V,H,S)\), where \(V\) is a finite Boolean-variable set, \(H\) is a finite set of hard clauses over \(V\), and \(S=((C_i,w_i))_{i=1}^m\) is a list of soft clauses with \(w_i\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}\). Its feasible assignments and objective are
\[X_I=\{x\in\{0,1\}^{V}:x\models C\text{ for every }C\in H\},\qquad f_I(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m w_i\mathbf{1}[x\not\models C_i].\]
The interface denotes \(\min_{x\in X_I}f_I(x)\); repeated soft clauses contribute separately unless the format explicitly aggregates them.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted CNF consists of mandatory hard clauses and weighted soft clauses. A feasible assignment satisfies every hard clause and minimizes the total weight of violated soft clauses.
assumptions_latex: \(V\), \(H\), and \(S\) are finite.
All soft-clause weights are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The serialized instance denotes \(\min_{x\in X_I}f_I(x)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation matches weighted partial MaxSAT semantics and fits the terminal container. However, no citation is supplied, and the use of arbitrary nonnegative real weights and the repeated-clause convention may not match a concrete weighted-CNF interchange standard, which commonly imposes format-specific numeric domains.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The claim is sound, but its hard-sentinel translation boundary is canonically owned by Format Translation Boundaries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let ordinary soft weights be nonnegative with total \(W\), and give every intended hard clause weight \(T\). If the intended hard clauses are jointly satisfiable and \(T>W\), every optimum satisfies every intended hard clause.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A numeric top weight emulates hard clauses when it exceeds the total ordinary soft weight and the intended hard clauses are feasible.
assumptions_latex: Ordinary soft weights are nonnegative and sum to \(W\).
The intended hard clauses are jointly satisfiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every optimum satisfies all clauses assigned weight \(T\).
knowledge_statements.title: Top-Weight Hard-Clause Equivalence

intermediate_metadata.reason: Weighted-CNF mathematical semantics are locally owned, but the topic remains incomplete without a versioned grammar, metadata contract, and numeric domain. children.title: MaxSAT Instance Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Instance-level interfaces carrying MaxSAT hard-clause and soft-clause semantics.

knowledge_statements.title: MaxSAT Instance Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic contract exposed by an interface for partial weighted MaxSAT instances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A MaxSAT instance interface exposes a finite variable set \(V\), clauses \(C_1,
\ldots,C_m\), hardness indicators \(h_i\in\{0,1\}\), and weights \(w_i\ge 0\) for indices with \(h_i=0\). For an assignment \(x\in\{0,1\}^{V}\), the interface returns feasible exactly when \(x\models C_i\) for every \(i\) with \(h_i=1\), and then returns
\[f(x)=\sum_{i:h_i=0}w_i\mathbf{1}[x\not\models C_i].\]
A solver result is semantically complete when it reports infeasibility or returns a feasible \(x^*\) together with \(f(x^*)=\min\{f(x):x\text{ is feasible}\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The interface identifies variables, hard and soft clauses, and soft weights. It evaluates feasibility and violated weight, while a complete solver result reports infeasibility or an optimum.
assumptions_latex: The clause and variable collections are finite.
Weights of soft clauses are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The interface defines feasibility, objective evaluation, and the meaning of an optimal MaxSAT result.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The feasibility and objective formulas are coherent and representation is a suitable kind. A source is needed to establish the claimed interface contract, including whether an interface must expose hardness indicators and whether semantic completeness includes the stated optimal-result behavior.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed objective equivalence is mathematically sound but canonically owned by the existing Preference Semantics topic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For hard-feasible \(x\), if \(W=\sum_iw_i\), \(S(x)=\sum_iw_i\mathbf 1[x\models C_i]\), and \(U(x)=\sum_iw_i\mathbf 1[x\not\models C_i]\), then \(S(x)+U(x)=W\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Satisfied and violated soft weight sum to the fixed total weight.
assumptions_latex: The soft family is finite.
Each soft occurrence has one fixed weight.
Optimization is restricted to hard-feasible assignments.
knowledge_statements.title: Constant-Total Weight Identity

intermediate_metadata.reason: The local inventory is the MaxSAT instance contract: variables, hard and soft clause roles, weights, hard feasibility, violated-weight evaluation, and complete-result meaning. The proposed constant-total identity is deferred as duplication of Preference Semantics. Serialization and translation failures remain in sibling leaves; search and proof artifacts are excluded.

children.title: Format Translation Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Semantic limits arising when translating between weighted-CNF variants.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted-CNF translation guarantee that preserves optimizers while allowing a declared objective scale and offset.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose relations between source- and target-feasible assignments cover both feasible sets, preserve the represented source decision under projection, and every related pair \((x,y)\) satisfies \[f_{T(I)}(y)=\alpha f_I(x)+\beta\] for fixed \(\alpha>0\) and \(\beta\). Then corresponding optimizer sets are preserved and \[\operatorname{opt}(T(I))=\alpha\operatorname{opt}(I)+\beta.\] Numerical optimum values are preserved exactly only when \(\alpha=1\) and \(\beta=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed positive affine transformation of every corresponding cost preserves optimizers, while changing the reported optimum by the same scale and offset.
assumptions_latex: The correspondence covers feasible assignments on both sides and preserves represented source decisions.
The same \(\alpha,\beta\) apply to every corresponding pair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Corresponding optimizer sets are preserved and \(\operatorname{opt}(T(I))=\alpha\operatorname{opt}(I)+\beta\).
knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Affine Cost Preservation

assumptions_latex: \(I\) and \(T(I)\) use minimization by violated soft weight.
The correspondence maps cover every feasible assignment on both sides, including prescribed values of auxiliary variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Under the two-sided feasibility and cost correspondence, \(\operatorname{opt}(I)=\operatorname{opt}(T(I))\); a format or correspondence failure removes that guarantee.

notation.meaning: map from source-feasible to target-feasible assignments
map from target-feasible to source-feasible assignments

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which weighted-CNF interchange preserves MaxSAT feasibility and objective values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) translate a MaxSAT instance \(I\), with feasible set \(X_I\) and objective \(f_I\), to a weighted-CNF artifact with feasible set \(X_{T(I)}\) and objective \(f_{T(I)}\). Exact feasibility-and-cost preservation is guaranteed when maps \(\pi:X_I\to X_{T(I)}\) and \(\rho:X_{T(I)}\to X_I\) satisfy \(f_{T(I)}(\pi(x))=f_I(x)\) for every \(x\in X_I\) and \(f_I(\rho(y))=f_{T(I)}(y)\) for every \(y\in X_{T(I)}\). This guarantee can fail when a source weight is not representable, arithmetic overflows, a hard-clause sentinel is not greater than every attainable soft cost, or auxiliary variables permit target-feasible assignments without a cost-preserving source counterpart. After such a failure, feasibility or optimum values need not be preserved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact translation must cover feasible assignments in both directions while preserving their costs. Unrepresentable weights, overflow, an invalid hard-clause sentinel, or target assignments created by inadequately constrained auxiliaries can invalidate the equivalence.
knowledge_statements.title: Format Translation Boundaries

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic normalization applicable to OPB-style constraints independently of surface grammar.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For Boolean \(x_j\), \(a_j(1-x_j)=a_j-a_jx_j\). Consequently, \[\sum_{j\in P}a_jx_j+\sum_{j\in N}a_j(1-x_j)\ \bowtie\ b\] is equivalent to \[\sum_{j\in P}a_jx_j-\sum_{j\in N}a_jx_j\ \bowtie\ b-\sum_{j\in N}a_j.\] The same identity applies to an objective, with its constant offset retained when objective values are reported.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complemented Boolean literals can be eliminated exactly by negating their variable coefficients and shifting the right-hand side or objective constant.
assumptions_latex: Arithmetic is exact and every normalized coefficient is representable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The original and normalized expressions have identical values on every Boolean assignment.

notation.meaning: indices of positive and complemented literals

knowledge_statements.title: Complemented-Literal Normalization
OPB Pseudo-Boolean Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Core mathematical semantics of an OPB-style pseudo-Boolean optimization artifact.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An OPB pseudo-Boolean interface represents binary variables \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\), an optional linear objective \(c_0+\sum_{j=1}^n c_jx_j\), and finitely many constraints
\[\sum_{j=1}^n a_{ij}\ell_{ij}\ \bowtie_i\ b_i,\qquad \bowtie_i\in\{\le,=,\ge\},\]
where each literal \(\ell_{ij}\) is \(x_j\) or \(1-x_j\), and coefficients and right-hand sides belong to the format's supported integer domain. The represented problem minimizes the objective over assignments satisfying every constraint. If no objective is present, the artifact represents a feasibility problem rather than assigning an implicit optimization criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An OPB artifact encodes binary linear inequalities or equalities and an optional linear objective. Without an objective it denotes feasibility; otherwise it denotes minimization over feasible assignments.
assumptions_latex: Variables are Boolean.
All numbers lie in the integer domain accepted by the selected OPB version.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The artifact denotes either pseudo-Boolean feasibility or linear pseudo-Boolean minimization.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record fits the OPB representation leaf, but its accepted comparison operators, literal syntax, coefficient domain, and optional-objective semantics depend on the OPB version. No versioned grammar or specification with an inspectable locator is cited.

children.title: Model Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Interfaces for emitting feasible assignments or reconstructed models.

knowledge_statements.title: Model Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interface contract for checking a reported Boolean model and its objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an optimization instance \(I\) with feasible set \(X_I\) and objective \(f_I\), a model-interface artifact is a total assignment \(x:V_I\to\{0,1\}\), optionally accompanied by a claimed value \(v\). The checker accepts the artifact as a feasible-model certificate exactly when \(x\in X_I\). If \(v\) is present, consistency additionally requires \(v=f_I(x)\), computed from the original instance rather than trusted from the artifact. Such acceptance certifies feasibility and an attained value, but does not by itself certify optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A model artifact supplies a complete Boolean assignment and possibly its value. Rechecking the original instance certifies feasibility and attained cost, but not optimality alone.
assumptions_latex: The artifact and instance use the same variable identifiers and truth-value convention.
The checker evaluates constraints and objective from the original instance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Acceptance certifies \(x\in X_I\) and, when supplied, \(v=f_I(x)\), but not \(v=\min_{y\in X_I}f_I(y)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Certificate is an appropriate role because the statement concerns a checked model artifact rather than merely its serialization. The mathematical distinction between feasibility/value certification and optimality is precise, but the asserted interface contract has no supporting source.

children.title: Bound Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Interfaces for reporting objective bounds and optimal values.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combination of multiple global bounds for one interpreted minimization instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z^*\) be the finite optimum of a minimization instance. If every \(L_i\) is a valid global lower bound and every \(U_j\) is a valid global upper bound for the same interpreted instance, then \[\max_i L_i\le z^*\le\min_j U_j.\] These are the strongest bounds obtainable by selecting among the supplied values. Bounds referring to different instances, assumptions, numeric conventions, or subproblem scopes cannot generally be aggregated this way.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For one minimization instance, aggregate valid global lower bounds by maximum and valid global upper bounds by minimum. Incompatible or local bounds cannot be combined as global bounds.
assumptions_latex: \forall i:\ L_i\le z^*
\forall j:\ z^*\le U_j
All bounds use the same instance, objective convention, numeric interpretation, and global scope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \max_iL_i\le z^*\le\min_jU_j.
knowledge_statements.title: Sound Aggregation of Bound Artifacts

assumptions_latex: \(X_I\ne\varnothing\) and \(z^*\) is finite.
The bound direction and numeric representation are explicit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Valid bounds satisfy \(L\le z^*\le U\), and \(L=U\) certifies the optimal value.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direction-aware contract for objective bounds in Boolean minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization instance \(I\) with nonempty feasible set \(X_I\) and finite optimum \(z^*=\min_{x\in X_I}f_I(x)\), a bound-interface artifact declares a value \(b\) and a direction. A lower-bound artifact is valid exactly when \(b\le z^*\); an upper-bound artifact is valid exactly when \(b\ge z^*\). A model \(x\in X_I\) with \(f_I(x)=b\) directly verifies an upper bound. A lower bound requires a sound derivation or proof artifact. Matching valid bounds \(L=U\) certify \(z^*=L\); neither bound alone generally certifies optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For minimization, lower bounds do not exceed the optimum and upper bounds do not fall below it. Equal valid bounds certify the optimum; feasible models directly support upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Bound Interfaces

children.title: Proof Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Interfaces for emitting machine-checkable certification artifacts.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Relative Completeness of a Proof Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Completeness relative to the interface's declared claim language and proof calculus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal Q_I\) be the declared claims about instance \(I\). The interface is complete for \(\mathcal Q_I\) exactly when \[\forall Q\in\mathcal Q_I,\quad Q\text{ true}\Longrightarrow\exists P\;\operatorname{Check}(I,Q,P)=\operatorname{accept}.\] This property is logically independent of checker soundness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proof interface is complete for a declared claim class when every true claim in that class has an accepted artifact. Completeness is distinct from soundness.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal Q_I\) is the claim class declared by the interface.
Artifacts and claims use fixed calculus and numeric conventions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall Q\in\mathcal Q_I,\;Q\text{ true}\Rightarrow\exists P\;\operatorname{Check}(I,Q,P)=\operatorname{accept}.\)

notation.meaning: declared claim class for instance I

knowledge_statements.title: Relative Completeness of a Proof Interface

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical limits of rejection and portability of acceptance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a sound checker, \[\operatorname{Check}(I,Q,P)=\operatorname{reject}\not\Longrightarrow\neg Q.\] Acceptance under checker version \(v\) transfers to version \(v'\) only when both versions give the same relevant semantics to the instance, claim, artifact, arithmetic, and inference rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rejecting an artifact does not refute its claim. Acceptance is version-bound unless all relevant checker semantics remain compatible.
assumptions_latex: The checker is sound for its declared semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Rejection does not certify \(\neg Q\), and semantically incompatible checker versions cannot inherit an acceptance result.
knowledge_statements.title: Rejection and Checker-Version Boundary

assumptions_latex: The checker terminates on the supplied finite artifact.
The checker's acceptance rule is sound for its declared proof calculus.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\operatorname{Check}(I,Q,P)=\operatorname{accept}\), then \(Q\) holds for \(I\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract checker contract for infeasibility and lower-bound proof artifacts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix an instance \(I\), a claim \(Q\), and a deterministic checker \(\operatorname{Check}\). Under a sound acceptance rule, a proof-interface artifact \(P\) certifies \(Q\) when \(\operatorname{Check}(I,Q,P)=\operatorname{accept}\), because soundness requires \(\operatorname{Check}(I,Q,P)=\operatorname{accept}\Longrightarrow Q\). Typical claims are that \(I\) is infeasible or that its minimization optimum satisfies \(z^*\ge L\). The interface must bind \(P\) to the exact instance, claim, proof calculus, and numeric conventions. Acceptance certifies only the claim interpreted under those declared conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proof artifact is meaningful relative to an exact instance, claim, calculus, and checker. Under checker soundness, acceptance certifies the bound, infeasibility statement, or other declared claim.
knowledge_statements.title: Proof Interfaces

children.title: Cross-Artifact Consistency
children.top_down_role: Consistency requirements linking models, reported bounds, and proofs.

assumptions_latex: The proof checker is sound.
All artifacts use a common exact numeric interpretation.
The feasible set \(X_I\) is nonempty and \(z^*=\min_{y\in X_I}f_I(y)\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Cross-consistency gives \(L\le z^*\le U\); if \(L=U\), then \(x\) is optimal.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint consistency predicate for model, bound, and proof artifacts of one minimization instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) be a minimization instance with feasible set \(X_I\), objective \(f_I\), and finite optimum \(z^*=\min_{y\in X_I}f_I(y)\). Let \(x\) be a model artifact, \(U\) its claimed value, \(L\) a lower-bound claim, and \(P\) a proof artifact for that claim. The artifacts are cross-consistent exactly when they identify the same canonical instance and conventions and satisfy \[x\in X_I,\qquad U=f_I(x),\qquad \operatorname{Check}(I,z^*\ge L,P)=\operatorname{accept},\qquad L\le U.\] If the checker is sound and \(L=U\), the artifacts jointly certify that \(x\) is optimal and \(z^*=L=U\). A mismatch of instance identity, objective convention, or numeric interpretation invalidates the joint certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Model, bound, and proof artifacts must reference the same interpreted instance. A feasible model establishes the upper bound, a soundly checked proof establishes the lower bound, and equality certifies optimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Artifact Consistency

children.title: Configuration Preference Models with Soft Clauses

knowledge_statements.title: Configuration Feasibility Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hard-clause feasibility semantics for Boolean configuration models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(V\) be a finite set of Boolean configuration decisions and \(H\) a finite family of hard clauses encoding mandatory dependencies, exclusions, cardinalities, and environmental requirements. The configuration-feasibility structure is
\[X_H=\{x\in\{0,1\}^{V}:x\models C	ext{ for every }C\in H\}.\]
A configuration is admissible exactly when it lies in \(X_H\). Soft preference clauses do not alter \(X_H\); they rank its members. Thus the configuration model is feasible exactly when \(X_H\ne\varnothing\), independently of the weights attached to soft preferences.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hard clauses define the admissible configurations. Soft preferences rank admissible configurations but cannot make an assignment feasible or infeasible.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) and \(H\) are finite.
Every mandatory configuration rule is represented in \(H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasibility is precisely membership in \(X_H\), and the model is feasible exactly when \(X_H\ne\varnothing\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition precisely separates hard-clause feasibility from soft-clause ranking and fits the configuration-feasibility leaf. No source supports the configuration-to-MaxSAT modeling claim or its stated scope.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Additive Weights Do Not Express Preference Interactions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expressiveness boundary of independent weighted soft clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An objective \(F(x)=\sum_i w_i\mathbf1[x\not\models P_i]\) assigns each joint violation set the sum of fixed per-preference costs. It cannot represent an interaction surcharge or discount \(\gamma\ne0\) applying only when \(P_i\) and \(P_j\) are both violated unless an additional clause or auxiliary representation encodes that interaction. In particular, desired costs \(0,w_i,w_j,w_i+w_j+\gamma\) for violating neither, only \(i\), only \(j\), or both cannot be produced by the two original additive weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent weights cannot express a special cost for jointly violating preferences; the interaction must be encoded explicitly.
assumptions_latex: Only the two original violation indicators and fixed additive weights are used.
\(\gamma\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nexists\alpha_i,\alpha_j:\ (0,\alpha_i,\alpha_j,\alpha_i+\alpha_j)=(0,w_i,w_j,w_i+w_j+\gamma).\)
knowledge_statements.title: Additive Weights Do Not Express Preference Interactions

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonic ordering induced by nonnegative additive preference penalties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For feasible \(x\), let \(V(x)=\{i:x\not\models P_i\}\). With \(F(x)=\sum_{i\in V(x)}w_i\) and \(w_i\ge0\), \(V(x)\subseteq V(y)\) implies \(F(x)\le F(y)\). If the inclusion is proper and some preference in \(V(y)\setminus V(x)\) has positive weight, then \(F(x)<F(y)\). Consequently, if every weight is positive, every optimum has an inclusion-minimal violation set; zero weights can admit nonminimal optimal violation sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Violating a subset of another configuration's preferences cannot cost more; with positive weights, every optimum has a minimal violation set.
assumptions_latex: Both configurations satisfy the hard constraints.
Preference penalties are additive and nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V(x)\subseteq V(y)\Rightarrow F(x)\le F(y)\), with strict inequality when the added violations have positive total weight.
knowledge_statements.title: Violation-Set Dominance

assumptions_latex: \(X_H\ne\varnothing\).
The preference list is finite and its weights are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Optimal configurations are the members of \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X_H}F(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive penalty representation of soft preferences over feasible configurations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a nonempty configuration-feasibility set \(X_H\), let \((P_i,w_i)_{i=1}^m\) be preference clauses with \(w_i\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}\). Weighted configuration preferences define \[F(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m w_i\mathbf{1}[x\not\models P_i],\qquad x\in X_H.\] An optimal configuration is any \(x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X_H}F(x)\). Equivalently, when \(W=\sum_{i=1}^m w_i\) is fixed, it maximizes the satisfied preference weight \(W-F(x)\). This representation assumes additive compensation: violating several preferences costs the sum of their weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each violated soft preference incurs its nonnegative weight. An optimal feasible configuration minimizes total penalty, equivalently maximizing satisfied preference weight under additive semantics.
knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Configuration Preferences

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact level-by-level method avoiding large scalarization multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_0=X_H\). For \(r=1,\ldots,k\), compute \(v_r=\min_{x\in X_{r-1}}F_r(x)\) and set \(X_r=\{x\in X_{r-1}:F_r(x)=v_r\}\). If \(X_H\) is finite and nonempty, every member of \(X_k\) is lexicographically optimal for \((F_1,\ldots,F_k)\), and every lexicographically optimal configuration belongs to \(X_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimize the highest-priority penalty, fix its optimum, and repeat at lower levels; the final survivors are exactly the lexicographic optima.
assumptions_latex: \(X_H\) is finite and nonempty.
Each \(F_r\) is defined on \(X_H\).
Every level subproblem is solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X_k=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X_H}^{\mathrm{lex}}(F_1(x),\ldots,F_k(x))\).

notation.meaning: configurations optimal through priority level r
optimal level-r penalty after higher levels are fixed

knowledge_statements.title: Sequential Lexicographic Optimization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of a weighted-sum encoding without strict dominance over lower-level variation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider feasible configurations with penalty vectors \(F(x)=(0,2)\) and \(F(y)=(1,0)\). Lexicographic minimization prefers \(x\). The scalar objective \(M_1F_1+M_2F_2\) instead prefers \(y\) when \(M_1<2M_2\) and ties them when \(M_1=2M_2\). Thus a multiplier lacking strict dominance over attainable lower-level variation need not encode lexicographic priority.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a higher-level multiplier is too small, a lower-level improvement can outweigh a worse higher-priority penalty.
assumptions_latex: Both displayed penalty vectors are attainable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_1\le2M_2\Rightarrow\operatorname*{argmin}(M_1F_1+M_2F_2)\text{ need not equal the lexicographic argmin}.\)

notation.meaning: two-level penalty vector of configuration x

knowledge_statements.title: Insufficient Multipliers Can Reverse Priorities

assumptions_latex: \(X_H\ne\varnothing\).
Each level penalty is integer-valued and has a finite valid upper bound \(B_r\).
All preference weights are nonnegative integers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The dominance inequalities make scalar minimizers exactly the lexicographically minimal feasible configurations.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lexicographic optimization of integer-valued configuration penalties ordered by priority level.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition the finite set of soft configuration preferences into index sets \(I_1,\ldots,I_k\), where level \(1\) has the highest priority. For each feasible \(x\in X_H\), define \[F_r(x)=\sum_{i\in I_r}w_i\mathbf{1}[x\not\models P_i],\qquad r=1,\ldots,k.\] A configuration \(x^*\) is multilevel-optimal when \((F_1(x^*),\ldots,F_k(x^*))\) is lexicographically minimal over \(X_H\). Suppose every \(w_i\) is a nonnegative integer and \(0\le F_s(x)\le B_s\) for every feasible \(x\). Then one weighted sum \(\sum_{r=1}^k M_rF_r(x)\) represents the lexicographic order whenever the positive multipliers satisfy \(M_r>\sum_{s>r}M_sB_s\) for every \(r<k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Preferences are grouped into ordered levels and their integer-valued penalty vectors are minimized lexicographically. A scalar encoding is exact when each higher-level multiplier dominates every possible lower-level contribution.
knowledge_statements.title: Multilevel Configuration Priorities

children.title: Configuration Explanations
children.top_down_role: Explanatory artifacts for configuration feasibility or preference outcomes.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient reuse condition and failure boundary after changing active constraints or preferences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(E\models\ell\) and every member of \(E\) remains asserted in a new context \(K'\), then \(K'\models\ell\). If some member of \(E\) is removed, the old certificate alone no longer establishes \(K'\models\ell\), although the entailment may still hold for another reason; validity in \(K'\) must then be checked anew.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retaining every cited premise preserves an explanation; removing one invalidates reuse of that certificate but does not by itself disprove the decision.
assumptions_latex: E\models\ell.
E\subseteq K'\text{ for the preservation implication}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: E\subseteq K'\Longrightarrow K'\models\ell;\qquad E\nsubseteq K'\text{ means the old certificate alone is insufficient}.
knowledge_statements.title: Context Scope of Configuration Explanations

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Consistency Does Not Establish Explanatory Entailment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counterexample separating compatibility from explanation of a decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E=\{x\lor y\}\) and \(\ell=x\). The set \(E\) is satisfiable, but \(x=0,y=1\) satisfies \(E\land\neg\ell\). Hence \(E\not\models\ell\), so satisfiability or co-occurrence with one configuration is insufficient for an entailment-based explanation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint set can be compatible with a decision without explaining it; explanation requires entailment.
assumptions_latex: E=\{x\lor y\}.
\ell=x.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: E\text{ is satisfiable but }E\not\models\ell.
knowledge_statements.title: Consistency Does Not Establish Explanatory Entailment
Configuration Explanations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Entailment-based explanations for a configuration decision under hard constraints and selected preferences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be hard Boolean constraints, \(P\) a set of activated preference clauses, and \(\ell\) a literal describing a configuration decision. A set \(E\subseteq H\cup P\) is an explanation of \(\ell\) when \(E\) is satisfiable and \(E\models \ell\), equivalently when \(E\land\neg\ell\) is unsatisfiable. Thus \(E\), together with an unsatisfiability certificate for \(E\land\neg\ell\), certifies that every configuration satisfying the cited constraints and preferences contains the decision \(\ell\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An explanation is a satisfiable subset of active constraints and preferences that entails the selected configuration decision.
assumptions_latex: \(H\cup P\) is a finite set of Boolean clauses.
\(H\land\bigwedge P\) is satisfiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E\models\ell\).
review_flags: Exact source for entailment-based configuration explanations is missing; supplied locator hints are not specific to Boolean configuration explanations.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate formulation is mathematically plausible and fits the configuration-explanation leaf, but no citation supports this particular entailment-based notion of explanation.

children.title: Configuration Conflict Sets
children.top_down_role: Conflicting configuration requirements or preferences exposed as diagnostic sets.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Empty Conflict Diagnoses an Inconsistent Knowledge Base
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating request conflicts from inconsistency already present in hard constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The empty set is a configuration conflict relative to \(H\) exactly when \(H\) itself is unsatisfiable. Thus satisfiability of \(H\) is necessary if every reported conflict is to identify incompatibility caused by at least one request or preference.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the hard knowledge base is inconsistent, the empty request set is already a conflict.
assumptions_latex: H\text{ is a finite Boolean configuration theory}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \varnothing\text{ is a conflict relative to }H\Longleftrightarrow H\text{ is unsatisfiable}.
knowledge_statements.title: Empty Conflict Diagnoses an Inconsistent Knowledge Base

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural closure property of configuration conflict sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(C\subseteq A\) is a configuration conflict relative to hard constraints \(H\), then every \(D\) satisfying \(C\subseteq D\subseteq A\) is also a conflict: \(H\land\bigwedge_{c\in C}c\) unsatisfiable implies \(H\land\bigwedge_{d\in D}d\) unsatisfiable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every superset of a configuration conflict is also a conflict.
assumptions_latex: C\subseteq D\subseteq A.
H\land\bigwedge_{c\in C}c\text{ is unsatisfiable}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H\land\bigwedge_{d\in D}d\text{ is unsatisfiable}.
knowledge_statements.title: Upward Closure of Configuration Conflicts
Configuration Conflict Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unsatisfiable subsets identifying mutually incompatible configuration requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be hard Boolean constraints and \(A\) a finite set of requested configuration literals or activated preference clauses. A set \(C\subseteq A\) is a configuration conflict set when \(H\land\bigwedge_{c\in C}c\) is unsatisfiable. Consequently, no valid configuration can satisfy all members of \(C\) simultaneously. An independently checkable refutation of \(H\land\bigwedge_{c\in C}c\) is a certificate of the conflict.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conflict set is a subset of requests or preferences that cannot all coexist with the hard configuration constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) and \(A\) are finite Boolean constraint sets.
\(H\) is satisfiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H\land\bigwedge_{c\in C}c\) is unsatisfiable.
review_flags: Exact source for configuration conflict sets is missing; supplied locator hints do not support this Boolean diagnosis definition.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The unsatisfiable-subset certificate fits the conflict-set leaf, but no configuration-diagnosis source is cited for the definition or its intended treatment of requests and preference clauses.

children.title: Explanation Minimality
children.top_down_role: Minimality criteria for configuration explanations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle procedure for obtaining one inclusion-minimal explanation without a minimum-cardinality guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given finite \(E_0\subseteq U\) with \(Q(E_0)=1\), inspect each original element once and delete \(e\) whenever \(Q(E\setminus\{e\})=1\) for the current set \(E\). If \(Q\) is monotone, the final set \(E'\) is valid and inclusion-minimal. The procedure uses at most \(|E_0|\) validity-oracle calls; different inspection orders may return different minimal explanations and need not return a minimum-cardinality explanation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Greedily delete every dispensable item. For a monotone validity predicate the result is inclusion-minimal, but it can depend on deletion order and need not be smallest.
assumptions_latex: \(E_0\) is finite and \(Q(E_0)=1\).
\(Q\) is monotone under set inclusion.
Each oracle call decides \(Q(F)\) exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q(E')=1\land\forall e\in E',\ Q(E'\setminus\{e\})=0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Deletion-Based Minimalization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent inclusion-minimality test for an upward-closed explanation predicate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\) be finite and let \(Q:2^U\to\{0,1\}\) be monotone: \(E\subseteq F\) and \(Q(E)=1\) imply \(Q(F)=1\). For any \(E\subseteq U\) with \(Q(E)=1\), \(E\) is inclusion-minimal if and only if \(Q(E\setminus\{e\})=0\) for every \(e\in E\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an upward-closed explanation predicate, testing every one-item deletion is equivalent to testing every proper subset.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) is finite.
\(Q\) is monotone under set inclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E\text{ is inclusion-minimal}\iff\forall e\in E,\ Q(E\setminus\{e\})=0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Single-Deletion Test for Monotone Explanations

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation between inclusion minimality and minimum cardinality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U=\{a,b,c\}\) and define \(Q(E)=1\) exactly when \(a\in E\) or \(\{b,c\}\subseteq E\). Then \(\{a\}\) and \(\{b,c\}\) are both inclusion-minimal valid explanations, but only \(\{a\}\) has minimum cardinality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A monotone validity predicate can have minimal explanations of different sizes, so inclusion minimality does not imply minimum cardinality.
assumptions_latex: \(Q(E)=1\iff a\in E\text{ or }\{b,c\}\subseteq E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{b,c\}\text{ is inclusion-minimal but not minimum-cardinality}.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Inclusion-Minimal Need Not Mean Smallest
Explanation Minimality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subset-minimality, not minimum cardinality, for explanations and conflict sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite ground set \(U\) and a predicate \(Q:2^U\to\{0,1\}\), a set \(E\subseteq U\) satisfying \(Q(E)=1\) is subset-minimal when \[Q(E)=1\quad\text{and}\quad Q(E')=0\ \text{for every proper subset }E'\subsetneq E.\] For entailment explanations, \(Q(E)=1\) means that \(E\) is satisfiable and entails the decision. For conflict explanations, \(Q(E)=1\) means that the hard constraints conjoined with \(E\) are unsatisfiable. Subset-minimality does not imply that \(E\) has minimum cardinality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An explanation is subset-minimal if it is valid but every proper subset ceases to be a valid explanation.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) is finite.
\(Q\) is the chosen explanation-validity predicate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q(E)=1\land\forall E'\subsetneq E,\ Q(E')=0\).

notation.meaning: finite set of candidate explanatory items

review_flags: A source distinguishing subset-minimal from minimum-cardinality explanations is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The subset-minimality condition is precise and correctly distinguished from minimum cardinality, but it has no supporting citation.

children.title: Conflict-Set Ranking
children.top_down_role: Prioritization of configuration conflicts by cost, relevance, or repair value.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consequence of additive cost minimization over verified configuration conflict sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal C\subseteq2^A\) be a nonempty finite family of valid conflict sets and let \(w(a)>0\) for every \(a\in A\). If \(C^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{C\in\mathcal C}\sum_{a\in C}w(a)\), then no proper subset of \(C^\star\) belongs to \(\mathcal C\). This implication can fail when zero-cost elements are allowed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every minimum-cost conflict is inclusion-minimal when all item costs are positive; zero-cost items can invalidate that conclusion.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) and \(\mathcal C\) are finite.
\(\mathcal C\ne\varnothing\).
\(w(a)>0\) for every \(a\in A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nexists C\in\mathcal C:\ C\subsetneq C^\star\).
knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Cost Ranking Implies Inclusion Minimality
Conflict-Set Ranking
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lexicographic or scalar ranking of valid configuration conflict sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal C\) be the family of configuration conflict sets and let \(w:A\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}\) assign a cost to each request or preference. A cost-ranked conflict set solves \[C^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{C\in\mathcal C}\left(\sum_{c\in C}w(c),\ |C|,\ \tau(C)\right),\] where tuples are compared lexicographically and \(\tau\) is a fixed deterministic tie-breaker. Every returned \(C^\star\) must first satisfy the conflict predicate; ranking orders valid conflicts and does not replace conflict verification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conflict sets can be ranked lexicographically by total item cost, cardinality, and a deterministic tie-breaker.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) and hence \(\mathcal C\) are finite.
\(w(c)\ge0\) for every \(c\in A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C^\star\) is a lexicographically least member of \(\mathcal C\).
review_flags: Ranking criteria are application-dependent; no source was supplied for this particular lexicographic convention.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is internally coherent, but the particular lexicographic ordering by cost, cardinality, and tie-breaker is an application-dependent convention with no cited support.

children.title: Minimum-Correction Models
children.top_down_role: Models centered on minimum-cost removal or relaxation of conflicting elements.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle procedure for extracting one inclusion-minimal correction set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(H\) is satisfiable. Start with \(T_0\subseteq S\) such that \(H\cup T_0\) is satisfiable. Inspect each clause of \(S\setminus T_0\) once, adding \(C\) to the current \(T\) whenever \(H\cup T\cup\{C\}\) remains satisfiable. The final \(T\) is maximal satisfiable and \(R=S\setminus T\) is an inclusion-minimal correction set. At most \(|S\setminus T_0|\) satisfiability calls are used; different orders may return different MCSs and need not return a minimum-cardinality correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Greedily grow a satisfiable subset to maximality and return its complement; the result is an MCS but need not be smallest.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is satisfiable.
\(H\cup T_0\) is satisfiable.
Satisfiability calls are exact.
\(S\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T\text{ is an MSS and }S\setminus T\text{ is an MCS}.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Grow-and-Complement MCS Extraction

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Minimal Corrections Can Have Different Cardinalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit separation of inclusion-minimal and minimum-cardinality correction sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H=\{p\leftrightarrow q\}\) and let the removable unit clauses be \(S=\{p,
eg p,
eg q\}\). Then \(R_1=\{p\}\) is an inclusion-minimal correction set of cardinality one, while \(R_2=\{
eg p,
eg q\}\) is an inclusion-minimal correction set of cardinality two. Hence \(R_2\) is inclusion-minimal but not minimum-cardinality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One instance can have inclusion-minimal corrections of different sizes, so an arbitrary MCS need not be a smallest correction.
assumptions_latex: \(H=\{p\leftrightarrow q\}\).
\(S=\{p,\neg p,\neg q\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_1\text{ and }R_2\text{ are MCSs, but }|R_1|=1<2=|R_2|.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Minimal Corrections Can Have Different Cardinalities

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inclusion-minimal correction, distinguished from the minimum-cardinality correction optimized by the immutable seed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be nonremovable clauses and \(S\) removable clauses. A set \(R\subseteq S\) is a correction set when \(H\cup(S\setminus R)\) is satisfiable. It is inclusion-minimal when it is a correction set and \(H\cup(S\setminus R')\) is unsatisfiable for every proper subset \(R'\subsetneq R\). Every minimum-cardinality correction set is inclusion-minimal, but the converse can fail.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inclusion-minimal correction restores satisfiability and no proper subset does; it need not be a smallest correction.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) and \(S\) are finite.
At least one correction set exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R\text{ is an MCS}\iff\operatorname{SAT}(H\cup(S\setminus R))\land\forall R'\subsetneq R,\ \neg\operatorname{SAT}(H\cup(S\setminus R')).\)
knowledge_statements.title: Inclusion-Minimal Correction Set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hypergraph duality between minimal correction sets and relative minimal unsatisfiable subsets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(H\) is satisfiable. Let \(\mathcal U\) be the family of all inclusion-minimal sets \(U\subseteq S\) such that \(H\cup U\) is unsatisfiable. Then \(R\subseteq S\) is an inclusion-minimal correction set if and only if it is an inclusion-minimal hitting set of \(\mathcal U\). Minimum-cardinality correction sets are minimum-cardinality hitting sets of \(\mathcal U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimal correction sets are exactly the minimal hitting sets of all relative minimal unsatisfiable subsets; smallest corrections are smallest such hitting sets.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is satisfiable.
\(H\) and \(S\) are finite.
\(\mathcal U\) contains every relative minimal unsatisfiable subset.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R\in\operatorname{MCS}(H,S)\iff R\in\operatorname{MinHit}(\mathcal U).\)

notation.meaning: family of all relative minimal unsatisfiable subsets

knowledge_statements.title: MCS–MUS Hitting-Set Duality

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact complement relation between minimal corrections and maximal satisfiable subsets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(T\subseteq S\), call \(T\) a maximal satisfiable subset relative to \(H\) when \(H\cup T\) is satisfiable and \(H\cup(T\cup\{C\})\) is unsatisfiable for every \(C\in S\setminus T\). Then \(R\subseteq S\) is an inclusion-minimal correction set if and only if \(S\setminus R\) is a maximal satisfiable subset relative to \(H\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A correction set is inclusion-minimal exactly when the clauses it retains form a maximal satisfiable subset.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) and \(S\) are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R\text{ is an MCS}\iff S\setminus R\text{ is an MSS relative to }H.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Correction–Maximal-Satisfiable Complement Duality
Minimum-Correction Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boolean optimization representation of minimum correction subsets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be hard clauses and \(S=\{C_1,\ldots,C_m\}\) removable clauses. Introduce \(r_i\in\{0,1\}\), where \(r_i=1\) permits removal of \(C_i\). A minimum-correction model is \[\min_{x,r}\ \sum_{i=1}^m r_i\quad\text{subject to}\quad x\models H,\qquad x\models C_i\ \text{whenever }r_i=0.\] If \((x^\star,r^\star)\) is optimal, then \(R^\star=\{C_i:r_i^\star=1\}\) has minimum cardinality among all \(R\subseteq S\) for which \(H\cup(S\setminus R)\) is satisfiable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary removal variables select a smallest set of removable clauses whose deletion restores satisfiability.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) and \(S\) are finite sets of Boolean clauses.
At least one subset \(R\subseteq S\) restores satisfiability.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}\{|R|:R\subseteq S,\ H\cup(S\setminus R)\text{ is satisfiable}\}\).

notation.meaning: indicator that clause i is removed

review_flags: Standard MaxSAT diagnosis formulation, but no supplied source locator specifically supports minimum correction subsets.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Boolean optimization representation correctly describes a minimum-cardinality correction set, but no MaxSAT or diagnosis source is cited for the formulation.

children.title: Fault-Localization Models
children.top_down_role: Models centered on identifying likely faulty components or constraints.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifiability boundary for component-level fault localization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_1\ne D_2\) be candidate fault sets. If their fault models admit exactly the same observable behaviors, \[\operatorname{proj}_O\operatorname{Mod}(M_{D_1})=\operatorname{proj}_O\operatorname{Mod}(M_{D_2}),\] then no procedure using only observations over \(O\) can distinguish \(D_1\) from \(D_2\). Unique localization requires the retained true candidate to have an observable signature different from every competitor.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fault sets with identical observable behavior cannot be uniquely distinguished using those observations alone.
assumptions_latex: The localization procedure receives only values of observables \(O\).
Both candidate fault models remain admissible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_O\operatorname{Mod}(M_{D_1})=\operatorname{proj}_O\operatorname{Mod}(M_{D_2})\Rightarrow\text{unique localization between }D_1,D_2\text{ is impossible}.\)

notation.meaning: system model under candidate fault set D

knowledge_statements.title: Observational Indistinguishability Prevents Unique Localization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic limitation of abnormality variables that merely disable normal behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the weak-fault model \(M=\bigwedge_i(\neg a_i\rightarrow B_i)\), setting \(a_i=1\) imposes no abnormal behavior for component \(i\); it only removes \(B_i\). A feasible abnormality set \(D\) therefore certifies consistency after releasing the normal constraints of \(D\), but does not by itself certify that those components physically produced the observations. Such a causal conclusion requires explicit fault-mode constraints or additional evidence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weak-fault diagnosis identifies normal-behavior assumptions that may be released; it is not proof that the selected components caused the observation.
assumptions_latex: Abnormality appears only through implications \(\neg a_i\rightarrow B_i\).
No explicit abnormal behavior is imposed when \(a_i=1\).
knowledge_statements.title: Weak-Fault Diagnoses Are Consistency Explanations
Fault-Localization Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Component-level localization through abnormality variables and consistency restoration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M=\bigwedge_{i=1}^m(\neg a_i\rightarrow B_i)\) be a component model, where \(a_i\) denotes that component \(i\) is abnormal, and let \(O\) encode observations. A cardinality-based fault-localization model is \[\min_{a,x}\ \sum_{i=1}^m a_i\quad\text{subject to}\quad x,a\models M\land O,\qquad a_i\in\{0,1\}.\] The localized set \(D^\star=\{i:a_i^\star=1\}\) is a minimum-cardinality collection of components whose behavioral constraints may be disabled so that the model becomes consistent with \(O\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Abnormality variables identify a smallest component set whose behavioral constraints must be disabled to match the observations.
assumptions_latex: Each \(B_i\) is a finite Boolean or pseudo-Boolean component constraint.
The observations are consistent with the model after some components are declared abnormal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D^\star\) has minimum cardinality among consistency-restoring abnormal-component sets.
review_flags: Model-based diagnosis source for the abnormality-variable formulation is missing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The abnormality-variable representation fits fault localization and is mathematically coherent, but it lacks a model-based diagnosis citation supporting these semantics.

children.title: Cost-Aware Diagnosis
children.top_down_role: Diagnosis regimes using weighted fault likelihoods or repair costs.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Minimum-Cost Diagnosis as Weighted Conflict Hitting Set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conflict-based characterization of consistency-restoring component diagnoses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) be a finite set of component normality assumptions and let \(\mathcal C\subseteq2^A\) contain every inclusion-minimal set of assumptions inconsistent with the system description and observations. Under weak-fault semantics, where diagnosing a component removes its normality assumption, \(D\subseteq A\) is a diagnosis if and only if \(D\cap C\ne\varnothing\) for every \(C\in\mathcal C\). Hence minimum-cost diagnosis with nonnegative costs is weighted hitting set over \(\mathcal C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under weak-fault semantics, diagnoses are exactly the hitting sets of all minimal conflicts, so minimum-cost diagnosis is weighted hitting set.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is finite.
\(\mathcal C\) contains every inclusion-minimal conflict over the normality assumptions.
Declaring a component abnormal only removes its normal-behavior assumption.
At least one diagnosis exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D\text{ is a diagnosis}\iff\forall C\in\mathcal C,\ D\cap C\ne\varnothing.\)
review_flags: Equivalence requires a complete conflict family and weak-fault semantics.
knowledge_statements.title: Minimum-Cost Diagnosis as Weighted Conflict Hitting Set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Probabilistic interpretation of additive diagnosis costs under independent failures and equal feasible-diagnosis likelihoods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose component failures are independent with priors \(p_i\in(0,\tfrac12]\), and every consistency-restoring diagnosis has the same observation likelihood. For diagnosis \(D\), the posterior ranking is therefore proportional to \(\prod_{i\in D}p_i\prod_{i\notin D}(1-p_i)\). Maximizing it is equivalent to minimizing \[\sum_{i\in D}\log\frac{1-p_i}{p_i}.\] The costs are nonnegative under \(p_i\le\tfrac12\). Correlated failures or diagnosis-dependent observation likelihoods generally require nonadditive terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With independent failure priors no greater than one half and equal feasible-diagnosis likelihoods, MAP diagnosis is additive minimization using nonnegative log-odds costs.
assumptions_latex: Component failure events are independent a priori.
All consistency-restoring diagnoses have the same observation likelihood.
\(0<p_i\le\tfrac12\) for every component.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmax}_{D\in\mathcal D}\Pr(D\mid O)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{D\in\mathcal D}\sum_{i\in D}\log\frac{1-p_i}{p_i}.\)

notation.meaning: prior probability that component i is faulty

review_flags: The MAP interpretation depends on independence and equal observation likelihood across feasible diagnoses.
knowledge_statements.title: Independent-Failure MAP Costs
Cost-Aware Diagnosis
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted diagnosis with nonnegative component or correction costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal D\subseteq2^{\{1,\ldots,m\}}\) be the family of diagnoses that restore consistency between a system model and its observations, and let \(c_i\ge0\) be the cost of diagnosing component \(i\) as faulty. A cost-aware diagnosis is any \[D^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{D\in\mathcal D}\sum_{i\in D}c_i.\] Equivalently, with abnormality indicators \(a_i\), minimize \(\sum_i c_i a_i\) subject to the encoded model and observations. Zero costs permit multiple optima; strictly positive costs ensure every optimum is inclusion-minimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cost-aware diagnosis minimizes the total assigned cost of components declared faulty while restoring consistency.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal D\) is finite and nonempty.
\(c_i\ge0\) for every component \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D^\star\) minimizes \(\sum_{i\in D}c_i\) over \(D\in\mathcal D\).

notation.meaning: cost of declaring component i faulty

review_flags: Weighted diagnosis is standard, but the supplied locators do not establish this diagnosis-specific formulation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The weighted diagnosis formulation is precise, including the effect of positive versus zero costs, but no diagnosis-specific source is supplied.

children.title: Design Fault Localization Models
children.top_down_role: MaxSAT or PB models for locating faulty design elements.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Consistency-Restoring Sets Need Not Identify Actual Faults
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Epistemic boundary of relaxation-based design fault localization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subseteq[m]\) be a minimum-weight set such that \(V\land\bigwedge_{i\notin D}B_i\) is satisfiable. This establishes that \(D\) is a minimum-weight consistency-restoring suspect set. Without completeness of the fault model and faithful abnormal-behavior semantics, it does not follow that \(D\) equals the actual causal fault set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An optimal relaxation localizes a cheapest explanation of inconsistency, not necessarily the true causal faults.
assumptions_latex: D\in\operatorname*{argmin}\left\{\sum_{i\in S}w_i:V\land\bigwedge_{i\notin S}B_i\text{ is satisfiable}\right\}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D\text{ consistency-restoring}\;\not\Rightarrow\;D\text{ equals the actual fault set}.

notation.meaning: constraint associated with design element i

knowledge_statements.title: Consistency-Restoring Sets Need Not Identify Actual Faults
Design Fault Localization Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Localization of suspect design elements using validation evidence and activation variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a design be encoded by element constraints \(B_1,\ldots,B_m\), let \(V\) encode a failing validation scenario and its required outcome, and introduce \(a_i\in\{0,1\}\). The localization model is \[\min_{a,x}\ \sum_{i=1}^m w_i a_i\quad\text{subject to}\quad V\land\bigwedge_{i=1}^m(\neg a_i\rightarrow B_i),\qquad w_i>0.\] An optimal set \(D^\star=\{i:a_i^\star=1\}\) identifies minimum-weight suspect design elements whose constraints can be relaxed to make the design consistent with the validation evidence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted abnormality variables locate design elements whose relaxation most cheaply reconciles the design with failing validation evidence.
assumptions_latex: The design and validation evidence have a finite Boolean or pseudo-Boolean encoding.
Relaxing some design elements makes the validation constraints satisfiable.
\(w_i>0\) for every design element.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D^\star\) is a minimum-weight consistency-restoring set of suspect design elements.
review_flags: A design-debugging source is needed to validate the intended granularity and semantics of design elements.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation plausibly specializes abnormality-based diagnosis to design elements, but a design-debugging source is required to establish the intended element and relaxation semantics.

children.title: Design Correction Models
children.top_down_role: Optimization models for selecting minimal or preferred design changes.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of the minimality interpretation of weighted correction objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(S\in F\) is minimum-cost, \(j\notin S\), \(c_j=0\), and \(S\cup\{j\}\in F\). Then \(S\cup\{j\}\) is also minimum-cost although it is not inclusion-minimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With zero-cost edits, a minimum-cost correction can contain an unnecessary edit.
assumptions_latex: S\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{U\in F}c(U).
j\notin S,\quad c_j=0.
S\cup\{j\}\in F.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S\cup\{j\}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{U\in F}c(U),\qquad S\subsetneq S\cup\{j\}.

notation.meaning: sum of costs of edits in U

review_flags: Revised to require that the smaller feasible correction is already optimal; feasibility alone was insufficient in the Builder claim.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Cost Edits Destroy Guaranteed Inclusion-Minimality

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural minimality induced by strictly positive edit costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq2^{[k]}\) be the feasible family of validated edit sets and let \(c_i>0\). If \(S^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{S\in F}\sum_{i\in S}c_i\), then no \(S\in F\) satisfies \(S\subsetneq S^\star\). The converse need not hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strictly positive edit costs make every optimum inclusion-minimal, but an inclusion-minimal correction need not have minimum cost.
assumptions_latex: F\subseteq2^{[k]}.
c_i>0\quad(i\in[k]).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S^\star\text{ optimal}\Longrightarrow\nexists S\in F:\ S\subsetneq S^\star.
knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Cost Optima Are Inclusion-Minimal Corrections
Design Correction Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimization over admissible design edits that satisfy validation constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z\in\{0,1\}^k\) select admissible design edits, let \(B(z,x)\) encode the edited design, let \(V(x)\) encode required validation properties, and let \(c\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}^k\). A design correction model is \[\min_{z,x}\ c^\top z\quad\text{subject to}\quad B(z,x)\land V(x),\qquad z\in\mathcal Z,\] where \(\mathcal Z\subseteq\{0,1\}^k\) encodes allowed edit combinations. An optimum \(z^\star\) specifies a least-cost admissible correction for which the corrected design satisfies the encoded validation requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A design correction model chooses a least-cost admissible set of edits that makes the design satisfy its validation requirements.
assumptions_latex: \(B\), \(V\), and \(\mathcal Z\) have finite Boolean or pseudo-Boolean encodings.
At least one admissible edit vector yields a validated design.
\(c_j\ge0\) for every edit \(j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}\{c^\top z:z\in\mathcal Z,\ \exists x\ B(z,x)\land V(x)\}\).
review_flags: The supplied modeling locators do not specifically support Boolean optimization models for design correction.

children.title: Design Validation Models
children.top_down_role: Models for checking design conformance against weighted validation conditions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of the zero-optimum certificate in weighted validation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the weighted violation model, \(\operatorname{opt}=0\) need not imply \(B\models P_j\) when \(w_j=0\). A zero-weight condition must instead receive positive weight or be imposed as a hard constraint to be covered by the certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero weighted-violation score does not certify conditions assigned zero weight.
assumptions_latex: w_j=0\text{ for some validation condition }j.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{opt}=0\;\not\Rightarrow\;B\models P_j\quad\text{when }w_j=0.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: MaxSAT or pseudo-Boolean scoring of multiple validation conditions for a fixed encoded design.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B(x,u)\) encode a satisfiable design domain and let \(P_j(x,u)\) be validation conditions with weights \(w_j\ge0\). Introduce \(v_j\in\{0,1\}\) with \(v_j\leftrightarrow\neg P_j(x,u)\). Then \[\max_{x,u,v}\sum_jw_jv_j\quad\text{subject to}\quad B(x,u)\land\bigwedge_j\bigl(v_j\leftrightarrow\neg P_j(x,u)\bigr)\] finds a behavior having maximum violated-condition weight. Its optimum is zero exactly when every behavior satisfying \(B\) satisfies every positive-weight condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted validation finds a design behavior maximizing violated-condition weight; with a nonempty design domain, zero optimum certifies all positive-weight conditions.
assumptions_latex: B\text{ and every }P_j\text{ have finite exact encodings}.
\exists x,u\;B(x,u).
w_j\ge0.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counterexample-based validation of finite Boolean design models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B(x,u)\) encode a design under environment input \(u\), and let \(P(x,u)\) be the required property. Validation is represented by the counterexample formula \[B(x,u)\land\neg P(x,u).\] The design is valid over the encoded finite domain exactly when this formula is unsatisfiable. If it is satisfiable, any satisfying assignment \((x^\star,u^\star)\) is a concrete validation counterexample. When inputs are partitioned into valid and invalid scenarios, their domain restriction must be conjoined with the formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite Boolean design is valid exactly when no assignment satisfies the design while violating the required property.
assumptions_latex: \(B\) and \(P\) are finite Boolean or pseudo-Boolean encodings.
The quantified validation domain is explicitly encoded.
