children.title: Debugging–Validation Interaction
children.top_down_role: Interfaces through which validation outcomes guide debugging objectives.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Termination of counterexample-guided debugging when rejected corrections are permanently excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal Z\) be a finite set of admissible corrections. At iteration \(t\), validation either certifies \(B(z_t)\models P\) or returns a counterexample inducing a sound constraint that excludes \(z_t\) while retaining every globally valid correction. If rejected corrections are never selected again, the loop has at most \(|\mathcal Z|\) failed validations. Exhaustion of all candidates certifies that no correction in \(\mathcal Z\) satisfies the encoded property.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A counterexample-guided loop over finitely many corrections has at most one failed validation per correction when rejected candidates are permanently excluded without excluding valid ones.
assumptions_latex: |\mathcal Z|<\infty.
\text{Every learned counterexample constraint retains every globally valid correction.}
\text{No rejected correction is selected again.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{fail}}\le |\mathcal Z|.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Candidate-Space Termination Bound
Debugging–Validation Interaction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterative interaction between counterexample generation, localization, correction, and revalidation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B_t\) denote the design after iteration \(t\), and let \(P\) be the required property. If \(B_t\land\neg P\) is satisfiable, a satisfying assignment \(q_t\) is added to the accumulated validation evidence \(Q_{t+1}=Q_t\cup\{q_t\}\). A debugging step chooses an admissible correction producing \(B_{t+1}\) such that every \(q\in Q_{t+1}\) satisfies the corrected requirement. Revalidation must then test \(B_{t+1}\land\neg P\); passing only the accumulated scenarios does not certify global validity. Termination with an unsatisfiable counterexample formula certifies the encoded property.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Validation supplies counterexamples to debugging; corrections must address accumulated evidence and then undergo global revalidation.
assumptions_latex: The design, property, and admissible corrections have finite encodings.
Each correction preserves all previously imposed validation scenarios.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_t\land\neg P\text{ unsatisfiable}\) is the stopping certificate for encoded validity.
review_flags: A source is needed for this counterexample-guided debugging–validation loop and its termination criterion.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle appropriately connects counterexample generation, correction, and global revalidation, but its correction obligations and stopping criterion lack a supporting counterexample-guided debugging source.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-template program repair as weighted Boolean optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z\in\{0,1\}^k\) select edits from a finite repair template, let \(P_z\) denote the edited program, and let \(T=\{t_1,\ldots,t_n\}\) be required tests. Suppose \(\operatorname{Pass}(P_z,t_j)\) has a finite Boolean encoding for each test. An optimum is a least-cost template-bounded repair passing every encoded test.

\(c_i\ge0\) for every edit.

Test-Suite Reduction Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted set-cover representation preserving specified test requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T\) be a finite test suite, \(R\) the required behaviors or faults, and \(a_{rt}\in\{0,1\}\) indicate whether test \(t\) covers requirement \(r\). With selection variables \(x_t\in\{0,1\}\), positive test costs \(c_t\), and required multiplicities \(q_r\ge 1\), test-suite reduction is represented by

assumptions_latex: \(T\) and \(R\) are finite.
\(c_t>0\) and \(q_r\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}\).

m\ge1.

Minimizing \[\sum_{u,v,k}d_{uvk}q_{uvk}+\sum_{r,k}p_{rk}R_{rk}(x)\] over that encoding returns a plan of minimum modeled transition-plus-resource cost.

For actions \(A\) and periods \(k=0,\ldots,H-1\), let \(x_{ak}\in\{0,1\}\) indicate execution of action \(a\) at period \(k\). Let \(P_H(x)\) be a Boolean or pseudo-Boolean encoding of the initial state, transitions, action applicability, concurrency rules, and goal attainment by horizon \(H\). With action costs \(c_{ak}\ge0\), a minimum-cost plan is represented by
\[\min\left\{\sum_{k=0}^{H-1}\sum_{a\in A}c_{ak}x_{ak}:P_H(x)\right\}.\]
Every feasible assignment decodes to a horizon-bounded plan, and its objective equals the plan's additive action cost.

\(P_H\) is sound and complete for the chosen planning semantics.

notation.meaning: monitor is in state q at time k

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Monitor Encoding of Trajectory Preferences

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact indicator semantics for credited satisfaction and charged violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each preference \(\varphi_j(x)\), impose \(s_j\leftrightarrow\varphi_j(x)\) and \(v_j\leftrightarrow\neg\varphi_j(x)\). Then \(\max\sum_jw_js_j\) and \(\min\sum_jw_jv_j\) differ by the constant \(\sum_jw_j\) and select the same plans. The one-way implication \(s_j\Rightarrow\varphi_j(x)\) preserves optimal plan values when every \(w_j>0\), but leaves zero-weight indicators potentially untruthful.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact reification makes preference rewards and violation penalties equivalent; one-way credit implications do not determine zero-weight indicators.
assumptions_latex: Each preference has an exact Boolean encoding over feasible plans.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: With exact indicators, reward maximization and violation minimization select identical plans.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Preference Reification
Planning Preference Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted partial satisfaction of soft planning preferences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P_H(x)\) be a hard finite-horizon planning encoding and let \(\varphi_j(x)\) be a Boolean preference with weight \(w_j\ge0\). Introduce \(s_j\in\{0,1\}\) and enforce \(s_j\Rightarrow\varphi_j(x)\). The weighted preference model is
\[\max\left\{\sum_{j=1}^{q}w_js_j:P_H(x),\ s_j\Rightarrow\varphi_j(x)\ \text{for all }j\right\}.\]
Equivalently, the model minimizes total weight of violated preferences. Lexicographic preference levels are obtained by optimizing successive groups while fixing each earlier level's attained value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Find a feasible plan maximizing the total weight of satisfied soft preferences, optionally using lexicographic priority levels.
assumptions_latex: \(P_H\) defines the admissible plans.
\(w_j\ge0\) for every preference.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An optimum satisfies a maximum-weight collection of jointly attainable planning preferences.

notation.meaning: indicator that preference j is credited as satisfied

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The weighted soft-preference representation fits the leaf, but the cited general modeling section does not support the planning-preference or lexicographic claims.

children.title: Cost–Preference Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Priority, weighting, and compromise regimes connecting cost with preference satisfaction.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of positive weighted sums to recover every discrete nondominated outcome.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For attainable vectors \(Y=\{(0,2),(1,3/2),(2,0)\}\), \((1,3/2)\) is nondominated but cannot minimize \(\alpha C+\beta V\) for any \(\alpha,\beta>0\): comparison with the first endpoint requires \(\alpha\le\beta/2\), while comparison with the second requires \(\alpha\ge3\beta/2\). It is attainable through \(\min C\) subject to \(V\le3/2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A discrete nondominated outcome may be invisible to every positive weighted sum but recoverable by an epsilon constraint.
assumptions_latex: The three displayed criterion vectors are attainable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Positive weighted sums need not generate every nondominated discrete cost-preference outcome.
knowledge_statements.title: Unsupported Nondominated Tradeoff

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict-priority combination of plan cost and preference violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonempty feasible plan set \(X\), lexicographically minimizing \((V(x),C(x))\) is equivalent to first finding \(V^*=\min_{x\in X}V(x)\) and then solving \(\min\{C(x):x\in X,\ V(x)=V^*\}\). Reversing the tuple gives strict cost-first priority.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lexicographic optimization gives one criterion absolute priority and uses the other to break optimal ties.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is nonempty and both criteria attain their successive minima.
\(C\) and \(V\) are well-defined on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Successive constrained optimization returns the selected lexicographic optimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Lexicographic Cost-Preference Tradeoff
Cost–Preference Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalarized tradeoff between plan cost and preference violations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For feasible plans \(x\) satisfying \(P_H(x)\), let \(C(x)\ge0\) be execution cost and let \(V(x)=\sum_jw_j(1-s_j)\) be weighted preference violation. For coefficients \(\alpha,\beta>0\), the scalarized tradeoff is
\[\min\{\alpha C(x)+\beta V(x):P_H(x)\}.\]
Every optimizer is weakly Pareto efficient for the criterion pair \((C,V)\). Alternatively, an epsilon-constraint model minimizes \(C(x)\) subject to \(V(x)\le\varepsilon\); varying \(\varepsilon\) can recover supported and unsupported nondominated outcomes in a finite discrete planning model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Balance plan cost and preference violations by positive weighting, or bound violations and minimize cost to explore nondominated plans.
assumptions_latex: The feasible plan set is nonempty and finite.
\(\alpha,\beta>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each scalarized optimum is weakly Pareto efficient with respect to \((C,V)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The positive weighted-sum claim is mathematically sound, and the epsilon-constraint statement is plausible for finite discrete outcomes, but the cited general modeling section does not support these multiobjective assertions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correct linkage between a soft scheduling condition and its penalty variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a Boolean scheduling condition \(\psi_\ell(y)\), the equivalence \(v_\ell\leftrightarrow
eg\psi_\ell(y)\) makes \(ho_\ell v_\ell\) its exact violation penalty. If \(ho_\ell>0\), \(
eg\psi_\ell(y)\Rightarrow v_\ell\) suffices for optimal objective values. Imposing only \(v_\ell\Rightarrow
eg\psi_\ell(y)\) is unsound because a violation may retain \(v_\ell=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A charged violation variable must be forced on whenever its soft scheduling condition is violated.
assumptions_latex: \(\rho_\ell\ge0\).
\(\psi_\ell\) has an exact Boolean encoding.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Equivalence gives exact penalty semantics for every feasible schedule.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Soft-Scheduling Violation Indicators

knowledge_statements.scope_note: General separable integer completion-time penalties represented by threshold indicators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For integer \(C_j\in\{0,\ldots,H\}\), exact indicators \(z_{jt}=\mathbf1[C_j\ge t]\) represent any function \(g_j\) on that domain as \[g_j(C_j)=g_j(0)+\sum_{t=1}^{H}\bigl(g_j(t)-g_j(t-1)\bigr)z_{jt}.\] Thus \(\sum_jg_j(C_j)\) becomes a linear pseudo-Boolean objective when the indicators are linked exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any finite integer-domain completion penalty can be expressed as a linear sum of exact threshold indicators.
assumptions_latex: Completion times have a finite integer domain.
Every threshold indicator is linked exactly to its completion time.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The threshold expression equals \(g_j(C_j)\) for every feasible schedule.

notation.meaning: indicator that job j completes at or after threshold t

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Domain Completion Penalties

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical due-date penalties over hard-feasible schedules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For completion time \(C_j\) and due date \(d_j\), define \(E_j=\max\{d_j-C_j,0\}\), \(T_j=\max\{C_j-d_j,0\}\), and \(U_j=\mathbf1[C_j>d_j]\). Minimizing \(\sum_j(\alpha_jE_j+\beta_jT_j+\gamma_jU_j)\) with nonnegative coefficients yields the minimum modeled due-date penalty. Weighted total tardiness and weighted number of late jobs are obtained by retaining only the corresponding terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Standard due-date objectives charge early completion, tardiness magnitude, and/or a fixed cost for being late.
assumptions_latex: Completion times are linked exactly to hard scheduling decisions.
\(\alpha_j,\beta_j,\gamma_j\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The objective equals the selected separable due-date penalty of each feasible schedule.
knowledge_statements.title: Earliness, Tardiness, and Late-Job Penalties
Scheduling Penalty Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Time-indexed scheduling with weighted lateness and soft-constraint penalties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(y_{jt}\in\{0,1\}\) assign each job \(j\) one admissible start time \(t\), with hard pseudo-Boolean constraints enforcing \(\sum_t y_{jt}=1\), resource capacities, and any precedence relations. Define completion time \(C_j=\sum_t(t+p_j)y_{jt}\) and tardiness \(T_j\ge C_j-d_j\), \(T_j\ge0\). With nonnegative weights \(w_j\) and optional violation indicators \(v_ell\), a scheduling penalty model minimizes
\[\sum_jw_jT_j+\sum_ell\rho_ell v_ell.\]
The hard constraints determine admissibility; the objective prices lateness and explicitly designated soft-constraint violations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Assign jobs feasible start times while minimizing weighted tardiness and penalties for explicitly modeled soft scheduling violations.
assumptions_latex: Jobs and admissible start times are finite.
\(p_j,d_j,w_j,\rho_ell\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An optimum is an admissible schedule of minimum modeled penalty.

notation.meaning: job j starts at time t

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited penalty-function section does not support the time-indexed scheduling formulation. Moreover, the violation indicators are not linked to any stated soft constraints, so the exact model requires scheduling-specific evidence and clarification.

knowledge_statements.title: Pseudo-Boolean Resource-Allocation Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary allocation under capacities, assignment rules, and additive value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x_{ij}\in\{0,1\}\) indicate allocation of item \(i\) to resource \(j\). If item \(i\) consumes \(a_{ik}\ge0\) units of resource type \(k\), location \(j\) has capacity \(b_{jk}\), and allocation yields value \(v_{ij}\), a standard pseudo-Boolean model is
\[\max\sum_{i,j}v_{ij}x_{ij}\quad\text{subject to}\quad \sum_i a_{ik}x_{ij}\le b_{jk},\quad \sum_jx_{ij}\le1.\]
Additional Boolean clauses may encode eligibility, dependencies, or mutual exclusions. Every feasible binary assignment respects the stated capacities and single-allocation rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Allocate each item to at most one resource while respecting capacities and maximizing total assignment value.
assumptions_latex: The item, resource, and resource-type sets are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An optimal binary assignment maximizes total value subject to capacity and allocation constraints.

notation.meaning: item i is allocated to resource j
resource-type k consumption of item i
capacity of type k at resource j

source_refs.locator: 1.2.1 Resource allocation in production planning p. 4

source_witnesses.locator: 1.2.1 Resource allocation in production planning p. 4

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of aggregate-demand comparison for indivisible mandatory allocation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Three mandatory items of demand \(2\) and two resources of capacity \(3\) satisfy total demand \(6\le6\), but each resource can hold at most one item, so no feasible allocation exists. Hence \(\sum_i a_i\le\sum_jb_j\) is necessary but not sufficient for indivisible allocation feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enough total capacity does not guarantee that indivisible items fit into the individual resources.
assumptions_latex: Every item must be assigned to exactly one resource.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Aggregate capacity alone is not a sufficient feasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Aggregate Capacity Is Not Sufficient

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-charge extension coupling allocation to resource activation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y_j\in\{0,1\}\) indicate activation of resource \(j\). Constraints \(x_{ij}\le y_j\), or \(\sum_i a_{ik}x_{ij}\le b_{jk}y_j\), prohibit allocation to inactive resources. A term \(f_jy_j\) in a minimization objective charges each activated resource once.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A binary activation variable gates assignments and represents a fixed resource-opening cost.
assumptions_latex: \(x_{ij}\) and \(y_j\) are binary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every positive allocation requires activation, and every activated resource incurs its modeled fixed cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Resource-Activation Costs

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Assignment-row variants of the pseudo-Boolean allocation template.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For item \(i\), \(\sum_{j\in E_i}x_{ij}=1\) requires exactly one eligible resource, whereas \(\sum_{j\in E_i}x_{ij}\le1\) permits rejection. Introducing \(u_i\in\{0,1\}\) and imposing \(\sum_{j\in E_i}x_{ij}=u_i\) makes acceptance explicit and permits an acceptance reward or rejection penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equality rows model mandatory assignment; an acceptance variable gives exact optional-assignment semantics.
assumptions_latex: Each eligibility set \(E_i\) is finite.
Allocation and acceptance variables are binary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed rows have exactly the stated mandatory or optional assignment semantics.

notation.meaning: item i is accepted for allocation

knowledge_statements.title: Mandatory and Optional Allocation Variants

children.title: Feature Selection Models
children.top_down_role: Weighted selection of optional features subject to compatibility constraints.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite Boolean feature selection over an explicitly declared valid-configuration relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be finite, \(x_f\in\{0,1\}\), and let \(H(x)\) be the declared feature-model constraints. With benefit \(u_f\), nonnegative cost \(c_f\), and budget \(B\ge0\), feature selection is \(\max\{\sum_{f\in F}u_fx_f:H(x),\ \sum_{f\in F}c_fx_f\le B\}\). A requires relation \(f\Rightarrow g\) is \(x_f\le x_g\), and pairwise exclusion is \(x_f+x_g\le1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a highest-benefit valid feature configuration within budget, using Boolean implications and exclusions for dependencies and incompatibilities.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is finite.
\(H(x)\) explicitly defines valid configurations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^*\in\arg\max\left\{\sum_fu_fx_f:H(x),\sum_fc_fx_f\le B\right\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Constrained Feature-Configuration Selection

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact Boolean encodings of mandatory, optional, OR, and XOR child groups.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For parent \(p\) and finite child group \(C\), child legality requires \(x_c\le x_p\) for every \(c\in C\). A mandatory child satisfies \(x_c=x_p\); an optional child needs only \(x_c\le x_p\); an OR-group satisfies \(x_p\le\sum_{c\in C}x_c\le|C|x_p\); and an XOR-group satisfies \(\sum_{c\in C}x_c=x_p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mandatory, optional, OR, and XOR feature-tree relations have exact binary linear encodings.
assumptions_latex: The feature tree and child groups are finite.
\(x_f\in\{0,1\}\) for every feature.
Every OR or XOR group is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The inequalities admit exactly the selections satisfying the declared group semantics.}
knowledge_statements.title: Feature-Tree Group Encodings
Feature Selection Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boolean feature-model feasibility with weighted benefit and cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a finite feature set \(F\), let \(x_f\in\{0,1\}\) indicate selection and let \(H(x)\) contain mandatory, optional, requires, excludes, and group constraints. With benefit \(u_f\), cost \(c_f\ge0\), and budget \(B\), feature selection may be represented by
\[\max\left\{\sum_{f\in F}u_fx_f:H(x),\ \sum_{f\in F}c_fx_f\le B\right\}.\]
A requires relation from \(f\) to \(g\) is encoded by \(x_f\le x_g\), while exclusion is encoded by \(x_f+x_g\le1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select a feasible, budget-limited feature configuration maximizing total feature benefit while respecting dependencies and exclusions.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is finite.
\(H(x)\) faithfully encodes the feature-model semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An optimum is a maximum-benefit valid feature configuration within budget \(B\).

notation.meaning: benefit and cost of feature f

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Boolean selection model is coherent, but the cited general mathematical-programming section does not support feature-model semantics, including mandatory, group, requires, and excludes constraints.

children.title: Requirement Selection Models
children.top_down_role: Prioritized inclusion of requirements under budget or feasibility pressure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural characterization of requirement sets satisfying prerequisite implications.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subseteq R\times R\) encode \(r\Rightarrow s\), and let \(D^*\) be its transitive closure. A set \(S\subseteq R\) satisfies all implications if and only if \(r\in S\) and \((r,s)\in D^*\) always imply \(s\in S\). Replacing \(D\) by any directed graph having the same transitive closure preserves the implication-feasible sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A requirement set obeys its prerequisites exactly when it contains every transitive prerequisite of each selected requirement.
assumptions_latex: \(R\) is finite.
Every arc \((r,s)\) means selecting r requires selecting s.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S\text{ satisfies }D\iff\forall(r,s)\in D^*:\ r\in S\Rightarrow s\in S.

notation.meaning: transitive closure of the prerequisite relation

knowledge_statements.title: Implication-Closure Characterization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-family form of value-maximizing requirement selection under budget and logical restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\) be finite and let \(\mathcal A\subseteq2^R\) contain exactly the requirement sets satisfying all mandatory, prerequisite, and exclusion rules. With values \(v_r\), costs \(c_r\ge0\), and budget \(B\ge0\), select \(S\in\arg\max\{\sum_{r\in S}v_r:S\in\mathcal A,\ \sum_{r\in S}c_r\le B\}\). An implication \(r\Rightarrow s\) requires \(r\in S\Rightarrow s\in S\), while a conflict forbids the relevant subset from being wholly contained in \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose the highest-value admissible requirement set within budget, respecting mandatory choices, prerequisites, and exclusions.
assumptions_latex: \(R\) is finite.
\(\mathcal A\) faithfully represents the declared requirement rules.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S^*\in\arg\max_{S\in\mathcal A,\ \sum_{r\in S}c_r\le B}\sum_{r\in S}v_r.
knowledge_statements.title: Admissible Requirement-Set Optimization
Requirement Selection Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value-maximizing requirement selection under budget and logical constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For requirements \(R\), let \(y_r\in\{0,1\}\) indicate selection, with value \(v_r\), cost \(c_r\ge0\), and budget \(B\). Let \(G(y)\) encode mandatory requirements, implications, and conflicts. The requirement-selection model is
\[\max\left\{\sum_{r\in R}v_ry_r:G(y),\ \sum_{r\in R}c_ry_r\le B\right\}.\]
An implication \(r\Rightarrow s\) is encoded by \(y_r\le y_s\), and a conflict by \(y_r+y_s\le1\). Weighted soft clauses may replace additive values when benefits depend on combinations of requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a highest-value feasible set of requirements subject to budget, implication, mandatory, and conflict constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(R\) is finite.
\(G(y)\) faithfully encodes requirement constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An optimum is a maximum-value admissible requirement set within budget \(B\).

notation.meaning: value and cost of requirement r

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits requirement selection, but the general modeling citation does not support the requirements-engineering interpretation or its stated constraint semantics.

children.title: Feature–Requirement Traceability
children.top_down_role: Links between selected features and the requirements they realize.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of treating distinct trace meanings as interchangeable implications.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose requirement \(r\) is traced to distinct features \(f_1,f_2\). With \(y_r=1,x_{f_1}=1,x_{f_2}=0\), existential realization is satisfied, universal necessity is violated, and feature-justification constraints alone do not require \(y_r\) to have any realizing feature unless the converse coupling is also imposed. Thus the three trace interpretations are not equivalent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One selected traced feature can realize a requirement existentially while failing universal necessity, and justification alone does not imply realization.
assumptions_latex: \(r\) has trace links to two distinct features.
The indicators are Boolean.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Existential realization}\not\equiv\text{universal necessity}\not\equiv\text{feature justification}.
knowledge_statements.title: Untyped Trace Non-Equivalence Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boolean encodings for explicitly declared realization, necessity, and justification trace meanings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L\subseteq R\times F\), with requirement indicators \(y_r\) and feature indicators \(x_f\). Under existential realization, \(y_r\le\sum_{f:(r,f)\in L}x_f\). Under universal necessity, \(y_r\le x_f\) for every \((r,f)\in L\). Under feature justification, \(x_f\le\sum_{r:(r,f)\in L}y_r\). These constraints are alternatives determined by the declared meaning of each trace relation, not equivalent translations of an untyped edge.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Trace links constrain selections only after their realization, necessity, or justification meaning has been declared.
assumptions_latex: \(R\), \(F\), and \(L\) are finite.
Each applied trace relation has an explicitly declared semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Feasible assignments satisfy the coupling associated with each declared trace type.}
knowledge_statements.title: Typed Feature–Requirement Trace Constraints
Feature–Requirement Traceability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boolean coupling induced by requirement-to-feature trace links.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x_f\in\{0,1\}\) and \(y_r\in\{0,1\}\) select features and requirements, and let \(L\subseteq R\times F\) be a traceability relation. If selecting requirement \(r\) requires at least one traced feature, impose
\[y_r\le\sum_{f:(r,f)\in L}x_f.\]
If every selected traced feature is mandatory for \(r\), impose \(y_r\le x_f\) for each \((r,f)\in L\). Conversely, when feature \(f\) is allowed only if justified by a selected traced requirement, impose \(x_f\le\sum_{r:(r,f)\in L}y_r\). The chosen trace semantics determines which coupling constraints are hard.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Translate trace links into Boolean constraints requiring selected requirements and features to justify or realize one another.
assumptions_latex: \(R\), \(F\), and \(L\) are finite.
Each trace link has an explicitly chosen existential, universal, or justification semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasible assignments satisfy every feature–requirement coupling induced by the declared trace semantics.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The leaf appropriately calls for a representation, but existential, universal, and justification interpretations of trace links are domain-dependent and currently unsupported by any citation.

children.title: Selection Conflict Regimes
children.top_down_role: Cases involving incompatible choices, unmet dependencies, or competing priorities.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact distinction between avoidable and forced conflicts under other hard constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H(x)\) contain all non-conflict hard constraints and \(\mathcal C\) the forbidden subsets. A conflict-free selection exists exactly when \(H(x)\land\bigwedge_{C\in\mathcal C}(\sum_{i\in C}x_i\le|C|-1)\) is satisfiable. If this conjunction is unsatisfiable while \(H\) is satisfiable, every \(H\)-feasible selection violates at least one conflict; with strictly positive penalties, every such selection has positive conflict cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conflicts are unavoidable exactly when the remaining hard requirements are feasible but become infeasible after all conflicts are prohibited.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) and \(\mathcal C\) are finite.
Penalties are strictly positive for the positive-cost conclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H\text{ satisfiable and }H\land\bigwedge_{C\in\mathcal C}\left(\sum_{i\in C}x_i\le|C|-1\right)\text{ unsatisfiable}\Rightarrow\text{every }H\text{-feasible selection violates a conflict}.
knowledge_statements.title: Unavoidable-Conflict Boundary

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hard, Soft, and Budgeted Higher-Order Conflicts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact encodings for forbidden jointly selected subsets and their violations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each nonempty forbidden subset \(C\), a hard conflict is \(\sum_{i\in C}x_i\le|C|-1\). For a soft conflict introduce \(z_C\in\{0,1\}\), impose \(z_C\le x_i\) for all \(i\in C\) and \(z_C\ge\sum_{i\in C}x_i-|C|+1\), so \(z_C=1\) exactly when all members of \(C\) are selected. Violations may be penalized by \(\sum_C\rho_Cz_C\), \(\rho_C\ge0\), or limited by \(\sum_Cz_C\le K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A forbidden subset may be prohibited outright, assigned an exact violation indicator and penalty, or counted against a violation budget.
assumptions_latex: The selectable set and conflict family are finite.
Every forbidden subset is nonempty.
\(x_i,z_C\in\{0,1\}\), \(\rho_C\ge0\), and \(K\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: z_C=\prod_{i\in C}x_i.

notation.meaning: indicator that every member of C is selected

knowledge_statements.title: Hard, Soft, and Budgeted Higher-Order Conflicts
Selection Conflict Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hard, soft, and budgeted encodings of pairwise selection conflicts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x_i\in\{0,1\}\) select item \(i\), and let \(E\) be a set of conflicting pairs. In the hard-conflict regime impose \(x_i+x_j\le1\) for every \(\{i,j\}\in E\). In the soft-conflict regime introduce \(z_{ij}\in\{0,1\}\), impose \(z_{ij}\ge x_i+x_j-1\), and minimize or subtract \(\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}\rho_{ij}z_{ij}\). A budgeted-conflict regime additionally imposes
\[\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}z_{ij}\le K.\]
Thus conflicts may be forbidden, penalized, or permitted only up to a declared count.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Model pairwise selection conflicts as absolute prohibitions, weighted penalties, or violations limited by a conflict budget.
assumptions_latex: The selectable item set and conflict set \(E\) are finite.
\(\rho_{ij}\ge0\) and \(K\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The feasible and optimal selections obey the chosen hard, soft, or budgeted conflict regime.

notation.meaning: indicator that conflict pair ij is jointly selected

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The hard, penalized, and budgeted encodings are mathematically plausible, but the cited generic penalty-function section does not specifically support the three selection-conflict regimes or their application semantics.

children.title: Covering Models
children.top_down_role: Weighted models for selecting objects that satisfy coverage obligations.

knowledge_statements.title: Covering Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary minimum-cost set covering over a finite incidence system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U=\{1,\ldots,m\}\) be requirements and let \(S_1,\ldots,S_n\subseteq U\) be available sets with costs \(c_j\ge 0\). Define \(A_{ij}=1\) exactly when \(i\in S_j\). A minimum-cost covering model is
\[\min\left\{\sum_{j=1}^n c_jx_j: \sum_{j=1}^n A_{ij}x_j\ge 1\ \text{for every }i\in U,\quad x\in\{0,1\}^n\right\}.\]
Its feasible vectors select set families whose union contains \(U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select a minimum-cost family of available sets so that every requirement belongs to at least one selected set.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) and the family \(\{S_j\}_{j=1}^n\) are finite.
\(c_j\ge 0\) for every \(j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\) is feasible if and only if \(U\subseteq\bigcup_{j:x_j=1}S_j\).

notation.meaning: indicator that set j is selected

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe preprocessing for nonnegative-cost set covering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(S_j\subseteq S_k\) and \(c_k\le c_j\), and no side constraint distinguishes \(j\) from \(k\), then an optimal cover exists with \(x_j=0\). Therefore \(S_j\) may be deleted without changing the optimal value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set contained in a no-more-expensive set can be removed when no side constraint distinguishes them.
assumptions_latex: Selection costs are nonnegative.
No side constraint distinguishes sets j and k.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Deleting the dominated set preserves the optimal value and at least one optimal solution.
knowledge_statements.title: Dominated-Set Elimination

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical approximation algorithm for nonnegative weighted set cover.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Starting with uncovered requirements \(R=U\), repeatedly select a set minimizing \(c_j/|S_j\cap R|\) among sets with \(S_j\cap R\ne\varnothing\), then remove its covered requirements from \(R\). For a feasible instance with \(m=|U|\), the returned cover has cost at most \(H_m\operatorname{OPT}\), where \(H_m=\sum_{r=1}^m1/r\le1+\ln m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Greedy repeatedly minimizes cost per newly covered requirement and achieves a harmonic approximation guarantee.
assumptions_latex: The instance is feasible.
\(c_j\ge0\), and \(U\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: c(\mathrm{greedy})\le H_m\operatorname{OPT}.
knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Greedy Set-Cover Algorithm

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical exact-computation boundary for finite set cover.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The decision problem asking whether an explicitly represented finite set system has a cover using at most \(K\) sets is NP-complete. Hence minimum-cardinality set cover and its nonnegative weighted generalization are NP-hard.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact minimum set cover is NP-hard even with unit selection costs.
assumptions_latex: The incidence system and \(K\) are explicitly encoded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Unless \(\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}\), no polynomial-time algorithm solves every explicit set-cover instance exactly.
knowledge_statements.title: Set-Cover Computational Hardness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact feasibility test for unconstrained finite set cover.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The model is feasible if and only if every requirement belongs to at least one available set: \[\forall i\in U\quad\{j:i\in S_j\}\ne\varnothing.\] This equivalence assumes no side constraints restrict simultaneous set selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unconstrained finite set-cover instance is feasible exactly when every requirement occurs in an available set.
assumptions_latex: No side constraints limit simultaneous set selection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasibility is equivalent to every incidence-matrix row containing at least one 1.
knowledge_statements.title: Set-Cover Feasibility Boundary

knowledge_statements.statement_title: LP Packing Dual and Optimality Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-relaxation duality for minimum-cost covering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The covering relaxation \[\min\{c^\top x:Ax\ge\mathbf1,\ x\ge0\}\] has dual \[\max\{\mathbf1^\top y:A^\top y\le c,\ y\ge0\}.\] Every dual-feasible \(y\) lower-bounds every integral cover. If an integral cover \(\bar x\) and a dual-feasible \(\bar y\) satisfy \(c^\top\bar x=\mathbf1^\top\bar y\), then \(\bar x\) is an optimal integer cover.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasible requirement prices give lower bounds, and equality with an integral cover certifies global optimality.
assumptions_latex: Costs are nonnegative.
The covering instance is feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Matching integral-cover and dual values certify optimality of the cover.

notation.meaning: dual price assigned to requirement i

knowledge_statements.title: LP Packing Dual and Optimality Certificate

children.title: Hitting-Set Models
children.top_down_role: Weighted models for intersecting every conflict, core, or requirement set.

knowledge_statements.title: Hitting-Set Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted hitting set for a finite hypergraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and let \(\mathcal E=\{E_1,\ldots,E_m\}\) be nonempty subsets of \(V\). With costs \(c_j\ge 0\), a minimum-weight hitting-set model is
\[\min\left\{\sum_{j=1}^n c_jx_j: \sum_{j\in E_i}x_j\ge 1\ \text{for }i=1,\ldots,m,\quad x\in\{0,1\}^n\right\}.\]
The selected set \(T=\{j:x_j=1\}\) intersects every hyperedge in \(\mathcal E\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose minimum-cost elements whose selected set intersects every hyperedge.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) and \(\mathcal E\) are finite.
\(E_i\ne\varnothing\) for every \(i\), and \(c_j\ge 0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\) is feasible if and only if \(T\cap E_i\ne\varnothing\) for every \(E_i\in\mathcal E\).

notation.meaning: family of hyperedges to be hit
indicator that element j is selected

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard greedy approximation for explicitly represented weighted hitting set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Starting with no hit edges, repeatedly select a vertex minimizing its nonnegative cost divided by the number of newly hit edges. For \(m=|\mathcal E|\ge1\), this algorithm returns a hitting set of cost at most \(H_m\) times optimum, where \(H_m=\sum_{i=1}^m1/i\), and runs in polynomial time under explicit incidence representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cost-per-new-edge greedy gives an H_m-approximation for weighted hitting set.
assumptions_latex: All edges are nonempty and explicitly represented.
Vertex costs are nonnegative.
\(m=|\mathcal E|\ge1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: c(T_{\mathrm{greedy}})\le H_m\,\mathrm{OPT}.
knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Greedy Hitting-Set Approximation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Private-Edge Certificate for Minimal Hitting Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact certificate of inclusion-minimality for a finite hitting set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(T\) hits every edge of a finite hypergraph \((V,\mathcal E)\), then \(T\) is inclusion-minimal if and only if every \(v\in T\) has an edge \(E_v\in\mathcal E\) satisfying \(E_v\cap T=\{v\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hitting set is inclusion-minimal exactly when every selected vertex uniquely hits some edge.
assumptions_latex: \((V,\mathcal E)\) is finite.
\(T\cap E\ne\varnothing\) for every \(E\in\mathcal E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T\text{ is inclusion-minimal}\iff\forall v\in T\;\exists E_v\in\mathcal E:\ E_v\cap T=\{v\}.

notation.meaning: private edge witnessing the necessity of vertex v

knowledge_statements.title: Private-Edge Certificate for Minimal Hitting Sets

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hitting-Set Complexity Boundary by Edge Size
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical decision complexity and its singleton-edge boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an explicitly represented finite hypergraph and \(k\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\), deciding whether a hitting set of cardinality at most \(k\) exists is NP-complete, even when every edge has size two, where the problem is Vertex Cover. If every nonempty edge has size one, the unique required vertices can be collected directly in polynomial time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hitting set remains NP-complete for two-element edges but is immediate for singleton edges.
assumptions_latex: The hypergraph is represented explicitly.
All edges are nonempty and \(k\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \textsc{Hitting Set}\text{ is NP-complete for }\max_{E\in\mathcal E}|E|=2.
knowledge_statements.title: Hitting-Set Complexity Boundary by Edge Size

knowledge_statements.scope_note: LP dual and lower-bound certificate for weighted hitting set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For edge-vertex incidence matrix \(A\) and \(c\ge0\), the relaxation \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax\ge\mathbf1,\ x\ge0\}\) has dual \(\max\{\mathbf1^Ty:A^Ty\le c,\ y\ge0\}\). Every dual-feasible fractional edge packing therefore lower-bounds the integral minimum hitting-set cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The LP dual fractionally packs edges under vertex capacities, providing certified lower bounds.
assumptions_latex: The hypergraph is finite.
\(c\in\mathbb R_{�\ge0}^{V}\).

children.title: Cover–Hit Duality
children.top_down_role: Structural correspondence between coverage obligations and sets requiring interception.

knowledge_statements.title: Cover–Hit Duality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incidence-transpose equivalence between finite covering and hitting-set formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite set system \((U,\mathcal S)\), form the dual hypergraph with vertex set \(\mathcal S\) and hyperedges \(E_u=\{S\in\mathcal S:u\in S\}\) for \(u\in U\). A subfamily \(\mathcal C\subseteq\mathcal S\) covers \(U\) if and only if \(\mathcal C\) is a hitting set of \(\{E_u:u\in U\}\). Consequently, the binary constraints of both models are identical under the incidence-matrix transpose interpretation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A family covers every ground element exactly when it hits every dual hyperedge formed by the sets containing that element.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) and \(\mathcal S\) are finite.
Every \(u\in U\) belongs to at least one member of \(\mathcal S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bigcup_{S\in\mathcal C}S=U\iff \mathcal C\cap E_u\ne\varnothing\ \text{for all }u\in U\).

notation.meaning: dual hyperedge consisting of sets containing u

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal-transversal form of finite cover–hit duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite hypergraph \(\mathcal H\), let \(b(\mathcal H)\) be the clutter of its inclusion-minimal hitting sets. Then \(b(b(\mathcal H))=\min_{\subseteq}(\mathcal H)\), the family of inclusion-minimal edges of \(\mathcal H\). In particular, \(b(b(\mathcal H))=\mathcal H\) when \(\mathcal H\) is a clutter.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Taking minimal hitting sets twice recovers the inclusion-minimal edges, and therefore recovers every finite clutter unchanged.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal H\) is a finite hypergraph.
\(b(\mathcal H)\) contains all inclusion-minimal hitting sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: b(b(\mathcal H))=\min_{\subseteq}(\mathcal H).
knowledge_statements.title: Transversal-Hypergraph Involution

children.title: Partial-Coverage Regimes
children.top_down_role: Soft or budget-limited regimes permitting selected obligations to remain uncovered.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical approximation for the unit-cost budgeted variant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When every selected set has unit cost and at most \(k\ge1\) sets may be chosen, repeatedly adding a set of maximum marginal covered weight produces \(S_k\) satisfying \(W(S_k)\ge(1-(1-1/k)^k)\mathrm{OPT}\ge(1-1/e)\mathrm{OPT}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a cardinality budget, maximum-marginal-coverage greedy attains at least a 1−1/e fraction of optimum.
assumptions_latex: Element weights are nonnegative.
The incidence system is finite.
The budget is a cardinality limit \(k\ge1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: W(S_k)\ge\left(1-(1-1/k)^k\right)\mathrm{OPT}\ge(1-1/e)\mathrm{OPT}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact feasibility boundaries for nonnegative finite partial coverage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the set-function formulation, quota covering is feasible exactly when \(Q\le W([n])\). A budgeted instance with \(B\ge0\) always admits \(S=\varnothing\), and its optimum is positive exactly when some set of cost at most \(B\) covers an element of positive weight.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quota cannot exceed total attainable covered weight; positive budgeted value requires an affordable set covering positive weight.
assumptions_latex: The incidence system is finite.
All weights and costs are nonnegative and \(B,Q\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists S:W(S)\ge Q\iff Q\le W([n]).
knowledge_statements.title: Quota and Budget Attainability Boundaries

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Budgeted maximum-coverage and quota-covering formulations using distinct covered weight.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For selectable sets indexed by \([n]\), define \(W(S)=\sum_{i:\exists j\in S,\ A_{ij}=1}w_i\) and \(C(S)=\sum_{j\in S}c_j\), with \(w_i,c_j\ge0\). Budgeted maximum coverage is \(\max\{W(S):C(S)\le B\}\); quota covering is \(\min\{C(S):W(S)\ge Q\}\). Each element contributes at most once regardless of how many selected sets cover it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partial coverage either maximizes distinct covered value within a budget or minimizes cost while attaining a coverage quota.
assumptions_latex: The incidence system is finite.
\(w_i,c_j,B,Q\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \max_{C(S)\le B}W(S)\quad\text{or}\quad\min_{W(S)\ge Q}C(S).

notation.meaning: total weight of distinct elements covered by S

assumptions_latex: \(A\) is a finite binary incidence matrix.
\(w_i,c_j,B,Q\ge 0\).

selection budget and required coverage quota

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Budgeted and quota-constrained partial covering with explicit coverage indicators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\{0,1\}^{m\times n}\), element values \(w_i\ge 0\), and set costs \(c_j\ge 0\). Introduce \(x_j,y_i\in\{0,1\}\) with
\[y_i\le\sum_{j=1}^n A_{ij}x_j\quad(i=1,\ldots,m).\]
The budgeted regime maximizes \(\sum_i w_iy_i\) subject to \(\sum_j c_jx_j\le B\). The quota regime minimizes \(\sum_j c_jx_j\) subject to \(\sum_i w_iy_i\ge Q\). In either regime, \(y_i=1\) records credited coverage of element \(i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partial covering either maximizes credited coverage under a selection budget or minimizes selection cost while meeting a coverage quota.
knowledge_statements.title: Partial-Coverage Regimes

children.title: Ranking Models
children.top_down_role: Boolean optimization models for producing ordered alternatives.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partial-output variant with an ordered leading set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(1\le k\le n\), a top-\(k\) ranking is an injective sequence \((i_1,\ldots,i_k)\). It orders the listed items, places each listed item ahead of every unlisted item, and leaves the unlisted items mutually unordered.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A top-k ranking orders k distinct leading items and leaves the remainder mutually unordered.
assumptions_latex: V\text{ is finite with }|V|=n.
1\le k\le n.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (i_1,\ldots,i_k)\text{ defines an ordered prefix rather than necessarily a complete order}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact permutation-matrix representation of a strict total ranking.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(n=|V|\), let \(y_{ik}=1\) mean item \(i\) occupies rank \(k\). Constraints \(\sum_k y_{ik}=1\) for every \(i\), \(\sum_i y_{ik}=1\) for every \(k\), and \(y_{ik}\in\{0,1\}\) encode strict total rankings bijectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A permutation matrix exactly represents a strict total ranking.
assumptions_latex: V\text{ is finite}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{y\text{ feasible}\}\longleftrightarrow\{\text{strict total orders on }V\}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-domain representation of a strict total ranking.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assign each item \(i\) a rank \(r_i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and impose \(\operatorname{AllDifferent}(r_i:i\in V)\). With \(n\) items and \(n\) ranks, each feasible vector is a permutation and hence a strict total ranking.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distinct integer ranks from one through n exactly represent a strict total ranking.
assumptions_latex: r_i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\text{ for all }i.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{AllDifferent}(r)\iff r\text{ encodes a strict total ranking}.

Ranking Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary linear-order representation for a finite item set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a finite item set \(V\), let \(x_{ij}=1\) mean that distinct item \(i\) precedes \(j\). Strict total rankings are exactly the binary vectors satisfying
\[x_{ij}+x_{ji}=1\quad(i\ne j),\qquad x_{ij}+x_{jk}-x_{ik}\le 1\quad(i,j,k\ \text{distinct}).\]
Any linear objective \(\sum_{i\ne j}c_{ij}x_{ij}\) then selects a total order optimized according to the specified pairwise costs or rewards.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary precedence variables represent a strict total ranking when completeness, antisymmetry, and transitivity constraints hold.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is finite.
\(x_{ij}\in\{0,1\}\) is defined for every ordered pair with \(i\ne j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The feasible vectors are in bijection with strict total orders on \(V\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The binary linear-order formulation is mathematically plausible and the representation content kind fits the leaf, but no source or standard-field rationale is supplied. An authoritative locator supporting the exact completeness and transitivity formulation is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The submitted rankings and voter weights determine every \(q_i\). The vector \((q_i)\), together with the declared tie rule, validates a proposed positional aggregate exactly when the order is nonincreasing in \(q_i\) and all equalities obey that rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recomputed scores and the tie rule validate a positional-scoring aggregate.
assumptions_latex: \text{The scoring vector and tie rule are fixed}.
\text{All rankings and voter weights are available}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Computational boundary for exact disagreement minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Computing a strict total order minimizing the sum of Kendall disagreements with strict complete submitted rankings is NP-hard; equivalently, exact maximization of the induced weighted pairwise-agreement objective is NP-hard.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact Kemeny aggregation is NP-hard although evaluating a proposed ranking is polynomial.
assumptions_latex: \text{Candidate and voter sets are finite}.
\text{Inputs are strict complete rankings}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Weighted Kemeny optimization is NP-hard}.

A weighted Kemeny aggregate is a strict total order maximizing \(\sum_{i\ne j}p_{ij}x_{ij}\); equivalently, it minimizes the weighted sum of Kendall pairwise disagreements with the submitted orders.

Preference-Aggregation Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted Kemeny aggregation of complete voter rankings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let each voter \(v\) supply a strict total order on finite \(V\), with weight \(\alpha_v\ge 0\). Define \(p_{ij}=\sum_v\alpha_v\mathbf 1\{i\prec_v j\}\). A weighted Kemeny aggregate is any strict total order encoded by feasible precedence variables \(x\) that solves
\[\max\sum_{i\ne j}p_{ij}x_{ij}.\]
Equivalently, it minimizes the weighted sum of pairwise disagreements, or Kendall distances, from the submitted orders.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Kemeny aggregate chooses the total ranking with maximum weighted pairwise agreement, equivalently minimum total Kendall disagreement.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) and the voter set are finite.
Every voter supplies a strict total order and has weight \(\alpha_v\ge 0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^*\in\arg\max\{\sum_{i\ne j}p_{ij}x_{ij}:x\text{ encodes a strict total order}\}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Size of the Direct Pairwise CNF Encoding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural size of the complete direct encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(n=|V|\), the ordered-pair version uses \(n(n-1)=\Theta(n^2)\) variables, \(2\binom n2=\Theta(n^2)\) pair clauses, and at most \(n(n-1)(n-2)=\Theta(n^3)\) ordered-triple transitivity clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The direct pairwise encoding has quadratic variables and pair clauses and cubic transitivity clauses.
assumptions_latex: \text{All ordered triples receive transitivity clauses}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{var}=\Theta(n^2),\qquad N_{clause}=\Theta(n^3).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pairwise Completeness Does Not Prevent a Cycle
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal witness requiring global order-consistency clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For items \(a,b,c\), set \(x_{ab}=x_{bc}=x_{ca}=1\) and all reverse variables to zero. Exactly one direction is selected for every pair, but the result is the cycle \(a\prec b\prec c\prec a\), not a strict total order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exactly one orientation per pair can still form a three-cycle.
assumptions_latex: x_{ij}+x_{ji}=1\text{ for every unordered pair}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Pairwise completeness and antisymmetry do not imply transitivity}.

For every ordered pair of distinct items use \(x_{ij}\), with hard clauses \((x_{ij}\lor x_{ji})\) and \((

\(w_{ij}\ge 0\) for every encoded preference.

children.title: Aggregation-Induced Ranking Conflicts
children.top_down_role: Inconsistency, cyclicity, or priority conflicts arising during aggregation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-time construction of a compatible ranking or cycle witness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Topological sorting of the explicit digraph \((A,P)\) runs in \(O(|A|+|P|)\) time. If all vertices are output, the order extends \(P\); otherwise, a directed cycle in the remaining subgraph certifies that no total ranking extends every edge.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Topological sorting either constructs a compatible total ranking or identifies a cycle witnessing inconsistency in linear graph time.
assumptions_latex: The aggregated relation is represented explicitly as a finite directed graph.
knowledge_statements.title: Topological Consistency Test

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact extension boundary for aggregated strict pairwise preferences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite alternative set \(A\) and irreflexive strict preference relation \(P\subseteq A\times A\), a strict total order extending every edge of \(P\) exists if and only if the directed graph \((A,P)\) is acyclic. Any directed cycle therefore certifies that every total ranking must reverse or omit at least one edge of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All aggregated pairwise preferences can be respected exactly when their directed graph is acyclic; a cycle certifies inconsistency.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is finite.
Edges of \(P\) are interpreted as strict ordering requirements.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P\text{ has a strict total-order extension}\iff(A,P)\text{ is acyclic}.
knowledge_statements.title: Directed-Cycle Certificate of Ranking Inconsistency

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Majority Aggregation Can Create a Ranking Cycle
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite profile showing that majority aggregation need not preserve transitivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let five equally weighted voters rank \(a,b,c\): two use \(a\prec b\prec c\), two use \(b\prec c\prec a\), and one uses \(c\prec a\prec b\). Pairwise majority yields \(a\prec b\), \(b\prec c\), and \(c\prec a\). Hence the collective relation is cyclic although every individual ranking is a strict total order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Five individually transitive rankings can aggregate by pairwise majority into a directed three-cycle.
assumptions_latex: All five voters have equal positive weight.
Each voter submits a strict total order.
Pairwise preferences are aggregated by simple majority.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (a\prec b)\land(b\prec c)\land(c\prec a),\text{ which is incompatible with transitivity}.

notation.meaning: precedes in an individual or collective strict preference relation

knowledge_statements.title: Majority Aggregation Can Create a Ranking Cycle
Aggregation-Induced Ranking Conflicts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condorcet-cycle counterexample for pairwise majority aggregation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let three equally weighted voters rank three items by \(a\prec b\prec c\), \(b\prec c\prec a\), and \(c\prec a\prec b\), respectively. Pairwise majority then prefers \(a\prec b\), \(b\prec c\), and \(c\prec a\). These three collective preferences form a directed cycle, so no strict total order can satisfy all majority comparisons simultaneously; any feasible aggregate must reverse at least one majority edge.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Three cyclically arranged voter rankings produce a majority cycle, forcing every total aggregate ranking to violate a majority preference.
assumptions_latex: The three voters have equal positive weight.
Each submitted ranking is a strict total order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((a\prec b)\land(b\prec c)\land(c\prec a)\) is incompatible with transitivity.

notation.meaning: precedes in a ranking or pairwise majority relation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The three-voter construction correctly produces a Condorcet cycle, and counterexample is an appropriate content kind for this conflict leaf. The record nevertheless supplies no evidence or explicit standard-field rationale, so an authoritative locator is required.

children.title: MaxSAT-Native Modeling Templates
children.top_down_role: Reusable application structures expressed primarily through hard and soft clauses.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Clause-Relaxation Encoding of Weighted Partial MaxSAT
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact encoding of soft-clause violation costs with fresh relaxation variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every soft clause \((C_k,w_k)\), introduce fresh \(r_k\in\{0,1\}\) and impose \(C_k\lor r_k\). Then \[\min\left\{\sum_k w_kr_k:H\land\bigwedge_k(C_k\lor r_k)\right\}\] preserves the weighted partial-MaxSAT optimum and projected optimal assignments. If \(w_k>0\), every optimum has \(r_k=1\) exactly when \(C_k\) is false. With zero weights, \(r_k\leftrightarrow\neg C_k\) is required for truthful indicators on every feasible augmented assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fresh relaxation variable permits a soft-clause violation and charges its weight, with exact reification needed for truthful zero-weight indicators.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is satisfiable.
\(w_k\ge0\), and each \(r_k\) is fresh.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The relaxation-variable formulation preserves the optimum and projected optimal solutions.

notation.meaning: relaxation variable for soft clause k

knowledge_statements.title: Clause-Relaxation Encoding of Weighted Partial MaxSAT

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Priority-stratified soft-clause optimization over hard-feasible assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition the soft clauses into ordered levels \(S_1,\ldots,S_p\), and let \(V_\ell(z)\) be the violated weight at level \(\ell\). Lexicographic MaxSAT minimizes \((V_1(z),\ldots,V_p(z))\) lexicographically subject to all hard clauses. Equivalently, optimize the levels successively while fixing every earlier level at its attained optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lexicographic MaxSAT minimizes higher-priority violation before considering lower-priority levels.
assumptions_latex: The hard-clause family is satisfiable.
All clause families and priority levels are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Successive level optimization returns a lexicographically minimum violation vector.

notation.meaning: weighted violation at priority level ell

knowledge_statements.title: Lexicographic MaxSAT Template

assumptions_latex: \(H\) and \(S\) are finite clause families.
\(w_k\ge 0\) for every soft clause.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the hard-clause family is satisfiable, an optimum satisfies every clause in \(H\) and minimizes \(\sum_{k:C_k(z)=\mathrm{false}}w_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted partial MaxSAT template with hard feasibility and soft penalties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be hard clauses and \(S=\{(C_k,w_k)\}_{k=1}^q\) weighted soft clauses with \(w_k\ge 0\). The native weighted partial MaxSAT model is
\[\max_{z\in\{0,1\}^n}\left\{\sum_{k=1}^q w_k\mathbf 1[C_k(z)=\mathrm{true}]:D(z)=\mathrm{true}\ \text{for every }D\in H\right\}.\]
When the hard-clause family is satisfiable, this equivalently minimizes the total weight of falsified soft clauses while never permitting violation of a hard clause.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hard clauses define feasibility; when they are jointly satisfiable, weighted soft clauses define an objective that rewards satisfaction or penalizes violation.
knowledge_statements.title: MaxSAT-Native Modeling Templates

children.title: Pseudo-Boolean-Native Modeling Templates
children.top_down_role: Reusable application structures expressed primarily through linear Boolean constraints and objectives.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine transformations normalizing pseudo-Boolean objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maximizing \(c^\top x\) is equivalent to minimizing \(-c^\top x\). Expanding a complemented objective literal \(1-x_j\) adds a fixed constant and negates the coefficient of \(x_j\). With the corresponding objective sense, these transformations preserve the optimizer set and transform the optimum value affinely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Objective-sense reversal and complemented-literal expansion preserve pseudo-Boolean optimizers under the corresponding affine transformation.
assumptions_latex: The feasible set is unchanged.
Objective sense is reversed when the objective is multiplied by a negative scalar.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The transformed and original objectives rank feasible assignments identically after accounting for objective sense.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Sense and Literal-Complement Equivalence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact inclusion of clauses and cardinality conditions as pseudo-Boolean rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(C=\ell_1\lor\cdots\lor\ell_q\), let \([\ell]=x_j\) for a positive literal and \([\ell]=1-x_j\) for a negative literal. Then \(C\leftrightarrow\sum_r[\ell_r]\ge1\). At-most-, at-least-, and exactly-\(k\) cardinality constraints are respectively \(\sum_jx_j\le k\), \(\sum_jx_j\ge k\), and \(\sum_jx_j=k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clauses and cardinality constraints are exact special cases of linear pseudo-Boolean constraints.
assumptions_latex: All variables are Boolean.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed rows accept exactly the assignments satisfying the corresponding Boolean conditions.
knowledge_statements.title: Clause and Cardinality Embedding

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact normalization of signed coefficients, equalities, and complemented literals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Using \(1-x_j\) for \(\neg x_j\), every signed linear pseudo-Boolean row can be rewritten with nonnegative literal coefficients; specifically \(-ax_j=a(1-x_j)-a\) for \(a>0\), with the constant transferred to the right-hand side. Equality is the conjunction of its two inequality directions, and multiplying by \(-1\) reverses an inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complemented literals, sign changes, and equality splitting give exact linear pseudo-Boolean normal forms.
assumptions_latex: Coefficients and right-hand sides are integral.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: These normalizations preserve exactly the feasible Boolean assignments.
knowledge_statements.title: Pseudo-Boolean Constraint Normalization
Pseudo-Boolean-Native Modeling Templates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Native binary linear objective with pseudo-Boolean constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A pseudo-Boolean optimization template has Boolean variables \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\), objective coefficients \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and constraints
\[\sum_{j=1}^n a_{ij}x_j\mathrel{\bowtie_i}b_i\quad(i=1,\ldots,m),\]
where \(a_{ij},b_i\in\mathbb Z\) and \(\bowtie_i\in\{\le,=,\ge\}\). The model minimizes or maximizes \(c^\top x\) over assignments satisfying every displayed constraint; cardinality constraints are the special case \(a_{ij}\in\{0,1\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pseudo-Boolean models optimize a linear function of Boolean variables subject to integer-coefficient linear inequalities or equalities.
assumptions_latex: \(m,n\) are finite.
\(a_{ij},b_i\in\mathbb Z\), while \(x_j\in\{0,1\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The feasible region is \(\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:Ax\mathrel{\bowtie}b\}\), with objective \(c^\top x\).

notation.meaning: integer constraint coefficients and right-hand sides

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite pseudo-Boolean optimization template is mathematically standard and representation is the correct content kind, but the record has no citation or explicit standard-field rationale. A source with a specific definition or section locator is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Infeasible Hard-Clause Layer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of weighted partial MaxSAT when mandatory clauses are jointly unsatisfiable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a weighted partial MaxSAT instance with hard-clause conjunction \(F_H=\bigwedge_{D\in H}D\), the hard layer is infeasible exactly when
\[\{z\in\{0,1\}^n:F_H(z)=\mathrm{true}\}=\varnothing.\]
In that case no feasible assignment exists, regardless of the soft clauses or their weights. Removing, relaxing, or reclassifying at least one hard clause from an unsatisfiable core is necessary before the soft objective can have a feasible optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the hard clauses are jointly unsatisfiable, soft clauses and weights cannot restore feasibility; a hard-clause core must be changed.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a finite family of clauses over finitely many Boolean variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_H\) unsatisfiable implies that the weighted partial MaxSAT feasible set is empty.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificates for hard-layer inconsistency and minimal unsatisfiable hard subsets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H'\subseteq H\). A sound unsatisfiability proof for \(\bigwedge_{D\in H'}D\) certifies infeasibility of the entire hard layer \(H\). Moreover, \(H'\) is a minimal unsatisfiable subset exactly when it is unsatisfiable and \(H'\setminus\{D\}\) is satisfiable for every \(D\in H'\). Thus an unsatisfiability proof for \(H'\), together with one satisfying assignment for every single-clause deletion, certifies both hard-layer infeasibility and subset minimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unsatisfiable hard-clause subset proves the whole hard layer infeasible; deletion models additionally certify that the subset is minimal.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a finite clause family.
Unsatisfiability proofs are checked by a sound proof checker.
Each deletion witness satisfies every clause remaining in that deletion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H'\text{ unsatisfiable}\Rightarrow H\text{ unsatisfiable}\), and \(H'\text{ is minimal unsatisfiable}\iff\forall D\in H',\ H'\setminus\{D\}\text{ is satisfiable}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Hard-Layer Unsatisfiability and Minimality Certificates
Incorrect Hard–Soft Classification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-variable example showing that exchanging mandatory and preferential clauses changes semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\) be Boolean. In the intended model, take the hard clause \((x)\) and the unit-weight soft clause \((\lnot x)\); its unique feasible optimum has \(x=1\). If the classifications are exchanged, the hard clause becomes \((\lnot x)\) and the soft clause becomes \((x)\), so the unique feasible optimum has \(x=0\). Thus hard–soft misclassification can reverse the modeled decision, not merely rescale its objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Swapping one hard clause with a conflicting soft clause reverses the unique optimal Boolean decision and changes the model's semantics.
assumptions_latex: Hard clauses must be satisfied, and the soft clause has positive weight.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The intended optimum is \(x=1\), whereas the misclassified model has optimum \(x=0\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient value and optimizer preservation conditions for promoting or demoting one clause.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v^*\) and \(X^*\) be the optimal value and optimizer set of a feasible weighted partial MaxSAT model. If a soft clause \(D\) is promoted to hard without otherwise changing costs, the optimal value is preserved exactly when \(X^*\cap\{x:D(x)=1\}\ne\varnothing\), and the optimizer set is preserved exactly when every member of \(X^*\) satisfies \(D\). If a hard clause \(D\) is instead demoted to a soft clause of finite penalty \(\lambda>0\), let \(q(x)\) be the resulting objective on assignments satisfying the remaining hard clauses. The old optimizer set is preserved exactly when \(\inf\{q(x):D(x)=0\}>v^*\); equality preserves the optimal value but introduces a violating optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Promoting a soft clause preserves all old optimizers only if they all satisfy it. Demoting a hard clause preserves them only if every newly admitted violator is strictly more expensive than the old optimum.
assumptions_latex: The original model is feasible and has a finite attained optimum.
Only the classification of \(D\) changes.
All other clauses and objective contributions remain unchanged.
The infimum over an empty violating set is \(+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed promotion and demotion conditions are necessary and sufficient for the stated value or optimizer-set preservation.

notation.meaning: objective after demoting the hard clause

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Preservation Tests for Reclassification

children.title: Weight-Scale Distortion
children.top_down_role: Loss of intended tradeoffs caused by poorly calibrated objective weights.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Two-Point Optimizer Change Under Unequal Rescaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal witness that unchanged componentwise orders do not ensure weighted-sum invariance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{a,b\}\), \(f(a)=(0,2)\), \(f(b)=(1,0)\), and \(w_1=w_2=1\). The original weighted objective selects \(b\), since its costs are \(2\) and \(1\). After replacing \(f_1\) by \(3f_1\) without compensating its weight, the costs are \(2\) and \(3\), so the optimizer changes to \(a\), although each component's ordering is unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unequal unadjusted rescaling can reverse the selected compromise while preserving every component's individual ordering.
assumptions_latex: Both feasible points and both objective components are evaluated exactly.
The original weights remain fixed after rescaling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{F}(f_1+f_2)=\{b\}\) but \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{F}(3f_1+f_2)=\{a\}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Two-Point Optimizer Change Under Unequal Rescaling

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact invariance obtained by compensating weights for changed component units.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\widetilde f_i(x)=a_if_i(x)+b_i\) with \(a_i>0\), and set \(\widetilde w_i=w_i/a_i\). Then \[\sum_i\widetilde w_i\widetilde f_i(x)=\sum_iw_if_i(x)+\sum_i\frac{w_i b_i}{a_i}.\] The second term is independent of \(x\), so the objectives induce identical comparisons and argmin sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive component rescaling causes no distortion when each weight is divided by the component scale; fixed component offsets add only a constant.
assumptions_latex: \(a_i,w_i>0\) for every component.
Each \(b_i\) is independent of the feasible assignment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}\sum_iw_if_i(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}\sum_i\widetilde w_i\widetilde f_i(x)\).

notation.meaning: scale and offset used to change component units

knowledge_statements.title: Compensated Positive-Affine Rescaling
Weight-Scale Distortion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted-sum objectives whose optimizer changes under nonuniform rescaling of component criteria.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) be nonempty, let \(f_i:F\to\mathbb{R}\), and let \(w_i>0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,p\). Weight-scale distortion occurs when positive scale factors \(a_i\) preserve every componentwise ordering but alter the weighted-sum solution set: \[\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}\sum_{i=1}^p w_i f_i(x)\neq\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}\sum_{i=1}^p w_i a_i f_i(x).\] A common scaling \(a_1=\cdots=a_p\) cannot cause this distortion; the boundary therefore concerns unequal component scales.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unequal positive rescaling of objective components can change weighted-sum optimizers even though each component’s individual ordering is unchanged.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) is nonempty.
\(w_i>0\) and \(a_i>0\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}\sum_i w_i f_i(x)\neq\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}\sum_i w_i a_i f_i(x)\) characterizes the failure.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct finite weighted-sum invariance and failure definition
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind and statement match the leaf, and the finite weighted-sum claim is mathematically coherent. However, no inspectable citation is supplied for the scale-sensitivity characterization; the standard-field rationale alone does not satisfy the statement-review citation requirement.

children.title: Dominating-Weight Pathologies
children.top_down_role: Cases where extreme weights suppress otherwise meaningful optimization distinctions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient condition for one criterion to receive strict priority under a scalar weighted objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q(x)=w_kf_k(x)+g(x)\), where \(g(x)=\sum_{i\ne k}w_if_i(x)\), on a finite feasible set \(F\). Criterion \(k\) has strict priority under \(Q\), meaning \(f_k(x)<f_k(y)\Rightarrow Q(x)<Q(y)\) for all \(x,y\in F\), exactly when \[w_k\bigl(f_k(y)-f_k(x)\bigr)>g(x)-g(y)\] for every feasible pair satisfying \(f_k(x)<f_k(y)\). If \(w_i>0\), \(\delta_k\) is the smallest positive feasible gap of \(f_k\), and \(R_i=\max_F f_i-\min_F f_i\), then \(w_k\delta_k>\sum_{i\ne k}w_iR_i\) is a uniform sufficient certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A criterion has strict weighted priority exactly when its weighted improvement exceeds the actual compensation from all other criteria for every feasible pair; a gap-versus-range inequality is a compact sufficient test.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is finite.
All objective values and weights are finite.
For the range certificate, \(w_i>0\) and \(f_k\) assumes at least two distinct feasible values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_k(x)<f_k(y)\Rightarrow Q(x)<Q(y)\ \forall x,y\in F\iff w_k(f_k(y)-f_k(x))>g(x)-g(y)\) for every such pair.

notation.meaning: aggregate contribution of criteria other than k
smallest positive feasible gap of criterion k

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Pairwise Dominance Characterization
Dominating-Weight Pathologies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sufficient boundary at which one weighted criterion overrides every possible change in the remaining criteria.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be finite and consider minimizing \(\sum_{i=1}^p w_i f_i(x)\) over \(F\), with \(w_i>0\). For criterion \(k\), define its positive value gap \(\delta_k=\min\{|f_k(x)-f_k(y)|:x,y\in F,\ f_k(x)\neq f_k(y)\}\) and ranges \(R_i=\max_F f_i-\min_F f_i\). If \[w_k\delta_k>\sum_{i\neq k}w_iR_i,\] then every feasible improvement in \(f_k\) outweighs all possible deterioration in the other criteria. Thus the weighted objective imposes strict priority on criterion \(k\), whether or not that priority was intended.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sufficiently large weight makes any improvement in one criterion dominate every possible combined change in all other criteria.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is finite and \(f_k\) assumes at least two distinct values on \(F\).
\(w_i>0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(w_k\delta_k>\sum_{i\neq k}w_iR_i\) implies strict dominance of criterion \(k\).

notation.meaning: smallest positive feasible gap of criterion k
