intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite gap-versus-range inequality is a correct sufficient dominance condition, and failure_boundary is appropriate. An inspectable authoritative source with a section, theorem, or page locator is still required.

children.title: Priority-Semantics Mismatch
children.top_down_role: Disagreement between encoded weights and intended hierarchical priorities.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-assignment witness for unintended indifference or reversal under scalarization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{x,y\}\) with intended relation \(x\prec_P y\), and let \(f(x)=(0,1)\), \(f(y)=(1,0)\). For \(g_w=w_1f_1+w_2f_2\), equal weights give \(g_w(x)=g_w(y)\), while \(w_2>w_1\) gives \(g_w(x)>g_w(y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two conflicting criterion vectors exhibit both ways a scalar objective can violate a declared strict priority.
assumptions_latex: \(x\prec_P y\) is the declared strict preference.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(w_1=w_2\) causes unintended indifference, and \(w_2>w_1\) causes reversal.
knowledge_statements.title: Minimal Priority Tie and Reversal
Priority-Semantics Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of a scalar weighted objective to preserve the modeler’s declared priority order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\), let \(\prec_P\) be the intended strict priority relation on \(F\), and let \(g_w(x)=\sum_{i=1}^p w_i f_i(x)\) be minimized. A priority-semantics mismatch exists precisely when there are \(x,y\in F\) such that \[x\prec_P y\quad\text{and}\quad g_w(x)\ge g_w(y).\] The inequality includes both reversal and unintended indifference. Consequently, scalarization represents the declared priorities only if \(x\prec_P y\) implies \(g_w(x)<g_w(y)\) for every feasible pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mismatch occurs when the intended priority ranks one assignment higher but the weighted objective ties it with or ranks it below another.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) is nonempty.
\(\prec_P\) is the intended strict priority relation on \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists x,y\in F:\ x\prec_P y\ \land\ g_w(x)\ge g_w(y)\) is the mismatch predicate.

children.title: Lexicographic Boundary Cases
children.top_down_role: Regimes where scalar weighting inadequately represents strict priority levels.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Pairwise Criterion for Weighted Lexicographic Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-set boundary for a weighted sum to preserve every lexicographic comparison.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be finite and \(g_w=\sum_{i=1}^p w_i f_i\), with \(w_i>0\). For distinct \(x,y\in F\), let \(k(x,y)=\min\{i:f_i(x)\ne f_i(y)\}\). Then \(g_w\) represents the lexicographic order exactly if and only if, whenever \(f_k(x)<f_k(y)\) for \(k=k(x,y)\), \[w_k\bigl(f_k(y)-f_k(x)\bigr)>\sum_{j>k}w_j\bigl(f_j(x)-f_j(y)\bigr).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weighted sum exactly represents lexicographic order when every first-difference improvement outweighs the net adverse contribution of all lower-priority criteria for that feasible pair.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a nonempty finite set.
\(w_i>0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_w\) preserves every strict lexicographic comparison if and only if the displayed pairwise inequalities hold.

notation.meaning: first criterion on which x and y differ

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Pairwise Criterion for Weighted Lexicographic Representation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Two-Point Failure Below the Dominance Threshold
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal counterexample showing why a finite weight ratio need not enforce the first priority.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{a,b\}\), \((f_1(a),f_2(a))=(0,M)\), and \((f_1(b),f_2(b))=(\varepsilon,0)\), where \(M,\varepsilon>0\). Lexicographic minimization with \(f_1\) first selects \(a\). The weighted sum \(w_1f_1+w_2f_2\) selects \(b\) when \(w_1\varepsilon<w_2M\) and ties the points when equality holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lower-priority gain reverses or ties the lexicographic choice when the first-priority weight does not dominate the relevant feasible gap.
assumptions_latex: \(w_1,w_2,M,\varepsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(w_1\varepsilon\le w_2M\), the scalar objective fails to reproduce the strict lexicographic choice.
knowledge_statements.title: Two-Point Failure Below the Dominance Threshold

assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a nonempty finite set.
\(f_k:F\to\mathbb{R}\) for \(k=1,\ldots,p\), and \(w_k>0\) for every \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequalities \(w_k\delta_k>\sum_{j=k+1}^p w_jR_j\) for every nonconstant \(f_k\) with \(k<p\) suffice for the weighted sum to induce the lexicographic ordering on \(F\).

notation.meaning: minimum positive feasible gap of nonconstant criterion k
positive scalarization weight at priority level k

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite gap-versus-range lexicographic weighting bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-domain weight bounds separating exact lexicographic scalarization from possible priority failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a nonempty finite set, let \(f_k:F\to\mathbb{R}\) for \(k=1,\ldots,p\), and minimize \((f_1,\ldots,f_p)\) in lexicographic order with criterion \(1\) highest. For each nonconstant \(f_k\), define \(\delta_k=\min\{|f_k(x)-f_k(y)|:x,y\in F,\ f_k(x)\ne f_k(y)\}\), and for every \(j\) define \(R_j=\max_{x\in F}f_j(x)-\min_{x\in F}f_j(x)\). If \(w_k>0\) for every \(k\) and, for every nonconstant \(f_k\) with \(k<p\), \[w_k\delta_k>\sum_{j=k+1}^p w_jR_j,\] then minimizing \(\sum_{k=1}^p w_kf_k(x)\) induces exactly the lexicographic ordering on \(F\). If one of the applicable inequalities fails, exact lexicographic semantics are no longer guaranteed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a finite feasible set, gap-versus-range inequalities make a positive weighted sum reproduce lexicographic ordering. Constant criteria require no gap condition, and failure of an applicable inequality removes the guarantee.
knowledge_statements.title: Lexicographic Boundary Cases

assumptions_latex: \(E\) is a fixed instance-to-instance encoding map.
The binary input lengths satisfy \(|I_n|\to\infty\).
Input and output sizes include the binary lengths of encoded coefficients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(|E(I_n)|\) is not \(O(|I_n|^d)\) for any constant \(d\), then \(E\) is not a polynomial-size reformulation on \((I_n)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: asymptotic polynomial-size and exponential-size definitions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic loss of compactness when translating a Boolean optimization representation into another formalism.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed encoding map \(E\), let \(|I|\) be the binary length of an input instance and let \(|E(I)|\) be the binary length of the complete encoded output, including symbols and encoded coefficients. For an instance family \((I_n)\) with \(|I_n|\to\infty\), encoding-size blowup is superpolynomial when, for every constant \(d\ge 0\), \(|E(I_n)|\) is not \(O(|I_n|^d)\). Exponential blowup means that there is a constant \(c>0\) such that \(|E(I_n)|\ge 2^{c|I_n|}\) for infinitely many \(n\). A superpolynomial encoding is not a polynomial-size reformulation on that family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For input instances whose binary lengths grow without bound, an encoding has superpolynomial blowup when no fixed polynomial in the input length bounds the complete binary output length; the stated exponential lower bound is a stronger case.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pseudopolynomial boundary for binary-coded numerical data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If an encoding produces \Theta(W) symbols from a binary-coded nonnegative integer W, then its output is polynomial in the numerical value W but can be exponential in the input length m=\lceil\log_2(W+1)\rceil. On the family W=2^m-1, the output length is \Theta(2^m).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An encoding linear in a binary-coded number can still be exponentially large in the actual input length.
assumptions_latex: W is encoded in binary.
Output size counts all generated symbols.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: W=2^m-1\Longrightarrow\Theta(W)=\Theta(2^m).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closure rule distinguishing harmless staged encodings from size blowup.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let E_1 and E_2 be fixed encodings satisfying |E_1(I)|\le p(|I|) and |E_2(J)|\le q(|J|) for fixed polynomials p and q. Then |E_2(E_1(I))|\le q(p(|I|)), so their composition is polynomial-size. Hence a superpolynomial composed output implies that at least one stage lacks a polynomial bound relative to its immediate input on the induced family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polynomial-size encodings remain polynomial-size under composition; superpolynomial final growth must arise at some stage.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Existentially Exact Encoding with Missed Unit Consequence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Small Boolean example showing that existential solution equivalence does not imply propagation equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C(x)\equiv x\) and introduce an auxiliary variable \(y\). Define \(E(x,y)=(x\vee y)\wedge(x\vee\neg y)\). For every total assignment to \(x\), \(C(x)\iff\exists y\,E(x,y)\). Under the empty assignment neither clause is unit, so unit propagation derives neither \(x\) nor contradiction although \(C\models x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A two-clause auxiliary encoding of the unit constraint x preserves all solutions but unit propagation fails to infer x.
assumptions_latex: \(x,y\) are Boolean variables.
Unit propagation starts from the empty assignment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C(x)\iff\exists y\,E(x,y)\), but \(C\models x\) while unit propagation on \(E\) does not derive \(x\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates the two principal original-variable inference failures of an existentially exact CNF encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C(X)\) and \(E(X,Y)\) satisfy \(C(x)\iff\exists y\,E(x,y)\) for every total assignment \(x\). Relative to semantic consequences of \(C\), conflict weakness occurs if some partial assignment \(\alpha\) on \(X\) makes \(C\wedge\alpha\) unsatisfiable while unit propagation on \(E\wedge\alpha\) derives no contradiction. Literal weakness occurs if \(C\wedge\alpha\models\ell\) for an unassigned original-variable literal \(\ell\), while unit propagation derives neither \(\ell\) nor contradiction. Literal completeness implies conflict completeness by testing both values of an original variable, but conflict completeness alone need not derive every forced literal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A solution-exact encoding may be weak because unit propagation misses either an inconsistency or a forced original-variable literal.
assumptions_latex: \(C(x)\iff\exists y\,E(x,y)\) for every total assignment \(x\).
\(\alpha\) assigns only original variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Propagation weakness has distinct missed-conflict and missed-literal forms, with literal propagation strictly the stronger requirement in general.
knowledge_statements.title: Conflict and Literal Propagation Weakness
Weak-Propagation Encodings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical equivalence without preservation of deductions obtainable under partial assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C(X)\) be a Boolean constraint and let \(E(X,Y)\) be an existentially equivalent CNF encoding, so \(C(x)\) holds exactly when \(E(x,y)\) has an extension \(y\). The encoding is weakly propagating relative to a reference propagator \(P_C\) if some partial assignment \(\alpha\) on \(X\) makes \(P_C\) derive inconsistency or an original-variable literal \(\ell\), while unit propagation on \(E\) under \(\alpha\) derives neither inconsistency nor \(\ell\). Thus satisfiability preservation alone does not ensure preservation of inference strength.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weak encoding preserves solutions but unit propagation misses a contradiction or original-variable consequence detected by the source constraint’s propagator.
assumptions_latex: \(C(x)\iff\exists y\,E(x,y)\) for every total assignment \(x\).
\(\alpha\) assigns only variables in \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_C(\alpha)\) derives more on \(X\) than unit propagation on \(E\wedge\alpha\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal incompatibility caused by retaining a clause while changing an auxiliary variable's meaning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At stage 0 let y mean x_1\lor x_2 and retain the valid clause \neg x_1\lor y. If stage 1 reinterprets the same y as x_1\land x_2, then (x_1,x_2)=(1,0) requires y=0 under the new meaning but violates the retained clause. knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of an encoding to support constraint additions by monotone extension while retaining prior clauses and meanings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_0,C_1,\ldots\) be successively strengthened Boolean models on original variables \(X\), and let \(E_t(X,Y_t)\) encode \(C_t\). The encoding scheme is incrementally compatible when the auxiliary sets can be chosen with \(Y_t\subseteq Y_{t+1}\), retained auxiliary variables keep the same meanings, and, for every \(t\), there is a formula \(\Delta_t\) over \(X\cup Y_{t+1}\) such that \[E_{t+1}=E_t\wedge\Delta_t\] and \(C_{t+1}(x)\iff\exists y_{t+1}\,E_{t+1}(x,y_{t+1})\) for every total assignment \(x\) to \(X\). Incremental incompatibility occurs when these conditions fail at some stage unless retained clauses are deleted or modified or retained auxiliary variables are reinterpreted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An encoding is incrementally incompatible when some strengthened model cannot be encoded solely by adding constraints and possibly new auxiliary variables while preserving all retained clauses and auxiliary meanings.

children.title: Assignment Reconstruction Failures
children.top_down_role: Failures when mapping reduced or encoded solutions back to original variables.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence of some valid assignment decoder, distinct from correctness of a prescribed decoder and exact inversion of a forward reformulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\subseteq G\) be finite, and for each \(y\in H\) let \(K(y)\subseteq F\) contain exactly the original feasible assignments compatible with the information retained in \(y\). A decoder \(R:H\to F\) satisfying \(R(y)\in K(y)\) for every \(y\in H\) exists if and only if \(K(y)\neq\varnothing\) for every \(y\in H\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Some valid decoder exists exactly when every encoded assignment requiring recovery has a compatible original feasible assignment.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is finite.
\(K(y)\) is the compatibility fiber determined by the retained encoded information.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists R:H\to F\;\forall y\in H,\ R(y)\in K(y)\iff\forall y\in H,\ K(y)\neq\varnothing\).

knowledge_statements.title: Existential Assignment-Recovery Boundary

assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) and \(G\subseteq\{0,1\}^m\) are the original and encoded feasible sets.
\(R:G\rightharpoonup\{0,1\}^n\) is the prescribed, possibly partial reconstruction rule.
\(H\subseteq G\) is the set of encoded assignments for which reconstruction is required.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Reconstruction fails exactly when some \(y\in H\) has undefined, infeasible, or coordinate-inconsistent reconstructed output.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Encoded feasible or optimal assignments that cannot be decoded into valid original assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) be the original feasible set, let \(G\subseteq\{0,1\}^m\) be the encoded feasible set, and let \(H\subseteq G\) be the assignments for which reconstruction is required, with \(H=G\) for feasible-assignment reconstruction or \(H\) equal to the encoded optimum set for optimum-only reconstruction. Let \(R:G\rightharpoonup\{0,1\}^n\) be the prescribed reconstruction rule. Reconstruction succeeds when \(R\) is defined on every \(y\in H\), satisfies \(R(y)\in F\), and agrees with every original coordinate explicitly represented by \(y\). It fails when at least one of these conditions is violated for some \(y\in H\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reconstruction fails when an encoded assignment requiring reconstruction has no defined, feasible, and coordinate-consistent decoded assignment for the original model.
knowledge_statements.title: Assignment Reconstruction Failures

assumptions_latex: \(R:G\to F\) is a valid assignment decoder.
\(H\subseteq G\) is the set of encoded assignments for which objective values must be reconstructed.
Reconstruction may use only the retained datum \(h(y)\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure to recover original objective values from encoded solutions and retained encoded data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R:G\to F\) decode encoded feasible assignments, let \(H\subseteq G\) be the set for which objective-value reconstruction is required, let \(f:F\to\mathbb{R}\) be the original objective, and let \(h:G\to D\) be the retained encoded datum. Objective-value reconstruction on \(H\) succeeds when there is a function \(q:h(H)\to\mathbb{R}\) satisfying \(q(h(y))=f(R(y))\) for every \(y\in H\). It fails exactly when there are \(y_1,y_2\in H\) such that \(h(y_1)=h(y_2)\) but \(f(R(y_1))\ne f(R(y_2))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Objective-value reconstruction fails on the specified reconstruction domain when the same retained encoded datum corresponds to two different decoded original objective values.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Value Reconstruction Failures

children.title: Objective-Semantics Loss

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Optimizer Preservation Does Not Preserve Objective Semantics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite minimization example separating optimizer and optimum-value preservation from preservation of all preferences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=G=\{a,b,c\}\), let \(R\) be the identity, and define \(f(a)=0,f(b)=1,f(c)=2\) and \(g(a)=0,g(b)=2,g(c)=1\). Both objectives have unique minimizer \(a\) and optimum value \(0\), but \(f(b)<f(c)\) while \(g(b)>g(c)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two objectives can share their unique optimizer and optimum value while reversing the ranking of nonoptimal assignments.
assumptions_latex: Both objectives are minimized.
The decoder is the identity on the three feasible assignments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}f=\operatorname*{argmin}g=\{a\}\) and \(\min f=\min g=0\), but the induced preorders differ.
knowledge_statements.title: Optimizer Preservation Does Not Preserve Objective Semantics
Objective-Semantics Loss
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A reformulation that fails to preserve the original preference ordering among represented assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the original feasible set, let \(G\) be a reformulated feasible set, and let \(R:G\to F\) be a surjective decoder. For original objective \(f\) and reformulated objective \(g\), minimization semantics are preserved when, for all \(y_1,y_2\in G\), \[f(R(y_1))<f(R(y_2))\iff g(y_1)<g(y_2),\] with equality preserved as well. Objective-semantics loss occurs when some pair violates either equivalence, even if feasibility or the reported optimum value remains preserved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Objective semantics are lost when the reformulated objective reverses, collapses, or invents a preference between decoded original assignments.
assumptions_latex: \(R:G\to F\) is a surjective feasible-assignment decoder.
Both objectives use minimization convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A disagreement between the preorders induced by \(f\circ R\) and \(g\) constitutes semantics loss.

children.title: Noninvertible Reformulation Boundary
children.top_down_role: Transformations lacking sufficient information for faithful solution recovery.

knowledge_statements.title: Noninvertible Reformulation Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary at which a reformulation no longer permits recovery of the represented original assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:F\to G\) map original feasible assignments into reformulated assignments. Exact assignment recovery requires a decoder \(R:G\to F\) satisfying \(R(T(x))=x\) for every \(x\in F\). Such a left inverse exists on \(T(F)\) exactly when \(T\) is injective. Hence the noninvertible boundary is crossed when distinct \(x_1,x_2\in F\) satisfy \(T(x_1)=T(x_2)\); no decoder using only the reformulated assignment can then reconstruct both originals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reformulation becomes noninvertible when two distinct original assignments have the same reformulated image, making exact recovery impossible.
assumptions_latex: \(T:F\to G\) is the assignment transformation.
The decoder receives only \(T(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists x_1\neq x_2:\ T(x_1)=T(x_2)\) if and only if no left inverse exists on the image.

children.title: Large Unsatisfiable Cores
children.top_down_role: Core-guided search regimes dominated by cores containing many soft constraints.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic criterion for an unsatisfiable family in which no small core exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite unsatisfiable clause set \(F\), define \(\mu(F)=\min\{|U|:U\subseteq F,\ U\text{ is unsatisfiable}\}\). A family \((F_n)\) has unavoidable core size at least \(s(n)\) when \(\mu(F_n)\ge s(n)\). Equivalently, every subset of \(F_n\) with fewer than \(s(n)\) clauses is satisfiable. Thus extracting one large nonminimal core does not by itself establish unavoidable large-core behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A family has unavoidable large cores when its smallest unsatisfiable subset grows, not merely when one extractor returns a large core.
assumptions_latex: Each \(F_n\) is a finite unsatisfiable clause set.
A core is any unsatisfiable subset of the clause set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mu(F_n)\ge s(n)\iff\forall V\subseteq F_n,\ |V|<s(n)\Rightarrow V\text{ is satisfiable}.\)

notation.meaning: minimum cardinality of an unsatisfiable core of F
claimed lower bound on unavoidable core size

knowledge_statements.title: Unavoidable Core Size
Large Unsatisfiable Cores
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unsatisfiable families for which every core necessarily contains a growing number of clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(n\ge 1\), define the CNF formula \[F_n=(x_1)\wedge\bigwedge_{i=1}^{n-1}(\neg x_i\vee x_{i+1})\wedge(\neg x_n).\] The formula is minimally unsatisfiable: it is unsatisfiable, but deleting any one of its \(n+1\) clauses makes it satisfiable. Therefore its only unsatisfiable core is the complete clause set, of size \(n+1\). This family exhibits a linear core-size boundary and supplies no small core for a core-guided exact-search step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A chain of implications between contradictory endpoint units is minimally unsatisfiable, so every unsatisfiable core contains all n+1 clauses.
assumptions_latex: A core is a subset of clauses that is itself unsatisfiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every unsatisfiable core of \(F_n\) has size \(n+1\).

notation.meaning: Boolean variables in the implication chain

children.title: Noninformative Unsatisfiable Cores
children.top_down_role: Cores that provide weak discrimination among objective choices.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact implication test and LP certificate for redundancy of a proposed core inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be the current master-feasible set and \(U\) a proposed core. The inequality \(\sum_{i\in U}y_i\ge1\) is redundant on \(P\) exactly when \(\inf_{y\in P}\sum_{i\in U}y_i\ge1\). If \(P=\{y:Ay\ge b,\ y\ge0\}\) is a nonempty polyhedron, any \(\lambda\ge0\) satisfying \(A^T\lambda\le\mathbf1_U\) and \(b^T\lambda\ge1\) certifies redundancy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A core is noninformative precisely when minimizing its hitting-inequality left side over the existing master gives a value of at least one; an LP dual vector can certify this.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is the master-feasible set before the proposed inequality is added.
The auxiliary minimization is solved or globally bounded on the domain for which implication is claimed.
For the dual certificate, \(P\) has the displayed linear form and is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{i\in U}y_i\ge1\text{ on }P\iff\inf_{y\in P}\sum_{i\in U}y_i\ge1\).

notation.meaning: incidence vector of the proposed core

knowledge_statements.title: Optimization Test for Core Redundancy
Noninformative Unsatisfiable Cores
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Redundancy boundary for cores supplied to a hitting-set master problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal C\) be the cores already known to a hitting-set master with relaxation variables \(y_i\in[0,1]\), and let \(U\) be a newly returned unsatisfiable core. The core inequality is \(\sum_{i\in U}y_i\geq 1\). Call \(U\) noninformative relative to \(\mathcal C\) when this inequality is implied by \(\{\sum_{i\in C}y_i\geq1:C\in\mathcal C\}\) together with the master constraints. In particular, if some \(C\in\mathcal C\) satisfies \(C\subseteq U\), then the new inequality is dominated and removes no master-feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A core is noninformative when its hitting constraint is already implied by previous core constraints; any core containing a previously known core has this defect.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) and every \(C\in\mathcal C\) index relaxable Boolean constraints.
\(y_i\geq0\) for every relaxation variable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C\subseteq U\) for some \(C\in\mathcal C\) implies that \(U\)'s core inequality does not strengthen the master feasible region.

notation.meaning: indicator or relaxation variable for removing constraint i

children.title: Core-Minimization Pressure
children.top_down_role: Cost versus utility considerations surrounding smaller extracted cores.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes deletion-based shrinking from minimum-cardinality core extraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U=\{(x),(
eg x),(y),(
eg y\vee z),(
eg z)\}\). It contains inclusion-minimal unsatisfiable subcores \(U_2=\{(x),(
eg x)\}\) and \(U_3=\{(y),(
eg y\vee z),(
eg z)\}\), of cardinalities two and three. A deletion pass that first removes the two \(x\)-clauses can return \(U_3\), whereas another deletion order can return \(U_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Disjoint unsatisfiable subcores of sizes two and three show that deletion-based shrinking can return a larger inclusion-minimal core depending on deletion order.
assumptions_latex: The satisfiability oracle is exact.
Deletion tests use the current surviving clause set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U_2\) and \(U_3\) are inclusion-minimal and \(|U_2|<|U_3|\); deletion order may select either.

notation.meaning: inclusion-minimal unsatisfiable subcores of different sizes

knowledge_statements.title: Inclusion-Minimal Is Not Minimum-Cardinality
Core-Minimization Pressure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle burden incurred when shrinking an extracted core to inclusion minimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an unsatisfiable core \(U=\{c_1,\ldots,c_m\}\), deletion-based minimization tests each surviving constraint by querying whether the current set without that constraint remains unsatisfiable. One complete pass uses at most \(m\) additional satisfiability-oracle calls and returns an inclusion-minimal core if every deletion is tested against the current surviving set. Thus, if core extraction occurs in \(K\) outer iterations, eager minimization can add at most \(\sum_{k=1}^{K}|U_k|\) oracle calls, creating pressure whenever oracle time dominates master-solution time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deletion-based core minimization costs at most one extra satisfiability query per member of each extracted core, potentially dominating the outer exact-search loop.
assumptions_latex: The oracle decides satisfiability exactly.
A constraint, once deleted successfully, remains deleted during the pass.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The additional oracle-call count is at most \(\sum_{k=1}^{K}|U_k|\).

notation.meaning: core extracted at outer iteration k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The deletion-based oracle-call bound and inclusion-minimality claim are plausible and the complexity-bound kind fits, but they require an authoritative algorithm locator.

children.title: Core-Quality Search Impact
children.top_down_role: Effects of core size and relevance on bound progress or master-problem growth.

knowledge_statements.title: Core-Quality Search Impact
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dominance relation connecting core inclusion with master-relaxation strength.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonnegative master variables \(y_i\), let cores \(U'\subseteq U\) induce inequalities \(\sum_{i\in U'}y_i\geq1\) and \(\sum_{i\in U}y_i\geq1\). The first inequality implies the second and therefore defines a master feasible region contained in that defined by the second. Consequently, replacing a core by an unsatisfiable subcore cannot weaken the hitting-set master relaxation. This ordering concerns relaxation strength only: it does not by itself guarantee fewer iterations or lower runtime, because obtaining the smaller core may require additional oracle work.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smaller unsatisfiable subcore gives a dominating hitting constraint, but the stronger master relaxation may not repay the cost of finding that subcore.
assumptions_latex: \(U'\subseteq U\) and both sets are unsatisfiable cores.
\(y_i\geq0\) for all indexed master variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{y:\sum_{i\in U'}y_i\geq1\}\subseteq\{y:\sum_{i\in U}y_i\geq1\}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The nested-core dominance property is correct for nonnegative variables, but the record provides no source for its core-guided search interpretation.

knowledge_statements.title: Overlapping-Core Stagnation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-search regime where successive cores provide little independent master information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a core sequence \(U_1,U_2,\ldots\), define the novelty of iteration \(k\) by \(\nu_k=|U_k\setminus\bigcup_{j<k}U_j|\). An overlapping-core stagnation regime occurs on an interval \(I\) when \(\nu_k\leq r\) for every \(k\in I\), while each new core inequality is necessary to exclude the current master solution. Even with \(r=0\), distinct nondominated cores may continue to arrive, so bounded novelty does not bound the number of oracle iterations. Heavy overlap is therefore a failure boundary for progress measures based only on newly exposed constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Search stagnates when successive necessary cores mostly reuse old constraints; even zero new variables does not limit the number of distinct cores or iterations.
assumptions_latex: Each \(U_k\) is an unsatisfiable core returned against the current master solution.
The master retains all preceding core inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A uniform bound \(\nu_k\leq r\) alone gives no finite bound on the number of distinct core-generation iterations.

notation.meaning: number of previously unseen core members

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed novelty measure is coherent, but the named stagnation regime and the iteration implication are domain-specific claims without supporting evidence.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pseudopolynomial bound for residual-weight extraction with separately retained fragments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose original constraint \(i\) has positive integer weight \(W_i\). Each time a core-guided extraction involves its residual fragment, subtract a positive integer \(\delta\), retain the extracted amount as a separate fragment, and never recreate consumed residual weight. Then the number \(t_i\) of positive extractions involving that residual satisfies \(t_i\le W_i\). Thus constraint \(i\) creates at most \(W_i\) extracted fragments and at most one residual fragment, and \(N_{\mathrm{frag}}\le\sum_i(W_i+1)\). This bound is pseudopolynomial and need not be polynomial in the binary encoding length of the weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With integer weights, each extraction consumes at least one unit, bounding fragmentation by the numerical weight sum but not by its binary length.
assumptions_latex: \(W_i\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\) for every original weighted constraint.
Every extraction subtracts an integer \(\delta\ge1\) from the residual fragment.
Extracted fragments remain separate, and consumed weight is not recreated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(t_i\le W_i\quad\text{and}\quad N_{\mathrm{frag}}\le\sum_i(W_i+1)\).

notation.meaning: original integer weight of constraint i
number of positive residual extractions involving constraint i

knowledge_statements.title: Integral-Weight Fragment Bound
Weighted-Core Fragmentation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bookkeeping growth caused by repeated weight splitting in weighted core-guided search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a weighted core \(U\) contains residual weights \(w_i>0\), and a core-guided step extracts \(\delta=\min_{i\in U}w_i\), replaces each residual weight by \(w_i-\delta\), and represents the extracted amount in a new relaxation layer. Weighted-core fragmentation occurs when repeated extractions split one original weighted constraint into many positive-weight layers. After \(t_i\) distinct positive extractions involving original constraint \(i\), its representation may contain \(t_i\) extracted fragments plus one residual fragment; hence total fragment count can grow as \(\sum_i(t_i+1)\), even though the original constraint count is fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated minimum-weight extraction can split each original weighted constraint into many layers, enlarging the encoded instance without adding original constraints.
assumptions_latex: All weights are positive integers or positive rationals represented exactly.
Each extraction preserves separate relaxation layers rather than immediately merging equivalent fragments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The fragment count can scale with \(\sum_i t_i\), independently of the number of original constraints.

notation.meaning: current residual weight of original constraint i
minimum residual weight extracted from a core
number of positive extractions involving constraint i

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Explicit Exponential Family of Minimal Cores
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Indexed-clause construction witnessing exponentially many minimal relaxable cores.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(n\ge1\), let the fixed hard formula contain \(D=(\neg x_1\vee\cdots\vee\neg x_n)\). For every \(i\), introduce two separately indexed relaxable clauses \(A_i^0=(x_i)\) and \(A_i^1=(x_i)\). For each \(\sigma\in\{0,1\}^n\), the indexed set \(U_\sigma=\{A_i^{\sigma_i}:1\le i\le n\}\) is a minimal relaxable core relative to \(D\). These are \(2^n\) distinct cores among \(m=2n\) relaxable constraints, so any explicit complete enumeration has output size and running time \(2^{\Omega(m)}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One hard negative clause and two indexed copies of each positive unit clause produce exponentially many distinct minimal cores.
assumptions_latex: Differently indexed clause occurrences are distinct relaxable constraints even when their clauses are identical.
Each core is evaluated together with the fixed hard formula.
Output cores are represented explicitly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\ge2^n=2^{m/2}\), hence complete explicit enumeration requires \(\Omega(M)=2^{\Omega(m)}\) output time.

notation.meaning: indexed relaxable copy of unit clause x_i
minimal core selected by binary vector sigma

knowledge_statements.title: Explicit Exponential Family of Minimal Cores
Core-Enumeration Explosion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Output-size boundary for methods that explicitly enumerate distinct minimal cores.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an instance with \(m\) relaxable constraints, every minimal unsatisfiable core is a distinct subset of the constraint index set, so their number \(M\) satisfies \(M\leq2^m\). Boolean instances exist whose number of minimal unsatisfiable cores is exponential in \(m\). Therefore, any procedure required to output every minimal core has worst-case running time \(\Omega(M)\) and worst-case exponential output size, regardless of the delay between consecutive cores. Exact search that waits for complete core enumeration consequently has no polynomial worst-case bound in the input size alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimal cores can be exponentially numerous, so explicitly listing all of them necessarily has exponential worst-case output and runtime.
assumptions_latex: Cores are represented explicitly as subsets of \(m\) relaxable constraints.
Writing one output core requires at least one unit of time.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Complete enumeration requires \(\Omega(M)\) time, and \(M\) can be \(2^{\Omega(m)}\).

notation.meaning: number of distinct minimal unsatisfiable cores

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The output-sensitive lower bound is valid, and the complexity-bound kind fits, but the existence of exponentially many minimal unsatisfiable cores requires an authoritative construction or theorem locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Hitting-Set Master–Oracle Imbalance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Runtime imbalance between master optimization and satisfiability-oracle phases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In iteration \(k\) of a hitting-set exact-search method, let \(T_M(k)\) be the time to solve the accumulated weighted hitting-set master and \(T_O(k)\) the time for the Boolean oracle to test the selected residual instance and return a core when infeasible. For a threshold \(\rho>1\), master–oracle imbalance occurs when either \(T_M(k)\geq\rho T_O(k)\) or \(T_O(k)\geq\rho T_M(k)\) throughout a sustained iteration interval. The total time on that interval is then controlled, up to a factor \(1+1/\rho\), by the dominant phase, so accelerating only the subordinate phase yields limited end-to-end improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When master or oracle time persistently exceeds the other by a large factor, total runtime is essentially controlled by the dominant phase.
assumptions_latex: Master and oracle phases execute sequentially in each measured iteration.
Bookkeeping time is excluded or negligible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(T_M(k)\geq\rho T_O(k)\), then \(T_M(k)+T_O(k)\leq(1+1/\rho)T_M(k)\), with the symmetric result when the oracle dominates.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The timing inequality is elementary and correct, but the sustained-interval definition and its placement in a hitting-set exact-search workflow need domain evidence.

children.title: Coefficient-Growth Regimes
children.top_down_role: Derivations or transformations that produce rapidly increasing coefficients.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coefficient Growth Under Nonnegative Linear Combination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step magnitude and bit-length accounting for a standard pseudo-Boolean derivation operation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let inequalities \(P_r\) have coefficients and right-hand sides of magnitude at most \(B_r\), and form \(Q=\sum_{r=1}^m\lambda_rP_r\) with nonnegative integer multipliers \(\lambda_r\). Every coefficient and the right-hand side of \(Q\) have magnitude at most \(\sum_r\lambda_rB_r\). If \(B_r\le B\) and \(\lambda_r\le\Lambda\), the magnitude is at most \(m\Lambda B\), and its binary length is at most \(\lceil\log_2(m\Lambda B+1)\rceil\), apart from any separately stored sign bit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative linear-combination step grows magnitude by at most the weighted sum of premise bounds, so multiplier size is part of exact bit-length accounting.
assumptions_latex: Premise coefficients, right-hand sides, and multipliers are integers.
\(\lambda_r\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_Q\le\sum_r\lambda_rB_r\le m\Lambda B\).

notation.meaning: largest absolute coefficient or right-hand-side magnitude in the derived inequality

knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient Growth Under Nonnegative Linear Combination
Coefficient-Growth Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bit-length boundary for exact pseudo-Boolean derivations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider an exact pseudo-Boolean derivation whose \(t\)-th inequality has integer coefficients and right-hand side bounded in magnitude by \(B_t\). Define its arithmetic length by \(L_t=\lceil\log_2(B_t+1)\rceil\). A coefficient-growth regime occurs when \(\max_{t\leq T}L_t\) is superpolynomial in the input encoding length, or exceeds a prescribed machine-word bound. In that regime, counting proof steps alone does not give a polynomial-time implementation: every exact representation of a largest coefficient needs \(\Omega(L_t)\) bits, and arithmetic, storage, and comparison costs must be charged in bit complexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pseudo-Boolean derivation enters coefficient growth when coefficient bit lengths become superpolynomial or exceed machine words, invalidating unit-cost arithmetic estimates.
assumptions_latex: All derived coefficients and right-hand sides are represented exactly as integers.
Input size is measured by binary encoding length.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any exact implementation storing a magnitude-\(B_t\) coefficient requires \(\Omega(L_t)\) bits.

notation.meaning: largest coefficient or right-hand-side magnitude at step t

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bit-length boundary is mathematically coherent and appropriately classified as a failure boundary, but its pseudo-Boolean derivation context lacks a supporting locator.

children.title: Arithmetic-Precision Pressure
children.top_down_role: Reliability pressure arising from large or heterogeneous numeric magnitudes.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fixed-Width Wraparound Changes a Pseudo-Boolean Test
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete semantic failure caused by unchecked unsigned arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(200x_1+100x_2\ge250\) with \(x_1,x_2\in\{0,1\}\). At \((x_1,x_2)=(1,1)\), exact arithmetic gives \(300\ge250\). If the sum is accumulated in unchecked unsigned 8-bit arithmetic, it wraps to \(300\bmod256=44\), so the implementation instead evaluates \(44\ge250\) as false.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unchecked 8-bit wraparound rejects an assignment satisfying the exact pseudo-Boolean inequality.
assumptions_latex: Intermediate addition uses unsigned arithmetic modulo \(256\).
The comparison is performed after the wrapped accumulation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The fixed-width evaluation disagrees with exact integer semantics at \((1,1)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Width Wraparound Changes a Pseudo-Boolean Test
Arithmetic-Precision Pressure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactness boundary for fixed-width and floating-point pseudo-Boolean arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an implementation manipulate integer pseudo-Boolean coefficients of magnitude at most \(B\). Unsigned \(w\)-bit arithmetic cannot represent all such coefficients when \(B\geq2^w\). Likewise, binary floating-point with \(p\) significand bits cannot represent every integer exactly once \(B>2^p\). Beyond either boundary, unchecked arithmetic may change a derived inequality through overflow or rounding. Exact soundness then requires wider integers, arbitrary-precision arithmetic, or a separately verified rounding rule that guarantees the emitted inequality remains logically implied by its premises.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coefficients beyond fixed-width or exact floating-point ranges create overflow or rounding risk, requiring wider exact arithmetic or verified sound rounding.
assumptions_latex: Coefficients are nonnegative integers.
The implementation must preserve logical implication of every derivation step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(B\geq2^w\) or \(B>2^p\), the corresponding native representation does not exactly cover all admissible coefficients.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed-width and binary floating-point exactness thresholds are correctly stated under the assumptions, but no authoritative numerical-arithmetic source is cited.

children.title: Arithmetic-Cost Pressure
children.top_down_role: Runtime and memory burdens attributable to expensive coefficient operations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Encoded-Derivation Storage and Verification Lower Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arithmetic cost measured over the complete binary encoding of a pseudo-Boolean derivation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a derivation with explicitly encoded steps \(P_1,\ldots,P_T\), let \(S=\sum_{t=1}^T|\operatorname{enc}(P_t)|\). Storing the complete encoding requires \(\Omega(S)\) bits, and any verifier required to read every encoded coefficient and right-hand side uses \(\Omega(S)\) bit operations. Thus a polynomial number of inference steps does not imply polynomial encoded size or full-verification time when \(S\) is superpolynomial in the input length.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Total encoded arithmetic length, rather than step count alone, lower-bounds explicit proof storage and full verification time.
assumptions_latex: The complete derivation is represented explicitly in binary.
The verifier is required to inspect every encoded arithmetic datum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathrm{storage}=\Omega(S)\) and \(\mathrm{verification\ time}=\Omega(S)\).

notation.meaning: total binary encoding length of the derivation

knowledge_statements.title: Encoded-Derivation Storage and Verification Lower Bound
Arithmetic-Cost Pressure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bit-operation cost hidden by unit-cost pseudo-Boolean reasoning models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an exact pseudo-Boolean step reads or writes integers of maximum binary length \(L\). Merely scanning such an operand costs \(\Omega(L)\) bit operations. Addition and comparison admit \(O(L)\) bit complexity, while multiplication costs \(M(L)\), where \(M(L)\geq\Omega(L)\) denotes the chosen integer-multiplication bound. Hence a derivation of \(T\) nominal inference steps has an unavoidable \(\Omega(TL)\) bit-cost lower bound when every step processes an \(L\)-bit coefficient. Large coefficients can therefore make a short inference sequence expensive even when the number of Boolean variables remains unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact reasoning on L-bit coefficients costs at least linear time in L per processed step, so short proofs can still be arithmetically expensive.
assumptions_latex: Integers use a standard binary representation.
Each of the \(T\) counted steps processes at least one \(L\)-bit operand.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The derivation requires \(\Omega(TL)\) bit operations under the stated access model.

notation.meaning: bit complexity of multiplying L-bit integers

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional lower bound follows from the stated access model and the complexity-bound kind fits, but an authoritative bit-complexity source is required.

children.title: Coefficient-Control Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Inference-strength consequences of limiting, reducing, or saturating coefficients.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical exact coefficient cap for nonnegative pseudo-Boolean inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be \(\sum_{i=1}^n a_i\ell_i\ge b\), with \(a_i\ge0\), \(b>0\), and \(\ell_i\in\{0,1\}\). Replacing every coefficient by \(a_i'=\min\{a_i,b\}\) preserves all Boolean models: \[\sum_i a_i\ell_i\ge b\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\sum_i a_i'\ell_i\ge b.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a nonnegative threshold inequality, capping each coefficient at the threshold is exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Threshold saturation preserves the represented Boolean constraint exactly.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Saturation at the Threshold

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coefficient reduction preserving an integral pseudo-Boolean inequality exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be \(\sum_{i=1}^n a_i\ell_i\ge b\), where \(a_i\in\mathbb Z\), \(\ell_i\in\{0,1\}\), and a positive integer \(d\) divides every \(a_i\). Then \[\sum_i a_i\ell_i\ge b\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\sum_i(a_i/d)\ell_i\ge\lceil b/d\rceil.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A common coefficient divisor can be removed exactly when the threshold is divided and rounded upward.
assumptions_latex: \(d>0\) divides every coefficient \(a_i\).
All literals and data are integral.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The original and normalized inequalities have identical Boolean models.

notation.meaning: common positive divisor of all coefficients

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Common-Divisor Normalization
Coefficient-Control Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound coefficient reduction trades arithmetic size against inferential strength.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be a pseudo-Boolean inequality and let \(R(P)\) be a coefficient-controlled inequality such that every Boolean assignment satisfying \(P\) also satisfies \(R(P)\). Replacing \(P\) by \(R(P)\) is sound, but if the implication is strict then there exists a Boolean assignment satisfying \(R(P)\) and violating \(P\); the replacement has lost exclusion or propagation strength. Coefficient control is therefore exact only when \(P\) and \(R(P)\) are equivalent on \(\{0,1\}^n\). Otherwise, smaller coefficients must be evaluated against the additional assignments admitted by the reduced inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sound reduced-coefficient inequality may be strictly weaker; coefficient control preserves all strength exactly only when both inequalities have identical Boolean models.
assumptions_latex: \(P\Rightarrow R(P)\) holds for every assignment in \(\{0,1\}^n\).
Coefficient size is measured in binary encoding.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(R(P)\not\Rightarrow P\), coefficient reduction admits at least one Boolean assignment excluded by \(P\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The implication/equivalence tradeoff is logically correct and fits a principle container, but its pseudo-Boolean coefficient-control interpretation is unsupported by a citation.

children.title: Weakening Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Constraint simplification regimes balancing compactness against inference strength.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical weakening obtained by deleting any set of nonnegative terms and compensating the threshold by their total coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C:\sum_{i=1}^n a_i\ell_i\ge b\), where \(a_i\ge0\) and \(\ell_i\in\{0,1\}\). For any \(J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\), define \[W_J(C):\sum_{i\notin J}a_i\ell_i\ge b-\sum_{j\in J}a_j.\] Then \(C\models W_J(C)\). The converse can fail: from \(3x+2y\ge4\), deleting the term \(3x\) gives \(2y\ge1\), which is satisfied by \((x,y)=(0,1)\) although the original inequality is violated. The representation loses exactly the \(|J|\) deleted literal occurrences before any serialization-dependent simplification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deleting nonnegative terms and lowering the threshold by their total coefficients is sound but can strictly weaken the constraint; single-literal weakening is the case where the deleted set has size one.
assumptions_latex: a_i\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}.
J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C\models W_J(C),\quad\text{while generally }W_J(C)\not\models C.

notation.meaning: Constraint obtained by deleting terms indexed by J and lowering the threshold by their total coefficients.

knowledge_statements.title: Compensated Literal-Set Weakening
Weakening Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound division rule illustrating coefficient reduction with possible loss of strength.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For Boolean variables \(x_i\in\{0,1\}\), nonnegative integers \(a_i,b\), and integer \(d\geq1\), the inequality \(\sum_i a_i x_i\geq b\) implies the divided inequality \(\sum_i\lceil a_i/d\rceil x_i\geq\lceil b/d\rceil\). The converse need not hold, so division can reduce coefficients while weakening the constraint. For example, \(3x+3y\geq4\) divided by \(d=2\) yields \(2x+2y\geq2\); assignment \((x,y)=(1,0)\) satisfies the divided inequality but violates the original one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ceiling division gives a valid reduced-coefficient inequality, but it may admit Boolean assignments excluded by the original constraint.
assumptions_latex: \(a_i,b\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\) and \(d\in\mathbb Z_{\geq1}\).
\(x_i\in\{0,1\}\) for every index.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_i a_i x_i\geq b\Rightarrow\sum_i\lceil a_i/d\rceil x_i\geq\lceil b/d\rceil\), while the reverse implication can fail.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The ceiling-division implication and counterexample are correct, and the property kind fits the leaf, but the pseudo-Boolean division rule requires an authoritative locator.

children.title: Division Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Coefficient-reduction regimes with implications for learned-constraint utility.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lossless division distinguished from rounded coefficient reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be \(\sum_{i=1}^n a_i\ell_i\ge b\), where \(a_i,b\in\mathbb Z\), \(\ell_i\in\{0,1\}\), and \(d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\) divides every \(a_i\) and \(b\). Then \[\sum_i a_i\ell_i\ge b\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\sum_i(a_i/d)\ell_i\ge b/d.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dividing every coefficient and the threshold by a common positive divisor is an equivalent normalization rather than a weakening.
assumptions_latex: d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}.
d\mid a_i\text{ for every }i\text{ and }d\mid b.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C\equiv C/d.

notation.meaning: Constraint obtained by exact division of every coefficient and the right-hand side by d.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Common-Divisor Reduction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal witness of information loss under ceiling division.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C:x+2y\ge2\) and \(d=2\). Then \(D_2(C)\) is \(x+y\ge1\). The assignment \((x,y)=(1,0)\) satisfies \(D_2(C)\) but violates \(C\), so the rounded division is strictly weaker.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ceiling-dividing x+2y≥2 by two yields x+y≥1, which admits x=1,y=0 although the original inequality does not.
assumptions_latex: Division uses the ceiling rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D_2(C)\not\models C.

notation.meaning: Assignment admitted by the divided inequality but excluded by the original

knowledge_statements.title: Residue-Induced Strict Weakening

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical rounded division for positive-coefficient pseudo-Boolean inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(C:\sum_{i=1}^n a_i\ell_i\ge b\), where \(a_i,b\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), \(\ell_i\in\{0,1\}\), and \(d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), define \[D_d(C):\quad \sum_{i=1}^n\left\lceil\frac{a_i}{d}\right\rceil\ell_i\ge\left\lceil\frac{b}{d}\right\rceil.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ceiling division divides each positive coefficient and the threshold by a positive integer and rounds every quotient upward.
assumptions_latex: \(a_i,b,d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\).
\(\ell_i\in\{0,1\}\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D_d(C)=\left\{\sum_i\lceil a_i/d\rceil\ell_i\ge\lceil b/d\rceil\right\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Ceiling Division Rule

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numeric-size effect of ceiling division under binary coefficient serialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every positive integer \(t\) and divisor \(d\), \[1\le\left\lceil\frac{t}{d}\right\rceil\le t,\qquad \left\lceil\frac{t}{d}\right\rceil\le\frac{t+d-1}{d}.\] Thus ceiling division does not increase any positive coefficient or the positive threshold, nor their ordinary binary bit lengths. If \(d>1\) and \(t>1\), then \(\lceil t/d\rceil<t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ceiling division never increases positive coefficients, the threshold, or their binary lengths, and strictly reduces every value greater than one when the divisor exceeds one.
assumptions_latex: \(t,d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\).
Values are serialized as ordinary positive binary integers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{bitlen}(\lceil t/d\rceil)\le\operatorname{bitlen}(t).
knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient-Magnitude Contraction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Entailment guarantee for the explicitly defined rounded division rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every positive-coefficient pseudo-Boolean inequality \(C:\sum_i a_i\ell_i\ge b\) and every positive integer \(d\), \[C\models D_d(C).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every Boolean assignment satisfying the original positive-coefficient inequality also satisfies its ceiling-divided consequence.
assumptions_latex: \(a_i,b,d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\).
\(D_d\) is the ceiling division rule defined in this topic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C\models D_d(C).

notation.meaning: Every Boolean model of C is a model of its ceiling division

knowledge_statements.title: Soundness of Ceiling Division

assumptions_latex: \(C:\sum_{i=1}^n a_i\ell_i\ge b\) has integer coefficients and Boolean literals \(\ell_i\in\{0,1\}\).
\(d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\) is the chosen divisor.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The rounded divided constraint may be weaker than the exact rational rescaling, while coefficient and proof-arithmetic sizes decrease.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covers strength-versus-size effects of sound division with outward integer rounding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be \(\sum_{i=1}^n a_i\ell_i\ge b\), with \(a_i,b\in\mathbb Z\), and let \(d>0\). A sound division rule replaces \(C\) by an integer-rounded consequence \(D_d(C)\). Division reduces coefficient magnitudes approximately by \(d\), but rounding discards residue information whenever some \(a_i\) or \(b\) is not divisible by \(d\). Consequently, \(C\models D_d(C)\), whereas generally \(D_d(C)\not\models C\); propagation or conflict strength can therefore decrease despite cheaper arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Division shrinks coefficients and proof arithmetic, but rounding away nondivisible residues can weaken propagation and conflict information even when the reduced constraint remains sound.
knowledge_statements.title: Division Tradeoffs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is cited. The exact soundness and information-loss claims depend on the division rule's coefficient and right-hand-side rounding conventions, which are not defined precisely enough to validate C entails D_d(C) or the claimed propagation tradeoff.

children.title: Saturation Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Coefficient-capping regimes balancing numeric control against retained structure.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Idempotence and Scale Equivariance of Threshold Saturation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural properties of coefficient capping for nonnegative PB inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(C:\sum_i a_i\ell_i\ge b\) with \(a_i\ge0\) and \(b>0\), define \(S_b(a_i)=\min\{a_i,b\}\). Then \(S_b(S_b(a_i))=S_b(a_i)\). Moreover, for every \(k\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), \[S_{kb}(ka_i)=kS_b(a_i).\] Thus repeated saturation makes no further change, and positive integral scaling commutes with threshold saturation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Threshold saturation is idempotent and commutes with positive integral scaling of the entire inequality.
assumptions_latex: a_i\ge0\text{ for every }i.
k\in\mathbb Z_{>0}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S_b\circ S_b=S_b\quad\text{and}\quad S_{kb}(ka_i)=kS_b(a_i).
knowledge_statements.title: Idempotence and Scale Equivariance of Threshold Saturation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Saturation Can Erase Coefficient-Based Branching Priorities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete information-loss witness for a specified coefficient-scoring operation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(C:7x+5y+z\ge4\), let \(\sigma_C(v)\) equal the coefficient of literal \(v\) in \(C\). Then \(\sigma_C(x)=7>5=\sigma_C(y)\). Threshold saturation gives \(S(C):4x+4y+z\ge4\), for which \(\sigma_{S(C)}(x)=\sigma_{S(C)}(y)=4\). The inequalities have identical Boolean satisfying assignments, but saturation eliminates this strict coefficient-based priority.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Threshold saturation preserves Boolean feasibility but can turn a strict coefficient-based branching preference into a tie.
assumptions_latex: \sigma_C(v)\text{ is the coefficient of }v\text{ in }C.
S_b(a)=\min\{a,b\}\text{ with }b=4.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sigma_C(x)>\sigma_C(y)\quad\text{and}\quad\sigma_{S(C)}(x)=\sigma_{S(C)}(y).

notation.meaning: Coefficient-based literal score in constraint C.
Constraint obtained by capping coefficients at the right-hand side.

knowledge_statements.title: Saturation Can Erase Coefficient-Based Branching Priorities

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Foundational equivalence for normalized nonnegative pseudo-Boolean inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C:\sum_{i=1}^n a_i\ell_i\ge b\), where \(a_i\ge0\), \(b>0\), and \(\ell_i\in\{0,1\}\). Define \(S(C):\sum_i\min\{a_i,b\}\ell_i\ge b\). Then \(C\) and \(S(C)\) have identical Boolean satisfying assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Capping every nonnegative coefficient at the positive threshold preserves exactly the Boolean solutions.
assumptions_latex: a_i\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}.
b\in\mathbb R_{>0}.
\ell_i\in\{0,1\}\text{ for every }i.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C\equiv S(C)\quad\text{over Boolean assignments}.

notation.meaning: Constraint obtained by capping coefficients at the threshold

knowledge_statements.title: Boolean Equivalence of Threshold Saturation

assumptions_latex: \(C:\sum_{i=1}^n a_i\ell_i\ge b\) is normalized with \(a_i\ge0\), \(b>0\), and \(\ell_i\in\{0,1\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Saturation preserves Boolean feasibility but can erase coefficient distinctions used by later reasoning.

notation.meaning: Coefficient saturation at the right-hand side

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Addresses feasibility preservation and information loss under coefficient saturation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the normalized constraint \(C:\sum_i a_i\ell_i\ge b\), define \(S(C):\sum_i\min\{a_i,b\}\ell_i\ge b\). Because every selected term with \(a_i\ge b\) already satisfies the threshold alone, \(C\) and \(S(C)\) have the same Boolean satisfying assignments. Nevertheless, saturation identifies all coefficients at least \(b\); thus it can destroy magnitude and divisibility information relevant to subsequent division, cancellation, or heuristic scoring, even though feasibility is unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Saturating each coefficient at the threshold preserves Boolean solutions, but it removes coefficient magnitude and divisibility information that later reductions or heuristics may exploit.
knowledge_statements.title: Saturation Tradeoffs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Boolean-equivalence statement for nonnegative normalized constraints is precise, and failure_boundary fits this tradeoff leaf, but no source supports either saturation or the broader claims about later division, cancellation, and heuristic scoring.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Threshold Capping Is Not Valid for Arbitrary Signed Forms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Builder proposal rejected because it supplies no failing assignment and its displayed example remains equivalent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The proposed record gives \(2x-2y\ge1\) and \(x-2y\ge1\), then explicitly observes that they remain equivalent. It therefore does not establish the claimed failure of saturation on signed forms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proposed signed-form boundary is unsupported by its own example and is deferred.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The proposed record does not establish a signed-form failure boundary}.
review_flags: signed forms should first be normalized to nonnegative literals or governed by a separately defined operator
knowledge_statements.title: Threshold Capping Is Not Valid for Arbitrary Signed Forms

intermediate_metadata.reason: The inventory covers threshold capping, Boolean equivalence, idempotence, scale behavior, and loss of coefficient-based distinctions. The builder's nonprobative signed-form claim was deferred. Weakening, division, and multi-operator interactions were excluded as sibling scopes.

children.title: Combined Reduction Regimes
children.top_down_role: Interactions among weakening, division, and saturation choices.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete order-sensitive composition of precisely specified sound pseudo-Boolean reductions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For positive-coefficient inequalities, define \[W_j\!\left(\sum_i a_i\ell_i\ge b\right):\ \sum_{i\ne j}a_i\ell_i\ge b-a_j\] and \[D_d\!\left(\sum_i a_i\ell_i\ge b\right):\ \sum_i\left\lceil\frac{a_i}{d}\right\rceil\ell_i\ge\left\lceil\frac{b}{d}\right\rceil.\] For \(C:x+2y\ge2\) and \(d=2\), \[D_2(W_x(C)):y\ge1,\qquad W_x(D_2(C)):y\ge0.\] Thus these sound reductions do not commute, and division after weakening yields the strictly stronger consequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For x+2y≥2, weakening x before ceiling division yields y≥1, while division before weakening yields the tautology y≥0.
assumptions_latex: Weakening deletes a positive term and subtracts its coefficient from the threshold.
Division rounds every positive coefficient and the threshold upward.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D_2(W_x(C))\ne W_x(D_2(C)),\qquad D_2(W_x(C))\models W_x(D_2(C))\not\models D_2(W_x(C)).

notation.meaning: Specified sound weakening operator deleting term j

knowledge_statements.title: Weakening–Division Order Is Noncommutative

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sound Composition Does Not Imply Equivalence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between consequence soundness and preservation of satisfying assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For Boolean \(x,y\), \(C:x+y\ge2\) entails the sound weakening \(C_1:y\ge1\), but \((x,y)=(0,1)\) satisfies \(C_1\) and violates \(C\). Thus stepwise entailment guarantees \(C\models C_k\), not \(C\equiv C_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Composing sound reductions preserves consequence validity but need not preserve the original satisfying assignments.
assumptions_latex: \text{Weakening deletes }x\text{ and subtracts its coefficient from the threshold}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C\models C_1\quad\text{and}\quad C_1\not\models C.
knowledge_statements.title: Sound Composition Does Not Imply Equivalence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operator-independent entailment result for finite reduction sequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_0=C\) and \(C_j=R_j(C_{j-1})\) for \(j=1,\ldots,k\). If \(C_{j-1}\models C_j\) for every \(j\), then \(C\models C_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite sequence of individually sound consequence reductions remains sound.
assumptions_latex: k\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}.
C_{j-1}\models R_j(C_{j-1})\text{ for every }j.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C\models(R_k\circ\cdots\circ R_1)(C).
knowledge_statements.title: Soundness of Sequential Reductions

assumptions_latex: Each reduction in a sequence \(R_k\circ\cdots\circ R_1\) is a sound pseudo-Boolean consequence transformation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Combined reductions remain sound, but their order can change the final constraint and its inferential strength.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covers sequential weakening, division, and saturation rather than one isolated rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_0=C\) and \(C_j=R_j(C_{j-1})\), where every \(R_j\) is sound, so \(C_{j-1}\models C_j\). Then \(C\models C_k\). However, reductions involving rounding, literal deletion, or saturation need not commute: for two such operators, \(R_2(R_1(C))\) can differ from \(R_1(R_2(C))\), and neither result need imply the other. Hence local coefficient simplification may compound information loss, making reduction order part of the strength-size tradeoff.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sequence of sound reductions stays sound, but rounding, weakening, and saturation may not commute; their order can compound information loss and produce incomparable constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: Combined Reduction Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Soundness of a composition follows from the stated entailments, but the asserted noncommutativity and possible incomparability are not valid for every unspecified pair of sound reduction operators. A source and a precisely delimited class of weakening, division, and saturation operators are required.

children.title: Nonasserting Learned Constraints
children.top_down_role: Learned constraints that fail to force useful propagation at the relevant search state.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conflict-Blocking Clause With No Backtrack Assertion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clause-level witness separating exclusion of the analyzed conflict from immediate propagation after backtracking.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(L=
eg a\lor
eg b\lor c\) exclude the conflicting assignment \(a=b=1,c=0\). After backtracking, suppose the retained trail assigns only \(a=1\), leaving \(b\) and \(c\) unassigned. The residual clause \(
eg b\lor c\) has two unassigned literals and causes no unit propagation, so \(L\) is nonasserting at this backtrack state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conflict-blocking learned clause can retain two unassigned literals after backtracking and therefore propagate nothing immediately.
assumptions_latex: Propagation is ordinary clausal unit propagation.
The retained trail assigns \(a=1\) and assigns neither \(b\) nor \(c\).
\(L\) is a valid learned consequence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L\text{ blocks the analyzed assignment but is nonasserting on the retained trail}.
knowledge_statements.title: Conflict-Blocking Clause With No Backtrack Assertion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational definition for normalized nonnegative pseudo-Boolean inequalities under an explicitly specified propagation convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L:\sum_i a_i\ell_i\ge b\), with \(a_i\ge0\) and Boolean literals \(\ell_i\). For a consistent retained trail \(\tau\), define maximum slack \(s_\tau=\sum_{\ell_i\text{ true or unassigned under }\tau}a_i-b\). An unassigned \(\ell_j\) is forced true exactly when \(a_j>s_\tau\). Under this convention, \(L\) is asserting at \(\tau\) when at least one unassigned literal is forced and nonasserting when \(s_\tau\ge0\) and \(a_j\le s_\tau\) for every unassigned \(\ell_j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under maximum-slack pseudo-Boolean propagation, a nonconflicting learned constraint is nonasserting exactly when no unassigned literal has coefficient greater than the remaining slack.
assumptions_latex: L\text{ is a learned consequence in normalized nonnegative literal form}.
\tau\text{ is a consistent retained trail}.
\text{Propagation uses the stated maximum-slack rule}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L\text{ is nonasserting at }\tau\iff s_\tau\ge0\ \land\ \forall j\text{ unassigned},\ a_j\le s_\tau.

notation.meaning: Maximum achievable left-hand side under the retained trail minus the threshold

review_flags: asserting terminology is tied explicitly to the stated propagation convention
knowledge_statements.title: Pseudo-Boolean Nonassertion Under Maximum-Slack Propagation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Clausal Nonassertion at a Backtrack State
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clausal specialization under ordinary unit propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L\) be a learned clause and \(\tau_b\) the trail retained after backtracking. Then \(L\) is asserting exactly when it is unsatisfied and has one unassigned literal. It is nonasserting exactly when it is already satisfied or has at least two unassigned literals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A learned clause is nonasserting after backtracking when it is already satisfied or still has at least two unassigned literals.
assumptions_latex: L\text{ is entailed by the input formula}.
\tau_b\text{ is consistent}.
\text{Propagation is ordinary clausal unit propagation}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L\text{ is nonasserting at }\tau_b\iff L|_{\tau_b}\text{ is satisfied or has at least two unassigned literals}.

notation.meaning: Residual learned clause under the retained trail

knowledge_statements.title: Clausal Nonassertion at a Backtrack State

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonassertion Is Relative to the Retained Trail
knowledge_statements.scope_note: State dependence of assertion for a fixed learned clause.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(L=
eg a\lor
eg b\lor c\), the trail \(	au_1=\{a=1\}\) leaves \(
eg b\lor c\) and is nonasserting, whereas \(	au_2=\{a=1,b=1\}\) leaves the unit clause \(c\) and is asserting.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The same learned clause can be nonasserting at one retained trail and asserting at another.
assumptions_latex: \text{Propagation is ordinary clausal unit propagation}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{asserting}(L,\tau_1)\ne\operatorname{asserting}(L,\tau_2).
knowledge_statements.title: Nonassertion Is Relative to the Retained Trail

assumptions_latex: A solver is at decision level \(d>0\) under trail \(\tau\).
A learned constraint \(L\) is entailed by the original constraints and is falsified by the conflicting trail before backtracking.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(L\) is not unit at its computed backtrack level, learning \(L\) produces no immediate forced literal there.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the operational notion of assertion after nonchronological backtracking.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(b<d\) be the level to which conflict analysis backtracks. The learned constraint \(L\) is asserting at \(b\) precisely when, after retaining assignments of levels at most \(b\), its slack makes exactly one currently unassigned literal mandatory. If this condition fails, \(L\) is nonasserting: it remains a valid consequence and excludes the analyzed conflicting assignment, but it causes no immediate propagation upon backtracking to \(b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A learned constraint is nonasserting when it is valid and blocks the conflict but forces no literal immediately after the chosen backtrack.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonasserting Learned Constraints

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and operational focus fit the leaf, but no pseudo-Boolean conflict-analysis source is supplied. The phrase 'slack makes exactly one currently unassigned literal mandatory' also requires the solver's propagation and slack conventions before the characterization can be validated.

children.title: Low-Utility Learned Constraints
children.top_down_role: Learned constraints with little value for pruning, propagation, or conflict reuse.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Past Inactivity Does Not Preclude Future Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-window counterexample to interpreting zero observed use as permanent uselessness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the original clauses be \(x\lor y\) and \(\neg x\lor z\), with learned resolvent \(L=y\lor z\). An observation window \(W\) containing no assignment that makes \(L\) unit may give \(U_W(L)=0\). At a later trail with \(y=0\) and \(z\) unassigned, unit propagation on \(L\) forces \(z=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A learned clause can be unused during one finite observation window yet propagate at a later trail.
assumptions_latex: \(L=y\lor z\) is the resolvent of \(x\lor y\) and \(\neg x\lor z\).
\(U_W\) counts successful propagations during the finite window \(W\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: U_W(L)=0\not\Rightarrow L\text{ never propagates after }W.

notation.meaning: Observed propagation utility of learned constraint L during window W.

knowledge_statements.title: Past Inactivity Does Not Preclude Future Propagation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Logical Safety of Deleting an Entailed Learned Constraint
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correctness boundary separating logical deletion safety from heuristic search utility and proof-state dependencies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the permanent solver formula and let \(L\) be a learned constraint satisfying \(F\models L\). Then \(F\) and \(F\land L\) have exactly the same models. Consequently, deleting \(L\) from the learned database preserves satisfiability and every objective value defined solely on models of \(F\), although it may weaken propagation and enlarge future search. If retained derivations or an emitted proof reference \(L\), those dependencies must be deleted, rederived, or otherwise justified before physical removal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deleting a learned consequence preserves the underlying solutions and objective values, although it can weaken search and requires proof-dependency management.
assumptions_latex: F\models L.
The objective is evaluated solely on assignments satisfying the permanent formula \(F\).
Every retained proof or learned-constraint dependency on \(L\) is managed soundly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Mod}(F)=\operatorname{Mod}(F\land L),\qquad\operatorname{OPT}(F)=\operatorname{OPT}(F\land L).

notation.meaning: Entailed learned constraint considered for deletion.

knowledge_statements.title: Logical Safety of Deleting an Entailed Learned Constraint

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational definition parameterized by a declared observation and scoring policy.
