children.title: MaxSMT Boundary
children.top_down_role: Optimization over satisfiability-modulo-theories instances beyond Boolean-only MaxSAT.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between joint soft satisfiability and unavoidable positive cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume H is T-satisfiable and every soft weight is strictly positive. The optimal weighted MaxSMT cost is zero if and only if T\cup H\cup\{S_i:i\} is satisfiable. If zero weights are allowed, zero cost requires only joint satisfaction of H and all positive-weight soft formulas; zero-weight soft formulas may remain false.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With positive weights, zero MaxSMT cost is equivalent to joint theory satisfiability of all hard and soft formulas; zero-weight formulas create the precise exception.
assumptions_latex: H is T-satisfiable.
The soft family is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\forall i\;w_i>0)\Longrightarrow\left[z^*=0\iff T\cup H\cup\{S_i\}_i\text{ is satisfiable}\right].
knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Cost MaxSMT Criterion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact cost representation for finite weighted partial MaxSMT.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For hard formulas H and weighted soft formulas (S_i,w_i) over theory T, introduce fresh Boolean variables r_i and impose H\land\bigwedge_i(S_i\lor r_i). Then minimizing \sum_iw_ir_i over T-models has the same optimal value as minimizing \sum_iw_i\mathbf 1[M\not\models S_i]. For a fixed theory model, a minimum-cost relaxation assignment sets r_i=1 for every violated positive-weight soft formula and r_i=0 for every satisfied positive-weight soft formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relaxing each soft theory formula with a costed Boolean variable gives an exact weighted MaxSMT formulation.
assumptions_latex: The hard and soft families are finite.
w_i\ge0.
Every r_i is fresh and Boolean.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_{M\models_T H}\sum_iw_i\mathbf1[M\not\models S_i]=\min_{M,r\models_T H\land\bigwedge_i(S_i\lor r_i)}\sum_iw_ir_i.

notation.meaning: relaxation variable for soft formula S_i

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Variable MaxSMT Formulation
MaxSMT Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates theory-aware weighted satisfiability from purely propositional MaxSAT or SAT reasoning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A weighted partial MaxSMT instance over a background theory \(T\) consists of hard formulas \(H\) and weighted soft formulas \((S_i,w_i)\) with \(w_i\ge0\). Its feasible models are the \(T\)-models satisfying every formula in \(H\), and the objective is \(\min\sum_i w_i\mathbf{1}[M\not\models S_i]\). A Boolean abstraction alone is insufficient: a propositionally consistent assignment may select theory atoms that are jointly \(T\)-inconsistent. Exact MaxSMT therefore requires theory-consistency checks and theory-valid lemmas, in addition to an optimization mechanism that certifies the minimum soft-violation cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: MaxSMT minimizes weighted soft violations subject to hard formulas and background-theory consistency; Boolean satisfiability alone cannot exclude theory-inconsistent assignments.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) supplies a defined model relation for all formulas.
\(H\) and the indexed soft family are finite, with \(w_i\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An optimum is a \(T\)-model \(M^\star\models H\) minimizing \(\sum_i w_i\mathbf{1}[M^\star\not\models S_i]\); propositional consistency alone is not a feasibility certificate.
review_flags: No supplied source locator covers weighted partial MaxSMT semantics or theory-consistency certification.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The weighted partial MaxSMT semantics and theory-consistency boundary are mathematically plausible and fit the leaf, but no source locator supports the definition or certification claim.

children.title: Theory-Optimization Boundary
children.top_down_role: Optimization mechanisms relying on native background-theory reasoning.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Witness that feasibility-exact abstraction need not preserve objective values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In real arithmetic, minimize f(x)=x over 0\le x\le1. If the abstraction contains no atom distinguishing values of x, every feasible model maps to one Boolean value b. The abstraction is exact for feasibility, but assigning b any objective value other than the fiber value g(b)=0 gives the wrong infimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A one-state Boolean abstraction can preserve feasibility while losing the real objective variation required for exact optimization.
assumptions_latex: The objective is minimized over the closed interval [0,1].
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{feasibility-exact abstraction}\not\Longrightarrow\text{objective-exact abstraction}.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Information Loss Under Boolean Abstraction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact value decomposition of theory optimization through a finite Boolean abstraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \mathcal M_T be the set of theory-feasible models, let B be a nonempty finite Boolean abstraction domain, and let \alpha:\mathcal M_T\to B. Define g(b)=\inf\{f(M):M\in\mathcal M_T,\alpha(M)=b\}, with g(b)=+\infty for an empty fiber. Then \inf_{M\in\mathcal M_T}f(M)=\min_{b\in B}g(b), using extended-real conventions. If a minimizing fiber has a model attaining its fiber infimum, that model is globally optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Theory optimization decomposes exactly into the best attainable value in each Boolean abstraction fiber, with empty fibers assigned infinite cost.
assumptions_latex: B is finite and nonempty.
f is defined on \mathcal M_T with values interpreted in the extended real line.
Empty-fiber infima are +\infty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf_{M\in\mathcal M_T}f(M)=\min_{b\in B}g(b).

notation.meaning: infimum of f over abstraction fiber b

review_flags: The identity is a value decomposition, not a claim that every exact fixed-instance reduction must explicitly represent every fiber.
knowledge_statements.title: Abstraction-Fiber Value Decomposition
Theory-Optimization Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes when theory-aware optimization can be replaced exactly by optimization over a Boolean abstraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be a background theory, let \(A\) be a finite set of theory atoms, and let \(\alpha(M)\in\{0,1\}^{A}\) record their truth values in a model \(M\models T\). Define \(F_T=\{b:\exists M\models T,\ \alpha(M)=b\}\). For an objective \(f\), a purely Boolean optimization is exact only if it represents \(F_T\) and assigns each \(b\in F_T\) the value \(g(b)=\inf\{f(M):M\models T,\ \alpha(M)=b\}\). Under these conditions, \[\inf_{M\models T}f(M)=\inf_{b\in F_T}g(b).\] The theory-optimization boundary is crossed when theory feasibility is omitted or when objective values cannot be recovered from abstraction fibers; Boolean optimality then need not imply theory-level optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Boolean optimization is exact only when it captures precisely the theory-feasible assignments and the best objective attainable within every abstraction fiber.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) has a specified model semantics.
\(A\) is finite and \(\alpha\) is defined on every model considered.
The infima are interpreted in the extended real line.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{M\models T}f(M)=\inf_{b\in F_T}g(b)\) under exact feasibility and fiber-value representation; otherwise the Boolean reduction may fail.

notation.meaning: Boolean valuation induced by theory model M
set of Boolean valuations extendable to models of T
best theory-level objective value in abstraction fiber b

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind fits this boundary leaf, but the record has no citation. The stated "only if" condition is not necessary for exactness of one fixed optimization instance: equality of optimal values can occur without representing every theory-feasible Boolean assignment or every fiber value. Necessity would require an explicit universal notion of exact representation, such as preservation for all admissible objectives or recovery of the full value function. The domain and codomain of f are also not introduced, and the plain statement omits this quantification issue. An authoritative OMT or abstraction source and a precise exactness criterion are required.

children.title: Boolean-Abstraction Interface
children.top_down_role: Connections through Boolean abstraction, refinement, or delegated theory checks.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal witness that skeleton satisfiability over-approximates theory satisfiability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In linear real arithmetic, let a denote x\le0 and b denote x\ge1. The Boolean skeleton p_a\land p_b has the satisfying valuation p_a=p_b=1, but the selected theory literals \{x\le0,x\ge1\} have no real model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Selecting both x at most zero and x at least one satisfies the Boolean skeleton but is impossible over the reals.
assumptions_latex: The background theory is linear real arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p_a=p_b=1\not\Longrightarrow\exists x\in\mathbb R:(x\le0\land x\ge1).
knowledge_statements.title: Propositionally Consistent but Theory-Inconsistent Abstraction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condition under which a theory conflict may be learned at the Boolean level.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let C be a finite set of signed theory literals. If T\cup C is unsatisfiable, then T\models igvee_{\ell\in C}
eg\ell. Under the fixed mapping a\mapsto p_a, with 
eg a represented by 
eg p_a, the corresponding Boolean clause blocks every valuation selecting all literals in C and blocks no valuation induced by a T-model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A theory-inconsistent literal set yields a sound Boolean blocking clause when atom and polarity mappings are fixed.
assumptions_latex: T is an axiom set with a defined entailment relation.
Each atom has a fixed Boolean representative and negation is represented by opposite Boolean polarity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T\cup C\text{ unsatisfiable}\Longrightarrow T\models\bigvee_{\ell\in C}\neg\ell.
knowledge_statements.title: Theory-Conflict Clause Soundness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resolves the signed-literal and semantic conventions required by the Boolean-abstraction interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let T be an axiom set, let A be the finite set of theory atoms in a quantifier-free formula \varphi, and replace each a\in A by p_a to obtain B(\varphi). For a total Boolean valuation b define L_b=\{a\in A:b(p_a)=1\}\cup\{\neg a:a\in A,\ b(p_a)=0\}. Then \varphi is T-satisfiable if and only if there exists b\models B(\varphi) for which T\cup L_b is satisfiable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Boolean valuation selects exactly one signed literal for every abstracted atom, and it represents a theory solution exactly when that complete literal set is theory-consistent.
assumptions_latex: \varphi is quantifier-free over the semantics specified by the axiom set T.
Each atom a has one fixed Boolean representative p_a.
b is total on all representatives occurring in B(\varphi).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T\text{-SAT}(\varphi)\iff\exists b\models B(\varphi):T\cup L_b\text{ is satisfiable}.

notation.meaning: complete signed theory-literal set selected by b

knowledge_statements.title: Complete Signed-Literal Abstraction
Boolean-Abstraction Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specifies the sound interface between a propositional skeleton and a background-theory feasibility oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\varphi\) be a quantifier-free theory formula whose distinct theory atoms form \(A\), and replace every atom \(a\in A\) by a propositional variable \(p_a\) to obtain the skeleton \(B(\varphi)\). A Boolean valuation \(b\models B(\varphi)\) represents a feasible theory solution exactly when the corresponding literal set \(L_b\) is \(T\)-satisfiable. Thus \[\varphi\text{ is }T\text{-satisfiable}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\exists b\models B(\varphi)\text{ such that }T\cup L_b\text{ is satisfiable}.\] If \(T\cup C\) is inconsistent for some \(C\subseteq L_b\), the interface may return the theory-valid blocking clause \(\bigvee_{\ell\in C}\neg\ell\). Skeleton satisfiability without this theory-consistency test is only an over-approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A satisfying Boolean assignment denotes a theory solution only when its selected theory literals are jointly satisfiable; theory conflicts yield valid blocking clauses.
assumptions_latex: \(\varphi\) is quantifier-free over a fixed background theory \(T\).
Each theory atom has one consistent propositional representative.
The theory oracle decides satisfiability for the literal sets submitted to it.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T\text{-SAT}(\varphi)\iff\exists b\models B(\varphi):T\cup L_b\text{ is satisfiable}\).

notation.meaning: propositional skeleton of the theory formula
theory-literal set selected by Boolean valuation b
theory-inconsistent subset used to form a blocking clause

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind is appropriate for the Boolean-abstraction interface, and the core satisfiability equivalence is standard. However, no source or inspectable locator is cited. The record should specify that L_b contains, for every atom a in A, a when b(p_a)=1 and its negation when b(p_a)=0. It must also clarify whether T denotes a class of structures or an axiom set, because expressions such as M models T and T union L_b mix semantic and syntactic presentations. The blocking clause is valid only after the correspondence between theory literals and their Boolean representatives is made explicit. A specific authoritative SMT source is required.

children.title: Theory-Lemma Certification Boundary
children.top_down_role: Proof-support limits arising from theory-specific lemmas or optimization claims.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic requirements for a theory-aware minimization certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let P_v be an encoding satisfying P_v\text{ is }T\text{-satisfiable}\iff\exists M\models_T H:f(M)<v. If a checker verifies a model M^\star\models_T H with f(M^\star)=v, the soundness and completeness of the threshold encoding, a refutation of P_v, and the T-validity of every theory lemma used by that refutation, then M^\star is globally optimal with value v.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible model and a checked refutation of an exact strict-threshold encoding certify theory-level optimality.
assumptions_latex: Objective evaluation is exact.
P_v is sound and complete for theory-feasible models of objective below v.
Every proof step and theory lemma is checked under its declared proof system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f(M^\star)=v\land\neg\exists M\models_T H:f(M)<v\Longrightarrow M^\star\in\arg\min_{M\models_T H}f(M).

notation.meaning: encoding of theory-feasible solutions with objective below v

review_flags: Concrete threshold encodings, proof formats, and lemma certificates remain theory dependent.
knowledge_statements.title: Threshold-Refutation Optimality Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trust boundary induced by unchecked theory lemmas.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a Boolean refutation \pi use input clauses F and learned theory clauses L_1,\ldots,L_m. Mechanical verification of \pi alone establishes unsatisfiability of F\land\bigwedge_iL_i. It establishes T-unsatisfiability of F only when every L_i is independently certified as T-valid. Otherwise the conclusion is conditional on the unchecked lemmas.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Checking the Boolean proof but not its theory lemmas yields a proof relative to those lemmas, not an unconditional theory certificate.
assumptions_latex: The Boolean proof system is sound.
Every non-input clause and its required justification are identified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Check}(\pi)\land\bigwedge_i(T\models L_i)\Longrightarrow F\text{ is }T\text{-unsatisfiable}.
knowledge_statements.title: Relative Versus Unconditional Theory-Lemma Certification
Theory-Lemma Certification Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States when theory lemmas support an independently checkable optimality certificate in theory-aware Boolean optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem over theory \(T\), a certificate of optimal value \(v\) consists of a feasible model \(M\) with \(f(M)=v\), a Boolean derivation refuting every encoded solution with objective value strictly below \(v\), and every theory lemma \(L_i\) used by that derivation. Certification requires a checker to verify \(M\models T\), the objective value, the Boolean derivation, and \(T\models L_i\) for every \(i\). These checks establish \[f(M)=v\quad\text{and}\quad\neg\exists N\models T\text{ with }f(N)<v.\] The certification boundary is crossed if a theory lemma is accepted merely as an opaque oracle assertion: the Boolean derivation then certifies optimality only relative to unverified assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An optimality certificate is complete only when feasibility, objective value, Boolean reasoning, and every theory-lemma entailment are independently checkable.
assumptions_latex: The optimization problem is a minimization problem with a well-defined objective \(f\).
The Boolean derivation system has a mechanically checkable proof format.
Each theory lemma has a decidable certificate or trusted checking procedure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Verified feasibility and lower-bound refutation imply that \(M\) is optimal with value \(v\); an unchecked theory lemma prevents unconditional certification.

notation.meaning: theory lemma used in the Boolean derivation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind fits the exact leaf, but the proposed certificate model is not supported by any citation and is not precise enough to establish the displayed conclusion. The record does not define the encoding of solutions with f(N)<v, state its soundness and completeness relative to T, or specify how each entailment T models L_i is certified. A checkable Boolean refutation establishes the lower bound only when the threshold encoding and all theory lemmas are independently validated under a stated proof system. Because these details determine the mathematical force of the certificate, an authoritative proof-logging or OMT-certification source with a specific locator is required.
